analysisSections.title: Phase 0 — Routing & FX
analysisSections.text: Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results / pre-H1 trading update. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state. FX Revenue Check: The RNS contains no Currency Movements section with explicit percentage breakdowns. AB Dynamics sells internationally with EUR and USD exposure. The RNS references a "€9.7m contract" but this represents approximately 8% of the £124m FY revenue base. No single non-GBP currency is explicitly stated as exceeding 30% of revenues. No FX Rule 1 triggered. Proceeded to Phase 1 without FX penalty.

analysisSections.title: Phase 1 — Data Context
analysisSections.text: Consensus forecasts (pre-RNS): FY1 (FY26, year-end 31 Aug 26) EPS = 79.9p, Revenue = £124.2m. FY2 EPS = 87.9p, Revenue = £134.4m. Consensus target price = £21.98 vs current price £12.65 — implying 74% upside to consensus TP. The scale of this gap indicates TPs are stale / pre-derating. 12-month forecast momentum: EPS net change over the full weekly snapshot period = +8.3% (73.8p → 79.9p). Revenue moved from £120.9m to £124.2m (+2.7%). A significant step-up occurred in mid-November 2025 (EPS jumped from 75.2p to 80.9p, Revenue from £116.4m to £125.2m), followed by a modest drift back. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Net positive over 12 months dominated by that single November 2025 upgrade event. 3-year average H1 % of full year (historical actuals only): — Revenue H1 %: 46.9% (3yr avg: FY23 38/83=45.8%, FY24 49/101=48.5%, FY25 52/111=46.8%) — EPS H1 %: 43.4% (3yr avg: FY23 19.9/48.1=41.4%, FY24 27.1/60.8=44.6%, FY25 30.9/70.0=44.1%) Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS consensus): — Revenue: FY1 £124.2m − H1 consensus £58m = H2 £66.2m implied. Prior H2 actual £59m. Implied H2 YoY = +12.2% — EPS: FY1 79.9p − H1 consensus 37.0p = H2 42.9p implied. Prior H2 actual 39.1p. Implied H2 YoY = +9.7%

analysisSections.title: Phase 2 — RNS Extraction
analysisSections.text: RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Half Year Trading Update for period to 28 Feb 2026; full P&L not published; H1 results due 14 April 2026) 1. Revenue figures: — H1 FY26 revenue: approximately £49m — vs seasonal baseline (46.9% × £124.2m = £58.3m): −£9.3m / −15.9% miss — Management framing: "in line with expectations" — consistent with previously guided 40/60 H1/H2 weighting — Implied H2 revenue (to hit FY26 consensus £124.2m): £75.2m — Implied H2 YoY vs prior H2 actual (£59m): +27.5%

analysisSections.quote: "Group revenue in the first half was approximately £49m, in line with expectations, and consistent with the previously guided trading performance weighting of approximately 40% / 60% towards the second half of the current year, set against the context of a greater first half bias in FY25 than typically expected."

analysisSections.text: 2. EPS / Earnings: — No H1 EPS figure disclosed in this update — FY26 guidance: "expects to deliver FY26 adjusted operating profit in line with current expectations" — Footnote confirms analyst consensus mean = £24.4m adjusted operating profit for year ended 31 Aug 2026 — This is an explicit in-line hold — no upgrade, no cut to FY guidance — H1 EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE until 14 April 2026 full results

analysisSections.quote: "The Board remains confident that the Group will make further financial and strategic progress this year and expects to deliver FY26 adjusted operating profit in line with current expectations. [Footnote: Company compiled analyst expectations is for a mean adjusted operating profit for the year ended 31 August 2026 of £24.4m.]"

analysisSections.text: 3. In light of this, the Group will record an impairment of the Chinese testing services business and will undertake a strategic review of that business during the second half of the year."

Capital returns / financial position: — Net cash: £39.3m (28 Feb 2025: £27.2m; 31 Aug 2025: £41.4m) — robust balance sheet, modest H1 cash deployment — No buyback or special dividend announced — Active pipeline of potential acquisition targets referenced — DPS: FY1 fc 10.50p, FY2 fc 11.50p (no change in this update)

analysisSections.title: Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
analysisSections.text: H1 TRACKING SIGNAL Signal classification: 🔴 REVENUE SELL SIGNAL (−7.4pp vs seasonal average) Critical overlay: Management pre-guided 40/60 H1/H2 weighting — this deviation is anticipated. Seasonal baselines (3yr avg): — H1 Revenue % of FY: 46.9% → Implied baseline: £58.3m — H1 EPS % of FY: 43.4% → Implied baseline: 34.7p RNS H1 actuals: — Revenue: £49m → 39.5% of FY1 cns → Deviation: −7.4pp — EPS: Not disclosed → UNTRACKABLE Buy trigger thresholds (for 14 Apr 2026 H1 results): — H1 Rev ≥ £60.1m (≥+1.5pp signal) — H1 EPS ≥ 35.9p (≥+1.5pp signal) Sell trigger thresholds: — H1 Rev ≤ £56.4m (≤−1.5pp signal) — H1 EPS ≤ 33.5p (≤−1.5pp signal) H2 burden read-through: — H2 must deliver £75.2m revenue (+27.5% YoY vs £59m prior H2) to hit FY26 consensus — H2 EPS burden: 42.9p = 53.7% of FY26 consensus EPS — broadly manageable (hist avg H2 was ~56.6%) — 70% cover from H1 delivered + £47m order book provides credible support for H2 ramp Watch date: H1 full results → 14 April 2026 Historical hit rate: In FY24 and FY25, when H1 revenue tracked near or above seasonal average, full-year results delivered growth. FY26 H1 is deliberately below seasonal norm per guided phasing — no direct historical precedent for this pre-guided 40/60 scenario in recent years. HALF-ON-HALF HISTORICAL DATA Period | Rev £m | YoY % | EPS p | YoY % -------------|--------|---------|-------|------- FY23 H1 | 38 | — | 19.9 | — FY23 H2 | 45 | — | 28.2 | — FY24 H1 | 49 | +28.9% | 27.1 | +36.2% H1 Rev% FY: 48.5% vs avg: +1.6pp FY24 H2 | 52 | +15.6% | 33.7 | +19.5% FY25 H1 | 52 | +6.1% | 30.9 | +14.0% H1 Rev% FY: 46.8% vs avg: −0.1pp FY25 H2 | 59 | +13.5% | 39.1 | +16.0% FY26 H1 (act)| 49 | −5.8% | — | — H1 Rev% FY: 39.5% vs avg: −7.4pp [pre-guided] FY26 H2 (imp)| 75.2 | +27.5% | 42.9 | +9.7% FY26 cns | 124.2 | +11.9% | 79.9 | +14.1% Full-year trajectory: — Revenue: FY23→FY24: +21.7%; FY24→FY25: +9.9%; FY25→FY26cns: +11.9% → Classification: Decelerating then stabilising — EPS: FY23→FY24: +26.4%; FY24→FY25: +15.1%; FY25→FY26cns: +14.1% → Classification: Decelerating gradually Implied H2 momentum: Revenue +27.5% YoY → Strong (requires). EPS +9.7% YoY → Moderate. Forecast momentum overlay: EPS +8.3% net over 10 months (step-up Nov 2025 dominated). Last 4 weeks FLAT. Price derating of −44.9% vs EPS +8.3% = severe divergence. P/E compressed from ~31x to ~16x. Structural flags: China impairment removes a growth vector. 40/60 rev phasing is a permanent H1/H2 shift for FY26. Macro/tariff risk flagged by management.

analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text: 1. Dominant line items: #1: China impairment (~£16m non-underlying) + strategic review. Even as non-cash/non-underlying, the loss of a China growth foothold will headline all broker notes. FY27 estimates must be revised. #2: H1 revenue miss vs seasonal norm / 40/60 phasing. £49m vs £58m implied seasonal expectation will dominate risk-reward debate — partially resolved by pre-guidance. 2. Forecast revision direction and magnitude: FY1 (FY26) — Revenue: Hold / −0 to −3%. EPS (underlying): Hold / −0 to −2%. Adj. operating profit explicitly confirmed £24.4m. FY2 (FY27) — Revenue: −3% to −6% (China contribution removed). EPS: −2% to −5%. 3. Target price and recommendation implications: Consensus TP £21.98 is severely stale vs £12.65 market price. Expect significant TP cuts toward £14–18 range. Recommendations likely held at Buy/Add but with flagged caution. No upgrades to recommendation from this RNS. 4. "Conservative guidance" read-through: FY26 guidance references the specific £24.4m footnote — this is a quantified in-line hold, not a conservative "not less than" framing. No upgrade cycle language. 40/60 phasing pre-communicated since January update. Partially cushions H1 miss interpretation. 5. Key risk / offsetting factor: H2 delivery requires a 27.5% YoY revenue ramp. 70% cover from order book is supportive but execution risk is real given macro uncertainty and geopolitical commentary. China uncertainty clouds FY27 visibility. 6. Overall broker-note tone forecast: Cautious but constructive. Brokers maintain medium-term Buy thesis (structural demand, OEM-agnostic, regulatory tailwinds for active safety/AV) while flagging near-term H2 execution risk and China strategic overhang. TP cuts likely across the board. First notes probably titled "In line, but China and H2 the focus" — holding conviction with reduced near-term momentum.

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: Final Score: 43 / 100 Band: 30–49 — Likely Flat to Slight Cut Confidence range: 38–48 Mode: Pre-H1 Score components: +40 Base (FY guidance confirmed in-line, quantified at £24.4m) −9 China impairment + strategic review (FY27 revenue/EPS cuts required) −8 H1 rev −7.4pp seasonal miss (partially mitigated by pre-guided 40/60 phasing) −5 H2 burden +27.5% YoY revenue requirement (execution risk) +6 Order book £47m +11.9% YoY, 70% FY26 cover +3 Net cash £39.3m, robust balance sheet −2 EPS trend +8.3% but flat 4-week momentum; price/TP gap signals stale TPs −2 Macro/geopolitical risk language; no upgrade trigger language = 43 The score of 43 reflects a genuine "hold the line" RNS. FY26 underlying estimates are likely to be maintained, preventing a formal cut cycle. However, the China impairment forces FY27 revision, the H1 revenue miss (however pre-guided) elevates H2 scrutiny, and the large gap between stale consensus TPs and the market price creates a headwind for any re-rating catalyst. The key near-term event is the full H1 results on 14 April 2026 — that will be the scorecard that matters for FY26 delivery confirmation.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

ABDP · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/8/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). Incoming RNS = H1 FY26 results (6 months to 28 February 2026).
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e, pre-RNS): EPS 79.8p · Revenue £117.8m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e, pre-RNS): EPS 87.6p · Revenue £127.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change full period: +8.1% (73.8p → 79.8p). Pattern: flat at ~73.9p until late Oct 2025, then step-up in Nov 2025 to 80.9p (FY25 results), minor trim to 79.8p by Jan 2026, flat since. Revenue: 120.9m → peak 125.2m (Nov 2025) → trimmed to 117.8m (Mar 2026). Clear step-down in revenue consensus post-FY25 results as brokers cut to reflect the signalled H1 weakness. 4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT (79.8p unchanged).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg FY23–FY25): Revenue 46.9% of FY = £55.2m (46.9% × £117.8m) · EPS 43.4% of FY = 34.6p (43.4% × 79.8p)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1, ended Feb 2025): Revenue £58.0m · EPS 37.0p (adjusted diluted per RNS)
  • Implied H2 YoY (FY26, pre-RNS): Revenue: £117.8m − prior-year H1 adj baseline → H2 implied = £117.8m − £48.8m (H1 actual) = £69.0m vs FY25 H2 £56.7m = +21.7% (RNS-derived, as H1 actual now known). EPS: FY26e 79.8p − H1 actual 31.3p = implied H2 48.5p vs FY25 H2 43.3p = +12.0% (consensus-derived H2; RNS confirms H1 is 31.3p adjusted diluted).
  • FX: RNS discloses constant currency impact: constant currency revenue £49.7m vs reported £48.8m — a +£0.9m FX headwind on revenue (+1.8%). Adjusted operating profit constant currency £9.3m vs reported £9.1m — £0.2m FX headwind. USD and Yen weakened vs GBP; EUR strengthened vs GBP. Total FX headwind is modest (c.1.8% on revenue). Non-GBP exposure: USD (Bakersfield, VTS Michigan, ~20%+ of revenue?), EUR (European operations), JPY (Japan). RNS states: "constant currency revenue would have been £0.9m higher." This is a small headwind but below the 30% single-currency threshold. Phase 0B not triggered — FX impact confirmed minimal via constant currency disclosure. No FX badge.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY24 H1 −£21.3m (net cash) / FY25 H1 −£27.2m / FY25 H2 (FY25 YE) −£41.4m / FY26 H1 (RNS-disclosed) −£39.3m net cash / FY26fc −£42.3m / FY27fc −£52.9m · ND/EBITDA: FY23 −1.70x / FY24 −1.60x / FY25 −0.90x / current −1.20x / FY26fc −1.50x / FY27fc −1.70x · Interest cover FY26fc: 55.7x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — £39.3m net cash at H1, deepening through forecast period. No Phase 5 scored row.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

ABDP · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/8/26

RNS type: Half Year Results

1. Revenue figures H1 FY26 revenue: £48.8m (H1 FY25: £58.0m = −16% YoY). Pre-RNS H1 consensus proxy: 3yr avg 46.9% × £117.8m = £55.2m → H1 actual £48.8m = −11.6% miss vs baseline.

Full year FY26 guidance: "adjusted operating profit expected to be in line with current expectations" — analyst mean adjusted operating profit of £24.4m. Sharescope revenue consensus: £117.8m. H2 implied: £117.8m − £48.8m = £69.0m (+21.7% vs FY25 H2 £56.7m, consensus-derived for FY full year remaining unchanged).

"Revenue decreased by 16% reflecting the previously communicated delays in the timing of order intake and customer delivery requirements, together with the weaker than anticipated volumes at our VadoTech Testing Services business in China."

2. EPS / earnings figures H1 FY26 adjusted diluted EPS: 31.3p (H1 FY25: 37.0p = −15.4% YoY). Pre-RNS H1 EPS baseline: 3yr avg 43.4% × 79.8p = 34.6p → H1 actual 31.3p = −9.5% miss vs seasonal baseline (−3.3pp deviation).

Statutory diluted EPS: −53.0p (H1 FY25: +21.9p) — dominated by £16.8m exceptional VadoTech impairment.

FY26e consensus adjusted EPS: 79.8p (pre-RNS). H2 implied adjusted EPS: 79.8p − 31.3p = 48.5p vs FY25 H2 adjusted 43.3p = +12.0% YoY.

EPS quality check: Adjusted effective tax rate: 20% (H1 FY25: 20%) — in line with prior year and stated normalised rate. No deviation. ✅ No restatement required. The headline adjusted EPS of 31.3p uses a consistent normalised rate; no quality concern on adjusted basis.

However: statutory loss driven by £16.8m VadoTech impairment (predominantly non-cash). This is a non-recurring exceptional — does not affect adjusted EPS but removes a business that was previously contributing (or expected to contribute) to FY26/FY27 models.

3. FY26e EPS bridge (FY1→FY2 bridge, for FY27) (1) New base: FY26e adjusted EPS — brokers will likely revise FY26e downward post-H1 miss and VadoTech (see below). If FY26e settles at ~70p (guidance intact but H1 miss shifts mix), FY27e bridge: (2) Inorganic annualisation: no acquisitions in H1. ABD Solutions and ClearTrack at early stage — no material EPS contribution modelled. (3) Organic EBITDA growth: medium-term ambition of 10% p.a. organic growth + >20% margin. FY26e EBITDA consensus £29.2m. VadoTech strategic review will likely reduce FY27 revenue base (China business impairing). Ex-VadoTech FY26 revenue c.£48.8m H1 + ~£69m H2 = £117.8m less VadoTech's contribution (~£4–6m H2 being wound down). FY27e EBITDA £32.0m (consensus) ex-VadoTech may need revision. (4) Interest step-up: net cash deepening — no interest cost concern. Implied FY27e EPS revision risk: consensus £87.6p may be at risk if VadoTech removal reduces FY26e base and medium-term growth ambitions require recalibration. Flagged — formal revision range in Phase 4.

4. Order book / forward work Period end order book: £47m (H1 FY25: £42m, FY25 YE: £32m). H2 order book: £29m for delivery in H2. Combined with H1 revenue delivered: £48.8m + £29m in-hand = £77.8m against expected FY26 revenue (£117.8m consensus) = 66%+ coverage. RNS states "circa 70% coverage."

"Period end order book of £47m (H1 2025: £42m), which in addition to revenue already delivered in the first half gives circa 70% coverage of expected full year revenue, providing good visibility for the rest of FY 2026."

Order book YoY: +£5m / +11.9% vs H1 FY25 — positive signal. Recovery from £32m at FY25 YE.

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • H1 FY26 adjusted operating margin: 18.6% (H1 FY25: 18.6%) — flat YoY despite −16% revenue decline. Management explicitly held margin through operational gearing mitigation.
  • H1 FY26 gross margin: 63.7% (+350bps vs H1 FY25 60.2%) — strong improvement driven by positive revenue mix and full-year effect of operational improvements.
  • Adjusted EBITDA margin: 23.2% (H1 FY25: 22.2%, +100bps)
  • VadoTech exceptional charge: £16.8m (predominantly non-cash impairment) — isolated issue, already actioned via strategic review
  • Medium-term margin target: >20% adjusted operating margin. Current 18.6% — gap remains but trajectory positive given the operational gearing improvements demonstrated in H1.

"Operating margin maintained at 18.6%, as the negative impact of operational gearing was offset by a combination of the full year effect of operational improvements, management implemented cost mitigation actions and positive revenue mix."

6. Capital returns / per-share items Interim dividend: 3.08p per share (+10% vs H1 FY25 2.80p). Payment 15 May 2026. FY25 final dividend 6.36p paid 30 Jan 2026. Progressive dividend policy confirmed — signal of board confidence despite the H1 miss.

Net cash: £39.3m (H1 FY25: £27.2m, FY25 YE: £41.4m). Cash conversion rolling 12 months: 102% of adjusted EBITDA — strong.

7. Qualitative tone "Absent an extended disruption, the Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations [mean £24.4m]." H2 revenue bias: 55–60% of FY (explicit guidance). Order book £47m; 70% FY coverage. Middle East situation monitored. VadoTech strategic review to conclude H2.

"Whilst we are mindful of the current geopolitical uncertainty, absent an extended disruption, the Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "The Board expects adjusted operating profit for FY 2026 to be in line with current expectations [mean £24.4m]"

  • Additional qualifier: "absent an extended disruption" (Middle East caveat)
  • Guidance nature: numeric — specific reference to analyst mean £24.4m adjusted operating profit
  • Year coverage: FY26 only
  • Nature assessment: Management maintains FY26 OP guidance despite a −16% revenue H1 miss. This requires a significant H2 (+21.7% revenue YoY) to close the gap. The guidance is maintained but qualified with a geopolitical caveat — "absent an extended disruption." This is a conditional in-line statement, not an upgrade.
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — guidance maintained at consensus with explicit caveat. Given the H1 revenue miss of −16%, maintaining guidance requires extraordinary H2 confidence. However, the order book coverage (70% of FY) and guided 55–60% H2 bias make this achievable arithmetically. The conditional language introduces caution.
  • Provisional points: 0 to +3
  • Divergence check: Current year H1 missed revenue and EPS vs seasonal baseline, but full-year guidance maintained. This is a H1-miss / FY-hold divergence — somewhat unusual but explained by the front-loaded H2 order book recovery. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — H1 operational miss but FY guidance held; H2 delivery risk elevated. Carry as named row in Phase 5.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: ABDP's H1 FY26 result is defined by a −16% YoY revenue decline to £48.8m (H1 FY25: £58.0m) and adjusted diluted EPS of 31.3p (−15.4% YoY). Against the seasonal baseline, both metrics fired 🔴🔴 SELL SIGNALS: revenue at −5.5pp deviation and EPS at −4.2pp deviation vs 3yr averages. Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Post-H1, brokers will cut FY26e EPS by −5 to −10% (79.8p → 71–76p) as they discount the H2 delivery risk and remove VadoTech contribution assumptions. FY27e EPS cuts of −5 to −12% (87.6p → 77–83p) are expected as the VadoTech revenue base is removed and growth ambitions are recalibrated. Target prices will be cut from the stale £21.98 consensus to approximately £14–17, representing −20% to −35% TP cuts — though this still implies significant upside from the current £11.44 price. The +92% TP upside at current price makes ABDP a potential value case for patient investors, but the upgrade cycle is suspended pending proof of H2 execution. Key watch: H2 FY26 results (due October 2026) — if £69m H2 revenue and 48.5p H2 EPS are delivered, the medium-term growth case revives. If motion platform contracts slip or VadoTech review reveals further costs, a formal profit warning is possible. 🏁 Material broker cuts expected on FY26e and FY27e EPS; TP reductions to £14–17 likely; hold ratings probably maintained given strong balance sheet — the upgrade case is deferred, not destroyed.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Note: AUA £110.2bn at 31 March 2026 (+20% YoY) is a strong leading indicator. If management fee yield is ~0.24% on AUA, implied annualised revenue = £264m platform fees. Total revenue £348.7m consensus includes other items. AUA trajectory is very positive for revenue tracking.

Revenue baseline for FY26 H1: 3yr avg H1% = 47.4%. £348.7m × 47.4% = £165.3m. Buy trigger: £165.3m × 1.015 = £167.8m. H1 results (21 May 2026) will be the tracking date.

Implied H1 from AUA leading indicator: AUA growth +20% YoY is a proxy for revenue growth. If revenue grows at a similar rate: FY25 H1 £131.3m × 1.20 = £157.6m implied H1 revenue. vs baseline £165.3m: deviation = £157.6m/£348.7m = 45.2% vs 47.4% baseline → indicative deviation −2.2pp. Flag as 🟡 PROBABLE CAUTION (implied deviation ≤ −1.5pp — AUA growth rate does not fully translate to revenue growth at same rate due to mix shift in fees). The real concern is that H2 EPS is essentially flat at 13.5p vs 13.4p FY25 H2 despite +20% AUA growth and +22% customer growth. This suggests significant investment spending in H2 or fee compression from competitive pricing.

TICKER 9: ALU

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as Q3 FY25/26 trading update (third quarter of the year ending 30 June 2026). Next year end = 30/6/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

ALU · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). RNS is a Q3 FY25/26 trading update (third quarter of year ending 30 June 2026 = October–December 2025 or January–March 2026). Per the RNS: "Q3 FY25/26" covers the period to end March 2026. Market expects full-year FY26 results (September 2026 per Cavendish note: "Next results FY Sept").
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 29.0p · Revenue £113.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 33.0p · Revenue £119.1m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over snapshot: −2.7% (29.8p → 29.0p). Net downgrade cycle from peak 30.9p (Sept 2025) down to 29.0p. Revenue: £110.5m → £113.6m (upgrade) but EPS fell. Disconnect: revenue upgraded but EPS cut. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 29.0p / £113.6m for 19 weeks since November 2025).

Consensus vintage check: The pre-RNS FY1 consensus of 29.0p was set during a downgrade cycle from 30.9p (Sept 2025) to 29.0p (Nov 2025). This was set BEFORE the Q3 FY26 trading update. The Cavendish broker note (April 16, same day as RNS) cuts FY26E adj EPS from 29.1p to 22.2p — a −23.8% cut. This is a major revision embedded in the broker note. Pre-RNS consensus of 29.0p does not yet reflect the Cavendish cut.

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.5% of FY = 49.5% × £113.6m = £56.2m · EPS 50.3% of FY = 50.3% × 29.0p = 14.6p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £57.4m · EPS 15.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc £113.6m − H1 actual £50.4m = implied H2 £63.2m vs FY25 H2 £56.1m → +12.7% YoY — 🟢 strong (pre-RNS). Post-RNS with Cavendish £109m guidance: implied H2 = £109m − £50.4m = £58.6m vs FY25 H2 £56.1m = +4.5% — 🟡 flat/moderate (RNS-derived).
  • FX: UK-based building products. Some international (Chek Lap Kok airport Hong Kong, Changi Airport Singapore). International revenues likely <20% of total. Phase 0B: no single non-GBP currency >30%. No FX penalty.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

ALU · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Q3 FY25/26 trading update — this is effectively a profit warning combined with strategic commentary).

  1. Revenue — Q3 FY25/26: Q3 revenues 2% ahead of prior year (Q3 FY24/25). Average monthly run-rate 8% ahead of H1 FY25/26. Year-to-date: H1 actual £50.4m. Implied Q3 revenue: average monthly run-rate 8% ahead of H1 average (£50.4m/6 months = £8.4m/month H1; +8% = ~£9.1m/month in Q3 = ~£27.2m Q3). YTD through Q3 ≈ £77.6m.

"Q3 FY25/26 revenues were 2% ahead of the prior year, with an average monthly run-rate 8% ahead of H1 FY25/26"

  1. FY26 profit warning — PBT guidance: "The Board is adopting a more cautious view of the Group's outlook for the remainder of the 2026 calendar year, and now expects FY25/26 underlying profit before tax to be approximately £11m." Pre-RNS Cavendish previous estimate: PBT £14.4m. Cut to £11.0m = −23.6%. Cavendish in the broker note (same day) cuts adj EPS from 29.1p → 22.2p (−23.8%).

"the Board is adopting a more cautious view of the Group's outlook for the remainder of the 2026 calendar year, and now expects FY25/26 underlying profit before tax to be approximately £11m"

  1. FY26e EPS bridge (using Cavendish revised figures as most current broker estimate):
  • New FY26 PBT guidance: £11.0m (explicit numeric guidance).
  • Tax: ~25% effective rate (standard UK) → PAT ~£8.3m / 36.0m shares = ~22.9p EPS — consistent with Cavendish 22.2p (slight difference in tax assumption).
  • FY27 (FY2) bridge: Cavendish maintains FY27E revenue +5% to £114.4m (on lower FY26 base of £109m). PBT £13.0m → EPS 26.2p vs Sharescope pre-RNS FY2 consensus 33.0p — a ~20% implied FY27 cut also needed.
  1. Order book / visibility: Order book at end of March 2026: 28% higher than March 2025 (+8% vs December 2025). Strong order intake validates structural demand. MACE GB Energy schools not relevant here. Chek Lap Kok airport: £1.3m remaining orders, may not ship until FY26/27. Changi Airport Singapore: first phase deliveries NOT expected this financial year.

"The order book at the end of March 2026 was 28% higher than March 2025, and 8% higher than December 2025."

  1. Margin / profitability: PBT cut from £14.4m → ~£11.0m on revenue cut from £113.4m → £109m = −£4.4m revenue → −£3.4m PBT. Margin compresses from ~12.7% to ~10.1% — confirming high operational leverage (every £1m revenue loss = ~77p PBT drop = ~17p drop-through vs 27p max). The Board notes "self-help initiatives" in Water Management division but no quantum provided. Building Envelope and Housebuilding Products performing well.
  2. Capital: Balance sheet "strong" — net bank debt leverage ratio expected approximately 0.4x at year end. £25.0m RCF + £4.0m overdraft available. Dividend: FY1fc DPS 11.40p (Sharescope) — Cavendish models £3.8m dividend (flat YoY). FCF forecast: Cavendish £5.3m FY26 (down from £10.9m). Working capital outflow £3.5m from inventory buffer build.
  3. Qualitative tone: CEO Pamela Bingham (new appointment): "Market conditions have undoubtedly become more challenging since we published our Interim Results on 3 February, with increasing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty weighing on decision-making and project timelines... the Board is rightly taking a cautious view." "I see significant scope to drive performance through self-help initiatives, especially in our Water Management division."

EPS quality check: £11m PBT is an explicit guidance figure. No tax distortion. No exceptional one-offs. This is a clean profit warning. The "approximately £11m" language = floor, not midpoint.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

Explicit PBT guidance of ~£11m (cut from ~£14.4m) + cautious language + identified market deterioration.

Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — quantified downside (−£3.4m PBT), explicit guidance cut. Cautious macro language. Water Management self-help unquantified. "Approximately £11m" = floor-type language. Provisional points: −13.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY1 fc EPS 29.0p (pre-RNS) vs FY25 actual 29.2p → 🚨 FY1 fc EPS approximately flat/slight decline vs prior year (−0.7%). Post-RNS Cavendish cuts to 22.2p → 🚨 FY1 fc EPS −24.0% below prior year actual. Revenue: pre-RNS £113.6m vs FY25 £113.4m ≈ flat; post-Cavendish £109.0m → 🚨 −3.9% below prior year.

Step 2: FY2 fc EPS 33.0p (pre-RNS Sharescope) vs FY1 fc 29.0p → was growing; Cavendish now 26.2p → 🚨 FY2 fc EPS −5.3% below post-RNS FY1 estimate of 22.2p (using Cavendish FY26 as the revised FY1). Actually Cavendish FY27 26.2p > Cavendish FY26 22.2p — so growing on revised basis. But vs Sharescope FY2 fc 33.0p: 🚨 FY2 consensus will need to cut from 33.0p → ~26p (−21%).

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

ALU · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

#1 and #2 Drivers:

#1 FY26 PBT profit warning to ~£11.0m — Cavendish cuts adj EPS from 29.1p to 22.2p (−23.8%). This is the primary revision driver. The Cavendish broker note already reflects the damage — reducing FY26E, FY27E and TP from 442p to 363p. Other brokers will follow suit. The consensus of 29.0p pre-RNS becomes ~22p post-cut.

#2 FY27 EPS must also be cut — from Sharescope FY2 consensus 33.0p to approximately 26.2p (−20%). The lower FY26 base reduces the FY27 starting point; delays in Water Management (self-help benefits "from FY26/27 onwards") push the recovery timeline back. Brokers who still have 33p+ for FY27 face a ~7pp cut.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 (FY1) EPS: cut from 29.0p → approximately 22–23p (−21–24%). Cavendish already at 22.2p.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Approximately £11m" for PBT is management's best estimate given current visibility. The order book (+28% YoY) provides medium-term structural support — this is NOT a structural demand failure. However, macro timing uncertainty means "approximately" could slide further. The Middle East crisis impact on project decision-making is ongoing and not predictably resolvable.

Key risk: Further project delays in Water Management — the unquantified self-help is the key uncertainty. If Changi Airport (first phase deliveries now delayed beyond FY26) and Chek Lap Kok (£1.3m risk of slipping to FY27) both disappoint in Q4, the £11m PBT floor could be tested. CEO Pamela Bingham is new (recent appointment) — transition risk in executing the self-help programme.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is a quantified profit warning: ALU now expects FY25/26 underlying PBT of approximately £11.0m — down from Cavendish's prior estimate of £14.4m (−23.6%). This translates to adj EPS of approximately 22–23p vs the pre-RNS consensus of 29.0p (−21–24%). The primary driver is the Water Management division, where revenues were below expectations due to continued project delays exacerbated by macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty stemming from the Middle East conflict. The timing-specific nature of the miss is confirmed by the order book, which grew 28% YoY and 8% HoH to end-March 2026 — structural demand is clearly intact. However, order book growth is irrelevant to current-year earnings if projects are not physically commencing. The Building Envelope and Housebuilding Products divisions both delivered growth in challenging markets, partially offsetting the Water Management shortfall.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 signal is the operative metric. FY26 guidance of ~£109m − H1 actual £50.4m = implied H2 of £58.6m (+4.6% YoY vs FY25 H2 £56.0m) — 🟡 flat/moderate and a meaningful deceleration from the H2-driven growth of prior years. The H2 EPS implied is approximately 14.1p (vs FY25 H2 13.7p, +2.9%) — essentially flat. The upgrade resilience is limited: Changi Airport (first-phase deliveries not commencing this year) and Chek Lap Kok (£1.3m at risk of FY26/27 slippage) represent identified downside risks to even the revised £11m PBT guidance. The self-help programme in Water Management — under new CEO Pamela Bingham — is unquantified and described as delivering benefits "from FY26/27 onwards," providing no in-year earnings support. H1 EPS of 8.1p represented only 27.9% of FY1 consensus — a −22.4pp deviation below seasonal baseline, the most severe H1 underperformance in recent history.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Cavendish (nominated adviser and joint broker) has already cut: FY26E adj EPS from 29.1p → 22.2p (−23.8%) and FY27E from 32.8p → 26.2p (−20.1%), reducing TP from 442p → 363p. Other brokers (Peel Hunt — joint broker) will follow with comparable cuts, pushing the full consensus FY26 EPS to ~22–23p and FY27 to ~26–27p. The pre-RNS Sharescope FY2 consensus of 33.0p will need to be cut by approximately −18–21%. TP consensus will likely fall from 426p to the 350–375p range. Current price of 260p represents 35–44% upside to the revised TP range — this is structural discount rather than re-rating opportunity. The watch point is the Water Management self-help programme: Pamela Bingham's "significant opportunities" in efficiency and productivity need to be quantified at FY26 results (September 2026) to establish credibility for the FY27 recovery. Until then, ALU is a value trap risk at 260p — the structural thesis (housing shortage, infrastructure backlogs) remains intact but the near-term earnings delivery is impaired.

🏁 Profit warning confirmed — FY26 EPS heading to ~22p (−24% vs pre-RNS consensus); FY27 also needs a −20% reset; double downgrade cycle; structural order book growth (+28% YoY) prevents deeper cuts but recovery timeline pushed to FY27/FY28; cautious/downgrades verdict.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

AMCO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue figures FY25 actual revenue: £70.9m vs FY25e consensus £70.9m → exactly in line (0.0% beat/miss). Sharescope FY1 fc had already been revised to £70.9m in March 2026 — consensus was pre-aligned to the actual.

"Revenue increased by 22% to £70.9 million (2024: £58.1 million)"

YoY: +22.0% vs FY24 £58.1m. H1 FY25 = £31.8m (Sharescope current H1). H2 FY25 derived: £70.9m − £31.8m = £39.1m. H2 YoY: £39.1m vs FY24 H2 £30.8m = +27.0%.

2. EPS / earnings figures Basic EPS FY25: 4.20p (2024: 3.50p). Diluted EPS: 4.12p. Adjusted EPS: 5.42p (2024: 9.35p). Pre-RNS FY25e consensus EPS = 5.5p (adjusted basis per Sharescope). Adjusted EPS 5.42p = miss of −0.08p / −1.5% vs consensus 5.5p. Trivially below.

⚠️ EPS quality check: Basic EPS 4.20p vs adjusted EPS 5.42p implies adjustments of ~1.22p (exceptional items £0.4m, amortisation £0.4m, share-based payments £0.2m, etc.). The 2024 adjusted EPS of 9.35p is anomalous — the RNS explains: "Note the weighted average number of shares in issue during 2024 was considerably lower (refer to note 24)." FY24 basic EPS 3.5p / adjusted 9.35p: the adjusted EPS comparison is distorted by the significantly lower share count pre-IPO. This makes YoY adjusted EPS comparison misleading. Use basic EPS for YoY: FY25 4.2p vs FY24 3.5p = +20.0% YoY.

Effective tax rate: tax charge £1.14m on PBT £4.11m = 27.7% effective tax rate vs statutory 25%. Excess: +2.7pp — below the 3pp flag threshold. ✅ No EPS restatement required.

H2 EPS (basic): £4.20p − £2.40p (H1) = 1.80p H2. H2 YoY: 1.80p vs FY24 H2 0.8p = +125% YoY — large but partly distorted by the IPO cost drag in FY24 H2.

3. FY26e EPS bridge (for FY2 = FY26) (1) New base: FY25 basic EPS 4.2p (adjusted 5.42p — note adjusted basis likely used by brokers; use 5.42p as bridge base). (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: EMC acquired March 2025 (c.9 months in FY25), Electronix acquired July 2025 (c.5 months in FY25). Full year contribution in FY26: EMC adds ~3 months incremental; Electronix adds ~7 months incremental. Additionally, GridCore (National Compliance & Testing, Enerveo) conditional acquisition expected to complete May 2026 — partial FY26 contribution (~7 months). Combined annualisation uplift is moderate but not large individually. (3) Organic EBITDA growth: RNS guides FY26 "started well, in line with expectations." FY26e EBITDA consensus £9.8m vs FY25 £9.2m = +6.5% organic+inorganic growth implied. (4) Interest step-up delta: Net debt moved from ~−£10m net cash (FY24) to +£11.2m net debt (FY25) — a +£21m swing. Finance costs FY25 = £2.08m; finance income £0.096m; net £1.986m. With continuing acquisition-led drawdown, interest costs in FY26 likely stable to slightly rising. No >£50m drawdown in period; finance costs did not grow >15% YoY (FY24 finance cost £2.21m → FY25 £2.08m, slight decline). No mandatory step-up delta. Implied FY26e EPS (adjusted basis ~5.42p base + annualisation + organic): Sharescope FY2 fc EPS = 6.9p — implying +27.3% growth from FY25 adjusted 5.42p. This is a significant step-up driven by (a) full-year benefit of FY25 acquisitions, (b) GridCore partial contribution, (c) organic improvement. The bridge is broadly coherent. If GridCore (acquired for £1) provides meaningful profit, it could be incrementally accretive.

4. Order book / forward work No explicit order book figure. Drurys order book "extending well into 2027" (defence/aviation). IVS long-term contract at "UK's largest refinery" won Q4 2025. GridCore acquisition provides "established, UK wide specialist electrical test and compliance operation." Qualitative visibility signals.

"Drurys has seen a significant increase in earnings and margins winning several new long-term contracts in the defence aviation and surveillance sectors with a committed order book now extending well into 2027."

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Gross margin: 36.6% (FY24: 36.4%) — modest 20bps improvement. B2B gross margin improved to 33.3% (FY24: 30.8%) — material improvement. EE margin "slightly reduced to 39.5% (2024: 43.6%)" due to EMC project mix; expected to trend back up.
  • Adjusted EBITDA: £9.2m (+19.3% from £7.7m)
  • Operating profit: £6.1m (FY24: £3.9m, +56.4%)
  • PBT: £4.1m (FY24: £1.7m, +145%)
  • Admin expenses increased to £19.2m (FY24: £15.8m, +21.5%) — reflecting enlarged group and central investment
  • Finance costs: £2.08m (FY24: £2.21m) — slight reduction

"Within the B2B Division, gross margins increased to 33.3% (2024: 30.8%) and are expected to increase incrementally in FY26."

Forward-looking: B2B margins "expected to increase incrementally in FY26." EE margins "expected to trend up to prior levels." Both signals positive for FY26.

6. Capital returns / per-share items No dividend declared or planned. Net debt £11.2m at 31 Dec 2025 (including deferred/contingent consideration). Cash £8.6m. Shares issued: 72.0m approximately. Share-based payments £0.2m recognised. GridCore acquired for £1 (conditional, expected May 2026).

7. Qualitative tone FY26 "started well and is in line with expectations." Rail electrification recovery noted. Strong demand in defence, aerospace, power generation, energy. Middle East / supply chain risks monitored.

"Trading in FY26 has started well and is in line with expectations."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "Trading in FY26 has started well and is in line with expectations."

Additional colour: B2B margins "expected to increase incrementally in FY26"; EE margins "expected to trend up to prior levels"; increasing activity in rail electrification; "strong demand across defence and civilian aerospace, power generation and wider energy sectors."

  • Guidance nature: qualitative only — no numeric FY26 guidance given; directional positive language on margins and demand
  • Year coverage: FY26 (FY2)
  • Classification: 🟢 Constructive — "in line with expectations" plus multiple positive sector demand signals plus margin improvement trajectory. The combination of in-line trading confirmation, margin recovery narrative, and named end-market strength goes beyond standard "in line" language. Provisional points: +6 to +10

Divergence check: FY25 revenue and adjusted EPS were broadly in line with (adjusted EPS marginally below) consensus; basic EPS strong. Outlook Constructive with current year delivery in-line. No material divergence.

Acquisitions pipeline: Management explicitly pursuing further acquisitions including "discounted acquisition opportunities with specific operational challenges." This creates ongoing EPS bridge complexity and potential dilution/debt risk.

"This is likely to include certain discounted acquisition opportunities with specific operational challenges that we have the skills to resolve, in order to restore performance."

EE margin dilution (temporary): EMC project mix has compressed EE margin from 43.6% to 39.5%. If WJ Projects rail electrification and EMC project mix normalise in FY26, EE margin recovery could be a positive catalyst.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

AMCO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — Revenue: exactly in-line at £70.9m; strong +22% YoY: The top-line delivery at exactly the consensus figure removes any revenue-related uncertainty. More importantly, the split between EE (+44.7% to £37.2m) and B2B (+4.3% to £33.8m) reveals that EE is the growth engine — driven substantially by EMC and Electronix acquisitions. For a small-cap buy-improve-build model, validating the acquisition contribution is the primary confidence signal for brokers.

#2 Driver — Adjusted EPS 5.42p: marginal miss vs 5.5p consensus; FY26 constructive guidance: The −0.08p miss on adjusted EPS (−1.5%) is immaterial — within normal modelling variance. The more important data point is the trajectory into FY26: B2B margins explicitly guided to "increase incrementally," EE margins expected to "trend up to prior levels," and rail electrification recovery underway. These qualitative signals, combined with the full-year annualisation of FY25 acquisitions and GridCore in FY26, underpin the FY26e EPS step to 6.9p.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e Revenue: expected to hold or minor upgrade (+0 to +3%) — GridCore adds partial contribution from ~May 2026; EMC full year; Electronix full year. Most brokers will have modelled these. Small positive bias.
  • FY26e EPS (adjusted): expected hold at ~6.9p — in-line FY25 result, no EPS surprise; marginal miss on adjusted EPS may prompt 1 broker to trim slightly but not materially. Range: −2% to +3%.
  • FY27e: stable; GridCore full-year contribution may prompt modest upgrade (+2–5%) if its pre-acquisition earnings profile is disclosed in broker notes.
  • Target prices: small-cap, limited broker coverage; current consensus TP 143p equals current price 143p — stock is trading at consensus TP, implying the market has priced in current expectations. Post results, brokers may nudge TPs to 150–165p on FY26 confidence, but the upside case requires further acquisitions and organic delivery.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Trading in FY26 has started well and is in line with expectations" is standard language. It is not the "comfortable with current expectations" formulation that triggers a deliberate-caution read. The margin improvement language ("expected to increase," "expected to trend up") provides mild incremental confidence. Moderate positive read-through; not an explicit upgrade catalyst.

Key risk: Leverage is the most prominent constraint. Interest cover FY26fc at 3.3x means that any operational slippage — a delayed contract, integration friction, or GridCore underperformance — flows non-linearly to EPS. The £11.2m net debt position (including deferred/contingent consideration) at a company generating ~£6.6m operating cash is not alarming but limits further acquisition headroom without a refinancing or additional facility. This is the constraint brokers will flag.

"We remain confident in managing this position prudently, supported by strong cash flow control and disciplined financial management... The Group is actively assessing options, including acquisitions, to optimise its capital structure, and is exploring potential refinancing or additional facilities to support strategic growth."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = hold (trivial miss, no material change). Tone = 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — driven by positive FY26 language and margin improvement signals. Minor tension: hold on FY26e EPS numbers but constructive on direction. Resolve: constructive tone is appropriate given FY26 pipeline quality, and the EPS revision is hold not cut.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — particularly for FY27e as full-year acquisition annualisation is modelled.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: AMCO delivered FY25 revenue of £70.9m — exactly at the pre-RNS consensus of £70.9m and +22% YoY — with adjusted EBITDA of £9.2m (+19.3%) and PBT of £4.1m (+145%). PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: AGM Statement (pre-H1 mode trading update).

  1. Revenue/profit performance — RNS states current trading is "ahead of prior year and in line with full year analyst consensus expectations." No specific H1 revenue or EPS figure disclosed — qualitative only. Footnote confirms FY26 Revenue £50.3m, Adj EBITDA £10.3m, net cash £16.9m — matching Sharescope FY1 fc exactly.
The Group has made a good start to the year with revenue and profit performance ahead of prior year and in line with full year analyst consensus expectations, despite well-reported geopolitical and related economic conditions.
  1. Regional growth drivers — Middle East strong trading including first sales of new product AmpLIPhy; US growth across Bio-Vet and Anpario ranges; Australasia growth.
We are particularly encouraged by a strong trading performance in the Middle-East, including the first sales of our new product, AmpLIPhy.
  1. Cost pressures and mitigation — Logistics cost increases now largely passed through. Raw material inflation in acid-based eubiotic range (~20% of sales), addressed via targeted price rises. Gross margin in H1 26 consistent with H2 25 — flat sequentially, not expanding.
These actions are mitigating the external cost pressures, with gross margins in the first half of the year consistent with the second half of 2025.
  1. Capital returns — Buyback programme: £2.0m expended of £3.0m total authorisation, 365,982 shares repurchased to date. Dividend (bi-annual) totalled £2.1m in the last year. Cash balance £10.9m at 31 May 2026 vs £12.4m at 31 Dec 2025.
As at today's date, a total of £2.0m has been expended under the £3.0m buyback programme, with 365,982 shares repurchased.
  1. ESG recognition — ESG Company of the Year award. No financial impact.
  1. Qualitative tone — No explicit numeric H1 guidance beyond "in line with" consensus. Directionally positive overall.

EPS quality check: No effective tax rate or one-off items disclosed in this AGM statement — no headline EPS or PBT figure given at all, so not applicable this round.

Outlook & Guidance Classification: "in line with full year analyst consensus expectations" — qualitative confirmation of existing numeric consensus. Classification: In-line — explicit "in line with market expectations" language, no upgrade or downgrade signal. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

Divergence check: No divergence — current trading described as "ahead of prior year," and outlook commentary is reinforcing, not contradicting.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING
  1. Half-on-Half (HoH) growth pattern

Revenue trajectory: Accelerating — H2 FY24 -5.4%, H1 FY25 +11.1%, H2 FY25 +35.0% — clear acceleration into H2 FY25.

EPS baseline: 3yr avg H1% (44.5%) x FY1 consensus 41.9p = 18.6p

  1. Implied H2 momentum — No updated FY figure in RNS beyond reaffirmed consensus. Per routing-gated scoring rule: mode = pre-H1, so Phase 3.3 does not contribute a scored row to Phase 5.

Profit warning feasibility gate: Not applicable — no negative H1 deviation (H1 is untrackable, not negative). Gate does not fire.

  1. Buyback as capital allocation signal: Active £3.0m buyback (67% executed) running alongside the existing bi-annual dividend signals management confidence and reduces future share count.

During the period, the Group commenced a share buyback programme, reflecting its strong balance sheet and cash generation, with the Board taking the opportunity to repurchase shares at attractive levels, reflecting its confidence in the Company's future prospects.

New product launch (AmpLIPhy): First sales in Middle East — early-stage, no quantum disclosed, but flagged as potential incremental growth driver not yet in models.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 and #2 Drivers — #1: The qualitative confirmation that trading is "ahead of prior year and in line with...consensus," the only forward-looking signal directly addressing whether the strong FY25 acceleration is being sustained into FY26. #2: The active share buyback (£2.0m of £3.0m spent), a smaller but real EPS-accretive lever via reduced share count.

Forecast revisions — FY1: Revenue and EPS expected to hold (0% change) — the AGM language reaffirms rather than raises consensus. FY2: similarly expected to hold, though the buyback may prompt a very modest (+0-1%) EPS tweak from some brokers.

Target price and recommendation — Brokers likely to hold consensus TP unchanged (598p) given no new operational information beyond reaffirmation. Current price (520p) sits at a 15% discount to consensus TP.

Conservative guidance read-through — "in line with...consensus" is a straightforward reaffirmation rather than typically conservative phrasing. It does not, by itself, increase the probability of an upgrade cycle.

Key risk — The absence of any new H1 revenue or EPS figure leaves genuine uncertainty about the magnitude of the "ahead of prior year" claim, and gross margin commentary suggests cost pass-through is offsetting inflation rather than driving margin gains.

These actions are mitigating the external cost pressures, with gross margins in the first half of the year consistent with the second half of 2025.

Consistency check — Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold. Tone label consistent: Neutral.

Overall tone — Neutral / hold and wait

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Today's AGM statement contains no numeric H1 figures, only qualitative confirmation that revenue and profit are ahead of prior year and in line with full year analyst consensus expectations of £50.3m revenue and £10.3m Adj EBITDA. This matters because it confirms the FY25 acceleration is being sustained, not reversed — FY25 itself showed EPS growing +92.7% YoY in H2 and revenue +35.0% YoY in H2, off the back of a weaker FY24. The single definitive catalyst here is reaffirmation, not a beat: brokers already have £50.3m/£10.3m baked into FY26 consensus, and this statement simply removes the risk that trading had slipped since the FY25 results.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: With no H1 26 actuals disclosed, both Revenue and EPS H1 tracking are UNTRACKABLE this round — the seasonal baseline (Revenue £24.1m, EPS 18.6p) and buy-trigger thresholds (£24.5m / 18.9p) are now set for confirmation when H1 results land on 9 September 2026. The upgrade case holds even in a cautious read because the qualitative confirmation explicitly states performance is ahead of prior year, not merely in line with it — prior year (FY25) was itself a year of strong H2 acceleration, so "ahead of" a strong comparator is a meaningfully higher bar being cleared than "ahead of" a weak one. The structural buyback (67% of £3.0m programme executed) adds a small but real EPS tailwind independent of the operating business, while the flat-margin commentary caps near-term upside from margin expansion.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Broker FY1 (FY26) and FY2 (FY27) EPS and revenue are both expected to hold (0% change) on this statement — there is nothing here to justify even modest upgrades absent a numeric beat — though some brokers may apply a very small (+0–1%) EPS tweak purely for the buyback's mechanical share-count reduction. Consensus TP (598p) is likely to remain unchanged for now, leaving the current 15% discount (520p) as a pre-existing valuation gap rather than a fresh signal. The main watch point is the complete absence of a numeric H1 figure — the statement leans entirely on qualitative reassurance, and the real test of whether FY26 will deliver another acceleration year arrives at the 9 September 2026 H1 results, against the buy triggers of £24.5m revenue and 18.9p EPS.

🏁 HOLD/NEUTRAL — reaffirming statement only, no numeric H1 disclosure; FY26/FY27 consensus likely unchanged; key catalyst is H1 results on 9 Sept 2026 against buy triggers of £24.5m revenue / 18.9p EPS.

PHASE 2 — AO.

AO. · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update — full year to 31 March 2026.

1. Revenue

Total group revenue growth expected to be c.11%. B2C growth c.9.5%.

FY1 consensus: £1,257.8m. Prior-year FY25 actual: £1,137.6m. Implied FY26 actual: £1,137.6m × 1.11 = £1,262.7m. Beat vs consensus: +£4.9m / +0.4% — essentially in line, marginally ahead.

"Total Group revenue growth expected to be c. 11%."

2. EPS / Earnings

Adjusted PBT "at the top end of £45–£50m". Midpoint guidance top-end = £50m. Prior FY1 fc consensus PBT: £49.8m. RNS confirms at top end → beat vs consensus PBT of approximately +0.4% (£50m vs £49.8m).

RNS states "c.15% year-on-year adjusted PBT growth". Prior year H1+H2 PBT: £17.1m + £11.6m = £28.7m. 15% growth → ~£33.0m. Wait — FY25 actual Sharescope: H1 £17.1m + H2 £11.6m = £28.7m. 15% on £28.7m = £33.0m. That contradicts "top end of £45–£50m". Reconciliation: the c.15% must reference a different base. FY25 PBT was £28.7m per Sharescope but consensus FY1 fc was £49.8m — implying prior-year actual reported elsewhere. The FY25 annual report data in the IPX block doesn't apply. Resolution: FY25 adjusted PBT not directly stated for AO in data block. The guidance "c.15% YoY growth" and "top end of £45-£50m" imply prior year adjusted PBT ~£43.5m (£50m ÷ 1.15). Sharescope's H1+H2 PBT sum of £28.7m likely reflects IFRS PBT, not adjusted. Taking the RNS guidance at face value: adjusted PBT ~£50m at top end vs FY1 fc consensus £49.8m → marginal beat, effectively in line at top end of guided range.

"Adjusted profit before tax is expected to be in line with previously upgraded guidance; at the top end of £45-£50m. Demonstrating again that profits are growing quicker than sales, in the region of c15% year-on-year adjusted PBT growth."

FY26e EPS bridge (for FY27e):

  • New base: FY26 adj PBT ~£50m. Tax at ~25% = £37.5m PAT. Diluted shares 555.6m → implied FY26 adj EPS ~6.75p. (Note: FY1 fc consensus 6.3p — the bridge will reference this base.)
  • (1) New base EPS: ~6.75p (RNS-derived, slightly above consensus 6.3p given top-end PBT guidance)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: No acquisitions disclosed — nil
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY2 fc EBITDA £86.3m vs FY1 fc £79.3m = +8.8% organic growth. Applying to ~£50m PBT → ~£54.4m PBT. Tax 25% → £40.8m → ~7.34p EPS
  • (4) Interest step-up delta: Net debt virtually nil (FY1fc £4.3m, ND/EBITDA 0.05x); finance costs immaterial. No drawdown >£50m, no >15% finance cost growth. Mandatory row does not fire.
  • Implied FY27e EPS: ~7.3p. vs FY2 fc consensus 7.1p → +3% vs stale consensus. Bridge suggests consensus marginally stale to the upside given top-end FY26 delivery.

3. Order book / forward work

Not applicable (retailer). Membership model and "shared economics strategy" referenced. "Exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead."

4. Margin / profitability

Adjusted PBT growing faster than sales ("profits are growing quicker than sales"). Hedging in place: ~80% of forecast fuel usage and 100% of electricity usage for full FY27 trading period — explicit forward cost protection.

"The Group had hedging arrangements in place in advance of recent geopolitical developments, covering approximately 80% of forecast fuel usage and 100% of electricity usage which cover the full FY27 trading period."

5. Capital returns / per-share / cash

Free cash flow c.£65m FY26 (FY25: £23m) — +£42m YoY, +183%. Liquidity c.£200m at period end.

"At the period end we expect to have c. £200m of liquidity. Profit is converting to cash, with free cash flow of c.£65m (FY25 £23m) for FY26."

No dividend. No buyback disclosed.

6. Qualitative tone

CEO language strongly positive. "The numbers speak for themselves again." Trust milestone (1 million Trustpilot reviews at 4.9 rating). "All key metrics continue to improve, with an exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead."

EPS quality check: No exceptional items in FY26 per RNS ("There are no adjusting items in FY26"). FY25 had Music Magpie acquisition costs (£3.3m) and mobile goodwill impairment (£19.5m) — both excluded from adjusted. No tax distortion flagged. Headline adjusted PBT figure is clean. ✅ No restatement required.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements for FY27:

  • Hedging covering 80% fuel + 100% electricity for full FY27 period — explicit cost protection against geopolitical headwinds
  • "Exciting pipeline of new initiatives ahead"
  • "All key metrics continue to improve"
  • No numeric FY27 EPS or revenue guidance given
  • Management tone is bullish qualitative with specific cost hedge detail

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — confident qualitative language with concrete FY27 cost hedge, visible earnings driver (FCF step-up), ongoing market share gains. Not "upgrade-triggering" as no "ahead of" language for FY27 specifically, and no numeric uplift stated.

Guidance: qualitative only · covers one year ahead implicitly (FY27) · provisional points: +7 to +9

Divergence check: Current year delivery strong (PBT top end, FCF +183%). Outlook constructive. No divergence — both directionally positive. No flag required.

#1 Driver — FCF and liquidity step-change: The single most broker-moving element is FCF of ~£65m vs £23m in FY25, with liquidity reaching £200m. This is the clearest evidence that the profitability improvement is real and converting to cash. Brokers with buy ratings will use this to validate their models and likely nudge FY26/FY27 estimates upward. The FCF figure also signals potential for capital returns (dividend initiation or buyback) — a catalyst that has been absent from the investment case.

#2 Driver — PBT at top end of upgraded guidance range: Adj PBT "at the top end of £45–£50m" vs FY1 fc consensus £49.8m. Technically in line at top end, but combined with the pre-existing upgrade cycle (+16.7% EPS revision over the snapshot), this confirms the upgrade cycle is intact. Forecast revisions:

Target price & recommendation: Brokers likely to hold or marginally raise target prices. Current consensus TP 153p vs close 86.5p implies 77% upside — an unusually wide gap. Conservative guidance read-through: "At the top end of £45–£50m" is precisely the type of language brokers read as confirmation without hyperbole. Combined with "not less than" being absent, this is classic deliberate bottom-of-range anchoring — the actual outturn is likely £50m or just above. Increases probability of a modest upgrade cycle on results day (17 June 2026).

Key risk: The current share price (86.5p vs 153p TP) suggests the market is pricing in something more negative than the trading update implies — likely macro/tariff risk to consumer durables demand in FY27. "The Group had hedging arrangements in place in advance of recent geopolitical developments" — this sentence acknowledges the macro backdrop but mitigates one dimension of it. The residual risk is volume: if consumer confidence deteriorates in FY27 (tariff recession scenario), revenue growth could disappoint even with cost protection.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: AO's FY26 trading update lands clean: total revenue growth c.11%, implying ~£1,263m vs consensus £1,257.8m — a marginal beat. The headline is the adjusted PBT figure: "at the top end of £45–£50m", confirming ~£50m vs FY1 fc consensus £49.8m. But the #1 catalyst is the free cash flow of c.£65m — up from £23m in FY25, a +183% step-up — with liquidity of £200m. This is the number brokers will lead on: profits are not only growing but are now visibly converting to cash at scale. The prior upgrade cycle (+16.7% EPS consensus move since May 25) is confirmed, not threatened.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode the key signal is implied H2 momentum. RNS-derived: implied H2 revenue ~£677m vs prior-year H2 £625.5m = +8.3% (moderate); implied H2 EPS ~4.65p vs 3.7p = +25.7% (strong). The EPS H1 tracking deviation was 🟢🟢 +6.8pp — materially ahead of seasonal norms — confirming H1 was the strong half and H2 consensus burden at 4.2–4.65p is achievable. The bull case is protected by explicit FY27 hedging (80% fuel + 100% electricity for the full year), which neutralises the single largest bear concern in the current macro environment. Even in a volume-softer FY27, cost certainty should allow margins to hold. The H2 EPS burden at ~4.2p (consensus) is above historical H2 avg of 3.2p but entirely consistent with the c.15% PBT growth trajectory the company is executing.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Expect FY26 EPS to be revised modestly upward to ~6.5–6.7p (+3–6%), with FY27 seeing a similar +2–4% upgrade on the back of confirmed FCF and hedge protection. Target prices likely to hold or creep higher (consensus already 153p vs 86.5p share price — an 77% implied upside gap that brokers will emphasise). The main constraint on the score is the absence of explicit numeric FY27 guidance and the stalling EPS upgrade trend — the trigger for a new upgrade leg will be the 17 June FY26 results where the full actuals, dividend/buyback news and FY27 guidance will land. The current update is a confirmatory setup, not the final catalyst. 🏁 Verdict: clean confirmatory update with FCF as the standout; modest upgrade cycle intact and likely to accelerate on 17 June results. Score 69 reflects the confirmatory rather than breakthrough nature of this RNS — watch 17 June.

Material calibration point — FCF and working capital: ED explicitly flags that FCF of £64.6m "benefitted from a c.£20m working capital inflow, some of which may reverse in FY27E." This is a genuine constraint on the FY27 upgrade story that I did not sufficiently weight. It means the "structural FCF improvement" narrative is partially inflated by a one-off working capital timing benefit — sustainable FCF may be closer to £40–45m rather than £65m. My Phase 2 bridge and Phase 4 FY27 upgrade case was too bullish on FCF sustainability. The FY27 EPS upgrade probability is lower than my +2–4% suggested; ED's revision is essentially flat (+0.2% change on EPS, 0.2% on PBT for FY27).

EPS baseline calibration: ED uses adj diluted EPS 6.1p FY26E (diluted shares 582.1m). The Sharescope consensus shows 6.3p — ED is 3.3% below consensus. This is a mild discrepancy; ED is likely at the lower end of the range. My bridge of 6.75p was too aggressive — the working capital note explains part of this. The actual adj EPS on FY26 results will likely land at 6.0–6.2p range, not the 6.75p I implied from a clean PBT/tax/shares calculation. The difference is partly diluted share count (ED uses 582.1m vs my 555.6m from Sharescope shares in issue — the gap reflects treasury/EBT shares in the fully diluted count).

FY25 adj PBT baseline confirmed: ED shows FY25A adj PBT of £43.5m — this is the correct prior-year base for the c.15% growth claim. Validates: £43.5m × 1.15 = £50.0m. My Phase 2 reconciliation was correct; the Sharescope H1+H2 PBT figures of £28.7m were IFRS PBT not adjusted.

Fair value: ED 170p vs consensus TP 153p. Stock at 89p (ED's close) = 91% upside to FV. Validates the valuation gap observation in my Phase 4.

Score calibration for AO.: My score of 69 holds. The working capital flag is a genuine FY27 constraint I underweighted but it doesn't change the FY26 picture (confirmation in line, constructive). The FY27 EPS upgrade will be smaller than I implied — nearer flat-to-marginal. The FCF one-off partially deflates the "structural" argument. Had I known this, I might have trimmed the FCF component from +14 to +11 and the outlook from +8 to +6, landing at ~66. The 69 is marginally generous but within the confidence range of 63–75. Score defensible; FCF sustainability is the main calibration learning.

APN — PHASE 0

Phase 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (six months ended 31 January 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

International revenue £34.2m = 46% of H1 total, but spread across Middle East, LATAM, Europe, US — no single non-GBP currency identifiably exceeds 30% of revenues. The RNS Risk section flags USD on purchases, not revenues. Phase 0B: skip, no penalty.

APN — PHASE 1

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 FY26 results (H1 ended 31 Jan 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 11.4p · Revenue £140.3m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 12.6p · Revenue £155.2m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net +34.1% over full snapshot period (8.5p → 11.4p). Three distinct upgrade steps: Aug 25 (+7%), Nov 25 (+12%), Feb 26 (+6%). Multiple upgrades, zero downgrades. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 11.4p/291p since 21 Feb 26). Revenue net change +40.2% (£100.1m → £140.3m).
  • H1 baselines (1yr avg — limited IPO history): Revenue 52.7% × £140.3m = £73.9m · EPS: n/a per Sharescope (single year of adj split available: H1 FY25 4.2p / FY25 adj 9.1p = 46.2%; using this as proxy = 46.2% × 11.4p = 5.3p)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £47.6m · EPS (adj) 4.2p; statutory 3.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: £140.3m − £74.5m = £65.8m implied H2 vs prior H2 £59.5m = +10.6% YoY. EPS: 11.4p − 6.2p = 5.2p implied H2 vs prior H2 4.9p = +6.1% YoY
  • FX: N/A

APN — PHASE 2

RNS type: H1 Results — six months ended 31 January 2026

  1. Revenue: H1 FY26 £74.5m, +56.5% YoY (H1 FY25: £47.6m). FY guidance maintained at ~£140m. Revenue beat vs seasonal baseline of £73.9m = +£0.6m / +0.8pp above norm. "H1 FY26 revenue up 57% to £74.5 million (H1 FY25: £47.6 million)"
  2. EPS / Earnings: Adjusted basic EPS 6.2p (+47.6% vs H1 FY25: 4.2p). Statutory EPS 6.2p (+77.1% vs H1 FY25: 3.5p). Adjusted PBT £20.9m (+53.7%). vs FY1 H1 proxy baseline of 5.3p = +0.9p / +17% beat vs implied seasonal norm. Implied H2 EPS burden = 11.4p − 6.2p = 5.2p (vs prior H2 4.9p — burden moderately higher but manageable given FY guidance held). "Adjusted basic and diluted EPS...6.2p...H1 FY25: 4.2p...47.6%"
  3. Order book / forward work: No explicit order book figure. FY guidance of ~£140m confirmed and unchanged post period-end. Company notes H1-weighted profile explicitly flagged — management anticipate H2 lower than H1 due to elevated retailer stock levels and H1 product launch pull-forward. "due to a better than expected peak trading period and accelerated demand for a number of H1 FY26 product launches, this is expected to result in a more H1‑weighted revenue profile than in prior years"
  4. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 46.7% (H1 FY25: 46.8%) — virtually flat, down only 10bps despite revenue +57%. Adjusted EBITDA margin 28.9% (H1 FY25: 29.0%). Admin expenses 18.9% of revenue (held flat despite listed-company cost step-up). Whey protein headwind absorbed. "total gross margin was stable moving down 10bps to 46.7% (H1 FY25: 46.8%)"
  5. Capital / cash / per-share: Net cash £26.4m (H1 FY25: £10.9m). No dividend declared or anticipated before FY27. Capex H1 £0.2m; major capex (£2.0–2.5m manufacturing; £3.5–4.0m distribution facility) falls H2 FY26 / FY27. Construction commenced on global distribution facility post period-end; revenue capacity to increase to ~£300m. "Net cash4 at period end of £26.4m (H1 FY25: £10.9m)" "The Company does not anticipate declaring a further dividend before FY27"
  6. Qualitative tone: Explicitly H1-weighted revenue profile guided. H2 expected to see Middle East volume softness. Management confident FY £140m unchanged. New Morrisons out-licensing deal, Tesco ABE launch, Latin America +110%. Structural: manufacturing extension to ~£300m capacity underway — multi-year capacity headroom removes a key constraint. "Although we expect some reduction in volumes into the region during the second half, at this stage there is no change to FY26 guidance of full year revenue of approximately £140 million"

APN — PHASE 3

Full-Year YoY Growth Table

*FY26e = FY1 consensus

Revenue growth trajectory: Only two datapoints available. FY25 +70% → FY26e +31%. 🔴 Decelerating on headline rate, though absolute growth remains very strong and deceleration is base-effect driven.

EPS growth trajectory: FY25 +57% → FY26e +25%. 🔴 Decelerating — again base-effect driven. Underlying quality of earnings improving (margin held, cash strong).

1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

*H2 FY26 derived: FY1 consensus (£140.3m / 11.4p) minus H1 FY26 actuals

H2 derivation: Revenue £140.3m − £74.5m = £65.8m. EPS 11.4p − 6.2p = 5.2p.

Revenue trajectory: H1 FY25 → H2 FY25 → H1 FY26 YoY: n/a → n/a → +56.5%. Only one comparable YoY point available. Implied H2 FY26 +10.6%. 🟡 Volatile — H1 dominance flagged by management as structural shift for this year.

EPS trajectory: H1 +47.6%, implied H2 +6.1%. 🟡 Volatile — deliberately H1-weighted profile this year. Not a deterioration signal; management-guided.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • Revenue baseline: 52.7% (1yr avg) × £140.3m = £73.9m
  • EPS baseline (proxy): 46.2% (1yr proxy) × 11.4p = 5.3p
  • Revenue tracking: £74.5m ÷ £140.3m = 53.1% vs baseline 52.7% → deviation = 🟢 [+0.4pp]
  • EPS tracking: 6.2p ÷ 11.4p = 54.4% vs baseline 46.2% → deviation = 🟢 [+8.2pp]
  • H2 EPS burden: 11.4p − 6.2p = 5.2p vs historical H2 4.9p — burden HIGHER than prior H2 but management has explicitly guided FY £140m, so consensus already accommodates this
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [73.9m × 1.015] = £75.0m → actual £74.5m → 🔴 ✗ · H1 EPS > [5.3p × 1.015] = 5.4p → actual 6.2p → 🟢 ✓
  • Historical hit rate: Insufficient history (1 year of H1/H2 data) — cannot calculate

Revenue signal: +0.4pp deviation → 🟡 IN LINE (barely above seasonal norm; management has deliberately guided H1-heavy profile so this is almost exactly as anticipated)

EPS signal: +8.2pp deviation → 🟢 STRONG BUY — H1 EPS materially outperforming seasonal norm; H2 burden of 5.2p well below what the EPS beat implies consensus assumed

Important structural note: Management has explicitly flagged the H1-weighted revenue profile as a function of peak-season retailer stock-up and H1 product launch pull-forward. The EPS STRONG BUY signal is genuine — H1 adj EPS of 6.2p vs 5.3p baseline is a real beat — but the revenue IN LINE signal reflects management's own pre-signalling rather than underperformance.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode: compare implied H2 vs prior-year H2:

  • Revenue: implied H2 £65.8m vs prior H2 £59.5m = +10.6% → 🟢 moderate (0–10% band nearly breached; sits just above; classify moderate-to-strong)
  • EPS: implied H2 5.2p vs prior H2 4.9p = +6.1% → 🟡 moderate (+0–10%)

Despite the H1-weighting narrative, H2 is still expected to grow meaningfully YoY. This is consistent with FY guidance held.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: net change +34.1% over full period (8.5p → 11.4p). 3+ distinct upgrade rounds. Upgrades: multiple; downgrades: zero
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 11.4p/291p since 21 Feb 26 — results were today so upgrades not yet reflected)
  • Divergence: Price at 220.5p vs TP 291p = 32% upside to consensus TP pre-results. Strong upgrade cycle has outpaced price move. Broker momentum has been consistently ahead of price action — positive divergence favouring further re-rating on today's beat.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

H1-weighting shift: This year's revenue profile is explicitly more H1-weighted than prior years due to peak retailer stock-building and accelerated NPD demand. Brokers must model a lower H2 run-rate than H1 — this is not a negative flag, it is management-guided.

"due to a better than expected peak trading period and accelerated demand for a number of H1 FY26 product launches, this is expected to result in a more H1‑weighted revenue profile than in prior years"

Capacity expansion: New global distribution facility and manufacturing phase 3 targeting £300m revenue capacity — multi-year structural driver. Capex of £5.5–6.5m falling FY27, so no near-term EPS drag.

Middle East softness: Some H2 volume reduction expected in Middle East but no guidance change. Risk quantified and contained.

APN — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — H1 EPS beat vs expectation: The adjusted EPS of 6.2p vs the implied seasonal baseline of ~5.3p is an ~17% beat on the half. Brokers will lead with this in notes. The statutory EPS of 6.2p vs H1 FY25 statutory 3.5p (+77%) is eye-catching but adj-to-adj is what matters for revision models.

#2 Driver — FY guidance confirmation at £140m despite H1-weighting flag: The explicit maintenance of FY revenue guidance even while flagging Middle East softness and a more H1-heavy profile is the second key signal. Brokers will view this as deliberately conservative — the "no change to FY26 guidance" language after beating H1 is a classic de-risking statement that typically triggers modest upward pressure on H2 estimates.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: consensus already at £140.3m and management guided £140m — expect hold with slight tightening of range. Some brokers may nudge to £141–143m given the H1 beat.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 11.4p — with H1 adj at 6.2p implying H2 of 5.2p, most brokers will hold or nudge +2–5%. Expect FY1 EPS to move to 11.5–12.0p.
  • FY2 Revenue: expect +3–5% upgrades as capacity expansion and new channel wins (Morrisons out-licensing, Tesco launch, LATAM +110%) are factored into out-year models. FY2 to move towards £160–165m.
  • FY2 EPS: expect +5–8% upgrades on FY2 as operating leverage kicks in at higher revenue base. FY2 moves from 12.6p towards 13.0–13.5p.

Target price / recommendation: Consensus TP at 291p vs price 220.5p = 32% upside. Expect brokers to raise TPs to 300–325p range. No recommendation change warranted — stock already on buy ratings across the board. Upgrading to strong buy unlikely given the H1-weighting caveat and Middle East risk, but conviction on existing buys will increase.

Conservative guidance read-through: The maintenance of £140m guidance despite a materially better H1 and with Middle East headwinds acknowledged is classic under-promise language. The combination of "no change to guidance" + "some reduction in Middle East volumes" implies the underlying business ex-Middle East is running ahead of the full-year number. This increases the probability of an upgrade cycle into H2 results.

Key risk: H2 revenue shortfall from Middle East. International was 46% of H1 revenue (£34.2m), with Middle East a significant constituent alongside LATAM. If Middle East disruption is worse than anticipated, H2 revenue could undershoot the implied £65.8m. "we expect some reduction in volumes into the region during the second half" — the lack of quantification is a watch point.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

APN — PHASE 5

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

82/100 · Confidence: 76–87 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

🟢 H1 EPS beat vs seasonal baseline (+8.2pp, STRONG BUY signal)+22
🟢 Revenue +57% YoY, gross margin held at 46.7% (10bps dilution only)+18

🔴 Stock already re-rated +35% vs IPO — some beat priced in−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Applied Nutrition delivered a genuinely outstanding H1, with adjusted EPS of 6.2p against an implied seasonal baseline of ~5.3p — a +17% beat on the half and a +48% YoY improvement. Revenue of £74.5m grew +56.5% YoY, beating the seasonal norm of £73.9m by 0.6pp. The single definitive catalyst is the EPS STRONG BUY deviation of +8.2pp, which confirms that H1 earnings are materially outperforming the pattern implied by the FY consensus — even accounting for the company's own H1-weighting guidance. Gross margin of 46.7% is essentially flat YoY despite a £27m revenue uplift, which demonstrates genuine operating leverage and pricing power even as whey protein costs rose.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 tracking signal on EPS (+8.2pp) is the strongest signal in the scorecard. Implied H2 EPS of 5.2p represents only +6.1% YoY growth against prior H2 of 4.9p — a deliberately soft H2 embedded in FY consensus that management has explicitly guided via the H1-weighting narrative. The bear case is straightforward: Middle East volumes soften, H2 comes in at £60–62m revenue rather than the implied £65.8m. But FY guidance has been held at £140m precisely because management knew this when they confirmed it. The structural driver — new distribution facility targeting £300m revenue capacity, plus the Morrisons out-licensing, Tesco ABE, and LATAM +110% growth — ensures the FY27 upgrade story is firmly in place even if H2 FY26 is managed conservatively. The H2 burden of 5.2p is actually lower than it appears: the 4-week stalling in broker estimates means some brokers have already embedded a mildly conservative H2, so the actual revision gap is narrower than the +17% H1 EPS beat implies.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS is likely to move from 11.4p to 11.5–12.0p (range +1–5%), with FY1 revenue held near £140–143m. FY2 EPS revisions are more interesting: expect upgrades from 12.6p towards 13.0–13.5p (+3–7%) as new channel wins and operating leverage are modelled through. Consensus target price of 291p should move to 300–325p, representing 36–47% upside from the 220.5p close. The main watch-point is H2 Middle East quantification — if the company provides any colour at the full-year stage, that will determine whether FY2 gets a more aggressive upgrade. 🏁 APN is a clear hold-and-add on results: the H1 EPS beat is material, FY guidance is conservative, and the upgrade cycle has further to run into FY27 as capacity comes on stream.
