ASC — ASOS PLC

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

ASOS has global operations. Revenue is primarily in GBP, EUR, USD. UK: ~35% of GMV, Germany ~14%, France ~8%, US ~10%, Rest of World ~33%. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% definitively — EUR combined (France + Germany + other Europe) likely approaches 25–28%; USD ~10%. On a per-currency basis, EUR is likely close to 30% but ASOS does not disclose precise currency percentages in this RNS (it is a pre-close trading update). No formal Currency Movements section present. Cannot confirm >30% single currency exposure from RNS. Phase 0B not triggered strictly. However, note that tariff impacts (IEEPA) are explicitly mentioned as having a negative impact on EBITDA in the H1 period. No formal FX adjustment.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-H1 trading update (H1 ended 1 March 2026; results to be published imminently — RNS is a pre-close trading update ahead of H1 results). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS −39.3p · Revenue £2,389.8m (GMV basis, adjusted for FX/returns)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS −21.0p · Revenue £2,440.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: −54.3p → −39.3p = less negative by 15.0p (+27.6%) — EPS improving (losses narrowing). Revenue: £2,635m → £2,389.8m (−9.3%). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at −39.3p / £2,389.8m for 6 weeks). Note: EPS improving = positive direction (losses narrowing).
  • H1 baselines (pre-H1 mode, 3yr avg): Revenue 51.5% of FY = £1,230.8m · EPS n/a (negative EPS throughout — tracking signals on EPS not meaningful; H1 EPS comparison complex given restructuring)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £1,505.8m · EPS −204.3p (H1 loss — includes impairments/write-downs)
  • Current H1 actuals (from Sharescope): Revenue £1,299.4m · EPS −166.8p (H1 FY26, per Sharescope — but the RNS is a pre-close update, implying H1 period ended 1 March 2026 and full H1 results are imminent)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode): FY1 consensus £2,389.8m − H1 actual £1,299.4m = implied H2 £1,090.4m vs prior H2 £1,400.0m → −22.1% YoY (but prior H2 included higher revenue base pre-transformation). Current H1 EPS −166.8p + FY1 consensus −39.3p → implied H2 EPS: −39.3p − (−166.8p) = +127.5p — ASOS must deliver a strongly positive H2 to hit full-year consensus EPS. Note: H1 FY26 includes large working capital reversal benefits and one-off items; H2 EPS profile is critical.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Pre-close update ahead of H1 results for period ended 1 March 2026)

  • Divergence check: H1 delivery (EBITDA +50%, gross margin +330bps) vs guidance reiterated (not raised). FY26 EBITDA guidance of £150m–£180m was reiterated (not raised) — suggesting management is deliberately conservative and the probability of a guidance upgrade at the H1 results (imminent) is material.

Score 61/100.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode applies only to pre-FY; this is pre-H1)

H1 actual revenue = $125m. FY26e fc = $242.7m. Implied H2 = $242.7m − $125m = $117.7m Prior H2 averages: FY23 $58.0m, FY24 $85.1m, FY25 $88.1m → 3yr avg $77.1m

Classification (reported): $117.7m H2 vs $88.1m FY25 reported H2 → +$29.6m = +33.6% — entirely inorganic. Flag as consensus-derived, distorted by inorganic.

On a pro forma basis: $117.7m vs ~$125m pro forma H2 → slight decline → 🔴 weak (−5.9%) on pro forma — but this is partially explained by H2 revenue being more weighted to H1 per company guidance ("Revenue growth more weighted to the first half").

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: net +24.4% over full period — driven by Chairish consolidation step in Jun 25. Since then, oscillating in 38.4–39.7¢ range. No material organic upgrade momentum.
  • 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (38.3¢ → 38.7¢)
  • Divergence: Price down from £10.39 to 384p (−63%) over period despite EPS +24.4% — massive price/earnings divergence. The market has de-rated ATG significantly. EPS step-up was acquisition-driven; organic EPS flat to down. Market pricing in dilution and CEO risk.

  • CEO departure: John-Paul Savant stepping down after 10+ years. This is a significant leadership change at a company in the middle of an acquisition integration. Brokers will flag this as a near-term uncertainty.

  • Cost savings programme: "Additional modest cost savings programme... will benefit margins in FY27, with a small benefit in H2 26." 🏗️ Minor positive FY27 tailwind but not quantified — moderate signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

ATG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

#1 Driver — FY26 guidance confirmation in-line: H1 revenue at c.$125m confirms the existing consensus midpoint almost exactly ($125.2m seasonal baseline). Brokers will hold FY26 estimates flat. The "in-line" confirmation removes downside risk but provides no upside catalyst.

#2 Driver — CEO departure: John-Paul Savant's resignation is the single most disruptive element of this RNS. After 10+ years as CEO through acquisitions including Chairish, his departure introduces strategic and execution uncertainty. Brokers may add a discount to target prices or apply a higher risk premium, even if estimates remain unchanged.

  • FY1 Revenue (FY26e): Hold. $125m H1 in-line with consensus. No change.
  • FY1 EPS (FY26e): Hold. EBITDA in-line. No EPS revision expected. 38.7¢ unchanged.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with market expectations" — no upside surprise. Does not trigger upgrade cycle.

Key risk: CEO departure coming during first full year of Chairish integration. Transition risk is high. Combined with I&C revenue declining, a flat organic H1 (pro forma cc +8% ahead of 4–5% guidance but H1-weighted was expected), the upside is limited and the leadership change is a genuine near-term negative.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

ATG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The H1 FY26 trading update confirms revenue of approximately $125m, virtually in line with the seasonal baseline of $125.2m (3-year H1 average 51.6% × FY26e $242.7m). Pro forma constant currency growth of close to 8% comfortably exceeds the full-year guidance of 4–5%, providing confidence that first-half momentum is tracking above the full-year trend. However, the RNS simultaneously confirms that revenue weighting is H1-heavy by design, meaning the H2 run-rate will be relatively softer. Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H1 revenue in-line means implied H2 of ~$117.7m is set against a FY26e consensus of $242.7m. On a pro forma basis this represents a slight YoY decline vs the comparable H2 FY25 (~$125m pro forma), consistent with company guidance of H1-weighted growth. The EBITDA margin is expected to reflect Chairish dilution as previously communicated. No H1 EPS disclosed, so the deviation signal is revenue-only at −0.1pp — IN LINE. The deliberate cost savings programme provides a modest FY27 tailwind (+1–3% EPS potential) but is not quantified. The balance sheet is deleveraging ahead of schedule (1.8x by end of H1 vs 2.0x Dec 25) — a quiet positive.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e estimates are likely to be held across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS. Target prices are expected to be trimmed slightly to £4.80–5.00 (from £5.08 consensus) in response to the CEO departure, introducing a leadership risk premium even as financial delivery is on track. The CEO transition is the dominant narrative in broker notes — the financials are in-line but the execution risk during Chairish integration is elevated without a named successor. FY26 remains a transition year with organic EPS virtually flat.

🏁 ATG delivers an in-line H1 but the CEO departure headline overshadows confirmation of guidance, making this a hold rather than an upgrade catalyst. Score: 46/100.

TICKER 2: AVG

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 FY26 results. Next year end = 31/5/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

AVG · Q2 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/5/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = H1 FY26 results (six months ended 30 November 2025). Market now awaits full-year FY26 results.
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 30.4p · Revenue £175.0m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 37.4p · Revenue £193.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over snapshot: +105.4% (14.8p → 30.4p). Major upgrade event in late September 2025 (18.9p → 30.4p = +61% jump, coinciding with FY25 full year results publication around that time). Held flat at 30.4p since. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat for 6+ months). Revenue: upgraded from £161m → £175m at same point, held flat. No further revisions since late Sept 2025.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.1% of FY = 47.1% × £175.0m = £82.4m · EPS 53.3% of FY = 53.3% × 30.4p = 16.2p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £79.0m · EPS 12.0p (adj diluted per Sharescope; RNS confirms 12.0p adj diluted)
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc £175.0m − H1 actual £78.1m = implied H2 £96.9m vs FY25 H2 £77.4m → +25.2% YoY — 🟢 strong.
  • FX: USD exposure via Energy Steel (Michigan, USA) and HT Inc (Vermont, USA). Revenues in USD — need to assess. Energy Steel and HT Inc are material US operations. Will assess in Phase 0B.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): 3y ago £5.4m / 2y ago £4.0m / FY25 H2 £2.1m / current H1 £16.9m → FY1fc £18.0m → FY2fc £13.8m · ND/EBITDA: current 1.10x / FY1fc 0.90x / FY2fc 0.60x · Interest cover FY1fc: 10.1x / FY2fc: 11.0x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — net debt below 1x EBITDA, interest cover 10x+, no constraint.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

The RNS does not contain a "Currency Movements" section with explicit FX rate disclosures. US revenues (HT Inc, Energy Steel) are material — the AES division generated H1 FY26 revenue of £75.2m total. US-sourced revenues (HT Inc Vermont + Energy Steel Michigan) are significant but the exact USD % of total group revenue is not stated as a single figure. The company reports in GBP; US operations translate at average GBP/USD rates.

HT Inc won $16m KHNP contract + $10m TerraPower — these are USD contracts. Energy Steel is US-based. Rough estimate: US revenues likely 30–40% of AES (£75.2m H1). However, no explicit currency split disclosed in the RNS or Sharescope.

Given: (1) no Currency Movements table in RNS, (2) no explicit % USD disclosed, (3) GBP/USD has been range-bound, I cannot confirm >30% single currency exposure with precision. Applying missing baseline fallback: no penalty applied but flagging USD exposure risk with ±5pp confidence widening. State: USD exposure material (estimated 25–35% of revenues) but below the threshold confidence level for Phase 0B penalty application. No FX badge displayed.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

AVG · Q2 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/5/26

RNS type: Half Year Results (six months ended 30 November 2025).

  1. Revenue — H1 FY26: £78.1m vs H1 FY25 £79.0m = flat YoY (−1.1%). In line with management expectations. H1 vs FY1 consensus £175.0m: £78.1m = 44.6% — below the 47.1% historical H1 baseline (deviation −2.5pp). Company explicitly guided towards more normal 45:55 split (vs prior year's atypical H1-heavy result). Revenue flat YoY was expected.

"Group Revenue was flat at £78.1m (2025 H1: £79.0m), in line with management expectations"

  1. EPS — H1 FY26: Adj diluted EPS 14.6p vs H1 FY25 12.0p = +21.7% YoY. H1 actual 14.6p vs FY1 fc 30.4p = 48.0% — vs 53.3% historical H1 baseline → deviation −5.3pp. Absolute EPS beat on a YoY basis but tracking below seasonal H1% norm (though this is intentional — H2 expected to be stronger per 45:55 weighting).

"Adj. Diluted Earnings Per Share from continuing operations increased to 14.6p (2025 H1: 12.0p)"

  1. FY26e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base EPS (H1 FY26 actual): 14.6p. With H2 implied at 30.4p − 14.6p = 15.8p implied H2 vs FY25 H2 11.7p = +35.0% YoY. Consistent with 45:55 guidance.
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation: no acquisitions in period.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: H1 FY26 adj EBITDA £9.6m (+10.4% vs H1 FY25 £8.7m). Full year FY1 fc EBITDA £20.5m implies H2 EBITDA ~£10.9m vs FY25 H2 (derived: FY25 full year FY = £16.7m − H1 £8.7m = £8.0m... but Sharescope shows H2 FY25 EBITDA as −£8.7m which is clearly a field corruption. Using FY25 full year EBITDA: £8.7m × 2 ≈ £17.4m proxy — actual FY25 adj EBITDA per annual report). Per Sharescope FY25 full year EBITDA not directly given; implied from FY1 fc £20.5m being a step up.
  • (4) Interest step-up: net debt £16.9m, finance costs H1 FY26 £0.35m (vs H1 FY25 £0.77m — significant reduction). No material interest step-up.
  • Implied FY2 (FY27) EPS: 37.4p consensus. With H1 showing strong operational momentum and nuclear order flow accelerating, upside to FY27 consensus is plausible but not yet quantifiable from H1 data alone.
  1. Order book / forward work: AES order book "secured to achieve 95%+ of the FY26 market expectations" — extraordinary visibility. New nuclear orders since Jan 2026: >£10m (including £3m Iberdrola Cofrentes pump + prototype SMR orders) per the April 16 follow-on RNS. HS2 contracts £8.5m won at Booth. $16m KHNP nuclear contract at HT Inc. HT Inc order intake exceeded revenue in H1.

"Order book in AES secured to achieve 95%+ of the FY26 market expectations, providing strong visibility and confidence in meeting targets"

  1. Margin / profitability: Adj EBITDA £9.6m (+10.4%). Gross margin 31.7% (vs H1 FY25 30.0% — +170bps driven by aftermarket mix). Adj PBT £5.7m (+27.1% vs H1 FY25 £4.5m). AES EBITDA margin 14.7% (vs 14.3% H1 FY25). MII division LBITDA loss reduced to −£0.8m (vs −£1.7m H1 FY25). Operating cash inflow £7.6m (vs £4.9m H1 FY25 — +55.1%).

*"Adj.EBITDA increased by 10.4% to £9.6m, mainly driven by reduced losses in the Medical and Industrial Imaging division (2025 H1: £8.7m) also in line with management expectations"

  1. Capital returns: Interim dividend increased 5.3% to 2.0p (vs 1.9p H1 FY25). Payment 26 June 2026. Net debt ex-IFRS16 stable at £12.3m (unchanged from FY25 year-end £12.3m) despite continued MII investment. Strong operating cash conversion.
  2. Qualitative tone — FY26 outlook: Board "confident about achieving market expectations for FY26." Order book 95%+ coverage of FY26 expectations. Chairman: "We benefit from clear visibility over the revenue and profits of the second half of FY26." Nuclear tailwinds (AI/data centre demand for new nuclear, SMR momentum) described as accelerating. New nuclear orders >£10m post period end (per April 16 follow-on RNS) validate the nuclear thesis. MII at inflection with Adaptix 510(k) FDA clearance received and US distribution commencing. Strategic review of M&A and PIE exits explicitly mentioned.

EPS quality check: Adj diluted EPS 14.6p. Effective tax rate 15.8% (lower than standard due to US tax credit and UK loss utilisation). Normalised UK rate 25% + US mix. The 15.8% effective rate is lower than normalised, benefiting H1 EPS. If tax normalises to ~22% in H2, this is already factored into the 30.4p FY consensus. Not a distortion risk — the low rate is structurally explained by loss utilisation, not a one-off credit. No restatement required.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

The Board's language: "The Board is confident about achieving market expectations for FY26." This is explicitly "in line with" language — no upgrade, no downgrade. However, the April 16 follow-on RNS (strong nuclear orders >£10m) arrives simultaneously and provides a forward positive catalyst beyond the H1 results themselves.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — 95%+ FY26 order coverage, £10m+ new nuclear orders post-period, dividend increase, MII losses narrowing sharply. The "confident about meeting market expectations" language is floor, not ceiling. The nuclear order momentum (April 16 RNS) constitutes "record order book" language arriving concurrently. Combined, this is upgrade-triggering. Provisional points: +13.

Divergence check: H1 revenue flat (vs prior year's unusually strong H1) but this was guided and consistent with 45:55 split. H1 EPS up +21.7%. Outlook constructive/upgrade-triggering. No divergence.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

AVG · Q2 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 31/5/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 derivation checks:

  • FY25 H2: Sharescope shows H2 = −£8.7m (EBITDA field corrupt, contains negative of H1). For revenue: Sharescope 1y ago H2 = £77.4m; H1 + H2 = £79.0 + £77.4 = £156.4m vs stated FY £156.4m ✓. Revenue H2 clean.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

BILN · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

  1. Revenue — FY25 actual: £95.7m vs FY25fc £92.5m = +£3.2m / +3.5% beat. vs FY24 £113.1m = −15.4% YoY.

"Revenue reduced by 15.4% to £95.7 million (2024: £113.1 million)"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual: Underlying EPS 27.1p vs FY25fc 18.8p = +8.3p / +44.1% beat. Underlying PBT £4.1m vs FY25fc £3.5m = +£0.6m / +17.1% beat. EBITDA £6.1m vs FY25fc £5.4m = +13.0% beat. Basic EPS 10.4p (after £2.8m non-underlying costs including Yate closure). FY24 underlying EPS 66.2p.

"Underlying basic earnings per share: 27.1p (2024: 66.2p)"

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • New base: FY25 underlying EPS 27.1p (actual, confirmed)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil (no acquisitions)
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY26fc EBITDA £10.1m vs FY25 £6.1m = +£4.0m improvement guided. RNS CEO: "expect to deliver an improved financial performance in 2026, in line with market expectations." FY26fc EPS 44.8p = £8.3m PAT / 12.6m shares × tax = implies PBT ~£11.0m. From FY25 PBT £4.1m to FY26fc PBT implied ~£8.3m = +£4.2m improvement — driven by volume recovery, Yate closure cost savings, and higher productive hours already secured.
  • Interest step-up: nil (net cash).
  • FY26e implied: 44.8p consensus appears to be already reflecting the recovery. EPS bridge supports this — no new upgrade catalyst beyond confirmation that FY26 trajectory is intact. The beat on FY25 (27.1p vs 18.8p fc) is the relevant event today.
  1. Order book / forward work: "Strong and growing order book for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027." "Strong level of production hours secured for projects due to be delivered in 2026 and 2027." No specific order book value disclosed. Peter Marshall Steel Stairs: "strong order book for the current year and into 2027." SPC: "record year in 2025."

"The Group has a strong and growing order book for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027"

  1. Margin/cost signals: Underlying ROS: PBT £4.1m / Revenue £95.7m = 4.3% vs FY24 £10.8m/£113.1m = 9.5%. Yate facility closure (£2.8m non-underlying costs) — structural cost saving. Higher productive hours (+4.2%) vs lower revenue (−15.4%) reflects focus shift to complex, higher-margin projects with less steel content.
  2. Capital/balance sheet: Cash £20.5m (vs £21.7m FY24) — marginal reduction. Debt free. DPS 11.0p (vs 25.0p FY24) — 56% cut, covered 2.46× by underlying EPS.

"A dividend of 11.0 pence per share in respect of 2025 (25.0 pence per share paid in respect of 2024)"

  1. Qualitative tone FY26: "Entered 2026 with increased confidence and expect to deliver an improved financial performance in 2026, in line with market expectations." CEO points to order book visibility, improved cost base, and data centres/energy-from-waste market demand.

EPS quality check: Underlying EPS 27.1p vs basic EPS 10.4p — £2.8m non-underlying costs (Yate closure restructuring) excluded from underlying. This is appropriate and clean; £2.8m/12.6m = 2.4× difference correctly reflects the adjustments. The underlying figure is the operative metric for broker comparisons.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "in line with market expectations" with positive tone ("increased confidence," growing order book). Yate closure costs are one-off (non-recurring in FY26). The step-up from FY25 underlying EPS 27.1p to FY26fc 44.8p is a +65% guided recovery — very large. Guidance does not explicitly upgrade beyond the 44.8p/£125m consensus.

Classification: 🟡 In-line with positive undertone (confirmed order book, cost base improved). Points: +1 to +3.

No divergence: FY25 beat → FY26 in-line. No contradiction — beat confirms the trough is past.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

BILN · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

FY24113.1−14.6%66.2−16.5%
FY25e*95.7†−15.4%27.1†−59.1%
FY26e*125.0+30.5%44.8+65.3%

† RNS actual.

Revenue growth trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — +52.9%, −14.6%, −15.4%. Sharp reversal from FY23 peak.

EPS growth trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — +109.8%, −16.5%, −59.1%. Two-year decline, FY26 recovery guided.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: FY25 −15.4% vs FY24 −14.6% → no acceleration (marginal further decline). 🔴
  • EPS: FY25 −59.1% vs FY24 −16.5% → sharp deceleration, not acceleration. 🔴

3.1 HoH Growth

Revenue trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — H2 FY23 +79.0%, H2 FY24 −23.7%, H1 FY25 −27.8%.

EPS trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — H2 FY23 +79.7%, H2 FY24 −23.0%, H2 FY25 −56.1%.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY (pre-FY mode — written in full, not scored)

Revenue: H1 FY25 £41.8m ÷ FY25 actual £95.7m = 43.7% vs baseline 50.0% → deviation −6.3pp — significantly below seasonal norm. Explains why consensus was wrong about H2 recovery. H1 was disproportionately weak; H2 recovered partially.

EPS: H1 FY25 9.4p ÷ FY25 actual 27.1p = 34.7% vs baseline 28.4% → deviation +6.3pp — EPS H1 was actually ahead of seasonal norm due to the reversal in profitability structure.

Phase 3.2 not scored in Phase 5 — pre-FY mode.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored in Phase 5)

H2 base: RNS-derived. H2 FY25 revenue £53.9m, EPS 17.7p.

Revenue H2 YoY: £53.9m vs FY24 H2 £55.2m = −2.4% YoY → 🟡 flat (slight decline)

EPS H2 YoY: 17.7p vs FY24 H2 40.3p = −56.1% YoY → 🔴 severe

Contextual note: The severe H2 EPS decline reflects the pricing pressure, contract slippage, and restructuring costs hitting H2 FY25 disproportionately. FY26 recovery guided with Yate one-off costs removed.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum

  • EPS trend: −53.6% net (40.5p → 18.8p) — severe step-down in Oct 25. No further moves since then.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • Divergence: Price exactly equals consensus TP at 380p — remarkable coincidence or price anchored to TP. Zero upside at TP.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Net cash: FY22 +£5.7m → FY23 +£11.3m → FY24 −£0.1m (temporarily zero) → H1 FY25 +£17.1m → FY25 actual +£20.5m → FY26fc +£22.5m. Confirmed debt free. Cash generation excellent — £20.5m maintained despite £3.2m dividend paid in FY25.

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY25 underlying EPS 27.1p vs FY24 66.2p → 🚨 −59.1% decline. Revenue £95.7m vs £113.1m → 🚨 −15.4%. Both well below prior year. Note: FY25 beat consensus significantly (+44.1% EPS beat) suggesting the decline was anticipated. ⚠️ replace 🚨 with ⚠️ (consensus already modelled the decline; beat vs fc is the operative signal).

Step 2: FY26fc EPS 44.8p > FY25 27.1p ✅✅. FY26fc Revenue £125.0m > FY25 £95.7m ✅✅.

3.6 Structural Flags

Yate facility closure (non-recurring): £2.8m non-underlying costs in FY25, operations consolidated to Barnsley. This is a one-off that will not recur, improving FY26 underlying profitability by removing a structurally loss-making site. CEO confirms operational efficiency improved.

Market shift to complex projects: Higher productive hours (+4.2%) but lower revenue (−15.4%) reflects deliberate focus on complex, less steel-intensive work. This is a strategic margin improvement play — margin per productive hour rising, but volume measured by revenue declining. Net effect: FY26 recovery as volume normalises.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

BILN · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — Underlying EPS 27.1p vs consensus 18.8p (+44.1% beat): This is a massive beat on the key metric. Brokers had modelled 18.8p after the Oct 25 downgrade; the actual 27.1p is 44% above that. The beat reflects better-than-feared H2 recovery, Yate restructuring savings crystallising faster, and possibly higher-margin project mix. This will force an immediate formal revision to FY25 actuals.

#2 Driver — FY26 in-line guidance with "increased confidence": FY26fc 44.8p is the recovery year target (a +65% swing from FY25 trough). The CEO's "increased confidence" and growing order book for FY26/FY27 supports this trajectory. The question is whether 44.8p is conservative given the +27.1p base vs 18.8p baseline brokers used.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY25 EPS: Upgraded to 27.1p (from 18.8p = +44.1%). Revenue upgraded to £95.7m (from £92.5m = +3.5%).
  • FY26 EPS: Current consensus 44.8p. If brokers reset their FY25 base from 18.8p to 27.1p, they must reassess FY26 bridge assumptions. FY26 recovery was modelled as a bounce from 18.8p — with base now higher, the "recovery" may look different. However, the CEO guided "in line with market expectations" explicitly. Brokers likely hold FY26 at 44.8p — the recovery is already modelled. Possible small upward revision if the order book translates to higher volumes: +5–10% = 47–49p range.
  • FY26 Revenue: £125m consensus likely held/trimmed slightly if demand recovery is gradual. Structural steel market remains competitive.
  • TP: Consensus 380p = current price 380p. Zero implied upside at TP. Brokers will almost certainly raise TP given the underlying EPS beat — new TP likely £420–460p range (+10–20%).

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with market expectations" at the end of a massive underlying EPS beat = the guidance is anchored to a consensus that will itself be revised up. Post-revision, "in line with [new] expectations" will imply a higher actual outcome for FY26 if management maintains similar conservatism.

Key risk: FY24 was a peak year (£113.1m revenue, 66.2p EPS); the structural steel market has been in sustained demand decline with pricing pressure since. The Yate closure improves cost efficiency but doesn't resolve demand. FY26 revenue consensus of £125m (+30.5% from FY25 trough) assumes a significant market recovery — not guaranteed.

Consistency check: Net FY26 revision: hold to modest upgrade (+5–10%). But the key revision is FY25 actual (+44.1%). Tone: Constructive given scale of FY25 beat.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — the FY25 EPS beat is the dominant event and will drive TP upgrades; FY26 guidance held in-line but with a higher base.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

BILN

67/100 · Confidence: 60–74 · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

Raw: +15+7+6+5+4−2−3−5−4−3−3 = +17 → 50 base + 17 = ~67 (green-low band)

Para 1 — Headline numbers: BILN delivered FY25 underlying EPS of 27.1p against consensus of 18.8p — a +44.1% beat — the dominant catalyst. Revenue of £95.7m also beat by +3.5% vs £92.5m. Underlying PBT of £4.1m (+17% beat) and EBITDA of £6.1m (+13% beat) confirm that the H2 trough anticipated by brokers was not as deep as feared. The Yate facility closure generated £2.8m of non-underlying costs which are excluded from the underlying basis — these are clean one-offs that will not recur. The statutory PBT of £1.3m vs underlying £4.1m confirms the nature of the charge.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, H2 FY25 revenue of £53.9m was −2.4% YoY (🟡 flat) and H2 EPS of 17.7p was −56.1% YoY (🔴 severe) — both confirming the challenging conditions management described. However, the context is critical: the FY25 underlying EPS of 27.1p massively exceeded the consensus of 18.8p that was set post the Oct 25 downgrade, meaning the H2 weakness was already over-discounted. The order book for FY26/FY27 is described as "strong and growing," with production hours secured in data centres and energy-from-waste — markets with resilient demand. The clean balance sheet (£20.5m cash, debt free) provides full flexibility for FY26 execution.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: The FY25 EPS upgrade from 18.8p → 27.1p (+44.1%) is the primary revision event. FY26 EPS likely held at 44.8p (management guided explicitly in-line), but this may prove conservative given the higher FY25 starting point — modest upside to 47–49p (+5–10%) if the order book converts as indicated. TP will almost certainly be raised from 380p — the current price equals the stale TP, which is now definitively too low given the underlying beat; new TP range likely £420–460p from Cavendish. The dividend cut to 11p (from 25p) confirms the board is not yet signalling full recovery — watch: FY26 H1 results for order book momentum and whether pricing pressure has eased.

🏁 A 44% underlying EPS beat vs consensus is a high-conviction buy signal for FY25; FY26 recovery trajectory is confirmed in-line; TP upgrades highly probable. Score 67/100.

  1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

H2 EPS burden: 9.18p required vs 3yr avg H2 of 3.6p — burden MASSIVELY HIGHER than consensus assumes. Management guided "in line" implying brokers already modelled this extreme H2.

Historical hit rate: No prior year with H1 deviation of this magnitude in the 3yr dataset. Precedent absent.

Key note — deployment timing thesis: H1 FY26 contained only £0.57m upfront revenue vs £3.30m H1 FY25. Management states "the majority of these deployments have now been completed." If true, H2 catch-up is mechanistically secured.

  1. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • Implied H2 FY26: £25.65m vs £13.0m = +97.3% above 3yr avg

  • Classification: strong in direction — but binary execution risk. Not organic acceleration; a recovery trade.
  1. Forecast Momentum Overlay
  • EPS trend: 7.6p → 8.5p (+0.9p, +11.8%). Single upgrade event 18 Oct 25. No movement since.
  • 4-week trend: STALLING — 20 consecutive flat weeks
  • Revenue trend: £37.3m → £40.3m (+8.0%), single step
  • Divergence: Price −40.3% (335p → 200p) while EPS consensus +11.8%. Severe price/forecast divergence — market pricing in implicit downgrade risk not yet reflected in consensus.
  1. Structural / One-Off Flags
  • Revenue-share model transition [STRUCTURAL]: Exchange Cloud moving from upfront recognition to monthly revenue-share permanently. Depresses H1 during transition but improves revenue quality. "we expect it to deliver greater revenue in the medium term than the prior model"
  • Deployment lag [TIMING — RESOLVING]: "More pronounced than usual" in H1. "The majority of these deployments have now been completed" — key management assertion.
  • ACMRR vs P&L divergence [LEADING INDICATOR]: £32.8m ACMRR annualised (£16.4m/half) vs £14.65m reported H1. 12% gap = unrecognised contracted revenue due to convert.
  • H2 front-loading [YEAR-SPECIFIC ANOMALY]: £0.57m upfront H1 vs £3.30m prior H1. ~£3m from December Proximity Cloud wins due H2. Not a recurring pattern.
PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 — ACMRR growth (+15% to £32.8m) vs P&L divergence. Brokers anchor here as the forward revenue indicator validating the H2 recovery thesis. #2 — H2 recovery credibility. The specificity of management's visibility (£3m Proximity Cloud, BMV DR, TMX, nuam go-lives) gives concrete items to model. Most retain estimates but reduce conviction.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 Revenue: hold, possibly −2 to −4% if H2 slip risk modelled. FY1 EPS: hold to −5 to −10% cut (H1 loss worse than most models; H2 burden unprecedented). FY2 Revenue: hold to +0–3% upgrade on ACMRR strength. FY2 EPS: hold to +0–5% upgrade if H2 FY26 delivers.
  1. Target price / recommendation: Likely hold TP with some cuts −10 to −15%. Current TP 335p vs 200p spot = 67.5% upside. Extreme upside-to-TP gap means brokers unlikely to upgrade; stock needs to demonstrate H2. Possible TP range 250–310p from cautious brokers. Recommendations shifting to "hold" or "speculative buy."
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with its expectations" is neutral maintenance language, not "comfortable" or "not less than." Does not increase upgrade cycle probability. Minimum bar to avoid downgrades only.
  1. Key risk: H2 execution failure — any deployment slip on BMV, TMX, nuam, or Proximity Cloud wins beyond 30 June 2026 makes £25.65m H2 revenue and 9.18p EPS unachievable, requiring material FY consensus cuts. "the timing of deal signature can be hard to predict"
  1. Overall tone: Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — H1 P&L misses significant; H2 burden unprecedented; share price already at −40% signalling market scepticism. Most brokers will formally maintain FY estimates but cut TPs and lower tone.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
32
/100
Confidence range: 26–40 · FX penalty −10 pts: 45.8% USD · GBP headwind (H1 FY26 avg ~1.339 vs H1 FY25 avg ~1.291)
ACMRR +15% YoY — strong leading indicator+12
TCV +23% / £11.9m record — commercial momentum+8
Management "in line" FY guidance maintained+5
H2 deployment visibility (£3m Proximity, BMV, TMX, nuam)+6
Kraken profitable ahead of schedule+4
H1 revenue −7.3% YoY, −17.7% vs seasonal baseline−8
H1 EPS −0.68p vs +2.18p baseline — −33.7pp deviation−10
Gross margin collapse 38% → 30%, EBITDA −28%−7
Unprecedented H2 EPS burden (9.18p vs 3.6p 3yr avg)−8
Net cash decline, new debt drawn, FX headwind−5
Forecast momentum stalled, 20 weeks no movement−3
USD FX headwind (Rule 1)−10
Price/consensus divergence (−40% vs +12% EPS)−2

This is a structurally complex H1 result where the headline numbers are emphatically negative on every reported P&L metric, yet the leading commercial indicators tell an entirely different story. The #1 metric — ACMRR of £32.8m, up +15% YoY — is the number brokers must hold onto, because the reported figures are almost entirely a function of deployment timing rather than demand. H1 revenue of £14.65m was −7.3% YoY and −17.7% below the seasonal baseline of £17.8m, the largest H1 tracking deviation in the company's history. Underlying diluted EPS of −0.68p versus the 2.18p seasonal baseline is a −33.7pp deviation, triggering a mechanical 🔴 SELL SIGNAL on both metrics. The single definitive catalyst is the deployment timing thesis: H1 FY26 contained just £0.57m of upfront revenue versus £3.30m in the same period last year, with the majority of the December £6m Proximity Cloud contract wins deliberately back-loaded into H2. This is not a demand problem — TCV of £11.9m was signed in H1 alone, up +23% YoY and above the prior record — but a cash-conversion timing problem of unusual severity.

The H2 EPS burden is the central risk in this investment case. Consensus FY1 EPS of 8.5p requires 9.18p from H2 alone — more than double the 3-year average H2 of 3.6p and +99.6% above the prior comparable period H2 of 4.6p. Management has provided specific, itemised H2 revenue drivers: approximately £3m from December Proximity Cloud wins already contracted and deploying; BMV disaster recovery site go-live; TMX and nuam Exchange Cloud go-lives; and the Kraken Exchange Cloud contract now moving into monthly profitability in March 2026, ahead of schedule. The ACMRR run-rate of £32.8m annualised (implying £16.4m per half in pure recurring revenue) provides the base. The £10.1m of accrued income on the balance sheet will also unwind as cash, further supporting reported revenue. The downside case is contained if — and only if — deployments execute on schedule; the structural risk is that any single meaningful slip creates a domino effect on H2 deliverability. The FX headwind (GBP ~4.8c stronger vs the prior-year H1 average) applies a further mechanical drag on the 45.8% USD revenue base.

Brokers are likely to hold FY1 consensus formally — management's "in line" guidance gives cover — but with sharply increased confidence intervals. FY1 EPS held at 8.5p by most, with a subset cutting −5 to −10% to ~7.7–8.1p if they model deployment slippage. FY2 EPS of 10.3p may see modest upgrades (+0 to +5%) as ACMRR trajectory supports the medium-term narrative. Consensus TP of 335p likely to see cuts to 250–310p range from a majority of brokers. The main constraint on the score is the binary nature of the investment case: if H2 FY26 delivers, the stock is materially undervalued at 200p; if it does not, FY consensus requires a double-digit cut. Upgrade cycle probability is low over the next 6–8 weeks — the catalyst is H2 trading evidence, likely via a pre-close update in May or June. Score of 32/100 reflects that this RNS comprehensively fails the mechanical H1 tracking tests and delivers broker uncertainty rather than broker confidence, even as the underlying commercial picture is the strongest in the company's history.

BMS — Braemar PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year ended 28 February 2026, results due end of May 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Braemar is a shipping broker — revenues denominated in USD (shipping commissions), GBP (some UK broking) and other currencies. The RNS does not contain a Currency Movements section with explicit percentage breakdowns. Revenue ~£135m; prior-year £141.9m. No formal Currency Movements table present. Braemar's forward order book is quoted in USD ($72.5m), suggesting significant USD exposure. However, without explicit disclosure of >30% single currency exposure, Phase 0B criteria are not met by the RNS disclosure rules. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty. Note: USD strength/weakness will be relevant to broker modelling but not scorable here.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (FY ends 28 Feb 2026, results due end May). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 21.2p · Revenue £132.0m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 26.1p · Revenue £139.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 31.1p → 21.2p = −9.9p (−31.8%). Sharp cut in June 2025 (31.1p → 21.7p); then gradual moderation to 21.2p (Nov 2025). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 21.2p / £132.0m for 4+ months). Revenue: £146.4m → £132.0m (−9.6%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.3% of FY = £65.1m · EPS 52.9% of FY = 11.2p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £76.0m · EPS 12.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £132.0m − H1 actual £63.9m = implied H2 £68.1m vs prior H2 £65.9m → +3.3% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 21.2p − 8.1p = 13.1p vs prior H2 13.9p → −5.8% YoY — modest H2 decline embedded in consensus.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY ended 28 February 2026, results due end May 2026)

1. Revenue — actual vs consensus

FY26 revenue: approximately £135.0m (prior year: £141.9m, −4.9% YoY).

vs FY1 consensus of £132.0m: beat of £3.0m (+2.3%).

"Revenue of approximately £135.0m (FY25: £141.9m)"

2. Underlying operating profit — actual vs consensus

FY26 underlying operating profit (before acquisition-related expenditure): approximately £13.2m (FY25: £16.7m, −21.0% YoY).

vs consensus of £13.2m: in-line exactly (consensus was £13.2m per footnote 1, range £13.0–£13.8m).

"Underlying operating profit (before acquisition-related expenditure) of c.£13.2m (FY25: £16.7m), subject to audit."

3. Net debt / cash

Net debt at 28 February 2026: £2.9m (FY25: net debt £2.5m). "Returning to a net cash positive position during March 2026."

4. Forward order book

Forward order book at end February 2026: $72.5m (FY25: $82.2m, −11.8% YoY). Covers revenue to be earned up to 2039.

"The Group's forward order book at the end of February 2026 remains strong at $72.5m (FY25: $82.2m)."

5. Strategic progress

  • New Africa office opened
  • UK Organised Trading Facility launched (Securities business)
  • £2m share buyback programme completed
  • Key senior hires made
  • Acquisition opportunities being evaluated

6. Outlook

Middle East conflict creating uncertainty — increased rates but lower volumes in certain markets. Board "remains confident in the Group's prospects and delivering on its FY30 objectives." No numeric FY27 guidance.

EPS quality check: No EPS disclosed in trading update — operating profit basis only. EPS to be confirmed in May results. Cannot check tax rate.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "board remains confident in the Group's prospects and delivering on its FY30 objectives" — qualitative, covers long-term. No FY27 numeric guidance. Revenue beat (+2.3%) but operating profit exactly in-line vs consensus midpoint. H2 was stronger than H1 as guided.
  • The revenue beat and in-line profitability against an already-downgraded consensus is neutral to mildly positive.
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — operating profit in-line with consensus, revenue slightly ahead. Long-term confident language only. Provisional points: +1.
  • Divergence check: Revenue beat (+2.3%) + operating profit in-line + declining YoY (revenue −4.9%, OP −21.0%) = mixed picture. No divergence per se — both beat/in-line metrics are relative to the already-downgraded consensus. Decline vs prior year is the headline but this was expected.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

EPS trajectory (HoH YoY): H1: −9.9%, −36.7% — sharp H1 deterioration. H2: −12.0%, −5.8% (implied) — H2 relatively resilient. 🔴 Decelerating overall.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 49.3% × £132.0m = £65.1m
  • EPS baseline: 52.9% × 21.2p = 11.2p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £63.9m ÷ FY1 consensus £132.0m = 48.4% vs baseline 49.3% → deviation = 🟡 [−0.9pp] → 🟡 IN LINE
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 8.1p ÷ FY1 consensus 21.2p = 38.2% vs baseline 52.9% → deviation = 🔴 [−14.7pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL — H1 EPS dramatically below seasonal norm; H2 must deliver 13.1p (well above H1 8.1p) to hit consensus
  • H2 EPS burden: FY consensus 21.2p − H1 actual 8.1p = 13.1p required vs historical H2 avg ~14.6p — burden LOWER than historical H2 avg; H2 should cover it
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£65.1m × 1.015] = £66.1m → 🔴 ✗ (£63.9m < £66.1m) · H1 EPS > [11.2p × 1.015] = 11.4p → 🔴 ✗ (8.1p < 11.4p)
  • Actual H2 confirmed (from revenue total £135m): H2 £71.1m — above prior H2 £65.9m. H2 recovery materialized as guided. Revenue buy trigger missed but actual H2 exceeded.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • H2 Revenue actual: £71.1m vs prior H2 £65.9m → +7.9% YoY → 🟢 moderate (+0–10%)
  • H2 EPS implied: 13.1p vs prior H2 13.9p → −5.8% YoY → 🟡 flat (−5 to +5%)

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 31.1p → 21.2p, net −9.9p (−31.8%). Sharp cut June 2025 (FY25 results or profit warning), then flat. No recovery in EPS forecasts.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 4 months)
  • Divergence: Price 355p → 235p (−33%) broadly in line with EPS downgrade trajectory. Market has repriced for the new level.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Shipping market cyclicality]: Braemar's revenue is highly correlated to shipping market activity. Lower bulk carrier/tanker/LNG chartering volumes directly reduce commission income. The order book of $72.5m (down 11.8% vs $82.2m prior year) is a forward indicator of likely FY27 revenue pressure.

[Middle East conflict — asymmetric effects]: Increased rates benefit brokers via higher commission values; lower volumes reduce transaction count. Net effect uncertain — board acknowledges uncertainty.

[FY30 targets still intact]: Long-term objectives maintained — management has not downgraded the multi-year plan despite near-term weakness.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Operating profit exactly in-line at £13.2m, revenue +2.3% beat: For Braemar, after a year of downgraded estimates, an in-line result with a modest revenue beat is the best plausible outcome. No profit warning. H2 recovery materialised as guided (H2 stronger than H1). This is a "relief" note rather than an upgrade note.

#2 Driver — Forward order book −11.8% YoY ($72.5m vs $82.2m): The order book decline signals FY27 revenue will be under pressure. With FY26 revenue already declining −4.9% YoY, a further decline in FY27 is probable if the order book trend continues. This limits any TP or EPS upgrade.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY27) EPS: HOLD/minor down — from 21.2p to possibly 20.5–21.0p (small downward revision given order book). Revenue: HOLD at £132m or minor revision.
  • FY2 (FY28) EPS: HOLD from 26.1p — FY30 targets and acquisition pipeline could underpin.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 320p likely held at 300–320p — brokers may cut modestly given order book. At 235p, upside to TP 27–36%. No change in recommendation expected — Hold/Neutral maintained.

Key risk: Order book −11.8% YoY. If this reflects structural market weakening rather than timing, FY27 consensus of £132m/21.2p may be optimistic. The £2.9m net debt (near cash neutral) and buyback completion reduce near-term concerns but don't reverse the earnings trend.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold (minor downward pressure). Tone must be Neutral. → 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

46/100 · Confidence: 40–52 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Braemar delivered FY26 results in-line with expectations after a year of heavy forecast cuts: revenue of approximately £135.0m (+2.3% vs £132.0m consensus) and underlying operating profit of ~£13.2m (exactly in-line), with H2 delivering the recovery that was guided at the start of the year. This is a "no worse than feared" result — the absence of a profit warning is the primary catalyst, not a genuine beat. The #1 broker note metric is the operating profit in-line outcome, which validates the downgraded consensus and prevents another round of cuts on the FY26 baseline.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 recovery was real: H2 revenue of approximately £71.1m was +7.9% YoY vs prior H2 £65.9m, confirming the H2/H1 seasonality dynamic in shipping broking. However, the forward order book of $72.5m is −11.8% below FY25's $82.2m — this is the critical warning for FY27 and prevents brokers from initiating an upgrade cycle. With the H1 EPS tracking signal of −14.7pp (Sell Signal), the H2 recovery was the arithmetic necessity to hit full-year estimates, not a genuine operational acceleration. Braemar's FY30 growth targets and acquisition pipeline provide medium-term optionality, but near-term earnings trajectory is declining.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Minor downward revision risk on FY27 estimates (21.2p → possibly 20.5–21.0p) given order book decline. Revenue consensus at £132m for FY27 may prove optimistic if the $72.5m order book translates to further decline. TP from 320p likely held at 300–320p; upside from 235p is 27–36%. The watch point is the full year results in end May 2026, which will provide H1/H2 EPS split and updated order book guidance. 🏁 Neutral: revenue slightly ahead of downgraded consensus, operating profit in-line, H2 recovery confirmed — but order book decline signals FY27 pressure; no upgrade catalyst today, hold and wait for May results and new FY27 guidance. Score 46/100.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (Q2). RNS = FY Results year ended 31 December 2025. No FX rule triggered — Boku reports in USD, no single currency exceeds 30% of revenues.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 8.9p, Revenue $127.9m. FY2: EPS 10.8p, Rev $155.4m.
  • Momentum: EPS +7.2% (8.3p→8.9p). Revenue +7.0%. Last-4-week FLAT. Stock de-rated 246p→166p despite improving EPS — asymmetric re-rating opportunity.
  • Implied H2 (pre-RNS): Rev H2 cns $64.6m vs prior H2 $52.0m = +24.2% YoY. Actual H2 $65.5m = +1.4% beat vs implied H2 cns.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

FY Results — Year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue: $128.8m vs cns $127.9m = +0.7% beat. +30% YoY. +15% vs start-of-year cns $112m (explicitly flagged by management).
    "particularly against consensus expectations at the start of the year of c.$112m for revenue and c.$36m for adjusted EBITDA"
  2. Adj EBITDA: $41.3m vs cns ~$40.1m = +3.0% beat. +36% YoY. Margin 32.1% (+1.6pp). Underlying ex-FX reclassification = 34.0%.
    "Adjusted EBITDA increased by 36% to $41.3m… adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.1% (FY 2024: 30.5%)"
  3. Digital Wallets & A2A: +67% to $43.5m, 34% of revenues (FY24: 26%). C.$3m non-recurring launch-phase pricing from single DW connection in H1.
    "Digital Wallets & Account to Account revenues grew by 67%… This included c.$3m from launch-phase pricing related to a single Digital Wallet connection in H1 2025"
  4. Bundling: +71% to $14.9m. Non-DCB now 45% of revenues (FY24: 35%, FY23: 27%). Core diversification thesis on track.
    "Bundling revenues increased by 71% year-on-year, contributing 11% of total revenues"
  5. MAUs +31% to 114.4m; TPV +27% to $15.7bn. Q4 milestone: >100m transacting monthly.
    "Monthly Active Users in December 2025 +31% to 114.4m… Total Payment Volume +27% to $15.7bn"
  6. Own cash +28% to $102.9m. Debt-free. Buyback $12.3m FY25 + new 4m programme completed Feb 2026 ($11.9m).
    "Own cash grew by 28% to $102.9m… 4 million shares were repurchased in January-February 2026, at a total cost of $11.9m"
  7. FY26 new catalysts: Brazil PIX (authorised), India UPI (final approval), UK PISP (authorised) — all going live to merchants in 2026.
    "In Brazil, we secured Payment Institution authorisation… which we expect to make available to merchants in 2026"
  8. Medium-term guidance unchanged: >20% CAGR; >30% EBITDA margin; progressive accretion from FY26.
    "we expect organic revenue growth exceeding 20%… adjusted EBITDA margin exceeding 30% with progressive accretion from 2026"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: FY24 $99.3m → FY25A $128.8m = +29.7%. Two consecutive years ~30% growth. Steady at ~30% pa — tracking ahead of >20% CAGR guidance.
  • Non-DCB diversification: 45% (FY23: 27%, FY24: 35%, FY25: 45%). Linear trajectory accelerating. Core re-rating thesis.
  • H2 FY25: Rev $65.5m (+25.9% vs H2 FY24 $52.0m). Beat implied cns H2 by +1.4%. EPS recovery sharp from near-zero historical base.
  • Structural risk — $3m non-recurring + take-rate dilution: H1 FY26 faces elevated comparator; Bundling growth dilutes blended take-rate (guided to trend down).

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 — $112m→$128.8m narrative (+15% vs start-of-year cns): Management explicitly called this out. Investec and Peel Hunt will lead with this. Third consecutive year of ~30% growth tracking ahead of >20% CAGR guidance.
2#2 — EBITDA margin +1.6pp to 32.1%, opex +27% vs rev +30%: First clear evidence of operating leverage. "Progressive accretion from FY26" gives brokers licence to model meaningful margin expansion in FY26–27.
3FY2 revisions: Revenue +3–7% to $160–165m; EPS +5–10% to ~9.4–9.8p. $3m non-recurring H1 element creates FY26 comparator headwind — brokers will model explicitly.

Baseline+50

Boku delivered its strongest FY results to date: revenue $128.8m (+30% YoY, +15% vs start-of-year consensus), adj EBITDA $41.3m (+36%) with margin expanding to 32.1% (+1.6pp) — first clear evidence of operating leverage as opex grew only 27% vs revenue +30%. Non-DCB revenues reached 45% of total (FY24: 35%, FY23: 27%), with Digital Wallets +67% and Bundling +71%. MAUs +31% and TPV +27% confirm the platform is scaling faster than revenue.

Medium-term guidance of >20% CAGR confirmed unchanged — but FY25's 30% delivery makes this effectively conservative, giving brokers licence to model above the floor. New regulatory licences in Brazil (PIX), India (UPI) and UK (PISP) provide incremental FY26 revenue streams. The stock's 44% de-rating from recent highs (327p → 166p) despite improving fundamentals creates asymmetric re-rating potential.

Brokers Investec and Peel Hunt are expected to publish strongly positive upgrade notes within 24–48 hours, raising FY2 EPS to ~9.4–9.8p (+5–10%), FY2 revenue to $160–165m (+3–7%), and TPs to 350–380p. Watch points: H1 FY26 clean underlying growth ex-$3m non-recurring item, first PIX/UPI merchant revenues, and Bundling Americas momentum.

TICKER 8: BOOM

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY25 Full Year Results. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

BOOM · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025) + Q1 FY26 trading update simultaneously published.
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 21.5p · Revenue $82.7m (USD)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 30.9p · Revenue $93.9m (USD)
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over snapshot: +1.9% (21.1p → 21.5p). Revenue: $83.3m → $82.7m — slight downward drift. Modest upgrades and reversals throughout — essentially flat. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.0% of FY = 50.0% × $82.7m = $41.4m · EPS: history too erratic for meaningful baseline (large negative swings from onerous contracts).
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24 H1): Revenue $34.1m · EPS −8.2p (cents equivalent)
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc $82.7m − H1 actual $35.1m = implied H2 $47.6m vs FY24 H2 $39.3m → +21.1% YoY — 🟢 strong.
  • FX: USD reporting company. Revenue in USD, functional currency USD for Austin Advertising and Audioboom Inc. UK entity (Audioboom Limited) has GBP functional currency, consolidated into USD. Phase 0B: USD is the reporting currency (Sharescope Currency = USD). Phase 0B not applicable as a penalty mechanism — the GBP/USD rate affects GBP share price translation but not USD-reported earnings. No Phase 0B adjustment.
  • Reporting currency & debt: USD · Net debt/(cash): FY24 H2 −$0.4m / current H1 −$1.6m / FY1fc −$5.0m / FY2fc −$9.9m · ND/EBITDA: FY1fc −1.0x / FY2fc −1.4x · Interest cover: FY1fc 22.5x / FY2fc 22.7x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — increasingly cash-generative; onerous contracts concluded.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

BOOM · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (FY25) + simultaneous Q1 FY26 trading update.

  1. Revenue — FY25 actual: $80.4m vs FY1 consensus $82.7m → miss of −$2.3m / −2.8%. Revenue up 10% vs FY24 $73.4m but below consensus. Showcase revenue $30.4m (+31%). Premium $40.9m (+4%). Sonic $8.7m (−17%).

"2025 revenue of US$80.4 million, up 10% on 2024 (US$73.4 million)"

  1. EPS/earnings — FY25 actual: Adj EBITDA $5.1m (+54% vs FY24 $3.4m) — ahead of 2025 market expectations. Basic EPS 5.6 cents (5.6p approx). Vs FY1 fc EPS 21.5p — significant miss on consensus EPS. However: the consensus EPS in USD terms needs careful assessment. Sharescope EPS is in pence but the company reports in USD cents. FY25 EPS = 5.6 cents ($0.056). At GBP/USD ~1.28, = ~4.4p. Pre-RNS consensus was 21.5p — this cannot be correct if the actual is 5.6 cents. ⚠️ Reporting currency gate: Sharescope EPS for BOOM is in pence (GBP). Company reports in USD cents. The conversion is via GBP/USD exchange rate. 5.6 cents at say 1.28 = 4.4p. Consensus 21.5p implies ~27 USD cents at 1.28 — which is not plausible for a company with $80m revenue and $5.1m EBITDA.

Resolution: The Sharescope FY1 fc EPS of 21.5p is likely denominated in pence but based on USD cents × a different share count or FX rate assumption. The actual adj EBITDA-based EPS is approximately: ($5.1m adj EBITDA − D&A ~$0.2m − finance ~$0.4m − tax ~$0.03m) / 18.0m diluted shares ≈ $0.25/share = ~25 cents = ~19.5p at 1.28. This is below the 21.5p pre-RNS consensus. However, the RNS states adj EBITDA was "ahead of 2025 market expectations" — implying the EBITDA consensus was below $5.1m. The EPS vs consensus comparison is ambiguous due to FX and share count differences. Use EBITDA as the primary metric: $5.1m actual vs implied consensus below $5.1m = beat.

  1. FY26e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base: adj EBITDA $5.1m FY25, basic EPS 5.6 cents.
  • (2) Inorganic: Adelicious full-year in FY26 (acquired July 2025; contributed $4.3m revenue and $0.1m PBT from acquisition date). Full year = ~$8m additional revenue.
  • (3) Organic: Q1 FY26 revenue $22.5m (+30% vs Q1 FY25 $17.3m); adj EBITDA Q1 $1.5m (+118% vs Q1 FY25 $0.6m).
  • (4) Onerous contract elimination: final onerous contract expired 31 December 2025 — removes drag on both EBITDA and cash. "Board expecting adjusted EBITDA in 2026 to once again serve as a proxy for cash generation."
  • (5) Interest: no debt, interest cover 22.5x — negligible.
  • Implied FY26 adj EBITDA: Q1 $1.5m implies annualised $6m minimum; Showcase growing 31% YoY; Adelicious full year; onerous contract removal → consensus $4.9m FY1fc EBITDA looks too low. Actual FY26 EBITDA likely $6–8m. FY2 fc EPS 30.9p consensus appears reasonable if EBITDA reaches $7–8m.
  1. Order book / forward work: Q1 FY26 revenue $22.5m (+30% YoY). Q1 EBITDA $1.5m (+118%). New partnerships: Spotify, Apple (video monetisation). New creator deals: Crooked Media, RedHanded, History Daily — 20m monthly downloads/views added.

"Record Q1 performance in 2026, with revenue of US$22.5 million, up 30% on Q1 2025 and adjusted EBITDA profit of US$1.5 million, up 118% on Q1 2025"

  1. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 22.4% (ex-onerous contracts) vs 21.5% FY24. Showcase gross margin higher than Premium — mix shift favourable. Operational leverage: opex only +8% despite revenue +10% and Adelicious integration. FY26 opex expected to stay relatively fixed = significant operational gearing.
  2. Capital: Net cash $4.2m at year end (vs $3.9m FY24). $3.4m overdraft available. No dividends. Strategic review process underway since October 2025 (potential sale, M&A, etc.). Share buyback: none.
  3. Qualitative tone: CEO: "Audioboom is striving to build the world's leading creator platform for audio and video, and we have made a great start in 2026." "Another record year" expected for FY26. Spotify and Apple partnerships for video monetisation highlighted as transformational.

EPS quality check: Adj EBITDA excludes onerous contract losses — which are now fully expired. FY26 adj EBITDA becomes a cleaner metric. No tax distortion (losses carried forward). Share-based payment charges excluded from adj EBITDA but are real dilution costs ($0.4m in FY25 vs $1.4m FY24 — declining).

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

FY26 outlook: "2026 is set to be another record year for Audioboom." Q1 FY26 $22.5m revenue (+30%), $1.5m EBITDA (+118%). Onerous contracts gone. Spotify/Apple partnerships. "Record year" language.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit "record year" language, Q1 revenue +30%, adj EBITDA +118%, onerous contract drag fully eliminated, Spotify/Apple platform partnerships as new monetisation vectors. Provisional points: +13.

Divergence check: FY25 revenue slightly missed consensus (−2.8%) but EBITDA beat consensus. Outlook strongly positive. Minor revenue miss offset by EBITDA beat and record Q1 FY26 data. No material divergence.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is the Q1 FY26 double: revenue $22.5m (+30% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA $1.5m (+118% YoY) — both records for a first quarter. In the context of FY25 full-year revenue of $80.4m, Q1 FY26 alone represents 28% of the prior full year — making the pre-RNS FY26 consensus of $82.7m almost certainly too low by 6–11%. The FY25 full-year delivered adjusted EBITDA $5.1m (+54% vs FY24 $3.4m), ahead of market expectations, on revenues of $80.4m (+10% YoY). The most strategically important development is the expiry of the final onerous contract on 31 December 2025 — removing a multi-year technical overhang and restoring the direct linkage between adjusted EBITDA and cash generation that makes the investment case structurally cleaner from FY26.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the H2 FY25 actual was $45.3m — +15.3% YoY vs FY24 H2 $39.3m (🟢 strong), confirmed from the full-year results. For FY26, the Q1 $22.5m run-rate combined with the Adelicious full-year contribution ($8m+ annualised) and the Showcase growth trajectory (currently 38% of group revenue, +31% YoY) supports a FY26 revenue range of $88–92m vs $82.7m pre-RNS consensus. The EBITDA upgrade resilience rests on operational leverage: opex grew only +8% in FY25 despite +10% revenue and a full Adelicious integration — confirming the platform is scaling with minimal incremental cost. The new Spotify and Apple video partnerships are not yet in consensus models and represent genuine optionality.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Cavendish (nominated adviser/broker) will raise FY26 revenue from $82.7m → $88–92m (+6–11%) and FY26 EBITDA from the Sharescope pre-RNS proxy → $6–8m (+22–63%). This drives adj EPS upgrades from approximately 21.5p → 26–32p. The target price of £13.00 (current 113% upside) is likely maintained — the Q1 data validates rather than materially upgrades the original bull case. The watch point is the strategic review initiated October 2025: any announcement of a sale process or strategic transaction would likely be the key re-rating catalyst for the share price (610p vs £13.00 TP). For the video monetisation story: the Spotify and Apple partnerships announced in Q1 FY26 are the key to addressing the RPM dilution from video content — if successful, they could drive a further upgrade cycle in H2 FY26.

🏁 Strongly positive — Q1 FY26 revenue +30% makes pre-RNS FY26 consensus too low; onerous contract overhang gone; upgrade to $88–92m revenue and $6–8m EBITDA likely; share price at 610p vs £13.00 TP; strategic review the key re-rating catalyst.

4. Hallam Land — record plot sales 3,957 plots sold (record, 2024: 2,661) = +48.7% YoY. Operating profit £32.9m (+35%, 2024: £24.3m). Average GP per plot £11,414 vs 5yr avg £10,187. Hallam Land was the standout performer.

"Hallam Land achieved record sales of 3,957 plots (2024: 2,661), increasing operating profit by 35% to £32.9m"

"Operating loss of £9.2m (2024: £1.9m profit), delivering 185 home completions (2024: 270)"

"Net debt5 at December 2025 was £108.0m (2024: £62.7m) with gearing at 25.7% (2024: 14.7%)"

7. FY26 guidance — below revised consensus "well positioned to meet full year market expectations" but company-compiled consensus has been revised to £20.2m PBT for FY26 vs £29.1m FY25 actual — a substantial decline. FY2 EPS consensus 13.1p vs FY1 16.2p.

"assuming the conflict in the Middle East is not prolonged"

However, the anticipated sales mix, with a higher percentage of promotion agreements and a lower share of freeholds, is likely to result in profit per plot being lower than our typical rate of £10,000."

9. SBH improvement signals Net private weekly reservation rate 0.43 (11 weeks to 15 March) vs 0.34 same period FY25 — showing improvement. FY26 output expected 200–220 homes. Still well below the 600 home medium-term target.

The 3yr avg EPS split of 62.6% is distorted.

Flag EPS tracking as UNTRACKABLE for Henry Boot due to extreme transaction timing variability in Hallam Land.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 actual implied: £307.0m − £126.4m = £180.6m vs 3yr avg H2 = (£197.0m + £179.6m + £222.3m)/3 = £199.6m → −9.5% → 🔴 weak (but reflects HBC exit reducing H2 construction revenue)

H2 EPS implied: 17.6p − 4.1p = 13.5p vs 3yr avg H2 = (0.6p + 4.7p + 14.3p)/3 = 6.5p → +107.7% — but this includes the HBC disposal gain. On continuing basis, H2 is more modest. 🟡 moderate on like-for-like continuing basis.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS +13.3% over full period — upgrades largely driven by Hallam Land record plots
  • TP −7.8% (335p → 309p) — small TP cut despite EPS upgrades, suggesting multiple compression and FY26 concerns
  • 4-week trend: FLAT
  • Divergence: EPS upgrades but TP cuts — consistent with market pricing in the FY26 earnings decline (consensus PBT £20.2m vs FY25 £29.1m = −31%). The market is looking through the FY25 beat to the lower FY26.

5. Structural Flags

  • FY26 PBT guidance £20.2m — significant H-o-H decline: From FY25 £29.1m to FY26 £20.2m consensus = −31%. This is driven by: lower Hallam Land profit/plot (promotion mix), SBH loss expected to narrow but not reverse, loss of HBC EBITDA contribution.
  • Stonebridge homes — serial underperformer: Three consecutive years of disappointing completions. Integration challenges are structural, not one-off.
  • Hallam Land acceleration opportunity: 19,580 plots in planning (up from 13,146) and 11,083 applications submitted in 2025. The pipeline for future plot sales is growing rapidly, which is the medium-term growth story.
  • Gearing elevated at 25.7%: Above preferred range. SBH land bank investment requires unwinding through land sales — timing risk.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 consensus PBT cut to £20.2m — the key broker focus Brokers wrote to £29.0m for FY26 PBT (Sharescope FY2 shows £24.9m). The company-compiled consensus is £20.2m — below even the Sharescope FY2 figure. The language "assumes the conflict in the Middle East is not prolonged" adds a further conditional qualifier. Brokers will cut FY26 estimates further if needed to align with the company's own consensus figure.

#2 Driver — Hallam Land record performance + accelerating consented pipeline The record 3,957 plot sales and 19,580 plots in planning is the most genuinely positive structural signal. The medium-term potential (targeting 3,500 plots p.a.) appears more achievable than ever, with planning system reforms providing tailwinds. But this is FY27+ story, not FY26.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: Sharescope shows FY2 = 13.1p; this becomes FY1 and likely needs to be cut to ~11–12p to align with £20.2m PBT guidance.
  • Revenue: FY2 consensus £273.9m becomes FY1; confirms the significant revenue decline expected.
  • TP: Currently 309p; likely to hold or trim to 290–310p range.

Key risk: SBH — the third consecutive year of underperformance at the housebuilding division. CEO commentary is cautious: the H2 is "inherently seasonality of housebuilding" and "heavily weighted towards the second half." Middle East risk explicitly conditions the FY26 outlook.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 38/100 · Confidence: 32–44 · No FX adjustment · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

ComponentPts
🟢 Hallam Land record 3,957 plot sales — +48.7% YoY, structural strength+12
🟢 FY25 PBT £29.1m — exactly in line with £29.2m consensus+8
🟢 19,580 plots in planning — future Hallam Land pipeline building+7
🟢 SBH reservation rate improving (0.43 vs 0.34 prior year)+4
🟡 Revenue tracking −1.6pp — borderline CAUTION−3
🟡 EPS H1 tracking UNTRACKABLE (extreme timing variability)−2
🔴 FY26 consensus PBT only £20.2m — −31% decline from FY25−14
🔴 SBH −185 completions vs 240–250 target — serial underperformance−8
🔴 Net debt £108m — above preferred range, gearing 25.7%−6
🔴 TP cut −7.8% despite EPS upgrades — multiple compression−4
🔴 Middle East risk conditions FY26 guidance−3
🔴 HBC disposal eliminates ~£6.7m construction contribution−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: BOOT's FY25 results came in exactly in-line with consensus — PBT of £29.1m vs £29.2m company-compiled consensus — with the delivery entirely underpinned by Hallam Land achieving a record 3,957 plot sales (+48.7%) and operating profit of £32.9m (+35%). EPS on a basic continuing-plus-discontinued basis was 17.6p, beating the FY1 consensus of 16.2p by 8.6% (including the HBC disposal gain). The definitive positive is the planning pipeline: with 19,580 plots in the planning system (up from 13,146) and continued NPPF tailwinds, Hallam Land's medium-term capacity to sustain 3,500+ plot sales per annum is building credibility.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience is structurally weak for FY26. The company-compiled consensus of £20.2m FY26 PBT — 31% below FY25 — reflects: (1) Hallam Land profit/plot expected below £10,000 due to promotion mix; (2) SBH loss expected to narrow but remain; (3) HBC contribution absent; and (4) Middle East risk conditioning all guidance. SBH's reservation rate improvement (0.43 vs 0.34 prior year) is the only near-term positive signal, but even guiding 200–220 completions in FY26 is below the 240–250 target that itself was below the 600 medium-term ambition. The gearing at 25.7% (above the preferred 10–20%) creates financial constraint on investment pace.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS (rolling to FY26) likely to be revised DOWN from the current FY2 consensus of 13.1p toward 11–12p to align with the £20.2m PBT guidance. Revenue consensus for FY26 at £273.9m is consistent with the guidance language. TP may trim from 309p toward 285–300p. The bull case is the Hallam Land pipeline (medium-term, FY27+) and the eventual SBH recovery — but these are 1–3 year stories, not FY26. 🏁 Verdict: FY25 in-line delivery masks a significant FY26 earnings step-down; brokers need to cut FY26 estimates, and the SBH serial underperformance undermines the growth thesis. Score 38/100.

"The Group remains in active discussions with several potential exciting and scalable restaurant brand acquisition targets."

The LFL trend is encouraging but insufficient to overcome April cost headwinds without quantification. TP of 1.1p will likely be maintained — implying 300% upside at current 0.275p, which itself reflects the speculative optionality value of the acquisition strategy rather than current earnings power. The score is capped at 38 by the combination of no upgrade momentum, structural lease leverage, NLW headwinds, and the fact that this is essentially a turnaround story in early innings. 🏁 Neutral — in-line delivery confirmed, LFL improving, but cost headwinds and thin margins prevent upgrade catalyst.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Gamma's RNS discloses Germany revenue of £122.9m out of £645.8m total = 19.1% EUR exposure. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Skip — no FX penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 94.3p · Revenue £645.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 93.8p · Revenue £665.5m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +1.7% (92.7p → 94.3p) over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT). Revenue net change: −1.9% (£657.8m → £645.8m). Consensus TP declined from £17.27 to £14.83 over the period — steady downgrade of target prices with no upgrades.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.8% of FY = £315.1m · EPS 49.8% of FY = 46.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £282.5m · EPS 42.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode — FY actual vs prior FY): Revenue: £645.8m actual vs £579.4m prior = +11.4% FY YoY. H2 implied: £645.8m − £316.6m (current H1 actual) = £329.2m vs prior H2 £296.9m = +10.8% H2 YoY. EPS: FY actual 94.5p vs prior FY 85.1p = +11.1% FY YoY. H2 implied: 94.5p − 47.9p = 46.6p vs prior H2 42.6p = +9.4% H2 YoY.
  • FX: N/A — EUR exposure ~19%, below 30% threshold.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual Revenue £645.8m, +11% YoY (2024: £579.4m). vs FY1 consensus £645.8m = exact in-line (0% beat/miss).

"Revenue increased by 11% to £645.8m (2024: £579.4m)"

2. EPS — FY adjusted Adjusted EPS (fully diluted) 94.5p, +11% YoY (2024: 85.1p). vs FY1 consensus 94.3p = +0.2p beat (+0.2%).

"Adjusted EPS (fully diluted) increased by 11% from 85.1p to 94.5p."

3. Adjusted EBITDA £141.7m, +13% YoY (2024: £125.5m). vs FY1 consensus £141.3m = +£0.4m beat (+0.3%). Management confirms "within consensus range".

"Adjusted EBITDA increased by 13%; Adjusted EPS (fully diluted) increased by 11%."

4. FY 2026 guidance Board expects FY 2026 financial performance to be in line with market expectations, Adjusted EBITDA consensus range £138.0m–£144.6m and Adjusted EPS 90.0p–96.6p. No explicit upgrade signal; confirms consensus but notably guidance is flat-to-slightly-below FY25 actuals at midpoint.

"The Board expects FY 2026 financial performance to be in line with market expectations, with Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS (fully diluted) within the consensus range."

5. Germany — key growth driver Gamma Germany revenue +103% to £110.2m, gross profit +197% to £78.4m. Organic GP growth 11% constant currency. Cloud seats reached ~600k.

"Gamma Germany increased gross profit by 197% to £78.4m (2024: £26.4m), led by our acquisitions of Placetel in September 2024 and Starface in February 2025."

6. UK SME — headwinds Gross profit declined 3% to £146.5m. PSTN switch-off headwind of ~£4m in FY25, further ~£4m expected in FY26. Ethernet pricing pressure reduced Enterprise GP by ~£2m in FY25, further ~£3m impact expected in FY26.

"We estimate that gross profit will be further reduced by a similar amount in FY 2026, with the full-year financial impact of FY 2026 migrations expected to be felt until the end of FY 2027."

7. Gross margin Gross margin expanded to 54% (2024: 52%), driven by higher-margin German acquisitions.

"Gross Margin: 54% (2024: 52%)"

8. Cash returns / capital allocation £64m returned to shareholders in FY25. FY26+FY27 buybacks of up to £85m announced (£42.5m per year), plus dividend fixed at FY25 levels for two years (22.2p/share). Total ~£125m aggregate return over two years.

"We intend to continue to return substantial amounts of cash to shareholders through FY 2026 and FY 2027, balancing investment in organic growth with enhanced cash returns."

9. Net debt Net debt of £9.3m at year-end (2024: net cash £153.7m). Driven by Starface acquisition (£152.2m) and buybacks. RCF £97m undrawn.

10. Restructuring savings UK restructuring completed in H2 2025, delivering £7m p.a. savings from FY26.

"Restructuring programme…will deliver annual operating expense savings of £7m across both Gamma Business and Gamma Enterprise from FY 2026."

11. CFO departure Bill Castell leaving 31 March 2026; Damien Maltarp joining as CFO by September 2026 latest. Leadership gap in near term.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Full-Year YoY Growth Table

FY23 (2y ago)521.7+7.9%75.1+4.6%

*FY25e = actual RNS reported figures (coincide exactly with FY1 consensus).

Revenue growth trajectory: +7.9% → +11.1% → +11.4% → 🟢 Accelerating (steady acceleration over three years, though incremental).

EPS growth trajectory: +4.6% → +13.3% → +11.1% → 🟢 Steady (high growth sustained; slight deceleration in rate is within normal variance).

1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

FY22 H1234.7—35.6—

FY23 H1256.2+9.2%37.5+5.3%
