FY25 H1316.6+12.1%47.9+12.7%
FY25 H2*329.2+10.8%46.6+9.4%

*FY25 H2 derived: Rev = £645.8m − £316.6m = £329.2m; EPS = 94.5p − 47.9p = 46.6p

Revenue trajectory: +10.3% → +11.8% → +12.1% (H1s accelerating); H2s: +6.2% → +11.8% → +10.8% → 🟢 Steady

EPS trajectory: H2s: +3.9% → +13.3% → +9.4% → 🟡 Volatile (big jump then deceleration in H2, though H1 trend steadier)

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline (pre-FY mode — tracking against FY1 consensus)

FY1 consensus at snapshot = £645.8m revenue / 94.3p EPS.

  • Revenue baseline: 48.8% × £645.8m = £315.2m. H1 actual £316.6m ÷ £645.8m = 49.0% vs baseline 48.8% → deviation = 🟢 [+0.2pp] → 🟡 IN LINE
  • EPS baseline: 49.8% × 94.3p = 46.9p. H1 actual 47.9p ÷ 94.3p = 50.8% vs baseline 49.8% → deviation = 🟢 [+1.0pp] → 🟡 IN LINE

Buy triggers: Rev > baseline × 1.015 = £320.0m: H1 actual £316.6m → 🔴 ✗ · EPS > 46.9p × 1.015 = 47.6p: H1 actual 47.9p → 🟢 ✓

H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 94.3p − 47.9p actual H1 = 46.4p required H2 vs historical H2 avg ~38.8p (3yr avg H2: (36.2+37.6+42.6)/3). Burden HIGHER than historical H2 average — but H2 actual came in at 46.6p, essentially exactly meeting the full-year number. In retrospect the burden was met.

Historical hit rate: In 2 of 3 years, positive H1 deviation preceded a FY beat (FY23 and FY24 H1 deviations were positive and full-year results came in at/above).

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode)

H2 actual: Revenue £329.2m vs 3yr avg H2 = (£249.9m + £265.5m + £296.9m)/3 = £270.8m → +21.6% above historical H2 average → 🟢 strong

H2 EPS: 46.6p vs 3yr avg H2 = (36.2+37.6+42.6)/3 = 38.8p → +20.1% above historical → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: +1.7% net change over full period (92.7p to 94.3p).
  • Revenue: −1.9% net change (£657.8m to £645.8m).
  • Target price: declined steadily from £17.27 to £14.83 — a -14.1% TP cut over the period.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STEADY (flat for ~3 months)
  • Divergence: EPS estimates held or crept up slightly while TP was cut significantly — suggests brokers repriced the growth multiple downward while not cutting numbers materially. The in-line result does not reverse the TP trajectory; FY26 guidance "in line with consensus" rather than ahead removes the catalyst for TP recovery.

5. Structural Flags

  • PSTN headwind (structural but temporary): ~£4m GP drag per year expected through end of 2027. Not a permanent structural change but a multi-year drag.
  • German margin dilution: Starface/Placetel have higher GP margins but also higher opex, meaning EBITDA margin growth is constrained despite GP expansion. "They structurally have higher operating expenses."
  • Interest income reversal: Move from net cash £153.7m to net debt £9.3m eliminates ~£7m annual interest income tailwind vs FY24.
  • CFO transition: Gap between Castell departure (31 March 2026) and new CFO arrival (by September 2026) = 6-month leadership gap.
  • FY26 guidance at midpoint below FY25: Consensus EBITDA midpoint £141.3m vs FY25 actual £141.7m implies flat-to-slight decline. EPS midpoint ~93.3p vs 94.5p actual = slight decline. This is a structural de-rating signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 guidance "in line" (not ahead) The single most influential broker note item will be that FY26 guidance is explicitly "within the consensus range" at the exact midpoint, with consensus EPS actually below FY25 actuals (93.3p midpoint vs 94.5p). After a year of 11% EPS growth, guidance for flat-to-down FY26 EPS is the dominant signal. Brokers expecting a re-acceleration narrative will be disappointed. This is the #1 driver of broker tone.

#2 Driver — FY25 in-line delivery + Germany strength FY25 came in spot on — revenue and EBITDA within 0.3% of consensus. Germany's 197% GP growth shows the acquisition thesis is working. This is a positive "beat and confirm" on FY25 but since the bar was exactly met, upgrade risk from this alone is limited. It prevents downgrades on the FY25 number but doesn't catalyse upgrades.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (now FY26) revenue: consensus already at £665.5m; guidance language "in line" means estimates hold; possible minor downside 0–2% if PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly modelled.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 94.3p (pre-RNS for FY25, now rolling to FY26 at ~93.8p); FY26 guidance "in line with consensus range" of 90.0p–96.6p confirms midpoint ~93.3p — no revision needed, hold.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: £93.8p consensus; likely held or very modest trim as PSTN headwinds expected to resolve by end 2027.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers are likely to hold target prices or trim marginally (−5% range) given the steady TP decline from £17.27 to £14.83 already underway. Current upside to £14.83 from 866p is +71%. Despite high numerical upside, the TP drift lower suggests brokers are unwilling to call a recovery catalyst. No recommendation change likely; hold with cautious tone dominates.

Conservative guidance read-through: The RNS says "within the consensus range" — not "comfortable with" or "not less than." This is the most neutral guidance language possible, essentially confirming midpoint expectations. It does not trigger an upgrade cycle; if anything it confirms flat EPS growth for the year ahead, removing the momentum-based bull case.

Key risk: The single largest counter-argument is the multiple compression risk from flat FY26 EPS at the same time as the market is repricing growth stocks. With EPS guidance flat-to-slightly-down and ongoing TP cuts, there is no earnings growth catalyst to arrest de-rating. "We estimate that gross profit will be further reduced by a similar amount in FY 2026." — the PSTN and ethernet headwinds are explicitly quantified and recurring.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 57/100 · Confidence: 52–62 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 FY25 revenue in-line with consensus+8
🟢 Adjusted EPS +11% YoY, +0.2p beat vs consensus+8
🟢 Germany GP +197%, thesis working+8
🟢 £7m annual UK opex savings from restructuring from FY26+5
🟢 £125m capital return commitment (buybacks + fixed dividend)+5
🟢 Adjusted EBITDA +13%, at top of consensus range+4
🟡 H1 seasonal tracking IN LINE — no material deviation−2
🟡 EPS broker momentum FLAT over 10 weeks−2
🔴 FY26 guidance "in line with consensus" — no upgrade trigger−8
🔴 FY26 EPS guidance midpoint ~93.3p vs 94.5p actual — flat/down−7
🔴 Consensus TP cut −14% over review period (£17.27→£14.83)−5
🔴 Net income from interest reverses ~£7m headwind in FY26−3
🔴 CFO transition gap (6 months) — governance uncertainty−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: GAMA delivered FY25 results that were essentially spot on consensus — revenue of £645.8m (+11%, exactly matching FY1 forecast) and adjusted EPS of 94.5p (+11%, a 0.2p beat). Adjusted EBITDA of £141.7m (+13%) landed at the top of the £138–£144.6m consensus range. The definitive catalyst is Germany: Gamma Germany gross profit surged 197% to £78.4m, transforming the group's earnings mix and validating the Starface/Placetel acquisition thesis. This is an unambiguously clean delivery — no misses, no hidden charges, audited results with an unqualified opinion.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £329.2m and EPS of 46.6p are both roughly 20% above the three-year historical H2 average, confirming that the German contribution is genuinely structural rather than a one-off. "Adjusted basic earnings per share 7.50p (2024: 8.18p) (8.3%)"

5. Adjusted EBITDA £12.4m (−11.4%, 2024: £14.0m). vs FY1 EBITDA consensus £12.7m = −£0.3m miss (−2.4%).

"Adjusted EBITDA £12.4m (2024: £14.0m) (11.4%)"

6. Exceptional items — significant one-offs £2.4m total exceptional charges: £1.4m Watlington closure costs, £0.4m Hathern Terra Cotta wind-down, £0.6m other restructuring. These reduce statutory profit to £4.3m (reported PBT vs adj PBT of £8.1m gap = £3.8m including amortisation and exceptionals).

"Exceptional items of £2.4 million. These relate to £1.4m of costs incurred due to the closure of our Watlington operation including all wind-down operating costs, redundancy costs, dilapidation and decommissioning and non-repeating site overheads."

7. Key operational driver: Carlton shutdown delay Extended Carlton shutdown by two weeks in Q1 2025 cost ~3 million manufacturing units — not recovered in H2. A one-off operational drag on FY25 profits.

"The extended shutdown at Carlton by two-weeks and the subsequent commissioning period, combined to reduce our manufacturing volumes by three million units in the year at this key site"

8. Floren — Belgium market severely challenged Floren despatches and revenue declined ~20%. Belgium housing ~40% below 2022 peak. Floren production paused twice (Q1 and Q3). Management temporarily stopped production twice.

"Our Floren brand was significantly impacted by the domestic macro market which was very challenging throughout the year. The Belgium building permits granted in 2025 declined again during the year and the broader market remains over a third below the levels from 2022."

9. UK market — low single digit volume growth, competitive pricing UK brick despatch volumes +low single digit, in line with management expectations. Sector production ahead of despatch = competitive pricing environment. Sector inventory at ~550m bricks (above 5yr average). Market pricing "highly competitive throughout the year."

10. Dividend — maintained at 4.60p Final dividend 3.00p, total 4.60p (2024: 4.60p). Yield at 75p = 6.1%. Maintained despite earnings decline.

"Final dividend per share proposed of 3.00p resulting in full year dividend of 4.60p (in line with 2024)"

11. FY26 outlook — confident growth statement "The Directors are confident that the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025." Order intake ahead of manufacturing capacity at start of 2026 but "confidence and predictability from our order intake levels have been diluted."

"Whilst these headwinds create a challenging trading environment, the Directors are confident that the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025."

12. CFO departure Rachel Warren resigned immediately; Ryan Mahoney (CEO) assumes CFO responsibilities interim. Warren had only joined in September 2025.

13. Balance sheet — moved to net debt Net debt £0.7m (2024: net cash £6.0m). £20m borrowing facility in place until Aug 2028.

5. Structural Flags

  • Carlton production delay (one-off): The two-week extended shutdown and commissioning delay cost ~3m units manufacturing output, suppressing FY25 EBITDA. This is non-recurring and will normalise in FY26.
  • Watlington closure (one-off): £1.4m exceptional cost but removes a cash-consuming leasehold. FY26 benefits from eliminated overheads.

  • CFO transition: Warren resigned after only ~6 months. Mahoney taking CFO responsibilities again. Second CFO change in under 12 months creates governance concern.
  • Mineral reserves extension at Floren: New exhaust scrubber system enabled change in input materials, significantly extending Floren's mineral reserves. Long-term structural positive.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Adjusted EPS 7.50p beats consensus 6.7p by +12% The dominant broker note item will be the EPS beat — consensus had been progressively cut to 6.7p and the actual came in at 7.50p, largely due to a low effective tax rate (15.9% vs 25% normalised). Brokers will debate whether to adjust for the tax benefit (~1.3p) or use the headline figure. Either way, FY25 adj EPS of 7.50p is above prior consensus 6.7p, arresting the downgrade cycle.

#2 Driver — FY26 growth guidance and one-off cost normalisation Management explicitly states "confident the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025." The Carlton production delay was one-off, and Watlington closure removes ongoing overhead. Floren is still challenged but the Belgium market commentary ("70,000 homes/year target") provides a medium-term recovery story. FY26 consensus will be revised upward from current 8.4p.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: consensus 8.4p pre-results; given 7.50p FY25 base and "growth" guidance, FY26 EPS likely held or modestly upgraded to 8.0–9.0p range. The tax rate normalises to ~25% in FY26, so operating profit growth needs to be substantial to maintain EPS vs FY25's low-tax number.
  • FY1 revenue: consensus £69.0m (matching FY25 actual); guidance for growth implies £70–73m range in FY26.
  • TP: Currently 135p; likely to hold or marginally move given the mixed picture. At 75p, stock at 56% discount to TP.

Conservative guidance: "Confident the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025" — this is modestly positive but not aggressive. Order intake ahead of capacity is a positive leading indicator, but "predictability from order intake diluted" tempers enthusiasm.

Key risk: The tax benefit of 15.9% effective rate is non-recurring. At 25% normalised rate, FY25 adj profit after tax would have been: adj PBT £8.1m × 75% = £6.1m vs £6.8m actual. FY26 EPS will face a ~1.3p headwind from tax normalisation alone. Brokers will explicitly model this. Additionally the CFO departure is the second in under 12 months — governance concern. "Rachel Warren is stepping down from the Group Board with immediate effect due to personal reasons"

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — The EPS beat is real but tax-distorted, Floren remains challenged, and the CFO instability adds uncertainty.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Raw score: 40/100 · FX adjustment: −8 pts → Final score: 32/100 · Confidence: 24–39 (widened ±5pp for missing EUR prior avg rate) · 🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~33% EUR (Floren) · GBP headwind · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

🔴 Net debt £0.7m (from net cash £6.0m) — balance sheet weakening−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: MBH delivered FY25 results that were better than the market feared on EPS but not better in quality terms. Adjusted EPS of 7.50p beat the 6.7p consensus by 12%, but this was substantially driven by a 15.9% effective tax rate (vs 25% normalised) due to prior-year tax credits — stripping this out, underlying EPS was closer to 6.1p. Revenue of £68.9m missed £69.0m consensus marginally and declined 1.7% YoY. The primary operational driver of underperformance was a two-week extended Carlton shutdown in Q1 (costing ~3m manufacturing units) and Floren Belgium revenue declining ~20% as housing activity in Belgium remained ~40% below 2022 peak. Adjusted EBITDA of £12.4m was 2.4% below the £12.7m consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £33.1m is 4.9% below the three-year H2 average (borderline flat classification), reflecting the ongoing market malaise. H2 implied adj EPS of ~4.2p is roughly 19% below the three-year H2 average, though this is distorted by the tax benefit falling in the year. The seasonal tracking deviation was only −0.2pp on EPS and +0.4pp on revenue — IN LINE rather than signalling any directional breakout. The upgrade resilience rests on: (1) Carlton production delay is non-recurring; (2) Watlington closure removes cash-consuming overhead; (3) management's explicit "growth in 2026" statement. However, the FX headwind (GBP stronger vs EUR) is a tangible, ongoing drag on Floren's GBP-reported contribution that is absent from historical baselines. The CFO transition risk is the most unpredictable variable.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus of 8.4p should be held or modestly trimmed to 7.5–8.5p range once brokers normalise the tax rate — the 7.50p FY25 EPS at a 15.9% tax rate becomes approximately 6.1p on a like-for-like 25% tax basis, making "growth in 2026" against a normalised base more demanding than the headline implies. TP of 135p likely maintained or cut marginally to 125–130p. At 75p, there is 73% upside to TP on paper but the low price reflects sustained earnings disappointments and a challenging European market backdrop. The main watch point is Belgium housing recovery timing and whether the FX headwind persists. 🏁 Verdict: EPS beat is tax-distorted; underlying performance continues to disappoint against pre-2022 peak; Floren structural headwind + CFO instability + FX drag make this a cautious hold. FX-adjusted score 32/100.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (FY26 ending 28 February 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Bytes Technology Group is a UK/Ireland IT software business. Revenues predominantly GBP. Skip — no FX threshold breach.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results / full-year trading update for FY26 (year ended 28 February 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 21.8p · Revenue £223.6m (note: this is Bytes' "gross profit" equivalent — Bytes reports Revenue as gross profit/net revenue rather than billings)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 22.7p · Revenue £242.7m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change −11.4% (24.6p → 21.8p) — persistent downgrades driven by Microsoft incentive changes. Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (22.7→21.9→21.9→21.8p — slowly declining). TP cut from 604p to 459p (−24.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.6% of FY = £113.1m · EPS 45.3% of FY = 9.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £108.1m · EPS 11.6p (Sharescope current H1 = FY26 H1 = 6mo to Aug 2025)
  • Implied H2 YoY: H2 implied = £223.6m − £108.1m = £115.5m vs prior H2 (FY25 H2): FY25 total = £105.5m+£111.7m = £217.2m implied; H2 = £111.7m → H2 YoY £115.5m vs £111.7m = +3.4%. EPS H2: 21.8p − 11.6p = 10.2p vs prior H2 EPS (FY25 H2 = 24.2p... wait Sharescope shows "1y ago H1/H2 = 12.2/24.2" which looks too high).
  • Note: Sharescope "1y ago H2 = 24.2p" appears to include the R&D/accounting one-off. Per the RNS the FY26 gross profit guidance is c.£167m and operating profit c.£62m. These are the operative figures.
  • FX: N/A

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Trading Update (year ended 28 February 2026) — not full results; full results on 12 May 2026

1. Gross profit — in line with October guidance "gross profit of c.£167m" — vs prior year FY25 gross profit. Note: Bytes' Sharescope Revenue consensus £223.6m = gross profit in Bytes' terminology. Actual c.£167m vs consensus £223.6m — this appears to be a substantial miss. However the consensus likely includes billings not gross profit. Need to reconcile: Bytes' Revenue (gross profit) prior year = £108.1m (H1) + £111.7m (H2) = £219.8m — close to the £223.6m consensus. Actual £167m vs £223.6m = −25.3% miss? This can't be right.

Re-reading: The RNS says "double-digit gross invoiced income growth, gross profit of c.£167m and operating profit of c.£62m." The £167m is gross profit. The Sharescope Revenue consensus £223.6m is almost certainly gross invoiced income (total billings/revenue), not gross profit. Bytes reports both. Consensus "revenue" in Sharescope = gross invoiced income (billings). So: gross profit actual c.£167m — needs comparison to consensus gross profit separately from revenue.

From prior year context: FY25 gross profit was £105.5m + £111.7m = £217.2m? No — that's the Sharescope H1/H2 revenue data which for Bytes IS gross profit (net revenue). So actual FY26 gross profit c.£167m vs FY25 gross profit (which = revenue £217.2m approx) = a significant decline? This implies FY26 gross profit DECLINED vs FY25.

The RNS says "double-digit gross invoiced income growth" — so billings grew. But gross profit c.£167m — what was FY25 gross profit? From Sharescope H1 prior = £108.1m (H1 FY26 actual) and FY25 H2 = £111.7m → FY25 total revenue/gross profit = c.£219.8m. So FY26 £167m vs FY25 £219.8m = −24% gross profit decline?

Wait — I need to reconsider the Sharescope data interpretation. The "Current H1" of £108.1m and "1y ago H1/H2 of £105.5m/£111.7m" in Sharescope likely refer to Bytes' own gross profit metric. So FY25 gross profit = £105.5m + £111.7m = £217.2m and FY26 projected £167m would be a −24% decline. But this contradicts the "double-digit gross invoiced income growth" language.

The resolution is: Bytes' "Revenue" in Sharescope = gross invoiced income (billings/revenue per IFRS 15), not the gross profit. So FY1 consensus Revenue £223.6m = gross invoiced income. And gross profit (what matters for earnings) = c.£167m per RNS.

From FY25 reported gross profit (from FY25 annual results): Bytes H1 FY26 = gross profit per their own metric; and "1y ago H1/H2 = 12.2/24.2" are EPS, not revenue. The prior year (FY25) gross profit would be disclosed in the FY25 annual — but from the RNS text: "FY26 was impacted by changes to Microsoft enterprise incentives and the phasing effects of the private sector sales realignment." This implies FY26 gross profit is LOWER than FY25. The "c.£167m" is below what the market was expecting.

Given prior period context and the explicit statement that FY26 was "in line with the outlook provided in October 2025" — the October trading update had already guided to this lower level. So brokers will have already incorporated c.£167m gross profit into their estimates. The Sharescope EPS consensus of 21.8p reflects the October guidance, not the original 24.6p.

"For FY26, BTG delivered results in line with the outlook provided in October 2025 with double-digit gross invoiced income growth, gross profit of c.£167m and operating profit of c.£62m."

2. Operating profit — in line c.£62m — vs FY1 consensus operating profit implied from EPS. Previous FY25 operating profit would be ~£77m (based on prior EPS). So FY26 c.£62m represents a significant decline.

3. Cash conversion — strong "Cash conversion exceeded 100%, with a year-end cash balance of over £98m." Excellent liquidity position.

4. H2 recovery — "performance strengthened in the second half" H2 (Sep 2025–Feb 2026) gross profit grew c.6% YoY against a "strong comparator" — the inflection point after the Microsoft incentive changes stabilised.

"Encouragingly, performance strengthened in the second half, with gross profit growing c.6% year-on-year in January and February 2026 against a strong comparator."

5. FY27 guidance — return to growth "high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in gross profit" in FY27 (March 2026–Feb 2027). Operating profit "broadly flat" due to c.£4.5m of cost normalisation. So FY27 gross profit ~£182–185m and operating profit ~£62m.

"For FY27, we expect high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in gross profit, with operating profit broadly flat as the Group absorbs c.£4.5m of cost normalisation"

6. Go-to-market realignment from July 2026 Bytes Software Services → private sector; Phoenix Software → public sector. Structural clarity improving. "From July 2026, the Group will further align its go-to-market approach."

Wait, there is clear confusion in the Sharescope data. The "1y ago H1/H2 = 12.2/24.2" EPS shows a massive H2 EPS — likely a one-off (tax credits, buybacks). Let me use what the company discloses: FY26 (ending Feb 2026) = gross profit c.£167m, operating profit c.£62m. FY27 guidance: gross profit £182–188m (+8–12%), operating profit ~£62m.

The gross profit decline from what appears to be FY25 (ending Feb 2025) gross profit. From the RNS context: "FY26 was impacted by changes to Microsoft enterprise incentives and the phasing effects of the private sector sales realignment." The decline was flagged in October 2025 revised guidance.

Gross profit trajectory: +12.1% (FY24→25) → +4.9% (FY25→26 context) → −23.1% (FY26→27 implied) — this trajectory is 🔴 Decelerating severely.

But FY27 guidance reverses this: +8–12% gross profit growth from FY26 base. So the FY26 year is the trough.

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline and Tracking Deviation (pre-FY mode)

Since this is a FY trading update (not H1 results for next year), the H1 tracking is against FY26 actuals.

H1 FY26 actual = £108.1m (current H1 Sharescope). FY26 actual gross profit c.£167m → H1 represents 64.7% of FY total. vs baseline 50.6% → deviation = 🟢 [+14.1pp] — but this is the FY that just ended, not a forward signal.

For forward H1 FY27 tracking: UNTRACKABLE — no H1 FY27 actuals yet.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode)

H2 FY26 implied = £167m − £108.1m = £58.9m vs H2 FY25 £98.3m → −40.1% — but this reflects the known Microsoft incentive headwind. H2 recovery signal: January/February 2026 showed c.6% gross profit growth YoY — this is the forward indicator for FY27 H1.

For FY27 implied H2: Using FY27 guidance of £182–188m gross profit and assuming similar H1 split: H2 FY27 implied ~£90m vs H2 FY26 £58.9m = +52.7% — but this is from a depressed H2 FY26 base.

🟢 strong H2 FY27 recovery implied by guidance

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: −11.4% over full period — consistent downgrade cycle driven by Microsoft changes
  • TP: −24.0% (604p → 459p) — significant broker confidence reduction
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (21.9p → 21.8p — small but directionally negative)
  • Divergence: The declining EPS and TP contrast with the positive recovery narrative in FY27 guidance. The market (300p) vs TP (459p) gap = 53% upside — but the TP has been falling.

5. Structural Flags

  • Microsoft incentive changes — one-time reset completed: The FY26 impact is now fully crystallised. FY27 grows from the new lower base. The c.6% H2 FY26 growth in gross profit signals the bottom has been reached.
  • Operating profit flat in FY27 despite gross profit growth: £4.5m cost normalisation (higher tech costs, return to normal bonus levels) absorbs the gross profit recovery. This limits EPS recovery in FY27.
  • Go-to-market restructuring risk: The July 2026 private/public sector split creates execution risk during transition.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 in line with October guidance — no surprise (positive or negative) Results exactly match the October 2025 pre-announced guidance. No new information on FY26 fundamentals. The broker focus is entirely on FY27: "high single-digit to low double-digit gross profit growth" is the key number.

#2 Driver — FY27 gross profit recovery (+8–12%) but operating profit flat The £4.5m cost normalisation in FY27 means gross profit growth does NOT flow through to operating profit. This constrains EPS recovery — FY27 EPS likely similar to FY26 (~21–23p). Brokers will not significantly upgrade FY27 EPS despite the top-line recovery.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY27) EPS: consensus 22.7p — likely maintained or very minor uplift (0–3%) given operating profit flat guidance.
  • FY1 gross profit: FY2 consensus £242.7m likely maintained (consistent with +8–12% guidance on £167m base = £180–188m — FY2 consensus appears to be FY27 as a higher base).
  • TP: Currently 459p; likely to be maintained. Some recovery from 300p stock price toward 400–450p as the trough is confirmed.

Key risk: The "broadly flat operating profit" for FY27 despite gross profit recovery is the critical constraint. And the go-to-market restructuring in July 2026 introduces execution uncertainty.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 48/100 · Confidence: 42–54 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

Para 1 — Headline numbers: BYIT's FY26 trading update confirms results "in line with the outlook provided in October 2025" — gross profit c.£167m and operating profit c.£62m, both in line with pre-announced guidance. There is no new negative or positive surprise vs the October update. The #1 catalyst for brokers is the H2 FY26 confirmation: gross profit grew c.6% YoY in January and February 2026 against a strong comparator — signalling the Microsoft incentive change headwind has been absorbed and the business is re-inflecting.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 FY26 recovery (£58.9m implied gross profit) was weak in absolute terms (−40% vs FY25 H2), entirely explained by the known Microsoft changes. The upgrade resilience is built on FY27 guidance: high single-digit to low double-digit gross profit growth implies £182–188m gross profit in FY27 — a meaningful recovery from the £167m trough. However, operating profit is guided "broadly flat" in FY27 at ~£62m as c.£4.5m of cost normalisation offsets the gross profit recovery. This means the EPS recovery is limited to ~2p uplift at best in FY27 — insufficient to drive a significant re-rating.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY27 EPS consensus of 22.7p should be maintained with minor variation (±5%). TP at 459p likely to hold — the trough confirmation provides a floor argument but the flat operating profit guidance prevents upgrades. Stock at 300p (−35% vs TP) represents a mean-reversion opportunity for patient investors, but catalysts are limited until the go-to-market restructuring lands in July 2026 and the full-year results in May 2026 provide complete transparency. The main watch point is whether the Bytes/Phoenix split drives incremental new client wins in the private sector (AI, cloud, security) — management is optimistic on customers moving from AI experimentation to deployment. 🏁 Verdict: Trough confirmed but recovery constrained by cost normalisation; neutral hold pending full-year results and FY27 H1 evidence of recovery. scorecards.analysisTitle: CBG · Close Brothers Group PLC · 17 Mar 2026
scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (six months ended 31 January 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Close Brothers is a UK specialist banking group. Revenue is overwhelmingly GBP-denominated (domestic UK lending). No single non-GBP currency approaches 30% of revenues. No FX Rule 1 penalty applies.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 43.6p, Revenue n/a (banking model, not tracked). FY2 consensus: EPS 61.1p.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period = −39.6% (from 72.2p to 43.6p). A sustained cutting cycle throughout the period driven by escalating motor finance provisions. Last-4-week trend: FLAT — the cutting cycle has plateaued at 43.6p since late January. Momentum classification: bottomed / dormant.
  • 3-year average H1 % of FY (EPS): 41.9% (3yr avg). Revenue H1 avg: n/a (no revenue consensus data).
  • H1 actual EPS: Adjusted basic EPS from continuing operations = 27.1p. H1 tracking vs seasonal norm: 27.1p / 43.6p FY1 cns = 62.2% vs 3yr avg 41.9% → deviation = +20.3pp → 🟢 STRONG BUY SIGNAL.
  • Implied H2 from consensus: FY1 43.6p − H1 27.1p = 16.5p implied H2. This would require H2 adj EPS to fall −48.8% vs H2 FY25 (32.2p) — an implausibly severe collapse not supported by trading commentary. FY consensus is materially too low.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Adjusted operating profit H1 FY26: £65.2m vs H1 FY25 £80.5m = −19.2% YoY. Driven by reduced income (lower loan book) partly offset by lower impairment charges.
    "Adjusted operating profit decreased 19% to £65.2 million (H1 2025: £80.5 million), driven by reduced operating income, partly offset by lower impairment losses."
  2. Adjusted basic EPS H1 FY26: 27.1p (H1 FY25: 33.8p). Vs FY1 consensus H1 implied (43.6p × 41.9% = 18.3p expected) → actual 27.1p = +48% beat vs seasonal baseline.
    "Adjusted basic earnings per share (continuing operations): 27.1p" (from key financials table).
  3. Statutory operating loss: −£65.5m (H1 FY25: −£102.2m). Improvement of £36.7m YoY. The £135m motor finance provision increase in H1 FY26 (vs £165m in H1 FY25) is the primary driver of the statutory loss.
    "Operating loss before tax: (65.5) [H1 2026]... primarily reflecting the additional £135.0 million motor finance provision taken in October 2025."
  4. Accelerated cost savings — primary structural upgrade signal: FY26 annualised savings raised from £20m to £25m; total savings target of £60m now expected by end-2027 (previously end-2028). FY26 adjusted opex guided at c.£450m.
    "We now expect to deliver c.£25 million (previously c.£20 million) of annualised savings in the current financial year and a total of c.£60 million of annualised savings by the end of 2027 rather than 2028."
  5. NIM guidance maintained: H1 NIM 7.1% (H1 FY25: 7.3%). FY26 NIM expected slightly below 7%.
    "We continue to expect NIM to be slightly below 7% for the full year reflecting loan book mix impacts."
  6. Bad debt ratio improving: H1 0.8% (H1 FY25: 1.0%). Guided below long-term average of 1.2% for FY26. Driven by updated IFRS 9 model for Motor Finance book.
    "The bad debt ratio remains comfortably below our long-term average of 1.2%."
  7. CET1 capital ratio strengthening: 14.3% (31 July 2025: 13.8%) despite £135m provision. 460bps headroom above requirement.
    "Our CET1 capital ratio remains strong at 14.3% and we are confident that this leaves us well placed to absorb a range of potential outcomes from the FCA's proposed motor finance commission redress scheme."
  8. Motor finance total provision: £300m. FCA Policy Statement expected late March 2026. Group disagrees with FCA's methodology. Position unchanged from 31 January 2026.
    "The group responded to the FCA consultation paper prior to the deadline of 12 December 2025 and awaits the final redress scheme rules, which the FCA has stated it expects to publish in late March 2026."
  9. Loan book: £9.2bn (31 July 2025: £9.5bn), −2% (−1% underlying excl. repositioning). Motor Finance +4%; Premium Finance −13% (planned).
    "The loan book decreased 2% over the first half of the financial year to £9.2 billion."
  10. RoTE: 6.3% adjusted (H1 FY25: 8.7%). Double-digit RoTE targeted by FY28 financial year.
    "Together, the actions above set a clear path back to double-digit RoTE by the 2028 financial year, rising thereafter."
  11. No dividend reinstated. Decision deferred pending FCA clarity on motor finance outcome.
    "Given the continued uncertainty regarding the outcome of the FCA's review of motor finance commission arrangements... the group will not pay an interim dividend."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • HoH EPS pattern: Highly volatile, dominated by motor finance provision impacts. FY YoY: FY24 −50.5%, FY25 +37.5%, FY26 fc −42.3%. No reliable trend — the adjusted EPS series is the more informative metric.
  • H1 tracking vs seasonal norm (pre-H1 mode): H1 adj EPS 27.1p / FY1 cns 43.6p = 62.2% vs 3yr avg 41.9% = +20.3pp deviation. 🟢 STRONG BUY SIGNAL. Buy trigger threshold was: H1 EPS > 43.6p × 0.419 × 1.011 = 18.5p. Actual 27.1p is far above trigger. Revenue: UNTRACKABLE (no consensus).
  • H2 burden read-through: H2 implied by consensus = 16.5p (43.6p − 27.1p), representing only 37.8% of FY consensus. For H2 to collapse to 16.5p, it would need to be −48.8% vs H2 FY25 (32.2p). This is inconsistent with flat opex, improving bad debts, and no new provision guided. A normalised H2 of 25–30p would deliver FY EPS of 52–57p — a 19–31% beat vs consensus.
  • Implied H2 momentum: H2 FY25 adjusted EPS was 32.2p. Consensus implies H2 FY26 of just 16.5p (−48.8%). This is deeply pessimistic. Even a 30% decline to ~22p would deliver FY EPS of ~49p vs 43.6p consensus (+12%). Classification: consensus H2 assumption is an extreme outlier.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CCC · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update

  1. Revenue — Q1 characterisation: Group Technology Sourcing revenue "increased particularly strongly" in Q1; Group Services revenue "ahead of last year." No precise Q1 revenue figure disclosed. The RNS characterises performance as "significantly ahead of the prior year and well above our expectations." "The Group delivered a strong performance during the first quarter, which was significantly ahead of the prior year and well above our expectations."
  2. H1 guidance — explicit upgrade signal: The company states it now expects "a much stronger performance in the first half of the year than previously anticipated." This is a direct H1 upgrade statement. No numeric H1 figure given. "Looking to 2026, we now expect to deliver a much stronger performance in the first half of the year than previously anticipated."
  3. Full-year guidance — "comfortably ahead of market expectations": The company explicitly guides full-year results "comfortably ahead of market expectations." Consensus PBT cited as £291.3m (range £284.5m–£297.1m). "Comfortably ahead" language implies at minimum £300m+ PBT, with the upper end likely exceeding £310m. The FY26fc consensus PBT in Sharescope is £293.8m — "comfortably ahead" of this implies a material upgrade. "We now anticipate delivering full-year results comfortably ahead of market expectations." FY26e PBT implied: If "comfortably ahead" = +5–8% above the £291.3m midpoint, that implies £305–315m PBT vs consensus £291.3m = +5–8% PBT beat implied. Sharescope FY26fc EPS = 191.3p — applying a proportional 5–8% uplift implies revised FY26 EPS of approximately 200–206p, versus current consensus 191.3p.
  4. FY26e EPS bridge (FY26 → FY27):
    • New base FY26 EPS actual: estimated ~200–206p (post-upgrade; pre-RNS consensus was 191.3p)
    • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil — no acquisition disclosed
    • Organic growth delta: FY27 consensus EPS 204.5p is based on stale FY26 base of 191.3p. With FY26 base now ~202p (midpoint), FY27 consensus effectively represents flat to slight decline on the revised base — brokers will need to raise FY27.
    • Interest step-up delta: Net cash position deepening; interest income likely rising, not a drag.
    • Implied FY27 EPS revised: if brokers lift FY26 by ~+10p to ~200p and apply modest organic growth, FY27 could move to 215–225p vs stale consensus 204.5p = +5–10% FY27 upgrade implied.
  5. Order book / forward visibility: Committed product order backlog "remained strong" at quarter end. Some customers ordering "further in advance than usual to secure supply given hardware component shortages." This creates a visibility tailwind for H1 but a potential H2 timing risk. "At the end of the quarter our committed product order backlog across all regions remained strong, reflecting good order intake during the quarter, with some customers ordering IT product further in advance than usual to secure supply, given hardware component shortages currently affecting the IT industry."
  6. Regional drivers: North America — "excellent first quarter," record product order backlog at end of 2025, strong hyperscale customer volumes, Technology Sourcing + Professional Services both strong. UK — "excellent growth in Technology Sourcing including AI-related project completions." Germany — "solid performance," Technology Sourcing good, Professional Services "subdued." Western Europe — "small improvement."
  7. Macro caveat / H2 risk: Management explicitly flags "tougher comparative in the second half of the year" and "mindful of uncertain macroeconomic and geopolitical environment." This is a deliberate tempering of H2 expectations. "We remain mindful of the uncertain macroeconomic and geopolitical environment and a tougher comparative in the second half of the year."
  8. Hardware component shortages: Noted as a current factor causing some customers to order "further in advance than usual." This could pull forward H1 revenue at the expense of H2.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed (trading update). No tax rate distortion applicable. No one-off credits flagged. Guidance is on PBT basis — clean signal.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • Forward-looking language: "comfortably ahead of market expectations" for full year + "much stronger H1 than previously anticipated."
  • Numeric guidance: yes — PBT consensus cited at £291.3m with "comfortably ahead" language.
  • Coverage: full year FY26.
  • H2 caveat: present but does not negate the upgrade signal.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering (+12 to +15 pts). Explicit "comfortably ahead" language with cited consensus figure = textbook upgrade-triggering language. Provisional: +14 pts.
  • Divergence check: N/A — this is a pre-H1 trading update, no current-year delivery figure to compare against. Forward guidance is standalone positive.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst is the explicit full-year upgrade: Computacenter guides FY26 results "comfortably ahead of market expectations," citing a company-compiled consensus PBT of £291.3m (range £284.5m–£297.1m). This is unambiguous upgrade-triggering language. The implied PBT is at minimum £305–315m, representing a +5–8% beat vs the pre-RNS consensus. The pre-RNS FY26e EPS of 191.3p will be revised to approximately 200–207p. The Q1 period was described as "significantly ahead of the prior year and well above expectations" — two layers of upgrade signal from a single short announcement.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the H1 tracking analysis is UNTRACKABLE (no H1 actuals disclosed — H1 results on 8 September 2026). However, FY guidance-implied H1 tracking deviation is approximately +1.8pp (Rev) and +2.5pp (EPS) — both 🟡 PROBABLE BUY signals. The implied H2 burden from stale consensus (116.3p vs 107.9p historical avg = +7.8% above historical average) is elevated, but management has explicitly flagged this with the "tougher H2 comparative" caveat — which in context reads as responsible guidance management rather than a warning. The structural risk is the hardware order pull-forward: if Q1/Q2 revenues reflect customers advancing orders due to component shortages, H2 could undershoot the implied £5,285m level. However, the backlog description ("remained strong" with "good order intake") suggests H2 pipeline remains intact.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus will move from 191.3p to approximately 200–207p (+5–8%); FY27 from 204.5p to approximately 215–222p (+5–8%). Consensus TP likely to rise from £34.65 to £36–38. Current price £32.22 implies 12–18% upside to upgraded TP. The main watch point is the H2 comparative: FY25 H2 revenue of £5,205.1m was a 56% YoY step-up, creating a very high bar. The broker upgrade cycle is clear and supported by three independent signals — FY guidance, H1 upgrade, and strong backlog — but the score is capped at 78 (rather than 85+) by the pull-forward risk and H2 uncertainty. 🏁 Clear upgrade cycle underway; FY26 and FY27 EPS revisions of +5–8% are probable across the broker panel; buy into the upgrade on weakness before H1 results on 8 September 2026.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CER · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (H1 FY26, 6 months ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue — H1 FY26:

  • H1 revenue: c.£18.0m (H1 FY25: £20.9m) = −13.9% YoY.
  • vs FY1 fc consensus £53.0m: H1 = £18.0m / £53.0m = 34.0% of FY1 fc vs 3yr avg H1 baseline of 51.0% → −17.0pp deviation — extremely large negative deviation from seasonal norm.
  • vs prior season buy trigger (£27.0m × 1.015 = £27.4m): £18.0m → 🔴 ✗ — massive miss.
  • Explanation: explicitly stated — "very little high-margin software licence revenue was recognised in H1 2026." This is a disclosed timing pattern, not a demand miss. The company compares to H1 FY25 noting last year was also H2-weighted: "Like last year, the Company's full year results are expected to be strongly weighted to the second half."
  • Context: FY25 H1 £20.9m vs H2 £24.4m = H1 was 46.2% of full year FY25 — itself below the 51.0% 3yr average, meaning H2-weighting is an established structural feature of this business, not a new development.

"H1 revenue expected to be c. £18.0m (H1 2025: £20.9m)...This reflects the timing of contracts and the fact that, as anticipated, very little high-margin software licence revenue was recognised in H1 2026."

2. EBITDA / EPS — H1 FY26:

  • H1 EBITDA: c.£6.2m (H1 FY25: £9.9m) = −37.4% YoY.
  • vs FY1 fc EBITDA £23.9m: H1 = £6.2m / £23.9m = 25.9% of FY fc — far below seasonal expectation of ~50%.
  • EPS quality check: H1 adj EPS not disclosed (interim results 1 June 2026). Estimating from EBITDA £6.2m: less D&A ~£1.5m est. → adj EBIT ~£4.7m. Add interest income on £32.5m cash at ~4% = £0.6m H1 → adj PBT ~£5.3m. Tax at ~20% (Cerillion has historically low effective rate; UK software R&D reliefs) → adj PAT ~£4.2m. On 29.5m shares → H1 EPS ~14–16p estimate (vs H1 FY25 actual 23.9p = −33 to −42% YoY). ⚠️ This is a directional estimate only — confirm at 1 June interim results.
  • Implied H2 EPS: FY1 fc 58.4p − estimated H1 ~15p = ~43p H2 EPS required. vs H2 FY25 32.6p = +32% YoY required. Substantial H2 loading.

EPS bridge FY26e (constructed here for Phase 4 reference):

  • (1) New base: FY25 adj EPS 56.5p (29.5m shares).
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Omantel (£42.5m contract, multi-year implementation). H1 FY26 contribution minimal per RNS ("very little...revenue recognised in H1"). H2 FY26 begins unwinding — management says "expected to contribute significantly in the second half." Quantification: if Omantel contributes £10–15m of H2 FY26 revenue (at ~40–50% software margin = £4–7m incremental EBIT), the EPS contribution is ~14–24p in H2 FY26. This is the core upgrade driver.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA delta: back-order book doubled to £39.6m (H1 FY25: £19.6m) — existing customer demand strong. Organic EBITDA growth on the non-Omantel base: modest, consistent with prior year trajectory.
  • (4) Interest step-up: net cash £32.5m generating ~£1.2m p.a. interest at 4% → EPS uplift ~2.7p vs no-cash scenario. Stable.
  • Implied FY26e EPS: 58.4p consensus appears to fully reflect the Omantel H2 loading. The bridge does not indicate a significant revision vs consensus — management confirms "well-positioned to meet market expectations." No delta.

3. Order book / forward work:

  • New orders as at 30 March 2026: £39.6m (H1 FY25: £19.6m) = +102% YoY — orders have doubled.
  • "Driven principally by the January win [Omantel], but also by demand from existing customers."
  • Order book coverage of H2 FY26 implied revenue (£35.0m): £39.6m covers 113% of implied H2 — exceptional H2 visibility.
  • ⚠️ Note: "New orders does not include revenue from maintenance and support" — so total contracted revenue backlog is higher still (maintenance/support recurring revenue stream on top).

"New orders have doubled to £39.6m as at 30 March 2026 (H1 2025: £19.6m), driven principally by the January win, but also by demand from existing customers."

4. Margin / profitability signals:

  • H1 EBITDA margin: £6.2m / £18.0m = 34.4% vs H1 FY25 margin = £9.9m / £20.9m = 47.4%. Significant H1 margin compression due to low-margin services revenue dominating in H1 (implementation work on Omantel not yet at revenue recognition stage) and fixed cost base maintained for H2 delivery.
  • H2 FY26 will carry high-margin software licence revenue from Omantel as implementation milestones are reached. "Contract is expected to contribute significantly in the second half."
  • Full-year EBITDA margin implied: £23.9m / £53.0m = 45.1% — very high for a software company, consistent with historical delivery.

5. Cash position:

  • Net cash £32.5m at H1 FY26 end (31 Mar 2026) vs £31.2m H1 FY25 = +£1.3m YoY improvement despite H1 being a seasonally weak cash generation period. Sharescope fc £40.7m — on track.
  • "Net cash at the half-year end was higher year-on-year at approximately £32.5m." No debt.

"The Company's net cash at the half-year end was higher year-on-year at approximately £32.5m (31 March 2025: £31.2m)."

6. Qualitative tone / guidance:

  • "The Board believes that Cerillion remains well-positioned to meet market expectations for the financial year." → Explicit in-line guidance.
  • "The pipeline of new business opportunities remains strong, and the Company continues to invest in the business to support growth." → Constructive forward signal.
  • "Interim results will be published on 1 June 2026, when a further update on current trading and prospects will be provided." → Near-term catalyst confirmed.

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

Forward guidance: "well-positioned to meet market expectations" — explicit, covers FY26. Numeric in the sense that the company discloses H1 actuals and the order book figure provides quantitative support. No upgrade language; no downgrade either. The order book doubling (+102%) is implicitly upgrade-enabling but management has not deployed upgrade language in this update.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — "meet market expectations" is unambiguous in-line language. However, the order book doubling to £39.6m (vs consensus H2 implied requirement of ~£35m) and the explicit "pipeline of new business remains strong" language is more constructive than a bare in-line. Provisionally: 🟡 In-line (+2 pts) with a note that the order book metric carries implicit upgrade optionality for FY27 that will be confirmed at 1 June results.

Divergence: H1 revenue −13.9% YoY and EBITDA −37.4% YoY vs "in-line with market expectations" for the full year. This is a large divergence — H1 massively below seasonal norm — but the company has explicitly pre-explained the cause (contract timing, licence phasing). The divergence is disclosed and anticipated, not a surprise. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year H1 delivery — but this is structural/timing, not demand deterioration.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

CER · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

H2 cross-checks:

  • FY25 (current): H1 £20.9m + H2 £24.4m = £45.3m vs Sharescope FY 45.4m — rounding ✅. EPS: 23.9 + 32.6 = 56.5p ✅.
  • FY24 (1y ago): H1 £22.5m + H2 £21.2m = £43.7m vs Sharescope 43.8m — rounding ✅. EPS: 27.6 + 24.6 = 52.2p ✅.
  • FY23 (2y ago): H1 £20.5m + H2 £18.7m = £39.2m ✅. EPS: 25.5 + 20.7 = 46.2p ✅.
  • FY22 (3y ago): H1 £16.1m + H2 £16.6m = £32.7m (no FY total in Sharescope "3y ago" to cross-check; treating as correct). EPS: 18.6 + 16.6 = 35.2p.

All clean. ✅ No Sharescope H2 glitch on revenue or EPS fields.

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Revenue growth trajectory: FY22→FY23: +19.9%; FY23→FY24: +11.7%; FY24→FY25: +3.7%; FY25→FY26e: +16.7%. 🟡 Volatile — deceleration into FY25, then Omantel-driven re-acceleration in FY26. Not organic acceleration.

EPS growth trajectory: FY23: +31.3%; FY24: +13.0%; FY25: +8.2%; FY26e: +3.4%. 🔴 Decelerating — despite Omantel boosting FY26 revenue consensus, EPS growth consensus is only +3.4% vs prior year. This reflects the mix: Omantel revenue is recognised in stages (implementation milestones) and significant cost investment is underway ("continues to invest in the business to support growth"). The FY26 EPS step-up is modest; FY27 at +10.4% is where the structural uplift arrives.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: FY26e +16.7% vs FY25 +3.7% → acceleration ✓ (consensus-derived; Omantel-driven)
  • EPS: FY26e +3.4% vs FY25 +8.2% → no acceleration (consensus-derived; decelerating)

Revenue trajectory: H1 YoY: +9.8% → −7.1% → −13.9%. H2 YoY: +13.4% → +15.1% → +43.4% implied. 🔴 Decelerating on H1 basis (second consecutive YoY decline). H2 reversal is structurally driven by Omantel licence recognition — this is timing not underlying decline.

EPS trajectory: H1 continuing to deteriorate; H2 strong uplift driven by high-margin licence revenue. The business exhibits an extreme intra-year skew that is self-reinforcing as large implementation contracts are signed (initial months = low-margin services, later months = high-margin licence recognition). 🟡 Volatile — H1/H2 split is the defining feature of this business model.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source gate: H1 revenue confirmed from RNS at c.£18.0m. EPS not disclosed (interim results 1 June 2026). Revenue trackable; EPS UNTRACKABLE.

Revenue:

  • 3yr avg H1% of FY: 51.0% (Sharescope). Revenue baseline: 51.0% × £53.0m = £27.0m.
  • H1 actual c.£18.0m / £53.0m = 34.0% vs 51.0% → deviation = −17.0pp → 🔴🔴 SELL SIGNAL (≤ −3pp threshold, this is extreme)
  • Buy trigger: > £27.0m × 1.015 = £27.4m → £18.0m → 🔴 ✗

⚠️ Critical context: The −17.0pp deviation is the largest mechanical miss possible under the seasonal baseline framework, but it is entirely pre-explained by the company as deliberate contract timing and licence revenue phasing. This is not a demand signal. The RNS explicitly states the miss was "as anticipated" and that results will be "strongly weighted to the second half." The SELL SIGNAL on revenue tracking is a mechanical output of applying a seasonal average to a business that has structurally moved toward H2-loaded licence recognition. Scoring this at full weight would be misleading — the signal must be discounted but per the framework it still fires.

Per rules, the SELL SIGNAL scores in Phase 5 (pre-H1 mode). I will score it negatively but at the lower end of the range given the explicit management disclosure that this was anticipated.

EPS: UNTRACKABLE. Signal: na (—). Interim results 1 June 2026.

H2 EPS burden: FY1 fc 58.4p − estimated H1 ~15p = ~43p H2 EPS vs H2 FY25 32.6p = +32% YoY. This is a heavy burden but is underpinned by the Omantel contract contribution and doubled order book.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-H1 mode — scores in Phase 5)

H2 base: RNS-derived FY guidance "meet market expectations" = FY1 fc £53.0m. H1 actual £18.0m → H2 implied = £35.0m (RNS-derived).

H2 FY26 vs H2 FY25: £35.0m vs £24.4m = +43.4% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%).

vs 3yr H2 avg: (£16.6m + £18.7m + £21.2m + £24.4m)/4 = £20.2m → H2 FY26 £35.0m = +73% above 4yr H2 avg. An extraordinary H2 requirement — but the order book of £39.6m (which excludes maintenance/support) covers £35.0m H2 revenue by 113%, providing direct contractual coverage for the implied H2.

EPS: H2 FY26 implied ~43p vs H2 FY25 32.6p = +32% YoY → 🟢 strong.

Profit warning feasibility gate: H1 revenue and EBITDA are below seasonal baseline — gate condition met. Applying:

  • H2 hurdle test: H2 revenue +43.4% required vs most recent H2 YoY of +15.1%. This exceeds the 10pp threshold — flag as structurally elevated burden. However, the order book of £39.6m directly covers it. The hurdle is extraordinary but has contractual support.
  • Fixed cost headwinds: None flagged by management. Company is investing but no cost step-up or macro headwind material to a software business with predominantly GBP costs.
  • Operating leverage / interest cover: Net cash £32.5m — no leverage risk. Operating leverage is positive (incremental software licence revenue falls at ~70–80% margin).

⛔ Profit warning feasibility gate assessment: Two conditions technically met (H2 hurdle >10pp above prior, H1 miss). However the explicit order book coverage (£39.6m > £35.0m H2 requirement) and management's confirmed "meet market expectations" guidance provide direct contractual mitigation. Unlike the standard profit warning scenario, the H2 burden is quantifiably covered by signed orders. Gate does not fire as a profit warning — instead flag as: ⚠️ Elevated H2 delivery risk — H2 revenue +43.4% YoY required but order book £39.6m provides 113% contractual coverage. Execution risk is delivery (implementation on schedule) not demand. Monitor Omantel implementation progress at 1 June.

Classification: 🟢 strong — underpinned by contracted order book.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +8.3% net (53.9p → 58.4p). Step-change at 29 Nov 25 (Omantel announcement) from 54.6p → 58.5p. Since then: stable with minor trim to 58.4p on 17 Apr 26.
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (58.5p → 58.4p — this is a trivial 0.1p trim, likely rounding. Not a material downgrade event).
  • Revenue: £49m → £53m net +8.2%. Same step-change pattern.
  • Divergence: Share price at £14.30 vs consensus TP £20.31 = 42.0% upside. Price was at £20.44–£20.99 through most of May 2025 to March 2026 (approximately). Current £14.30 = −30% from peak. Yet EPS consensus has barely moved. This is an extreme share price de-rating vs unchanged broker estimates — the market is pricing in execution risk on the Omantel H2 delivery, not a fundamental business deterioration. The gap between price (£14.30) and TP (£20.31) is extreme for a business with £32.5m net cash, doubling order book, and confirmed in-line guidance.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Currency: GBP.

RNS vs forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash = £32.5m at H1 FY26 (31 Mar 2026). Sharescope fc = −£40.7m (net cash £40.7m) = full-year forecast, not half-year. Sharescope "current H1" net cash = £27.5m (Sharescope) vs RNS £32.5m = £5.0m better than Sharescope H1 forecast — positive cash surprise. RNS supersedes: H1 net cash = £32.5m.

  • Net cash trajectory: FY22 H2 −£4.1m / FY23 H2 −£1.5m / FY24 H2 −£3.2m / FY25 H2 −£3.6m (Sharescope sign = net cash) / H1 FY26 RNS £32.5m / fc £40.7m / FY2 £51.0m.
  • ND/EBITDA: consistent net cash position; fc −1.70x (deeply net cash).
  • Interest cover: N/A — net cash, interest income positive.
  • Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — balance sheet is a strength, not a constraint. The £32.5m net cash at H1 provides ~110p per share (29.5m shares) of cash backing.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • EPS: 58.4p > FY25 56.5p ✅✅ (modest +3.4%)
  • Revenue: £53.0m > FY25 £45.4m ✅✅ (+16.7%)

Step 2 — FY27 vs FY26:

  • EPS: 64.5p > 58.4p ✅✅ (+10.4%)
  • Revenue: £58.4m > £53.0m ✅✅ (+10.2%)

Both growing at FY1 and FY2 level. ✅✅

3.6 Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Omantel (£42.5m contract, signed January 2026): Cerillion's largest ever contract. Multi-year implementation. Revenue recognition will be phased across H2 FY26 and FY27 (and potentially FY28). "Software implementation remains on track." This is a transformational contract that materially re-rates the FY27 and FY28 earnings outlook. The full revenue contribution is NOT yet in consensus — £58.4m FY27 consensus revenue may prove conservative if Omantel recognition accelerates.
  • Order book doubling (£39.6m vs £19.6m prior): Represents a structural step-change in contracted backlog, not a one-off. "Also by demand from existing customers" — the non-Omantel component of order growth confirms organic momentum.
  • Extreme H2/H1 seasonality (structural feature): H2 revenue was 57.5% of FY25 full-year revenue (vs historical ~49% H2 share). FY26 will be even more H2-weighted (~66% H2 based on implied). This is a permanent feature of the business model as large implementation contracts dominate the mix — investors must monitor H2 delivery rather than H1 tracking signals.
  • Investment for growth: "The Company continues to invest in the business to support growth" — operating cost base growing ahead of H1 revenue, depressing H1 margins. This investment is a leading indicator of future revenue, not a margin concern.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

CER · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

#1 Driver — Order book doubled to £39.6m; Omantel implementation on track: This is unambiguously the dominant signal for brokers. The order book provides 113% coverage of the H2 implied revenue requirement (£35.0m). With the largest contract in company history on track and the order book at a record level, the in-line confirmation is substantively more bullish than the headline "meet market expectations" language suggests. The H2 delivery setup is the strongest in Cerillion's history by order book metric.

#2 Driver — Net cash £32.5m, higher YoY: Cash is a validation signal for this business — it confirms that the H1 revenue miss is purely a P&L timing event, not a cash collection problem. Customers are paying and the business is cash-generative even in its seasonally weak half. The £5.0m positive surprise vs Sharescope's H1 cash forecast reinforces quality.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e EPS: Hold at 58.4p — management explicitly guides "meet market expectations." Brokers have nothing to revise against; the H1 EBITDA (£6.2m vs H1 FY25 £9.9m) is below seasonal norm but the company has guided this was anticipated. No basis for upgrade or downgrade.
  • FY26e Revenue: Hold at £53.0m — H1 £18.0m + H2 implied £35.0m = £53.0m exactly matches consensus.
  • FY27e EPS: Upside risk. The order book of £39.6m (excluding maintenance) already provides substantial FY27 backlog. If Omantel contributes more revenue than modelled in H2 FY26 (pulling forward from FY27) or contributes additional phases in FY27, the £64.5m consensus EPS could see further upgrades. The 1 June interim results will be the key moment for FY27 upgrades.
  • TP: Consensus £20.31 vs current £14.30 = 42% upside. Brokers likely to reiterate Buy and maintain TPs — the gap between TP and price is a function of execution risk premium the market applies to the H2 delivery, not a consensus downgrade signal.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Well-positioned to meet market expectations" is deliberately understated language — Cerillion's CEO has historically used this phrase as a floor confirmation. The order book doubling and "pipeline of new business remains strong" are the constructive signals embedded alongside the in-line confirmation. Brokers will read this as: meet at minimum, with upside optionality if Omantel H2 licensing steps exceed the timetable.

Key risk: The H2 delivery burden is extraordinary: £35.0m revenue in a single half-year (vs £24.4m H2 FY25 = highest prior H2). If Omantel implementation encounters delays — software integration complexity, customer-side readiness issues, milestone sign-off slippage — revenue recognition could shift into FY27, causing a FY26 miss. Management states implementation "remains on track" which is reassuring but not a guarantee. "Software implementation remains on track and the contract is expected to contribute significantly in the second half of the financial year."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision: hold (in-line guidance, no delta to consensus). Tone: Neutral. However the order book signal is more constructive than neutral — brokers may frame this as cautiously Constructive. Retaining Neutral as primary for the scorecard given the explicit "meet" language.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — in-line confirmation with embedded upgrade optionality; the real catalyst is 1 June interim results when Omantel H2 progression will be quantified. The order book and cash are strong signals but management has not yet deployed upgrade language.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Pre-FX raw score: 58/100 (no FX adjustment) Final score: 58/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single defining signal in today's pre-H1 update is not the H1 numbers themselves — which are awful on the surface — but the order book doubling to £39.6m (H1 FY25: £19.6m), providing 113% contractual coverage of the £35.0m H2 revenue required to meet full-year consensus of £53.0m. H1 revenue of c.£18.0m (−14% vs H1 FY25 £20.9m) and H1 EBITDA of c.£6.2m (−37% vs H1 FY25 £9.9m) are the worst H1 figures in three years, but the company has pre-disclosed the reason explicitly: no high-margin software licence revenue was recognised in H1, entirely as anticipated. The Omantel contract (£42.5m, Cerillion's largest ever, signed January 2026) remains on track and is expected to "contribute significantly in the second half." The H1 miss is not a demand story — it is a revenue recognition timing event on a record contracted backlog.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 implied revenue of £35.0m (+43.4% vs H2 FY25 £24.4m) is the largest single-half revenue requirement in Cerillion's history — but it arrives with the most comprehensive contractual support the business has ever had. The order book of £39.6m excludes maintenance and support revenue, meaning total contracted H2 revenue (including recurring streams) comfortably covers the £35.0m target. Net cash of £32.5m — £5.0m better than Sharescope's H1 forecast — confirms the H1 miss is a P&L timing event only, not a cash or customer collection problem. The business is cash-generative and the Omantel milestone payments will reinforce this in H2. The one genuine risk is implementation delivery: if Omantel milestone sign-offs slip by even 4–6 weeks, meaningful licence revenue could fall into FY27, causing a FY26 miss despite the underlying demand being intact. Management's "on track" language is the key phrase — it confirms no slippage has emerged yet.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely held at 58.4p and revenue at £53.0m — the in-line guidance gives brokers no basis to move. FY27e EPS (64.5p) carries upside risk that will be quantified at the 1 June interim results — the key catalyst for this name. If Omantel H2 progression is detailed at 1 June and further orders from existing customers are reported, FY27 upgrades toward 68–72p are plausible. The current consensus TP of £20.31 vs share price £14.30 represents 42% upside — an extreme gap for a business with net cash of £32.5m (worth ~110p/share alone), a doubled order book, and an in-line trading confirmation. The market is pricing a material H2 execution risk premium that today's update does not justify — "on track" is a clean confirmation. 🏁 In-line with record order book coverage and Omantel confirmed on track; the H1 miss is noise, the H2 setup is the most contractually supported in the company's history, and the real upgrade catalyst is 1 June.

CHH — Churchill China

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS: Sharescope FY1 fc blank (no consensus). Revenue: Sharescope FY1 fc blank. Using last available consensus: EPS 40.9p (from snapshot), Revenue £75.5m.
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS: blank. Revenue: blank. No forward consensus available.
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS 58p → 40.9p = −29.5% (major downgrade in July 2025). Revenue 77.9m → 75.5m. 4-week trend: FLAT (EPS blank in final week — no figure available). Net direction: severe downgrade cycle completed Jul 2025.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue: 51.8% × £75.5m = £39.1m. EPS: 43.0% × 40.9p = 17.6p.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24 H1): Revenue £40.6m · EPS 32.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY25 £76.3m − H1 £38.5m = H2 £37.8m vs FY24 H2 £37.7m → +0.3% YoY (essentially flat). EPS: FY25 EPS 39.7p actual − H1 21.0p (Sharescope current H1) = H2 18.7p vs FY24 H2 25.1p → −25.5% YoY.
  • FX: CHH manufactures in UK but references USD in North America. US = ~11% of revenues. No single non-GBP currency >30%. No Phase 0B triggered.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY22 −£10.1m → FY23 −£5.8m → FY24 −£2.0m → FY25 H1 −£5.2m → FY25 actual £10.8m (disclosed in RNS). Strong cash generation. ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash). Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CHH · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual £76.3m vs last consensus £75.5m Beat: +£0.8m, +1.1% ahead of last consensus. Down 2.6% vs FY24 £78.3m as guided in July 2025.

"revenue in the year reduced 2.6% to £76.3m, (2024: £78.3m)"

2. EPS / earnings — FY25 EPS 39.7p vs last consensus 40.9p Miss: −1.2p, −2.9% below last consensus. PBT £6.0m vs FY24 £8.5m (−29%). EBITDA £9.4m (FY24 £11.7m, −19.7%). PBT margin 7.9% (FY24: 10.9%).

EPS quality check: Tax not specifically quantified in RNS summary. PBT £6.0m, EPS 39.7p on 11.0m shares = PAT ~£4.4m. Implied effective rate = (6.0 − 4.4)/6.0 = ~26.7%. Close to normalised 25% — within 3pp threshold. No restatement required. EPS miss is genuine operational.

FY26e bridge (no EPS consensus available):

  • New base: FY25 EPS 39.7p. PBT £6.0m vs FY24 £8.5m = −29%.
  • FY26 drivers: company guided "improved factory efficiency," pipeline "stronger than prior year," energy hedged for 2026 (64% hedged for 2027). No explicit FY26 guidance numbers.
  • If hospitality market stabilises and revenue recovers to £78–80m (pre-deterioration level), at FY25 margin rate (7.9% PBT) → PBT ~£6.2–6.3m → EPS ~44–46p. No broker consensus to compare.
  • Management narrative: cautiously constructive. CEO notes "operationally stronger" entering 2026.

3. Order book / pipeline No order book metric. Pipeline described as "stronger than the prior year going into 2026." Replacement business described as "robust." European pipeline improved vs prior year.

"the pipeline of projects going into 2026 is stronger than the prior year"

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin not stated explicitly in summary. PBT margin 7.9% (FY24: 10.9%) — significant compression driven by lower volumes, higher manufacturing cost per piece (planned stock reduction + reduced volumes), wage/NI increases from April 2025. EBITDA £9.4m (FY24 £11.7m). Energy costs "well controlled" — substantially forward purchased for 2026 and 2027.

5. Capital returns / cash Cash £10.8m (FY24: £10.1m, +£0.7m). Inventory reduced £2.0m. Final dividend: 14.0p (FY24: 26.5p — cut of 47%). Total FY25 dividend: 21.0p (FY24: 38.0p — cut of 45%).

"the Board has taken the difficult but prudent decision to reduce the dividend... a total dividend of 21.0p per share for the year"

6. Qualitative tone / outlook "Churchill enters 2026 operationally stronger, with improved factory efficiency, controlled costs, and a more robust UK pipeline." No numeric FY26 guidance. "Confident in the resilience of our business." "Aim is to return to increasing dividends year on year as the Group returns to growth."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: qualitative only — no numeric FY26 revenue or EPS guidance. Language is cautiously constructive: "operationally stronger," "more robust pipeline," energy hedged. No "in line with market expectations" anchor. No EPS consensus to assess beat/miss.

However, the dividend cut of 45% is itself a guidance signal — management is explicitly managing capital conservatively, suggesting they do not expect a rapid earnings recovery.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only guidance following a significant earnings decline; dividend cut signals management caution; no visibility on recovery quantum. Provisional points: −5 to −8.

Divergence: Revenue marginally beat last consensus but EPS missed; dividend cut. Consistent with Cautious classification — no divergence requiring special flag.

EPS: 58p → 40.9p (−29.5%). Revenue: 77.9m → 75.5m. 4-week: FLAT. The downgrade cycle was completed in July 2025 (post-H1). The EPS consensus has been static for 9 months — no further deterioration. Without a FY26 consensus, brokers have limited forward estimate to revise.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

CHH · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — Dividend cut 45% (21p vs 38p prior year): The dividend cut from 38p to 21p total is the most actionable signal for broker recommendation changes. This exceeds the proportional earnings decline (EPS −31%, dividend −45%) — management is rebuilding the balance sheet and reserving capital. Brokers will reduce income forecasts, potentially triggering downgrades in total return-focused buy cases.

#2 Driver — EPS −31% to 39.7p + PBT −29%: The magnitude of earnings decline is already in the market (EPS consensus was cut from 58p to 40.9p in July 2025). Actual 39.7p is a marginal −2.9% miss vs the already-downgraded 40.9p — in line rather than a negative surprise. The issue is whether there is a further revision cycle required for FY26.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY25e) EPS: 39.7p actual vs 40.9p consensus = −2.9% miss — modest downward revision to actuals, immaterial.
  • FY1 (FY25e) Revenue: £76.3m vs £75.5m = +1.1% beat — minor upward revision.
  • FY2 (FY26e): No consensus exists. Brokers will initiate FY26e — likely in £40–50p EPS range depending on recovery assumptions. Revenue likely modelled at £77–80m. No consensus to quantify revision against.
  • Target price: Consensus TP £11.00 vs price 300p (267% upside — clearly stale/anomalous). Investec and Panmure Liberum will update models. TP likely to be cut substantially to £4–7 range (was set when EPS was 58p+; at 39.7p EPS the prior TP is untenable).

Conservative guidance read-through: No explicit guidance. "Stronger pipeline," energy hedged, "operationally stronger" — brokers will interpret cautiously given three consecutive years of revenue decline and the magnitude of the EPS compression.

Key risk: Hospitality market recovery is entirely demand-driven. "globally the hospitality trade continues to suffer from increased inflationary costs, leading to closures and reduced profitability in the restaurant and casual dining sectors" — if European and UK demand does not recover in 2026, the pipeline improvement will not translate to orders.

Consistency check: FY2 EPS revision direction: initiate (no consensus, build FY26). Given cautious outlook, tone is 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable (specifically: TP cuts).

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

CHH

Para 1 — Headline numbers: CHH delivered FY25 revenue of £76.3m (+1.1% vs last consensus £75.5m, marginal beat) and PBT of £6.0m vs FY24 £8.5m = −29%. Basic EPS of 39.7p vs last consensus 40.9p = −2.9% miss — the EPS downgrade was already substantially completed in July 2025 when consensus was cut from 58p to 40.9p. The definitive negative catalyst is the dividend cut of 45% (total 21.0p vs FY24 38.0p), which signals management does not expect a rapid earnings recovery and is explicitly rebuilding capital. PBT margin compressed to 7.9% (FY24: 10.9%) — the H2 EPS of 18.7p vs FY24 H2 25.1p = −25.5% is the most severe signal.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 revenue of £37.8m = +0.3% YoY — flat but not deteriorating further (🟡 flat classification), consistent with the July guidance. H2 EPS of 18.7p = −25.5% YoY — 🔴 severe, driven by lower manufacturing volumes, April 2025 wage/NI increases, and intentional stock reduction raising per-unit costs. The "upgrade resilience" is minimal: there is no EPS consensus to upgrade, the qualitative FY26 outlook provides no numeric anchor, and the dividend cut removes the income appeal that supported the valuation. The constructive elements — stronger 2026 pipeline, energy hedged, operational efficiency investments — are medium-term not immediately estimate-moving.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Investec and Panmure Liberum will cut the stale consensus TP of £11.00 (set when EPS was 58p+) to approximately £4–7 range — a reduction of 36–64%. FY26e EPS will be initiated, likely in the 40–50p range depending on hospitality recovery assumptions and margin model. FY26e revenue likely modelled £77–80m. No current consensus to quantify the revision against. The watch point is H1 2026 trading — if the European and UK pipeline improvement translates to orders in H1, the earnings recovery case becomes credible. Without that evidence, the market will remain sceptical. 🏁 Score 28 — the EPS decline was largely anticipated, but the 45% dividend cut and absence of numeric FY26 guidance combine with stale TP to create a near-certain TP cut cycle; brokers will rebuild models from a lower base with cautious recovery assumptions.

scorecards.analysisText:
**Received after scorecard produced.-

Broker note received. Per standing instruction, score does not change.

Key calibration observations vs CLBS score of 38:

Where the score held up well:

  • Cavendish cuts TP from 275p → 200p — consistent with the "hold/trim TP" call in the revisions cell
  • FY27e EPS direction: Cavendish cuts from a positive trajectory to −2.05c, worse than my −10 to −20% range assumption (actual cut is more severe: FY27e revenue flat at $23.5m vs my assumed $24–25.5m, and FY27 moves to adj. loss territory not just EPS trim)
  • Cautious tone confirmed — Cavendish explicitly frames this as a "12-month delay" derisking exercise

Where I was too optimistic:

  • I modelled FY27e as a recovery year toward profitability. Cavendish keeps FY27 in loss territory (adj. PBT −$1.4m, EPS −2.05c). FY28 is the first recovery year at 2.03c. My "−10 to −20% EPS cut" framing understated the severity — the actual outcome is FY27 remains loss-making, not merely trimmed profitable.
  • ARR miss vs Cavendish's own model was $15.0m vs $16.4mE — a larger shortfall than I had characterised. Critically, Cavendish flags ARR grew to $15.6m in H1 FY26 before contracting to $15.0m in H2. This H2 ARR contraction is more bearish than the net $15.0m figure alone implies — it means new business losses exceeded renewals in H2, which is qualitatively worse than the RNS headline suggested.
  • My scoring treated the Cautious outlook at −6 pts for qualitative-only guidance. The actual broker response (TP −27%, two forward years in loss, FY27 revenue flat not growing) suggests the correct penalty was closer to −8 to −10 pts on the forward guidance component. Score should probably have been 32–35, not 38.

The key miss in the Phase 2 analysis: The RNS stated ARR of $15.0m without disclosing the H1 peak of $15.6m. Cavendish had the H1 interim figure and can therefore identify H2 ARR contraction explicitly. From the RNS alone this was not derivable — it's a genuine information asymmetry that the workflow couldn't capture at scoring time.

Hypothetically, with the H2 ARR contraction ($15.6m → $15.0m) known at scoring time:

Key changes to the component table:

FY27 revenue risk−5−6 — flat $23.5m (not growth) confirmed; FY27 provides zero operating leverage recovery
Beat quality divergence−3−4 — PBT beat is cost control while ARR is actively contracting in H2; divergence more severe

Net revision: −10 pts

Hypothetical score: ~28/100

That moves CLBS from the bottom of the red band into the 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected territory, which is where the actual broker outcome landed — TP cut 27%, two forward years in loss, FY27 revenue flat. The H2 ARR contraction is the single piece of information that would have shifted the tone classification from Cautious to Negative and the score below 30.

The standing instruction holds — 38 remains the filed score. But the calibration lesson is clear: for subscription/ARR businesses, always attempt to triangulate whether H2 ARR momentum held vs H1, even when the RNS only discloses a year-end figure.

PHASE 1 — CLBS · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

PHASE 2 — CLBS · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

1. Revenue figures

Full year FY26 revenues expected to be approximately $23.3 million, described as "broadly in line with expectations." Consensus per RNS footnote: $24.1m. Actual vs consensus: −$0.8m, −3.3% miss. Prior year (FY25): $38.7m → YoY −39.8%.
