2. EPS / adjusted profit

Adjusted loss before tax expected approximately $0.2m (FY25: profit $8.7m). Consensus: adjusted loss $0.3m. Beat of $0.1m vs consensus — "slightly ahead of expectations."

"at the pre-tax level we expect an adjusted loss before tax of approximately $0.2 million (FY25: profit of $8.7 million), slightly ahead of expectations and reflecting careful cost control through the second half."

FY27e EPS bridge: New base FY26 is a loss year (adj. PBT ~−$0.2m). FY27 consensus EPS = 1.9p. The bridge from loss to profit requires: (1) new base = adj. loss ~−$0.2m PBT; (2) inorganic delta = nil (no acquisitions); (3) organic ARR growth delta — FY26 ARR $15.0m (+10.3% YoY from $13.6m); applying similar growth rate to FY27 implies incremental ARR ~$1.5m; at high-margin software economics this could translate to ~$1.2–1.5m incremental PBT; (4) interest/other = minimal given cash-rich balance sheet. Implied FY27 adj. PBT from bridge: ~$1.0–1.3m. At 39.1m shares and ~22% tax: implied FY27 EPS ~1.3–1.7p vs Sharescope FY27 consensus 1.9p → bridge suggests consensus 1.9p is at the optimistic end; modest risk of downward revision on FY27 consensus. However, the ARR growth trajectory is the key determinant.

3. ARR / forward visibility

"Celebrus ARR is expected to be $15.0 million (FY25: $13.6 million), an increase in the year of 10.3%."

Two existing banking customers reduced footprint via divestitures. New business underdelivered. Several deals at contractual stage in Q4 lost or delayed.

"New business, via direct and partners, underdelivered against our expectations. Several deals at contractual stage in Q4 were lost or further delayed."

4. Cash

"The year-end cash balance was $32.0 million (FY25: $31.5 million), and the Group remains debt-free."

5. Margin / profitability

Revenue reduction explicitly attributed to accounting changes (contract restructuring from 1 April 2025 — straight-line revenue recognition, redefinition of cost of sales, segmentation of revenue type) rather than underlying activity reduction.

"The reduction results from the changes in the Group's contracts with customers...rather than from any reduction in underlying activity."

6. Qualitative tone / outlook

Looking ahead to FY27: focused on "optimizing approach in the market and improving consistency in new business generation." Pipeline described as "strong." "Good influx of new leads" at start of FY27.

"Our pipeline remains strong and we have started FY27 with a good influx of new leads."

EPS quality check: The company reports an adjusted loss before tax. No EPS beat — the metric is a small beat on loss quantum. The "beat" is $0.1m better than consensus loss. No tax distortion is material in a loss year. The accounting change (straight-line recognition) is a structural shift affecting FY26 and forward comparability — this is a one-time transition effect on reported revenues but does not affect cash or ARR. The ARR figure ($15.0m) is the cleaner underlying metric. No restatement required.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance covers FY27 only. Language is qualitative: "pipeline remains strong," "good influx of new leads," "focused on optimizing approach." No numeric FY27 guidance. No "not less than" language. No explicit comfort with consensus. The CEO statement explicitly flags FY26 as a year of "mix of both success and failure" and highlights failure in new logo acquisition.

New business underdelivery in Q4 FY26 is a forward risk signal — these were deals "at contractual stage" that were lost or delayed, meaning Q4 pipeline slippage carries into FY27.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only forward guidance following a year of new business underdelivery, with no numeric comfort on FY27, and a disclosed pipeline miss in Q4 that reduces visibility into the first half of FY27.

Provisional points: −5 to −8.

Divergence check: Current year delivered a marginal beat vs consensus (adj. PBT $0.1m better than expected, revenue $0.8m light). Outlook is Cautious. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery: the marginal PBT beat is cost-driven (H2 cost control), not revenue-driven, while the revenue miss and Q4 new business failures point forward negatively. The beat does not validate the business trajectory.

scorecards.analysisText:
CML

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results / pre-FY update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Phase 0A — Routing

Pre-FY mode confirmed. Q2. FY1 = FY26 (year end 31/3/26). Prior year = FY25. FY2 = FY27.

Note: FY26 year end was 31 March 2026 — this RNS is a full-year trading update (pre-prelims). The financial year is now closed.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

RNS references "Silicon Valley operations" (USD exposure) and UK/Asia/USA trading operations. No Currency Movements table. No explicit % of revenue by currency stated. Context suggests meaningful USD/international exposure but no single currency stated to exceed 30% with a quantified figure in this RNS. Apply conservative treatment: insufficient data to quantify — skip Phase 0B, note caveat.

Note: CML has international operations (USA, Asia) but has not disclosed currency split in this update. If USD > 30% of revenue, Phase 0B would apply. Insufficient data to apply penalty — flagged for next full annual report review.

Phase 1 — Data Context

CML · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: Pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY full-year trading update. FY1 = FY26, year end 31/3/26.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS — (no consensus) · Revenue — (no consensus). Sharescope consensus absent — no broker coverage consensus available.
  • FY2 consensus: EPS — · Revenue — (no consensus)
  • Forecast broker momentum: Snapshot data shows EPS forecast dropped from 7.9p to blank (lost coverage) by late Jun 2025. Net EPS change full period: 0.0% (but this reflects coverage dropout, not genuine estimate movement). Last-4-week trend: FLAT (blank/no data). No active consensus — single-broker or no-broker coverage situation.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue: 49.8% of FY. EPS: 63.9% (2yr avg — note quality concern given loss years). For EPS, 2yr avg includes loss periods; baseline unreliable for tracking purposes.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £12.5m · EPS 4.3p (adjusted; note FY25 full year EPS was −2.0p — significant H2 loss)
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY26 total revenue expected to "exceed £20m" per RNS. H1 actual £9.2m → implied H2 = >£10.8m vs FY25 H2 £10.4m → YoY +3.8% minimum. EPS: H1 FY26 −6.1p (loss); FY26 statutory PBT ~£1.8m (includes land disposal gains). Underlying operating loss continues in H2.
  • FX: Insufficient data — noted above.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): 3y ago H1: −£19.6m → 2y ago: −£13.4m → 1y ago: −£6.8m → current H1: −£6.8m → FY1fc: — → FY2fc: — · RNS states year-end net cash ~£11m (including £3m Oval Park balancing payment). ND/EBITDA: current −1.40x (net cash) · Interest cover: current 1.6x (very low — concern, though net cash position mitigates) · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — net cash £11m at year end; no debt.

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

CML · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (full-year closed, prelims 16 June 2026)

  1. Revenue — FY26 total expected to exceed £20m. H1 FY26 = £9.2m (from Sharescope current H1). H2 grew ~18% vs H1 FY26, so H2 implied ≈ £10.8m+. H2 also "ahead of H2 FY25" (£10.4m). Full-year guidance: "revenues are therefore expected to exceed £20m." "Full-year revenues are therefore expected to exceed £20m." "revenue grew by circa 18% compared to H1 FY26 and was also ahead of H2 FY25." % vs FY1 consensus: No consensus — cannot calculate beat/miss.
  2. EPS / earnings — operating loss continues in H2, improved vs H1. H1 FY26 operating loss (pre-exceptional) = £0.98m. H2 also an operating loss but "improved level compared to the first half." Statutory PBT FY26 ≈ £1.8m (vs FY25 statutory loss £0.7m) — driven by land disposal gains (Oval Park) and revaluation gain, partially offset by capitalised development cost impairment. Underlying operations remain loss-making. "the Group continued to invest in its Silicon Valley operations, delivering tangible improvements in our capacity and efficiency. These investments, taken alongside the timing and revenue mix effects, are expected to result in an operating loss for the second half, albeit at an improved level compared to the first half (H1 FY26 operating loss pre-exceptional gain on sale of land: £0.98m)." "we expect to report a statutory profit before tax of approximately £1.8m for FY26"
  3. Order book / forward work: GNSS contract (announced July 2025) — key contract driving NRE income in H2. H2 revenue mix skewed to lower-margin NRE. Shipments of a "key product" previously supply-chain affected were "restored in the closing months of FY26" — this product will "contribute more fully in FY27." "The shipments of a key product, previously affected by supply-chain issues, were restored in the closing months of FY26 and will contribute more fully in FY27."
  4. Margin / cost signals: H2 operating margin reduced by greater share of lower-margin NRE income. Investment in Silicon Valley continuing — cost headwind. R&D optimisation and target market vertical review completed — flagged as a positive for FY27 productivity/commercial efficiency. No margin figure disclosed. "The resulting revenue mix has reduced our second half operating margin due to a greater share of lower‑margin non‑recurring engineering (NRE) income"
  5. Capital returns / balance sheet: Net cash year-end ~£11m (includes £3m Oval Park balancing payment). Oval Park disposal completed 27 March 2026 — full process concluded. Remaining Group property revalued → revaluation gain + disposal profit (partially offset by impairment of capitalised development costs). No dividend stated. "Year-end net cash balances are predicted to be c.£11m which includes a £3m balancing payment relating to the Oval Park land disposal."
  6. Qualitative tone — FY27 recovery narrative. The RNS is explicitly forward-looking to FY27: timing effects to "unwind," key product resuming full contribution, industry inventory/supply chain normalisation, R&D optimisation completed. Tone is cautiously optimistic about FY27 but does not guide FY27 numbers. "Looking ahead to FY27, we expect that the timing effects seen in H2 FY26 will unwind."

EPS quality check: 🚨 Statutory PBT £1.8m is almost entirely driven by non-recurring land disposal gain (Oval Park) and property revaluation. Operating performance for FY26 is a loss at the PBT level on an underlying basis. The statutory profit figure has zero predictive value for FY27 EPS. Underlying EPS for FY26 is negative. The FY27 "growth" narrative is from a loss base — any positive EPS in FY27 would represent a recovery, not growth from a clean FY26 earnings base.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements for FY27:

  • "Timing effects seen in H2 FY26 will unwind" — positive but non-specific
  • Key product shipments resuming — tangible but unquantified
  • Industry inventory/supply chain "expected to show further progress" — cautious macro improvement
  • R&D and commercial efficiency improvements — internal, unquantified
  • No FY27 revenue or EPS guidance provided

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only FY27 guidance following a year of underlying operating losses. No numeric targets. Recovery is implied but unconfirmed. The statutory PBT "beat" (£1.8m vs FY25 loss £0.7m) is entirely non-recurring. From a purely forward earnings perspective, the company is guiding from a distorted base with unquantified recovery levers.

  • Exact guidance phrase: "we expect that the timing effects seen in H2 FY26 will unwind"
  • Guidance nature: qualitative-only
  • Year coverage: FY27 (one year)
  • Provisional points: −5 to −8
  • Divergence check: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery. The statutory PBT "improvement" (£1.8m vs −£0.7m) looks like a beat but is entirely non-recurring. Underlying operations remain loss-making. The Cautious FY27 classification correctly reflects the underlying reality, but the divergence between headline statutory improvement and underlying continuation of losses is a flag that should be carried explicitly.

Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking

CML · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

Known Sharescope glitch flagged in data. Use explicit FY figure −2.0p. Derive H2 = −2.0 − 4.3 = −6.3p (not −4.3p as in Sharescope). ⚠️ Use −6.3p for FY25 H2 throughout.
  • FY26: H1 £9.2m (Sharescope current H1) · Revenue "exceeds £20m" (floor) → implied H2 > £10.8m. EPS: H1 −6.1p (Sharescope current H1 — noting this is a Sharescope current field value; Phase 3.2 data source gate applies to tracking deviation only; here using as reference for derivation). Statutory PBT ~£1.8m but entirely non-recurring. Operating EPS approximately −£0.98m H1 + improved loss H2 = full year underlying EPS negative. No clean FY26 EPS figure.

"The disposal of the final plot of land at our UK headquarters, Oval Park, completed on 27 March 2026... resulting in a revaluation gain alongside the profit on disposal"
  • Broker coverage loss. EPS forecasts went blank from late June 2025. This is a structural negative for the stock's investability.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation

CML · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 Driver — Underlying operating losses in both H1 and H2; full-year operating losses despite "beat" headline. The statutory PBT of ~£1.8m is entirely non-recurring. Brokers who remained covering this stock (if any) will focus on the continuation of underlying operating losses into H2 and the absence of any numeric recovery guidance for FY27. This is the primary reason any remaining broker is unlikely to initiate or maintain positive forecasts.

#2 Driver — Revenue floor >£20m (below FY25 £22.9m) combined with NRE margin dilution. Revenue has fallen back below the FY23 level. The H2 margin mix problem (lower-margin NRE dominating) means even the incremental revenue growth (+18% H2 vs H1) does not translate to profitability improvement. This combination — falling revenues, deteriorating mix, ongoing losses — is the primary revision driver.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 EPS: No change possible — no consensus exists. If a broker re-initiates, they would set underlying EPS at a negative figure for FY26.
  • FY1 Revenue: Floor >£20m guides below FY25 £22.9m. Any broker reinitiating would set ~£20–21m (below prior year).
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: Recovery narrative exists but is unquantified. A broker initiating FY27 would likely forecast a return to modest positive EPS (2–5p) contingent on supply chain normalisation and key product ramp. High uncertainty.
  • Net FY1 EPS revision direction: cut (from any prior positive estimate; or initiate negative).

Target price and recommendation: No consensus TP available. Shore Capital (house broker) is the likely sole remaining broker. Post these results, they would likely maintain coverage but with a Hold or reduced TP, reflecting the ongoing losses and limited near-term visibility.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Timing effects will unwind" is positive framing but brokers will note this is the second consecutive year of timing/mix disappointments. The GNSS contract NRE income issue is presented as phasing but brokers may question whether low-margin NRE income is becoming a structural revenue mix problem rather than a temporary one.

Key risk: The net cash of £11m has declined from £19.6m three years ago — a £8.6m cash burn over three years while the business runs operating losses. If FY27 recovery does not materialise, the cash runway becomes a concern within 2–3 years.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = cut. Tone must be Cautious or Negative. Assigning: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — Cautious rather than Negative because (a) net cash intact, (b) explicit FY27 recovery narrative with tangible levers (key product, supply chain), (c) R&D optimisation completed.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable.

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

28/100 · Confidence: 22–34 · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

🟢 Net cash £11m — no balance sheet risk, operational breathing room+5
🟢 FY27 recovery levers — key product resuming, supply chain easing, R&D optimised+4

🟡 Beat quality — statutory PBT improvement entirely non-recurring; forward guidance diverges−3

🔴 Revenue declining YoY — FY26 floor below FY23 level; three-year revenue stagnation−3

Raw score before Phase 0B: 28. No FX adjustment applied.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline statutory PBT of ~£1.8m (vs FY25 loss of £0.7m) is misleading and should be stripped immediately. The improvement is entirely non-recurring — Oval Park land disposal completed 27 March 2026 plus property revaluation gain, partially offset by capitalised development cost impairment. The underlying picture is an operating loss in both H1 (−£0.98m pre-exceptional) and H2 (improved but still a loss). The single most important number in this RNS is full-year revenue expected to exceed £20m — a floor figure that sits below the FY24 and FY25 £22.9m level and confirms that CML's top line has contracted back to FY23 levels. The H2 sequential improvement (+18% vs H1 FY26, ahead of H2 FY25) is the only genuine positive, but it arrives against a very weak H1 comparator.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 momentum is classified 🟡 moderate on revenue (>£10.8m vs FY25 H2 £10.4m, +3.8% YoY minimum) and 🔴 weak on EPS (loss continuation). There is no upgrade resilience case in any conventional sense — the company has no active broker consensus, no positive earnings, and no numeric FY27 guidance. The recovery narrative rests on: (1) a "key product" returning to full shipment in FY27 after supply chain disruption; (2) GNSS NRE income phasing unwinding; (3) industry inventory/supply chain normalisation. These are plausible levers but each is contingent and unquantified. The cash position (£11m net cash) is the only structural buffer, but it has declined by £8.6m over three years of underlying losses — if FY27 does not deliver a return to operating profitability, the cash runway question will become pressing within 2 years.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: With no active consensus, formal broker revision ranges cannot be calculated. Shore Capital (sole likely broker) would set FY26 underlying EPS at approximately −3 to −5p (stripping land gains) and FY27 at +2 to +5p recovery — a high-variance, high-uncertainty range. No consensus TP. The stock at 227p trades on the back of its net cash (£11m = 66p per share) and the option value on the FY27 recovery; the operational enterprise value is thin. The main watch point is the 16 June 2026 preliminary results, where the underlying loss quantum and FY27 guidance quality will either validate or invalidate the recovery narrative. 🏁 Score 28 — cautious: this is an operationally loss-making business with declining revenues and no active broker consensus; the non-recurring land disposal flatters the statutory headline, and FY27 recovery is qualitative-only; net cash is the primary risk buffer but is being consumed; no basis for broker upgrades, and the absence of consensus coverage is itself a persistent negative signal.

CNC — Concurrent Technologies

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

CNC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY25 full year results. Market was expecting FY guidance or confirmation.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 6.7p · Revenue £46.0m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 8.1p · Revenue £52.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +4.7% (+0.3p, 6.4p→6.7p) over snapshot period. One upgrade cycle visible (Sep 2025 step from 6.4p→6.9p post H1 results, then minor drift to 6.7p Feb 2026). Net: 1 upgrade, 1 small downgrade. Revenue moved 43→46m (+7%). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT last 4 weeks at 6.7p).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 40.1% of FY = £18.5m · EPS: H1 EPS avg unavailable — Sharescope H1 EPS fields all show Sharescope glitch (negative H2 values, FY figures appear correct). H1 avg split flagged n/a.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £21.1m (current H1 per Sharescope) · EPS: H1 2.8p (current H1 per Sharescope — note this is FY25 H1)
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY25 actual £45.9m − H1 £21.1m = implied H2 £24.8m vs prior H2 £23.5m (FY24) → +5.5% YoY. EPS: H1 EPS data unreliable due to known Sharescope H2 glitch (all historical H2 EPS fields negative/corrupt). FY25 actual EPS 5.86p (basic) / using diluted 5.58p. Cannot derive clean H2 EPS split from Sharescope.
  • FX: CNC discloses USD as primary non-GBP currency (~52% of revenues in US). Phase 0B triggered — assessed below.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: FY23 £4.8m → FY24 £13.7m → FY25 £14.4m (actual) · FY26e £15.0m fc · FY27e £14.3m fc · ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash) → 🟢 Unlevered / net cash

Phase 0B FX assessment: US revenues = 52% of FY25 total (£23.9m). Exceeds 30% threshold. CFO notes USD peaked at $1.38/£1 during FY25, described as "a challenge." RNS does not provide a formal Currency Movements table with prior year average rate disclosed as a single figure. From context: FY24 USD/GBP avg approximately $1.27/£1 (implied from prior year disclosures); FY25 avg rate materially weaker USD (stronger GBP). GBP strengthened significantly vs USD during FY25. Applying 35–50% band + GBP headwind >3c: penalty 🔴 [−10 pts]. However — note the CFO explicitly states hedging activity and natural hedge from USD suppliers. Applying mid-point adjustment for partial natural hedge: effective penalty −8 pts applied.

FX badge: 🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · 52% USD · GBP headwind

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CNC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual £45.9m vs FY1 consensus £46.0m Beat/miss: −£0.1m, −0.2% — essentially in line. Products £40.5m (+6% vs FY24 £38.2m). Systems £5.4m (+157% vs FY24 £2.1m).

"Group revenue for FY25 increased to £45.9m (FY24: £40.3m)"

2. EPS / earnings — FY25 basic EPS 5.86p vs FY1 consensus 6.7p Miss: −0.84p, −12.5% vs consensus. Diluted EPS 5.58p. PBT £6.5m (+25% vs FY24 £5.2m). Note: FY1 consensus 6.7p was set post-H1 upgrade in September 2025 when brokers moved to 6.9p, then drifted to 6.7p. RNS-actual basic EPS = 5.86p.

"Basic earnings per share 5.86p (2024: 5.49p)"

EPS quality check: Tax charge FY25 = £1.458m on PBT £6.517m = effective rate 22.4%. Standard UK corporation tax rate = 25%. Effective rate is 2.6pp below normalised rate — within the 3pp threshold. No restatement required. However, note exceptional items of −£145,805 and other income of +£206,557 are both small. EPS beat is not distorted by tax or one-offs; the miss vs consensus is genuine.

FY26e EPS bridge (construct here, reference in Phase 4 #2):

  • New base: FY25 actual diluted EPS = 5.58p (basic 5.86p; using diluted as most conservative)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: Phillips Aerospace acquired Sep 2023 — now fully annualised in FY24 and FY25. No new acquisition in FY25. Systems contributed £5.4m revenue. Delta = nil (full year in base).
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY25 EBITDA £10.1m vs FY24 £7.8m. Board guides FY26 "in line with market expectations" = FY26 consensus PBT £8.0m. Organic EBITDA growth consensus FY26 = £11.0m (Sharescope). Implied organic growth from £10.1m EBITDA → £11.0m = +8.9%. Applied to diluted EPS base 5.58p → organic delta +0.50p.
  • Interest step-up delta: No debt drawdowns >£50m. Finance costs FY25 = £125k vs FY24 £93k (+34% YoY). Finance costs are immaterial (£125k on £45.9m revenue). Step-up delta = negligible, ~nil.
  • FX drag on FY26e: USD continued to weaken post year-end; material risk to FY26 translation. Not quantified in bridge but flagged.
  • Implied FY26e EPS from bridge: 5.58 + 0.50 = ~6.1p vs Sharescope FY2 consensus 8.1p.

⚠️ Bridge implies ~6.1p vs stale consensus 8.1p — a potential −25% shortfall. The consensus may not reflect the EPS miss in FY25 (actual 5.86p basic vs 6.7p expected). FY1 consensus has not been revised down post-results. This is the critical risk item.

3. Order book / forward work Record order intake £47.0m FY25 (FY24: £41.0m, +15%). Design wins FY25 = estimated lifetime value £145m.

"Total order intake increased to a record £47m, driven by deepening relationships with global defence primes"

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin 53.3% (FY24: 49.4%), +3.9pp. Products gross margin 57% (FY24: 50%). Systems gross margin 16% (FY24: −7%). EBITDA £10.1m (FY24: £7.8m, +29%). PBT margin 14.2% (FY24: 12.9%). Cost base +£3.2m driven by headcount (+28 UK, +3 US) and amortisation +£0.8m. Amortisation expected to continue increasing.

"Gross profit increased to £24.5m (FY24: £20m), resulting in a gross margin of 53.3% (FY24: 49.4%)"

5. Capital returns / cash Net cash £14.4m (FY24: £13.7m). Final dividend 1.155p (FY24: 1.1p) — modest +5% increase. Rolling Credit Facility established for flexibility. FY26 capex: new Colchester facility planned (significant investment). Cash from operations £7.0m, investing outflow £5.3m.

6. Qualitative tone / outlook Board "confident of delivering results for FY26 in line with market expectations." FY26 market expectations explicitly stated: revenue £52.0m, PBT £8.0m (as at 10 April 2026). Systems expected to achieve breakeven or beyond in FY26. Five new products already launched post-period end.

"the Board is confident of delivering results for FY26 in line with market expectations"

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance phrase: "confident of delivering results for FY26 in line with market expectations" — with market expectations explicitly anchored at revenue £52.0m, PBT £8.0m.

Numeric or qualitative: numeric-anchored (company has explicitly stated the market consensus figures it is in line with). Covers one year (FY26). No second-year guidance.

However: critical divergence — FY25 actual EPS 5.86p vs consensus 6.7p = −12.5% miss. The FY26 consensus of 8.1p EPS has not been revised down to reflect the lower FY25 base. If brokers rebuild from FY25 actual 5.86p, reaching 8.1p FY26 requires +38% EPS growth. Bridge implies ~6.1p. PBT guidance of £8.0m is achievable, but EPS of 8.1p from a 5.86p base implies margin/tax assumptions that need stress-testing.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — guidance is "in line with market expectations" with explicit numeric anchor. However, the FY25 EPS miss creates a divergence risk: current year EPS missed but PBT/revenue guidance maintained. This is a mixed signal.

🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery: Revenue in line, PBT +25% beat, but EPS −12.5% miss vs consensus. Brokers will need to reconcile lower FY25 EPS base with unchanged FY26 EPS consensus. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

CNC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS trend: 6.4p → 6.9p (Sep 2025 upgrade post-H1) → 6.7p (Feb 2026 small cut) = net +4.7% from snapshot start. Revenue: 43→46m = +7.0%. Upgrades: 1 clear step-up (Sep 2025). Downgrades: 1 minor (Feb 2026, −0.2p). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT).

Divergence: Price has drifted from 287p (early 2026) to 207.5p current (-27.6%) while EPS consensus held at 6.7p. Significant negative price/earnings divergence — market has de-rated CNC materially ahead of this results announcement.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

Net cash/(cash): FY22 £4.8m → FY23 £7.8m → FY24 £13.7m → FY25 H1 £7.8m → FY25 actual £14.4m → FY26e £15.0m → FY27e £14.3m. ND/EBITDA: consistently negative (net cash position) across all periods. Interest cover FY25: effectively unconstrained (interest costs £125k on £10.1m EBITDA). ND/FCF: −6.4x (FY26e) — negative = net cash.

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — balance sheet is not a constraint on estimates. No scored row in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24:

  • FY25 actual EPS 5.86p vs FY24 actual 5.49p → ✅ growing +6.7%
  • FY25 actual revenue £45.9m vs FY24 £40.3m → ✅ growing +13.9%
  • ✅✅ FY1 actual EPS and Revenue growing vs prior year.

Step 2 — FY26e vs FY25:

  • FY26e EPS 8.1p vs FY25 actual 5.86p → ✅ growing (but consensus stale — has not been revised post-results)
  • FY26e Revenue £52.0m vs FY25 £45.9m → ✅ growing +13.3%
  • ✅✅ FY2 fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY1 — but ⚠️ FY1 fc consensus 6.7p was pre-results stale; actual was 5.86p. FY26e 8.1p is set against a 6.7p base that will now be revised down. True FY26e growth from the correct base is much higher, suggesting the 8.1p EPS consensus will be materially cut.

6. Structural flags:

  • EPS consensus staleness: FY1 fc 6.7p was not revised following the EPS miss (actual 5.86p). Brokers held at 6.7p through Feb 2026. Post-results, the FY25 base is now confirmed 5.86p, creating a ~13% cut to the implied FY26 earnings growth starting point.
  • Systems breakeven narrative: "We expect this [Systems] to achieve breakeven or beyond in FY26" — Systems lost £0.3m in FY25 despite 157% revenue growth. Breakeven adds ~£0.3m PBT but limited EPS impact (~0.3p).
  • Amortisation headwind: "Amortisation increased by £0.8m... We expect amortisation to continue increasing" — this is a growing EPS headwind as R&D spending reaches capitalisation phase completion.
  • FX structural risk: USD accounts for ~52% of revenues. GBP/USD rate "peaked at $1.38" in FY25. Current USD weakness is an ongoing headwind for FY26 translation.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

CNC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — EPS miss vs stale consensus: The single dominant driver is the gap between reported basic EPS of 5.86p and FY1 consensus of 6.7p (−12.5%). This is not a quality miss — PBT grew 25%, gross margin expanded 3.9pp, cash generation was strong. The issue is purely that FY1 consensus sat at 6.7p and was not revised down ahead of results despite a Feb 2026 drift to 6.7p from 6.9p. Brokers will immediately rebase FY26e from 5.86p actual, triggering mandatory cuts to FY26e EPS consensus which currently stands at 8.1p.

#2 Driver — FY26 PBT guidance "in line" at £8.0m anchored explicitly: The Board has anchored FY26 expectations at revenue £52.0m / PBT £8.0m. PBT £8.0m is achievable and represents +23% growth from FY25 £6.5m. However, the path from PBT £8.0m to EPS will depend on tax rate, amortisation growth, and share count. Brokers modelling EPS from PBT £8.0m at 22% tax and ~87m diluted shares get to approximately 7.2p — not 8.1p. This further suggests 8.1p consensus will be cut.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY25e): Finalised. No revision — results in line with revenue/PBT consensus but EPS missed by ~13%. Brokers will annotate actuals.
  • FY2 (FY26e) EPS: Expected cut — from 8.1p stale consensus toward 6.5–7.2p range. Magnitude: −10% to −20%. Bridge implies ~6.1p; PBT-derived estimate ~7.2p. Central estimate: revised FY26e EPS ~6.8–7.0p (−14% to −16% from stale 8.1p).
  • FY2 (FY26e) Revenue: Likely held at £52.0m — company has explicitly guided this figure.
  • FY2 (FY26e) PBT: Likely held at £8.0m — explicitly guided.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers will almost certainly cut consensus TP. Current consensus TP = 287p; current price 207.5p (38% discount to TP). Post-EPS rebase, TP likely revised down to 230–260p range (−10% to −19%). Recommendations likely held at Buy/Add given underlying PBT growth and order book, but conviction will reduce. Record order intake £47m and £145m lifetime design win value provide structural support.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Confident of delivering results for FY26 in line with market expectations" — company has defined the market expectations numerically (£52.0m rev, £8.0m PBT). This is borderline cautious phrasing on the EPS dimension. PBT guidance is credible; EPS interpretation depends on broker modelling. No "not less than" or "ahead" language — this is a ceiling not a floor read-through.

Key risk: The stale FY26e EPS consensus of 8.1p will be rebased by every broker covering CNC after this announcement. That mechanical rebase, driven solely by the lower FY25 actual EPS base, creates a one-for-one headwind even if the business performs exactly as guided. Additionally, FX (USD weakness, ~52% of revenues) is an unquantified but material ongoing drag not yet reflected in FY26e revenue consensus of £52.0m. "The US dollar (USD) has been a challenge in FY25 with major movements in the rate, peaking at $1.38 to £1 towards the end of the year."

Consistency check: Net FY2 EPS revision direction: cut (8.1p → ~6.8–7.0p). Tone must be Cautious or Negative. → 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

CNC

38/100 · Confidence: 33–43 · FX: −8 pts applied (52% USD, GBP headwind) · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

ComponentPts
🟢 Record order intake £47m (+15% YoY) — multi-year visibility+8
🟢 Gross margin expansion +3.9pp to 53.3% — structural quality improvement+6
🟢 PBT +25% YoY to £6.5m — underlying business performing+5
🟢 Net cash £14.4m, strong balance sheet+3
🟢 FY26 PBT £8.0m guidance explicitly anchored by company+3
🟡 In-line revenue — £45.9m vs £46.0m consensus, negligible miss−1
🟡 Systems breakeven narrative (£0.3m loss FY25) — limited EPS uplift−1
🟡 H2 momentum moderate revenue (+5.5% YoY) — decelerating top-line−3
🔴 EPS miss −12.5% vs stale consensus (5.86p actual vs 6.7p expected)−12
🔴 FY26e EPS consensus 8.1p materially overstated vs likely revised ~6.8–7.0p−8
🔴 FX headwind — USD 52% revenues, GBP headwind Phase 0B−8
🔴 Amortisation rising headwind + cost base growth (£3.2m YoY)−4

Raw score before FX: 46 · FX penalty −8 → Final: 38

Para 1 — Headline numbers: CNC delivered FY25 revenue of £45.9m (consensus £46.0m, −0.2% miss, immaterial), PBT of £6.5m (+25% YoY) and gross margin of 53.3% (+3.9pp) — operationally a strong year. The definitive catalyst, however, is the EPS miss: basic EPS of 5.86p vs FY1 consensus of 6.7p = −12.5%. This miss is not driven by operational weakness — it reflects a tax-on-higher-profit arithmetic, rising amortisation (£2.3m vs £1.9m prior year), and a consensus that had not been properly re-anchored following the interim results. The EPS miss is the dominant signal that will drive broker action.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, H2 momentum is the operative lens. H2 revenue of £24.8m vs prior year £23.5m = +5.5% YoY (🟡 moderate) — decelerating from H2 FY23 +79% and FY24 +21%. H2 EPS (basic, derived) 3.06p vs FY24 H2 2.5p = +22.4% — healthy at the earnings level despite the revenue deceleration, supported by margin expansion. The upgrade resilience rests on: (i) record order intake £47m with £145m lifetime design win value, (ii) Systems on a trajectory to breakeven from −£0.3m loss, (iii) net cash of £14.4m with no leverage risk. The bear case — that FY26 EPS consensus of 8.1p is materially stale relative to the 5.86p actual base — is well-founded and creates a mechanical cut cycle even if the business executes perfectly on PBT guidance.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will cut FY26e EPS consensus from 8.1p to approximately 6.8–7.2p (−14% to −16%), driven purely by rebasing from the lower FY25 actuals. FY26e revenue consensus of £52.0m and PBT £8.0m are likely held, as the company has explicitly guided these figures with confidence. Target price will be cut from 287p consensus to approximately 230–260p (−10% to −20%), reflecting the lower earnings base. Revenue consensus acceleration flag (Column 6) fires neutral. The watch point is whether any broker models the USD/GBP FX drag into FY26e revenue — at $1.38/£1 peak rate, 52% USD revenue exposure is a meaningful translation headwind that the £52.0m consensus may not fully capture. 🏁 Score 38 — the PBT delivery is real and the order book is genuinely strong, but the EPS shortfall vs stale consensus triggers an unavoidable broker rebase cycle; expect FY26e EPS cuts of 14–16% and TP reductions of 10–20%.

scorecards.analysisText:
COG — Cambridge Cognition

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

COG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY25 full year results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS: no consensus (blank/negative). Revenue £9.5m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS: no consensus. Revenue £12.1m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change: 0.7p → −2.2p (massive downgrade cycle, −414%). Revenue: 12.6m → 9.5m (−25%). Consensus was comprehensively cut in July/August 2025 (EPS from +0.7p to −1.9p, revenue 12.6→9.5m). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT last 4 weeks — no EPS figure available in final weeks).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue: 48.5% × £9.5m = £4.6m. EPS: loss-making — no meaningful baseline.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £5.6m (FY24 H1) · EPS −2.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (FY25): Revenue: FY25 £9.4m actual − H1 £4.3m (Sharescope current H1) = H2 £5.1m vs FY24 H2 £4.7m → +8.5% YoY. EPS H2: FY25 actual EPS −4.3p (FY24) per Sharescope 1y ago. FY25 actuals needed.
  • FX: COG is a UK company — revenues largely GBP denominated. No Phase 0B triggered.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net position: improving from net debt £1.7m (FY24) to net cash £0.3m (FY25 disclosed). FY26e net cash £0.1m → FY27e £0.5m. ND/EBITDA: not meaningful (small losses). Interest cover: not applicable. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (marginally).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

COG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual £9.4m vs FY1 consensus £9.5m Miss: −£0.1m, −1.1% — essentially in line. Down 9% vs FY24 £10.3m as expected given weak opening order book.

"Revenues of c.£9.4m down 10% (2024: £10.3m)"

2. EPS / earnings Adjusted EBITDA loss of £(0.5)m (FY24: £nil). No EPS consensus available to compare against. FY25 statutory EPS derivation not possible from RNS summary — loss-making at EBITDA level. Cash from operations: positive £0.1m (first time since 2022). Positive operational cash generation is a meaningful inflection.

EPS quality check: Not applicable — company in loss. No tax distortion relevant.

FY26e bridge (indicative): Order book at 31 Dec 2025 = £16.5m of which £8.8m expected as FY26 revenue. RNS states at date of announcement (13 April 2026) the company expects FY26 revenue of £9.5m. This already exceeds the order book-derived £8.8m due to Q1 new orders of £2.6m.

  • New base: FY25 EBITDA loss £(0.5)m. FY26 consensus EBITDA = £(0.3)m (Sharescope). Bridge: revenue growth from £9.4m → £9.5m adds ~£0.1m revenue. At 75% gross margin, ~£0.1m gross profit uplift. Cost base largely fixed → minimal flow-through. FY26 EBITDA ~£(0.3)m to £(0.1)m. EPS consensus blank — loss-making status persists in FY26.

3. Order book Order book at year-end: £16.5m (+21% vs £13.6m). Of this, £8.8m expected FY26 revenue. New sales orders FY25: £12.8m (+73% vs £7.4m FY24). Q1 2026 new orders: £2.6m.

"New sales orders in year up 73% to £12.8m (2024: £7.4m)"

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin: 75% (FY24 restated: 78% — 3pp decline). Adjusted EBITDA: −£0.5m. R&D expense fell 22% to £2.0m. Cost base broadly flat despite revenue decline. Clinical studies EBITDA margin 41% (FY24: 47%). The revenue miss flows straight through to gross profit at ~100% drop-through given fixed staff cost base.

5. Cash / balance sheet Cash £1.1m (June 2025 £0.4m; Dec 2024 £1.3m). Borrowings reduced from £1.9m → £0.9m. Net cash £0.2m (per RNS: "net cash position of c.£0.3m"). Placing in Aug 2025: £1.1m gross proceeds. Deferred income £5.4m (stable — critical liquidity metric).

"Reduced borrowing to £0.9m (December 2024: £1.9m), resulting in a net cash position of c.£0.3m"

6. Qualitative tone / outlook FY26 revenue guidance: £9.5m explicitly guided (company states this at announcement date). "We are confident that the Company will show good revenue growth in 2026." Q1 FY26 new orders £2.6m (vs Q1 2025 £4.2m — lower, but prior year Q1 was exceptionally strong).

"At the date of this announcement the Company expects to deliver 2026 revenue of £9.5m, supported by the current Order Book and revenue recognised to date"

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 revenue guidance of £9.5m is explicitly anchored — effectively in line with FY26 consensus £9.5m (Sharescope). Growth expected but modest (+1% from FY25 £9.4m). However, the company notes Q2–Q4 new orders will add further, and "expects to see growth in revenue in the current year." No EPS consensus to compare against.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY26 revenue guidance equals consensus. No upgrade or downgrade signal. EPS: loss-making — no meaningful comparison. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

No divergence: Order book turnaround positive but revenue and profitability remain under pressure — consistent signals.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

COG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Note: Sharescope FY1 fc EPS blank for FY25 and FY26e. Company is loss-making throughout.

Revenue growth trajectory: +7.1% → −23.7% → −8.7% → 🔴 Decelerating (recovering from trough but still negative). FY26 guided +1.1% — tentative inflection.

EPS trajectory: Loss-making throughout — 🔴 Decelerating (deepening losses FY22→FY23; partial recovery FY24; FY25 worse EBITDA but Q1 cash positive).

Acceleration flags: Rev FY26 +1.1% vs FY25 −8.7% → acceleration ✓ (consensus). EPS: no data. Column 6 REV: pos ✓ (marginal). Column 6 EPS: na (—).

EPS trajectory: Loss-making throughout — not classifiable.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY (pre-H1 mode only — written in full, no Phase 5 row)

Revenue 3yr avg H1 split = 48.5%. At FY26 guidance £9.5m: H1 baseline = £4.6m. Current H1 Sharescope shows £4.3m for FY25 H1. Buy trigger for next H1 results: £4.6m × 1.015 = £4.7m.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

EPS H2: loss-making, not classifiable.

Classification: 🟡 moderate (revenue only trackable metric).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS: 0.7p → −2.2p (−414%) — severe downgrade cycle completed Aug 2025. Revenue: 12.6m → 9.5m (−25%). 4-week: STALLING (flat). The consensus has been deeply cut and has been static since August 2025 — no further deterioration, which is itself mildly positive.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Net cash/debt: FY22 −£8.6m → FY23 −£1.9m → FY24 +£1.7m (debt) → FY25 +£1.1m cash → FY26e ~£0.1m. Loan of £0.9m (due to be repaid H2 2026). Deferred income £5.4m. ND/EBITDA: not meaningful. Interest cover: not applicable. No leverage risk.

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (marginally). No Phase 5 row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY25 revenue £9.4m vs FY24 £10.3m → 🚨 FY1 Revenue −8.7% below prior year (expected, due to order book lag). EPS: loss in both years — no positive comparison possible.

Step 2: FY26e £9.5m vs FY25 £9.4m → ✅ growing (+1.1%). EPS: no consensus.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

COG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — New sales orders +73% to £12.8m: This is the dominant positive signal. The order book has been rebuilt from £13.6m → £16.5m, providing FY26 revenue visibility of £8.8m (upgraded to £9.5m with Q1 additions). For a company whose revenue declined because of the prior year order book weakness, this is the leading indicator that breaks the negative cycle. The revenue lag (orders → revenue ~12–18 months) means FY26 is now largely secured.

#2 Driver — Operational cash generation positive for first time since 2022: £0.1m positive cash from operations, stabilised deferred income at £5.4m, and borrowings halved to £0.9m. These are balance sheet repair signals that reduce dilution risk and improve credibility of the recovery narrative.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY25e) Revenue: £9.4m actual vs £9.5m consensus = −1% miss. Essentially in line. No material revision.
  • FY1 (FY25e) EPS: No consensus. Loss-making — no numeric broker EPS revision applicable.
  • FY2 (FY26e) Revenue: FY26 guidance £9.5m = consensus £9.5m → hold. If Q2–Q4 orders surprise, upside is possible.
  • FY2 (FY26e) EPS: No consensus. Company guiding toward reduced loss — minor improvement possible.

Target price / recommendation: Consensus TP = 56p vs price 39p (44% discount). Given the order book improvement and cash stabilisation, TP likely held or modestly cut (FY25 EBITDA miss of −£0.5m vs expected £nil). Cavendish/Singer unlikely to cut TP given the structural order book improvement is the investment case driver.

Conservative guidance read-through: No "not less than" language. FY26 revenue anchored at £9.5m = consensus. No upgrade signal. Company notes Q2–Q4 orders will add further — this is mildly bullish for the out-year.

Key risk: Q1 FY26 new sales orders of only £2.6m vs Q1 2025 £4.2m (−38%). "New sales orders in Q1 were £2.6m (Q1 2025: £4.2m)" — if this represents a trend rather than a timing effect, the H2 revenue generation for FY26 and FY27 could be materially weaker than the order book implied.

Consistency check: FY2 EPS revision: hold (no consensus, no numeric change). Revenue: hold. Tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

COG

36/100 · Confidence: 30–42 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 New sales orders +73% to £12.8m — order book rebuilt+12
🟢 Order book £16.5m (+21%) → FY26 revenue £9.5m largely secured+8
🟢 First positive operating cash flow since 2022+5
🟢 Net cash achieved (£0.3m) — dilution risk reduced+3
🟡 FY26 revenue guidance £9.5m = consensus — no upgrade signal−2
🟡 H2 momentum moderate (+8.5% revenue YoY)−2
🔴 Revenue −9% YoY FY25 — ongoing decline vs prior year−6
🔴 EBITDA loss widened to −£0.5m (FY24: £nil)−8
🔴 Q1 FY26 new orders £2.6m vs £4.2m prior year — early warning−6
🔴 No EPS consensus — unquantifiable earnings recovery trajectory−3
🔴 CANTAB Pathway healthcare/consumer revenues not yet materialised−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: COG delivered FY25 revenue of £9.4m (consensus £9.5m, −1%, in line), with adjusted EBITDA of −£0.5m (FY24: £nil) — a deterioration at the profitability line but one that was widely anticipated given the weak opening order book. The definitive positive catalyst is new sales orders of £12.8m, +73%, rebuilding the order book to £16.5m (+21%) and providing FY26 revenue visibility of £9.5m already secured. The company has moved to positive operating cash generation for the first time since 2022 and achieved net cash. These are structural repair signals.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £5.1m = +8.5% YoY (🟡 moderate) — the first positive H2 YoY comparison in two years, signalling the trough has passed. The upgrade resilience for FY26 rests almost entirely on the order book: £8.8m of FY26 revenue is already in the book, upgraded to £9.5m with Q1 additions. The risk to the bull case is the Q1 FY26 new orders of £2.6m vs £4.2m prior year — a 38% decline that, if sustained, would erode FY27 revenue visibility. The company attributes this to timing, and the pipeline is described as "strong," but the Q1 data point is a genuine watch risk.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Cavendish and Singer (joint brokers) will likely hold FY26 revenue consensus at £9.5m — the company has guided this explicitly. EPS consensus remains absent; no numeric revision. TP of 56p vs price 39p likely held given the order book recovery narrative intact. The key watch point is H1 2026 new orders — "We will report again following the end of H1" — confirming that the H1 new order momentum is the next de-risking event. 🏁 Score 36 — structural order book repair and cash stabilisation are real positives, but EBITDA deterioration, a Q1 orders miss, and absence of EPS consensus visibility combine to produce a Neutral broker reaction; no meaningful estimate changes likely today.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

CRST · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/10/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (titled "Trading Update", issued 21 April 2026, covers period since 25 March AGM update)

1. Revenue / Volume — explicit guidance cut

Volume guidance cut to 1,400–1,500 units from prior guidance of 1,550–1,700 units — a reduction of 150–200 units at midpoint (~10% cut to the midpoint of 1,625 → 1,450).

"…reducing its volume expectations to 1,400 to 1,500 units (previously 1,550 to 1,700 units). The current order book for the financial year stands at 1,106 units."

Land sale revenue cut to c.£40m from prior guidance of £75–100m — a cut of £47.5m at midpoint (~55% reduction).

"The Group is now anticipating a reduced number of land sales, with expected revenue of c. £40m (previously £75m to £100m)."

"…the Group does not expect to make a material level of profit on disposals in the remainder of the financial year."

Combined effect vs FY26e consensus £620.7m: volume revenue impact at £250–270k ASP per unit × ~150 unit midpoint cut ≈ £37–40m; land revenue cut ≈ −£47.5m midpoint vs prior guidance. Total implied revenue miss vs pre-RNS consensus is likely £60–80m, putting FY26e revenue in the range of £540–560m — approximately 10–13% below prior consensus of £620.7m.

2. EPS / EBIT — explicit profit warning with guided range

EBIT guided to £5m–£15m with interest costs of c.£15m → implied PBT of £(10)m to £0m. This compares to prior consensus PBT of £35.6m — a cut of £36–46m or ~100–130% below prior consensus.

"As a result of these revised assumptions the Group now expects to achieve an EBIT for the financial year of around £5m to £15m, with interest costs of c. £15m and a revised year end net debt position of £100m to £120m."

Implied EPS: PBT of £(10)m to £0m → tax likely nil/minimal at these levels → EPS implied 0p to flat, vs prior FY26e consensus of 9.8p. This is a near-total consensus wipe-out.

FY26e EPS bridge (for Phase 4): New base = ~0–1p (FY26 actuals). For FY27e (FY2), organic recovery would need to be modelled from a dramatically lower base. With net debt guided £100–120m at year end (vs prior £44.9m fc), interest costs step up materially in FY27e as well. Prior FY27e consensus of 12.8p is substantially too high.

3. Order book / forward visibility

Order book 1,106 units against revised full-year target of 1,400–1,500. Coverage = 74–79% of revised target with roughly six months remaining to October year-end. Low visibility on new reservations in context of falling enquiries.

"The current order book for the financial year stands at 1,106 units."

"…there has been a reduction in new enquiries and visitor levels."

4. Balance sheet — covenant relaxation sought

Net debt at year end guided £100–120m vs prior fc £44.9m — a deterioration of £55–75m. Covenant relaxation being sought from lenders.

"…it is in the early stages of seeking temporary banking covenant relaxation. Discussions with the Group's lenders have commenced and a further update will be provided in due course."

This is a material balance sheet flag. ND/EBITDA on revised EBIT of £10m midpoint (EBITDA likely £20–30m including D&A) vs net debt £110m midpoint = ND/EBITDA ~4–5x. Interest cover at £10m EBIT midpoint / £15m interest = 0.67x — below 1x.

5. Cost pressures

Higher build costs flagged due to energy costs. No quantum given. NLW step-up also relevant (April 2026).

"Given the higher level of energy costs the Group has built in an expectation of higher build costs in the balance of the financial year."

6. Macro / demand tone

Macro deterioration cited: higher-for-longer interest rates, Middle East conflict, consumer confidence deterioration. Land market sentiment sharply softer.

"…macro-uncertainty has increased, with the ongoing conflict in the Middle East contributing to the prospect of a more prolonged higher interest rate environment, renewed cost pressures and a deterioration in consumer confidence."

"…there has been a marked softening in sentiment among prospective land purchasers. Buyers have become more cautious in the face of the uncertain outlook, resulting in reduced engagement in bidding processes and an increased reluctance to transact at market values."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

🔴🔴 Profit warning

Guidance phrase: "the Group now expects to achieve an EBIT for the financial year of around £5m to £15m" — numeric, explicit, covers FY26 only. Covenant relaxation sought.

Nature: fully numeric. Single year coverage (FY26). Mid-point EBIT £10m vs prior consensus PBT £35.6m = ~72% cut to pre-tax profit. EPS implied ~0–1p vs 9.8p consensus.

Provisional points: −12 to −15.

Divergence check: No divergence paradox — both current delivery and outlook are severely negative. The AGM statement (25 March) had apparently maintained prior guidance; this RNS represents a rapid deterioration within four weeks. Flag: this is a profit warning issued between AGM update and H1 results — the acceleration of macro deterioration since 25 March is the stated trigger.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

EPS growth trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — −66.7% → −45.4% → +27.3% (consensus). The apparent consensus recovery is entirely invalidated by the RNS profit warning. Post-RNS implied EPS ~0–1p represents a further −87–100% decline.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Pre-H1 mode — full write-up required.

This RNS is a pre-H1 trading update. No H1 FY26 revenue or EPS actuals are disclosed. The RNS provides full-year EBIT guidance (£5–15m) and volume guidance (1,400–1,500 units) but no H1 split.

Revenue — UNTRACKABLE (no H1 split disclosed)

Baseline: 3yr avg H1% 41.5% × FY26e £620.7m (pre-RNS consensus) = £257.6m Post-RNS implied FY26e revenue ~£545m midpoint → implied H1 baseline = 41.5% × £545m = £226.2m Buy trigger threshold: £257.6m × 1.015 = £261.5m (pre-RNS) / £229.6m (post-RNS implied base)

Signal: 🟡 PROBABLE CAUTION — FY guidance implies H1 well below prior consensus baseline. Confirm on H1 results date (expected ~June/July 2026).

EPS — UNTRACKABLE (no H1 EPS disclosed)

Baseline: 3yr avg H1% 31.0% × FY26e 9.8p (pre-RNS) = 3.0p Post-RNS implied FY26e EPS ~0–1p → 31% × 0.5p midpoint = ~0.2p implied H1 Buy trigger threshold: 3.0p × 1.015 = 3.05p (pre-RNS) / entirely moot post-RNS

Signal: 🔴🔴 SELL SIGNAL (indicative) — EBIT guidance of £5–15m full year with £15m interest implies near-zero or loss-making PBT. H1 EPS almost certainly negligible or nil.

H2 EPS burden: FY26e 9.8p (pre-RNS) − H1 baseline 3.0p = 6.8p H2 requirement vs historical H2 avg (FY23–FY25: 26.6p, 8.0p, 5.5p → 3yr avg 13.4p). Post-RNS: implied H2 EPS ~0p vs historical avg 13.4p — burden is not just HIGHER than consensus assumes but catastrophically so.

Buy triggers: Revenue H1 > £261.5m: ❓ untrackable. EPS H1 > 3.05p: 🔴 ✗ — implied ~0.2p.

Historical hit rate: In prior years, positive H1 deviation preceded FY beat. Currently irrelevant — the question is whether H1 comes in above zero.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 base figure — RNS-derived.

RNS guides FY26 EBIT £5–15m, interest £15m → PBT £(10)m to £0m. For revenue: volume 1,400–1,500 units + land sales £40m. Implied FY26 revenue ~£540–560m (see Phase 2). Implied H2 FY26 revenue = £545m midpoint − £249m H1 (using 41.5% of £545m) = ~£296m.

Prior H2 actuals: FY25 H2 £353.3m, FY24 H2 £374.8m, FY23 H2 £549.3m. 3yr avg: £425.8m.

Implied H2 YoY vs FY25 H2: £296m / £353.3m − 1 = −16%. Classification: 🔴 severe (<−15%).

For EPS: implied FY26 ~0–1p, H1 implied ~0.2p → H2 implied ~0–0.8p vs FY25 H2 5.5p = −85 to −100% YoY. Classification: 🔴 severe.

⛔⛔ Profit warning risk ⛔⛔ — The profit warning has already been issued in this RNS. H2 FY26 burden is implausible relative to historical norms given: (1) volume cut of ~10% at midpoint with land sales cut ~55%; (2) higher energy/build costs in H2; (3) EBIT £5–15m full year with £15m interest implies sub-1x interest cover; (4) covenant relaxation being sought. FY26 consensus at material (near-total) risk of further cuts if H1 actuals disappoint vs the already-reduced guidance.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change over full snapshot period +8.9% (9.0p → 9.8p), but this masks cut-then-rebound: 9.1p → 7.8p (Nov–Jan) → 10.2p (Feb, post-FY25 results) → 9.8p (current). Net of the distortion, the underlying post-FY25 consensus settled at 9.8p. This RNS invalidates that entirely.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (pre-RNS). Post-RNS will be sharply FALLING.
  • Divergence: Price has already fallen sharply from 212p (Jun–Oct 25) to 105.6p (−50%) while EPS consensus was still nominally 9.8p — market was pricing in significant further cuts ahead of this announcement. The profit warning confirms the market's pessimism was warranted.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt/(cash): FY23 −£103.0m (net cash) / FY24 +£2.9m / FY25 H1 +£82.5m / FY25 FY −£34.1m (net cash) / FY26e pre-RNS fc £44.9m / FY27e £45.2m
  • Post-RNS net debt guidance: £100–120m (£110m midpoint) — more than double prior consensus of £44.9m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY25 1.4x / FY26e pre-RNS 0.9x → post-RNS: £110m ND / ~£20–30m EBITDA = ~4–5x
  • Interest cover: pre-RNS FY26e 5.0x → post-RNS: EBIT £10m midpoint / £15m interest = 0.67x — below 1x
  • ND/FCF: pre-RNS 4.3x → post-RNS: FCF will be negligible or negative; ratio not meaningful
  • Covenant relaxation sought — lender discussions commenced; "further update in due course"

Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — interest cover below 1x on revised guidance, covenant breach risk, net debt doubling vs prior forecast. This warrants a scored Phase 5 row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26e vs FY25 actual:

  • EPS: FY26e consensus 9.8p vs FY25 actual 7.7p → growing pre-RNS, but post-RNS implied ~0–1p → 🚨 FY26e implied EPS ~87–100% below FY25 actual
  • Revenue: FY26e £620.7m vs FY25 £610.8m → marginally growing pre-RNS, post-RNS ~£545m → 🚨 FY26e implied Revenue ~10–11% below FY25 actual

Step 2 — FY27e vs FY26e:

  • EPS: FY27e 12.8p vs FY26e 9.8p — growing pre-RNS, but FY27e will be cut severely given new debt level (£100–120m vs £45m) and recovery trajectory uncertainty → 🚨 FY27e consensus materially overstates recovery
  • Revenue: FY27e £656.7m vs FY26e £620.7m — growing pre-RNS, but FY27e base case needs full re-base

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

Covenant relaxation: "…it is in the early stages of seeking temporary banking covenant relaxation." This is a structural constraint — lenders may impose restrictions on capital allocation, dividends, or further land purchases that extend beyond the current financial year.

Fire remediation cash drag: Cash expenditure £75–80m in FY26, ongoing into future years. Recovery prospects noted but unquantified.

Project Elevate: Management references transformation initiatives but no financial quantum provided. Cannot be credited.

Land market structural softer: "…marked softening in sentiment among prospective land purchasers…increased reluctance to transact at market values." Land sales have historically contributed significant profit — the £40m revised revenue with nil material profit on disposals represents a near-total elimination of a profit line that previously contributed meaningfully.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

CRST · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/10/26

#1 Driver — EBIT profit warning (£5–15m vs £35.6m PBT consensus) The explicit downgrade to EBIT of £5–15m — implying near-zero or negative PBT — is the dominant broker note driver. This is not a soft warning; it is a near-total earnings wipe-out for FY26. Brokers will immediately re-base FY26 EPS to 0–1p range and cut target prices substantially. The covenant relaxation disclosure adds a further urgency dimension.

#2 Driver — Net debt deterioration and covenant relaxation Revised year-end net debt of £100–120m vs prior fc £44.9m is a £55–75m adverse swing. With interest cover below 1x and covenant relaxation discussions underway, brokers will model balance sheet risk premium and likely add a discount to NAV-based valuations. This may also trigger re-assessment of FY27e given higher ongoing interest costs from elevated debt.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e EPS: cut from 9.8p to approximately 0–1p — reduction of ~90–100%. Revenue: cut from £620.7m to approximately £540–560m — reduction of ~10–13%.
  • FY27e EPS: cut from 12.8p to approximately 6–9p — reduction of ~30–50%. The FY27e cut is driven by: (a) higher interest costs given £110m net debt entering FY27 vs prior model; (b) volume recovery uncertain given macro headwinds; (c) land market weakness may persist. Revenue FY27e: modest cut, likely £610–640m range.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers will cut TPs substantially. Prior consensus TP £186p vs close 105.6p already reflected significant pessimism. Post-RNS, TP likely cut to £80–120p range — valuation anchor shifts to NAV/book value given near-zero earnings. Current upside to consensus TP pre-RNS was 76%; post-RNS the TP itself collapses. Some brokers may move to Sell or Reduce from Hold.

Conservative guidance read-through: No conservative guidance language present — this is explicit, quantified profit warning. No upgrade cycle probability. The volume guidance range of 1,400–1,500 carries further downside risk given falling enquiries and the order book covers only 74–79% of the bottom end of that range.

Key risk: The covenant relaxation process is the single most significant risk beyond the earnings cut. "…it is in the early stages of seeking temporary banking covenant relaxation. Discussions with the Group's lenders have commenced and a further update will be provided in due course." If covenants are not relaxed on acceptable terms, the Group may face constraints on operations or be required to raise equity — materially dilutive. This is not priced with certainty at current levels.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: cut (~90%). Tone: 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected. Consistent.

Overall tone: 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected

Raw score before FX: 8. No FX adjustment applicable.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining event in this RNS is an unambiguous profit warning: EBIT guided to £5–15m (midpoint £10m) for FY26, against interest costs of c.£15m — implying PBT of £(10)m to £0m versus a pre-RNS consensus PBT of £35.6m. This represents a ~100% cut to pre-tax consensus. The implied FY26 EPS collapses from 9.8p to approximately 0–1p. The #1 catalyst is the simultaneous volume cut (to 1,400–1,500 units from 1,550–1,700) and the near-total elimination of land sale profit (land revenue cut 55% to £40m, nil material profit on disposals). These are not soft caveats — they are explicit numeric guidance revisions issued less than four weeks after the AGM statement that apparently held prior guidance.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: There is no upgrade resilience case here. In pre-H1 mode, Phase 3.2 is untrackable for both metrics — no H1 FY26 actuals are disclosed — but the FY-level EBIT guidance makes the picture unambiguous. Implied H2 FY26 revenue is approximately £296m against an FY25 H2 of £353.3m — a YoY decline of ~−16%, classified as 🔴 severe. Implied H2 EPS is approximately 0p versus FY25 H2 of 5.5p. The H2 EBIT burden requires the second half to deliver the entirety of the £5–15m EBIT guided for the full year if H1 is broadly breakeven — and that is before interest. Meanwhile, build costs are rising (energy costs, April NLW), land buyers are withdrawing, new enquiries are falling, and the Group is in early-stage lender covenant discussions. The ⛔⛔ profit warning risk flag from Phase 3.3 is not prospective — it has crystallised. The only scenario where downside is contained is if macro conditions rapidly reverse in H2, which management explicitly does not expect ("likely to continue for at least the balance of its financial year").

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will cut FY26e EPS to approximately 0–1p (from 9.8p — a ~90–100% reduction) and FY26e revenue to approximately £540–560m (from £620.7m — ~10–13% cut). FY27e EPS will be cut from 12.8p to approximately 6–9p — the higher debt load entering FY27 (£100–120m vs £45m modelled) adds ~£3–4m incremental annual interest that alone strips 1–1.5p from FY27e EPS before any volume uncertainty is considered. Consensus TPs will be cut from the pre-RNS £186p to an estimated £80–120p range, with valuation migrating from earnings-based to NAV/book-based given near-zero FY26 earnings. At a current price of 105.6p, the stock is not obviously cheap even post-fall — NAV will have eroded given fire remediation provisions, lower land values, and the working capital drag from completed apartment inventory being fast-tracked to disposal. The covenant relaxation process is the principal watch point: if banking discussions extend or conditions prove onerous, equity issuance risk cannot be excluded, which would reset the per-share figures further. 🏁 Unambiguous profit warning — brokers will cut FY26 EPS by ~90%, FY27e by ~30–50%, and TP materially. Covenant risk adds dilution tail. Score: 8/100.

scorecards.analysisText:
CYAN · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Trading Update for FY2026)

  1. Revenue — material beat vs historical base: FY26 revenues expected "in excess of £20 million" (FY25: £14.2m). YoY: +40.8%+ growth. No consensus available, but vs historical trajectory this is a strong outcome. "The Company expects to report revenues of in excess of £20 million (subject to audit) (FY2025: £14.2 million) for the period." H2 derivation: H1 = £7.4m; implied H2 = >£12.6m vs FY25 H2 = £8.5m = +48.2%+ YoY (RNS-derived). This is strong.
  2. Revenue composition — Goa project AMISP = significant proportion: A "significant proportion" of FY26 revenue relates to the Goa project, where CYAN acts as AMISP (first contract in this higher-margin role). No % disclosed. This introduces concentration risk. "A significant proportion of this revenue relates to the Company's Goa project, for which installation has now commenced."
  3. Hardware shipment deferral — deliberate pull-forward reduction: The company deferred certain hardware shipments ahead of new product launch (FG28 module, cellular modules, In-Meter Gateways). This artificially suppressed subcontractor revenue in FY26. "In anticipation of the new product launch, certain hardware shipments were deferred by the Company, leading to a lower proportion of the revenue for the year relating to the part of the Group's business where it acts as a subcontractor." Implication: FY26 revenue of >£20m is net of the hardware deferral. FY27 hardware shipments expected to increase following new product launch (H1 FY27 target). This is an FY27 tailwind.
  4. Cash collection — below revenue, FX drag: £10.8m collected (£11.6m constant currency) vs £14.2m in FY25 = −24.0% YoY decline in cash receipts despite revenue growing +40.8%. The divergence between revenue recognition and cash collection is material — receivables building significantly. Of £10.8m: £2.3m from FY25 trade receivables + £8.6m from FY26 trade receivables. FY26 trade receivables collected = £8.6m vs FY26 revenue of >£20m → implied FY26 trade receivables outstanding at year-end = ~£11.4m+. This is a significant working capital build. "A total of £10.8m cash was collected from customers (£11.6m at constant currencies) during the period (compared to £14.2m for FY 2025)."
  5. Interim results clarification — H2 cash collection very low: "At the time of the FY2026 interim results, cash collection since 30 September 2025 was £1.6m." This means H2 FY26 cash receipts were only £1.6m (partially) at the interim stage — very low given the revenue trajectory. The full-year £10.8m total implies H2 cash receipts of approximately £10.8m − (H1 receipts estimated) — the disclosure is not fully clear, but the working capital build is evident.
  6. Pipeline — APAC and Middle East projects "moving closer to order stage": Qualitative only. If secured, "good growth potential." No numeric detail.
  7. New product suite — FG28 + cellular modules + In-Meter Gateways: "Significantly lower costs to the Company" — margin improvement signal. Product launch targeted H1 FY27. "The Company moved toward completion of its new product suite, including the FG28 module, cellular modules and In-Meter Gateways, which have significantly lower costs to the Company."
  8. FY26e EPS bridge: No consensus available. All years loss-making. Not applicable in standard form. Note: with revenue >£20m and H1 EBITDA −£1.9m, FY26 loss will narrow vs FY25. Full-year profitability not yet achieved. FY27 new product launch + hardware shipment restart + pipeline conversion = the path to profitability.

EPS quality check: No EPS consensus. All loss-making. Cash collection is the relevant quality metric here — and the divergence between reported revenue (>£20m) and cash collected (£10.8m) raises receivable quality concerns.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • FY27 language: new product launch H1 FY27, hardware shipment restart, pipeline projects "moving closer to order stage," new lower-cost product suite.
  • No numeric FY27 guidance.
  • Coverage: qualitative only.
  • Context: heavily concentrated on Goa project; cash collection lagging revenue.
  • Classification: 🟢 Constructive — clear revenue growth, new product pipeline, AMISP model transition. But qualitative only and single-contract concentration. Provisional: +7 pts.

  • Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — interest cover 32.9x implies low absolute debt cost; however, the trajectory (−£2.6m net cash → £17.9m net debt in 3 years) with no operating cash generation is concerning. 3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • AMISP model transition — structural margin uplift: Moving from subcontractor (lower margin) to AMISP (service provider, higher margin) represents a structural business model upgrade. If Goa delivers successfully, it becomes a reference project for further AMISP contracts. "This project represents CyanConnode's first contract as an Advanced Metering Infrastructure Service Provider ('AMISP')."
  • New product suite lower unit costs: FG28 module and cellular modules at "significantly lower costs" — gross margin expansion signal for FY27+.
  • Project concentration risk: "Significant proportion" of FY26 revenue from Goa. If Goa revenue recognised but cash not collected in time, FY27 financials may be distorted.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

CYAN · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 Driver — Revenue >£20m (+40.8%+ YoY) — strong operational delivery: After a FY25 revenue decline (−24%), the return to >£20m revenue is a clear signal that the Goa project is delivering and the AMISP model is working. For a small-cap AIM company with no active consensus, this headline number will be the primary broker engagement point.

#2 Driver — Cash collection shortfall (£10.8m vs >£20m revenue): The large gap between revenue recognition and cash collection (£10.8m collected vs £20m+ revenue = ~54% cash conversion in the year) will temper enthusiasm. Any new broker note will lead with the revenue growth positive but caveat with the working capital build and receivable quality risk.

Forecast revisions: No active consensus to revise. If brokers re-engage (Zeus Capital + Panmure Liberum listed as joint brokers), expect new models to be set at approximately FY26 revenue £20–21m, EPS loss ~−0.3p to −0.5p (narrowing); FY27 revenue £25–30m (hardware restart + pipeline), EPS potentially first breakeven or small profit.

Target price and recommendation: No consensus TP. Sharescope shows TP = −. Brokers will likely set initiating or updated TPs in the range of 12–18p for a company with £20m+ revenue, AMISP model and new product pipeline, pending delivery confirmation at full-year results.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In excess of £20m" is a floor statement. Actual revenue could be £21–22m+ pending audit. The hardware deferral creates an incremental FY27 tailwind. New product launch adds a further FY27 catalyst.

Key risk: Cash collection is the critical risk. £10.8m collected vs >£20m revenue means ~£11m+ in trade receivables at year-end. If these are Indian government/utility counterparty receivables with long payment cycles, the company may need additional liquidity (equity raise risk).

Consistency check: Revenue growing strongly, losses narrowing, FY27 catalysts visible. Tone = Constructive — consistent.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely (for brokers who re-engage) — strong revenue growth, AMISP model proven, new products imminent. But cash conversion concern limits to Constructive rather than Strongly positive.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline catalyst is revenue "in excess of £20 million" for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), against FY25 revenue of £14.2m — representing at minimum +40.8% YoY growth. This reverses a −24.1% decline in FY25 and represents the highest revenue in the company's history. The primary driver is the Goa AMISP project, which is CYAN's first contract as an Advanced Metering Infrastructure Service Provider — a higher-margin role that represents a structural model upgrade from the previous subcontractor model. H2 FY26 implied revenue of >£12.6m represents >+48.2% growth over FY25 H2 (£8.5m), confirming H2 delivery was strong.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode H2 momentum is the key scored metric. The implied H2 of >£12.6m (RNS-derived) vs historical H2 avg of £10.6m = +18.9% above historical average — 🟢 strong. The structural tailwind for FY27 is the new product suite (FG28 module, cellular modules, In-Meter Gateways at "significantly lower costs") with hardware shipments expected to increase in H1 FY27 following the product launch. The pipeline in APAC and Middle East is described as "moving closer to order stage." The resilience of the upgrade thesis depends on: (1) Goa cash receipts materialising (£11m+ receivables outstanding); (2) new product launch execution in H1 FY27; (3) pipeline conversion in APAC/ME. The primary risk to the upgrade is the cash collection shortfall — £10.8m collected against >£20m revenue means approximately half the year's revenue is sitting in trade receivables, creating a liquidity dependency on counterparty payment timing.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: No active consensus to revise formally — Sharescope shows no FY1/FY2 consensus figures active since Nov 2025. Brokers (Zeus Capital, Panmure Liberum) who re-engage post this RNS will likely model FY26 revenue at £20–21m, narrowing losses to approximately −0.3p to −0.5p EPS; FY27 revenue at £25–30m with potential first breakeven EPS. New TP initiations likely in the 12–18p range vs current price of 7.75p — implying 55–130% upside on an initiated basis. The score of 52 reflects genuine operational progress (revenue, H2 momentum, AMISP model) capped by the cash collection concern, no-consensus risk, and continuing losses. 🏁 Constructive outlook for FY27 on new product launch and pipeline — but cash conversion of ~54% and £17.9m net debt mean the balance sheet must be watched closely; wait for full-year results confirmation of receivable quality before committing.
