scorecards.analysisText:
DEVO

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Note: Sharescope Next year end = 31/12/25 and routing = Q2. The RNS is FY2025 full year results published 9 April 2026. Sharescope has not yet rolled forward to 31/12/26 — consistent with the rule that Sharescope does not roll until FY results are published. So FY1 = FY25 (the year just reported), FY2 = FY26 (the current live year).

Five explicit row label mappings:

  • Next year end 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25
  • FY1 − 1 = FY24 (1y ago)
  • FY1 − 2 = FY23 (2y ago)
  • FY1 − 3 = FY22 (3y ago)
  • FY2 = FY26

PHASE 0B — FX CHECK — DEVO

DEVO reports in USD. Sharescope Currency: USD. Revenues are earned via third-party distribution platforms (Steam, consoles) — global revenues, no single geographic disclosure provided per Note 2 of accounts: "The Group does not provide any information on the geographical breakdown of revenues." No Currency Movements section in RNS. Cannot identify single non-GBP currency >30% from RNS. No Phase 0B penalty applicable. No FX badge.

PHASE 1 — DEVO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY25 full year results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 1.7p · Revenue $106.0m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 2.3p · Revenue $115.5m (Sharescope). Note: Zeus broker note uses FY26E EPS $0.024 = ~1.8p. Sharescope FY2 fc = 2.3p may be a blended consensus vs Zeus above-consensus.
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +13.3% (1.5p → 1.7p). Momentum 🟢 RISING — gradual upward drift over the period, with one small upgrade step in August 2025 (1.5p → 1.6p) and further drift to 1.7p. Revenue net change: $112.5m → $106.0m = −5.8%. Revenue consensus has drifted down while EPS has risen — reflects improving margin expectations.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 45.4% × $106.0m = $48.1m · EPS: H1 avg split n/a (historical H1 EPS all negative in a loss-making company)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue $51.6m · EPS −1.0p (H1 loss)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): RNS actual FY25 revenue $107.9m. H1 actual $38.8m → Implied H2 = $107.9m − $38.8m = $69.1m vs FY24 H2 $53.2m → +29.9% YoY. EPS: FY25 reported adj. diluted EPS −1.0p (in pence). Sharescope FY1 fc = 1.7p. The Zeus broker note confirms adj. diluted EPS (p) FY25A = −1.0p. Sharescope FY1 fc 1.7p was pre-results consensus — the actual delivered −1.0p vs 1.7p forecast. However, Zeus note shows FY26E EPS = 1.8p (their above-consensus figure). This requires careful treatment — see Phase 2.
  • FX: USD reporting, no adjustment.
  • Reporting currency & debt: USD · Net cash (ex. leases): current H1 $33.7m → FY1fc $37.2m (Sharescope) / RNS actual $36.6m → FY2fc $39.0m · ND/EBITDA: all periods net cash · Interest cover FY1fc: 0.2x (anomalous — reflects near-zero EBITDA in Sharescope FY1 consensus which was pre-results; actual EBITDA $7.1m gives much higher coverage) · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — $36.6m cash, zero borrowings.

PHASE 2 — DEVO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue

FY25 actual revenue: $107.9m, +3.0% YoY (FY24: $104.8m). vs Sharescope FY1 consensus $106.0m → +$1.9m, +1.8% beat. vs Zeus estimate $107.5m → essentially in line (+0.4%).

"Revenue performance was in line with guidance given at the start of the year, rising 3.0% year-on-year to US$107.9 million."

2. EPS / Adjusted EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA (post impairments): $7.1m (FY24: $5.1m), +39.4% YoY. vs Sharescope FY1fc EBITDA $10.5m → miss on Sharescope consensus. vs Zeus estimate $7.0m → in line (+1.4%). Note: the Sharescope EBITDA fc $10.5m likely embeds impairments-excluded definition vs Zeus using post-impairment. This discrepancy is definitional.

Adj. diluted EPS (pence): FY25A = −1.0p (Zeus note). Sharescope FY1 fc was 1.7p. This is a large apparent miss. However: the Zeus note adj. EPS definition = post non-cash impairments of released titles, pre share-based payments. The statutory EPS is −$0.034 (−2.6p approx). The difference between the 1.7p Sharescope forecast and the −1.0p actual is driven by: (1) the $4.3m non-cash performance impairment; (2) the $14.6m non-cash deferred tax write-down. The DTA write-down is entirely non-cash and non-recurring — it does not affect adj. EBITDA.

EPS quality check: The statutory net loss of $16.0m is dominated by a non-cash DTA write-down of $14.6m. This is a one-off non-cash item with zero operational significance. Adj. EBITDA of $7.1m and positive FCF in H2 are the relevant operating metrics. The effective tax charge (statutory) was $13.4m on PBT of −$2.6m — this is entirely the DTA write-down. Restating adj. EPS on an operating basis (pre DTA write-down): adj. PBT = $7.3m (from Zeus note) × ~20% tax = ~$5.8m PAT / 474.5m shares = ~$0.012 = ~0.9p. Sharescope consensus 1.7p vs actual ~0.9p adj. = still a miss, driven primarily by the $4.3m impairment charge flowing through to adj. EBITDA post-impairment. 🚨 Impairment-driven EPS shortfall vs Sharescope consensus: headline adj. EPS ~−1.0p vs 1.7p fc; difference = $4.3m impairment + share count dilution. Impairments are non-cash but broker-visible.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here, referenced in Phase 4): (1) New base: FY25 adj. EBITDA (post impairments) = $7.1m. (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: nil in FY25 — no acquisitions (Zeus notes $5.6m acquisition assumed in FY26E). (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: RNS guides "continued revenue and Adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026." Zeus models FY26E adj. EBITDA = $14.6m. The organic driver: 15+ new releases in H1-weighted schedule, STARSEEKER release in June, Steam Publisher Sale. Revenue consensus FY26e = $115.5m (+7.1% organic growth). Applying similar EBITDA margin improvement (from 6.6% to ~11.8% per Zeus) = incremental EBITDA ~$7.5m. (4) Interest step-up: nil — net cash company, no debt drawdown. Finance costs FY25 = $0.16m. Implied FY26e adj. EBITDA: ~$14–15m. EPS: $14.6m EBITDA − $0.2m depreciation − tax ~$2.9m = ~$11.5m PAT / 484m diluted shares = $0.024 = ~1.8p. Bridge-implied FY26e EPS: ~1.8p vs Sharescope FY2 fc 2.3p → bridge supports Zeus (1.8p) but suggests Sharescope consensus (2.3p) is optimistic by ~25%. Risk of FY26 consensus cut from 2.3p toward 1.8–2.0p range.

3. Order book / pipeline

Pipeline: at least 13 new titles in FY26, including STARSEEKER: Astroneer Expeditions, Serious Sam: Shatterverse, and several lower-cost third-party releases. Over 30 titles in pipeline for next three years.

"Pipeline of at least 13 new titles in FY26 with greater visibility and control over our release cadence."

Front catalogue revenues: $37.9m (+218% YoY from $11.9m). Back catalogue: $68.9m (−24% YoY from $91.1m but improving in H2 vs H1's −38%).

4. Margin / profitability

Gross margin: 30.7% (FY24: 28.7%) — +200bps expansion. Driven by 11% reduction in marketing costs and 24% decline in game development expenditure. Adj. operating expenses −1.1% YoY to $26.5m.

"Gross margins expanded to 30.7%, up from 28.7% in 2024, primarily due to an 11% reduction in marketing costs, and a 24% decline in game development expenditure."

FY26 guidance: "significantly first half weighted" due to platform deals, Steam Publisher Sale, and release cadence. EBITDA expected to grow.

5. Capital / cash

Cash: $36.6m at 31 Dec 2025 (FY24: $41.6m). Positive FCF in H2 2025. No borrowings. Company expects positive FCF continuation through 2026.

6. Qualitative tone

Strong 2026 start: January — three titles in Steam Global Best Sellers Top 10 (Devolver's first). BALL x PIT content updates + console/mobile launch. Quarantine Zone: The Last Check performing strongly.

"Positive start in January 2026 with Quarantine Zone: The Last Check performing strongly in the weeks after release and three titles in Steam Global Best Sellers Top 10 list, a Devolver 'first'."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "Expect to deliver continued revenue and Adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026." H1-weighted release schedule. "Significantly stronger" H1 than H2. Strong start confirmed. CEO statement: "excited about the opportunities for continued progress in the year ahead."

Language is constructive with a specific H1-weighting qualifier and strong January trading evidence. Not "not less than" but directionally positive with visible catalysts (STARSEEKER release, Steam Publisher Sale).

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — "comfortable" equivalent language with visible earnings drivers, confirmed strong start, H1-biased release schedule already partially confirmed. Provisional points: +6 to +10.

Divergence check: FY25 delivered revenue beat and EBITDA growth — consistent with Constructive outlook. No divergence. ✓

PHASE 3 — DEVO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

PHASE 0A — ROUTING
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (26 weeks to 28 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). H1 results 26 weeks to 28 Dec 2025.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 15.2p · Revenue £1,090.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 18.6p · Revenue £1,131.0m

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.9% of FY = £544.0m · EPS 33.0% (2yr avg) of FY = 5.0p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £504.5m · EPS 5.3p (underlying)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS): Revenue £546.6m (+3.9% vs prior H2) · EPS 10.2p (+175.7% vs prior H2 3.7p)
  • FX: N/A
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results (26 weeks ended 28 December 2025)

  1. H1 Revenue — in-line / slight beat: £547.7m vs baseline £544.0m = [+£3.7m / +0.7%] vs seasonal baseline. +8.6% YoY vs prior H1 £504.5m.

"Revenue growth of 8.6% reflecting the growth in order intake and the benefit of a stronger opening order bank"

  1. H1 Underlying EPS — massive beat: 9.8p vs baseline 5.0p = [+4.8p / +96%] vs seasonal baseline. H1 EPS as % of FY1 consensus = 64.5% vs 33.0% historical baseline.

"Underlying basic EPS: 9.8p (H1 FY25: 5.3p)"

  1. H1 PBTu(A) — strong beat: £30.9m vs H1 FY25 £17.0m = [+£13.9m / +81.8% YoY]. H1 alone = 65.1% of FY1 Sharescope consensus PBT £47.5m.

"Underlying profit performance, PBTu(A) up significantly (+£13.9m) YoY to £30.9m reflecting the impact of operational leverage"

  1. FY guidance reiterated — conservative framing: Full year PBTu(A): £43–50m range. Company consensus: £47.3m (within range, near top). Midpoint £46.5m. H1 £30.9m already delivered = 65.3% of company consensus. Implied H2: £12.1m (floor) to £19.1m (ceiling) vs prior H2 £13.8m. Floor requires only −12.3% H2 YoY decline vs prior H2.

"we are comfortable reiterating our guidance of full year PBTu(A) in the range of £43-50m"

  1. Gross margin — approaching target: 57.8% (+110bps YoY). 4th consecutive year of expansion. Bridge: Volume +£24.0m (0bps rate), Product margin +30bps (+£1.4m), FX +30bps (+£1.9m), Freight +50bps (+£2.7m). 30bps below 58% target.

"Gross margin increased 110bps to 57.8%, approaching our 58% target. This is the fourth consecutive year of margin expansion"

  1. Net bank debt — major improvement: £60.6m vs £116.7m H1 FY25 = [−£56.1m / −48.1% YoY]. Leverage 0.8x (1.0x WC-adjusted) — now within 0.5x–1.0x target range. Peak debt was £164.8m at FY24; total reduction of £104.2m over 18 months.

"Strong free cash flow generation and cash discipline reducing net bank debt to £60.6m, down over £100m over the last eighteen months"

  1. Dividend reinstated: Interim dividend 1.0p/share declared. First dividend reinstated after pause. To be paid 29 May 2026.

"Recognising the Group's improved financial position an interim dividend of 1.0 pence / share has been declared"

  1. Order intake: Group +2.3% YoY (DFS +2.0%, Sofology +3.4%) vs +10.1% prior year comparator. Market broadly flat. Home (non-upholstery) +14% YoY. Post-period: softening in footfall linked to adverse weather.

"2.3% YoY order intake growth achieved in a subdued market and against a strong comparator of +10.1%"

  1. Operating leverage: Underlying operating costs 49.1% of revenue (H1 FY25: 49.5%) — improved despite volume, marketing and wage/NIC cost increases. Finance costs £16.7m vs £20.3m (−£3.6m) — lower debt + lower SONIA.
  1. Medium-term targets reaffirmed: £1.4bn revenue + 8% PBT margin. ROCE 21.6% (H1 FY25: 13.8%). Sofa Delivery Company: first two third-party delivery contracts signed — new profit stream.

"Market volumes remain c.20% below pre-pandemic levels...operational leverage in the business is expected to result in high profit growth with revenue to profit drop through at around 40%"

  1. Post-period / H2 risk: Adverse weather impact on footfall since half year. Consumer confidence "delicately balanced." Lease payment timing reversal expected (£7.3m lower in H1, unwinds in H2). Geopolitical supply chain caveat. FY guidance assumes "no material supply chain disruption."
PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Half-on-Half Table

H1 FY23: Rev £556.5m / EPS 7.2p

H2 FY23: Rev £593.3m / EPS 9.6p

H1 FY24: Rev £544.5m (−2.2%) / EPS 2.2p (−69.4%)

H2 FY24: Rev £544.4m (−8.3%) / EPS 7.3p (−24.0%)

H2 FY25: Rev £525.8m (−3.4%) / EPS 3.7p (−49.3%)

H1 FY26: Rev £547.7m ([+8.5%]) / EPS 9.8p ([+84.9%])

Implied H2 FY26*: Rev ~£542.9m (+3.3%) / EPS ~5.4p (+45.9%)

*H2 FY26 derived: Rev = FY1 cns £1,090.6m − H1 £547.7m = £542.9m. EPS = FY1 cns 15.2p − H1 9.8p = 5.4p

1. Half-on-Half Growth Pattern

  • Revenue trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — H2 FY25 −3.4%, H1 FY26 [+8.5%], H2 FY26 implied +3.3%. Clear inflection after three consecutive declining halves.
  • EPS trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — H2 FY25 −49.3%, H1 FY26 [+84.9%], H2 FY26 implied +45.9%.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% (49.9%) × FY1 £1,090.6m = £544.0m
  • EPS baseline: 2yr avg H1% (33.0%) × FY1 15.2p = 5.0p
  • Revenue tracking: £547.7m ÷ £1,090.6m = 50.2% vs 49.9% baseline → [+0.3pp] → 🟡 IN LINE (trigger requires +1.5pp; narrowly missed)
  • EPS tracking: 9.8p ÷ 15.2p = 64.5% vs 33.0% baseline → [+31.5pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY
  • Note on +31.5pp EPS deviation: Structural, not seasonal. Driven by operational leverage on recovering revenue + 4 years of margin expansion + finance cost reduction from £56.1m debt paydown.
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 cns 15.2p − H1 9.8p = 5.4p vs 3yr historical H2 avg 6.9p → H2 burden LOWER than consensus implies by 1.5p. Meaningful downside protection.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£544.0m × 1.015] = £552.2m → £547.7m ✗ (missed by £4.5m) · H1 EPS > [5.0p × 1.015] = 5.1p → 9.8p ✓

3. Implied H2 Momentum

  • Implied H2 rev £542.9m vs last 3 H2 avg £554.5m = −2.1% (below avg) but +3.3% YoY vs prior H2.
  • H2 classification: moderate on revenue (+0–10% YoY). PBT H2 midpoint £15.6m = moderate (+13.0% YoY vs H2 FY25 £13.8m).
  • Wide H2 range: floor £12.1m (−12.3% YoY) to ceiling £19.1m (+38.4% YoY). Post-period weather/footfall softening is the primary swing factor.

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +6.8p (+81.0%) net over 10-month period. Two sharp upgrade events (Oct 25 +49%, Jan 26 +15%). Revenue +£64.5m (+6.3%). FLAT last 7 weeks — market had not pre-positioned for today's print.
  • Share price: 256p peak (late Jan/Feb 26) → 169p close = −34.0% in ~6 weeks. This is a severe disconnect: consensus upgraded to 15.2p at the same time the price peaked then sold off sharply. Today's H1 directly contradicts this bearish price action.
  • ROCE 21.6% vs 13.8% H1 FY25 — near-doubling of returns in one year.

5. Structural Flags

  • [Operational leverage at sub-peak volumes]: Market volumes ~20% below pre-pandemic. 40% revenue-to-profit drop-through on recovery. H1 FY26 demonstrates leverage is already firing at below-peak volumes. Significant unearned upside if market recovers.
  • [Debt paydown enabling capital reallocation]: Leverage at 0.8x vs 2.5x at FY24 peak. Dividend reinstated. Shift from deleveraging mode to growth/returns mode beginning.
  • [H2 lease timing reversal]: £7.3m H1 benefit unwinds in H2 — non-cash PBT neutral but affects reported FCF.
  • [Post-period footfall softening]: Weather-related but not quantified. Creates downside risk to top end of guidance range.
PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 = H1 EPS 9.8p vs consensus-implied ~5.0p H1 expectation. This number forces every broker to rebuild their H1/H2 split assumption. The operational leverage thesis is proving materially more powerful in H1 than models anticipated. #2 = FY guidance reiterated at £43–50m (unchanged) despite H1 at £30.9m (65% of consensus already banked). Classic conservative framing post-strong H1. Floor of £43m requires only £12.1m H2 — easily achievable. Brokers will model toward £47–50m and upgrade accordingly.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 EPS: ↑ 17–18p (+10–20% from 15.2p). FY1 Revenue: ↔ £1,095–1,105m (+0–2%). FY2 EPS: ↑ 20–22p (+8–18% from 18.6p). FY2 Revenue: ↔ ~£1,135–1,145m~~. Target price: ↑ 270–300p+++ from 256p.
  1. Target price / recommendation: All brokers likely at Buy currently (TP 256p vs 169p = 51.5% upside). Post-results TPs raised to 270–300p. Some Hold → Buy upgrades from more cautious analysts. The 34% price decline from the Jan/Feb peak — concurrent with the consensus upgrade — represents a significant opportunity for upgrading brokers.
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: Reiteration of £43–50m after H1 £30.9m is effectively conservative guidance signalling. Management chose not to upgrade the range. Brokers will model toward top end (£50m) given H1 momentum; some may build forecasts marginally above £50m. Increases probability of upgrade cycle.
  1. Key risk: Post-period footfall softening due to adverse weather. If H2 order intake softens materially, the wide guidance range (£7m spread) provides limited cushion. Consumer confidence "delicately balanced" — any macro deterioration (tariffs, Middle East escalation) could push toward the lower end of the range. Wide H2 guidance range is the reason this scores 79 not 85+. "Since the half year we have seen some softening in footfall linked to adverse weather conditions over the period and consumer confidence remains delicately balanced"
  1. Overall tone: Constructive / modest upgrades likely — H1 EPS beat is emphatic, leverage story intact, balance sheet transformed, dividend reinstated. Unchanged guidance (rather than upgrade) and post-period footfall softening prevent a full re-rating but confirm a meaningful upgrade cycle is underway.

DFS Furniture's H1 FY26 results are emphatically better than consensus had modelled, with the definitive catalyst being the H1 underlying EPS of 9.8p — nearly double the ~5.0p seasonal expectation derived from the 33% historical H1 split, and a deviation of +31.5pp above the seasonal baseline. This single figure forces every broker model to be rebuilt. H1 underlying PBT(A) of £30.9m already represents 65.1% of the Sharescope FY1 PBT consensus of £47.5m — delivered with the less profitable H1 seasonality. Revenue of £547.7m was essentially in-line (+0.3pp above baseline, narrowly missing the +1.5pp buy trigger), confirming the earnings beat is an operational leverage and margin story rather than a volume surprise. Gross margin of 57.8% (+110bps YoY) is the fourth consecutive year of expansion and sits just 30bps below the stated 58% target, with the bridge attributing gains to product margin improvements (+30bps), FX (+30bps) and freight normalisation (+50bps). The H1 print directly confronts the 34% share price sell-off from the 256p peak to 169p that occurred in the 6 weeks prior to today's announcement.

The STRONG BUY signal from H1 EPS tracking (+31.5pp) is structural, not seasonal. The H2 EPS burden is 5.4p (FY1 consensus 15.2p − H1 actual 9.8p) versus the 3-year historical H2 average of 6.9p — the H2 burden is 1.5p lower than the consensus implies, providing meaningful downside protection even if H2 disappoints. The full-year PBT guidance range of £43–50m is deliberately wide: the floor of £43m requires only £12.1m of H2 PBT (−12.3% vs prior H2 £13.8m), while the ceiling of £50m requires £19.1m (+38.4%). Post-period footfall softening linked to adverse weather is the primary risk to the top end of the range, but provides no threat to the floor. The structural driver is the combination of operational leverage (40% revenue-to-profit drop-through on market recovery), four consecutive years of gross margin expansion, finance cost reduction from £56.1m of debt paydown, and the completed £50m Cost-to-Operate programme. Market volumes remain ~20% below pre-pandemic levels — the leverage story is nowhere near peak. The dividend reinstatement (1.0p interim) is a symbolic but important confirmation that management views the balance sheet improvement as durable.

Broker revisions will be material. FY1 EPS (currently 15.2p) is expected to be upgraded to the 17–18p range (+10–20%) as models are rebuilt with H1 actual 9.8p and a conservatively modelled H2. FY1 Revenue is unlikely to move materially (+0–2% to ~£1,095–1,105m). FY2 EPS (currently 18.6p) is expected to be revised to the 20–22p range (+8–18%) as the structural margin and leverage thesis rolls forward. The consensus target price of 256p is expected to be raised to the 270–300p range — and at a current share price of 169p, the stock is trading at a 34% discount to even the unrevised consensus TP, with 51.5% implied upside. The main constraint on the score — and why this is a constructive/moderate upgrade rather than a full re-rating — is the unchanged and deliberately wide guidance range and the post-period footfall softening disclosure. Upgrade cycle probability: high. The H1 EPS beat is the most powerful number DFS has reported since pre-pandemic levels, the balance sheet is the cleanest it has been in years, and the stock is at a 34% discount to a TP that will itself be revised upward today. The weather/footfall caveat and conservative guidance framing are the only governors on a stronger reaction.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as a pre-H1 trading update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX: Brief trading update — no Currency Movements section and no explicit revenue-by-currency breakdown. Diploma has material USD/CAD exposure through North American operations but no single non-GBP currency is confirmed above 30% in this RNS. No FX penalty applied — insufficient confirmed exposure data.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Consensus: FY1 (FY ending 30 September 2026) EPS 195.8p, revenue £1,665.0m; FY2 EPS 207.8p, revenue £1,758.5m. Analyst consensus adjusted operating profit for FY26: £377m — cited verbatim in the RNS footnote by management (as at 17 March 2026).
  • Forecast momentum: EPS upgraded 160.9p → 195.8p over ~10 months (+21.7%) — one of the most consistent upgrade cycles in this batch. Large step in November 2025 (172→188p), further step December–January (191→196p). Last 4 weeks: FLAT. Revenue +13.4%.
  • 3yr avg H1% of FY: revenue 46.6%, EPS 45.0%. Consensus H1 baselines: revenue £776.9m; EPS 88.1p. Buy triggers: H1 Rev > £788.6m; H1 EPS > 89.4p. Assessable at HY results 19 May 2026.
  • H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE. No H1 actual numbers provided in this qualitative pre-H1 update. Both column 5 indicators fire as N/A. H1 results due 19 May 2026.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Organic revenue growth guidance upgraded to 9% (from 6%). +3pp upgrade to the primary growth metric. Remaining H1-weighted per management commentary.
    "Organic revenue growth increased to 9% (from 6%), remaining H1 weighted"
  2. Operating margin guidance upgraded to c.25% (from c.22.5%). +250bps expansion. On FY1 consensus revenue ~£1,665m, this implies operating profit ~£416m vs prior consensus £377m = ~+10.3% OP upgrade.
    "Operating margin increased to c.25% (from c.22.5%)"
  3. "c.13% upgrade to consensus operating profit." Management cites prior consensus OP (£377m, dated 17 March 2026) then states it needs to increase by 13% — exceptional transparency; rare for a FTSE 100 company to self-quantify a consensus upgrade in a trading update.
    "Representing a c.13% upgrade to consensus operating profit. Analyst consensus adjusted operating profit for FY26 is £377m, as at 17 March 2026."
  4. "Earnings growth over 20%." Explicit EPS guidance — not a range. Current consensus 195.8p; 20% growth on any reasonable base implies minimum ~215–235p, materially above current consensus.
    "We expect another year of sustainable quality compounding, with earnings growth over 20% at strong returns on capital"
  5. Peerless — "outstanding organic growth performance in H1, with H2 returning to more typical growth rates." H2 moderation explicitly guided — management pre-managing expectations to avoid a negative H2 surprise against very strong comparators.
    "We expect another outstanding organic growth performance in the first half, with the second half returning to more typical growth rates against very strong comparators."
  6. Windy City Wire — "performing very well... strong growth in datacentres and digital antenna systems." Structural AI/datacentre demand driver within the Controls segment.
    "Windy City Wire is performing very well. Strong growth supported by excellent execution in markets including datacentres and digital antenna systems."
  7. International Seals — "remains challenging, particularly in the UK." Drag on overall Seals H1 growth, consistent with FY25 growth rates.
    "International Seals remains challenging - particularly in the UK - and will somewhat hold back overall Seals H1 growth rates, consistent with FY25 growth rates."
  8. Organic growth excluding Peerless — "strong and well ahead of our financial model." Critical signal: the upgrade is not Peerless-dependent. Confirms broad-based portfolio outperformance.
    "Organic growth excluding Peerless is strong and well ahead of our financial model."
  9. 8 acquisitions in preceding two quarters, ~£130m consideration, ~£20m annualised OP contribution. Not included in guidance — represents potential further upside if further deals completed.
    "we completed 8 acquisitions in the preceding two quarters for c.£130m with expected annualised operating profit contribution of c.£20m."
  10. Life Sciences — "performing consistently in a tough healthcare market, with share gains across medtech and IVD." Third segment delivering steady share gains despite market headwinds.
    "Life Sciences: Performing consistently in a tough healthcare market, with share gains across medtech and IVD."
  11. Net acquisition growth unchanged at 3%. M&A pipeline described as "healthy" near-term. Could increase if further acquisitions completed.
    "Net acquisition growth unchanged at 3%. This will increase if further acquisitions are made"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: Strongly Accelerating. H1 FY24 +30.0%, H2 FY24 +9.4%, H1 FY25 +9.6%, H2 FY25 +17.4%. Now guiding ~12% total FY26 (9% organic + 3% acquisition). Continuous acceleration across every successive period.
  • EPS trajectory: Accelerating. H1 FY24 +25.4%, H2 FY24 +11.1%, H1 FY25 +10.4%, H2 FY25 +19.8%. Now guiding "over 20%" for full FY26 = acceleration continuing.
  • H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE. No H1 actuals in this RNS — this is a qualitative pre-H1 update only. Baselines and buy triggers set for assessment on 19 May 2026 HY results: H1 Rev baseline £776.9m (buy trigger > £788.6m); H1 EPS baseline 88.1p (buy trigger > 89.4p). Qualitative signals (Peerless "outstanding," ex-Peerless "well ahead of model") are strongly positive but cannot be quantified for column 5 scoring until actuals are available.
  • Implied H2 momentum: Organic upgrade is H1-weighted; H2 returns to "more typical" rates for Peerless (~5–7% organic). With 3% acquisition growth, total H2 ~8–10%. Margin expansion to 25% applies to both halves. H2 classified moderate/solid — management has fully pre-communicated the moderation, substantially reducing surprise risk.
  • Forecast momentum: +21.7% EPS upgrade — the most consistent sustained upgrade cycle in this batch. Currently FLAT. This update restarts the cycle definitively — "over 20% earnings growth" requires a minimum upgrade from 195.8p to ~215–235p (+10–20%).
  • Structural flags: (1) Peerless aerospace: "demand and supply characteristics are favourable and sustainable" — multi-year structural tailwind. (2) Windy City Wire: AI/datacentre demand cited explicitly. (3) IS Group and Clarendon in "structurally growing markets like energy, defence and aerospace" — geopolitical tailwinds embedded in end-markets. (4) Eight acquisitions in two quarters — M&A compounding at pace; £20m annualised OP contribution not in any guidance figure.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — Formal, quantified OP margin upgrade to c.25% (+250bps) = ~13% OP upgrade to consensus: Management stated the prior consensus OP figure (£377m) and said it needs to increase by 13%. For a FTSE 100 quality compounder, a self-quantified guidance upgrade of this magnitude is extremely rare and will dominate every broker note.
2#2 Driver — "Earnings growth over 20%" as an explicit EPS guidance statement: Current consensus 195.8p. 20% growth on FY25 underlying EPS of ~175p implies ~210p; 20% on 195.8p implies 235p. Either framing puts current consensus materially below the floor. Brokers are forced to upgrade FY1 EPS to at minimum 215–235p range.
3Forecast revisions — FY1 EPS +13–20%, FY2 EPS +8–12%: Operating margin 25% on £1,710–1,730m revenue = £428–433m OP vs prior £377m. After finance costs and tax (~26% effective rate), EPS of ~215–235p. Target prices: £60.40 → £65–72+ range. Revenue upgrades to £1,710–1,730m range.
4Conservative guidance read-through: Management has 5 months of FY26 visibility when issuing this guidance (Oct 2025 – Mar 2026 largely locked). "Over 20% earnings growth" is a floor statement. Peerless H2 moderation is explicitly pre-communicated — downside risk in H2 is substantially reduced by this pre-management of expectations.
5Key risk — Peerless H2 moderation after exceptional H1: H2 returns to "more typical" growth vs "very strong comparators." International Seals UK remains challenging. If both headwinds converge in H2, the upgrade could partially reverse — but management has pre-communicated both, substantially reducing surprise risk.
6Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. A FTSE 100 quality compounder with a 7-year track record of 18% EPS CAGR issuing a self-quantified ~13% OP upgrade with "over 20% earnings growth" guidance, broad-based organic outperformance (ex-Peerless also "well ahead"), and a healthy M&A pipeline. Every major broker covering Diploma will issue an upgrade note today.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
94
/100
Confidence range: 89–98 · No FX adjustment applied
Formal ~13% OP upgrade to consensus (quantified by company in RNS footnote)+22
Organic growth upgraded 6%→9% (H1-weighted, broad-based)+12
Operating margin upgraded 22.5%→25% (+250bps)+10
"Earnings growth over 20%" — explicit company floor statement+8
Organic ex-Peerless also "well ahead of model" — truly broad-based+7
8 acquisitions in 2 quarters, £130m, £20m OP contribution not in guidance+5
Upgrade cycle momentum (+21.7% over period; restarting now)+5
Peerless H2 moderation flagged (comparator risk; H2 will be softer)−7
International Seals UK challenging (drag on overall Seals segment)−5
H1 UNTRACKABLE — no actual H1 numbers to verify (19 May 2026)−3

Diploma has issued one of the most explicit and shareholder-friendly trading upgrades in its recent history. The direct citation of prior consensus operating profit (£377m) followed by a stated ~13% upgrade, combined with "earnings growth over 20%" for the full year, leaves virtually no room for misinterpretation. For a FTSE 100 compounding business with a seven-year track record of 18% EPS CAGR, this clarity of language signals genuine management conviction that is rare at this stage of a financial year.

Critically, the upgrade is broad-based: organic growth ex-Peerless is described as "well ahead of our financial model," confirming outperformance is not concentrated in a single aerospace name. The structural drivers are intact — Peerless aerospace benefits from "favourable and sustainable" supply/demand dynamics, Windy City Wire captures AI/datacentre demand, Life Sciences takes share in medtech and IVD, and eight acquisitions totalling £130m with £20m annualised OP contribution are not in any guidance figure. Current consensus EPS of 195.8p requires an upgrade to at minimum 215–235p, representing a 10–20% step-up.

The primary constraint on a higher score is the explicit H2 moderation signal for Peerless and the fact that H1 actuals cannot yet be verified. However, management's exceptional transparency in quantifying the upgrade, the self-citation of prior consensus, and the broad-based organic outperformance make this the highest-conviction upgrade catalyst in the FTSE 100 this reporting season.

The current discount (share price 578p vs TP 873p = 51% premium) implies substantial re-rating potential if the order momentum is confirmed.

🏁 Q4 organic orders +15%, order book +9% CER, three consecutive quarters of orders ahead of sales — a clear demand recovery in motion. FY26 delivered in-line; FY27 upgrade cycle probable at June prelims. Score 67/100.

The company's H2 EPS had always carried a structurally extreme 76.8% of the FY consensus — leaving no buffer. PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

EAAS · Q1 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 FY26 trading update + FY25 unaudited results + revenue recognition policy update + FY26 guidance upgrade).

  1. FY25 revenue (unaudited actual): £19.0m. Pre-RNS FY1 consensus: £23.1m → miss of −£4.1m / −17.8%. Entirely attributable to revenue recognition policy change (30%→5% Solar/Batteries, 30%→0% LED/EV at contract signing) reducing FY25 by ~£4.0m with equal and opposite £4.0m addition to FY26. No cash impact, no operational deterioration. FY24 restated to £22.4m (was ~£26m on old basis). Clean audit opinion expected from Cooper Parry.

"Following engagement with its new auditor, Cooper Parry, the Group has adopted a more conservative approach to revenue recognition... resulting in a reduction of approximately £4.0m in FY25 reported revenue and a £4.0m increase in FY26 revenue. Importantly, there is no impact on cash generation and no change to underlying profitability of the individual contracts."

  1. FY25 EBITDA (unaudited): £2.2m vs FY24 restated −£0.7m loss → +£2.9m improvement. Operating cash inflow £2.5m — confirms EBITDA-to-cash conversion is real. FY25 EPS: not explicitly stated; consensus was −0.0p, consistent with the EBITDA/interest/loss position.

"Delivering an expected £2.2m Adjusted EBITDA in FY25 and underlying free cashflow of £2.5m from operations represents a fundamental shift in our operating model."*

  1. Q1 FY26 actuals: Revenue £11.0m · Adjusted EBITDA £0.7m · Forward contracted order book £10.7m (31 March 2026).

"The Group has made a strong start to a year, delivering, for Q1-26: Revenue of £11.0m · Adjusted EBITDA of £0.7m · Forward contracted order book of £10.7m"*

  1. FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here):
  • (1) New base EPS (FY25 actual): ~0.0p (near breakeven as confirmed).
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: nil — no acquisitions.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: FY26 EBITDA guided £4.5m vs FY25 £2.2m = +£2.3m. However £0.6m contract asset expensing offsets gross profit → net EBITDA uplift to £4.5m is the guided figure. D&A ~£0.5m → EBIT ~£4.0m. Interest ~£0.2m → PBT ~£3.8m. Tax: nil (losses carried forward). EPS = £3.8m / 387.2m shares = ~1.0p.
  • (4) Interest step-up: £1.0m Harwood facility being repaid — modest, no material step-up.
  • Implied FY26 EPS: ~1.0p vs FY2 consensus 0.5p = +100% potential revision to FY2 EPS. High uncertainty given small absolute numbers; sensitive to working capital and cost phasing.
  1. H1 FY26 guidance (key H1 tracking signal): Revenue ~£24.0m expected (vs H1 FY25 £10.1m = +137.6% YoY). Already ~£21.0m delivered or contracted. MACE GB Energy installations for 73 schools largely complete, on track by 31 May 2026.

"The Group expects to report record H1-26 revenues of circa £24.0m (H1-25: £10.1m), in line with management expectations which is underpinned by circa £21.0m of revenue already delivered or contracted to be delivered based on the revised revenue recognition policy."

  1. FY26 revenue guidance upgraded: £38.0m (vs FY2 consensus £34.2m = +11.1% beat vs pre-RNS consensus). Reflects mobilisation of larger contracts, pipeline conversion, framework/partnership contribution, and recognition policy reclassification (+£4.0m from FY25).

"The Board has increased its FY26 revenue expectations to £38.0m, reflecting improved visibility and the impact of revised revenue recognition on the year as a whole."

  1. FY26 EBITDA guidance: £4.5m — unchanged. Incremental gross profit from higher revenue broadly offset by £0.6m contract asset expensing. This constrains EPS upgrade magnitude despite the revenue upgrade.
  2. Capital: £1.0m Harwood facility — expects to repay ahead of 31 July 2026 due date. No dividend. Working capital invested in H2 FY25 expected to unwind in FY26, supporting cash generation. Santander NatWest £40m facility for public sector; Redaptive partnership up to £100m project funding — these are off-balance-sheet project finance structures, not corporate debt.
  3. Qualitative tone: "We entered FY26 with strong momentum and increased confidence with our strongest ever pipeline of opportunities." Tailwinds cited: energy volatility, Net Zero requirements, off-balance-sheet demand. Multi-channel platform described as "proving itself at scale."

EPS quality check: FY25 near-zero EPS with no tax distortion (losses shelter). The EBITDA includes £0.8m SBC add-back in FY25 (£0.2m in Q1 FY26) — adjusted EBITDA is a clean metric here given the company's stage. No one-off credits inflating the number. Revenue recognition change is a policy reclassification, not a quality issue.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

Guidance covers FY26 explicitly: Revenue £38.0m (numeric, explicit upgrade vs consensus), EBITDA £4.5m (unchanged). H1 FY26 revenue of ~£24.0m guided with £21.0m already contracted — exceptional forward visibility. The combined RNS is highly constructive for FY26.

The constraint is: EBITDA held at £4.5m despite revenue upgrade → EPS uplift from the revenue beat is partially neutralised. The £4.5m EBITDA is the operative figure for brokers modelling FY26.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — explicit FY26 revenue upgrade to £38.0m (+11.1% vs consensus), H1 FY26 ~£24.0m with £21.0m contracted, record order pipeline, clean audit opinion. EBITDA unchanged constrains to Constructive rather than Upgrade-triggering. Provisional points: +8.

Divergence check: FY25 revenue missed stale consensus (−17.8%) but this is 100% a recognition reclassification. Operationally FY25 EBITDA beat the implied prior trajectory. Outlook (Constructive for FY26) is consistent with the operational delivery. No divergence penalty — the "miss" is a policy change, not a trading deterioration. Flag explicitly: accounting reclassification, not an operational miss.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is the FY26 revenue upgrade to £38.0m, exceeding pre-RNS consensus of £34.2m by +11.1%. This is explicit management guidance, not soft language — and it is backed by ~£21.0m already delivered or contracted as at this RNS. Q1 FY26 delivered £11.0m revenue and £0.7m adjusted EBITDA, putting H1 FY26 tracking at ~£24.0m — a +137.6% YoY improvement vs H1 FY25's £10.1m. The FY25 revenue "miss" of −17.8% vs stale consensus is entirely an accounting reclassification (revenue recognition policy tightened under new auditor Cooper Parry), with zero cash impact and zero change to underlying contract economics. This distinction is critical: operationally, FY25 delivered EBITDA of £2.2m — the company's first profitable year — versus a £0.7m loss in FY24 restated. Operating cash conversion of £2.5m confirms the EBITDA is real.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the operative signal is the H1 FY26 tracking deviation. Against the 2yr avg H1 baseline of 34.8% of FY consensus, the guided H1 FY26 revenue of ~£24.0m represents 70.2% of FY2 consensus — a deviation of +35.4pp, the strongest possible signal (🟢🟢 STRONG BUY). The downside case is well-contained: with £21.0m already contracted, the gap to the £24.0m H1 target is only £3.0m, and the MACE/GB Energy school installations (73 schools) are largely complete with May 2026 completion expected. The H2 FY26 burden implied by the £38.0m guidance is only ~£14.0m vs FY25 H2 of £8.9m (+57.3% YoY), which is comfortably supported by the forward contracted order book of £10.7m at March 2026. The upgrade resilience rests on the contracted nature of revenues: EaaS project finance structures mean revenue is recognised against delivered infrastructure, not soft pipeline. The constraint on the upgrade is EBITDA held at £4.5m despite the revenue lift — the £0.6m contract asset expensing and thin project margins mean the revenue upgrade does not fully flow to earnings.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers (Canaccord Genuity as corporate broker) will raise FY26 revenue from £34.2m to ~£38.0m (+11.1%). FY26 EPS upgrades from 0.5p consensus to approximately 0.9–1.0p (+80–100% in percentage terms, ~+0.5p in absolute). FY25 revenue will be restated to £19.0m (from £23.1m) as a policy reclassification — this is not a cut, it is a restatement. Target prices are likely to be maintained at or near 12p (current 140% upside from 5p) given the clean audit confirmation removes the key downgrade risk. The main watch point is: can EBITDA exceed £4.5m guidance? The working capital unwind from H2 FY25 and the full revenue recognition catch-up in Q2 FY26 could push EBITDA slightly above guidance — this is the potential surprise that would drive a second upgrade cycle at H1 results. For now the score of 57 reflects genuine operational progress and a confirmed revenue upgrade, constrained by the thin EBITDA margins and recognition complexity that will keep some investors cautious until audited FY25 results are published.

🏁 Constructive/upgrade likely on FY26 revenue; EPS revision modest in absolute terms but material in %; clean audit removes overhang; share price at 5p vs 12p TP suggests the market has materially over-discounted the recognition restatement.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING

  • FX: Qualitative headwind noted; not formally penalised.
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year ending 31 March 2026)

  1. FY revenue — slight beat: Expected YoY increase of c.8% vs FY25 £79.6m = implied FY26 ~£85.9m. Disclosed consensus: £83.5m. Beat of ~£2.4m (+2.9%). Sharescope FY1 consensus £83.6m: beat of ~£2.3m (+2.7%).

"an expected year-on-year increase in revenue of c.8%, slightly ahead of market expectations (2025: £79.6 million)"

  1. Gross margin improvement: Structural positive — improved product pricing + cost of goods. Not described as one-off. Durability implications for FY27 base.

"The Company also expects to report improved gross margins for the year, primarily driven by improved product pricing and cost of goods"

  1. EPS (implied): No explicit figure. EBITDA materially ahead + H1 actual −0.5p = implied H2 EPS carries full profit load. Implied FY EPS range ~3.2–4.0p vs consensus 2.7p = potential beat of +19–48%.
  1. Geographic strength: North America and Latin America particularly strong despite currency headwinds and tariff challenges. Implies volume/price gains outweighed FX drag.

"Revenue growth has been particularly strong in North America and Latin America, despite currency headwinds and tariff challenges"

1. Half-on-Half Growth Pattern

  • H2 derivation: FY implied ~£85.9m − H1 £39.4m = H2 ~£46.5m
  • Revenue trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — H2 FY25 −9.7%, H1 FY26 [+18.7%], H2 FY26 (implied) +0.2%. Sharp H1 FY26 reversal from two consecutive declining halves is a strong signal.
  • EPS trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — structurally H2-weighted; H1 improving meaningfully (−3.7p → −0.5p); implied H2 3.2p+ on more normalised trajectory vs the −3.7/+5.2 extreme of FY25.

2. Seasonal H1 Tracking (pre-FY mode — informational)

  • Revenue: H1 actual £39.4m ÷ FY1 consensus £83.6m = 47.1% vs 3yr avg baseline 41.7% → [+5.4pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY signal fired in H1
  • Buy trigger: H1 Rev > [£34.8m × 1.015] = £35.3m → £39.4m ✓ (by £4.1m)
  • EPS H1 tracking: UNTRACKABLE (H1 avg split n/a due to historically negative H1 EPS)

3. Implied H2 Momentum (pre-FY mode)

  • Implied H2 revenue ~£46.5m vs last 3 H2 avg £49.4m = flat classification (−5 to +5% range; actual +0.2% YoY vs prior H2)
  • EBITDA beat context: if full-year EBITDA £9–10.5m and H1 EBITDA £3.0m, implied H2 EBITDA £6–7.5m — broadly in line with prior H2 £6.9m. Beat is from structural margin improvement flowing through the year, not H2 volume surge.

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +1.1p (+68.8%) net — major upgrade Jul–Aug 25, partial Dec 25 reversal, recovered to 2.7p. FLAT last 7 weeks — market has not yet reacted to today's beat.
  • Revenue: broadly flat at £83–84m throughout. 2.7% revenue beat vs consensus is modest; EBITDA leverage is the story.
  • Divergence: Price −39.3% (164p → 99.5p) while EPS consensus +68.8% higher. Severe disconnect — today's RNS directly addresses the market's scepticism. High conviction re-rating setup.

5. Structural Flags

  • [H2-loading pattern]: EAH structurally H2-weighted in revenue and profit (pig/poultry seasonal demand). H1 has historically been loss-making at EPS level. H1 FY26 loss narrowing to −0.5p from −3.7p is material structural improvement.
  • [Margin step-change]: Pricing + COGS improvement not described as one-off. If durable, changes FY27 base. "primarily driven by improved product pricing and cost of goods"
  • [Currency headwind in growth markets]: GBP vs USD/LatAm FX ongoing risk. No quantification. Ongoing monitoring required.
  • [Audit/provisioning caveat]: Explicit mention in trading update. Inventory provisioning and receivables can be material in animal health sector. Moderate but real risk.
PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 = EBITDA "materially ahead" of £7.6m consensus — implies ~£9–10.5m, a +18–38% positive surprise. "Material" in UK small-cap convention signals a genuine deviation, not a rounding difference. Brokers will raise EBITDA and EPS estimates significantly. #2 = Gross margin structural improvement (pricing + COGS) — durability of margin step-up changes the forward earnings base. Brokers modelling EAH on thin margins will need to step up structural assumptions for FY27+.

  1. Target price / recommendation: Current consensus TP 157p vs close 99.5p (58% upside). Material EBITDA beat likely drives TP upgrades toward 180–220p range. Some Hold → Buy upgrades probable. Stock 40% below peak despite improving fundamentals makes this high-conviction for momentum-focused brokers.
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: "Materially ahead" is the opposite of conservative guidance — this is strong positive signal language. Company is setting market expectations above consensus. Classic upgrade cycle language; increases probability of sustained re-rating.
  1. Key risk: Audit provisioning caveat is the primary risk. "Customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning" explicitly opens the door to balance sheet adjustments that could reduce reported profitability vs trading update. In animal health, inventory provisioning and receivables can be material. "The final outcome for the full year will be subject to the usual audit process, including the customary assessment of balance sheet provisioning"

ECO Animal Health's pre-FY trading update for the year ending 31 March 2026 delivers a clear and decisive beat on the most watched metric. Full-year revenue is expected to grow approximately 8% YoY from £79.6m to approximately £85.9m, versus the disclosed consensus of £83.5m — a beat of approximately £2.4m (+2.9%). Against the Sharescope FY1 consensus of £83.6m, the beat is nearly identical. More significantly, adjusted EBITDA is guided to be "materially ahead of market expectations" against a consensus of £7.6m — language that in UK small-cap convention implies outperformance of ≥15–20%, pointing to an implied EBITDA figure of approximately £9.0–10.5m. The #1 metric driving broker reaction will be this EBITDA beat, which represents a 18–38% positive surprise against a consensus that was itself already above the prior year (£7.6m vs £7.3m FY25 actual). This is not a modest beat — this is a material positive step-change in profitability.

In pre-FY mode, the H1 tracking signal (informational) confirms the strength visible in the FY guidance: H1 revenue of £39.4m represented 47.1% of the FY1 consensus, against a 3-year average seasonal baseline of 41.7% — a deviation of +5.4pp which clears the STRONG BUY threshold with significant margin. The buy trigger fired (H1 Rev £39.4m >> trigger of £35.3m by £4.1m). The structural driver behind the beat is gross margin improvement from pricing discipline and cost-of-goods reduction — not a one-off mix effect. This matters for durability: if the margin step-up is structural, FY27 estimates are too low. The implied H2 revenue of approximately £46.5m is broadly flat YoY (+0.2%), confirming the beat is entirely a margin and H1-momentum story rather than H2 volume. The balance sheet is a further positive — net cash (ND/EBITDA −2.8x) removes any financial leverage risk. The audit provisioning caveat is the single material downside risk that constrains the score below 90.

Broker revisions will be significant. FY1 EPS is expected to be upgraded from the current 2.7p consensus to approximately 3.5–5.0p — a +30–85% revision, with the wide range reflecting uncertainty in the EBITDA-to-EPS walk and the provisioning caveat. FY1 Revenue upgrades will be modest: approximately £83.6m → £85.9m (+2.7%). FY2 EPS (currently 3.1p) is likely upgraded to the 3.8–5.5p range as brokers roll forward the higher structural margin base. The consensus target price of 157p is expected to be raised materially — likely into the 180–220p range by the most constructive brokers — while the stock at 99.5p represents a 58% discount to current consensus TP and would still sit at a 45–55% discount even to the upgraded TP range. Upgrade cycle probability: high. The combination of "materially ahead" EBITDA language, structural margin improvement, a 40% share price decline from peak, and a 58% discount to even the unrevised consensus TP creates a textbook upgrade cycle setup. The July results presentation will be the confirmation catalyst.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 0 — ROUTING & FX
PHASE 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

ECEL is a UK-domiciled manufacturer selling almost entirely in the UK. Geographical segment data confirms UK revenue of £401.3m out of £403.5m total — Republic of Ireland £2.2m (0.5%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B: skip. No FX penalty applied.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY 2025 Preliminary Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS consensus state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 15.1p · Revenue £403.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 18.8p · Revenue £429.8m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over snapshot period: 16.4p → 15.1p = −1.3p (−7.9%). Downgrades dominated: sharp cut in early Sept 2025 (17.4p → 15.0p), then marginal nudge up to 15.1p in late Jan 2026. Last-4-week trend: FLAT (15.1p unchanged 24 Jan → 13 Mar 2026). Revenue net change: £409.4m → £403.8m = −1.4%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.7% of FY = £200.7m · EPS 44.1% of FY = 6.66p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £175.7m · EPS 5.6p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode): FY1 consensus £403.8m minus current H1 actual £193.2m = implied H2 £210.6m vs prior H2 £182.2m = +15.6% YoY. FY1 consensus EPS 15.1p minus current H1 EPS 5.9p = implied H2 9.2p vs prior H2 8.7p = +5.7% YoY.
  • FX: N/A — >99% UK revenue, no non-GBP exposure exceeding 30%.
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary Results for the year ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue — FY actual: £403.5m, up 13% on 2024 (£357.9m). vs FY1 consensus £403.8m → miss of −£0.3m (−0.07%) — essentially in line. Organic revenue flat vs 2024; organic volumes −2%. Alunet contributed £46.7m (10 months post-acquisition).

"Sales for the year were £403.5 million, up 13% on 2024 (£357.9 million), or flat excluding Alunet, with organic volumes down 2%."

  1. EPS / earnings — FY adjusted basic EPS: 14.6p vs FY1 consensus 15.1p → miss of −0.5p (−3.3%). Reported basic EPS 9.5p. Adjusted PBT £19.0m vs consensus £20.0m → miss of −£1.0m (−5.0%). Higher finance costs (£5.1m vs £2.8m in 2024) post-Alunet acquisition the primary drag.

"Adjusted basic earnings per share were 14.6 pence and diluted earnings per share for the year were 14.5 pence (2024: 14.4 pence and 14.3 pence respectively)."

  1. Order book / forward work: No explicit order book quantum. Strategy references pipeline visibility: 250-site branch target, c.30 new sites over 3–4 years, £500m revenue / £50m op profit 5-year target. Alunet expected "another year of good growth in 2026."

"We expect another year of good growth in 2026, driven by further market share gains and new product introductions, alongside capturing group-wide synergies and manufacturing efficiencies."

  1. Margin, profitability, cost signals: Adjusted operating profit £24.1m, +6% vs 2024 (£22.8m) — in line with expectations. Gross margin 50.9% vs 52.6% in 2024 (organic: 52.6% flat). Overheads £153.8m, +10% (organic +1%). Adjusted EBITDA £51.5m vs consensus £51.1m — slight beat. IT infrastructure investment totalling ~£13m over 2024–27; annualised cost savings of c.£4m already delivered; recycling consolidation expected to yield c.£1.5m p.a. from 2027.

"Adjusted operating profit was £24.1 million, up 6% on 2024. This reflects a strong contribution from Alunet and effective cost control, partially offset by lower organic volumes, competitive pressure on selling prices in the branches, labour cost inflation and targeted investment to maintain momentum in our strategic initiatives."

  1. Capital returns and per-share items: Total DPS 6.4p (interim 2.3p + proposed final 4.1p), +5% vs 2024 (6.1p), in line with FY1 consensus 6.40p. £5m buyback complete. Intention to continue buybacks. Pre-IFRS 16 net debt £22.1m (0.7x pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA), down from £29.0m at H1. RCF refinanced March 2026, matures 2030, £75m facility.

"The Board proposes a final dividend of 4.1 pence per share (2024: 3.9 pence per share), which results in total dividends for the year of 6.4 pence per share (2024: 6.1 pence per share), up 5%."

  1. Qualitative tone: Cautiously constructive. Management acknowledges RMI demand "remains sluggish." Middle East uncertainty cited twice as a caveat to buyback continuation. Strategy targets reaffirmed (£500m rev / £50m OP) but with explicit caveat on timing: "the timing and pace of market recovery will continue to be a factor." CEO change (Darren Waters out, Will Truman appointed 9 Feb 2026 from NED position) is an organisational risk flag. No explicit FY2026 revenue or EPS guidance given.

"Demand in the RMI market remains sluggish, and we are therefore continuing to focus on operational improvements and cost control. The potential impact of the evolving situation in the Middle East is difficult to assess at this time."

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

| FY | Rev £m | Rev YoY % | EPS p | EPS YoY % |

|||||---|

| FY22 (3y ago) | 381.2 | — | 21.3 | — |

| FY23 (2y ago) | 364.5 | −4.4% | 11.0 | −48.4% |

| FY24 (1y ago) | 357.9 | −1.8% | 14.4 | +30.9% |

| FY25e* | 403.5 | +12.7% | 14.6 | +1.4% |

Revenue growth trajectory: Volatile — −4.4%, −1.8%, +12.7%. The jump in FY25 is wholly acquisition-driven (Alunet +£46.7m); organic revenue flat.

EPS growth trajectory: Volatile — −48.4%, +30.9%, +1.4%. Sharp trough in FY23, recovery in FY24, near-flat in FY25 despite higher finance costs. No consistent directional trend.

1. Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

| Period | Rev £m | YoY % | EPS p | YoY % |

|||||---|

| H1 FY22 | 188.8 | — | 11.5 | — |

| H2 FY22 | 192.4 | — | 9.8 | — |

| H1 FY23 | 184.4 | −2.3% | 4.3 | −62.6% |

| H2 FY23 | 180.1 | −6.4% | 6.7 | −31.6% |

| H1 FY24 | 175.7 | −4.7% | 5.6 | +30.2% |

| H2 FY24 | 182.2 | +1.2% | 8.7 | +29.9% |

| H1 FY25 | 193.2 | +10.0% | 5.9 | +5.4% |

| H2 FY25* | 210.3 | +15.4% | 8.7 | +0.0% |

H2 FY25 derivation: Revenue = £403.5m − £193.2m = £210.3m. EPS = 14.6p − 5.9p = 8.7p.

EPS trajectory (HoH): Volatile — H1 FY25 +5.4%, H2 FY24 +29.9%, H1 FY24 +30.2%. H2 FY25 implied at 8.7p = flat YoY. Organic EPS stagnant; Alunet masks weakness.

Revenue trajectory (HoH): Accelerating in nominal terms — H2 FY24 +1.2%, H1 FY25 +10.0%, H2 FY25 implied +15.4%. However, acquisition-driven; organic is flat/negative.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% (49.7%) × FY1 consensus £403.8m = £200.7m
  • EPS baseline: 3yr avg H1% (44.1%) × FY1 consensus 15.1p = 6.66p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £193.2m ÷ FY1 consensus £403.8m = 47.8% vs baseline 49.7% → deviation = [−1.9pp] → 🟡 IN LINE (borderline CAUTION)
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 5.9p ÷ FY1 consensus 15.1p = 39.1% vs baseline 44.1% → deviation = [−5.0pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL (H1 materially underperforming seasonal norm; H2 burden elevated)
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 15.1p − H1 actual 5.9p = 9.2p required in H2 vs historical H2 avg 8.4p. H2 burden HIGHER than historical average.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£200.7m × 1.015] = £203.7m → H1 actual £193.2m ✗ · H1 EPS > [6.66p × 1.015] = 6.76p → H1 actual 5.9p ✗
  • Historical hit rate: Positive H1 deviation preceded FY beat in 1 of last 3 years.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • Implied H2 FY25 Revenue: £210.3m vs 3yr H2 avg £184.9m → +13.7% → strong (acquisition-inflated)
  • Implied H2 FY25 EPS: 8.7p vs 3yr H2 avg 8.4p → +3.6% → moderate (organic flat, Alunet contribution marginal at H2 level)

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change −1.3p (−7.9%) over snapshot period. One significant downgrade wave Sept 2025 (−2.4p step). Upgrades: 1 minor nudge (+0.1p Jan 2026).
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (15.1p unchanged since 24 Jan 2026 through 13 Mar 2026)
  • Divergence: Price fell from 255p to 210p (−17.6%) over the same period while EPS cuts were front-loaded. The share price has declined further than forecast cuts suggest — stock is pricing in ongoing concern about organic recovery pace and CEO transition risk.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Alunet H2-weighting shift: Alunet acquired March 2025 — 10-month contribution in FY25. From FY26 onwards, Alunet contributes full 12 months, adding ~£6.6m of incremental revenue. This mechanically shifts the H2-weighting of the consolidated group slightly, as Alunet's seasonality is not yet disclosed.

"In the period from the acquisition at the beginning of March to 31 December 2025, Alunet added sales of £46.7 million to the Group."

  • ERP cost drag (non-recurring, running to end-2026): Total expected non-underlying IT cost ~£13m over 2024–27. £6.4m expensed to end-2025. Remaining ~£6.6m over 2026–27. This will continue to suppress reported earnings and is a source of noise in EPS comparisons.

"Total expected non-underlying costs for the system replacement are in the region of £13 million over the 2024-27 period, with transition to the new systems expected at the end of 2026."

  • CEO change risk: Darren Waters departed 9 Feb 2026. Will Truman (prior NED/CFO at Imagesound) appointed internally — reduces transition risk but introduces strategic continuity uncertainty at a critical juncture.
  • Recycling consolidation: February 2026 project to close Selby, consolidate to Ilkeston. £2.6m capex, ~£3m non-underlying charge (including £1.5m non-cash). c.£1.5m annualised savings from 2027.
PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — EPS miss vs consensus: The adjusted EPS of 14.6p vs FY1 consensus 15.1p is a −3.3% miss at the headline level, driven by higher-than-expected finance costs (£5.1m vs ~£2.8m implied in prior consensus). This will be the primary focus of broker notes — the magnitude is small but comes on top of a year of progressive downgrading. Brokers will scrutinise whether FY26 finance costs remain elevated (debt facility refinanced, Alunet contingent consideration unwinding through P&L) and whether organic volume recovery is credible.

#2 Driver — Alunet contribution beat / organic miss divergence: Alunet delivered £4.8m adj. operating profit (10 months), which represents a strong £1.8m uplift vs corresponding 2024 period. However, organic Branch Network adj. OP collapsed from £6.5m to £3.4m (−48%), and Profiles OP fell 10%. The organic business substantially missed. Brokers will separate these: Alunet provides a genuine positive (FY26 full-year benefit), while organic weakness signals the market has not recovered as management and consensus hoped.

#3 Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26): Revenue likely held/nudged up marginally — Alunet's full-year effect adds ~£6.6m mechanically, partially offset by continued organic caution. Net: hold to +1–2%. EPS: FY26 consensus 15.1p — brokers likely to cut FY26 EPS modestly by −2 to −5% given organic softness, higher finance costs, and no explicit FY26 guidance — revised FY26 EPS range likely 14.0–14.8p. FY2 (FY27): EPS currently 18.8p — likely held or trimmed to ~17.5–18.5p, with recovery story intact but back-end loaded.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: No explicit FY26 guidance issued. The language is deliberately cautious — "demand in the RMI market remains sluggish," "timing and pace of market recovery will continue to be a factor." No "comfortable with current expectations" language. This is not classic sandbagging; it reads as genuine uncertainty, which limits the probability of an upgrade cycle. The one genuinely conservative element is Alunet: "good growth" in 2026 could imply upside to current consensus if organic recovers even modestly.

#5 Key risk: The organic Branch Network operating profit has fallen to £3.4m from £6.5m in a single year (−48%). If RMI demand does not recover in H1 2026, and the new branch programme continues to drag (£1.1m loss in 2025), the organic operating leverage story breaks down entirely and FY26 consensus EPS may prove too high even at the trimmed level.

"Branch Network adjusted operating profit for 2025 was £3.4 million, 48% below 2024, reflecting competitive pressure on selling prices in the branches and higher overheads."

#6 Overall tone: Neutral / hold and wait. The EPS miss is not catastrophic but confirms the bear case on organic. Alunet is a genuine positive offset. No guidance given. CEO change introduces an overhang. Brokers will likely trim FY26 EPS modestly, hold TPs or cut slightly, and remain on Hold/Neutral.

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

/100

Cost savings delivered (c.£4m p.a.)+4

H1 EPS deviation −5.0pp below seasonal baseline (🔴 SELL SIGNAL)−10

No FY26 guidance; CEO transition; Middle East caveat on buybacks−5
H2 EPS burden higher than 3yr avg; both buy triggers failed−5
ERP drag continues to 2027; recycling consolidation non-underlying charge−3
Organic gross margin pressure vs Alunet dilution−3

ECEL's FY25 preliminary results delivered revenue of £403.5m — a fractional −£0.3m miss (−0.07%) vs the FY1 consensus of £403.8m — and adjusted EPS of 14.6p, a miss of −0.5p (−3.3%) against consensus of 15.1p. The miss is not dramatic in isolation, but it lands after a year in which EPS consensus was already cut from 17.4p to 15.1p (−7.9%), so there is no "reset and beat" dynamic here. The #1 driver of the miss is elevated finance costs of £5.1m vs £2.8m in 2024, reflecting the debt drawn to fund the Alunet acquisition (initial consideration £22m, RCF drawdown average £28.1m). The operating line delivered: adjusted operating profit £24.1m, +6% YoY, with Alunet contributing £4.8m OP in its first 10 months — the clear headline positive in this set of results.

The pre-RNS H1 tracking analysis correctly flagged the risk: H1 FY25 EPS of 5.9p sat 39.1% of FY1 consensus vs a 3yr seasonal baseline of 44.1% — a deviation of −5.0pp, squarely in 🔴 SELL SIGNAL territory, with both buy triggers failing (Revenue H1 £193.2m vs trigger £203.7m; EPS H1 5.9p vs trigger 6.76p). The realised FY EPS of 14.6p confirmed the signal. Going forward into FY26, the H2 burden analysis is critical: the FY26 EPS consensus of ~15.1p requires implied H2 of ~9.2p — above the 3yr H2 average of 8.4p — meaning consensus already assumes organic recovery plus full-year Alunet contribution. The downside risk is not fully contained: if Branch Network OP remains near £3.4m (down from £6.5m), Alunet's incremental FY26 contribution (estimated c.£0.5–0.8m OP uplift from full-year vs 10-month) alone cannot close the gap. The structural positive — Alunet at £4.8m OP on 10 months, growing 28% in the acquisition period with market share gains — is a genuine offset, but it relies on continued outperformance in a business that has been under Eurocell's ownership for less than a year.

Brokers are likely to trim FY26 EPS estimates by −2% to −5%, taking consensus from c.15.1p toward 14.3–14.8p, reflecting: (i) higher finance costs now confirmed at £5.1m for FY25 likely running at a similar level in FY26 given £27.7m of debt still drawn; (ii) organic Branch Network fragility with no explicit recovery guidance; and (iii) continued non-underlying ERP costs (~£6.6m remaining over 2026–27). FY27 (FY2) EPS of 18.8p is likely held or trimmed marginally to 17.5–18.5p — the recovery thesis requires RMI market normalisation and Alunet synergies maturing, both of which remain timing-uncertain. Target price of consensus 210p — representing 76% upside to the current 119p — may see modest cuts toward 180–200p range as brokers reduce near-term EPS estimates. The stock has already been de-rated aggressively (from 255p to 119p, approximately −53% over the snapshot period), which provides valuation support, but there is no clear catalyst in this RNS to trigger re-rating. The Middle East caveat on buyback continuation is a subtle negative — removing the buyback support element reduces the total return story from the c.8% yield narrative. Upgrade cycle probability: low in the near term. This is a "show us the organic recovery" situation. The FY26 H1 results (due H2 2026) will be the genuine inflection point — if Branch Network volumes recover in spring 2026 and H1 EPS tracks materially above the new 44.1% seasonal baseline (which equates to ~6.7p on 15.1p FY26 consensus), the upgrade cycle can start. Until then, brokers hold, TPs drift modestly lower, and the stock remains range-bound around current distressed levels.
