scorecards.analysisText:
ELIX

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings:

  • FY22 = 3y ago · FY23 = 2y ago · FY24 = 1y ago (prior year actual) · FY25 = FY1 (current, results) · FY26e = FY2 (2y fc / forward year)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

ELIX · Q2 · FY Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as Full Year Results for FY25. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 54.9p · Revenue £149.0m (Sharescope pre-RNS)
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 64.9p · Revenue £185.6m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full period +13.2% (48.5p → 54.9p). Step-up events in Sep 25 (+6.7p — likely interim results upgrade), Oct 25 minor revision, Feb 26 modest nudge. 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (54.6p → 54.9p).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.5% of FY = £70.8m · EPS 49.7% of FY = 27.3p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £41.5m · EPS 18.5p
  • H2 implied (pre-RNS FY25): H1 FY25 actual = £71.4m (Sharescope current H1). H2 pre-RNS = £149.0m − £71.4m = £77.6m vs FY24 H2 = £111.3m − £41.5m = £69.8m → +11.2% YoY.
  • FX: Currency = GBP. ELIX 63% US revenue in FY25. USD exposure >30%. Phase 0B: USD exposure ~63% in FY25. Exceeds 30% threshold.

Need to assess GBP/USD spot vs prior year avg. RNS is full year results — need to check if constant currency data is disclosed.

From RNS: Revenue £149.6m (FY25). No constant currency growth explicitly stated alongside same-as-reported comparisons in this document — the company presents in GBP and US operations in USD. No currency movements section. The RNS mentions "currency translation on foreign currency net investments" = -£4.4m OCI in FY25 — this is translation loss on balance sheet, not P&L FX. For income statement, the 63% US revenue will be affected by GBP/USD.

Checking if constant currency = reported: The RNS does not disclose constant currency growth figures. Revenues grew 34% YoY; without a CC comparison, the constant currency override rule cannot fire (override requires CC growth within 0.5pp of reported).

GBP/USD: need spot rate vs FY24 average. ELIX FY25 = year ended 31 Dec 2025. Prior year average (FY24) GBP/USD was approximately 1.28–1.29. FY25 average rate approximately 1.27–1.28. GBP slightly weaker in FY25 vs FY24 — tailwind for USD revenues translated to GBP. Conservative estimate: GBP ~0.5–1.5¢ weaker (0.5–1.2% swing). This is within ±2¢ neutral band.

Searched the web

Phase 0B — FX Assessment for ELIX:

GBP/USD average in 2024: 1.2781 Exchange Rates UK. GBP/USD average in 2025: 1.3190 Exchange Rates.

GBP was significantly stronger in 2025 vs 2024: +4.1¢ (1.2781 → 1.3190). This is a GBP headwind for ELIX — USD revenues translate to fewer GBP at a stronger pound.

Exposure: ELIX US revenues = 63% of FY25 revenue. Exposure 50%+ band. GBP change: +4.1¢ = well above the >3¢ headwind threshold.

Penalty: 50%+ exposure + headwind (GBP stronger >3¢) = −11 to −12 pts (hard cap at −11 to −12).

However — the actual FY25 revenue delivered was £149.6m vs FY24's £111.3m = +34%. The FX headwind did not prevent a 34% revenue beat. This means the organic performance was even stronger than reported. The penalty applies to the score based on how much FX suppressed reported numbers vs what consensus assumed. Sharescope pre-RNS consensus = £149.0m. Actual = £149.6m = slight beat of £0.6m (0.4%).

If consensus was built on a neutral rate assumption (1.28) and actual rate was 1.319 (GBP stronger, USD headwind), some of the would-be reported revenue was reduced. The FX headwind is already embedded in the delivered number. The penalty should be applied to assess whether forward estimates adequately price FX risk for FY26e consensus (£185.6m).

Key insight: This is a retrospective full-year results RNS. The FX headwind was already embedded in the delivered FY25 number (£149.6m). The question for Phase 5 scoring is whether FY26e consensus (£185.6m) is at risk from GBP strength continuing. Current GBP/USD spot (April 2026) vs FY25 average 1.319: need to assess. Spot today ~1.32–1.33. If GBP is at similar level in FY26, the headwind is comparable to FY25 vs FY24 (neutral vs FY25 baseline). Apply reduced penalty given FX is already embedded in delivered actuals.

For Phase 0B scoring: FX headwind to FY26 forward estimates (vs FY25 baseline of 1.319). Spot ~1.325 = approximately neutral vs FY25 avg. Applying neutral band penalty: −5 pts for 50%+ USD exposure with neutral current rate vs prior year avg.

Phase 0B output: 63% USD exposure · GBP/USD FY25 avg 1.319 vs FY24 avg 1.278 — GBP was a headwind in FY25 vs FY24 (+4.1¢); but actual FY25 delivered strong results. FY26 forward: GBP/USD spot ~1.325 vs FY25 avg 1.319 → approximately neutral. FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · 63% USD · 🟡 neutral rate (current spot vs FY25 avg)

Now continuing ELIX Phases 1–5.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT (continued)

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • FX: 63% USD exposure. GBP/USD FY25 avg 1.319 vs FY24 avg 1.278 → GBP headwind in FY25. FY26 forward rate ~neutral. FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts). 🟡 neutral rate.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: H1 FY25 £11.3m → FY1fc (FY25) £25.0m (Sharescope). RNS actual: net debt £24.1m at year-end. ND/EBITDA: FY25fc 0.60x, FY26e fc 0.60x. Interest cover FY25: 25.2x, FY26e: 18.4x. ND/FCF: 0.8x FY25, 1.0x FY26. Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage (ND/EBITDA 0.6x, interest cover 25x, effectively negligible).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue FY25 actual: £149.6m vs pre-RNS consensus £149.0m → beat of £0.6m = +0.4%. Essentially in-line. Growth vs FY24: +£38.3m = +34% YoY.

"Revenue increased by 34% to £149.6 million (FY 24: £111.3 million)"

  1. Adj EBITDA FY25: £44.3m vs pre-RNS FY1fc £43.3m (Sharescope) → beat of £1.0m = +2.3%. Margin 29.6% vs FY24 28.0% → +1.6pp expansion. Strong operating leverage demonstrated.
  2. Adj diluted EPS FY25: 58.7p vs pre-RNS consensus 54.9p → beat of 3.8p = +6.9%. This is the headline EPS metric — a meaningful beat.

"Adjusted Diluted EPS: 58.7p (FY 24: 43.1p), +36%"

  1. FY26e EPS bridge (construct here):
  • New base: FY25 adj diluted EPS = 58.7p (actual, beats 54.9p consensus by 6.9%).
  • Inorganic delta: Kvadrant Consulting acquired Jan 2026 (post year-end). FY25 was TRC partial (£8.5m revenue contribution from Sep 2025 acquisition). Full year TRC in FY26 + Kvadrant from Jan 2026 full year.
  • TRC annualisation: RNS states if TRC acquired 1 Jan 2025, FY25 group revenue would have been £168.8m and PBT £36.5m. Actual FY25 revenue £149.6m. Pro-forma annualisation delta = £168.8m − £149.6m = +£19.2m additional TRC revenue in FY26 full year. PBT pro-forma = £36.5m vs actual PBT £27.6m → +£8.9m additional PBT if TRC was full year. After tax (~25%) → +£6.7m PAT. Per 49.7m diluted shares → +~13.5p. This is the inorganic annualisation uplift.
  • Kvadrant: Revenue £6.2m DKK53.4m / full year. Small contribution.
  • Organic EBITDA delta: FY25 adj EBITDA margin 29.6% (up from 28.0%). If applied to FY26 consensus revenue £185.6m: £185.6m × 29.6% = £54.9m EBITDA. Less D&A, interest = FY26 adj PBT. Organic revenue growth target: "confident in delivering sustainable growth." Management guides FY26 trading "in line with management expectations" with "record Q1."
  • Interest step-up: Net debt increased from nil to £24.1m (TRC acquisition). Finance costs FY25 = £2.305m (interest on RCF + term loan). FY26 will have higher average debt (Kvadrant acquisition £9.1m cash + TRC earn-out payments). Estimated FY26 finance costs = £2.5–3.0m. After tax = £1.9–2.3m headwind. Per share ~3.8–4.6p. Interest step-up delta: −4p approximately.
  • Dilution: TRC issued 1.43m shares in FY25. Kvadrant issued 415k shares Jan 2026. Total issued ~50.0m shares (per RNS: 50,031,154 shares as of Apr 2026 vs 49.7m diluted avg in FY25). Modest dilution ~0.5–1%.

FY26e EPS bridge summary:

  • FY25 base: 58.7p (actual)
  • TRC annualisation: +13.5p
  • Kvadrant (partial FY26): +~3–4p
  • Organic EBITDA growth on £185.6m consensus rev at 29.6% margin: +10–12p above FY25 contribution
  • Interest step-up: −4p
  • Share count dilution: −1.5p
  • Implied FY26e adj EPS = ~80–83p vs stale Sharescope consensus 64.9p = +23–28% revision

This is a very large implied FY26e revision from the stale consensus. The stale 64.9p appears to be significantly out of date given TRC and Kvadrant.

  1. Adj PBT FY25: £41.0m vs Sharescope FY1fc £39.7m → beat of £1.3m = +3.3%.
  2. Free cash flow: £31.1m (FY24: £28.1m). Net debt £24.1m at year-end vs FY24 net cash £7.5m (utilised RCF for TRC).
  3. Dividend: Total FY25 DPS 22.6p vs FY24 17.8p (+27%). Final dividend 15.0p. vs Sharescope fc DPS 21.40p → beat of 1.2p.
  4. Main Market listing: July 2025. Signals institutional scale.
  5. Inorganic: TRC (Sep 2025) performing ahead of acquisition case. Kvadrant (Jan 2026) — initial accounting not complete. Contingent consideration TRC max £47.8m, recognised £39.4m.
  6. Outlook FY26: "Trading in Q1 FY 26 has been in line with management expectations, with record Q1 revenue." "The Group...remains confident in its ability to deliver sustainable growth and long-term value." Qualitative only. No numeric FY26 guidance.

"Trading in Q1 FY 26 has been in line with management expectations, with record Q1 revenue providing a solid foundation for the year ahead."

EPS quality check: Adj diluted EPS 58.7p. Statutory EPS = 37.18p (basic 41.33p). Adjusted vs statutory: adjust items include M&A costs £0.878m, Main Market listing £1.473m, amortisation £5.466m, share-based payments £5.029m, contingent consideration finance cost £0.610m. All one-time or non-cash. Effective adj tax rate 24.2% vs statutory effective ~28.6% — consistent. Normalised tax rate check: adj PBT tax = £7.894m / £41.046m = 19.2%. Wait — the RNS shows adjusted profit before tax £41.046m and full tax charge £7.894m → 19.2%. But note they add back the tax impact of adjusting items too. Full tax rate on adjusted PAT = £7.894m + £2.036m (tax impact of adjusting items) = ~£9.93m effective tax on adj PBT → 24.2%. This is the adj tax rate. No material distortion vs 25% normalised. ✓ EPS quality: clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification: Forward guidance for FY26: "record Q1 revenue providing a solid foundation for the year ahead." Qualitative only. No FY26 numeric guidance. Confident but unquantified.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive (+6 to +10 pts)

  • Phrase: "record Q1 revenue...solid foundation for the year ahead" + "remains confident in its ability to deliver sustainable growth"
  • Guidance: qualitative only, FY26-directed
  • Multiple visible FY26 drivers: TRC full year, Kvadrant, organic AI consulting demand
  • No divergence: FY25 record beat + constructive FY26 outlook. ✅

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3.1 Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check: FY23 H1+H2 = 33.4+38.4 = 71.7 ✓. FY24 H1+H2 = 41.5+44.3 = 85.8 ≠ stated 85.9 → rounding. FY25 H1+H2: H1 = £71.4m (Sharescope), H2 = £149.6m − £71.4m = £78.2m (RNS actual FY). EBITDA H2 Sharescope: current H2 = -15.1 (negative mirror of H1 — glitch). ⚠️ Using EBITDA FY actuals from RNS.

FY - DecRev £mRev YoY %EPS pEPS YoY %
FY22————
FY2371.7—30.5—
FY2485.9+19.8%43.1+41.3%
FY25 (actual)149.6+74.2%58.7+36.2%
FY26e*185.6+24.1%64.9+10.6%

⚠️ FY25 revenue +74.2% is heavily acquisition-driven (TRC partial from Sep 2025). Organic: +15% organic per RNS. FY26e consensus 64.9p EPS appears significantly stale as demonstrated by EPS bridge showing ~80–83p implied.

Revenue trajectory: FY24 +19.8%, FY25 +74.2% (inorganic), FY26e +24.1% → 🟡 Volatile (acquisition-driven step-changes) EPS trajectory: FY24 +41.3%, FY25 +36.2% (consistent strong organic + inorganic) → 🟢 Accelerating

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS-implied FY25 +74.2%. FY26e consensus +24.1% (lower %). On organic basis both accelerating but inorganic distorts comparisons. Flag as volatile.
  • EPS: FY25 +36.2% vs FY24 +41.3% — slight deceleration on % growth (but absolute EPS growing strongly). FY26e stale +10.6% massively understates actual implied growth (~+35–40% on bridge). Using stale consensus: no acceleration. Using bridge: acceleration. Flag as: EPS acceleration uncertain from stale consensus; bridge implies significant FY26e upgrade — REV na · EPS na (consensus stale)

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode — write but do not score)

H1 FY25 actual = £71.4m. FY25 actual total = £149.6m. H1 as % of FY25 = £71.4m / £149.6m = 47.7% vs 3yr avg 47.5% → deviation = +0.2pp

Signal (informational): 🟡 IN LINE (extremely small deviation). Exactly in line with seasonal norm.

EPS H1 tracking: H1 actual EPS = 29.0p (Sharescope current H1 29.0p — this is FY25 H1 per Sharescope structure). FY25 actual EPS = 58.7p. H1 / FY25 = 29.0/58.7 = 49.4% vs 3yr avg 49.7% → deviation = −0.3pp — essentially perfect in-line.

Phase 3.2 not scored (pre-FY mode). Column 5: na.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored in Phase 5)

H2 actual (RNS-derived): FY25 £149.6m − H1 £71.4m = £78.2m Prior H2 FY24 = £44.3m (FY24 £85.9m − H1 £41.5m) H2 YoY = (£78.2m − £44.3m) / £44.3m = +76.5% — massively distorted by TRC acquisition in Sep 2025 (H2 contribution ~£8.5m organic in the half, plus TRC).

On a more meaningful organic basis: H2 FY25 organic portion = H2 FY25 − TRC contribution (£8.5m from Sep-Dec). Organic H2 ≈ £78.2m − £8.5m = £69.7m vs FY24 H2 £44.3m → +57.3% — still very high, reflecting Hypothesis/Insigniam acquisitions from FY24 also being in.

Classification (reported): +76.5% → 🟢 strong (well above +10%). But entirely driven by TRC inorganic. On organic-only basis still very strong. RNS-derived.

Phase 3.3 scored row: pre-FY mode → included in Phase 5. 🟢 strong (with acquisition caveat).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS net +13.2% over full period (48.5p → 54.9p). Step-up Sep 25 (+6.7p). Then modest drift upward.
  • 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (54.6p → 54.9p)
  • Revenue: £139.5m → £149.0m (+6.8%)
  • Divergence: Price fell from £10.37 to £7.10 (−31.5%) despite EPS +13.2% — massive de-rating. Market pricing in strategic/acquisition risk, possible contingent consideration liabilities, or general small-cap de-rating. Price/earnings divergence significant.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS net debt = £24.1m at 31 Dec 2025. Sharescope FY1fc net borrowing = £25.0m (net debt). Variance = £0.9m — essentially in-line. ND/EBITDA actual = £24.1m / £44.3m EBITDA = 0.54x vs Sharescope fc 0.60x — marginally better. No material variance.

  • Net debt/(cash): FY22 −£5.4m → FY23 −£9.9m → FY24 £2.0m (slight net debt) → FY24 H1 −£14.8m → FY24 H2 +£14.7m → FY25 H1 £11.3m → FY25 year-end £24.1m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY25 0.54x actual → FY26e 0.60x fc
  • Interest cover: FY25: 25.2x → FY26e: 18.4x (declining as debt rises)
  • ND/FCF: 0.8x FY25, 1.0x FY26

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — ND/EBITDA 0.54x, interest cover >25x. Declining slowly. Not a constraint. Phase 5 silent.

Forecast year earnings check:

  • Step 1: FY25 actual EPS 58.7p vs FY24 43.1p → ✅✅ growing +36.2%. Revenue £149.6m vs £85.9m → ✅✅ growing +74.2%.
  • Step 2: FY26e EPS 64.9p (stale — will upgrade massively) > FY25 58.7p → ✅ growing. Revenue £185.6m > £149.6m → ✅✅ growing.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • TRC full year in FY26: TRC acquired Sep 2025. FY26 gets full year. Pro-forma FY25 if TRC full year: revenue £168.8m, PBT £36.5m. This is a massive annualisation uplift.
  • Kvadrant acquisition (Jan 2026): Post-period, full year contribution in FY26. Revenue £6.2m FY25. Small but additive.
  • Contingent consideration overhang: TRC total contingent consideration up to £47.8m (max), £39.4m recognised. Up to £26.4m payable over FY26–28 in cash or shares. This dilution/cash overhang is a key market concern.
  • AI consulting demand: "AI-related revenue up >260% YoY" — fastest growing segment. Structural tailwind well aligned with ELIX's model.
  • Main Market: Listed Jul 2025 — FTSE 250 inclusion ambition with 50m shares now in issue.
  • Share-based payments stepped up: £5.0m FY25 vs £2.6m FY24. Option repricing £6.45 (20 Mar 2026) for 4.4m options — incremental SBP charge in FY26.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — FY25 EPS beat +6.9% vs consensus: Adj diluted EPS 58.7p vs 54.9p consensus = +3.8p beat. This is the primary catalyst. The number is clean — organic EPS growth of 36% YoY. Revenue +34%. Margin expanding +1.6pp. All quality metrics beat.

#2 Driver — FY26e massive stale consensus uplift (TRC annualisation): Stale FY26e EPS 64.9p does not capture TRC full year impact. EPS bridge implies ~80–83p. Brokers will significantly upgrade FY26e — potentially +20–30%+. This is the largest numeric revision in this batch.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue (FY25 actual): Confirmed £149.6m vs £149.0m. Minor +0.4%.
  • FY1 EPS (FY25 actual): Confirmed 58.7p vs 54.9p consensus. +6.9% beat.
  • FY2 Revenue (FY26e): Major upgrade. TRC full year + Kvadrant + organic. Stale £185.6m → likely £200–220m (+8–18%).
  • FY2 EPS (FY26e): Major upgrade from stale 64.9p to ~78–85p (+20–31%). This is the key broker action.
  • Target price: Current consensus TP £11.20 (Sharescope). Current share price 710p — already significant discount to TP. Post-upgrade cycle, TP likely moves to £9.50–11.50 range (upgrading EPS but widening acquisition premium / contingent consideration concerns). Price could re-rate toward £8–9.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Record Q1 revenue" for FY26 is a conservative but positive signal. No specific number, but sets expectation that organic growth continues. Moderate upgrade cycle driver.

Key risk: Contingent consideration liability (£39.4m recognised, max £47.8m for TRC alone) creates ongoing dilution/cash drain risk over FY26–28. Option repricing (4.4m options at £6.45) adds incremental SBP charge FY26. Share count creep. The massive FX headwind in FY25 (GBP strengthened 4.1¢) will be a FY26 neutral but reduces absolute FX sensitivity.

Net FY1 EPS revision: upgrade (+6.9% on FY25 actual; FY26e major upgrade). Consistency check: Tone Constructive or Strongly positive. FY25 beat is solid; FY26e upgrade magnitude is large. But "Constructive" is appropriate given qualitative FY26 guidance and contingent consideration overhang. ✅

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

(Not Strongly positive — the FY26e upgrade will be large in absolute terms but the market is already de-rated, contingent consideration is a drag, and FY26 guidance is qualitative only. The broker upgrade cycle is clear but not "trigger-happy" as with an explicit numerical beat-and-raise.)

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

ELIX · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

72/100 − 5 (FX) = 67/100 · Confidence: 62–72 · FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · 63% USD · 🟡 neutral rate · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

Net raw: ~77, minus FX −5 = 72. Adjusted to 67 reflecting FX penalty application and contingent consideration drag.

Final: 67/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The FY25 results deliver a clean earnings beat: adjusted diluted EPS of 58.7p exceeds the pre-RNS consensus of 54.9p by +3.8p (+6.9%). Revenue of £149.6m (+34% YoY) beats £149.0m consensus marginally; the quality is in the earnings line — EBITDA of £44.3m (+42% YoY, +2.3% vs Sharescope fc) and margin expansion of +1.6pp to 29.6% demonstrate operating leverage. The most significant forward signal is AI-related revenue up >260% YoY and TRC performing ahead of acquisition case — establishing the platform for a large FY26e upgrade.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode. H2 FY25 revenue of £78.2m represents +76.5% YoY versus FY24's £44.3m, substantially acquisition-enhanced (TRC from Sep 2025). The H1 seasonality at 47.7% of FY total was almost exactly in-line with the 47.5% 3-year average. The key upgrade catalyst is not the FY25 result but the FY26e stale consensus: at 64.9p, it fails to capture TRC's full-year annualisation (~+13p on EPS bridge), Kvadrant's contribution (~+3–4p), and organic growth at maintained margin. The EPS bridge points to ~80–83p FY26e, representing a +20–30% upgrade that brokers must now execute. The only meaningful downside risk is GBP/USD remaining elevated into FY26, which limits the USD revenue translation benefit — but current spot is approximately neutral vs FY25 average.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 actual EPS confirmed at 58.7p (+6.9% vs consensus). FY26e revenue will be upgraded from £185.6m to approximately £200–220m (+8–18%). FY26e EPS will be upgraded from the stale 64.9p to ~78–85p (+20–31%) — the largest percentage EPS revision in this session. Target prices may move toward £9.50–11.50 though the current share price at 710p already trades at a significant discount to the £11.20 consensus TP. The primary constraint is the contingent consideration overhang (TRC up to £47.8m over FY26–28) and incremental SBP charges from option repricing, both of which dilute the shareholder return from otherwise strong earnings growth.

🏁 ELIX delivers a clean FY25 EPS beat and triggers one of the largest FY26e consensus upgrades in this batch as TRC's full-year annualisation is properly modelled — but the de-rated share price and contingent consideration overhang limit the upgrade cycle's clean expression. Score: 67/100.

The leverage profile (ND/EBITDA 3.1x, interest cover 3.5x) creates significant non-linear EPS risk — any H2 EBITDA shortfall flows through to EPS at a multiplied rate.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will hold estimates flat — FY26 EPS at 63.7p, FY27 at 72.3p, Revenue at £5,564m. The reiteration of guidance prevents the feared downgrade (the 4-week FALLING consensus trend suggested market anxiety about a cut) but does not provide the catalyst for upgrades. Target prices remain near the existing 986p consensus — the 84% discount to TP is a valuation story driven by regulatory risk, HMRC litigation, and leverage that this RNS does not address. The watch point is H1 FY26 results: if sports margins normalise in Q2 and CEE begins recovering from the Croatia-heavy Q1, the H1 print could re-establish the upgrade cycle. For now, ENT is a hold-and-watch — the UK&I momentum is genuine but not sufficient to overcome the leverage discount and CEE drag.

🏁 In-line guidance reiterated; prevents feared downgrade but no upgrade catalyst; UK&I and AUS strength offset by CEE weakness and BetMGM soft guidance; leverage at 3.1x ND/EBITDA keeps EPS risk elevated; neutral verdict.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining fact of this H1 FY26 report is not the financials but the context: a recommended cash offer at 17p per share from founder Mark Furness, with an unconditional deadline of 8 May 2026. The share price at 16.65p represents a 2% discount to the offer — the market is pricing a small probability of lapse. Against that backdrop, the H1 results show revenue declining −25% to £7.8m (−23% constant currency), with Run Rate ARR falling −24% to £12.7m. The primary driver is the continued downsizing of a single large North American strategic customer plus the loss of a large UK client at December 2025 contract expiry. The adjusted EBITDA remained barely positive at £0.1m (vs £0.8m H1 FY25) — a testament to aggressive cost management but also a signal of how thin the financial cushion is.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the H1 tracking signal is the focus — but without FY1 consensus (no brokers covering), both revenue and EPS are UNTRACKABLE. The going concern disclosure is the dominant signal: directors have explicitly stated there are "material uncertainties which may cast significant doubt over the Group's ability to continue as a going concern." Cash at £0.9m, post-period outflows continuing, no debt facility secured, CFO departing end of April — the standalone operational trajectory is towards insolvency. The upgrade resilience is nil in the fundamental sense; the only resilience factor is the takeover offer. If the offer lapses, emergency equity or debt funding would be required within weeks. The gross margin improvement to 63% (from 59%) is a genuine structural positive from the Cloud product wind-down, but this matters only if the company survives as an independent entity.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: There are no meaningful broker revisions to model — coverage has been effectively suspended given the takeover. The sole relevant trading event is the 8 May 2026 unconditional deadline. If the offer becomes unconditional, shareholders receive 17p and the analysis ends. If the offer lapses, the company faces an acute cash crisis and the stock would likely collapse well below current levels. No TP assessment is appropriate. For the record: the standalone fundamental implies revenue continuing to contract toward £14–16m for FY26, EBITDA approaching zero in H2, and a capital raise requirement within 6–12 months.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Everplay (formerly Team17): EU revenue £135.7m of £166.0m total = 81.7% combined (EU + other). However, breaking down by single currency: the company operates primarily in USD and EUR through Steam/platform sales. No single currency exposure >30% is clearly identifiable from the RNS — the company reports in GBP and the major platform revenue streams (Steam ~30%, Sony ~16%, Nintendo ~11%, Apple ~14%) are in USD/EUR/GBP. Given the company reports revenues net in GBP without a Currency Movements section and does not have a single non-GBP revenue stream >30% from one currency per jurisdiction, applying the threshold test: USD from Steam/Apple/gaming platforms likely >30% in aggregate. However the penalty applies to individual named non-GBP currencies, and games companies like Everplay receive mixed-currency platform payments. Without explicit disclosure, I'll check if the RNS addresses this.

The RNS notes: "total other comprehensive income: Exchange Gain on translation of foreign operations £6,041,000" — a positive FX translation gain for FY25, suggesting GBP weakened vs EUR/USD in FY25 overall (astragon Germany contributes EUR). No Currency Movements section explicitly breaking out single currency >30%. Given Everplay has astragon Germany (EUR ~17% of revenue) and Team17 USD revenues (~unknown split), applying conservative judgment: no single named non-GBP currency is clearly >30% from the RNS data available. EWG — W.A.G Payment Solutions PLC (Eurowag)

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Eurowag reports in EUR (€). The Sharescope consensus revenue figure is in EUR (€327.5m FY1). Revenue is pan-European with CZK, PLN, EUR, RON exposure. The company's functional currency is EUR. GBP-listed but EUR-reporting. From the RNS: net revenue €330.1m; no formal GBP Currency Movements section exists as the company reports entirely in EUR. The Sharescope EPS data is in pence (5.8p), implying a GBP/EUR translation into pence — the primary FX sensitivity is GBP/EUR for UK investors, but this is a translation effect, not a revenue exposure in the traditional sense.

No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% in the traditional sense applicable to GBP-reporting companies. Phase 0B not applicable (EUR-reporting company). No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 5.8p · Revenue €327.5m (net revenue basis)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 7.1p · Revenue €362.2m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over snapshot: 6.2p → 5.8p = −0.4p (−6.5%). Direction negative: 6.2p (Sept 2025) → 6.0p (Nov) → 5.9p (Jan) → 5.8p (Feb). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 5.8p / £327.5m for 6 weeks). Revenue: £325.8m → £327.5m (+0.5%) — essentially flat.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.7% of FY = €162.7m · EPS 46.8% of FY = 2.7p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue €1,149.7m (gross; net not split) · EPS 2.5p. Note: Sharescope revenue data for EWG appears to show gross revenue (€1,149.7m H1 vs €327.5m FY net consensus) — the H1 split data is on a gross/net mixed basis. Using the net revenue basis from the RNS: FY25 net revenue = €330.1m; H1/H2 split not disclosed in this annual RNS.
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Insufficient clean H1/H2 net revenue split available from Sharescope data (gross/net mismatch). EPS: FY1 consensus 5.8p − H1 actual 2.9p = implied H2 2.9p vs prior H2 2.1p → +38.1% YoY — H2 must deliver material step-up vs H1.
  • FX: N/A — EUR-reporting company, Phase 0B methodology not applicable.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Net Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 net revenue: €330.1m, up 12.9% vs €292.5m in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of €327.5m: beat of €2.6m (+0.8%) — small beat, in line.

Payment solutions net revenue: €200.4m (+20.1%). Mobility solutions: €129.7m (+3.3%).

"Total net revenue increased +12.9% to €330.1 million (FY 2024: €292.5 million)."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Adjusted basic EPS: 4.83 cents per share (GBP pence equivalent ~3.6p at 1.35 EUR/GBP).

Basic statutory EPS: 0.30 cents.

vs FY1 consensus of 5.8p: The adjusted EPS of 4.83c = ~3.6p at current rates — a miss of ~−2.2p (−38%) vs Sharescope consensus. However, this requires careful reconciliation.

EPS quality check / Critical issue: The Sharescope EPS consensus of 5.8p is in pence. Eurowag's adjusted EPS is reported in euro cents (4.83 cents). At GBP/EUR of ~1.20 (implied by consensus translation), 4.83c = ~4.0p. At spot GBP/EUR of 1.17 (from RNS exchange note context): 4.83c / 1.17 = ~4.13p. Either way, the 4.83c adjusted EPS translates to approximately 4.0–4.2p vs Sharescope consensus 5.8p.

This appears to be a significant miss. However: (a) Sharescope consensus may have embedded a different GBP/EUR assumption, (b) the company distinguishes adjusted EPS (4.83c) from statutory (0.30c) — the windfall tax (€5.3m) is the key driver of the statutory miss. On adjusted basis at 4.83c this appears below the pre-RNS pence consensus. 🚨 Windfall tax €5.3m is one-off (Czech Republic, applicable 2023–2025 only) and excluded from adjusted EPS. However, adjusted effective tax rate is 34.8% vs prior 30.3% — high ongoing tax burden even ex-windfall. Restated adjusted EPS at 30.3% normalised rate: adjusted PBT €51.4m × (1−30.3%) = €35.8m ÷ 691.4m shares = 5.18c = ~3.8–4.3p in GBP pence. Still below the 5.8p consensus. The miss vs consensus appears genuine on an FX-adjusted basis.

3. Adjusted EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA: €132.1m (+8.5% vs €121.7m). Margin: 40.0% (2024: 41.6%), -1.6pp — margin declined due to higher employee expenses (+19.3% adjusted). Cash EBITDA: €98.0m (+10.5%).

"Adjusted EBITDA increased +8.5% to €132.1 million (FY 2024: €121.7 million), with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 40.0% (FY 2024: 41.6%)."

4. Net debt / deleveraging

Net debt reduced to €216.2m (2024: €275.5m). Net leverage: 1.9x (2024: 2.3x) — now within target 1.5–2.5x range. Significant balance sheet improvement.

"Net leverage at 1.9x (FY 2024: 2.3x)."

5. FY26 guidance

Low double-digit net revenue growth (consistent with recent trajectory). Adjusted EBITDA margin ~40%. Adjusted cash EBITDA €105–115m (2025: €98m, +7.1–17.3%). Capex below €50m cap. Leverage <2.0x. Second special dividend of 1.5p per share (~€12m) pending AGM.

"We remain confident in our ability to deliver in line with market expectations for FY 2026."

6. Eurowag Office platform

35% of customers now actively using platform. Majority of customers to be migrated by end-2026. NPS improved to 43.8 (2024: 40.0). Total active trucks +6.4% to 321,500.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "remain confident in our ability to deliver in line with market expectations for FY 2026" — explicit in-line language. Numeric: cash EBITDA €105–115m range. Covers one year. No upgrade language.
  • The FY25 results show EBITDA growth of 8.5% with margin -1.6pp; guidance for FY26 is in-line with market expectations — no upgrade trigger.
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — management explicitly guides in-line with expectations; cash EBITDA range of €105–115m is quantified but as a range consistent with consensus. Provisional points: +1.
  • Divergence check: FY25 net revenue +0.8% beat, adjusted EPS apparent miss vs GBP consensus. Outlook in-line. The apparent EPS miss + in-line outlook = consistent (both suggest limited near-term upgrade catalyst). No material divergence beyond FX translation complexity.

[Employee cost escalation — structural margin headwind]: Adjusted employee expenses +19.3% to €110.1m. This was the primary reason EBITDA margin fell 1.6pp despite 12.9% revenue growth. New Super LTIP approved Sep 2025 — ongoing SBC headwind. This is a structural cost item, not one-off.

The reconciling factor is that the consensus 5.8p likely embedded a more favourable EUR/GBP assumption and/or different tax rate assumptions. The RNS net revenue beat of €330.1m vs €327.5m consensus (+0.8%) is clean and positive, and Adjusted EBITDA of €132.1m (+8.5%) is in line. The #1 broker note catalyst is the windfall tax: €5.3m non-recurring charge (Czech Republic, final year of a 2023–2025 temporary tax) that depresses both statutory EPS and the adjusted effective tax rate in FY25 — but crucially, this headwind disappears entirely in FY26.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 EPS tracking signal of +3.2pp (Strong Buy) was contradicted by the FY outcome on a pence basis — primarily due to FX translation and the windfall tax hitting H2. The structural story is intact: net leverage of 1.9x is now within the 1.5–2.5x target, Toll revenues grew +52.3%, and 35% of customers are actively using Eurowag Office with majority migration targeted by end-2026. The bear case for major downgrades is limited by the windfall tax reversal (mechanical FY26 EPS uplift of ~0.6p) and the low-double-digit net revenue growth guidance. The structural risk is employee cost escalation — adjusted employee expenses grew +19.3% to €110.1m, contributing to the 1.6pp EBITDA margin compression. If this pace continues in FY26, the margin compression story extends despite revenue growth.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades to 6.2–6.6p (+7–14%) from 5.8p are likely, driven primarily by the windfall tax reversal and in-line revenue growth. Revenue in line with low-double-digit guidance (~€362m). TP from 127p to 130–140p, implying 27–37% upside from 102p. The Capital Markets Day (AGM in May 2026) will be the next catalyst — new monetisation data from the Eurowag Office platform will be the key variable. 🏁 Constructive: in-line operational delivery, balance sheet fixed, windfall tax reversal provides FY26 EPS uplift; employee cost inflation and FX translation create EPS quality concerns that will limit upgrade enthusiasm. Score 52/100.

Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (Q4). RNS = H1 Results for six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26). Eagle Eye year-end is 30 June. No FX rule triggered — GBP-denominated revenues.

  • FY1 cns: EPS 2.6p, Revenue £45.0m (FY26, updated after Jan 2026 trading update upgrade). FY2: EPS 8.9p, Rev £51.9m (FY27).
  • Momentum: EPS −85% over period (17.3p → 2.6p) — dominated by Sep 2025 NRS cut, then partial recovery. Revenue −5.7% (47.7m → 45.0m). Last-4-week FALLING. Stock: 900p → 400p (Jun 2025) → 530p (Feb 2026 post Jan upgrade).

  • H1 tracking (Revenue): £23.0m / £45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% → +2.9pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL. H2 burden reduced by ~£1.3m vs baseline expectation.

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

H1 Results — Six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26)

  1. H1 Revenue (inc NRS): £23.0m vs H1 FY25 £24.2m = −5%. Ex-NRS: £22.4m vs £19.3m = +16%. H1 tracking: £23.0m/£45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% = +2.9pp.

  5. FY27 guidance: "return to double digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27." Exit FY26 with 20% EBITDA margin run rate.
    "The Board continues to expect to exit FY26 with a 20% EBITDA margin run rate, and is confident that the momentum being achieved across the business will support a return to double digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27"
  6. US momentum: 4 wins, £2.5m new ARR in H1 FY26 — key validation of strategic expansion.
    "The US contributed £2.5m in new ARR in H1 2026, thanks to four significant wins"
  7. OEM: First 2 contracts secured — blue-chip European retailers. Estimated ARR c.£2.0m. Revenue-generating from FY27.

  8. Recurring revenue 85% (H1 FY25: 81%). NRR ex-NRS = 108% (H1 FY25: 104%). EagleAI +23% to £3.6m.

  • H1 Revenue tracking: £23.0m / £45.0m = 51.1% vs 3yr avg 48.2% = +2.9pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL. H2 burden slightly reduced — implied H2 = £22.0m vs prior H2 £24.0m (NRS loss explains decline, not organic deterioration).
  • Revenue YoY: FY24 +35.6% → FY25 +0.1% (NRS distorted) → FY26E ~0% (NRS distorted). Ex-NRS H1 FY26 +16% showing underlying recovery. Classification: Recovering from NRS disruption.
  • Structural — OEM + US: These are the FY27 catalysts. First OEM contracts signed; US ARR £2.5m in H1 alone.
  • H2 EBITDA burden: H1 adj EBITDA £4.3m. For 20% exit run-rate, H2 must deliver ~£4–5m. H2 is traditionally stronger for EYE. The pattern is achievable but requires execution.

Baseline+50

Eagle Eye delivered a strong H1 FY26, with H1 revenue tracking +2.9pp above the seasonal norm (£23.0m = 51.1% of FY1 consensus vs 3yr avg 48.2%), triggering a 🟢 Mild Buy Signal. The headline is ARR growth: underlying ARR +29% ex-NRS to £42.2m, with H1 new ARR exceeding the entirety of FY25 — a powerful leading indicator. Adj EBITDA of £4.3m at an 18% margin came in ahead of Board expectations, and the 20% FY26 exit run-rate remains on track. US momentum (4 wins, £2.5m ARR) and the OEM first contracts (c.£2.0m estimated ARR) provide clear FY27 growth catalysts.

FY26 full-year guidance is confirmed in-line with the recently upgraded consensus — this is a confirmation, not an upgrade. The FY1 EPS upgrade cycle is effectively complete at 2.6p. The score is driven by FY27 upgrade potential: brokers are expected to raise FY27 EPS from 8.9p towards 10–12p and revenue from £51.9m to £54–57m, based on the OEM ramp, NRS-free comparators, and the management guide of double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27.

The primary constraint on a higher score is that FY26 EPS (2.6p) is extremely low in absolute terms, making near-term institutional EPS upgrades immaterial. The re-rating is a FY27 story. Watch points: H2 EBITDA delivery (implied H2 = £22m revenue vs H1 £23m — NRS effect), first OEM revenue recognition timing, and US win pipeline conversion in H2.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The RNS discloses constant-currency revenue of −30% vs reported −31%. The difference is 1pp, which is within the 0.5pp threshold... actually 1pp exceeds the 0.5pp constant-currency override threshold. Let me assess properly.

Constant currency revenue decline: −30% vs reported −31%. Difference = 1pp. This exceeds the 0.5pp override threshold, so the override does not fire.

Geographic revenue split: UK £88.4m (49.7%), North America £45.8m (25.8%), APAC £28.5m (16.0%), EMEA £15.0m (8.4%). North America USD/CAD exposure = ~25.8% of revenue. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B: no penalty applies. Proceed to Phase 1.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 9.7p · Revenue £176.5m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 9.2p · Revenue £162.6m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period: 16.0p → 9.7p = −6.3p, −39.4%. Heavy downgrades concentrated in Jul–Aug 2025 (16.0p → 9.7p in one step). Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (price 289p → 273p; EPS flat at 9.7p but revenue oscillated 178→176.5m, slight downward drift). Revenue net change: £207.6m → £176.5m = −14.9%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 51.5% of FY = £90.9m · EPS 49.7% of FY = 4.8p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £140.2m · EPS 11.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY actual £177.7m − H1 actual £97.3m = H2 £80.4m vs prior-year H2 £117.5m → Revenue H2 YoY: −31.6%. FY actual EPS 10.0p − H1 actual 6.3p = H2 4.7p (cross-check below in Phase 3) vs prior-year H2 11.3p → EPS H2 YoY: −58.4%. Note: FY1 consensus EPS was 9.7p; actual delivered 10.0p — RNS-derived figures used throughout.
  • FX: No single currency >30% exposure. Phase 0B not triggered. N/A.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Preliminary Results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue figures FY 2025 actual: £177.7m, down 31% YoY (2024: £257.7m). Constant currency basis: −30%. vs FY1 consensus £176.5m: beat of +£1.2m / +0.7% — effectively in line.

2. EPS / earnings figures Adjusted basic EPS FY 2025: 10.0p (2024: 23.0p, −57%). vs FY1 consensus 9.7p: beat of +0.3p / +3.1%. Basic EPS: 5.2p (2024: 18.8p). Adjusted PBT: £13.7m (2024: £34.0m, −60%). Reported PBT: £7.6m.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 25.8% vs UK standard rate 25.0% — deviation of 0.8pp, well within the 3pp threshold. No tax distortion. Adjusted EPS excludes: share plan expense £0.2m, exceptional costs £2.6m, EMEA goodwill and asset impairment charge £3.3m. The impairment is non-recurring; the adjusted figure is the appropriate basis. No restatement required.

"Adjusted basic earnings per share was down 57%, to 10.0 pence (2024: 23.0 pence)."

3. Order book / forward work No order book or forward work coverage metric disclosed. Consultant headcount at year-end: 2,003 (2024: 2,578, −22%). scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 Results for the six months ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Fonix is described as a "UK focused mobile payments and messaging company." Revenue is overwhelmingly GBP-denominated with some EUR (Ireland, Portugal). No Currency Movements section present in the RNS; no single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. FX Rule 1 does not apply. No penalty.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 11.2p, Revenue £80.3m. FY2: EPS 12.1p, Revenue £85.9m.
  • Consensus net change: EPS +4.7% (10.7p → 11.2p) over full period, with three modest step-upgrades. Revenue broadly flat (some mid-period dip to £74.5m then recovered to £80.3m). Last-4-week EPS trend: FLAT. Momentum: stalling.
  • 3yr avg H1 % of FY: Revenue 52.0% (3yr avg); EPS 53.9% (2yr avg from Sharescope).
  • H1 actuals from RNS: Revenue £42.3m; Adjusted EPS 6.2p; Adjusted PBT £8.0m; Adj EBITDA £8.3m.
  • H1 tracking: Revenue 52.7% of FY1 cns vs 52.0% avg = +0.7pp (IN LINE). EPS 55.4% of FY1 cns vs 53.9% avg = +1.5pp (MILD BUY threshold).
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: H1 Results (six months ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue H1: £42.3m (+9.1% YoY from £38.8m). vs FY1 cns implied H1 (52.0% × £80.3m = £41.8m): +1.2% beat.
    "Revenue for the period grew by 9% to £42.3m (H1 FY25: £38.8m)"
  2. Gross profit H1: £10.5m (+7.1% YoY from £9.8m). GP margin 24.9% vs 25.2% prior — marginal compression. Growth driven by mobile payments +6%, messaging +20%, managed services +1%. UK +6%, rest of Europe +24% (Ireland + Portugal).
    "Gross profit for the period increased to £10.5m (H1 FY25: £9.8m) growing 7.1% on the previous period."
  3. Adjusted EPS H1: 6.2p — flat YoY (H1 FY25: 6.2p). H1 tracking = 6.2p / 11.2p = 55.4% vs 2yr avg 53.9% = +1.5pp ahead of seasonal norm. Implied H2 EPS = 11.2p – 6.2p = 5.0p vs prior H2 5.1p = –2% YoY.
    "Adjusted EPS 6.2p (H1 FY25: 6.2p) +0.0%"
  4. Adjusted EBITDA: £8.3m (+6.4% from £7.8m). Adjusted PBT £8.0m (+2.6% from £7.8m). Margin compression from lower interest income, higher amortisation, and rising effective tax rate. Operating costs +16% to £2.27m.
    "adjusted earnings per share rose only marginally, reflecting lower interest income, higher amortisation associated with increased capitalised software investment over the past three years and a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate."
  5. FY guidance: "in line with market expectations" — explicit confirmation. No upgrade language. Full year guidance reiterated.
    "The Board remains confident in the Group's strategy and its ability to deliver sustainable gross profit growth and long-term value for shareholders in line with market expectations."
  6. International expansion: Portugal live (second European market, launched Sept 2025, gaining traction). Third European market: pilot live with major broadcaster since end-February 2026. Fourth European market: legal entity established, first hire made, operator contracts and regulatory approvals progressing; launch targeted FY27. ITV contract extended — entering 10th year.
    "Fonix enters the second half of FY26 with continued positive momentum across its core UK and Ireland markets and encouraging progress internationally."
  7. Product innovation: PayFlex now live with first Irish broadcaster and two UK broadcaster deployments — contributing to gross profit growth. CompsPortal first customer launched December 2025. RCS (RichMessaging): second successful pilot; broader expanded trial underway. PayFlex expected to increase customers' transaction volumes by up to 2–3% in the medium term.
    "PayFlex is now live with our first Irish broadcaster, alongside two existing UK broadcaster deployments."
  8. Dividend: 3.1p interim (+6.9% from 2.9p). Progressive policy: ≥75% of adjusted EPS paid out. Payable 2 April 2026.
    "increased interim dividend of 3.1p per share, in line with the Group's progressive dividend policy to pay out at least 75% of adjusted EPS"
  9. Gambling risk: A small number of gaming customers ceased services ahead of UK tax changes in April 2026. Gaming now less than 6% of gross profit. Historically, volumes consolidate among remaining providers.
    "Gambling now represents less than 6% of Group gross profit and we therefore expect the impact to be manageable."
  10. Underlying cash: £9.2m (–16.4% from £11.0m), primarily reflecting additional shareholder distributions including a £3m special dividend paid in H2 FY25.
    "Underlying cash decreased to £9.2m (H1 FY25: £11.0m), primarily reflecting additional shareholder distributions in the current period, together with a £3m special dividend paid in H2 FY25."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue HoH trajectory: 3yr ago H1 £28.6m → 2yr ago H1 £32.8m (+14.7%) → 1yr ago H1 £39.7m (+21.0%) → current H1 £42.3m (+6.5%). FY YoY: 2yr ago £64.9m → 1yr ago £76.1m (+17.3%) → FY1 cns £80.3m (+5.5%). Classification: Decelerating — clear reduction in growth rate over three years.
  • EPS HoH trajectory: 2yr ago H1 4.9p → 1yr ago H1 5.7p (+16.3%) → current H1 6.2p (+8.8%). FY EPS: 2yr ago ~8.9p → 1yr ago ~10.8p (+21.3%) → FY1 cns 11.2p (+3.7%). H2 EPS historically volatile (3yr ago H2 was negative). Classification: Decelerating for EPS growth rate; opex investment constraining EPS leverage relative to gross profit.
  • H1 Tracking vs Seasonal Norm (pre-H1 mode): Revenue: H1 £42.3m / FY1 cns £80.3m = 52.7% vs 3yr avg 52.0% = +0.7pp → 🟡 IN LINE. No material deviation. EPS: 6.2p / 11.2p = 55.4% vs 2yr avg 53.9% = +1.5pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL — H1 tracking at upper edge of seasonal norm. H2 EPS burden = 5.0p / 11.2p = 44.6% of FY1 cns (within normal range). Buy triggers: H1 Rev > £42.3m (just met at £42.3m). H1 EPS > 6.1p (met at 6.2p).
  • H2 implied momentum: Revenue H2 required = £80.3m – £42.3m = £38.0m vs prior H2 £34.0m = +11.8% YoY (achievable given 9% revenue run-rate). EPS H2 implied = 5.0p vs prior H2 5.1p = –2.0% (slight weakness — opex drag). H2 revenue momentum: Moderate. H2 EPS momentum: Flat/weak.
  • Forecast momentum overlay: EPS net change +4.7% full period; 3 discrete step-upgrades (10.7 → 10.9 → 11.1 → 11.2p). Last 4 weeks: FLAT. Revenue was volatile mid-period (dipped to £74.5m in July-August) before recovering to £80.3m. No divergence between price (static at 297p throughout) and forecasts — suggests market already fully prices the consensus.
  • Structural flags: (1) International expansion creates medium-term revenue optionality (4 markets, FY27+ contribution). (2) PayFlex expected to add 2–3% transaction volume medium-term. (3) Opex investment rising faster than gross profit (+16% costs vs +7.1% GP) — structural margin headwind until international scale achieved. (4) ITV contract renewal provides 10-year relationship visibility. (5) EPS growth rate diluted by lower interest income and higher capitalised software amortisation.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — FY guidance "in line with market expectations": Cavendish (house broker) will lead with the explicit FY confirmation as the primary headline. This provides the strongest reassurance — brokers will not need to cut. The in-line guidance combined with H1 delivery at seasonal norm removes downside risk for FY26.
2#2 Driver — Gross profit growth +7.1% with international optionality: The volume momentum across all service lines (+6% payments, +20% messaging), Portugal traction, third market pilot, and fourth market investment collectively strengthen the medium-term revenue trajectory. Brokers will highlight the international pipeline as an unquantified but real source of future upgrades.
3Forecast revision FY1/FY2: Revenue FY1: HOLD with small potential +0–1% revision (H1 run-rate slightly above seasonal norm). EPS FY1: HOLD at 11.2p — EPS structural constraints (lower interest, higher amortisation, rising effective tax) prevent meaningful upgrade despite GP growth. FY2: HOLD at 12.1p; international optionality real but not yet quantifiable. Target price: likely reiterated at 297p (= current close price, implying zero market upside priced in — odd but consistent with the flat price action throughout the year).
4"In line" guidance read-through: This is a direct confirmation rather than conservative colouring. Unlike "not less than" language, it provides no upgrade optionality. Brokers will treat FY as confirmed at consensus and move focus to FY27/beyond. The four-market international pipeline is the medium-term catalyst narrative.
5Key risk — EPS leverage failure: The flat 6.2p H1 EPS despite 7.1% GP growth is the main concern. Gross profit grew by £0.7m but adjusted EPS was flat — implying the margin benefit was entirely absorbed by higher opex, lower interest income and rising tax. Brokers will flag this as a structural constraint: Fonix is investing heavily in international expansion and product development, which is the right strategy but depresses near-term EPS leverage. "adjusted earnings per share rose only marginally, reflecting lower interest income, higher amortisation...and a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate."
6Overall broker-note tone: Neutral / hold and wait. Cavendish will issue a brief confirmatory note reiterating buy recommendation and 297p target price, noting the strong GP growth, in-line FY confirmation, and international progress as medium-term catalysts. No upgrades to forecasts expected. Tone: constructive but not exciting. The flat EPS and guidance confirmation at consensus provide no near-term positive revision catalyst.
Neutral · Hold and Wait
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
56
/100
Confidence range: 52–60 · No FX penalty
EPS H1 tracking +1.5pp (mild buy signal)+4
Gross profit growth +7.1% (solid)+3
EPS consensus momentum +4.7%+2
International expansion optionality+2
EPS flat YoY; structural margin drag–4
Gambling headwind / gaming tax–1
Base midpoint (in-line guidance)+50

Fonix delivered a solid H1 with gross profit growth of +7.1% and revenue of £42.3m (+9.1% YoY), tracking modestly above the seasonal norm on both revenue (+0.7pp) and EPS (+1.5pp). The Board confirmed delivery "in line with market expectations" for the full year, removing downside risk. The EPS H1 tracking of 55.4% vs 53.9% historical average achieves the mild buy signal threshold, reducing H2 burden to 44.6% of FY1 consensus.

The structural constraint on the score is the flat adjusted EPS of 6.2p (unchanged YoY) despite 7.1% gross profit growth — the margin of that growth was entirely absorbed by rising opex investment (+16%), lower interest income, higher software amortisation and an increased effective tax rate. This pattern indicates the company is in an investment phase: international expansion across four European markets and new product rollouts (PayFlex, CompsPortal, RCS) are consuming earnings near-term for medium-term growth.

Broker reaction will be limited to a confirmatory note from Cavendish reiterating the buy at 297p. With the stock already at 297p (the consensus TP), there is no near-term price catalyst beyond FY guidance confirmation. The upgrade catalyst will come from FY27 estimates incorporating international revenue at scale — not from this RNS. Score of 56 reflects modest/mixed impact with a hold-and-wait stance from brokers.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

FOXT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 Trading Update, 3 months ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue figures

Q1 2026 Group revenue: £39.6m (Q1 2025: £44.1m), −10% YoY.

By segment: Lettings £26.4m (+5%); Sales £10.7m (−35%); Financial Services £2.6m (+3%).

No full-year numeric guidance stated. The RNS states "full year guidance remains unchanged." This is qualitative only — no quantification of the unchanged guidance figure.

Q1 2025 had an exceptionally strong comparator from elevated stamp duty deadline volumes. Vs Q1 2024 (normalised): like-for-like Sales revenue +£0.2m above Q1 2024's £9.5m — LFL basis effectively flat.

"The Group is trading in line with previous expectations and full year guidance remains unchanged."

"Sales revenue declined by 35% to £10.7m (Q1 2025: £16.4m), reflecting an exceptionally strong prior-year comparator that benefited from elevated transaction volumes ahead of the 31 March 2025 stamp duty deadline."

2. EPS / earnings figures

No Q1 EPS disclosed (trading update only). No H1 EPS figures. Annual EPS guidance not provided. FY guidance "unchanged" but no numeric EPS guide restated.

FY26e EPS bridge (construct here):

  • (1) New base EPS actual (FY25): Sharescope shows FY25 EPS as current H1 2.7p + H2 2.2p = 4.9p (or FY actual). FY1 fc 5.0p implies a +0.1p step-up from 4.9p actual — a very modest upgrade in consensus already baked in.
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Two acquisitions completed in Q1 2026 (Milton Keynes and Birmingham lettings businesses). No revenue quantum disclosed for these acquisitions individually. However, RNS states Q1 Lettings acquisition contribution = £0.9m of the £1.2m Lettings YoY increase. Annualising Q1 £0.9m acquisition contribution × 4 quarters ≈ £3.6m incremental annualised revenue. At Foxtons' Lettings operating margin (~18% EBIT margin on Lettings), this is approximately £0.65m incremental EBIT or ~0.2p EPS annualisation uplift for FY26.

The real broker action is at H1 results (expected May 2026) when actual H1 revenue, profit and net debt will allow a proper EPS bridge rebuild. TP consensus at 77p (80% implied upside at 42.7p) is unlikely to move on this quarter.

🏁 Verdict: in-line Q1 with a known-bad Sales comparator; Lettings holding up; cost action real but H2 burden elevated and acquisition interest cost a latent EPS risk. Score 37 — neutral hold, watch H1 results in May for the definitive signal on whether FY EPS consensus of 5.0p is achievable.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — EBITDA margin guidance 25-27% vs consensus implied ~30%: This is the primary catalyst for downgrades. The EBITDA miss implies £21-36m less EBITDA than consensus, flowing directly to EPS cuts of ~10-15%. Brokers who had modelled the Dec 2025 upgrade cycle (to 134.4p) will need to cut back aggressively.

#2 Driver — H2 organic revenue guided to decline low single digits: No prior guidance had flagged H2 revenue declines. "Low single digit" organic revenue decline in H2 combined with programmatic and ecommerce weakness driven by Google search session losses is a structural negative, not a timing issue. Brokers will debate whether this is a Google-zero transition cost or a permanent impairment.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: Hold/marginal cut — H1 "in line", H2 guided down low single digits. Full year likely £720-740m (consensus £737m roughly correct on revenue, or slight cut)
  • FY1 EPS: Cut −10 to −15% — from 130.5p to approximately 110-117p given EBITDA margin shortfall of 3-5pp vs consensus
  • FY2: Cut −5 to −10% — uncertainty on Google search trajectory; B2B and Go.Compare recovery timing uncertain
  • TP: Cut materially — consensus TP 977p vs current 389.2p (already implying 151% upside was a fantasy). Post-results TPs will fall further.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Future plc's pre-H1 update is net negative — while H1 revenue is "broadly in line with management's expectations," the critical miss is H1 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%, and full-year EBITDA margin guided to 25-27% — implying a £21-36m shortfall vs the £221m consensus EBITDA figure. The #1 broker-relevant metric is the margin guidance: at 25-27% on ~£737m revenue, EBITDA is £185-200m vs £221m consensus, driving EPS cuts of approximately 10-15% from 130.5p to ~110-117p. The proximate cause is Google search session losses that are "more pronounced than anticipated" — lower sessions suppress the highest-margin revenue lines (programmatic advertising and ecommerce), while also inflating PPC costs industry-wide. Revenue is "in line" at H1 but this is partly because SheerLuxe (Google-zero brand) is offsetting programmatic weakness — the mix is structurally worse even if the top-line holds.

Para 2 — H1 momentum and upgrade resilience: H1 tracking is UNTRACKABLE (no explicit H1 revenue or EPS figure disclosed — qualitative language only), so Column 5 renders na. The upgrade resilience is limited and depends on three pivots: (1) Go.Compare returning to growth in H2 (guided, not yet confirmed); (2) B2B new product launches delivering H2 revenue; and (3) Future Optic AI ad product scaling. All three are achievable but unquantified, and none offset the structural Google search headwind which the company has no direct control over. The H2 organic revenue decline guidance of "low single digits" vs prior H2 represents a continuation of the deceleration trend — H2 FY25 was −0.1%, and this guides H2 FY26 to −1 to −3%. Three consecutive years of revenue decline (FY24 −4.5%, FY25 −0.1%, FY26e −6.5%) signal a structural rather than cyclical issue.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and verdict: Brokers will hold FY1 revenue near consensus (~£720-740m, marginal cuts) but cut FY1 EPS by 10-15% to approximately 110-117p as margins disappoint. FY2 consensus of 140.2p EPS faces cuts of 5-10% as Google uncertainty and B2B/Go.Compare recovery timing remain unclear. The consensus TP of 977p is a fiction at current 389.2p — post-results TPs will fall further, though the buyback acceleration (the board explicitly flagging "fundamentally undervalued") provides some technical support. The main watch-point is whether the "Google-Zero" brand strategy (SheerLuxe, and future acquisitions) can scale fast enough to replace programmatic revenue structurally — if not, this is a multi-year margin compression story. 🏁 Verdict: Downgrade cycle accelerating — EBITDA margin miss is the decisive negative; H2 revenue decline guidance confirms the Google headwind is structural; EPS cuts of 10-15% likely with further risk to FY2.

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

The H1 adj EPS of 11.0p already exceeds FY26 EPS consensus — this triggers implicit upgrade-forcing maths even if the company only guides "in line" on AOP.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive for FY26 (in-line AOP guidance but EPS consensus revision forced by H1 actuals) + Upgrade-triggering for FY27 (medium-term targets well ahead of FY27 consensus £90.5m rev / 11.0p EPS vs £120m rev / ~20p+ EPS implied). Divergence check: H1 beat on profitability/EPS; H1 flat on revenue (slight miss vs seasonal baseline). Guidance "in line" on AOP. Divergence: revenue soft vs baseline but EPS crushed it → Mix/margin story is positive divergence. No conflicting signal — margin beat offsets revenue miss.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — H1 adj EPS of 11.0p vs FY26 consensus of 8.3p: This is unambiguously the dominant signal. H1 EPS has already beaten the full-year consensus by 32.5%. Brokers must revise FY26e EPS upward materially — the question is only by how much once H2 seasonality is modelled. At H1 11.0p + expected H2 of approximately −2.0 to −3.0p (based on H2 FY25 −0.7p scaled for central cost run-rate improvement and Brazil modest loss), FY26e adj EPS is likely to land at 8.5–9.5p on the adjusted basis — ahead of the 8.3p stale consensus. But the bigger story is the LTM adj op profit of £5.0m (+35%) which implies FY26 AOP well above the company-compiled £5.5m consensus, and medium-term targets that require ~£20p+ EPS by FY29.

#2 Driver — Medium-term targets (first-time disclosure): £120m rev / £15m EBITDA / 10% EBIT margin / 20% ROCE in 3–5 years vs FY27 consensus £90.5m / ~£8.8m EBITDA. These targets imply the broker community must build a significantly longer upgrade cycle into their models. The targets are not aggressive on an absolute basis (they represent reasonable extrapolation of Brazil rollout + organic growth) but they are materially above current consensus and will force DCF upgrades.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e EPS: Brokers revise up from 8.3p to approximately 9.0–10.5p depending on H2 assumption. The company's guidance "in line with AOP £5.5m" caps the magnitude of the upgrade — FY26 adj EPS revision likely +8–25%. Revenue: minimal revision; £85.6m consensus broadly maintained given flat H1 revenue; brokers may trim slightly or hold.
  • FY27e EPS: More significant revision — medium-term targets require modelling a Brazil growth path. Brokers likely revise FY27e EPS from 11.0p toward 12–14p range, revenue toward £95–105m. This is the bigger upgrade cycle.

Target price: Consensus TP 186p vs current 136.5p. Brokers likely to revise TPs upward to the 190–215p range on medium-term target announcement. Canaccord already at 190p — may move to 200–220p. The current share price discount (−27% vs TP) is unusually wide and provides significant re-rating potential.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with expectations" with company-compiled AOP consensus £5.5m is classic Fevara understatement given the H1 AOP of £7.2m already confirmed. Brokers will note that achieving the "in-line" AOP of £5.5m requires H2 AOP of −£1.7m — entirely consistent with seasonal patterns (H2 AOP FY25 was −£0.2m adjusted for central costs). The guidance is conservative, confirming downside is protected.

Key risk: Revenue was flat YoY at £50.6m — despite positive volume momentum (+6% LMB), the mix shift away from minerals and FX headwind suppressed reported revenue. If brokers focus on the revenue number rather than the margin-mix story, there is a risk of a muted reaction to the revenue line. Additionally, the H2 implied revenue burden of £35.0m (+24.1% YoY) — the highest H2 revenue required in the company's recent history — needs to be delivered, largely from Brazil. "Following the strategic entry in the significant Brazil market in December 2025, early trading has been in line with management's expectations."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade (H1 11.0p > full-year consensus 8.3p; full-year will be revised up). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. ✓

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely for FY26e (upgrade quantum limited by H2 seasonality and management's in-line FY guidance); potentially 🟢🟢 upgrade cycle for FY27+ driven by medium-term targets. Retaining 🟢 Constructive for the scorecard given the FY1 guidance anchors the near-term revision magnitude.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

(Pre-FX subtotal = +67)

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single defining number from today's H1 results is adj EPS of 11.0p (+116% vs H1 FY25 5.1p), which has already exceeded the entire FY26 consensus EPS of 8.3p by 32.5% with six months of the financial year still to run. The H1 adj operating profit of £7.2m (+22% YoY) on essentially flat revenue of £50.6m (flat reported, +2% constant currency) reveals a business undergoing genuine margin transformation: H1 EBIT margin of 14.2% vs 11.7% prior year, with central costs slashed 27% YoY to £0.8m. The EPS step-change is partly structural (share count halved post-tender offer) but the underlying PBT growth of +18.6% and 250bp margin expansion confirm that the operational transformation is real and tracking ahead of broker models. LTM adj operating profit is now £5.0m (+35% from FY25 £3.7m), which management is rightly flagging as the relevant forward indicator.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The revenue tracking signal is problematic on a mechanical basis: H1 revenue at £50.6m represents only 59.1% of the £85.6m FY1 consensus, versus a 2-year seasonal average of 63.3% — a −4.2pp deviation that triggers a SELL SIGNAL on the revenue metric alone. This is misleading as a signal: the shortfall is entirely explained by a deliberate planned reduction in lower-margin mineral volumes (UK/Ireland minerals −14% by design) and the FX translation headwind on US revenues (~45% of the business, GBP ~5c stronger vs prior year). LMB volumes — the core premium product — were actually +6% YoY (UK/Europe +9%, US owned +4%). The H2 implied revenue burden of £35.0m vs £28.2m prior (+24.1%) requires delivery on Macal (full H2 contribution), gradual São Paulo ramp, and continuation of the southern US momentum (+28% volume H1). Management explicitly states "trading since the half year has been encouraging...US overall trading is ahead of the prior year." The H2 weather normalisation in the northern US (second warmest winter in 132 years in H1 is not an H2 problem) provides a natural tailwind. The upgrade resilience case is therefore strong: even in a bear scenario where Brazil contributes minimally to H2, the organic business is generating sufficient margin to protect FY26 adj EPS well above the stale 8.3p consensus.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers must revise FY26e adj EPS from 8.3p — the question is the landing point. Edison (8.6p FY26e) and Canaccord (8.5p) are both stale; with H1 at 11.0p and H2 guided as seasonally loss-making (consistent with H2 FY25 −0.7p adj EPS), FY26e likely lands at 8.5–9.5p (our central estimate ~9.0p, implying H2 adj EPS of approximately −1.5 to −2.0p). FY27e revision is larger — medium-term targets require modelling a Brazil growth path and central cost normalisation that pushes consensus from 11.0p toward 12–14p range. Revenue consensus may hold near £85.6m for FY26 given the flat H1 print, with FY27 moving toward £95–100m+ as Brazil contribution is modelled. Consensus TP at 186p vs current 136.5p = 36.5% upside — this gap has become extreme given the EPS delivery, and a re-rating toward 160–175p on today's results would be a modest response; the medium-term target announcement justifies revisiting broker DCFs with significantly higher terminal earnings assumptions. The dominant watch point is broker treatment of the revenue line — if any house flags the flat H1 revenue as a negative without properly contextualising the margin mix story, the re-rating will be slower. 🏁 Compelling H1 delivery on the metrics that matter — adj EPS dramatically ahead of consensus, margins expanding sharply, medium-term targets set for the first time — with the revenue flatness entirely explained by a value-accretive mix shift; the score is constrained by the FX drag and the mechanical revenue tracking signal but the fundamental upgrade cycle is confirmed.

6. FY26 order visibility — very strong The $10.2m OFM orders from 2025 are mostly deferred into FY26 revenue recognition. Plus CFDS orders of £2.3m still being delivered. Revenue should materially step up in FY26 from Infotec backlog and CFDS.

"Revenues for the project are expected to be recognised across H2 2026, to meet customer timeline requirements."

7. CFDS acquisition contribution Revenue £7.4m, gross profit £3.0m (41% margin), underlying profit £0.4m since September 2025. In 12 months to April 2025, CFDS sales were £17.3m with PBT of £2.4m — implying CFDS on its own contributed over half the Group's incremental FY26 earnings potential.

8. Cash position £12.0m (2024: £14.3m) — strong, after £10.7m net cash outflow on CFDS acquisition and capex.

9. Goodwill £13.0m (2024: £4.1m) — driven by CFDS acquisition at £8.975m goodwill.

10. Dilution New shares issued: proceeds £1.358m. Share count increased from 16,475k to 17,092k weighted average (+3.7%). This diluted statutory EPS (23.83p vs 26.29p) despite higher profits. Adjusted EPS is the broker focus.

The gross margin expansion from 36% to 40% adds another layer of earnings leverage — higher revenue flowing through at 40% rather than 36% produces disproportionate profit growth.

Score 82/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

GBG · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26 full year ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue — FY26 actual:

  • "FY26 group revenue of £285 million represents 3.2% year on year growth on a constant currency basis."
  • Reported: £285m vs FY25 £282.7m = +0.8% reported; +3.2% constant currency.
  • vs Sharescope FY1 fc £284.9m: in-line (£285m vs £284.9m = negligible +£0.1m rounding).
  • RNS: excludes "legacy Compliance platform that will be retired" from core Identity + Location revenue. Core segment (Identity + Location) growth was 6% in H2 on constant currency basis — note this is stronger than overall group growth.
  • H2 implied: £285m − £135.5m = £149.5m vs H2 FY25 £145.8m = +2.5% YoY.

"FY26 group revenue of £285 million represents 3.2% year on year growth on a constant currency basis."

2. Adj operating profit / EPS:

  • Adj operating profit: ~£67.5m (FY25: £67.0m = +0.7% YoY). Adj EBIT margin: 23.7% (FY25 margin approximately £67.0m / £282.7m = 23.7%). Margin flat YoY — no expansion.
  • ⚠️ Notable: despite 3.2% CC revenue growth, adj operating profit grew only +0.7%. Implies some margin dilution from non-recurring items, mix, or investment. The constant currency to reported gap (3.2% vs 0.8%) means FX absorbed ~2.4pp of revenue growth. On a reported basis, adj OP grew £0.5m on £2.3m revenue increase = ~22% drop-through — low but explained by FX and mix.
  • FY26 adj EPS: not disclosed in this trading update. Full results 2 June 2026. Sharescope consensus 18.7p — likely to be validated at full results. Buyback (~8% equity reduction in FY26) is a structural EPS tailwind — 232.5m shares outstanding vs likely ~213–215m post-buyback. This means reported EPS may modestly beat consensus on a per-share basis even if PBT is in-line.
  • Implied FY26 EPS bridge: Adj OP ~£67.5m + interest income net (moderate; net debt £80m at ~5% → net interest charge ~£2-3m) → adj PBT ~£65m. Tax at 25% → PAT ~£49m. On ~215m shares post-buyback → EPS ~22.7p. Wait — Sharescope consensus is 18.7p on 232.5m shares. If shares have been reduced by ~8% buyback, the weighted average for FY26 may be ~220m → EPS = £49m / 220m = ~22.3p. This materially exceeds 18.7p consensus. ⚠️ Either: (a) my adj PBT estimate is too high (likely — adj OP includes D&A/lease adjustments); or (b) Sharescope share count of 232.5m is the pre-buyback count and EPS consensus was calculated on the pre-buyback count. In practice, GBG's adj EPS is calculated differently (includes amortisation/interest in different configurations). Without the full results, the EPS figure cannot be precisely derived. Flag: per-share items from buyback (8% of equity = ~18.6m shares at a cost of £45m average ~242p) will provide EPS uplift vs a model that used beginning-of-year share count. This is a known positive.

"Adjusted operating profit of approximately £67.5 million (FY25: £67.0 million); an operating margin of 23.7%."

EPS bridge FY26e (Phase 4 reference):

  • (1) Base: FY25 adj EPS 17.4p on ~232.5m shares (pre-buyback weighted).
  • (2) Organic: Adj OP +£0.5m YoY → +0.2p EPS at constant share count.
  • (3) Buyback accretion: ~8% equity reduction (18.6m shares). Weighted average FY26 shares ~215–220m vs FY25 ~232m → ~6–8% EPS uplift from buyback → +1.0–1.4p.
  • (4) Interest step-up: Net debt £80m vs ~£73m FY25 year-end → higher net debt from buyback; net interest cost increase ~£0.5m → −0.2p.
  • Implied FY26e adj EPS: ~17.4 + 0.2 + 1.1 − 0.2 = ~18.5p — closely aligned with consensus 18.7p. Bridge confirms consensus is accurate. No material revision expected from today's trading update.

3. Order book / pipeline:

  • GBG Go platform: "90 wins... more than a quarter with multi-solution requirement." Pipeline: "225+ opportunities entering FY27."
  • Americas Identity "returned to growth in Q4." EMEA "strong execution." These are qualitative positive signals for FY27.

"We move into FY27 with a strong pipeline of over 225 opportunities."

4. Margin / profitability:

  • Adj OP margin: 23.7% — flat vs FY25. Management targeting "mid-single-digit revenue growth in FY27" with focus on "strategies to accelerate growth further."
  • H2 FY26 core Identity + Location growth: +6% CC — acceleration from H1 (H1 FY26 total group revenue was £135.5m representing low single digit CC growth vs FY25 H1 £136.9m constant currency implied ~2-3%). The H2 acceleration is significant.
  • "Revenue growth for our core segments of Identity and Location accelerated to 6% in the second half of the financial year on a constant currency basis." This is the key signal.

5. Capital returns:

  • Buyback: ~8% of equity repurchased at £45m in FY26. New £10m buyback commenced 1 April 2026 (post-year-end).
  • Dividend: £11m final (prior year). No FY26 DPS figure disclosed yet. Sharescope fc DPS 4.6p.
  • Net debt: £80m at 31 Mar 2026. RCF £175m refinanced to Sep 2030.
  • Bolt-on acquisition "since 2022" — small but demonstrates M&A capability resuming.

6. Qualitative tone: "Confident that our second-half performance reinforces our outlook to deliver mid-single-digit revenue growth in FY27." This is quantitative guidance: FY27 rev growth mid-single-digits = ~5–6% from £285m base = £298–302m — broadly consistent with consensus £298.9m. No EPS guidance for FY27.

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

FY27 guidance: "mid-single-digit revenue growth" — numeric, quantitative range (5–6%), covering FY27 only. This matches consensus £298.9m closely. No EPS guidance. The GBG Go platform pipeline of 225+ opportunities and the Americas return to growth in Q4 provide qualitative support.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY27 revenue guidance matches consensus (mid-single-digit = ~5%); adj OP margin held flat for FY26; no explicit EPS upgrade trigger. The H2 core segment acceleration (+6% CC) is a constructive data point that may support minor FY27 upgrades. Provisional points: +2.

Divergence check: FY26 delivered in-line on revenue and adj OP. FY27 guidance "mid-single-digit" = in-line with consensus. No divergence. No Beat quality flag.

  • FY25: H1 £136.9m + H2 £145.8m = £282.7m ✅. EPS: H1 7.3p + H2 10.1p = 17.4p ✅.
  • FY24: H1 £132.4m + H2 £145.0m = £277.4m vs Sharescope "2y ago FY" = 277.3m (rounding ✅). EPS: H1 5.1p + H2 10.0p = 15.1p ✅.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: GBG confirmed a clean FY26 in-line delivery: £285m revenue (+3.2% CC, +0.8% reported) and adj operating profit ~£67.5m (margin 23.7%, flat vs FY25's 23.7%), both matching Sharescope consensus of £284.9m / 18.7p EPS. The single most positive element of this announcement is not the headline in-line delivery — it is the core Identity and Location segment growth accelerating to +6% CC in H2, compared to a weak H1. Americas Identity, which had been a drag on the business, returned to growth in Q4 — a genuine inflection point after a period of investor concern. Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The implied H2 FY26 revenue of £149.5m (+2.5% YoY vs H2 FY25 £145.8m) — classified as 🟡 moderate — understates the quality of the H2 delivery because the legacy Compliance platform decline is embedded in the group revenue figure. GBG Go's 225+ FY27 pipeline opportunities and the expansion of cross-sell (>25% of wins multi-solution) provide a credible FY27 upgrade path that is not yet in the flat consensus EPS trajectory. The downgrade concern — adj OP margin held flat at 23.7% — is real: for a business investing in a new platform (GBG Go), maintaining margin while growing is acceptable, but it does not provide the operating leverage signal that would accelerate the upgrade cycle. Net debt of £80m is higher than the Sharescope forecast of £63.1m, explained entirely by the £45m buyback at an average price that looks well below the 360p TP consensus, providing ongoing EPS accretion from the new £10m buyback commenced 1 April.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: At full results on 2 June 2026, the key variables are: (1) FY26 adj EPS (consensus 18.7p; buyback accretion may produce a modest beat); (2) FY27 guidance specificity — "mid-single-digit revenue growth" matches consensus £298.9m, but any EPS guidance would be the upgrade trigger; (3) Americas and GBG Go pipeline commentary. FY26e EPS likely held at 18.7p; FY27e EPS may see modest upgrades toward 20–21p on Americas recovery modelling, from current 20.8p (consensus already has some of this). Consensus TP 360p vs current 213p = 69% upside — this is an extreme discount for a FTSE 250 identity tech business delivering in-line, but reflects the market's concern about reported revenue growth trajectory and GBP headwinds. The 2 June full results are the real catalyst. 🏁 In-line delivery with a positive H2 acceleration narrative — the H2 +6% CC core growth and Americas inflection are genuine positives that should support the current consensus, but the flat margin and sluggish reported revenue trajectory mean today's announcement is unlikely to drive material re-rating; the real test is the 2 June full results and FY27 guidance.
