Revenue recognition note — critical for FY27

The accounts state explicitly: "The Mechanical Engineering segment of the Group contains large non-seasonal contracts, and therefore significant variations are to be expected year on year in the trade receivable, contract assets, work in progress and contract liabilities balances."

Contract liabilities at FY25: £34.75m (from £14.86m in FY24) — this is cash received from customers for work not yet delivered. A rising contract liability is a leading indicator of future revenue recognition. The £19.9m YoY increase in contract liabilities signals significant work front-loaded in payments that will flow through the P&L in FY26.

Dividend policy — the actual wording

The FY25 annual report contains the formal 58% payout policy, with the Board stating: "the Board is confident that the alteration of the dividend policy from 38% to 58% of post-tax profits plus depreciation and amortisation is a safe and viable change for now and the foreseeable future."

The March 2026 trading update then signals a potential reversion. The phrase used in the update ("considering whether to revert") against this language is jarring — the policy was confirmed as "safe and viable for the foreseeable future" only 8 months ago. This is the crux of the market's reaction.

Defence alone = 57% of a £287m workload = £163m of contracted/probable future work. This is what makes the Sellafield loss (nuclear, not defence) more containable than the market may be pricing — the defence backlog is enormous and multi-decade. Nuclear is only 9% of workload (£26m), so losing one Sellafield tender doesn't decimate the nuclear contribution as much as feared.

Goodwin International — the Sellafield SSB context

The Chairman states: "237 SSBs have been contractually awarded and 90 of these have been manufactured and shipped. However, it is reported that up to 747 of these SSBs could be required and, with no one else in the UK able to supply the product."

This is crucial. The Sellafield tender lost in the March 2026 update is for a new contract (the "unexpectedly" lost tender), but the existing SSB programme (237 contracted, 147 still to deliver) continues. The trading update says the Sellafield loss is on a new competitive tender — not on the existing SSB programme. The 147 remaining SSBs to be delivered (90 of 237 shipped) represent substantial ongoing work at premium margins.

The SSB programme alone (147 units × implied £150–200k per unit contribution) = £22–29m of residual revenues still to flow from the existing contract. This was not cancelled — only the new tender was lost.

Revised score — incorporating annual report data

Changes from the new information

1. Sellafield loss — less severe than initially modelled (score: +3 pts back)

The lost tender is a new competitive tender, not cancellation of the existing SSB programme. 147 SSBs remain to be delivered under existing contract. The nuclear workload is only 9% of the total £287m workload. Revenue impact of the new tender loss is spread over multiple years, and the existing work continues. I overpenalised this.

2. Performance obligations secured backlog — more visibility than I credited (+2 pts)

£201.5m audited performance obligations at April 2025, with the 2–5 year book growing materially (£125m vs £114m prior year). This structural backlog visibility supports FY27 earnings better than my initial model assumed. The £69.5m within-1-year tranche at April 2025 alone exceeds FY24 half-year revenue.

3. Contract liability increase — FY26 revenue more assured (+2 pts)

The £19.9m YoY increase in contract liabilities (cash already received, work still to deliver) is a leading indicator confirming FY26 revenue recognition will be strong. This further supports the >£71m trading PBT guidance reliability.

4. Mechanical Engineering margin base — FY25 was only 16.3%, H1 FY26 30.1% (+0, confirms step-change)

The H1 FY26 margin is extraordinary because FY25's 16.3% was itself a step-up from sub-15% in prior years. The FY27 question is whether margins revert to FY25's 16% or settle somewhere between 16% and 30%. Given the SSB deliveries continue, Northrop ramps, and Easat builds, a FY27 Mechanical margin of 20–22% (vs H1 FY26's 30%, vs FY25's 16%) is more realistic than my bear case of 16% reversion. This lifts the central FY27 PBT estimate.

5. Dividend policy — wording confirms severity of reversal (−2 pts, net of above)

The formal FY25 annual report policy language ("safe and viable for the foreseeable future") makes the March 2026 "considering reverting" signal a genuine governance negative — the Board contradicted its own stated confidence within 8 months. This is a trust issue, not just a financial one. Modestly increases the penalty.

6. Defence = 57% of workload — structural underpinning confirmed (+1 pt)

The £163m of defence backlog (57% of £287m workload) is materially larger than I had modelled. Multi-decade submarine programmes (Astute, Virginia, Columbia, Dreadnought, Type 26, Gerald R Ford, AUKUS) provide genuine long-cycle revenue visibility. This makes the FY27 downside less severe.

Final revised score

ComponentPts
🟢 FY26 profit ">£71m" confirmed, H1 £37.2m+20
🟢 H1 EPS +133% YoY, gross margin 49.3%+15
🟢 Defence = 57% workload, £163m multi-decade backlog+12
🟢 £201.5m audited performance obligations, 4–5yr book growing+10
🟢 Refractory stable, India facility operational, Easat profitable+7
🟢 Cash generation: £67m ops FY25, contract liabilities +£20m+6
🟢 Northrop $16m initial + >$200m pipeline MoU+5
🟡 Duvelco first commercial sales FY27 (modest, unproven at scale)−2
🟡 Easat Estonia radar tender lost (−£18m, single loss)−3
🔴 LNG dispatch delays Gulf — timing risk H2 FY26 and FY27−7
🔴 Sellafield new tender lost (existing SSB contract intact, 147 units remain)−10
🔴 Dividend policy reversal — "foreseeable future" contradicted in 8 months−12
🔴 FY27 peak-year margin compression: Mechanical from 30.1% → ~20–22% central−8

Raw total: +34 pts

Revised score: 56/100 — up from 55 in original session (minor), but the composition is meaningfully different. The positives are now better-grounded (SSB continuity, defence workload proportion, secured backlog). The negatives are more precisely calibrated (Sellafield loss contained to new tender only; dividend reversal confirmed as severe; FY27 margin compression central case ~20–22%, not full reversion to 16%).

What actually changes vs original 62

The original 62 was built without: the precise Mechanical margin at FY25 (16.3%), the SSB programme detail (147 units remaining on existing contract — not lost), the performance obligations breakdown (£201.5m audited, 2–5yr book expanding), the contract liability leading indicator, or the exact dividend policy language. The score moves to 56 because:

  • Sellafield is less bad than scored (−4 pts severity reduction)
  • Dividend reversal is more bad than scored (−2 pts severity increase)
  • Structural backlog and defence concentration is better than scored (+2 pts)
  • FY27 margin compression is more precisely modelled at 20–22% Mechanical, giving a central FY27 trading PBT of ~£65–68m (better than my earlier £61m, worse than £73m FY26)

56/100 · Neutral / hold and wait · Shore Capital will cut TP, revise FY27 model, but FY26 delivery remains intact and the SSB programme continues.

scorecards.analysisText:
GHH

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 trading update. Next year end = 30/9/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Five explicit row label mappings:

  • Next year end 30/9/26 → FY1 = FY26
  • FY1 − 1 = FY25 (1y ago)
  • FY1 − 2 = FY24 (2y ago)
  • FY1 − 3 = FY23 (3y ago)
  • FY2 = FY27

Sharescope note: Current H1/H2 shows 14.8/19.8 EPS and 70.9/79.6 revenue with FY total 34.6 — this represents FY25 actuals (the year just completed to 30/9/25). The current H1 in Sharescope = H1 FY26 (six months to 31/3/26). The RNS is a pre-H1 trading update for H1 FY26 (six months ended 31 March 2026). The Sharescope current H1 EPS 14.8p and Revenue £70.9m are H1 FY26 actuals embedded in Sharescope — but wait: "current H1 / H2 : 14.8 / 19.8 → FY: 34.6" and "FY1 fc EPS: 44.6" — the current H1 + H2 = 34.6p which is described as the FY figure, but FY1 fc = 44.6p. This suggests current H1/H2 = FY25 actual split (34.6p total FY25), not FY26 H1. So:

  • Current H1 14.8p / H2 19.8p = FY25 half-year split = H1 FY25 (Oct-Mar 2025) / H2 FY25 (Apr-Sep 2025) → FY25 = 34.6p actual ✓
  • FY1 fc EPS 44.6p = FY26 consensus forecast
  • The RNS H1 FY26 figures (six months to 31 March 2026) are in the RNS, not yet in Sharescope as "current H1"

Correction: Sharescope "current H1" = H1 FY25 (the most recently completed half) = £70.9m revenue / 14.8p EPS. The RNS provides H1 FY26 actual revenue of £81.9m — this is NOT in Sharescope yet. This is pre-H1 mode with H1 FY26 actuals disclosed in the RNS.

PHASE 0B — FX CHECK — GHH

GHH is a UK manufacturer of photonic components with operations in USA and Europe. Sharescope Currency: GBP. The RNS states H1 2026 revenue was £81.9m, "+9.1% on an organic, constant currency basis." This is the constant currency figure — reported revenue is £81.9m. Without prior period reported figures in the same sentence, we need to derive reported YoY. Prior H1 FY25 (Sharescope current H1) = £70.9m.

Reported H1 FY26: £81.9m vs H1 FY25: £70.9m = +15.5% reported YoY. Constant currency: +9.1%. Difference: 15.5% − 9.1% = +6.4pp FX tailwind (GBP weakened vs USD/EUR in this period).

Constant currency override test: Reported +15.5% vs cc +9.1% → difference = 6.4pp → NOT within 0.5pp → override does NOT fire.

GHH has significant US revenues (US operations, defence contracts). Likely >30% USD exposure. RNS discloses the cc vs reported gap explicitly. GBP weaker vs USD = tailwind.

FX tailwind: difference is 6.4pp. Exposure likely 35–50% USD + some EUR. Apply Phase 0B:

  • 35–50% exposure · tailwind (GBP weaker >3c equivalent) → +5 to +6 pts
  • Management guides revenue on constant currency basis (+9.1%) → reduce tailwind boost by 1–2 pts per the "management guides ex-FX" rule.

Applying +4 pts (after management ex-FX reporting reduction).

🟢 FX Rule 1 applied (+4 pts) · ~35–50% USD/EUR · GBP tailwind

PHASE 1 — GHH · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). RNS is H1 FY26 trading update (six months ended 31 March 2026).
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 44.6p · Revenue £174.4m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 53.5p · Revenue £188.5m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +16.1% over snapshot period (38.4p → 44.6p). Notable upgrade step in December 2025 (35.7p → 46.0p — a large one-step upgrade, likely following the FY25 results announcement) then revision to 44.6p in January 2026. Net trajectory: 🟢 RISING (but has been flat for 4 weeks post-January reset). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT per data). Revenue: £152.6m → £174.4m = +14.3% net upgrade over full period.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.0% × £174.4m = £80.2m · EPS 40.3% × 44.6p = 18.0p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £70.9m · EPS 14.8p (Sharescope current H1 = FY25 H1)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode — based on H1 tracking): Compute in Phase 3.3.
  • FX: 🟢 FX Rule 1 applied (+4 pts) · ~35–50% USD/EUR · GBP tailwind · management guides cc basis.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt (ex. leases): current H1 FY26 = £35.5m (Sharescope — but RNS states net debt £37.0m at 31 March 2026, ex lease liabilities) → use RNS figure £37.0m · FY1fc £42.4m · FY2fc £34.6m · ND/EBITDA: FY1fc 1.50x / FY2fc 1.10x · Interest cover FY1fc 11.1x / FY2fc 13.2x · ND/FCF: FY1fc 6.3x · Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — ND/EBITDA 1.5x with strong interest cover 11.1x, leverage declining through FY27.

Phase 3.5 gate: 🟡 → silent in Phase 5.

PHASE 2 — GHH · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update

1. Revenue

H1 FY26 revenue: £81.9m (H1 FY25: £70.9m), +15.5% reported YoY, +9.1% organic constant currency. RNS does not provide explicit FY guidance — states "Group continues to expect trading for FY 2026 to be in line with management's expectations."

vs H1 baseline (3yr avg 46.0% × £174.4m = £80.2m): +£1.7m, +2.1% above baseline → positive tracking signal.

"Revenue for H1 2026 was £81.9 million (H1 2025: £70.8 million), an increase of 9.1% on an organic, constant currency basis."

2. EPS / earnings

No H1 EPS or PBT figure disclosed. Pre-H1 trading update format — interim results due 2 June 2026. Only revenue and order book disclosed.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here): (1) New base FY25 actual EPS: Sharescope current H1 + H2 = 14.8 + 19.8 = 34.6p (FY25 actual). (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Global Photonics and Phoenix Optical acquired "during the last financial year" (FY25). These acquisitions contributed to FY25 for only part of the year — full-year contribution in FY26 adds incremental profit. RNS: "The integration of these two acquisitions is proceeding to plan." The annualisation delta is embedded in the December 2025 consensus upgrade (35.7p → 46.0p jump = +10.3p); this appears to capture both annualisation and organic growth. Quantifying separately: assume ~6–8p of the FY26e consensus step-up from FY25 (34.6p → 44.6p = +10.0p) is inorganic annualisation. (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: H1 FY26 revenue +9.1% organic cc → applying this to FY25 EBITDA base ~£24.1m (H1 £11.0m + H2 £13.1m) → ~+£2.2m organic EBITDA delta → ~+3-4p EPS. (4) Interest step-up: Net debt increased from £4.5m (FY25 year-end per Sharescope) to £37.0m (H1 FY26 per RNS) = +£32.5m drawdown for acquisitions. Finance cost step-up: Sharescope FY25 balance was near net cash (H2 FY25 = −£4.5m = net cash £4.5m); RNS H1 FY26 net debt = £37.0m. Incremental net debt ~£41.5m. At ~5% interest rate → ~£2.1m additional annual interest charge → ~£1.6m net of tax → ~3p EPS headwind. FY26e consensus already incorporates this at 44.6p. Bridge validation: FY25 34.6p + annualisation ~6p + organic ~3p − interest step-up ~3p = ~40.6p vs consensus 44.6p. The ~4p gap suggests consensus includes additional upside not captured in this simplified bridge. Broadly consistent — bridge supports consensus range 40–46p. No significant FY26 EPS revision risk from bridge analysis alone.

FY27e bridge: 44.6p FY26e + organic growth ~+8p (at Sharescope EBITDA consensus £31.4m FY27e vs £28.0m FY26e = +12% → ~4-5p delta) − modest interest reduction (debt declining) → ~50-52p vs Sharescope FY27e 53.5p. Bridge broadly supports FY27 consensus.

3. Order book

Order book: £167.3m at 31 March 2026 (30 Sept 2025: £142.3m), +17.6% in the period. On constant currency basis: +16.5%. Strong growth driven by Aerospace & Defence.

"During H1 2026, the Group's order book increased to £167.3 million (30 September 2025: £142.3 million). The increase on a constant currency basis was 16.5%."

£167.3m order book vs FY1 consensus revenue £174.4m = 96.0% of FY26 consensus revenue covered by order book. Very high visibility.

4. Margin / profitability

No specific margin disclosure in this pre-H1 trading update. Interim results 2 June will provide detail. RNS focuses on revenue and order book. General tone: capacity expansion underway at acquired businesses; capital expenditure in line with year's plan.

"Capacity is being expanded at both businesses in response to significantly increased demand, utilising the existing footprint at each site and in line with the year's expected capital expenditure."

5. Capital / net debt

Net debt (ex. leases) at 31 March 2026: £37.0m (31 March 2025: £24.1m; 30 Sept 2025: £29.9m). £15.7m available to draw on under facilities.

"As at 31 March 2026, net debt excluding lease liabilities was £37.0 million (31 March 2025: £24.1 million and 30 September 2025: £29.9 million) and the Group had £15.7 million available to draw upon."

Net debt building H1 FY26 — driven by capex expansion and working capital for growing order book. FY1fc ND per Sharescope £42.4m at year-end FY26 — debt expected to continue building before peak.

6. Qualitative tone / FY guidance

"Group continues to expect trading for FY 2026 to be in line with management's expectations." Interim results 2 June 2026.

New CFO appointment: James Corte joined today.

"The Group continues to expect trading for FY 2026 to be in line with management's expectations."

"I am pleased with the positive progress... The strong order book growth in the period demonstrates the increased confidence our customers have in G&H... the recovery in our Industrial and Semiconductor markets along with the strong growth in demand from our Aerospace and Defence markets should allow the Group to make further positive progress on our journey to mid-teens returns over the medium term."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "in line with management's expectations." This is neutral language — not "comfortable with market consensus" or "ahead of expectations." scorecards.analysisText:
HEAD — Headlam Group PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue: UK £498.7m (100% of continuing operations, ex-Continental Europe which is discontinued). Continental Europe presented as discontinued operation. Phase 0B not triggered (no ongoing non-GBP exposure material to continuing operations). No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS −36.8p · Revenue £531.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS −13.9p · Revenue £527.1m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: −30.3p → −36.8p = worsening by 6.5p (−21.5%). EPS deteriorated in two steps: Sept 2025 (−30.7p) and Nov 2025 (−36.8p), then flat. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at −36.8p / £531.8m for 4+ months). Revenue net change: £586.6m → £531.8m = −£54.8m (−9.3%). Sustained deterioration throughout year.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.5% of FY = £252.6m · EPS n/a (negative earnings, tracking meaningless for buy signals)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £256.4m · EPS −15.1p (loss)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £531.8m − H1 actual £244.7m = implied H2 £287.1m vs prior H2 £336.7m → −14.7% YoY — substantial expected H2 decline. Implied H2 EPS: −36.8p − (−19.0p) = −17.8p loss vs prior H2 −19.9p.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Full year results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 revenue (continuing): £498.7m, down 4.6% vs £525.7m in FY2024 (same working day basis).

vs FY1 consensus of £531.8m: miss of £33.1m (−6.2%) — significant revenue miss vs consensus expectation.

"Revenue reduced 4.6% year-on-year."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Underlying basic loss per share: −44.1p (2024: −31.0p), worse than prior year.

vs FY1 consensus of −36.8p: miss by 7.3p — actual loss is 19.8% worse than consensus expected.

Statutory basic loss per share: −102.0p (2024: −31.2p) — includes £30.1m non-underlying items.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on underlying loss: 10.4% (2024: 21.5%). Rate is below normal due to partial recognition of deferred tax asset on losses — tax losses only partially recognised. No positive EPS quality issue; this is a genuine loss business.

3. EBITDA / Cash flow

Underlying EBITDA: −£12.5m (2024: −£5.0m) — worsening. Underlying operating cash flow: −£18.6m (2024: +£27.0m outflow swing of £45.6m). Net debt: £31.4m (2024: net cash £10.9m).

"Underlying Loss Before Tax of £39.5m compared to a loss of £31.7m in 2024."

4. Balance sheet / Financing

New £85m ABL facility agreed post year-end (replacing RCF). Property portfolio valued at £75m. Three properties under offer for disposal — proceeds expected to reduce debt.

"Three-year £85m ABL facility agreed post year end, securing financing to 2029."

5. Transformation plan / Strategic update

Core customer strategy introduced November 2025 — exit low-margin large customers, focus on independent retailers/contractors. Range reduced from 27k to 16k SKUs. £10m+ annualised payroll savings achieved. Service delivery improving (strong momentum Q1 2026). Continental Europe (France/Netherlands) classified as discontinued, proceeds expected H1 2026.

6. Outlook — FY2026 material revenue reduction guided

"The new core customer strategy will see a material planned reduction in revenue over 2026 and 2027." Recovery to profitability in 2027 maintained as the guidance. Near-term trading challenging — Middle East conflict creating polypropylene/fuel cost pressures. No specific numeric guidance for FY2026. Going concern note present with material uncertainty disclosed.

"The Board therefore continues to have confidence in a return to profitability in 2027 as previously guided."

EPS quality check (additional): Going concern note in auditor's report — material uncertainty disclosed. The auditor's report is unmodified but references going concern risk contingent on property sales and working capital delivery.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "material planned reduction in revenue over 2026 and 2027" + going concern uncertainty + FY26 no profitability + return to profitability 2027.
  • Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — explicit below-consensus EPS delivery, material revenue reduction guided for FY26/FY27, going concern note, no numeric upgrade. Provisional points: −14.
  • Divergence check: FY25 EPS miss (−44.1p vs −36.8p consensus) + 🔴🔴 profit warning outlook = consistent. Both negative.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

FYRev £mRev YoY %EPS p (underlying)EPS YoY %
FY23 (3y ago)663.6†—+35.2—
FY24 (2y ago)656.5†−1.1%+10.9−69.0%
FY25 (1y ago)525.7−19.9%−31.0n/m
FY25 actual498.7−4.6%−44.1n/m

†FY23: H1 £323.8m + H2 £339.8m = £663.6m. FY24: H1 £331.8m + H2 £324.7m = £656.5m. Note: FY25 prior year represents only the period before the methodology change in H1 2025 reporting.

Revenue growth trajectory: −1.1%, −19.9%, −4.6% → 🔴 Decelerating (sustained multi-year decline).

EPS growth trajectory: −69.0%, then loss territory → 🔴 Decelerating — catastrophic multi-year deterioration.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: −30.3p → −36.8p, worsening by 6.5p (−21.5%). Two downgrade steps in 2025. Revenue: £586.6m → £531.8m (−9.3%). Sustained negative revision cycle.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat last 4 months — market ran out of downgrade room pre-results)
  • Post-results: Actual loss of −44.1p is 7.3p worse than −36.8p consensus. Revenue miss of £33.1m (−6.2%). Further consensus downgrades inevitable.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Going concern — material uncertainty disclosed]: The auditor's report references material uncertainty. This is a significant risk flag for institutional investors and mandates de-rating.

[Property portfolio £75m — key balance sheet support]: Three properties under offer. If property sales complete in H1 2026 as guided, net debt reduces materially from £31.4m. This is the primary near-term balance sheet stabiliser.

[Continental Europe sale — reduces ongoing losses]: Continental Europe contributed −£3.7m underlying loss in 2025 (discontinued). H1 2026 sale expected. Removes a loss contributor.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY25 underlying loss per share −44.1p vs consensus −36.8p (worse by 7.3p): Brokers must downgrade FY26 estimates further from −36.8p. Revenue miss of £33.1m adds pressure. The combined actual loss + revenue miss is the primary driver of further cuts.

#2 Driver — Material revenue reduction guided for FY26 + going concern note: The explicit guidance that revenue will "materially reduce" in 2026 as the core customer strategy is executed means revenue consensus of £531.8m is almost certainly too high. Brokers will model FY26 revenue at £400–470m range. Going concern note prevents Buy recommendation reinstatement.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: WORSE — from −36.8p to approximately −45 to −55p range, reflecting lower revenue base and ongoing transformation costs.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UNCHANGED or slight improvement — path to profitability in FY27 maintained but EPS recovery likely −10 to −5p range (marginally less negative).

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 315p appears completely detached from reality — this may be a stale estimate predating the full deterioration. Post-results, TP likely cut dramatically to 80–120p range or kept as a speculative recovery target. At 43.7p, the stock is effectively pricing in recovery or break-up value of the property portfolio. Brokers will maintain Sell/Hold ratings.

Key risk: The going concern note is the most significant risk. If property sales are delayed and working capital release slower than planned, the ABL facility covenants could be tested. This is not a theoretical risk — it is disclosed by management as a material uncertainty.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Headlam's FY25 results confirm a business in deep trouble. The underlying loss of −44.1p per share is 7.3p (19.8%) worse than consensus of −36.8p, and revenue of £498.7m missed consensus by £33.1m (−6.2%). The statutory loss per share is −102.0p, incorporating £30.1m of non-underlying charges (impairments, ERP write-off, restructuring). The #1 broker note catalyst is the combined EPS/revenue double-miss, which forces further downward revisions to already-negative FY26 consensus estimates. The going concern material uncertainty — disclosed by management and referenced in the auditor's report — is the single most damaging element for institutional ownership.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: There is no upgrade resilience in this RNS. The transformation plan, while showing early green shoots (service delivery improving, stock levels down, SKU rationalisation complete), is in early innings and will not prevent further losses in FY26. Management explicitly guides for "material planned reduction in revenue over 2026 and 2027" as the core customer strategy executes. The property portfolio (£75m, three disposals imminent) is the primary near-term stabiliser — if property sales complete in H1 2026, net debt falls from £31.4m and the ABL covenant headroom improves. Without property sales proceeding as planned, the going concern risk crystallises. The path to profitability in FY2027 is the medium-term anchor — achievable if the transformation plan delivers, but execution risk is high.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS will be revised from −36.8p to approximately −45 to −55p range; revenue from £531.8m to £400–470m as the planned low-margin revenue exit reduces the top-line materially. The consensus TP of 315p is almost certainly a stale pre-deterioration figure — brokers will cut dramatically to 80–120p if they maintain coverage at all. At 43.7p the stock is essentially a recovery option on the property portfolio plus the FY2027 profitability claim. 🏁 Severely negative: double miss on EPS and revenue, material FY26 revenue reduction guided, going concern material uncertainty disclosed — immediate and material broker downgrades on all metrics; recovery is a 2027 story at best with significant execution and balance sheet risk in the intervening period. Score 11/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

HIK · Q4 · Trading Statement (Pre-H1) · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (AGM trading statement)

1. Revenue figures

FY26 guidance reiterated: Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4%. No Q1 actual figures.

Implied FY26 guidance range (2–4% growth from FY25 $3,349m actual):

  • Low: $3,349m × 1.02 = $3,416.1m
  • High: $3,349m × 1.04 = $3,482.9m

vs FY26e consensus $3,466.5m — consensus within the guided range (at ~midpoint). ✅ No beat/miss vs guidance.

Segment guidance reiterated:

  • Injectables: revenue grow in low single digits; margin 27–28%
  • Branded: revenue grow 6–8%; margin ~25%
  • Hikma Rx: revenue broadly flat; margin close to 20%

"We continue to expect Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4%"

2. EPS / earnings figures

FY26 Group operating profit guidance: $720m to $770m.

FY25 actual revenue $3,349m × operating margin ~24.5% (from FY25 results) = ~$820m OP (approximate). FY26 $720–770m guidance implies operating profit is LOWER than FY25. This is a significant concern — PROFIT DECLINING despite revenue growing.

🚨 EPS quality check — operating profit declining: If FY26 OP = $720–770m vs FY25 ~$820m actual, that's a −6.1% to −12.2% YoY OP decline. With revenue growing 2–4%, this implies significant margin compression. EPS bridge:

  • FY25 adj EPS 226c (actual, H1+H2)
  • FY26 operating profit midpoint $745m vs FY25 ~$820m = −9% OP decline
  • D&A: similar levels ~$180–200m
  • Net interest: negative (net debt growing → higher interest cost)
  • Tax: ~21%
  • Share count: declining (buyback)

Rough EPS: OP $745m − D&A −$185m = EBIT $560m − net interest ~$80m = PBT $480m × 79% = PAT $379m / 211m shares ≈ 179c EPS. This is materially below the Sharescope FY26e consensus of 224.7c.

🚨 Major gap: consensus EPS 224.7c vs implied from OP guidance ~179c. Either: (a) The Sharescope consensus doesn't reflect the OP guidance, OR (b) My OP calculation is wrong (FY25 OP actual ≠ ~$820m), OR (c) The OP guidance and EPS consensus use different definitions (the OP guidance is likely "core operating profit" not "group operating profit" inclusive of all items)

Let me reconsider. HIK reports "core operating profit" as the primary metric. FY25 core OP was likely different from my estimate. The guidance of $720–770m is specifically "Group operating profit" in the RNS — this is the core/adjusted figure.

The Sharescope fc PBT is $585.6m for FY26e. If core OP $745m − D&A ~$175m = EBIT ~$570m, less interest ~$70m = PBT ~$500m. Tax ~$100m = PAT ~$400m / 215m shares = ~186c. Still below 224.7c consensus.

The consensus EPS of 224.7c appears materially above what the guided OP range implies. This is a significant EPS downside risk.

Possible explanation: the Sharescope EPS figure may use a different diluted share count or EPS definition (possibly Basic vs Diluted). Let me check: FY25 H1 121c + H2 105c = 226c. FY25 actual EPS. If FY25 actual EPS was 226c and consensus for FY26 is 224.7c (essentially flat), this makes sense if OP declines slightly but buyback reduces share count.

I may be overstating the OP decline. LSEG's FY25 results would clarify FY25 actual OP. Without that data confirmed here, I'll flag the concern but not over-assert.

EPS bridge (best estimate):

  • FY25 base EPS: 226c
  • OP decline −$50–100m (midpoint): ~−21–42c at post-tax per share (using ~79% tax retention, ~215m shares)
  • Buyback benefit: $250m at ~£13.43/share = ~14.2m shares repurchased. Share count decline from 216m to ~202m = +6% per share uplift on PAT = +6% × 224c ≈ +13c
  • Interest step-up: net ~−10c
  • Net: 226c − 30c (OP) + 13c (buyback) − 10c (interest) ≈ ~199–210c

This suggests consensus 224.7c is achievable only if OP decline is at the low end ($720m) and buyback timing is front-loaded. Downside risk to consensus of ~15–25c (−7 to −11%) if OP comes in at $720m.

FY26e EPS bridge summary: New base 226c. Inorganic delta: 503B compounding wind-down (strategic decision) = negative revenue impact, limited EPS impact (low margin business). Organic EBITDA delta: OP guided $720–770m = negative vs FY25. Interest step-up: net debt growing. Net result: implied EPS 200–215c vs consensus 224.7c — potential downgrade risk of −5 to −11%.

"We continue to expect Group revenue to grow in the range of 2% to 4% and for Group operating profit to be in the range of $720 million to $770 million in 2026."

3. Order book / forward work

No formal order book. Branded MENA: "largest pharmaceutical company by sales in the region." Injectables US: Tyzavan® (vancomycin bag) demand "accelerating." Hikma Rx pipeline: licensed agreements (tapentadol), Ellipta® device partnership signed.

Pipeline positive: generic Ellipta® programme (inhalation platform) — device partnership signed with unnamed partner for US, UK, Canada, EU, MENA. Represents future revenue optionality (medium term, not FY26 driver).

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Injectables margin guidance: 27–28% (vs FY25 core OP margin of ~27.6% per FY25 results). Essentially flat — no improvement guided.

Branded margin: ~25% — stable.

Hikma Rx margin: close to 20% — this is a step-down from FY25 Rx margin (which was approximately 22–23% based on full year results). Rx margin compression is a headwind.

Geopolitical cost pressures: "inflationary pressure, particularly linked to shipping, energy and insurance costs" — explicitly flagged. "Confident we can absorb these increased costs through strong business performance."

503B compounding wind-down: "strategic decision to wind down our 503B compounding business." This removes a small revenue stream but simplifies the business. Net: marginally negative for FY26 revenue/profit, positive for strategic focus.

5. Capital returns

Final dividend: 48 cents per share (subject to AGM approval). Full-year FY25 total dividend: 84 cents (+5% vs FY24). Sharescope fc DPS FY26e: 85.1c ≈ consistent (+1.3% growth expected).

Share buyback: $250m programme underway. To 17 April 2026: 4,374,095 shares purchased (note: RNS says "4,374,095 million" which appears to be a typo — should be 4,374,095 shares) at cost of £54.8m ($71.5m). ~$71.5m deployed of $250m = 28.6% deployed.

"Since the launch of the buyback programme on 26 February 2026 to 17 April 2026, Hikma has purchased 4,374,095 million ordinary shares at a cost of £54.8 million ($71.5 million)."

6. Qualitative tone

CEO: "Our three businesses are performing well, supported by our differentiated portfolio, recent product launches and our strong and growing commercial capabilities." "On track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." Upbeat.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: FY26 revenue +2–4%, OP $720–770m. Reiterated (from FY25 results). Qualitative overlap: "performing well," "on track." Numeric, one year. No change.

⚠️ The OP guidance of $720–770m implies year-on-year OP decline if FY25 OP was above $770m. The guidance range appears to be below the FY25 actual OP, not a step-up. This makes the classification potentially Cautious — guidance maintained but OP declining vs prior year.

However, the RNS says "on track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." "Revenue and profit growth" — CEO explicitly says PROFIT GROWTH. This contradicts my OP decline thesis. Resolution: either FY25 OP was below $720m (at the low end of the FY26 guidance range = guidance implies growth), OR the "profit growth" refers to adjusted EPS (post-buyback).

Per Sharescope, FY25 actual EPS was 226c and FY26e consensus 224.7c = essentially flat/slight decline. CEO language of "profit growth" may refer to operational earnings or PBT at the segment level. Without access to the FY25 full results breakdown, I'll give management benefit of doubt on "profit growth" language — the guidance is intended as growth vs FY25.

Revised interpretation: if FY25 core OP was $695–710m (in line with or slightly below the FY26 $720–770m range), then FY26 guidance = 2–11% OP growth. This would make the classification Constructive not Cautious.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — guidance reiterated with explicit "on track" language; "revenue and profit growth" CEO statement; but Hikma Rx broadly flat and OP guidance uncertainty creates ambiguity. No explicit upgrade trigger. Provisional points: +1 to +3.

Divergence check: CEO says "performing well" in Q1 — positive start. No explicit divergence. Consistent with In-line classification.

FY1-1 = FY25 (year ended 31/12/25). "1y ago" in Sharescope = FY25 actuals = $3,127m. "current H1/H2" = FY26 partial actuals = H1 ending 30/6/26 not yet known; these will be carryover figures.

Therefore "current" = FY25 actuals (just completed December 2025) and Sharescope hasn't rolled forward yet. "1y ago" = FY24. "2y ago" = FY23. "3y ago" = FY22.

So: FY25 actual = $3,349m (current H1+H2), FY24 actual = $3,127m (1y ago), FY23 = $2,875m (2y ago), FY22 = $2,517m (3y ago H1 $1,213m + H2 $1,304m).

Implied H2 Revenue: $1,757.7m vs 3yr avg ($1,448m, $1,558m, $1,691m) = avg $1,565.7m. $1,757.7m vs avg = +12.2% above avg. YoY: +0.6%. Classification: 🟡 flat (YoY basis).

EPS H2: 105.6c vs 3yr avg (33c, 94c, 105c) = avg 77.3c. 105.6c vs avg = +36.6% above avg. YoY vs FY25 H2: +0.6%. Classification: 🟡 flat (YoY).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: 230.5c → 224.7c = −5.8c (−2.5%). March 2026 spike (218.8c → 232.2c = +13.4c) followed by immediate reversion. This pattern suggests the Mar 2026 upgrade was post-FY25 results, then pulled back as brokers digested the FY26 OP guidance. Net: modest downgrade trend.
  • Revenue: +4.9% net change (driven by acquisition/organic growth expectations).
  • 4-week: 🟡 FLAT (224.7c stable for 4 weeks).
  • Price: £24.86 (May 2025) → £13.43 (current) = −46% decline. EPS −2.5%. Massive price/consensus divergence. Market pricing in significant downside vs consensus.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: USD.

Net borrowing: FY22 H2 −$167m (net cash) / FY23 H2 $648m / FY24 H2 $78m / FY25 H2 $65m → FY26e fc $1,375.2m / FY27e $1,217.9m.

RNS confirms $250m buyback programme = roughly $250m debt equivalent. Remaining FY26e debt step-up to $1,375.2m includes potential acquisition debt or other capital allocation.

ND/EBITDA: 1.6x / 1.3x. Interest cover: 5.3x / 6.0x. ND/FCF: 3.9x / 3.1x.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY26e EPS 224.7c vs FY25 actual 226c: 🚨 FY1 fc EPS −0.6% below prior year actual — declining. FY26e Revenue $3,466.5m vs FY25 $3,349m: ✅ growing +3.5%.

🚨 FY1 fc EPS slightly below prior year actual — rare flat-to-declining scenario.

Step 2: FY27e EPS 248.1c vs FY26e 224.7c: ✅ growing +10.4%. FY27e Revenue $3,635.6m vs FY26e: ✅ growing +4.9%. ✅✅ Both growing (FY27 recovery expected).

3.6 Structural flags

[Hikma Rx broadly flat — generic pipeline dependency]: Rx revenue broadly flat in FY26. Key contributors: generic Advair Diskus® remains "important contributor." Generic Ellipta® platform is the medium-term growth driver (device partnership just signed). New product launches (tapentadol AG) add incrementally. Rx flat in FY26 is a constraint on group growth.

[503B compounding wind-down]: Removing a business line creates short-term revenue headwind. Simplifies manufacturing footprint. Small net negative for FY26.

[Geopolitical Middle East risk]: MENA is ~35% of revenues (Branded division). Iran war context (per background news) — RNS notes "monitoring the evolving geopolitical situation." "Demand in the region remains robust" and "sufficient inventory levels" to mitigate supply disruptions. Some inflationary pressure from shipping/energy/insurance. Net: manageable currently but a tail risk.

[Buyback accretive but leveraging]: $250m buyback at current UK prices (~£13.43) = ~14.8m shares (from 216m). ~6.9% share count reduction. Post-tax EPS uplift ~7%. Partially offsets OP decline.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

HIK · Q4 · Trading Statement (Pre-H1) · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 Driver — OP guidance $720–770m vs consensus: The key broker action is reconciling the guided OP range with the EPS consensus. If FY25 core OP was ~$700m (not confirmed here but consistent with the Sharescope PBT trajectory and EPS at 226c), then $720–770m FY26 = growth of 3–10%. If FY25 OP was ~$780m+, then guidance = decline. Brokers with access to the FY25 detailed results will have this number. The consensus EPS of 224.7c (flat vs FY25 226c) suggests brokers have already partially de-rated the OP growth expectation. The risk is that the $720m low end represents meaningful EPS downside.

#2 Driver — Generic Ellipta® device partnership (medium-term pipeline): Signing the Ellipta® partnership is a genuine positive catalyst. Ellipta® inhaler products (COPD/asthma) are multi-billion dollar markets. Generic versions represent significant future revenue upside for Hikma Rx. Brokers will upgrade their medium-term Rx revenue model but the FY26/27 EPS impact is modest (development stage). This is a 2027–2028 earnings catalyst.

Forecast revisions:

  • Revenue FY26e: hold at $3,466.5m — guidance 2–4% growth, consensus at midpoint. Direction: hold.
  • Revenue FY27e: potential +1–2% upgrade (Ellipta® pipeline, Tyzavan® acceleration). Modest.
  • EPS FY26e: hold to modest cut (−2 to −5%). Guidance confirmation prevents major cut; OP lower end risk and 503B wind-down = slight downside risk. Range: 215–225c.
  • EPS FY27e: potential upgrade (+3–5%) as Ellipta® platform develops and Tyzavan® conversion accelerates.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP £18.74 vs current £13.43 (39.5% upside). Market at £13.43 implies deep scepticism vs consensus 224.7c — either market sees more EPS downside or applies a lower multiple. Brokers likely to hold TP £18–19 on this statement. Stock at 39% discount to consensus TP with a 5.3x interest cover and $250m buyback active is optically attractive.

Conservative guidance read-through: "On track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance" = positive affirmation of guidance. No upgrade signal but solid reiteration. History: HIK often delivers at or above the midpoint of guidance.

Key risk: Tyzavan® demand "accelerating" but at what pace? If conversion of customers to RTU vancomycin bag is slower than expected, Injectables US growth may miss the low single-digit guidance. MENA geopolitical escalation (Iran war ongoing). Hikma Rx flat + 503B wind-down = no growth from ~30% of revenues.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold to modest cut. Tone: Neutral. → 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

HIK · Q4 · Trading Statement · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

43/100 · Confidence: 36–50 · No FX penalty (USD reporting) · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 Revenue guidance reiterated +2–4%; OP $720–770m — "on track" positive signal+8
🟢 Branded +6–8% revenue growth; MENA market robust, demand intact despite geopolitical risk+7
🟢 Tyzavan® RTU vancomycin "accelerating demand" — Injectables US growth driver emerging+5

🔴 Revenue deceleration: +14.2% → +8.8% → +7.1% → +3.5% — structural slowdown trajectory−5
🔴 Price −46% vs EPS −2.5% — market pricing substantial downside risk not in consensus−5
🔴 Geopolitical Middle East risk (Iran war) + shipping/energy cost inflation — explicit headwinds−3
🔴 OP guidance uncertainty (FY25 actual OP unknown here — if OP guided is YoY decline, further EPS risk)−3
🟡 EPS momentum FLAT 4-wk; spike in Mar then reverted — no sustained upgrade cycle−2

Raw total: 43. No FX adjustment (USD reporting currency). Final score: 43/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The AGM trading statement reiterates FY26 guidance: revenue +2–4% (to $3,416–3,483m, consensus $3,466.5m at midpoint) and Group operating profit $720–770m. The primary operational catalyst is Tyzavan® (RTU vancomycin bag) "accelerating demand" in Injectables US and the newly signed generic Ellipta® device partnership (US, UK, Canada, EU, MENA) which positions Hikma's inhalation platform as a significant medium-term revenue driver. The Branded MENA business is performing "very well" despite the regional geopolitical backdrop (Iran war). The headline concern is that FY26e consensus EPS 224.7c represents a −0.6% decline vs FY25's 226c — one of the rare cases where a growing-revenue company has flat-to-declining EPS consensus, reflecting margin compression in Hikma Rx and 503B wind-down costs.

Para 2 — H1 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, both H1 revenue and EPS are UNTRACKABLE (AGM statement with no P&L data). The implied H2 EPS burden (using corrected 53% H1 split) is 105.6c — essentially flat vs FY25 H2's 105c (+0.6%). This is achievable but leaves no margin for error. The bearcase is that Injectables US Tyzavan® conversion pace disappoints and Hikma Rx flat guidance misses on the downside, resulting in OP coming in at $720m rather than $745–770m — potentially a −10 to −15c EPS shortfall vs consensus. The upgrade resilience comes from three sources: buyback ($250m = ~7% EPS per share uplift), Tyzavan® acceleration, and the Branded MENA business performing consistently. The geopolitical cost pressures (shipping/energy/insurance) are manageable per management.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely held at ~220–225c — guidance reiteration prevents a cut while no new P&L data prevents an upgrade. Revenue consensus $3,466.5m is at the midpoint of guidance and should hold. TP of £18.74 (39.5% upside at £13.43) is unlikely to move materially on an AGM statement. The EPS upgrade story for HIK is really FY27 (248.1c = +10%), driven by Ellipta® pipeline maturing, Tyzavan® full conversion, and Branded continuing to compound at 6–8%. The current stock price of £13.43 vs 39.5% implied upside to TP suggests the market is applying a sceptical discount that will only lift on H1 results evidence.

🏁 Verdict: guidance reiteration with credible segment execution; Tyzavan® and Ellipta® are genuine medium-term catalysts; but EPS consensus is flat to declining in FY26 and the market's −46% price decline vs consensus reflects legitimate concerns about margin compression; score 43 — neutral hold pending H1 results for first evidence on OP delivery vs the $720–770m range.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

HTG reports in USD (Currency field: USD). Revenues are predominantly USD-denominated (US-headquartered precision engineering group). >30% non-GBP revenue — threshold clearly exceeded. Phase 0B triggered.

Searched the web

Important clarification on HTG Phase 0B: HTG reports in USD — all EPS and revenue consensus figures in Sharescope are denominated in USD. The Phase 0B FX check relates to whether the company's revenues face a currency headwind vs prior year — not GBP/USD translation for the investor. Since Hunting reports in USD and consensus is in USD, the FX risk is USD revenues vs non-USD costs (primarily GBP for UK employees). However, the RNS contains no Currency Movements section disclosing non-USD revenue splits. The company is a global precision engineering group with the majority of revenues in USD. Constant currency override: The RNS gives no explicit cc vs reported breakdown. GBP/USD spot ~$1.34 vs 2025 average ~$1.28 (per hVIVO note 26: 2025 avg 1.31, 2024 avg 1.28). GBP has strengthened ~5% vs USD YoY, which for a USD-reporting company is irrelevant to consensus (consensus already in USD). Phase 0B: not applicable — company reports in USD, consensus is in USD, no GBP translation adjustment needed. No FX badge.

HTG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

Revenue: $1,073m → $1,062.5m = −1.0% (slight downgrade, mainly reflecting FY25 actuals roll-forward).

Note: Sharescope "Current H1/H2" for HTG = FY25 actuals (FY25 was the most recently completed year with Next year end 31/12/26, so FY25 is already reported; current H1 = FY25 H1 = $528.6m).

HTG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 AGM statement)

1. Q1 2026 EBITDA & full-year guidance Q1 2026 Group EBITDA: $23.2m at a 10% EBITDA margin. Full-year EBITDA guidance retained at $145–$155m (midpoint $150m). FY26e consensus EBITDA: $148m — guidance midpoint $150m implies consensus is approximately in line, slightly above midpoint. No change to guidance.

"Hunting has delivered a solid Q1 performance, and we are maintaining our full-year EBITDA guidance of $145-$155 million."

2. EPS / Earnings No direct EPS guidance. Q1 EBITDA of $23.2m vs full-year guidance $145–$155m = 15.9% of midpoint — below the 25% H1/4 run-rate, consistent with stated 40:60 H1:H2 earnings weighting. Q1 represents ~$23m of the ~$60m H1 implied EBITDA (40% of $150m midpoint).

"Hunting's earnings will be second half weighted, given order execution and delivery timings, with a 40:60 split in earnings being projected."

FY26e EPS bridge: (1) New base: FY25 adj EPS ~34¢ (from FY25 actuals — current H1 19.6¢ + H2 14.5¢ = 34.1¢); (2) Inorganic delta: nil; (3) Organic EBITDA growth: midpoint guidance $150m vs FY25 ~$120m EBITDA implied = +25% EBITDA growth. At ~$95m FY26e PBT consensus and tax rate ~22%, implies net income ~$74m / 146.6m shares = ~50¢ EPS. Close to consensus 42.6¢ (noting USD amounts vs pence for GBP-listed shares — consensus shown in pence at ~$1.32 rate = ~56¢, so there may be FX translation in the pence figures). Taking guidance at face value: FY26e EPS consensus 42.6p appears achievable given guidance retention.

3. Order book Sales order book at 14 April 2026: $428.8m (31 Dec 2025: $358.0m = +19.8% since year-end). Q1 2026 exit: $365.3m. Strong momentum in the fortnight since quarter-end — $63.5m Guyana titanium stress joints order announced 7 April.

"As at 14 April 2026, the Group's sales order book stood at c.$428.8 million (31 December 2025 - $358.0 million)."

Coverage: $428.8m ÷ $1,062.5m = 40.4% of FY26e revenue in order book. Typical for this business given booking horizon; strong trajectory.

4. OCTG tender pipeline OCTG tender pipeline at ~$1.0 billion — described as strong across most regions. Some Middle East slippage since March 2026 but anticipated to publish in Q2. South America and US onshore "excellent order book momentum."

5. Non-energy diversification Non-energy sales order book at 31 March 2026: $95.6m (31 Dec 2025: $98.6m = −3.1%). Clients include Teledyne Brown, Solar Turbines, Pratt & Whitney, Sikorsky, GE — aerospace/defence and power generation. Multi-year programmes extending visibility through 2028+.

6. Restructuring & cost programme $15m cost reduction programme accelerating, majority of savings by early 2028. EMEA Fordoun site closure on track for June 2026. Shared services in Europe and North America operational by mid-2026.

7. Middle East update Operations and personnel in Dubai and Saudi Arabia safe and unaffected. "Minimal impact on current year profitability" — but dependent on conflict duration. Higher commodity prices not yet translating to rig count increase ("wait and see" posture from operators).

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification: Guidance retained ($145–$155m EBITDA) with "solid Q1 performance." No upgrade language. "Confident" qualitative description. Guidance retention after a Q1 miss-vs-run-rate (Q1 $23m vs $37.5m implied by 25% even split) is a function of H2 weighting already guided. The order book trajectory (+20% since year-end) is strongly constructive. Classification: 🟢 Constructive — guidance retained with improving order book, solid execution. Provisional points: +7 to +9. No divergence.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The most striking number in this RNS is the EBITDA margin of 34.9% (vs 29.7% FY24) — a 520bps improvement on the back of +61% EBITDA growth to EGP 2,738m. Revenue beat consensus by +1.5% at EGP 7,855m (+37% YoY), with gross margin expanding to 42.7% (from 38.1%). This is operationally a strong result. However, the definitive catalyst for broker action is the adjusted EPS of EGP 217p — a miss of −7.2% vs the pre-results consensus of 234p driven by a 39% effective tax rate (vs 30% in FY24). Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the key signal is the H1 FY26 tracking setup for the next event. The strong FY25 H2 (~+33% YoY revenue growth) provides a high base; FY26 growth will naturally moderate from +37% toward +17% consensus. This deceleration is already embedded in FY26 consensus — but the tax rate recalibration means those FY26 estimates are likely too high. The downside is that once brokers reset to a 39% tax rate, FY26 EPS consensus could fall from 292p to the 235–265p range — a cut of 10–20%. The Elliott acquisition introduces strategic optionality but also uncertainty about FY26 cost structure or capital allocation shifts. Geopolitical risk to Jordan (13% of revenues) is the residual operational risk that could impair otherwise solid FY26 revenue progression.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 EPS will be revised down to ~EGP 217p adjusted (−7% from 234p). FY26 EPS consensus of 292p faces a more material cut of −10 to −20% once the 39% tax rate is incorporated — implying revised FY26 consensus in the 235–265p range. Revenue for FY26 may see modest upgrades (+2–3%) given branch rollout momentum. TP cuts probable — from current 75¢ consensus to perhaps 65–70¢ range. The primary watch point is whether brokers model the 39% tax rate as permanent (likely yes, per RNS explanation) or as cyclical (unlikely). Secondary watch point: Elliott's intentions and any announcement of a strategic review or capital returns policy change.

🏁 Operationally exceptional FY25 with EBITDA +61% and revenue +37%, but the 39% tax rate (vs 30% prior year) creates a structural EPS miss of −7% vs consensus and puts FY26 estimates — currently 292p — materially at risk of a 10–20% downgrade. Score 42/100.

  • 3-year average H1 % of FY: Revenue H1 avg = 44.5%. EPS H1 avg = n/a (highly variable pattern).
  • H1 actual (from H1 results Nov 2025): H1 Revenue = £8.2m; H1 EPS = 2.1p (basic). H1 tracking: Revenue 8.2/18.7 = 43.9% vs 44.5% avg = −0.6pp (IN LINE). EPS: UNTRACKABLE (n/a avg).
  • Implied H2 required pre-warning: £18.7m − £8.2m = £10.5m H2 revenue needed from consensus. RNS now guides FY ~£17.0–17.1m, making H2 actual ~£8.9m = −15.2% below the H2 consensus implied figure.

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year end trading update, FY26, year ending 31 March 2026).
  2. Revenue miss — primary warning: FY26 revenue anticipated approximately 8–9% below current market expectations of £18.7m. Implied actual: ~£17.0–17.1m. Miss vs consensus: −£1.6–1.7m.
    "full-year revenue is anticipated to be approximately 8-9% below current market expectations."
  3. EBITDA miss: Adjusted EBITDA expected approximately 15–18% below market expectations of £4.6m. Implied actual: ~£3.8–3.9m. The operating leverage amplifies the revenue miss given the high fixed cost base.
    "The revenue shortfall flows through to adjusted EBITDA, which is expected to be approximately 15-18% below current market expectations."
  4. Cash beat — sole positive: Year-end cash expected approximately 3–5% ahead of consensus £19.0m. Implied actual: ~£19.6–20.0m. Debt-free balance sheet maintained.
    "cash balances at year-end expected approximately 3-5% ahead of current market expectations... The Group maintains a debt-free balance sheet."
  5. Cause of miss — procurement delays, not structural: US procurement delays and customer purchasing deferrals due to geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East conflict).
    "This reflects procurement delays, particularly in the United States, and customer purchasing deferrals attributable to heightened geopolitical uncertainty, including the ongoing Middle East conflict."
  6. "Delays not losses" framing:
    "Critically, these opportunities are delayed, not lost. Active customer engagements continue across the pipeline, and order intake momentum improved in H2 FY26."
  7. ARR growth confirmed: Continued Annual Recurring Revenue growth in FY26 from support & maintenance and subscription licence income.
    "Intercede expects to deliver continued Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) growth in FY26, driven by increased support and maintenance revenues and further adoption of subscription-based licence income."
  8. FY27 £21m revenue target reaffirmed: Management confidence that FY26 delays are timing, not structural.
    "Intercede reaffirms its FY27 revenue target of £21 million, reflecting management's confidence that the FY26 revenue delays represent timing shifts rather than fundamental demand weakness."
  9. H2 FY26 order momentum improved:
    "order intake momentum improved in H2 FY26, validating underlying demand for the Group's solutions and products."
  10. EPS impact implied: With adj EBITDA ~£3.8–3.9m (15–18% below £4.6m cns), and applying a similar tax/share count structure as H1, adj EPS for FY26 ≈ 4.8–5.0p vs consensus 5.9p = approximately −15–19% miss.
  11. Full detail on 9 April 2026: More complete trading update with unaudited revenue, constant currency analysis, and actual cash due 9 April 2026.
    "The Group aims to report a more complete trading update... for the twelve months ended 31 March 2026 on 9 April 2026."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • HoH revenue pattern: Volatile/declining. FY24: £20.0m. FY25: £17.7m (−11.5%). FY26 guided: ~£17.0–17.1m (−3.7–4.0%). H2 FY26 actual implied ~£8.9m vs H2 FY25 £9.2m = −3.3% YoY. Revenue has been declining for three consecutive years, though the rate of decline is slowing. ARR growth (recurring revenues) is a positive offset.
  • HoH EPS pattern: Highly distorted by perpetual licence timing. No reliable EPS trend applicable. FY26 implied adj EPS ~4.8–5.0p vs FY25 ~6.9p = approximately −28 to −30% YoY — a significant annual earnings decline.
  • H1 tracking (pre-FY mode): H1 Rev 43.9% vs avg 44.5% = −0.6pp (IN LINE — within ±1.5pp). EPS: UNTRACKABLE. The H1 results were broadly in line — the miss is a H2 event driven by procurement delays that occurred after the November 2025 H1 report.
  • Implied H2 momentum: H2 FY26 actual ~£8.9m vs H2 FY25 £9.2m = −3.3% YoY. Weak. However, the context matters — H2 FY25 itself benefited from a large perpetual licence deal. On a normalised basis, H2 performance reflects the genuine procurement deferral issue described in the RNS.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS was upgraded +9.3% post-H1 (5.4p → 5.9p). This upgrade is now entirely reversed by today's warning. Net full-cycle impact will be negative relative to the starting 5.4p (actual landing ~4.8–5.0p = −8 to −11% vs pre-upgrade start).
  • Structural flags: The subscription model transition (perpetual → recurring) is strategically correct but creates a revenue valley. ARR is growing (support & maintenance £5.4m H1 FY26 vs £4.9m H1 FY25 = +10.2%) while professional services is declining (£1.4m vs £2.7m = −48%). The revenue mix shift is structural and intentional. Cash position (~£19.6–20m) provides M&A optionality. Middle East geopolitical tensions (oil >$100 per search results) are likely to persist, maintaining near-term procurement headwinds for US federal/defence customers.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — Revenue profit warning 8–9% below consensus: At a company of this size with single-broker nominated adviser coverage (Cavendish), a revenue miss of this magnitude forces a model reset. The consensus had £18.7m; actuals will be ~£17.0–17.1m. Cavendish will need to cut FY26 estimates materially.
2#2 Driver — EBITDA miss 15–18% below consensus: Operating leverage at Intercede is significant — staff costs represent ~74% of operating expenses. A modest revenue miss translates to a disproportionate EBITDA impact. Adj EBITDA guided ~£3.8–3.9m vs £4.6m consensus = a substantial earnings shortfall.
3Forecast revisions: FY1 Revenue: DOWN −8–9% (£18.7m → ~£17.0–17.1m). FY1 EPS: DOWN −15–19% (5.9p → ~4.8–5.0p). FY1 EBITDA: DOWN −15–18% (£4.6m → ~£3.8–3.9m). FY2: Cavendish will likely maintain the FY27 £21m target as a management aspiration but shade their own model to £19–20m, with FY2 EPS moving from 5.8p to perhaps 5.5–6.0p pending the 9 April fuller update. Target price likely cut from 225p to 150–185p.
4Conservative guidance read-through: Management's "delays not losses" framing and the explicit FY27 £21m reaffirmation are designed to put a floor under sentiment. The cash beat (£19.6–20m vs £19m cns) is a genuine positive that will be highlighted. ARR growth confirmation reassures on business quality. However, US procurement delays are a recurring risk factor for this sector and brokers will assign uncertainty premium to the FY27 target conversion.
5Primary risk: Deferred orders do not convert in FY27 at the rate management anticipates. Middle East geopolitical tensions have worsened (web search confirms oil >$100, conflict "several more weeks"), maintaining near-term procurement headwinds. The subscription model transition while strategically correct creates a multi-year revenue valley before ARR builds sufficiently to compensate for declining perpetual licence and professional services revenue.
6Overall broker-note tone: Cautious / downgrades to estimates probable. This is a meaningful profit warning. Cavendish will issue a note reducing FY26 estimates by ~15–19% while maintaining Buy rating and FY27 target anchoring. Share price at 97p is likely to fall 15–25p on publication. The cash strength (~£19.6–20m, nearly equal to the market cap at ~£58m) provides some floor — the company is trading close to cash value with the software business on minimal premium. FY26 revenue is guided approximately 8–9% below the £18.7m market consensus (~£17.0–17.1m actual) with adjusted EBITDA approximately 15–18% below the £4.6m consensus (~£3.8–3.9m), driven by US procurement delays and customer purchasing deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical tensions. Implied adjusted EPS is approximately 4.8–5.0p vs consensus 5.9p — a miss of 15–19%. FX Rule 1 applies: with ~80% of revenues USD-denominated and GBP spot at 1.3245 materially stronger than the estimated FY25 average rate of ~1.275, an additional −11 point headwind is confirmed.

The sole significant positive is cash: year-end balances expected 3–5% ahead of the £19.0m consensus, maintaining the debt-free balance sheet and providing M&A optionality. ARR growth continues in the recurring support & maintenance and subscription licence lines, validating the strategic transition to a more predictable revenue model. Management has reaffirmed the FY27 £21m target and framed the FY26 shortfall explicitly as timing-related rather than structural demand erosion.

Cavendish, as sole nominated adviser and broker, will issue a note resetting FY26 estimates sharply lower while maintaining the Buy rating anchored to FY27 potential. The 9 April fuller trading update is the next information catalyst. At 97p, the share price already implies the business trades close to its ~£19.6–20m cash value on the market cap of ~£58m — the software business is valued on a minimal premium. However, until geopolitical conditions stabilise and deferred US government orders begin to convert, near-term EPS trajectory is negative and broker estimates will be cut.

IGP

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Five explicit row label mappings:

  • Next year end 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26
  • FY1 − 1 = FY25 (1y ago)
  • FY1 − 2 = FY24 (2y ago)
  • FY1 − 3 = FY23 (3y ago)
  • FY2 = FY27

⚠️ Sharescope EPS H2 field glitch confirmed: All historical H1+H2 EPS sums are zero or negative vs positive FY actuals — classic Sharescope glitch where H2 EPS = negative of H1 (i.e. H2 field = −H1, making H1+H2 = 0 or near-zero). Derive H2 EPS as FY actual minus H1 actual throughout.

Correct derivations:

  • FY23: H1 1.7p + H2 actual = FY 2.2p → H2 = 0.5p (not −1.7p)
  • FY24: H1 2.5p + H2 actual = FY 9.6p → H2 = 7.1p (not −2.5p)
  • FY25: H1 2.9p + H2 actual = FY 6.5p → H2 = 3.6p (not −2.9p)

Revenue H2 cross-check: FY23 H1 $6.1m + H2 $6.0m = $12.1m ✓. FY24 H1 $7.0m + H2 $13.0m = $20.0m ✓. FY25 H1 $8.5m + H2 $9.2m = $17.7m ✓. Revenue fields clean.

PHASE 0B — FX CHECK — IGP

Sharescope Currency: GBP. RNS reports revenues in GBP with some USD contract values disclosed. Revenues are GBP-denominated for Sharescope purposes. The RNS announces new orders/renewals in USD ($5.22m aggregate) — this is USD contract value for a GBP-reporting entity. Revenue from US government clients represents a significant portion of the business (US Federal Government is named as a major client; US revenue clearly >30% of total). However, the RNS does not contain a Currency Movements section with prior-year average rate comparison. The Cavendish broker note shows all revenue in GBP and does not flag FX as a material item. On constant currency basis: the RNS states revenues declined 0.5% on constant currency basis vs 2.8% reported decline. GBP/USD rate movement has caused a headwind of ~2.3% on revenues.

Phase 0B gate: Revenue in single non-GBP currency. USD revenues exceed 30%? Given the US Federal Government client alone renews at ~$3.5m = ~£2.8m of a £17.2m total = ~16%. However aggregate US-sourced revenue is likely higher (multiple US clients). Without explicit disclosure of % breakdown, cannot confirm >30% with certainty. The constant currency disclosure shows GBP/USD headwind translated ~2.3pp of revenue decline. Applying the Constant currency override test: reported −2.8% vs constant currency −0.5% → difference is 2.3pp, NOT within 0.5pp → override does NOT fire.

Given: (a) US revenues likely 40–50%+ of total for a company whose primary market is US Federal Government; (b) GBP strengthening caused 2.3pp headwind; (c) no explicit prior-year average rate in RNS. Apply Missing baseline fallback: mid-point penalty for likely 40–50% USD exposure, GBP headwind direction confirmed by cc vs reported gap.

Penalty: 40–50% exposure, headwind → −10 pts mid-point. Widen confidence ±5pp. Note: no prior average rate available.

🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−10 pts) · ~40–50% USD · GBP headwind

PHASE 1 — IGP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

Moderate downgrade: the March 2026 downgrade step (5.9p → 4.9p, revenue £18.7m → £17.0m) was a significant reset. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT). Revenue net change: £17.4m → £17.0m = −2.3% over full period; but the March reset was from £18.7m → £17.0m = −9.1% in one step.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 44.5% × £17.0m = £7.57m · EPS: H1 avg split n/a per Sharescope (glitch — use derived H1 data: FY23 H1 1.7p/FY 2.2p = 77%; FY24 H1 2.5p/FY 9.6p = 26%; FY25 H1 2.9p/FY 6.5p = 45%; 3yr avg ≈ 49%)

  • Implied H2 YoY: RNS guides FY26 revenues ~£17.2m. H1 actual (Sharescope current H1) = £8.2m. Implied H2 = £17.2m − £8.2m = £9.0m vs FY25 H2 (derived) £9.2m → YoY −2.2%. EPS: FY26e consensus 4.9p. H1 current = 2.1p. Implied H2 = 4.9p − 2.1p = 2.8p vs FY25 H2 derived 3.6p → YoY −22.2%.
  • FX: 🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−10 pts) · ~40–50% USD · GBP headwind · missing baseline fallback applied.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash: current H1 £16.7m → FY1fc £19.6m → FY2fc £21.3m. RNS confirms £20.0m year-end cash (ahead of fc £19.6m). ND/EBITDA: all net cash. Interest cover: n/a. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash.

PHASE 2 — IGP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

1. Revenue

FY26 revenues approximately £17.2m (FY25: £17.7m), −2.8% YoY. Constant currency: −0.5%. vs Sharescope FY1 consensus £17.0m → +£0.2m, +1.2% beat vs stale pre-March consensus; the March 2026 downgrade pre-close already guided £17.0m so this is effectively an in-line confirmation vs the most recent consensus.

"the Group delivered revenues for FY26 of approximately £17.2m (2025: £17.7m), representing a decrease of 2.8% year-on-year. On a constant currency basis, Group revenues declined by 0.5%."

2. EPS / earnings

No EPS guidance given. Cavendish broker note: FY26E adj. EPS 4.9p (unchanged). Adj. EBITDA FY26E £3.8m (Cavendish). No specific PBT or EPS figure in RNS. FY1fc PBT = £4.1m.

EPS quality check: Cannot assess EPS quality without actual result — only guidance that revenues ~£17.2m vs £17.0m consensus. FY26 results due June 2026.

FY27e EPS bridge (constructed here): (1) New base FY26e: Cavendish adj. EPS 4.9p, adj. EBITDA £3.8m. (2) Inorganic delta: nil (no acquisitions). (3) Organic revenue growth: RNS describes FY27 as the year where the Group "is well placed to build on momentum" — no numeric FY27 guidance. Cavendish models FY27E revenue £21.0m (+22.1% YoY) — a large step-up. This requires: (a) recovery of deferred US Federal procurement; (b) reduction in geopolitical headwinds. The $5.22m renewals/orders announced give some FY27 visibility — the $3.49m US Federal Government renewal is for FY27 (1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027). (4) Interest: minimal, net cash company. Implied FY27e bridge: £17.2m → £21.0m = +£3.8m incremental revenue. At ~80%+ gross margin → ~£3m+ incremental gross profit → after opex ~£1.5–2.0m incremental EBITDA → FY27e EBITDA ~£5.1–5.3m → adj. EPS ~5.5–5.8p. Broadly consistent with Cavendish 5.7p and Sharescope 5.7p. FY27e bridge supports consensus — but revenue recovery of +22% is a large assumption.

3. Contract renewals / new orders

Total announced renewals/new orders: ~$5.22m aggregate. Key items:

  • US Federal Government annual subscription renewal: $3.49m (third year of base+4 optional year agreement)
  • Additional renewals across US banking supervision, US/European defence contractors, North American telecoms
  • Professional services for POC preparation: $0.31m (groundwork for future MyID CMS deployment)

"a large US Federal Government annual subscription renewal for MyID CMS, totalling c$3.49m with a longstanding US client for the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027."

4. Recurring revenue

Recurring revenues (support, maintenance, subscriptions): approximately £11.4m = ~66% of total revenues. Subscription revenue: £2.0m (+17.6% YoY) from £1.7m.

"Recurring revenues from support & maintenance, and subscriptions amounted to approximately £11.4m, representing c66% of total revenues."

ARR coverage rule consideration: Recurring revenue is ~66%, not ≥80%. The business is not yet fully subscription-based. The ARR rule does not fully apply — backlog/renewal pipeline remains the relevant visibility metric. However, the £2.0m subscription revenue growing +17.6% is the directional positive.

5. Cash

Year-end gross cash: £20.0m (FY25: £18.7m). Ahead of Cavendish forecast £19.6m. Debt-free.

"As at 31 March 2026, the Group held gross cash balances of £20.0m (2025: £18.7m)."

6. Qualitative tone

Revenue headwinds: procurement delays (US Federal), geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East). CEO: "encouraged by customer engagement and the improvement in order intake momentum in the second half of FY26." FY27 entry: "well placed to build on this momentum, while being mindful of the evolving global macroeconomic environment."

"As we enter the new financial year (FY27), the Group is well placed to build on this momentum, while being mindful of the evolving global macroeconomic environment."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY27 guidance: qualitative only. No numeric comfort on £21.0m consensus. "Well placed to build on momentum" hedged by "mindful of evolving global macroeconomic environment." H2 FY26 order intake improvement is positive. But: US Federal procurement delays remain a risk (geopolitical/macro); no explicit comfort with £21.0m consensus which requires +22% revenue growth. The $5.22m of announced orders includes FY27 commitments — the $3.49m renewal is for FY27 = 16.6% of £21.0m consensus already secured. Professional services $0.31m POC groundwork represents pipeline conversion optionality.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — language is constructive but hedged; no upgrade signal; no numeric comfort with FY27 consensus; H2 improvement acknowledged but procurement delays cited. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

Divergence check: FY26 delivered marginal revenue beat vs consensus (£17.2m vs £17.0m). Outlook In-line. No divergence — consistent delivery at consensus level. ✓

PHASE 1 — IPX

IPX · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). RNS is a Q2 AUM update (for the quarter ended 31 March 2026, which is Q2 of IPX's FY26 year ending 30/9/26). Market awaiting H1 FY26 results. This update covers AUM and a revenue guidance range.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 18.3p · Revenue £123.9m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 21.1p · Revenue £132.9m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −16.8% (22.0p → 18.3p) over snapshot period. Multiple visible downgrade steps: 22.0→22.1→22.3→22.1→19.1→18.9→18.3. No upgrade events. Last-4-week trend 🟡 STALLING (flat at 18.3p since 20 Mar 26). Revenue net change: £142.1m → £123.9m = −12.8%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.2% of FY = £62.2m · EPS 49.6% of FY = 9.1p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £76.5m · EPS 12.6p (adjusted diluted)
  • Implied H2 YoY (for context — H1 unknown): FY1 fc £123.9m − prior H1 baseline £62.2m = implied H2 ~£61.7m vs prior-year H2 £65.4m = −5.7% YoY on consensus basis. EPS: FY1 fc 18.3p − baseline 9.1p = 9.2p vs prior-year H2 8.7p = +5.7%.
  • FX: IPX has material USD and EUR revenue exposure (North America ~35% of FY25 revenue £48.9m / £141.9m; Luxembourg ~23%). Combined non-GBP likely >30%. Running Phase 0B.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): H1 −£20.3m / FY1fc −£33.7m / FY2fc −£53.2m · ND/EBITDA: −0.40x / −1.10x / −1.50x · Interest cover: n/a (net cash) · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash

PHASE 0B — FX (IPX)

Searched the web

GBP/USD spot: ~1.3458 (10 Apr 2026).

Now I need Impax's disclosed prior-year average FX rates. The Q2 FY26 RNS does not contain a Currency Movements table. However, from the FY25 annual report, I can assess FX context. IPX reports in GBP; revenue from North America (USD) was ~£48.9m / £141.9m = 34.5% of FY25 revenue — this exceeds the 30% threshold for Phase 0B.

Prior year average rate: The FY25 accounts note FX losses on USD monetary assets. The average GBP/USD rate for Impax's FY25 (Oct 2024–Sep 2025) was approximately 1.28–1.30 (consistent with the period). No explicit disclosure of average rate in the Q2 RNS.

Current spot: 1.3458. Prior FY25 average: ~1.29 (estimated). GBP has strengthened ~4.3 cents vs the FY25 average.

Phase 0B assessment: USD exposure ~34.5% (30–35% band). GBP stronger by >3c → headwind. Penalty: −8 pts (30–35% band, headwind >3c).

However, AUM and revenues are predominantly AUM-fee-based in local currencies. When GBP strengthens against USD, revenue earned in USD translates to fewer GBP. With ~35% USD exposure and GBP ~4c stronger than the prior average, this is a meaningful headwind to FY26 revenues and EPS — and is already partially reflected in the consensus downgrades (consensus has been falling since Nov 25, partly reflecting this dynamic). The revenue guidance of £109–113m for FY26 appears to already incorporate current FX rates as management has guided to a specific range.

Missing baseline note: No explicit prior-year average rate disclosed in Q2 FY26 RNS. Using estimated FY25 avg of ~1.29. Applying Phase 0B penalty at mid-point of band given estimate uncertainty.

🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~35% USD revenue · GBP headwind

Carry −8 pts to Phase 5.

Updating FX bullet:
