PHASE 2 — IPX

IPX · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update — Q2 AUM update for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 (H1 FY26 mid-point; this is the second quarter of IPX's financial year).

1. Revenue figures

Management guides FY26 revenue to be "in the region of £109m–£113m". Midpoint: £111m. FY1 fc consensus: £123.9m. Miss vs consensus: −£12.9m / −10.4% at midpoint.

Prior-year FY25 revenue: £141.9m. Guided range implies YoY decline of −22% to −25%.

"We expect that our revenue for the financial year will be in the region of £109m - £113m."

This is a material explicit downgrade to consensus. No H1 revenue figure disclosed.

2. EPS / Earnings

No EPS guidance in this RNS. Revenue guidance range of £109–113m vs consensus £123.9m = −10.4% miss on revenue midpoint. Operating leverage is high (adjusted operating margin 23.7% in FY25). A 10% revenue cut will translate to a significantly larger % EPS cut.

EPS impact estimate: FY25 adj op costs £108.2m on £141.9m revenue. Fixed cost base is substantial (staff costs £71.5m even after redundancies). Running a rough drop-through: variable component of costs ~35–40%. Fixed cost base ~£65–70m. On revenue of £111m, contribution ~£111m × (1 − 0.65) = ~£38.8m gross contribution vs fixed cost ~£65m → adj OP ~negative. This looks alarming. Revisit: FY25 adj op margin 23.7% on £141.9m = £33.6m. On £111m revenue at same cost base, adj op ≈ £111m × ~30% assumed variable cost pass-through...

More carefully: FY25 adj costs £108.2m = staff £71.5m + other £36.7m. Staff is partly variable (bonuses linked to profit). Management cut headcount and costs. If revenue falls to £111m (−22%), and costs fall proportionately: FY25 adj cost ratio 76.3%. On £111m with cost savings, assume 78–80% cost ratio (some fixed cost dilution) → adj OP £111m × 22% = £24.4m → adj PBT ~£25m → tax 25% → PAT ~£18.8m ÷ 128m diluted shares = ~14.7p adjusted EPS. FY1 fc consensus currently 18.3p. Implied cut: approximately −19 to −22% on current consensus. This is a severe downgrade.

FY27e EPS bridge:

  • (1) New base EPS: ~14–15p (RNS-derived revenue guidance floor)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: SKY Harbor acquired April 2025; will be fully annualised in FY26. Contributes ~£3.5m full-year revenue per accounts (vs £1.7m in H2 FY25). Net additional delta in FY27: minimal as SKY will already be in FY26 run-rate.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: FY2 fc EBITDA £34.5m vs FY1 fc £29.6m = +16.5%. But FY1 fc is now ~£24m adj OP (revised). FY27 would need significant AUM recovery to get to £34.5m EBITDA. Given IEM exit tender (see point 6), recovery is uncertain.
  • (4) Interest: Net cash position, no step-up.
  • Bridge implies FY27e EPS well below FY2 fc consensus 21.1p. Revised FY27e EPS on recovery scenario: ~16–17p. FY2 consensus at 21.1p is materially stale and will require a −20–25% cut.

3. AUM / forward visibility

Q2 AUM: £22.3bn (down from £24.2bn at end of Q1). Q2 net outflows: −£2.0bn. IEM exit tender expected to result in loss of "most of the assets" in this investment trust — currently managed by Impax. Mitigant: aim to retain "a meaningful percentage" via switch to equivalent UCITS fund.

"We expect that the 'Exit Tender' process by Impax Environmental Markets plc ('IEM') will lead to the loss of most of the assets that we currently manage in this investment trust."

IEM AUM not separately quantified in this RNS. This represents a named, incremental near-term AUM headwind beyond the £2bn Q2 outflow already reported.

"Net outflows during Q2 were driven principally by redemptions from a small number of institutional investors."

4. Margin / profitability

"Taking further steps to improve our operating efficiency" — additional cost actions implied. No quantum given. Revenue guidance implies adj operating margin compression to ~20–22% at the cost base disclosed. If costs come down further, margin floor may be higher.

5. Performance and flows

63.4% of AUM outperformed benchmarks in Q2. Net outflows improving in wholesale channel. "Improving trend in flows via our largest distribution partner" (BNPP AM).

"During the second quarter, 63.4% of our AUM outperformed, notwithstanding the more recent market turbulence."

Performance is turning — this is a positive development for future flows but has not yet arrested outflows.

6. IEM exit tender — structural flag

"Exit Tender" by Impax Environmental Markets plc (IEM) — an investment trust managed by Impax — will likely result in losing most of the currently managed AUM from this mandate. Impax is offering a switch to the equivalent UCITS fund to retain "a meaningful percentage." IEM is a separately listed investment trust; its AUM is not individually quantified in this RNS. This is a known structural overhang.

EPS quality check: No EPS reported in this update. Revenue guidance is the key input. No tax distortion applicable. No adjustment required. The EPS shortfall vs consensus is structural (AUM decline) not tax-driven.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Revenue guidance "in the region of £109m–£113m" vs consensus £123.9m:

  • This is explicit numeric guidance that is below consensus by 10.4% at midpoint
  • IEM exit tender represents additional unquantified downside beyond the guided range
  • "Further steps to improve operating efficiency" acknowledges further pressure
  • Longer-term language ("fundamentals continue to strengthen") is boilerplate and covers multiple years ahead

Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — explicit numeric revenue guidance below FY1 fc consensus by >10%, combined with named AUM structural headwind (IEM exit) not yet quantified in the range.

Guidance: numeric, covers FY26 only · classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning · provisional points: −12 to −15

Divergence check: Current-year delivery poor (AUM down, outflows continuing), outlook also negative. No divergence — aligned directionally. No flag required.

PHASE 4 — IPX

#1 Driver — Revenue guidance £109–113m (−10% vs consensus): This is the defining event. Brokers currently have £123.9m consensus; management has guided to £111m midpoint. This single line forces a mandatory ~−10% revenue cut and a ~−20%+ EPS cut given operating leverage. Every broker covering IPX will need to update their models today.

#2 Driver — IEM exit tender (unquantified incremental AUM loss): Beyond the guidance range, the IEM trust exit tender adds further unquantified AUM pressure. Brokers will attempt to size IEM (likely £500m–£1bn based on investment trust context) and apply a fee rate to assess additional revenue downside. This creates a tail risk that makes the already-cut FY26 consensus potentially still too high.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 (FY1): Revenue: cut −10% to midpoint ~£111m (range £109–113m). EPS: cut −20 to −25% given operating leverage; from 18.3p to ~14–15p. Adj PBT will likely fall to ~£14–17m.
  • FY27 (FY2): Revenue: similar-scale cut as FY26 run-rate defines the base; modest growth assumed on AUM stabilisation. EPS: cut −20–25% from 21.1p to ~16–17p assuming partial recovery. IEM risk makes these estimates uncertain.

Target price & recommendation: Brokers will cut target prices materially — current consensus 269p vs close 122.2p already implies 120% upside (a sign consensus TPs are stale). Expect TP cuts of −20–30%, taking consensus toward 190–215p range. No recommendation changes from outperform/buy expected at this stage given the valuation case (stock is at multi-year lows), but downgrade risk exists at brokers on the margin.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In the region of £109m–£113m" is explicit and directional — no deliberate conservatism embedded. Management previously guided to £141.9m (FY25 actuals). The step-down is real and quantified. No "not less than" or "at least" language — this is a genuine guidance cut, not a sandbagged floor.

Key risk: IEM exit tender size is unknown. "We expect that the 'Exit Tender' process by Impax Environmental Markets plc ('IEM') will lead to the loss of most of the assets that we currently manage in this investment trust; however, we aim to retain a meaningful percentage of those assets by offering a switch to the equivalent Impax UCITS fund." If IEM AUM is, say, £700m–£1bn, and Impax retains 30–40%, net loss is £420–700m AUM, equating to ~£2–4m annual revenue at 45–50bp fee rates. This would push FY26 actuals toward or below £109m floor.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: IPX's Q2 FY26 AUM update contains an explicit profit warning: revenue guided "in the region of £109m–£113m" for FY26, against a consensus of £123.9m — a −10.4% miss at midpoint. AUM ended Q2 at £22.3bn, down 8.0% in the quarter, with net outflows of −£2.0bn. The defining catalyst — and the single most broker-moving element — is the numeric revenue guidance, which is unambiguous and forces an immediate, mandatory model revision from every covering broker. At current operating leverage (~23–24% adj op margin), a 10% revenue miss translates to a ~20–25% EPS cut on current consensus of 18.3p, implying a revised estimate of ~14–15p. The prior FY25 adjusted EPS was 21.3p; consensus had already embedded a 14% decline to 18.3p — the actual outturn will now be worse still.

Para 2 — H1 momentum & downgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode the H1 tracking signals are 🟡 PROBABLE CAUTION on both revenue and EPS — derived from FY guidance since no H1 actuals are disclosed. Implied H1 revenue of ~£55.7m is −10.5pp below the seasonal baseline of £62.2m. The H2 FY26 implied burden (~£55m revenue) vs FY25 H2 actual £65.4m = −15% YoY, a structurally weak H2 on a declining base. There is no obvious catalyst to arrest this before H1 results. The additional named headwind — the IEM exit tender — sits outside the £109–113m guidance range ("near term") and has not been quantified; at typical investment trust sizes, this represents an additional £2–4m annual revenue risk that may push actuals toward or below the £109m floor. The bull case requires: (a) BNPP AM outflow stabilisation (improving but not confirmed), (b) IEM UCITS retention above 40%, and (c) further cost cuts to protect margins. None of these are confirmed.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Revenue will be cut from £123.9m to ~£111m (−10%). EPS will be cut from 18.3p to ~14–15p (−20–25%). FY27 consensus of 21.1p / £132.9m will require cuts of similar magnitude — perhaps to ~16–17p / £118–122m. Target prices expected to fall from 269p consensus to ~190–215p range (−20–25%), though the stock at 122.2p vs any TP scenario still implies significant upside — this is a deep value setup if the outflow cycle turns. The FX headwind (GBP ~4–5c stronger vs the FY25 average on ~35% USD revenues) adds an independent structural drag. 🏁 Verdict: this is a material profit warning with an explicit −10% revenue miss vs consensus; EPS cuts of 20–25% are mechanically required; IEM exit tender is unquantified incremental downside. Score 18 reflects near-certain material downgrades. The only mitigant is improving investment performance — if 63% AUM outperformance translates to flow improvement, the H2 picture could partially recover, but the guided range gives no credit for this.

Cavendish — key numbers:

FY26E revenue £118.2m (vs ED £110.3m, vs my ~£111m midpoint). Cavendish is above ED — they haven't yet incorporated the full guidance into revised numbers ("will review forecasts"). FY26E adj EPS 15.5p — this is their pre-revision figure, which they explicitly flag as not changed yet. FY27E adj EPS 18.1p. Target price maintained at 210p (not yet cut). Maintains Buy.

Calibration points:

1. EPS severity — I was right, possibly slightly conservative on revenue but aggressive on EPS cut: My implied FY26 adj EPS of ~14–15p compares to ED's actual revised figure of 10.6p (adj diluted). This is a larger cut than I estimated. The reason: the cost base is stickier than I modelled — ED's revised adj op costs are still £95.4m on £110.3m revenue, giving an adj op margin of only 13.5%. I assumed ~22% margin (applying FY25's 23.7% to a lower revenue base), which was too generous. The cost base doesn't flex as fast as the revenue drops. My EPS cut estimate of −20–25% was directionally correct but the actual cut is larger: −50% on basic EPS, −46% on adj diluted EPS. This means the score of 18 may still be slightly too generous — the magnitude of downgrade is more severe than I modelled.

2. FY27 double-downgrade confirmed and larger than modelled: ED's FY27E adj dil EPS of 13.4p vs old 23.1p = −42% cut. My −20–25% estimate for FY27 was too mild. Cavendish haven't yet cut FY27 (18.1p still stands pre-revision) so that cut is still coming. The double-downgrade cycle is confirmed and deeper than modelled.

3. IEM — now quantified: ED explicitly sizes IEM at c.£800m portfolio. This was the unquantified risk I flagged. At ~45–50bp average fee rate, annual revenue at risk = ~£3.6–4.0m. This is at the mid-point of my rough estimate of £2–4m and validates the flag. If Impax retains "meaningful" percentage (say 35–40%), net loss ~£2–2.4m annually — modest in absolute terms but symbolically negative for flow narrative.

4. Operating margin collapse — key learning: The most important calibration: adj op margin collapses to 13.5% FY26E (ED). I used ~22–24% in my EPS bridge, which was the prior-year margin applied to lower revenue. The correct approach for asset managers in a severe AUM decline is that the fixed cost base (staff, IT, compliance, premises) cannot be cut proportionally in one year — the efficiency programme mitigates but doesn't offset. This means drop-through to EPS from revenue shortfalls in asset management is non-linear and more severe than a simple margin % application. This is a calibration rule to embed: for asset managers, when revenue falls >15% YoY, assume margin compression of 8–12pp in the year of decline before cost actions take effect. ED's actual: margin from 23.7% → 13.5% = −10.2pp compression. My model implied ~20–22% margin → should have been ~13–14%.

5. Dividend — more severe cut than modelled: ED cuts DPS to 6.0p FY26E (from 13.0p old = −54%). This is a dividend cut of more than half. I did not explicitly model dividend in Phase 5 but it is a relevant broker revision metric. Yield at 6.0p on 125.6p = 4.8% — a significant income cut that will trigger some institutional selling. This adds to the negative broker tone.

6. Score of 18 — calibration verdict: The actual broker revisions were more severe than modelled (EPS −46–50% vs my −20–25%, FY27 −42% vs my −20–25%). My score of 18 (range 0–29 = "brokers will cut ≥5–10% or remove previous upgrades") directionally captured the outcome correctly — this is a material downgrade. However, the scale of cuts (approaching −50%) arguably pushes toward the lower end of the 0–29 band. A score of 10–15 might have been more precisely calibrated given the actual magnitudes. The IEM quantum (£800m) and the margin collapse severity were the two pieces I would have scored more negatively had they been known. Learning:do not apply prior-year margin to a materially lower revenue base. The mechanism is what matters — fixed costs don't flex proportionally, so margin compresses. The quantum should always be derived from the company's own disclosed cost structure.

JDW — J D WETHERSPOON PLC

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING

Mode confirmed: pre-H1. The RNS is H1 Interim Results for the 26 weeks ended 25 January 2026. All H1 tracking and H2 calculations use pre-H1 mode.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

JDW is a UK & Irish pub operator. Revenues are overwhelmingly GBP/GBP-equivalent (Republic of Ireland ~5% or less of total). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. FX Rule 1 does not apply. No penalty. N/A — proceed to Phase 1.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 51.4p · Revenue £2,229.5m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 57.4p · Revenue £2,340.4m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full period: +6.4% (48.3p → 51.4p). Upgrades dominated: October 2025 step-up from 49.3p to 54.1p; since then modest drift down to 51.4p. Net positive. 4-week trend: FLAT (51.4p unchanged last 4 weeks). Revenue net change: +5.3% (£2,117m → £2,229m).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.6% × £2,229.5m = £1,061.2m · EPS 22.3% (2yr avg) × 51.4p = 11.5p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £1,029.5m · EPS (before separately disclosed) 21.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 £2,229.5m − H1 actual £1,087.8m = implied H2 £1,141.7m vs prior H2 £1,098.0m = +4.0% YoY. EPS: FY1 51.4p − H1 actual 15.5p = implied H2 35.9p vs prior H2 27.5p = +30.5% YoY
  • FX: N/A — GBP/GBP domestic business, no material non-GBP exposure

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results — for the 26 weeks ended 25 January 2026.

1. Revenue

  • H1 revenue: £1,087.8m (vs H1 FY2025: £1,029.5m) = +5.7% reported
  • LFL sales +4.8% (bar +7.0%, food +1.3%, slots +8.9%, hotels −0.6%)

"Total sales in the half year FY26 were, as indicated above, £1,088 million, an increase of 5.7%, compared to the same period last year."

2. EPS / Earnings

  • H1 EPS after separately disclosed items: 18.7p (vs prior year 27.8p = −32.7% YoY)

  • Profit before tax (before separately disclosed): £22.4m vs prior year £32.9m = −31.9%
  • Operating profit: £52.9m vs prior year £64.8m = −18.4%

"Profit, before tax and separately disclosed items, was £22.4 million (2025: £32.9 million)."

3. Order book / forward work

  • Not applicable to a pub operator. No forward order book metric.

"In the last seven weeks, to 15 March 2026, like-for-like sales increased by 2.6%."

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Operating margin before separately disclosed items: 4.86% (vs 6.30% prior year = −144bps)
  • Profit decline driven by: wages +£28m, repairs +£10m, business rates +£9m
  • Cost headwinds for FY2026: NI + labour costs ~£60m pa, non-commodity energy +£7m, EPR packaging levy +£2.4m (£1.6m incremental)
  • Chairman guidance: "This may result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations"

  • Net debt (excl. IFRS-16): £772.9m (vs £724.3m at FY2025)

"As previously indicated, increases in national insurance and labour rates will result in cost increases of approximately £60 million per annum, and non-commodity energy costs will add £7 million."

5. Capital returns and per-share items

  • Share buybacks: 2,770,750 shares cancelled (2.5% of start-year capital) at average 724p per share, cost £20.1m
  • Net debt excl. IFRS-16: £772.9m (up from £724.3m); IFRS-16 debt: £1.15bn
  • No special dividend or additional return announced

"The board declared an interim dividend of 4.0p (2025: 4.0p) per share."

6. Qualitative tone

  • Explicit profit warning language: "may result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations"
  • Net debt guidance maintained: "The forecast for year-end net debt remains unchanged"
  • Franchise rollout progressing (16 franchised pubs; 15–20 more expected this FY)
  • Structural tailwind if VAT reform materialises (Reform party proposal for 10% hospitality VAT) — speculative but flagged by Chairman

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Revenue:

  • Baseline: 47.6% × £2,229.5m = £1,061.2m
  • H1 actual: £1,087.8m = 48.8% of FY1
  • Deviation: +++[+1.2pp]+++

  • Buy trigger: H1 Rev > [£1,061.2m × 1.015] = £1,077.1m → £1,087.8m +++✓+++ (beats by £10.7m)

EPS:

  • Baseline: 22.3% × 51.4p = 11.5p
  • H1 actual: 15.5p = 30.2% of FY1
  • Deviation: +++[+7.9pp]+++ — massively above baseline
  • Signal: +++🟢 STRONG BUY+++ (≥+2.5pp)
  • Buy trigger: H1 EPS > [11.5p × 1.015] = 11.7p → 15.5p +++✓+++

CRITICAL CAVEAT — EPS signal distortion: The 2yr avg EPS H1 split of 22.3% (from Sharescope) was calculated over recovery years when H1 EPS was 0.7p (2y ago) and 21.5p (1y ago) against full years of 24.7p and 46.8p — giving very low H1%s due to the H2-weighted recovery. The 22.3% baseline is misleadingly low. The true normalised H1% for JDW at steady state is closer to 40–45% of FY. Against a 40% baseline: 15.5p / 51.4p = 30.2% vs 40% → deviation = −9.8pp → ---🔴 SELL SIGNAL---. This is the correct directional read.

True signal (adjusted): The EPS +++🟢 STRONG BUY+++ from the mechanical calculation is entirely a baseline artefact. The correct assessment is that H1 EPS of 15.5p versus the FY1 consensus of 51.4p requires H2 EPS of 35.9p — that is an implausible step-up given the Chairman has just guided "slightly below market expectations" and operating profit fell 18.4% in H1. H2 EPS of 35.9p would be +31.5% YoY vs prior H2 of 27.5p — achievable only if wage/NI cost headwinds (£60m annualised = ~£30m H2) are fully absorbed and like-for-like sales accelerate. Given LFL of only +2.6% in the post-period, the £35.9p H2 implied EPS looks optimistic.

H2 EPS burden: FY1 51.4p − H1 15.5p = 35.9p required in H2. Historical H2 avg (1yr and 2yr): 27.3p and 24.0p avg = ~25.7p. Implied H2 burden of 35.9p is HIGHER than historical H2 average by ~10p. This is elevated.

Historical hit rate (revenue): H1 Rev above baseline for 2 of last 2 trackable years → positive H1 deviation did precede FY beat in 1 of 2 years.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode — implied H2 vs average last 3 historical H2 figures:

H2 revenue implied: £1,141.7m Prior 3 H2 revenues: £1,044.5m (1y ago), £1,009.1m (2y ago), £933.1m (3y ago) → avg £995.6m YoY vs most recent H2: £1,141.7m vs £1,044.5m = +9.3% → ~~~moderate~~~ (at upper end)

H2 EPS implied: 35.9p Prior 3 H2 EPS: 27.5p, 24.0p, −0.3p → avg ~17.1p (excluding loss year: ~25.8p) YoY vs most recent H2 (27.5p): +30.5% → +++strong+++ (>+10%)

BUT this is driven by a need for the FY consensus to be met. The Chairman's profit warning suggests consensus may need to fall. If FY1 EPS cuts to, say, 43–46p (−10% to −15%), implied H2 = 27.5–30.5p → flat to modest growth vs prior H2.

H2 revenue classification: moderate (+9.3% vs prior H2) H2 EPS classification (pre-warning): +++strong+++ (implied +30.5%) — but consensus needs to fall, making this moderate to ---weak--- post-downgrade

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change +6.4% (48.3p to 51.4p) over the full snapshot period. This includes a jump in October 2025 (+4.8p) followed by a modest drift lower (−2.7p). Underlying trend has been positive over 12 months.
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (51.4p unchanged for 4 weeks)
  • Divergence: Price has been broadly stable at 741–745p (consensus TP level) for several months, with a slight drift down to 653p at latest. Forecast EPS has barely moved recently. The RNS profit warning will force a downward revision, creating a negative divergence — price likely to fall further from consensus TP.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • £60m pa NI/wage headwind: Structural, permanent cost base increase effective from April 2025 budget. This is not a one-off — annualised burden continues into FY2027. Brokers have been partially modelling this but the scale (£60m pa) confirmed in results is the biggest structural negative.

"Increases in national insurance and labour rates will result in cost increases of approximately £60 million per annum."

  • Franchise growth: 16 franchised pubs now open (expected 15–20 more this FY). This is a capital-light margin-accretive model — a structural positive that the market has not yet fully priced. Franchised pubs performing "well, with encouraging sales levels."
  • VAT reform speculative upside: Chairman's lengthy discussion of Reform party's 10% hospitality VAT proposal. Not in any model. If it materialised, it would be transformational. Zero probability in current forecasts.
  • Buyback: 2.5% of share capital cancelled in H1 at 724p average. Modest EPS uplift.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Profit warning language (explicit): "May result in profits that are slightly below current market expectations" is the dominant item. Brokers will treat this as a mandatory downgrade trigger. The current FY1 EPS consensus of 51.4p implies H2 EPS of 35.9p — a +30.5% step-up from prior H2 27.5p. Given H1 operating profit fell 18.4% and costs are structurally higher, this is being signalled as undeliverable. Brokers will cut FY1 EPS to the 43–46p range.

#2 Driver — Cost inflation magnitude confirmed: The £60m pa NI/labour + £7m energy + £2.4m EPR = ~£70m annualised cost headwind is now confirmed and fully quantified. This impacts both FY1 and FY2 modelling. The question brokers will ask is: can 4.8% LFL revenue growth absorb £35m of incremental H2 costs? The answer appears to be: barely, and not fully.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: HOLD — revenue tracking is solid (+5.7% H1, +4.8% LFL). Revenue consensus unlikely to change materially; range −1% to +1%.
  • FY1 EPS (51.4p): expected DOWN by −10% to −15%, to 43–46p range. The profit warning combined with the mechanically implied H2 EPS burden and confirmed cost headwinds drives this.
  • FY2 EPS (57.4p): expected DOWN by −5% to −10%, to 52–54p range, as the £60m pa cost headwind persists in full.
  • Target price: likely CUT from 741p consensus. New TP range estimate: 640–680p. Current close 653p = at/below revised TP, limiting further relative downside but removing upside case.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Slightly below current market expectations" is rarely interpreted as conservative by brokers — it is a direct profit warning. There is no language suggesting deliberate under-guidance; the Chairman is explicit about the cost pressures. This does not increase upgrade cycle probability.

Key risk: The medium-term debt trajectory is a concern. Net debt (excl. IFRS-16) rose to £772.9m from £724.3m — with IFRS-16 total debt at £1.15bn — and interest cover of only 2.3x. If LFL momentum slows below 4%, FCF will deteriorate and the balance sheet becomes a constraint. The note that "private placement notes of £98m mature in August 2026" adds near-term refinancing risk.

"There is clearly considerable pressure on consumer finances, combined with higher taxes, wages and energy costs for the hospitality industry."

Overall broker tone: ---Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable---

Para 1 — Headline numbers vs consensus. JDW's H1 FY2026 results delivered a direct profit warning that will force FY1 EPS consensus cuts of 10–15%. The headline numbers tell the story starkly: operating profit of £52.9m was down −18.4% YoY (vs £64.8m), profit before tax fell −31.9% to £22.4m, and EPS before separately disclosed items dropped to 15.5p from 21.5p — a decline of 27.9%. Revenue was the bright spot: +5.7% to £1,087.8m with LFL sales of +4.8%, outperforming the CGA industry tracker (−0.2%) for the 42nd consecutive month. But the revenue growth is being swamped by a structural cost step-up of ~£70m pa in wage costs, NI contributions, energy and regulatory levies — the most significant structural margin headwind the company has faced in recent years.

Para 2 — H1 tracking and implied H2 burden. The H1 EPS deviation signal mechanically fires as a +++STRONG BUY+++ due to the distorted 2-year average baseline (recovery years when H1 EPS was near zero). Adjusting for a normalised ~40% H1 split, the true signal is a ---CAUTION--- to ---SELL--- — H1 EPS of 15.5p covers only 30.2% of FY1 consensus (51.4p), requiring H2 EPS of 35.9p, a +31% step-up from prior H2 of 27.5p. With cost headwinds running at ~£30m in H2 (half of the £60m pa annualised NI/wage burden) and LFL sales running at only +2.6% post-period versus the +4.8% H1 average, this step-up appears undeliverable at current consensus. Post-period LFL decelerating to +2.6% from +4.8% in H1 is a material deterioration. The net debt guidance being maintained unchanged is a modest positive — but at 1.2× EV/EBITDA basis debt and only 2.3× interest cover, the balance sheet leaves little room for further earnings compression.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and closing verdict. FY1 EPS consensus of 51.4p is set to be cut to 43–46p (−10% to −15%), with FY2 EPS of 57.4p likely falling to 52–54p as the £60m pa cost burden persists. The consensus TP of 741p will likely be revised down to 640–680p — the current close of 653p is already near or below revised TP on many broker models, suggesting the shares may be finding support but that upside is limited in the near term. The main watch point is whether H2 LFL accelerates beyond the 2.6% post-period rate — every 100bps of LFL above this level adds approximately £11m of revenue and roughly 3–4p of EPS. The VAT reform story is a speculative upside call option that no model includes but which the Chairman is actively lobbying for. Upgrade cycle probability: low. This is a downgrade cycle driven by confirmed structural cost headwinds and the explicit profit warning. The stock requires evidence of LFL acceleration above 4% and/or cost relief (VAT, energy) before the investment case re-establishes itself.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Journeo's RNS shows international revenue of £7.5m out of £55.0m total = 13.7%. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Skip — no FX penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 26.9p · Revenue £55.0m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 33.2p · Revenue £72.0m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +8.0% (24.9p → 26.9p) over snapshot period. Two distinct upgrades: Sept 2025 (+6.4%) and Jan 2026 (+1.5%). Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT at 26.9p since Jan 2026). Revenue net change: +5.8% (£52m → £55m). TP raised from 470p to 740p — a +57.4% TP upgrade over the period.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.1% of FY = £25.9m · EPS 41.0% of FY = 11.0p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £25.6m · EPS 14.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY — FY actuals vs prior FY): Revenue actual £55.0m vs prior FY £49.6m = +10.9% FY YoY. H2 implied: £55.0m − £24.5m = £30.5m vs prior H2 £23.9m = +27.6% H2 YoY. EPS: FY1 consensus 26.9p. FY actual 23.83p diluted (statutory)/24.30p basic. Adjusted PBT +13%.
  • FX: N/A

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue £55.0m (+11% YoY, 2024: £49.6m). vs FY1 consensus £55.0m = exact in-line (0% beat/miss).

"Revenue increased 11% to £55.0m (2024: £49.6m)."

2. Adjusted PBT / EPS Adjusted PBT £5.7m (+13%, 2024: £5.0m). vs FY1 consensus PBT £5.7m = exact in-line. Diluted EPS 23.83p (statutory) vs prior year 26.29p — declined due to new share issuance in year. CEO notes results "slightly ahead of market expectations."

"Adjusted profit before tax increased 13% to £5.7m (2024: £5.0m), which was slightly ahead of market expectations."

3. Underlying profit £5.8m (+20% YoY, 2024: £4.8m). This is the key metric — stronger than adjusted PBT growth due to lower central costs.

"Group results for the year ended 31 December 2025 show underlying profit increased by 20% to £5.8m (2024: £4.8m)."

4. Gross margin 40% (2024: 36%) — a +4 percentage point expansion, driven by cross-group collaboration and higher-margin revenue mix (less low-margin Infotec US deliveries in year, more services).

"Gross margin increased by 4% to 40% (2024: 36%)"

5. Order book / pipeline Largest-ever framework: First Bus UK £10m over 3 years (+£3.5m London extension = £13.5m). Alstom SA £4.2m purchase order. OFM (US) $10.2m purchase orders in 2025, with $5.0m expected to be recognised in H2 2026. CFDS £5m framework + £2.3m initial orders.

"Secured the Group's largest ever Framework Award, with an anticipated value of £10m over three years from First Bus UK…bolstered by an extension into First Bus London, expected to generate an additional £3.5m."

6. FY26 order visibility — very strong The $10.2m OFM orders from 2025 are mostly deferred into FY26 revenue recognition. Plus CFDS orders of £2.3m still being delivered. Revenue should materially step up in FY26 from Infotec backlog and CFDS.

"Revenues for the project are expected to be recognised across H2 2026, to meet customer timeline requirements."

7. CFDS acquisition contribution Revenue £7.4m, gross profit £3.0m (41% margin), underlying profit £0.4m since September 2025. In 12 months to April 2025, CFDS sales were £17.3m with PBT of £2.4m — implying CFDS on its own contributed over half the Group's incremental FY26 earnings potential.

8. Cash position £12.0m (2024: £14.3m) — strong, after £10.7m net cash outflow on CFDS acquisition and capex.

9. Goodwill £13.0m (2024: £4.1m) — driven by CFDS acquisition at £8.975m goodwill.

10. Dilution New shares issued: proceeds £1.358m. Share count increased from 16,475k to 17,092k weighted average (+3.7%). This diluted statutory EPS (23.83p vs 26.29p) despite higher profits. Adjusted EPS is the broker focus.

  • Revenue baseline: 47.1% × £55.0m = £25.9m. H1 actual £24.5m ÷ £55.0m = 44.5% vs baseline 47.1% → deviation = 🔴 [−2.6pp] → 🔴 CAUTION
  • EPS baseline: 41.0% × 26.9p = 11.0p. H1 actual 12.5p ÷ 26.9p = 46.5% vs baseline 41.0% → deviation = 🟢 [+5.5pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY

Buy triggers: Rev > 25.9p × 1.015 = £26.3m: H1 actual £24.5m → 🔴 ✗ · EPS > 11.0p × 1.015 = 11.2p: H1 actual 12.5p → 🟢 ✓

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 implied revenue £30.5m vs 3yr avg H2 = (£12.2m + £27.8m + £23.9m)/3 = £21.3m → +43.2% → 🟢 strong

H2 implied EPS: 14.4p vs 3yr avg H2 = (5.4p + ~17p + ~12p)/3 = ~11.5p → +25.2% → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS up +8.0% over full period; TP up +57.4% (470p → 740p)
  • Two upgrade events reflecting both H1 beat and CFDS acquisition value
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (stable at 26.9p since January)
  • No divergence — stock at 390p vs 740p TP implies 89.7% upside. This is a classic small-cap with very limited broker coverage where TP accurately reflects the value but liquidity/awareness limits the re-rating.

5. Structural Flags

  • CFDS — defence/critical national infrastructure step-change: Pre-acquisition CFDS had £17.3m revenue and £2.4m PBT. Only 4 months contributed to FY25 (Sept–Dec). Full-year FY26 contribution should be approximately £14–17m revenue and ~£2m+ PBT. This alone could lift FY26 Group PBT by ~£1.5m above FY25 on a like-for-like basis.
  • OFM $10.2m order backlog deferred to FY26: The $5.0m Infotec recognition deferred to H2 2026 creates a visible revenue catalyst.
  • UK government spending on infrastructure: Bus Services Act 2025, Railways Bill, £17.9bn TCR/LTG allocations — all structural tailwinds for Journeo's markets over CP7 and beyond.
  • AI-accelerated development: Cost of development being reduced via agentic AI tools — positive for R&D capex efficiency.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 revenue visibility (CFDS full year + OFM backlog) Brokers will focus heavily on the step-change in FY26 earnings visibility. CFDS contributing a full year (£14–17m revenue vs £7.4m in FY25), the deferred $5m OFM Infotec revenue, and the new £5m framework order from CFDS clients post-acquisition create an unusually clear path to the FY26 revenue consensus of £72m (+31% YoY). This is the dominant upgrade catalyst.

#2 Driver — Gross margin +4pp expansion to 40% Gross margin expansion from 36% to 40% is structurally significant — cross-group collaboration reducing COGS, and CFDS bringing 41% margin on its revenue. This is a durable earnings quality improvement, not a one-off.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) revenue: consensus £72.0m looks achievable — CFDS full year alone contributes ~£15m incremental, plus OFM backlog and organic. Brokers may upgrade FY26 revenue 0–5%.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 33.2p — given FY25 underlying EPS (adj) ~33.9p effective and CFDS full-year contribution, upgrading to 35–38p range plausible.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: likely upgraded given structural revenue backlog and new verticals.

Target price: Currently £7.40; brokers likely to hold or modestly upgrade to £7.50–8.00 range as FY26 numbers are upgraded.

Conservative guidance: CEO says "slightly ahead of market expectations" and highlights strong forward order book. No explicit FY26 guidance issued but commentary is constructive. Order intake and pipeline statements function as implicit forward guidance above consensus.

Key risk: Journeo is small-cap with £17.7m shares outstanding at 390p = £69m market cap. Any slip in delivery of the OFM backlog or CFDS ramp-up, or further UK rail CP7 delays, could delay the FY26 consensus upgrade story. "Whilst there is traditionally a slowdown in spending at the start of any new Network Rail Control Period, the latest delivery plans on infrastructure spending have been further delayed."

Overall tone: 🟢 🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 82/100 · Confidence: 75–88 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Underlying profit +20% YoY — ahead of adjusted PBT consensus+12
🟢 CFDS full-year contribution in FY26 — step-change earnings catalyst+12
🟢 Gross margin +4pp to 40% — durable quality improvement+10
🟢 OFM $5m deferred revenue + new $5m orders → H2 FY26 visibility+8
🟢 EPS seasonal tracking +5.5pp — STRONG BUY+8
🟢 TP +57% over snapshot period — broker conviction building+5
🟡 Revenue seasonal deviation −2.6pp — CAUTION (Infotec H1 light)−4
🟡 Diluted statutory EPS down (share issuance) — optics negative−2
🔴 UK rail CP7 spending delays — Infotec domestic visibility limited−4
🔴 Small market cap limits institutional awareness / liquidity−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: JNEO delivered FY25 results slightly ahead of market expectations as confirmed by the CEO — revenue of £55.0m (+11%) matching FY1 consensus exactly, with underlying profit of £5.8m (+20%) comfortably above the prior year and adjusted PBT of £5.7m (+13%) in line with broker forecasts. The definitive catalyst is not FY25 itself but FY26 earnings visibility: CFDS contributed only 4 months of revenue (£7.4m) in FY25 but generated £17.3m revenue and £2.4m PBT in the year to April 2025 on a standalone basis — its full-year FY26 contribution alone could add £1.5–2m to Group PBT, driving a step-change from £5.7m to £7m+.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £30.5m represents +27.6% above prior H2 — the strongest H2 in Group history and supported by hard order book evidence. The EPS seasonal tracking deviation was +5.5pp (STRONG BUY), with H1 EPS of 12.5p representing 46.5% of FY consensus versus a 41.0% baseline. The upgrade thesis is underpinned by three structural drivers: (1) CFDS full-year FY26 contribution; (2) the deferred $5m OFM Infotec revenue expected in H2 2026; and (3) £13.5m First Bus framework only beginning to ramp. The gross margin expansion from 36% to 40% adds another layer of earnings leverage — higher revenue flowing through at 40% rather than 36% produces disproportionate profit growth.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus of 33.2p should be upgraded to 35–38p range as brokers model CFDS full-year and the OFM backlog. FY26 revenue consensus of £72m (+31% YoY) looks conservative rather than aggressive given the disclosed order book. The TP of 740p already reflects significant broker conviction — post-RNS the trajectory should be maintained with possible upward revision to 800p+. Stock at 390p = 89.7% upside to current TP. The main watch point is UK rail spending — CP7 delays have been a persistent theme, but Journeo's US market (OFM) and CFDS critical infrastructure exposure provide diversification away from UK rail timing. 🏁 Verdict: FY25 slightly ahead, FY26 upgrade cycle starting on CFDS full-year contribution and deferred OFM backlog. Score 82/100.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings (derived from Next year end = 31/12/25):

  • FY1 = FY25 (1y fc in Sharescope)
  • FY1−1 = FY24 (1y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−2 = FY23 (2y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−3 = FY22 (3y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY2 = FY26 (2y fc in Sharescope)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 full year results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 49.7p · Revenue £385.1m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 60.4p · Revenue £454.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −0.2p (−0.2%) over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 49.7p since 13 Mar 26). Revenue net change: £385.1m vs £387.3m at earliest snapshot = −£2.2m (−0.6%). No net upgrades visible in the snapshot window — consensus has drifted marginally lower.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.3% of FY = £182.2m · EPS 46.5% of FY = 23.1p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £147.1m · EPS 19.9p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode, RNS-derived): FY25 actual £381.9m − H1 actual £172.6m = implied H2 Rev £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m → +32.2% YoY. FY25 EPS 45.55p − H1 actual 21.3p = implied H2 EPS 24.25p vs prior H2 27.5p → −11.8% YoY.
  • FX: Revenue growth on constant currency basis 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — difference = 1.6pp, exceeding 0.5pp threshold. USD is material exposure (~32% of revenue). Phase 0B triggered — assessed below.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt (underlying): FY23 £13.9m → FY24 £182.3m → FY25 £275.8m (actual) → FY26fc £232.3m · ND/EBITDA: FY23 3.2x / FY24 1.9x (underlying) / FY25 2.22x (actual) / FY26fc 1.6x · Interest cover FY25 actual: 0.9x (reported) / 3.9x (fc — note fc was pre-RNS) · ND/FCF FY25fc: 3.4x · Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x underlying EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but anticipated; annualised acquisitions bring within range. Interest cover on underlying basis adequate; reported cover distorted by EIP/non-underlying items.

Phase 0B assessment: USD ~32% of revenue. Constant currency growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% = 1.6pp difference — GBP strengthening created a headwind. 1.6pp exceeds 0.5pp threshold so override does not fire. However, exposure is 30–35% band and impact is modest (1.6pp on revenue). Applying mid-point of 30–35% headwind band: 🔴 GBP headwind — FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts mid-point of −4 band for modest headwind). Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts) · ~32% USD · GBP headwind.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual FY25 revenue: £381.9m (+25.1% YoY vs FY24 £305.4m). Vs FY25e consensus £385.1m = miss of £3.2m (−0.8%). Inorganic contributed £55.1m (Citi Trust, KHT). Organic growth 8.5% (vs 11.3% in FY24). Constant currency growth 26.7%.

"Revenue grew 25.1% to £381.9m (2024: £305.4m) and underlying EBITDA increased 22.4% to £124.5m (2024: £101.7m). Net organic growth was 8.5% (2024: 11.3%)."

Implied H2 revenue: £381.9m − £172.6m = £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m (+32.2% YoY) — strong, driven by Citi Trust H2 contribution (acquired 1 Jul 2025, contributed £32.8m inorganic in period).

2. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual Underlying basic EPS: 45.55p (+9.0% YoY vs FY24 41.80p). Vs FY25e consensus 49.7p = miss of 4.15p (−8.3%). Reported basic EPS 0.56p (2024: −4.44p). The EPS miss vs consensus is material.

"Underlying basic EPS (a / b): 45.55p (2024: 41.80p). The growth in underlying EPS of 9.0% was relatively lower than EBITDA growth of 22.4%. This was driven by the increased interest expense on our borrowings that fund M&A activity (with only a 6 month contribution from Citi and 2 months from KHT), and the increased volume of shares in the period."

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on underlying profit = £7.4m tax on £8.4m PBT (reported) = 88.8% — but this is heavily distorted by non-underlying items. On underlying basis: tax charge not separately broken out cleanly, but the CFO notes effective tax rate 5.8% on underlying basis (2024: 4.9%). 5.8% is low but consistent with Jersey domicile. No material deviation from prior year normalised rate. No tax-distorted beat — the miss is genuine. 🚨 Note: acquisition dilution (interest step-up from £184.2m drawdowns, share count increase from Galaxy EIP award exercise) compressed the EPS bridge materially.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here, referenced in Phase 4 #2):

  • New base: FY25 underlying EPS 45.55p (168.0m shares)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: Citi Trust contributed 6 months (H2 only) in FY25 — full annualisation in FY26 adds ~£32.8m × 2 − £32.8m = +£32.8m incremental revenue; at 32.6% EBITDA margin = ~+£10.7m EBITDA. KHT contributed 2 months — full year adds ~£14.5m revenue at ~37% margin = ~+£5.4m EBITDA. Combined annualisation EBITDA uplift ~£16.1m.
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: disclosed organic growth 8.5% — applying to FY25 organic revenue base ~£321m × 8.5% × 32.6% margin ≈ +£8.9m EBITDA organic contribution.
  • Interest step-up delta: FY25 bank loan interest £21.6m on average drawn debt. FY26 will see full-year cost of £184.2m net drawdowns at SONIA+ margin + US PP notes at 6.25%. Estimated FY26 interest: ~£28–30m (vs FY25 £21.6m) = incremental ~£6–8m interest headwind vs FY25 actuals.
  • Net EBITDA uplift (annualisation + organic): ~+£25m; minus additional D&A on acquired intangibles (~£5m uplift from full-year Citi/KHT); minus interest step-up ~£7m; minus tax at ~7% effective = net underlying profit uplift ~£11–13m.
  • Implied FY26 underlying profit: £76.5m + £11–13m = ~£87.5–89.5m. At 168m shares = ~52–53p EPS.
  • Stale FY26 consensus: 60.4p. Implied shortfall vs consensus: −7.4 to −8.4p (−12 to −14%).
  • This strongly suggests FY26 consensus needs to come down. The stale consensus appears to have assumed either higher organic growth or lower interest costs than actuals now imply.

3. Order book / forward work New business wins record: £43.5m (+21.8% vs FY24 £35.7m). Revenue retention 98.6% (FY24: 98.4%). Pipeline described as "healthy". No specific order book figure disclosed.

"We had another record year of new business wins totalling £43.5m at the period end (2024: £35.7m). The new business pipeline remains healthy."

4. Margin, profitability, costs Underlying EBITDA: £124.5m (+22.4% YoY). Underlying EBITDA margin 32.6% (FY24: 33.3%) — down 0.7pp. Management's medium-term guidance range: 33–38%. FY25 margin is below the bottom of the guidance range. ICS margin 28.8% (FY24: 30.6%) — deterioration flagged as investment-driven plus regulatory headwind on chargeable time. PCS margin 37.3% (FY24: 37.3%) — flat, showing Citi Trust integration delivered at JTC margins. Finance costs up 34.0% YoY (£31.2m vs £25.4m), driven by £184.2m debt drawdowns.

"Our underlying EBITDA margin reported a drop to 32.6% (2024: 33.3%). 2025 continued to be a year of market volatility, with the impact being most prominent in the ICS division."

Forward-looking margin guidance: nil explicit numeric. Management commentary references continued investment in infrastructure and regulatory compliance. No guidance for FY26 margin improvement stated.

5. Capital returns and balance sheet Dividend: 5p total for FY25 (FY24: 12.54p). Cut of 60.1% — driven entirely by the pending Permira acquisition. No final dividend declared due to offer period. This is a one-off structural event, not a going-concern signal.

Net debt (underlying) at FY25 year-end: £275.8m (vs FY24: £182.3m). Underlying ND/EBITDA: 2.22x (vs guidance 1.5–2.0x, above range as expected post-M&A). Undrawn facilities: £27.4m of £400m bank + $100m of $175m US PP.

"Our underlying net debt/underlying EBITDA leverage at the period end was 2.22x (2024: 1.79x), above our guidance range (1.5x - 2.0x). This increase was expected, with the period seeing increased M&A activity."

6. Qualitative tone / acquisition context Permira acquisition: agreed at £13.40/share (Nov 2025). Shareholder approval received Jan 2026. Expected to complete Q3 2026. This is the dominant structural overlay — the company is in an offer period, no earnings guidance can be given, no broker presentations held.

"Based on current expectations, the transaction is expected to complete during the third quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of the remaining conditions."

7. Constant currency / FX Constant currency revenue growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — 1.6pp drag from GBP strengthening vs USD.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

JTC is in an active offer period (Permira £13.40 cash bid). No FY26 guidance is given — legally restricted from doing so. The RNS closes the Cosmos era and introduces "Genesis" under private ownership. No earnings trajectory stated for FY26. No "comfortable with" language. No "ahead of expectations" language.

Classification: 🟡 In-line for outlook — but this is structurally constrained by the offer period. There is no positive upgrade signal and no downgrade warning beyond the mechanical miss on FY25 EPS vs consensus.

Exact guidance phrase: none — offer period restriction. Guidance: nil (qualitative only — "resilient", "record wins", "healthy pipeline"). Covers: not applicable. Provisional points: 0 to +3 (In-line, upper end given record new wins and healthy pipeline language, but nil numeric guidance caps this).

Divergence check: FY25 EPS missed consensus by 8.3%, yet qualitative language is constructive ("resilient performance", "record new business wins"). Current year miss + constructive qualitative tone = divergence. Carry as: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery (EPS missed consensus materially; qualitative tone does not reflect this adequately).

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-H1 mode only)

  • Revenue: 47.3% × £385.1m = £182.2m
  • EPS: 46.5% × 49.7p = 23.1p

H1 FY25 actuals are available from Sharescope current H1 field (£172.6m revenue, 21.3p EPS) — these are balance of year actuals embedded in the data. However, the data source gate requires RNS-disclosed figures. The RNS does not explicitly state H1 figures as a disclosed line item; the FY RNS provides only full-year numbers. The H1 result was separately reported earlier in the year. Sharescope current H1 figures used here are historic actuals from the H1 reporting date — not RNS-sourced from this document.

Tracking deviation (informational only — pre-FY mode, not scored):

  • Revenue: £172.6m ÷ £385.1m = 44.8% vs baseline 47.3% → deviation 🔴 [−2.5pp]
  • EPS: 21.3p ÷ 49.7p = 42.9% vs baseline 46.5% → deviation 🔴 [−3.6pp]

These signals are informational given we now have FY actuals. They confirm that JTC tracked below its seasonal baseline in H1, with H2 acquisition-driven catch-up partially restoring revenue but not EPS.

H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 49.7p − H1 actual 21.3p = 28.4p required vs historical H2 avg ~21.2p [(17.1+19.1+27.5)/3]. Burden was HIGHER than historical average — and FY25 actual H2 EPS of 24.25p fell below both the burden implied by consensus (28.4p) and the prior H2 (27.5p).

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored)

H2 base: RNS-derived. FY25 actual £381.9m / 45.55p. H1 actuals from prior reporting.

H2 Revenue: £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m → +32.2% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%) H2 EPS: 24.25p vs prior H2 27.5p → −11.8% YoY → 🔴 weak (−5 to −15%)

Revenue H2 strength is acquisition-driven (Citi Trust 6 months). Organic H2 revenue would strip out ~£32.8m inorganic → organic H2 ~£176.5m vs £158.3m = +11.5% — still strong organically.

EPS H2 weakness is structural: interest step-up (£184.2m drawdowns in FY25), share count marginally higher, partial EBITDA contribution from acquisitions (only H2 for Citi, only 2 months for KHT) vs full-year interest cost on drawdowns.

Revenue H2: 🟢 strong (RNS-derived) EPS H2: 🔴 weak (RNS-derived)

Profit warning feasibility gate (pre-H1 mode only): Not applicable — mode = pre-FY.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS trend: −0.2p (−0.2%) net change over full period (49.8p → 49.7p). Marginal drift lower — no upgrade cycle visible. Zero meaningful revision events in the 46-week snapshot window. 4-week trend: 🟡 STEADY/FLAT (no movement since 13 Mar 26).

Revenue trend: £387.3m → £385.1m = −£2.2m (−0.6%) net change. Mild drift lower in line with EPS.

Divergence: Price has risen from £12.43 to £13.00 over the period while forecasts have drifted very marginally lower. Price action entirely explained by the Permira offer at £13.40 (announced Nov 2025) — the price is trading at a discount to the offer, with spread reflecting regulatory/timing risk. Broker forecasts are effectively redundant as price anchors to the offer price.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt (underlying): FY22 ~n/a / FY23 £13.9m / FY24 £182.3m / FY25 H1 £276.5m / FY25 actual £275.8m / FY26fc £232.3m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY22 3.2x / FY23 n/a / FY24 1.9x (underlying) / FY25 2.22x (actual) / FY26fc 1.6x
  • Interest cover: FY25 actual reported 0.9x (distorted by non-underlying); underlying basis ~3.9x (pre-RNS fc) — actual underlying cover close to 3.9x given EBITDA £124.5m and finance cost (ex-unwinding NPV discounts) ~£22.5m = ~5.5x on EBITDA basis. FY26fc: 4.9x.
  • ND/FCF: FY25fc 3.4x / FY26fc 2.4x

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x ND/EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but explicitly anticipated and expected to revert to range when annualising acquisitions. Interest cover adequate. Covenant risk low given undrawn facilities. No Phase 5 scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24 actual:

  • FY25 actual EPS 45.55p vs FY24 actual 41.80p → ✅ growing (+9.0%)

scorecards.analysisText:
KOO

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS is Full Year Results for FY25. Market now shifts focus to FY26 guidance.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e — now actuals): EPS 9.0p · Revenue £63.3m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 9.4p · Revenue £63.1m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS started 9.0p in May 2025, drifted down to 8.3p by September 2025 (−8.3%), recovered to 9.4p in late January 2026 (+13.3%), then fell back to 9.0p at 28 March → 02 April. Net change over full period: 0.0%. Last 4 weeks: 🔴 FALLING (9.4p → 9.0p over 4 weeks, −0.44p). Revenue: £66.6m → £63.3m (−4.9% net). The revenue consensus has converged to exactly the FY25 actual — strongly suggesting the actual was pre-released or the guidance set this level. EPS sequence: down then up then down again = unstable consensus reflecting uncertainty about FX, Michigan timing.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 42.8% of FY = £27.1m · EPS: only 1yr avg available (47.6% of FY) = 4.3p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £32.5m · EPS 10.0p

Note: Sharescope shows FY1 fc EPS at 9.0p and current H1 EPS at −3.0p. This is a critical flag — the H1 was deeply loss-making while the full-year was expected to be 9.0p profit. The H2 was therefore bearing the entire earnings burden: FY1 fc 9.0p − H1 actual −3.0p = H2 burden 12.0p. This is an extraordinary H2 burden and the key analytical challenge for KOO.

  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 fc £63.3m − H1 actual £32.1m = implied H2 £31.2m vs FY24 H2 £34.3m → −9.1% YoY. EPS: FY1 fc 9.0p − H1 actual −3.0p = implied H2 12.0p vs FY24 H2 11.0p → +9.1% YoY.
  • FX: 74% of revenues in USD per RNS. Material — Phase 0B will trigger.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net cash (negative borrowings): FY23 −£0.1m (net cash £0.1m) / FY24 −£6.9m (net cash £6.9m) / H1 FY25 −£15.3m → FY1fc −£21.6m (net cash) / FY2fc −£25.4m · ND/EBITDA all negative (net cash position) · Interest cover: N/A (no debt) · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — £21.6m cash, zero debt, $9.5m undrawn facility.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

74% of revenues in USD. This exceeds the 50%+ threshold materially.

Searched the web

GBP/USD spot: ~$1.32 today. KOO's RNS discloses prior year FY25 average rate implicitly — CFO review states GBP appreciation against USD drove £3.3m FX headwind on ARR. The RNS explicitly states "approximately 74% of revenues and 50% of expenses denominated in US Dollars" and "realised foreign currency loss of £0.6m." The CFO confirms the FX impact: the 2025 GBP/USD average was materially stronger than 2024. From the RNS, a 10% rate change = £1.4m profit impact, implying a roughly $1.27–1.29 average in 2024 and $1.30–1.32 average in 2025 (consistent with search data: 2026 YTD average ~$1.35).

KOO Phase 0B:

  • USD exposure: 74% of revenues (>50% threshold)
  • Spot rate today: ~$1.32
  • Prior year (FY25) average from RNS context: ~$1.28–1.30 (consistent with reported FX loss of £0.6m on £46.1m US revenues)
  • FY24 average: ~$1.27 per CFO disclosures

For FY26 guidance purposes: spot $1.32 vs FY25 avg ~$1.29 → GBP slightly stronger. Modest ongoing headwind for FY26 but less severe than FY25's drag.

For FY25 actuals (the current RNS): the FX headwind is already baked into the reported numbers — £63.3m actual revenue includes the drag. The Phase 0B penalty for FY25 actuals is therefore already in the numbers and should not be double-counted. For FY26 forward guidance context, the spot is ~$1.32 vs FY25 avg ~$1.29 — neutral to marginal headwind.

Phase 0B for KOO FY25 results: FX headwind already reflected in actuals. The RNS explicitly quantifies: constant currency revenue −2.7% vs reported −5.1% → FX impact = ~2.4pp on revenues. For the Phase 5 scoring, the FX damage is already in the delivered numbers, so I will NOT apply a fresh Phase 0B penalty to the score (the actual result already incorporates it). However, I will flag FX as a structural risk for FY26 forward estimates.

Phase 0B override note: The RNS provides constant currency figures (−2.7% rev on CC basis vs reported −5.1%) — the CC disclosure confirms the FX impact is quantified but NOT equal to reported growth (2.4pp gap). Phase 0B override does NOT fire (requires CC within 0.5pp of reported). FX headwind confirmed and quantified in actuals. No additional penalty applied to Phase 5 score as it is already embedded in the delivered EPS/revenue figures.

Badge: For FY26 forward risk: FX headwind ongoing · 74% USD · $1.32 spot vs ~$1.29 FY25 avg · modest continued drag on FY26

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue FY25 actual revenue: £63.3m vs FY24 £66.7m = −5.1% YoY. vs FY1 pre-RNS consensus £63.3m = in line (consensus had already converged to the actual — the weekly Sharescope data shows consensus moving to exactly £63.3m on 30 January 2026, suggesting a pre-announcement briefing or interim guidance). Constant currency: −2.7%. ARR: £60.6m (2024: £66.4m), −8.7% reported, −3.7% constant currency.

"2025 revenue was £63.3m (2024: £66.7m), following a record year in 2024 in which revenues doubled. This figure reflects the impact of FX movements, a reduction in California product development revenues and delays in signing a contract with the State of Michigan."

H2 implied: £63.3m − £32.1m H1 = £31.2m vs FY24 H2 £34.3m = −9.0% YoY. Revenue was back-end light, consistent with Michigan contract revenue pushed to FY26.

2. EPS / Earnings Reported basic EPS: 7p (£0.07 per share). Diluted: 7p. Per Sharescope FY1 fc EPS 9.0p (adjusted basis).

From P&L: PBT £4.37m → tax £1.76m → PAT £2.61m. Diluted shares: 38.6m. Diluted reported EPS = 6.8p (£2.608m / 38.557m). The 9.0p FY1 Sharescope consensus is on an adjusted basis — need to derive.

Adjusted EBITDA: £11.3m (consensus "ahead of expectations" — this is the one explicit beat). Adj EBITDA FY24: £15.8m → FY25: £11.3m = −28.5%.

EPS quality check — CRITICAL: The CFO explicitly flags an effective tax rate of 40.3% vs standard rate of 25%. Two permanent differences cited:

  1. Transition from SME R&D to RDEC scheme: R&D now in "other income" (£0.3m) rather than as a tax credit. Prior year had £0.5m in tax credits.
  2. Share-based payment permanent difference: SBP charges not deductible on vesting where share price fell below grant price — caused ~10pp of ETR increase.

These are structural/accounting changes, not true earnings distortions in the trading sense. The RDEC reclassification is revenue-side neutral (£0.3m in "other income"). The SBP non-deductibility is a genuine non-recurring tax drag.

Restated at normalised 25% tax rate: PBT £4.37m × 75% = £3.28m PAT. Diluted EPS restated = £3.28m / 38.6m = 8.5p. The reported 6.8p includes ~1.7p of abnormal tax drag. This matters for assessing whether FY25 is a clean base for FY26. However — the RDEC/SBP issues may partly recur in FY26, so I will note the distortion but use the reported figure as the baseline.

🚨 EPS quality flag: Effective tax rate 40.3% vs normalised 25% — 15.3pp above standard rate. Restated adj EPS at 25% = ~8.5p vs reported ~6.8p. The £0.6m SBP non-deductibility and RDEC reclassification account for most of the gap. This is partly recurring (if SBP awards vest below grant, the permanent difference continues in FY26) and partly non-recurring (RDEC reclassification is now the new base). FY26 ETR should normalise towards ~30–32% as RDEC effect stabilises.

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • FY25 base: adj EBITDA £11.3m; D&A £6.2m; adj EBIT ~£5.1m; interest income £0.7m (cash deposits on £21.6m); PBT ~£4.4m (consistent with reported); at normalised 30% tax → PAT ~£3.1m; diluted EPS ~8.0p
  • (1) New base: ~8.0p on clean tax
  • (2) Revenue guidance FY26: "in line with current market expectations" — FY2 consensus £63.1m = essentially flat. No revenue growth assumption.
  • (3) Michigan contract: £2.6m signed post-period. This was delayed from FY25 — will now recognise in FY26. Net new FY26 revenue vs FY25: +£2.6m (partially offset by any California reductions). ARR at year-end £60.6m but contract backlog (revenue to come) £22.8m → all recognised within one year. Strong FY26 revenue floor from contracted backlog.
  • (4) California direct marketing: £8.1m in FY25 (vs £3.9m FY24). This is a "front-loaded" investment. The RNS implies this investment level does not need to repeat at the same intensity once users are registered. If direct marketing reduces to £4–5m in FY26, gross margin improves ~£3–4m → adj EBITDA improves materially.
  • (5) UK Soluna launch H2 2026: additional capex/opex ahead of revenue — dilutive short-term.
  • Implied FY26 EPS: £63.1m revenue × improving gross margin (~75–76% if marketing reduces) → gross profit ~£47–48m; opex broadly flat; adj EBITDA ~£12.5–13.5m; D&A ~£6.5m (capex slightly higher for Soluna UK); adj EBIT ~£6.0–7.0m; + interest income ~£0.8m; PBT ~£6.8–7.8m; at 30% tax → PAT ~£4.8–5.5m; diluted EPS ~12–14p at 36–38m diluted shares.

Wait — this is materially above the FY2 consensus of 9.4p. The FY2 consensus may be too conservative if marketing costs normalise. Alternatively, the consensus may be factoring in Soluna UK launch costs + continued California investment at elevated levels. The 9.4p consensus is likely the more realistic base given management's "in line with expectations" language is backward-looking on current consensus. I will flag this as a potential consensus upgrade scenario but not build upside into the base case.

3. Order book / forward visibility Revenue to come from contracts with unfulfilled obligations: £22.8m at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all expected within one year. Michigan contract ($2.6m = ~£2.0m) signed post-period — not in this figure. US revenue 71% of total in 2025, with one customer (California) at 71% of Group revenue.

"Revenue to come from contracts entered into with performance obligations not fulfilled or only partially fulfilled amounted to £22.8m as at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all of which is expected to be recognised within one year."

4. Margin / profitability Gross margin: 73.1% (FY24: 77.9%), −480bps. The decline is entirely attributable to £8.1m of California direct marketing in cost of sales (vs £3.9m FY24). Excluding the marketing investment: gross margin approximately 86% of revenues ex-marketing = ~80%+.

Adjusted EBITDA: £11.3m — stated "ahead of expectations." This is the only explicit beat in the RNS.

Operating profit: £3.4m (FY24: £9.2m). Admin expenses flat at £42.9m (−£0.1m YoY) showing discipline.

Free cash flow: net inflow £1.2m (FY24: £10.2m). Cash at year-end: £21.6m (FY24: £21.8m) — essentially flat, down only £0.2m despite heavy investment year.

5. Capital returns No dividend (policy: invest for growth). £1.5m share buyback completed in February 2025. No new buyback announced.

6. Qualitative tone — FY26 outlook CEO: "we anticipate that revenue and adjusted EBITDA for 2026 will be in line with current market expectations."

FY2 consensus: Revenue £63.1m, adj EBITDA (from Sharescope) £10.3m. So FY26 guided at flat-to-marginally-down EBITDA (£11.3m → £10.3m) and flat revenue (£63.3m → £63.1m). This is not a positive guide.

Key initiatives: Michigan contract now signed, New Jersey renewed, Soluna UK H2 2026 launch, AI product development, Kismet acquisition (paediatric platform, acquired for $1). No numeric uplift provided on any of these.

7. Post-period events Michigan contract: $2.6m (£~2.0m). This is incremental to FY25 revenue base.

EPS quality check summary: 🚨 ETR 40.3% vs 25% standard rate — 15.3pp gap. Two permanent items: SBP non-deductibility (~10pp) and RDEC reclassification (~5pp). Restated at 30% normalised FY26 rate → FY25 base EPS ~8.0–8.5p. FY26 consensus at 9.4p is plausible if: (a) revenue flat, (b) California marketing normalises somewhat, (c) ETR normalises to 30–32%. But the in-line guidance suggests management is not signalling a beat.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward language on FY26: "revenue and adjusted EBITDA for 2026 will be in line with current market expectations." Numeric coverage: qualitative-only, references current consensus. No uplift language. FY2 consensus EBITDA £10.3m is slightly below FY25 actual £11.3m — suggesting management is guiding to a Soluna UK launch cost drag. Revenue flat.

Divergence: FY25 current year EBITDA beat ("ahead of expectations") but FY26 guided in-line at a slightly lower EBITDA level. Beat quality divergence applies — current year beat but forward guide is not constructive.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — "in line with current market expectations." Numeric guidance provided (by reference to consensus). No upgrade or downgrade signal for FY26. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

Beat quality divergence: FY25 EBITDA beat but FY26 guided lower EBITDA (£10.3m vs £11.3m) — management is signalling the FY25 beat does not carry into FY26. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery — carry as named row in Phase 5.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

Phase 0A year label mappings:

  • Next year end: 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25
  • 1y ago = FY24 · 2y ago = FY23 · 3y ago = FY22
  • FY2 = FY26
  • Current H1/H2 = FY25 partial actuals

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-checks: FY23 H1+H2 = 9.0+11.1 = 20.1 ✅. FY24 H1+H2 = 32.5+34.3 = 66.8 ≠ 66.7 (£0.1m rounding) ✅. FY25 H1+H2 = 32.1+31.2 = 63.3 ✅ (implied H2 = FY actual − H1 = 63.3 − 32.1 = 31.2). EPS: FY23 −1.0+(−1.0)=−2.0 ✅. FY24 −2.0+2.0=0.0 ✅. FY25: H1 −3.0p; FY actual reported 6.8p diluted (£0.07). Sharescope FY1 fc = 9.0p (adjusted). Using reported 6.8p for the table since that is the actual P&L figure.

† Sharescope shows FY24 H1/H2 EPS as 10.0/11.0 = 21.0p. Per RNS FY24 basic EPS = £0.22 (36.6m shares) = 22p, close enough — rounding/adjusted vs reported. Using Sharescope 21.0p. ‡ FY25 actual reported diluted EPS = 7p per RNS P&L (£0.07). Sharescope shows FY1 fc at 9.0p (adjusted basis pre-RNS). Actual reported EPS 6.8p < consensus 9.0p — miss on a reported basis. However adj EBITDA beat expectations.

Revenue growth trajectory: FY23→FY24 +231.8% (revenue doubled — UK/US expansion) → FY24→FY25 −5.1%. Three-year: massive expansion then slight contraction. 🟡 Volatile — but the FY24 surge was unique (California launch, revenue doubled). The more relevant comparison is organic growth rate ex-FX: −2.7% constant currency in FY25. This is deceleration from a very high base.

EPS growth trajectory: FY23 −2.0p → FY24 +21.0p → FY25 6.8p (reported). 🟡 Volatile — the FY24 jump was extraordinary and the FY25 decline is partly base effect, partly tax drag, partly investment drag. Underlying adj EBITDA is the cleaner metric: £15.8m → £11.3m = −28.5%.

Acceleration flags (pre-FY mode — using FY actuals vs consensus):

  • Revenue: FY25 actual −5.1% vs FY24 +231.8% → no acceleration (consensus-derived, actuals now known). FY26 consensus −0.3% → no acceleration vs FY25 −5.1%... wait, −0.3% is better than −5.1% → marginal acceleration ✓ but essentially flat-to-flat.
  • EPS: FY26 consensus 9.4p vs FY25 reported 6.8p = +38.2% vs FY25→FY24 not comparable (n/m). On adj EBITDA basis: FY26 consensus £10.3m vs FY25 actual £11.3m = −8.8% → no acceleration on EBITDA.

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern
