† FY25 H2 EPS = FY25 reported 6.8p − H1 −3.0p = 9.8p (implied). This is the entire year's profit concentrated in H2, consistent with H1 investment phase.

EPS trajectory (last three H2 YoY): FY23 H2 n/m → FY24 H2 n/m → FY25 H2 implied 9.8p (−10.9% vs 11.0p FY24 H2). The H2 EPS decline confirms the California investment drag and FX headwind materialised in H2 as well as H1. 🔴 Decelerating on H2 EPS.

Revenue trajectory: FY24 H2 +208.9% → FY25 H1 −1.2% → FY25 H2 −9.0%. 🔴 Decelerating — revenue growth turned negative and the rate of decline accelerated in H2.

H2 revenue decline context: The −9.0% H2 revenue decline is primarily attributable to: (a) lower California product development revenues (£2m reduction per CFO), (b) Michigan contract delayed (recognised in FY26), (c) FX headwind (~£1.5m based on H2 weighting). Adjusting for Michigan delay and FX: underlying H2 −3–4% — not catastrophic but not growth.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-FY mode — written but NOT scored)

Data source gate: H1 actuals are RNS-sourced (FY25 H1: revenue £32.1m, EPS −3.0p).

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% = 42.8% × FY1 fc £63.3m = £27.1m
  • EPS baseline: 1yr avg H1% = 47.6% × FY1 fc 9.0p = 4.3p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £32.1m ÷ FY1 fc £63.3m = 50.7% vs baseline 42.8% → deviation = 🟢 [+7.9pp]. However, H1 actually represents an unusual period — revenue was £32.1m but embedded the California product development contribution. The baseline 42.8% is depressed by FY23 H1 (£9.0m / £20.1m = 44.8%) when the company was much smaller. The 3yr avg is not a clean seasonal baseline for a company that has grown 3x. Use with caution — flagged.
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual −3.0p ÷ FY1 fc 9.0p = −33.3% vs baseline 47.6% → deviation = 🔴🔴 [−80.9pp]. This extreme negative deviation reflects the H1 investment phase (direct marketing, H1 losses) — but the company was always expected to be H2-weighted this year. The EPS tracking signal is mechanically a SELL SIGNAL but is uninformative given the known H1/H2 skew in the business model.

Not scored in Phase 5 (pre-FY mode). Noted for completeness.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (scored in Phase 5 — pre-FY mode)

RNS provides FY25 actual: revenue £63.3m. H1 actual £32.1m → implied H2 = £31.2m (RNS-derived).

H2 YoY: £31.2m vs FY24 H2 £34.3m = −9.0% YoY. Classification: 🔴 weak (−9.0%, within −5 to −15% band).

EPS H2: FY25 reported 6.8p − H1 −3.0p = 9.8p implied H2 vs FY24 H2 11.0p = −10.9% YoY. Classification: 🔴 weak (−10.9%, within −5 to −15% band).

H2 momentum classification: 🔴 weak — both revenue and EPS H2 are down YoY. Revenue decline is partly structural (Michigan delay, lower Cal dev revenues); EPS decline partly reflects higher marketing in H1 flowing into lower gross margin for the full year.

Profit warning feasibility gate: H1 EPS was −3.0p (miss vs seasonal baseline). H2 burden was 12.0p (required to get to 9.0p FY consensus). Was the H2 burden implausible? The actual H2 delivered 9.8p reported — broadly in line, slightly above (full year 6.8p + H1 −3.0p restated... actually per the income statement: PBT £4.37m → PAT £2.61m → EPS 6.8p. H1 EPS was −3.0p per Sharescope, so H2 must be 9.8p reported). The 12.0p Sharescope-implied H2 burden (on adj basis) vs actual H2 ~9.8p (reported) gap reflects the adj vs reported difference. The H2 actually delivered, so no profit warning crystallised. The gate was concerned but the outcome was adequate.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Started 9.0p, fell to 8.3p in September 2025 (likely H1 results), recovered to 9.4p in January 2026 (FY26 expectation reset as FY25 converged), now falling back to 9.0p. Net: flat (+0.0%). 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (9.4p → 9.0p).
  • Revenue trend: £66.6m → £63.3m (−4.9%). Decline throughout, converging to actual.
  • Divergence: Share price has crashed from £3.87 in May 2025 to £1.07 today (−72% in 11 months) while EPS was flat. The de-rating is extreme and reflects: (a) risk appetite for loss-making H1, (b) California dependency concerns, (c) FX headwind, (d) FY24 comparator being exceptional. The 107p price vs 314p TP represents 193% upside — an extraordinary gap that suggests the market does not trust the TP models.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

  • Net cash: FY23 £0.1m / FY24 £6.9m / H1 FY25 £15.3m → FY1 (actual) £21.6m → FY2fc £25.4m
  • ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash). FY25: £21.6m cash / £11.3m adj EBITDA = −1.9x
  • Interest cover: infinite (no debt) — interest income £0.7m
  • ND/FCF: £21.6m cash / £1.2m FCF = significant cash reserves vs modest cash generation

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — £21.6m cash, zero debt. Not a constraint. No scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24:

  • FY25 reported EPS 6.8p vs FY24 21.0p → 🚨 FY1 (actual) EPS −67.6% below prior year
  • FY25 revenue £63.3m vs FY24 £66.7m → 🚨 FY1 (actual) Revenue −5.1% below prior year
  • Both declining. (Exception applies: the FY24 was genuinely exceptional — revenue doubled from California launch; FY25 decline is partly FX, partly investment, partly Michigan delay. ⚠️ Replace 🚨 with ⚠️ — decline partially explained by known one-off in comparison year (FY24 exceptional expansion year). Still flagged.)

Step 2 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • FY2fc EPS 9.4p vs FY25 actual 6.8p → ✅ FY2fc EPS +38.2% vs FY1 actual
  • FY2fc Revenue £63.1m vs FY25 £63.3m → 🚨 FY2fc Revenue −0.3% below FY1 — forward year declining (marginally)
  • Mixed: EPS growing on reported basis; Revenue essentially flat.

3.6 Structural Flags

California concentration risk: One customer accounts for 71% of Group revenue (£44.9m). Any adverse change to the California contract — political (state budget, governor priorities), contractual (termination for convenience clause exists per accounting policy), or performance-related — would be catastrophic for the business. The RNS provides strong mitigation: LA County motion directing all youth-serving departments to integrate Soluna, joint letter from CalHHS/DHCS/DOE, Northwestern University independent evaluation. But the concentration remains extreme.

"The group had one customer (2024: one) that accounted for more than 10% of total revenue in 2025. This customer accounted for 71% of group revenue (2024: 73%)"

Soluna UK launch H2 2026: Engineering and regulatory work "well-advanced." This is a new revenue stream but requires upfront investment. The capitalisation of Soluna UK costs is ongoing (£1.7m carrying value on balance sheet). Will increase amortisation in FY26–27.

Kismet Health acquisition: Acquired for $1 post-period. Paediatric telehealth platform — expands addressable market to under-12s. Transaction costs £33k capitalised. Carrying value £0.1m. Not yet amortised — not material to FY26 numbers.

Revenue backlog structure: Contracts include termination-for-convenience clauses with fixed notice periods (IFRS 15 note). This means the £22.8m contract backlog has a shorter "firm" duration than it appears — revenue is recognised monthly but contracts can be exited on notice. Risk asymmetry.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

KOO · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — Adj EBITDA beat and cash preservation: The only explicit financial beat in the RNS is adj EBITDA of £11.3m "ahead of expectations." Combined with year-end cash of £21.6m (essentially flat vs FY24's £21.8m despite heavy investment and £1.5m buyback) — this is the primary positive. Brokers will note that the investment year did not burn cash as feared, and EBITDA came in ahead. This provides confidence that FY26 EBITDA guidance of ~£10.3m (in-line) is achievable without major cash deterioration. Driver #1.

#2 Driver — California KPI beats and institutional embedding: 144,000+ youth registered on Soluna (exceeding performance targets), LA County directive, Northwestern University evaluation showing "significant and sustained improvements in wellbeing." These are the long-term valuation drivers — they demonstrate Soluna is becoming infrastructure rather than a pilot. The New Jersey renewal and Michigan contract ($2.6m) show the State Alliance model is generating repeat/expansion business. Brokers will use these KPIs to anchor their long-term DCF models (the TP of 314p implies a very long-term value creation thesis). Driver #2 for the investment case narrative.

#2 Forecast revisions — FY25 (FY1) and FY26 (FY2):

FY25 actuals vs consensus:

  • Revenue: £63.3m vs £63.3m consensus = in-line — no revision needed (consensus had pre-converged)
  • Adj EBITDA: £11.3m vs expectations = beat — brokers may upgrade FY25 EBITDA estimate upwards (if not already reflecting the in-line consensus)
  • Reported EPS: 6.8p vs Sharescope 9.0p consensus — significant miss on reported basis due to 40.3% ETR. Brokers using adj basis: adj EBITDA beat suggests adj EPS also beats adj consensus; but reported EPS is the headline that investors see.

FY26 (FY2):

  • Revenue: "in line with current market expectations" = £63.1m held → no change
  • Adj EBITDA: "in line" = ~£10.3m held → hold to modest trim (FY25 £11.3m → FY26 £10.3m already embedded; Soluna UK launch costs could pressure further)
  • EPS: reported EPS base is 6.8p; ETR normalising to ~30–32% in FY26 → FY26 adj EPS ~9.4p consensus achievable. Hold or marginal trim — no upgrade catalyst.

#3 Target price and recommendation: TPs will be held or marginally trimmed. The 314p consensus TP is a long-term DCF value — brokers are unlikely to cut it based on one in-line year. However, the share at 107p vs 314p TP (193% upside) reflects the market's fundamental distrust of that long-term thesis being delivered. Brokers will maintain Buy/Add but acknowledge the near-term uncertainty. No TP cuts expected, no increases expected. Hold TPs at 300–320p range.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with current market expectations" is explicitly neutral — not "comfortable with" (constructive) and not a beat flag. No conservative guidance premium. However, management has consistently underpromised and overdelivered on the EBITDA line (FY25 EBITDA beat); brokers may attribute a modest probability of FY26 EBITDA upside if California marketing continues to normalise.

#5 Key risk: California contract termination clause and concentration risk. 71% single-customer revenue with a termination-for-convenience clause is the dominant risk. The geopolitical/budget environment in California (state budgets under pressure, new administration priorities) creates uncertainty. Any California contract reduction or non-renewal would be a company-defining event.

"Revenue to come from contracts entered into with performance obligations not fulfilled or only partially fulfilled amounted to £22.8m as at 31 December 2025 (2024: £27.1m), all of which is expected to be recognised within one year."

The decline in backlog from £27.1m to £22.8m suggests revenue coverage for FY26 is thinner than FY25 was entering the year.

Consistency check: Net FY1 (FY25 actuals) outcome vs FY2 (FY26) revision direction = hold. Revenue in-line, EBITDA beat is FY25 not FY26. FY26 guided in-line. Tone = Neutral. ✅ Consistent.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

EBITDA beat and California KPI beats provide near-term comfort but: revenue flat, FY26 guided in-line at lower EBITDA, reported EPS significantly below adjusted expectations (tax distortion), extreme single-customer concentration. Brokers will maintain recommendations but not initiate upgrades.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT — KOO

42/100 · Confidence: 35–50 · FX already in actuals — no additional penalty applied · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 Adj EBITDA £11.3m ahead of expectations+8
🟢 Cash preservation: £21.6m year-end cash, essentially flat despite heavy investment + buyback+6
🟢 California KPI beats: 144k+ registered, LA County motion, Northwestern evaluation, NJ renewal + Michigan+7
🟢 Balance sheet unlevered — net cash £21.6m, zero debt, $9.5m undrawn facility+4
🟡 Revenue in-line: £63.3m vs £63.3m consensus — no beat but no miss either+2
🟡 Beat quality — FY25 EBITDA beat but FY26 guided in-line at lower EBITDA (£10.3m vs £11.3m)−3
🟡 FY26 guidance "in line with current market expectations" — neutral, no upgrade catalyst0
🔴 Reported EPS 6.8p vs adj consensus 9.0p — ETR 40.3% vs 25% standard; 15.3pp gap (partly recurring via SBP non-deductibility)−6
🔴 H2 revenue momentum weak: −9.0% YoY (Michigan delay, lower Cal dev revenues, FX)−5
🔴 71% single-customer concentration (California) with termination-for-convenience clause−6
🔴 Revenue backlog declined: £22.8m at Dec-25 vs £27.1m at Dec-24 — thinner FY26 coverage−4
🔴 EPS consensus falling last 4 weeks (9.4p → 9.0p) — market already downgrading ahead of results−3
🔴 Gross margin decline 73.1% vs 77.9% FY24 — California marketing structural drag; FY26 unclear if normalises−4
🔴 Share price −72% YoY at 107p vs 314p TP — market pricing in significant downside to broker models−4

Raw score: 42

Para 1 — Headline numbers: KOO delivered FY25 results that are best characterised as "broadly held together." Revenue of £63.3m (consensus exactly) and adj EBITDA of £11.3m "ahead of expectations" are the two headline figures — the EBITDA beat is the singular positive. The problem is what sits beneath: reported EPS of 6.8p (diluted) against a Sharescope adj consensus of 9.0p is a significant gap, driven by a 40.3% effective tax rate (vs 25% standard) caused by SBP non-deductibility (share price fell below grant price, ~10pp ETR impact) and the RDEC reclassification (~5pp). The FX headwind of ~£3.3m on ARR is already embedded. The #1 number that dominates is that one customer (California) accounts for 71% of Group revenue — the entire investment case rests on that contract deepening and diversifying.

Para 2 — H2 momentum and upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, H2 momentum is the key signal. KOO's implied H2 revenue was £31.2m — down 9.0% YoY vs FY24 H2's £34.3m. The decline is explained: £2m lower California development revenues, Michigan contract (~£2m equivalent) delayed to FY26, and ~£1.5m FX impact in H2. The H2 EPS implied was 9.8p (reported basis) — down 10.9% vs FY24 H2's 11.0p. Both metrics classify as 🔴 weak. The upgrade resilience is entirely structural rather than numerical: the 144,000+ California users, LA County integration directive, and Northwestern evaluation provide the qualitative floor under the investment case — but they do not directly translate into near-term EPS upgrades. FY26 guidance of "in line" with consensus revenue (£63.1m, effectively flat) and lower consensus EBITDA (£10.3m) means H2 momentum carries through to FY26 as well. The Michigan contract ($2.6m) provides a known incremental, partially offsetting the California development revenue reduction.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and verdict: Brokers will make minimal revisions. FY25 actuals are in-line on revenue (pre-converged consensus), slightly ahead on EBITDA — no meaningful FY25 number changes needed. For FY26: revenue held at £63.1m, EBITDA held at ~£10.3m (possibly trimmed marginally given Soluna UK launch costs), reported EPS towards 9–10p if the ETR normalises towards 30–32% (the SBP permanent difference will reduce if KOO shares recover). TP range 300–320p held, but the 107p share price vs 314p TP represents a credibility gap that today's RNS does not close — the market needs to see FY26 revenue growth and California contract durability evidenced. The single watch point is the California contract — a £22.8m contracted backlog covering only ~36% of FY26 revenue guidance means ~64% of FY26 revenue depends on contracts being renewed/extended over the course of the year. 🏁 Hold and wait: EBITDA beat is noted but insufficient to re-rate; FY26 "in-line" guidance removes upgrade catalyst; recovery hinges on Michigan ramp, Soluna UK launch, and California contract durability — none of which crystallise until H2 FY26.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

LBG · Q4 · Half-Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update / Half-Year Trading Update (H1 ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue — H1 FY26:

  • H1 revenue: £52.4m (+19% YoY vs H1 FY25 £43.9m; +22% constant currency).
  • vs FY1 fc £105m consensus: H1 = £52.4m = 49.9% of FY fc — above the 48.3% seasonal baseline by +1.6pp → 🟢 MILD BUY signal.
  • vs prior season buy trigger (£50.7m × 1.015 = £51.5m): £52.4m > £51.5m → 🟢 ✓ buy trigger met.
  • Direct revenue streams: >70% of H1 revenue = >£36.7m (FY25: ~55%). Major mix shift underway.
  • FY26 full year revenue guidance raised to c.£110m — upgrade of +£5m (+4.8%) from consensus £105m.

"Strong revenue momentum, up 19% to £52.4m (H1 25: £43.9m). Constant currency revenue growth of 22%."

2. Adj EBITDA / EPS — H1 FY26:

  • H1 adj EBITDA: £8.0m (H1 FY25: £12.2m) = −34.4% YoY.
  • vs FY26 consensus £25.4m full year: H1 = £8.0m = 31.5% of FY consensus vs H1 FY25 = £12.2m / £25.4m FY consensus = 48.0% of FY consensus. Massive underperformance vs seasonal baseline on EBITDA.
  • FY26 adj EBITDA guided to c.£22m vs consensus £25.4m = cut of −£3.4m = −13.4% on EBITDA. This is the profit warning component.
  • EPS (adj): not disclosed. With EBITDA cut from £25.4m to £22m, EPS revision: adj EBITDA − (D&A ~£2m + net interest income ~£0.5m) → adj PBT ~£20.5m at FY22 guidance → tax ~25% → PAT ~£15.4m → EPS on 209.1m shares = ~7.3p. vs consensus 7.5p = cut of ~−3%. More severe depending on D&A structure. EPS revision likely −5 to −10% from 7.5p to ~6.8–7.1p.

"Lower adjusted EBITDA of £8.0m (H1 25 £12.2m), reflecting three key factors."

EPS bridge FY26e (updated):

  • (1) New base: FY25 adj EPS 6.7p (full year). H1 FY26 adj EPS not disclosed; EBITDA £8.0m H1 vs £22m FY guidance → H2 implied EBITDA = £14.0m.
  • (2) EBITDA cut: FY guidance £22m vs consensus £25.4m → −£3.4m → EPS cut ~−0.7p on 209m shares after tax → revised FY26e EPS ~6.8–7.1p.
  • (3) Revenue upgrade: £110m vs £105m → +£5m revenue but at lower EBITDA margin → incremental revenue is from Direct (lower margin than Indirect).
  • Implied FY26e EPS: ~6.8–7.1p (centred ~7.0p) vs stale consensus 7.5p = cut of ~−6 to −9%.

3. EBITDA margin drivers — three stated factors:

  1. Planned investment in senior leadership and US/UK Direct sales capability.
  2. Revenue and margin mix moving toward Direct revenue (>70% in H1; FY25 ~55%) — Direct has lower margins than Indirect.
  3. No recovery in Indirect revenue (algorithmic/platform revenue-sharing) — Meta Facebook algorithm changes continuing; "referral volumes...in line with trends experienced in H2 25."

"Lower adjusted EBITDA...reflecting three key factors. Firstly, planned investment in senior leadership and sales capability...Secondly, revenue and margin mix moving towards Direct revenue streams...Thirdly, we did not see a recovery in our Indirect revenue streams."

4. Qualitative — H2 outlook and EBITDA recovery:

  • "H2 26 weighting for adjusted EBITDA reflects the benefit of senior hires, as well as cost savings made in H1 26." Implied H2 EBITDA: £22m − £8.0m = £14.0m vs H1 £8.0m — £6m H2 loading. H2 FY25 adj EBITDA = £12.2m (full year £25.4m consensus H1 portion £12.2m of £25.4m = 48% in H1 → H2 FY25 ~£13.2m). H2 FY26 guided £14.0m vs H2 FY25 ~£13.2m = +6.1% YoY. Plausible but reliant on senior hire benefits crystallising and cost savings in H1 carrying forward.
  • "Excellent momentum from Direct revenue streams...healthy pipeline for H2."
  • Meta/Facebook indirect headwind "continuing in line with trends experienced in H2 25" — no recovery expected.

5. Cash position:

  • Net cash £28.4m (31 Mar 2026) vs FY25 £30.8m. Slight decline driven by investment.
  • "Strong balance sheet and cash generation continues to support selective acquisitions."

6. Guidance Summary (Post-RNS):

  • FY26 Revenue: upgraded to c.£110m (from £105m consensus) = +4.8% upgrade.
  • FY26 adj EBITDA: guided to c.£22m (from £25.4m consensus) = −13.4% cut.
  • This is a revenue upgrade / EBITDA warning combination — the quality of earnings has deteriorated (Direct revenue at lower margins, Indirect structural decline continuing).

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

The RNS contains simultaneous revenue upgrade (+4.8%) and EBITDA profit warning (−13.4%). This is a textbook Beat quality divergence.

FY26 guidance: numeric, explicit: revenue £110m (above consensus) but EBITDA £22m (below consensus). The RNS is honest about the causes: margin mix (Direct lower-margin than Indirect), investment, and Indirect structural decline.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — EBITDA below consensus, margin dilution from structural Indirect decline, investment spend flagged. Despite revenue upgrade, the earnings quality is deteriorating. Provisional points: −6 to −8 pts.

Divergence check: Revenue beat vs EBITDA miss = explicit divergence. Current H1 revenue strongly growing (+19% YoY) but EBITDA sharply declining (−34%). Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery — revenue growth momentum positive but earnings quality declining. This is a separate scored row.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

LBG · Q4 · Half-Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26

  • FY23: H1 £24.8m + H2 £38.0m = £62.8m (no Sharescope FY total for 3y ago to cross-check; treating as correct). EPS: −0.9 + 4.2 = 3.3p.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source: H1 revenue confirmed from RNS at £52.4m. EPS not disclosed. Revenue is trackable; EPS is UNTRACKABLE.

Revenue:

Note: Sharescope gives 48.3% — this is based on their calculation which may include FY25 only (1yr) or different years. Using 3yr derived avg of 42.5% for robustness. ⚠️ Significant variance in H1% across years (39.5% to 47.6%) — LBG has very volatile seasonality due to Indirect revenue shifts. Sharescope's 48.3% baseline appears to be 1yr (FY25 only per data label "1yr avg"). Using 48.3% as directed by Sharescope.
  • Revenue baseline: 48.3% × £105m = £50.7m
  • H1 actual £52.4m / £105m = 49.9% → deviation = +1.6pp → 🟢 MILD BUY (just above +1.5pp threshold)

EPS: UNTRACKABLE — adj EPS not disclosed in trading update. Signal: na (—).

Revenue H2 burden: £105m consensus − £52.4m = £52.6m implied H2 vs H2 FY25 £48.3m = +8.9% YoY. But company now guides FY26 = £110m → implied H2 = £57.6m vs £48.3m = +19.2% YoY. H2 burden elevated but achievable per management guidance: "excellent momentum...healthy pipeline for H2 in the UK and US."

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-H1 mode — scores in Phase 5)

H2 base: RNS-guided FY £110m → H2 = £57.6m (RNS-derived) vs H2 FY25 £48.3m = +19.2% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%).

vs 3yr H2 avg: (£38.0m + £40.3m + £48.3m)/3 = £42.2m → H2 FY26 £57.6m = +36.5% above 3yr avg. Structurally elevated but consistent with the business's rapid growth from acquisitions (Betches in FY22, etc.) and Direct revenue acceleration.

H2 EBITDA burden: FY guidance £22m − H1 £8.0m = £14.0m H2 EBITDA vs estimated H2 FY25 ~£13.2m = +6.1% YoY. Achievable per management language. The question is whether senior hires and H1 cost savings deliver the H2 acceleration.

Classification: 🟢 strong on revenue (RNS-derived); 🟡 moderate on EBITDA (+6.1% YoY required in H2). Using 🟢 strong for revenue classification (per rules, revenue is the primary metric).

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: net +1.4% (7.4p → 7.5p). Largely flat. The large revenue upgrade in Feb 26 (£92m → £104.6m → £105.9m) was accompanied by minimal EPS movement — signalling the market already knew the revenue was going up but margins were uncertain.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 7.5p since 14 Feb 26).
  • Post-today: EPS will be cut — EBITDA guidance £22m vs consensus £25.4m = −13.4%. EPS revision: −6 to −9% from 7.5p to ~6.8–7.1p.
  • Revenue revision: +4.8% upgrade to £110m.
  • Divergence: Share price 55p vs consensus TP 144p = 162% upside. The stock has collapsed from 160p (May 2025) to 55p as the Indirect revenue decline narrative has played out. The TP has not moved (flat at 144p since Feb 26 upgrade) but the price has fallen to a fraction of TP.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Currency: GBP.

  • Net cash: FY23 −£1.3m (H2) / FY24 +£19.6m (Sharescope H2) / FY25 −£1.5m (H2 Sharescope — likely restated; FY25 year-end per company = £30.8m cash) / H1 FY26: −£30.1m (Sharescope current H1 = net cash £30.1m) / RNS confirms £28.4m net cash at 31 Mar 2026 — slight revision of Sharescope. ⚠️ Sharescope "current H1" net cash £30.1m vs RNS £28.4m (small discrepancy, no major flag).

RNS vs forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash £28.4m vs Sharescope fc −£34.6m (net cash per Sharescope sign convention: −£34.6m means net cash £34.6m). RNS £28.4m vs Sharescope fc £34.6m = £6.2m below forecast. Explained by investment ramp (senior hires, US Direct build-out) and H1 EBITDA shortfall.

  • ND/EBITDA: net cash (negative leverage). Interest cover: 27.9x (Sharescope current). No leverage concern.
  • Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — no constraint.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • Revenue: £110m > FY25 £92.2m ✅✅
  • EPS: ~7.0p (estimated post-cut) > FY25 6.7p ✅ (barely)

Step 2 — FY27 vs FY26:

  • Revenue: £116.9m > £110m ✅✅
  • EPS: 8.3p > ~7.0p ✅✅ (+18.6% — FY27 consensus will need revision once FY26e is confirmed)

3.6 Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Indirect revenue structural decline: Meta Facebook algorithm changes reducing referral traffic and platform revenue-sharing. "Did not see a recovery in our Indirect revenue streams in H1 26, with referral volumes and previously announced changes to Meta's algorithm for Facebook continuing in line with trends experienced in H2 25." This is an ongoing structural decline — not a cyclical dip. Indirect was ~45% of FY25 revenues; now declining to <30% of FY26 revenues.   • Direct revenue mix shift — margin dilution: >70% of H1 revenues now Direct (FY25: ~55%). Direct revenue growing at 20%+ but at "lower margins than Indirect revenue streams." The EBITDA margin compression from this mix shift is structural and ongoing through FY27.

Now I have both documents. Working from the actual disclosures chronologically.

When was the Indirect decline first visible in the numbers?

H1 FY25 results (June 2025) — the numbers looked fine on the surface

H1 FY25 reported Indirect revenue up 18% to £24.5m. Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to £12.2m. Margin improved to 27.8% from 26.4%. On the face of it, no alarm. But there was a tell buried in the segmental detail: the 18% Indirect growth was explicitly described as being against "a weak prior year comparator on social platforms" and Social specifically grew 12% — which management attributed to "improved platform performance versus a softer prior year." That "softer prior year" was itself caused by Facebook algorithm changes, meaning the H1 FY25 Social growth was bounce, not acceleration.

Web grew 27% in H1 FY25 — a genuinely strong number but attributed to resolution of "prior period web-related issues," again signalling the comparison base was distorted.

So the first numerical warning sign was not the headline EBITDA margin — it was the quality of the Indirect growth. H1 FY25 Indirect growth was entirely base-effect driven. Strip that out and the underlying trajectory of the Social revenue stream was flat to slightly declining in absolute terms relative to a normalised prior period.

The content costs line was the other signal that gets ignored: up 29% in H1 FY25 while revenue grew only 13%. Content costs growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue is a margin compression indicator even when EBITDA margin looks healthy, because it means the business is working harder per pound of revenue. The H1 FY25 EBITDA margin of 27.8% was flattered by Indirect performing on a weak comp and held up because overhead growth was disciplined. Remove the comp benefit and the underlying margin was already under pressure.

The current trading section of H1 FY25 (June 2025) was the most direct signal available. Management stated: "Within our Indirect business, we have seen the impact of macro and tariff uncertainty on advertising spend and advertising yields since the half year." And specifically: "We are seeing a steady build-up in our Social revenue stream and a stabilisation in the Web revenue stream." "Stabilisation" in Web after the prior year's Web decline is not a recovery — it means flat. And the language on Social ("steady build-up") is deliberately modest, contrasting with the 12% and 18% growth figures they were reporting for H1.

That current trading paragraph, combined with the FX headwind warning (£2m revenue, £1m EBITDA impact), was the signal. Anyone reading it carefully in June 2025 at ~110p had the information to ask: if Indirect is merely "stabilising" post-H1 and Direct is the only growth engine, what does the margin mix look like in H2 and into FY26?

FY25 full year results (February 2026) — the deterioration became explicit

By the time the FY25 results landed the picture was fully disclosed:

Indirect Web declined −13% on a like-for-like 12-month basis (£16.2m vs £18.7m). Management attributed this to "weaker referral volumes and a tough prior-year comparator." The prior-year comparator for Web was itself inflated by the resolution of prior-period web issues in H1 FY25 — so the Web revenue line was distorting the picture in both directions across consecutive periods.

Indirect Social grew 12% for the full year — but the year-end exit rate matters more than the annual average. The current trading section of the FY25 results states for H1 FY26 outlook: "We expect our higher growth Direct revenue streams to make up an increasing proportion of Group revenue (expected to exceed 50% of Group revenues and potentially reaching 70%)." Indirect was already at 45% of FY25 revenues, down from 56% in H1 FY25. That trajectory — 56% → 45% → expected <30% — is a structural decline in the highest-margin revenue stream embedded in the guidance.

The FY25 results also introduced for the first time explicit margin guidance by segment: Direct margins "before central costs in the mid-20% range" vs Indirect margins "remaining above 50%." This was the disclosure that made the EBITDA margin compression mechanically calculable. If Direct grows from 54% to 70% of revenues at 20-something percent margin, while Indirect (50%+ margin) shrinks proportionally, the blended group EBITDA margin must fall — and the company acknowledged this by saying Group EBITDA margins would "remain in line with consensus." That consensus at the time was £25.4m adj EBITDA on £105m revenue = 24.2% margin, down from 27.4% in FY25. The guidance was essentially flagging a 300bp+ margin compression was already baked in.

What would the first numerical signal have been for a quantitative investor?

Not EBITDA margin at the headline level — that was still expanding in H1 FY25. The first quantitative signal was:

Content costs as a % of revenue growing faster than revenue — H1 FY25: content costs 17.3% of revenue vs H1 FY24: 15.2%. That's a 210bp increase in the content cost ratio. For a business where Indirect revenue required near-zero incremental content cost (platforms pay you based on existing content), rising content cost ratio indicates the mix is shifting toward Direct (which requires actively commissioned content) faster than the revenue split suggests.

The second was the note about Social revenue in H1 FY25 being against a "weak prior year comparator." When a company describes its own growth number with reference to a weak comp rather than absolute demand, that is an implicit acknowledgement that the absolute level of Social revenue in H1 FY24 was abnormally low, and the H1 FY25 growth does not represent a sustainable run-rate.

On the share price timing — 110p in June 2025 to 48p now

The H1 FY25 results at 110p in June 2025 contained the current trading warning on Indirect and the FX headwind disclosure. The H2 FY25 would have been the period (April–September 2025) where Indirect Web was declining 13% and Social was stabilising rather than growing. The FY25 full results in February 2026 then confirmed the strategic pivot — essentially management saying the business is deliberately shrinking its highest-margin revenue stream while investing heavily to replace it with lower-margin Direct. The market had been pricing that transition risk progressively since June 2025.

Today's H1 FY26 update shows the transition is happening faster than consensus assumed: Indirect EBITDA contribution is collapsing (H1 EBITDA £8m vs £12.2m prior, −34%) while the revenue replacement from Direct (+19% top line) hasn't come with sufficient margin to compensate. The £22m FY26 EBITDA guidance vs £25.4m consensus is the finalisation of a process that was visible in outline from June 2025 if you looked at content cost ratios, the quality of the Indirect growth figures, and the current trading language carefully.

1. Revenue figures

No Q1 revenue figures disclosed. The RNS is an AGM-style trading statement. Full year FY26 guidance reiterated: organic constant currency revenue growth of 6.5–7.5% (from FY25 results press release; this Q1 statement says guidance is on track). No specific H1 or Q1 revenue number.

FY25 reported revenue (from Sharescope current = FY25 actual): £9,346m. Applying 6.5–7.5% CC organic growth:

  • Low end: £9,346m × 1.065 = £9,953m (CC)
  • High end: £9,346m × 1.075 = £10,047m (CC)

At current GBP/USD 1.3515 vs prior avg 1.278 (GBP +5.7% stronger), ~50% USD revenues → headline revenue ~3% lower than CC:

  • Reported guidance range: ~£9,653–£9,745m
  • vs FY26e consensus £9,878.2m — consensus appears to be ABOVE the implied reported range at current spot rate. Potential downside to consensus of ~−£133m to −£225m if GBP stays at 1.35.

Note: The Q1 trading statement RNS doesn't explicitly restate the CC guidance figures — these are derived from the FY25 preliminary results RNS.

2. EPS / earnings figures

No EPS data. The statement says the group is "on track to deliver revenue and profit growth, in line with our full year guidance." Full year guidance: Group operating profit in the range of $720–770m (per FY25 results).

Wait — that's HIK's guidance. Let me re-read LSEG. LSEG's statement: "Group full year outlook unchanged" — refers to organic CC revenue growth of 6.5–7.5% and underlying EBITDA margin expansion. No specific EPS guidance restated.

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • (1) New base EPS FY25 actual: 418.2p (H1 207.7p + H2 210.5p)
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: No major new acquisitions in Q1. LSEG sold Acadia (agreed sale completed 2025). Net: small positive from any partial-year disposals anniversary. Approximately +0 to +5p.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: CC revenue +6.5–7.5% × ~47% EBITDA margin = incremental EBITDA ~£280–330m. Post D&A/interest/tax and on ~490m diluted shares (post-buybacks): ~+15–25p EPS uplift from organic growth.
  • (4) Interest step-up: Incremental debt ~£5.8bn at ~5% = £290m gross interest incremental. However this is partly offset by buyback EPS benefit (fewer shares). Net: interest headwind roughly offset by share count reduction. Net delta: approximately 0 to −5p.
  • (5) FX headwind: GBP +5.7% vs avg on 50% USD revenues = ~2.8% reported revenue headwind = ~£276m revenue at risk. At ~47% EBITDA margin: ~£130m EBITDA at risk. Post-tax: ~£101m / 490m shares = ~21p EPS headwind from FX translation.

Implied FY26e EPS: 418.2p + 20p (organic) − 21p (FX) − 5p (interest net) + 5p (buyback share reduction) = ~417–425p. vs Sharescope FY1 fc 470.3p. Gap of ~45–53p — significant. The consensus appears to embed less FX headwind than current spot implies, or uses a more favourable FX assumption.

This suggests consensus EPS of 470.3p is optimistic at current GBP/USD levels — or that LSEG hedges a significant portion of USD revenue. The EPS bridge indicates meaningful downside risk to consensus if GBP/USD stays at 1.35 for FY26.

No margin data in Q1 statement. FY26 guidance from FY25 results: underlying EBITDA margin expansion expected (mid to high single-digit OCC revenue growth + moderate cost growth = positive operating leverage).

5. Capital returns

FY25 preliminary results context: £2.1bn returned in FY25 via buybacks. Further £3bn buyback planned by Feb 2027. Final dividend FY25: 103.0p per share (+15.7%). These are already embedded in consensus.

6. Qualitative tone

CEO (David Schwimmer): "We are pleased with the progress we've made at the start of 2026. Our strategy is working; we're meeting our customers' evolving needs and growing our business." Brief, positive, no specifics.

The EPS upgrade cycle — +73.7p (+18.6%) over the past 11 months, with a major step-change post-FY25 results — is the most constructive backdrop. But the headline story for brokers is not the trading statement itself; it is the FX headwind from GBP strengthening.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, H1 revenue and EPS are UNTRACKABLE. The upgrade resilience case is strong on a constant currency basis: CC organic revenue growth 6.5–7.5% compounds off a growing subscription base, EBITDA margin expansion is guided, and the buyback programme is reducing share count by an estimated ~25–35m shares from FY25. However, the FX translation problem is a structural overhang that brokers cannot ignore. At GBP/USD 1.3515 vs prior average 1.278 (GBP +5.7% stronger), approximately 50% of revenues are USD-denominated, implying a ~2.8% reported revenue headwind and ~20–25p EPS drag from pure translation. The implied H2 EPS burden of 235.1p vs FY25 H2's 210.5p (+11.7%) is achievable on a CC basis but may undershoot on a reported basis.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: On this Q1 statement, FY26e EPS will likely be held at ~470p (no P&L data to move numbers) but FX-aware brokers will caveat with a −20 to −25p sensitivity note if GBP/USD stays at 1.35. Revenue consensus of £9,878m carries −£200–280m downside at current spot. TP of £122.54 is likely to hold pending H1 results — the 29% implied upside at £95.10 reflects the market's scepticism about FX.

🏁 Verdict: credible subscription model with strong CC growth, but GBP headwind of −11 pts is the dominant quantifiable risk that is not reflected in consensus at current spot rate; score 44 post-FX penalty — neutral hold pending H1 results where FX impact will be disclosed.

LUCE — Luceco PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue by geography: UK £214.6m (79.1% of £271.4m), Europe £24.1m (8.9%), Americas £20.1m (7.4%), Middle East & Africa £9.4m (3.5%), Asia Pacific £3.2m (1.2%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. Revenue bridge shows currency impact of −£3.2m (−1.3%) — modest. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 14.2p · Revenue £271.2m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 15.1p · Revenue £283.6m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 12.6p → 14.2p = +1.6p (+12.7%). Steady upgrade: 12.6p (May) → 13.1p (May–Jul) → 12.9p (Aug cut) → 13.3p (Nov) → 14.1p (Jan 2026) → 14.2p (Feb). Notable: cut in August (12.9p) followed by recovery and further upgrades. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 14.2p / £271.2m for 6 weeks). Revenue: £263.2m → £271.2m (+3.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.4% of FY = £131.3m · EPS 47.2% of FY = 6.7p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £109.6m · EPS 5.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £271.2m − H1 actual £125.7m = implied H2 £145.5m vs prior H2 £132.9m → +9.5% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 14.2p − 5.9p = 8.3p vs prior H2 6.8p → +22.1% YoY — strong H2 leverage expectation in consensus already.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Audited results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 revenue: £271.4m, up 11.9% vs £242.5m in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of £271.2m: beat of £0.2m (+0.1%) — essentially exactly in line. Like-for-like revenue (ex-currency, ex-acquisitions): +4.6%. Acquisition contribution: +8.7% (D-Line and CMD full year).

"Revenue of £271.4m was £28.9m (11.9%) higher than 2024 with particularly strong revenue in the second half of the year."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Adjusted basic EPS: 15.0p, up 20.0% vs 12.5p in FY2024.

vs FY1 consensus of 14.2p: beat of +0.8p (+5.6%).

Statutory basic EPS: 13.5p (2024: 9.5p).

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on adjusted PBT: 18.7% (2024: 22.9%). Normal UK corporation tax rate: 25.0%. The 18.7% rate is materially below the standard rate. Reason stated: "recognition of a deferred tax asset in relation to US losses from prior years." This is a non-recurring tax benefit.

Restated EPS at normalised 22.9% rate: Adjusted PBT £27.8m × (1 − 22.9%) = £21.45m adjusted PAT. Shares ~150.5m basic. Restated adjusted EPS = ~£21.45m/150.5m = ~14.25p vs headline 15.0p. 🚨 Tax benefit inflates headline EPS by ~0.75p vs normalised rate. On a normalised basis, EPS beats consensus of 14.2p by only ~0.05p — essentially no beat on a like-for-like tax basis. This significantly changes the quality of the earnings beat. The adjusted EPS of 15.0p must be used with caution for forward guidance purposes.

3. Operating profit / margin

Adjusted Operating Profit: £33.8m, up 16.6% vs £29.0m in FY2024. Adjusted operating margin: 12.5% (2024: 12.0%) — +50bps expansion. Three-year CAGR above 15%.

"Adjusted Operating Profit of £33.8m, up 16.6% year on year (2024: £29.0m). Adjusted Operating Profit margin continuing to grow each year, up 50 basis points to 12.5%."

4. EV charging — Energy Transition

EV charging sales: £18.1m (+84.7%). Total Energy Transition revenue contribution growing strongly. Demand Flexibility revenue nascent but becoming meaningful in 2026 — incremental upside.

"Products sold relating to the Energy Transition have been key to the underlying growth with £18.1m of sales from EV chargers, which is an increase of 84.7%."

5. Free cash flow / balance sheet

Adjusted FCF: £30.4m (2024: £3.5m) — exceptional improvement driven by working capital reversal (£5.3m inflow vs £17.2m outflow in 2024). Bank Net Debt: £52.3m (2024: £68.6m), ND/EBITDA 1.2x (2024: 1.6x) — within 1.0–2.0x target.

"Adjusted Free Cash Flow of £30.4m which benefited from working capital inflows, reversing the working capital outflow from 2024."

6. Dividend

Proposed full year dividend: 6.0p (2024: 5.0p), +20%. Earnings cover: 2.5x. Dividend policy consistent.

7. FY2026 outlook — explicit guidance upgrade

"The Board now expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — vs consensus range of £34.7m–£36.5m (+1.4% to +6.6% beat at minimum). With the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility.

First two months of 2026: "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth."

"The Board now expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m, with the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — explicit numeric guidance above consensus. Covers one year (FY2026). Demand Flexibility provides additional upside not in current guidance. LFL double-digit revenue growth in Q1 2026.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit above-consensus numeric guidance for FY26. Provisional points: +14.
  • Divergence check: FY25 EPS beat of +5.6% (headline) / +0.05p normalised, plus 🟢🟢 upgrade-triggering FY26 guidance. However: the EPS beat quality is impaired by the tax deferred asset benefit (🚨 above). The FY26 guidance does NOT factor Demand Flexibility — so the upgraded guidance is on a conservative base. Direction consistent. Flag 🟡 Beat quality — FY25 adjusted EPS beat partly driven by below-normalised tax rate (DTA recognition); normalised EPS ~14.25p, not 15.0p. Carry as row in Phase 5.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Revenue growth trajectory: +1.3%, +16.0%, +11.9% → 🟢 Steady — strong growth in FY24/FY25 (acquisition-boosted). Organic LFL at 4.6%.

EPS growth trajectory: +0.9%, +12.6%, +20.0% → 🟢 Accelerating — three consecutive years of acceleration.

Revenue trajectory (HoH YoY): +8.4%, +23.3%, +14.7%, +9.6% → 🟢 Steady — consistent double-digit growth.

EPS trajectory (HoH YoY): H2: +9.7%, +33.8% — strong H2 acceleration. H1: +16.3%, +3.5% — H1 EPS growth modest in FY25 (partly due to restructuring charges in H1 per the RNS: £0.4m). 🟢 Accelerating on H2 basis; full year 🟢 Accelerating.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 48.4% × £271.2m = £131.3m
  • EPS baseline: 47.2% × 14.2p = 6.7p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £125.7m ÷ FY1 consensus £271.2m = 46.4% vs baseline 48.4% → deviation = 🔴 [−2.0pp] → 🔴 CAUTION
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 5.9p ÷ FY1 consensus 14.2p = 41.5% vs baseline 47.2% → deviation = 🔴 [−5.7pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL — H1 EPS materially behind seasonal norm; all resolved by H2 actual 9.1p (well above H2 norm of ~7.5p)
  • H2 EPS burden: FY consensus 14.2p − H1 actual 5.9p = 8.3p vs historical H2 avg ~6.5p — burden HIGHER than consensus assumed, yet delivered 9.1p. Excellent H2 execution.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [£131.3m × 1.015] = £133.3m → 🔴 ✗ (£125.7m < £133.3m) · H1 EPS > [6.7p × 1.015] = 6.8p → 🔴 ✗ (5.9p < 6.8p)
  • Historical hit rate: Both buy triggers missed at H1 stage. Yet FY delivered a beat — driven entirely by H2 outperformance. This is a company where H1 tracking signals were negative but H2 execution drove the outcome.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • H2 Revenue actual: £145.7m vs prior H2 £132.9m → +9.6% YoY → 🟢 moderate/strong (approaching >+10%)
  • H2 EPS actual: 9.1p vs prior H2 6.8p → +33.8% YoY → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 12.6p → 14.2p, net +1.6p (+12.7%). One hiccup (Aug cut to 12.9p) followed by recovery and sustained upgrades through Jan/Feb 2026.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 14.2p for 6 weeks)
  • Divergence: Price flat at 163–204p range in last 6 months despite EPS upgrades — suggests the market was cautious on EV/Energy Transition delivery. Post-results, the explicit £37m+ FY26 guidance should re-rate the stock.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Demand Flexibility — nascent but potentially transformative]: The EV charger installed base (10,000+ chargers enrolled in Demand Flexibility programme) creates a new recurring revenue stream with significant upside. Management says "significant potential upside to profit as more are enrolled" — not in current guidance. This is a genuine structural optionality item.

[FCF recovery — working capital normalisation]: £30.4m FCF (vs £3.5m in FY24) is partly a working capital reversal (Red Sea inventory build unwinding). Average 5-year FCF £20.3m — the 2025 figure is above-average and partly non-recurring. Sustainable FCF closer to £18–22m range.

[Deferred tax asset — one-off EPS boost]: As flagged in EPS quality check above — ~0.75p of the EPS beat is a non-recurring tax benefit. Forward guidance (£37m+ operating profit) is not subject to this distortion as it is an operating metric.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Explicit FY26 AOP guidance of "exceeds £37m" vs consensus £34.7–£36.5m: This is the primary re-rating catalyst. An explicit "exceeds" guidance above the entire consensus range triggers mandatory estimate upgrades. With H1 2026 already delivering "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth" and the Demand Flexibility upside not included in guidance, the tone is as bullish as Luceco has communicated in years.

#2 Driver — H2 FY25 EPS acceleration (+33.8% H2 YoY, 9.1p) — execution quality confirmed: Despite H1 tracking signals being weak (sell signal on EPS), the H2 delivery was exceptional. This demonstrates the back-half-weighted earnings structure and validates brokers who held Buy ratings through the soft H1.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: UP — from 14.2p to 15.5–16.5p (+9–16%), reflecting £37m+ AOP at ~18–20% tax rate normalised. Revenue: UP to £285–295m from £271.2m consensus.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UP — from 15.1p to 17.0–18.5p (+13–23%), with Demand Flexibility now in scope for broker models.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 204p likely revised to 220–250p range. At 163.4p, upside to revised TP: 35–53%. Brokers will reinforce Buy/reiterate Buy. No recommendation downgrades expected.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Exceeds £37m" with "potential for further significant outperformance" is classic two-tier conservative guidance. The floor is upgradeable. Demand Flexibility is explicitly called out as upside — this will feature prominently in broker notes.

Key risk: The deferred tax asset benefit in FY25 EPS creates noise. Brokers must normalise to ~14.25p FY25 EPS (not 15.0p) as the base — otherwise FY26 EPS comparatives will look disappointing when the DTA benefit unwinds. Americas/MEA revenue declining (Americas −10.7%, MEA −8.7%) — international headwinds persist.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade (+9–16%). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. → 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

76/100 · Confidence: 70–82 · No FX adjustment · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Explicit FY26 AOP guidance "exceeds £37m" — above entire consensus range (£34.7–36.5m)+16
🟢 H2 FY25 EPS +33.8% YoY — exceptional H2 execution+10
🟢 EV charging +84.7%, Demand Flexibility nascent upside not in guidance+8
🟢 FCF £30.4m — strong cash generation, ND/EBITDA 1.2x+7
🟢 LFL double-digit revenue growth in Q1 2026 confirmed+7
🟢 EPS upgrade cycle +12.7% over year — sustained direction+5
🟡 Beat quality — FY25 adj EPS headline 15.0p; normalised ~14.25p after DTA benefit−5
🟡 H1 EPS tracking: −5.7pp sell signal (resolved by H2, but H1 was genuinely weak)−3
🔴 Americas −10.7%, MEA −8.7% — international revenue declining−4
🔴 FCF partly non-recurring (working capital reversal, one-year benefit)−3
🔴 EPS revenue beat essentially zero at normalised tax (£271.4m vs £271.2m)−3
🔴 Demand Flexibility regulatory uncertainty — "evolving framework, uncertain end-user response"−3
🔴 D-Line/CMD integration margin drag — Wiring Accessories margin 14.8% vs 17.5% prior−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst is the explicit FY26 guidance: "Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £37m" — the entire analyst consensus range was £34.7–£36.5m, making this a minimum 1.4–6.6% beat before a single FY26 number is reported. Combined with "like-for-like double-digit revenue growth" in the first two months of 2026, this is the clearest upgrade-triggering language Luceco has used in several years. FY25 Adjusted Operating Profit of £33.8m (+16.6%, margin 12.5%) and adjusted EPS of 15.0p (+20%) met the headline beat vs 14.2p consensus — though on a normalised tax basis, the clean EPS is ~14.25p (🚨 deferred tax asset recognition boosted reported EPS by ~0.75p).

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 EPS tracking signal was a sell (−5.7pp), yet the FY beat was delivered entirely via H2 outperformance — H2 EPS was 9.1p (+33.8% YoY), comfortably exceeding the elevated H2 burden of 8.3p required vs consensus. This is a company structurally weighted to H2 (Energy Transition sales skew to autumn/winter via EV charging demand and contractor seasonality), and H2 execution confirmed the structural thesis. The bear case for downgrades is limited: Demand Flexibility is not yet in guidance but provides genuine upside optionality with 10,000+ chargers already enrolled generating nascent revenue — management targets this becoming "a more predictable, recurring and considerable long-term revenue stream" within 12–24 months.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades from 14.2p to 15.5–16.5p (+9–16%) are likely, with revenue moving to £285–295m and operating profit to £37m+ (potentially £38–40m with Demand Flexibility). FY27 EPS moves from 15.1p to 17.0–18.5p (+13–23%) — the widest upgrade range for any single company today. Target price from 204p to 220–250p, implying 35–53% upside from 163.4p. The main watch point: normalise FY25 EPS to ~14.25p before comparing FY26 estimates to avoid making the FY26 growth rate look overstated. 🏁 Strongly positive: explicit above-consensus FY26 guidance, H2 execution vindicated, Demand Flexibility as material upside catalyst — upgrade cycle starting; normalise for DTA before modelling EPS growth rate. Score 76/100.

scorecards.analysisTitle: MAB1 · Mortgage Advice Bureau Holdings · 17 Mar 2026
scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (Q2). RNS = FY Results year ended 31 December 2025. No FX rule — GBP-only UK mortgage intermediary.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 44.3p, Revenue £314.4m. FY2: EPS 51.7p, Rev £353.8m.
  • Momentum: EPS +2.5% (43.2p→44.3p). Revenue +4.5%. TP raised £10.75→£11.33 Feb 2026. Last-4-week FLAT. Classification: steady/stalling.
  • Implied H2 (pre-RNS): Rev H2 cns £166.2m vs prior H2 £142.6m = +16.5%. Actual H2 = £170.6m = +2.6% beat vs implied H2 cns.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

FY Results — Year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue: £318.8m vs cns £314.4m = +1.4% beat. +19.6% YoY (3rd consecutive year of acceleration: +3.8%→+11.3%→+19.6%).
    "Revenue up 19.6% to £318.8m (2024: £266.5m)"
  2. Adj diluted EPS: 44.5p vs cns 44.3p = +0.5% beat (in-line). +13.5% YoY.
    "Adjusted diluted EPS up 13.5% to 44.5p (2024: 39.2p)"
  3. Adj PBT: £36.3m (+0.6% beat). Margin 11.4% vs 12.0% (−0.6pp). 360bps gap to 15%+ medium-term target.
    "adjusted PBT margin was 11.4% (2024: 12.0%)"
  4. Admin cost ratio: 17.6% vs 17.1% (+0.5pp). Admin expenses +23% vs revenue +19.6%. FY26 cost ratio will increase further.
    "The cost ratio is therefore expected to increase in 2026 as these businesses are annualised within the Group, before moderating as integration progresses"
  5. FY26 current trading: Q1 apps +13% YoY. In line with Board expectations.
    "Mortgage applications in Q1 to date have increased by 13% year-on-year"
  6. Fixed-rate maturities: +19% in 2026 vs market forecast +3–6%.
    "The Group's fixed-rate maturities are 19% higher in 2026, materially ahead of the overall refinancing market"
  7. Adviser growth: +10% to 2,135; rev/adviser +13% to £157k.
    "Closing mainstream advisers up 10% to 2,135… Revenue per mainstream adviser up 13% to £157k"
  8. Dividend: Full-year 22.5p (policy change to 50% adj post-tax profit; prior 28.2p). Final 15.3p (+3.4%). Progressive policy adopted.
    "full-year dividend of 22.5p per share (2024: 28.2p)"
  9. Main Market listing Q2 2026: ESCC category, FTSE All-Share eligibility.
    "Subject to FCA approval, MAB expects to complete the move to the Main Market in Q2 2026"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: FY23 +3.8% → FY24 +11.3% → FY25 +19.6%. Classification: Accelerating — three consecutive years.
  • H2 FY25: Rev £170.6m (+19.6% vs £142.6m). Beat implied cns H2 by +2.6%. EPS 26.3p (+7.8% vs 24.4p) — moderate; admin costs explain gap.
  • Margin flag: Adj PBT margin 11.4% — 360bps below 15%+ target. FY26 cost ratio explicitly flagged to increase further. Constrains EPS upgrade magnitude.
  • Catalyst flag: Main Market Q2 2026 — FTSE All-Share eligibility, passive fund flows not yet in consensus.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 — Revenue beat +1.4% and 3yr acceleration (+19.6%): Lead item in all broker notes. Q1 +13% apps and +19% fixed maturity tailwind provide concrete FY26 evidence.
2#2 — Margin compression with explicit FY26 cost headwind: Adj PBT margin 11.4% (−0.6pp) with management warning admin cost ratio will increase further in FY26. 360bps gap to 15% target. Constrains upgrade magnitude.
3FY2 EPS +2–5% to ~53–54p; Revenue hold/+2%. Full-year annualisation of H2 2025 acquisitions supports EPS; near-term margin headwinds cap upside.
4TP raise to £12–13; Main Market Q2 2026 catalyst: FTSE All-Share eligibility adds incremental positive not yet priced. Current 540p vs TP £11.33+ implies wide upside even on modest upgrades.
5Key risk — FY26 cost ratio trajectory + Q1 pull-forward risk: Admin costs will increase in FY26 before synergies flow. Geopolitical Middle East uncertainty creates potential Q1 pull-forward from Q2.
6Overall tone: Constructive / modest upgrades. Peel Hunt, Berenberg, KBW publish positive notes. EPS upgrades 2–5% FY2. Main Market adds incremental catalyst. Wide price-to-TP gap means modest upgrades could drive material price recovery.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

Baseline+50

MAB1 delivered solid FY25 results: revenue beat of +1.4% (£318.8m vs £314.4m), adj diluted EPS in-line at 44.5p vs 44.3p, and a third consecutive year of accelerating revenue growth to +19.6% YoY. FY26 current trading is positive with Q1 applications +13% YoY and MAB's fixed-rate maturity book running 19% higher than the market's 3–6% forecast. Adviser count +10%, productivity +13%, and net debt reduced to £3.3m all point to a well-functioning organic growth engine.

The key constraint is margin compression with an explicit FY26 cost headwind. Adj PBT margin fell to 11.4% (−0.6pp, 360bps below 15%+ target) with admin costs growing faster than revenue. Management explicitly warned the admin cost ratio will increase further in FY26 as H2 2025 acquisitions annualise. This limits FY2 EPS upgrade magnitude to 2–5% rather than 10%+. Consensus had already partially re-rated (EPS +2.5%, TP raised Feb 2026).

Brokers are expected to publish constructive notes targeting TP raises to £12–13 and FY2 EPS upgrades of 2–5%. The Main Market listing in Q2 2026 (FTSE All-Share eligibility) adds an incremental re-rating catalyst not yet fully priced in. At 540p versus consensus TP of £11.33–13.00, even modest upgrades could have disproportionate price impact. Watch points: FY26 admin cost ratio trajectory, acquisition synergy realisation pace, and Q1 conversion to completions without H2 pull-forward effect.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MANO · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Full Year Trading Update for year ended 31 March 2026)

  1. Revenue — in-line with consensus: FY26 Realised Revenue expected at c.£28.0m (FY25: £29.5m). Consensus was £28.3m → −1.1% miss (marginal). YoY: −5.1% decline vs FY25. "FY26 Realised Revenue for the full year is expected to be in line with expectations at c.£28.0m (FY25: £29.5m)."
  2. EPS / PBT — ahead of consensus but complexity in the numbers: Adjusted Realised PBT of £1.9m expected (FY25: £0.6m) before potential bad debt provision of £1.5m–£2.0m. Consensus PBT = £1.5m → stated figure of £1.9m = +26.7% beat pre-provision. Post-provision (if £1.5–2.0m charged): PBT = −£0.1m to +£0.4m = effectively breakeven or slight miss vs £1.5m consensus. "The Company's expectation of Adjusted Realised Profit Before Tax (PBT) is £1.9m (FY25: £0.6m) before any adjustment for these debtors." "The Company will consider some provision against these debtors, which is likely to be in the region of £1.5m–£2.0m."
  3. EPS quality check — bad debt provision is a real economic item. The £1.5m–£2.0m bad debt provision relates to two debtors who have not paid for >6 months ("payment continues to be delayed"). While the board says it expects full recovery, the auditor-driven provision process is underway. This is not a one-off non-cash item — it reflects real credit risk. At £1.5m provision on a £1.9m pre-provision PBT, the post-provision PBT is approximately £0.4m, equating to approximately 0.9p EPS vs consensus 2.5p. 🚨 EPS quality: pre-provision beat is misleading; post-provision EPS likely ~0.4–0.9p vs 2.5p consensus = material miss. Apply to forward guidance assessment: FY27 guidance is based on a potentially overstated FY26 base.
  4. FY26e EPS bridge (FY26 → FY27):
    • New base FY26 EPS actual: ~0.9p post-provision (vs stale consensus 2.5p)
    • Forward book growth: £67m forward book (+37% YoY from £49m). This is the key forward driver — "higher value cases" underpinning FY27 confidence.
    • New case signings: £32m signed in FY26 (+23% YoY) — pipeline building
    • Bad debt resolution: if the £4.7m exposure is recovered in FY27, this provides an uplift
    • FY27 EPS consensus 6.3p vs likely revised FY26 base ~0.9p = +600% implied recovery — requires significant H1 FY27 case completion momentum. Achievable if forward book delivers, but starting from a lower actual base than consensus assumed.
  5. Cash receipts — solid operating signal: Gross cash receipts £26.6m (+£1.0m YoY vs £25.6m). Net debt £11.5m (FY25: £11.1m) — slightly higher. Free cash flow: −£0.2m outflow (FY25: +£0.5m inflow). Cash receipts are healthy but net debt ticked up and FCF turned negative — not alarming but directionally softer. "Gross cash receipts were strong at £26.6m and represent a £1.0m increase versus the prior year."
  6. Forward book — significant growth, key FY27 driver: Forward book at 31 March 2026 = £67m (vs £49m FY25 = +37% YoY). Large cases (>£0.5m forecast revenue) = £32m of the book (vs £21m = +52%). This is a genuine positive signal for FY27. "The forward book at 31 March 2026 was £67m and has grown by £18m or 37% year-on-year."
  7. New case signings — positive operational signal: £32m new cases signed FY26 (+23% YoY vs £26m). Management expects further increase in FY27 from enlarged team.
  8. Bad debt overhang — two debtors, £4.7m net exposure: Board "remains confident" of full recovery but auditor-driven review underway. This is a binary risk item — if provision = £1.5–2.0m in FY26 accounts, and if further provisions required in FY27, this overhang will weigh on EPS credibility. "Two of these payments continue to be delayed and the Company's net exposure to these debtors is approximately £4.7m."
  9. Leadership refresh — execution risk/opportunity: New CEO (Aug 2025), new CFO (Dec 2025), new NED (Mar 2026). New management team bringing fresh strategy but also early-stage execution. Former CEO share retention requirement waived by HSBC.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • FY27 language: "Board are confident of increasing Realised Revenue and Realised PBT in FY27."
  • Basis: £67m forward book (+37%) and elevated UK insolvency market.
  • Forward guidance: qualitative only. No numeric FY27 guidance.
  • Context: FY26 PBT beat is pre-provision; post-provision FY26 likely below consensus.
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — qualitative-only forward guidance following a beat driven by a distorted base (pre-provision PBT ahead but post-provision likely misses). Revenue in line. No numeric uplift. Provisional: +1 pt.
  • Divergence check: Current year revenue miss vs consensus (£28.0m vs £28.3m) + EPS quality distorted by bad debt provision. Forward guidance positive but qualitative-only on a potentially overstated base. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery — FY26 EPS quality impaired by provision; FY27 guidance built on a base that assumes provision recovery. Carry as named row in Phase 5.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

MANO · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Cross-checks:

  • FY26 H1 + implied H2: £12.7m + £15.3m (derived) = £28.0m (RNS confirmed)
  • FY25: H1 £14.4m + H2 £16.1m = £30.5m (vs stated £29.5m in RNS — ⚠️ discrepancy. Sharescope FY25 = £30.5m vs RNS-stated FY25 = £29.5m. Using RNS figure £29.5m as authoritative; Sharescope H2 FY25 £16.1m may include a restatement. Note discrepancy.)
  • FY24: H1 £11.2m + H2 £15.1m = £26.3m ✓; EPS 4.8p ✓
  • FY23: H1 £5.5m + H2 £15.2m = £20.7m ✓; EPS −4.4p

EPS: FY26 H1 −1.1p + H2 implied 3.6p (= 2.5p consensus). Post-provision: H2 EPS ~0.9p − (−1.1p) = 2.0p... Actually: if FY26 adjusted PBT = £1.9m pre-provision, and provision = £1.5–2.0m, the net PBT = £0.4m → EPS ~0.9p. So the 3.6p implied H2 from consensus is likely wrong. H2 implied adj EPS 4.2p vs 3yr avg H2 = (5.5p + 6.2p + 3.9p)/3 = 5.2p → −19.2% → 🔴 weak (but note H2 EPS boosted by low tax rate; underlying H2 weaker)

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS: −28.0% net change over full period (9.3p → 6.7p) — sustained downgrade cycle
  • TP: −10% (150p → 135p)
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (6.7p frozen for 10 weeks)
  • Divergence: EPS estimates stopped falling — consensus has stabilised at 6.7p. The actual beat of 7.50p vs 6.7p implies estimates were too low. Post-results, expect upgrades from 6.7p toward 7.0–7.5p.

5. Structural Flags

  • Carlton production delay (one-off): The two-week extended shutdown and commissioning delay cost ~3m units manufacturing output, suppressing FY25 EBITDA. This is non-recurring and will normalise in FY26.
  • Watlington closure (one-off): £1.4m exceptional cost but removes a cash-consuming leasehold. FY26 benefits from eliminated overheads.
  • Floren structural challenge: Belgium housing ~40% below 2022 peak with no near-term recovery catalyst. The prolonged Belgian market downturn is a medium-term structural drag; not a one-off.
  • CFO transition: Warren resigned after only ~6 months. Mahoney taking CFO responsibilities again. Second CFO change in under 12 months creates governance concern.
  • Mineral reserves extension at Floren: New exhaust scrubber system enabled change in input materials, significantly extending Floren's mineral reserves. Long-term structural positive.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Adjusted EPS 7.50p beats consensus 6.7p by +12% The dominant broker note item will be the EPS beat — consensus had been progressively cut to 6.7p and the actual came in at 7.50p, largely due to a low effective tax rate (15.9% vs 25% normalised). Brokers will debate whether to adjust for the tax benefit (~1.3p) or use the headline figure. Either way, FY25 adj EPS of 7.50p is above prior consensus 6.7p, arresting the downgrade cycle.

#2 Driver — FY26 growth guidance and one-off cost normalisation Management explicitly states "confident the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025." The Carlton production delay was one-off, and Watlington closure removes ongoing overhead. Floren is still challenged but the Belgium market commentary ("70,000 homes/year target") provides a medium-term recovery story. FY26 consensus will be revised upward from current 8.4p.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: consensus 8.4p pre-results; given 7.50p FY25 base and "growth" guidance, FY26 EPS likely held or modestly upgraded to 8.0–9.0p range. The tax rate normalises to ~25% in FY26, so operating profit growth needs to be substantial to maintain EPS vs FY25's low-tax number.
  • FY1 revenue: consensus £69.0m (matching FY25 actual); guidance for growth implies £70–73m range in FY26.
  • TP: Currently 135p; likely to hold or marginally move given the mixed picture. At 75p, stock at 56% discount to TP.

Conservative guidance: "Confident the Company will deliver growth in 2026 relative to 2025" — this is modestly positive but not aggressive. Order intake ahead of capacity is a positive leading indicator, but "predictability from order intake diluted" tempers enthusiasm.

Key risk: The tax benefit of 15.9% effective rate is non-recurring. At 25% normalised rate, FY25 adj profit after tax would have been: adj PBT £8.1m × 75% = £6.1m vs £6.8m actual. FY26 EPS will face a ~1.3p headwind from tax normalisation alone. Brokers will explicitly model this. Additionally the CFO departure is the second in under 12 months — governance concern. "Rachel Warren is stepping down from the Group Board with immediate effect due to personal reasons"

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — The EPS beat is real but tax-distorted, Floren remains challenged, and the CFO instability adds uncertainty.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Raw score: 40/100 · FX adjustment: −8 pts → Final score: 32/100 · Confidence: 24–39 (widened ±5pp for missing EUR prior avg rate) · 🔴 FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~33% EUR (Floren) · GBP headwind · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

ComponentPts
🟢 Adjusted EPS 7.50p — +12% beat vs consensus 6.7p+10
🟢 Revenue broadly in-line (−0.1% miss)+5
🟢 FY26 growth guidance explicit from management+5
🟢 Carlton one-off production delay non-recurring+4
🟢 Watlington closure removes ongoing overhead drag+3
🟡 H1 seasonal tracking IN LINE (both revenue and EPS)−2
🟡 EPS broker trend FLAT — no upgrade momentum pre-RNS−2
🔴 FX Rule 1 applied — ~33% EUR, GBP headwind−8
🔴 Adjusted EBITDA £12.4m — misses consensus £12.7m−4
🔴 EPS beat driven by one-off tax rate (15.9% vs 25% norm) — non-recurring−5
🔴 Floren Belgium structural decline continuing (~20% revenue drop)−5
🔴 CFO departure second in 12 months — governance concern−4
🔴 Net debt £0.7m (from net cash £6.0m) — balance sheet weakening−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: MBH delivered FY25 results that were better than the market feared on EPS but not better in quality terms. Adjusted EPS of 7.50p beat the 6.7p consensus by 12%, but this was substantially driven by a 15.9% effective tax rate (vs 25% normalised) due to prior-year tax credits — stripping this out, underlying EPS was closer to 6.1p. Revenue of £68.9m missed £69.0m consensus marginally and declined 1.7% YoY. The primary operational driver of underperformance was a two-week extended Carlton shutdown in Q1 (costing ~3m manufacturing units) and Floren Belgium revenue declining ~20% as housing activity in Belgium remained ~40% below 2022 peak. Adjusted EBITDA of £12.4m was 2.4% below the £12.7m consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £33.1m is 4.9% below the three-year H2 average (borderline flat classification), reflecting the ongoing market malaise. H2 implied adj EPS of ~4.2p is roughly 19% below the three-year H2 average, though this is distorted by the tax benefit falling in the year. The seasonal tracking deviation was only −0.2pp on EPS and +0.4pp on revenue — IN LINE rather than signalling any directional breakout. The upgrade resilience rests on: (1) Carlton production delay is non-recurring; (2) Watlington closure removes cash-consuming overhead; (3) management's explicit "growth in 2026" statement. However, the FX headwind (GBP stronger vs EUR) is a tangible, ongoing drag on Floren's GBP-reported contribution that is absent from historical baselines. The CFO transition risk is the most unpredictable variable.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus of 8.4p should be held or modestly trimmed to 7.5–8.5p range once brokers normalise the tax rate — the 7.50p FY25 EPS at a 15.9% tax rate becomes approximately 6.1p on a like-for-like 25% tax basis, making "growth in 2026" against a normalised base more demanding than the headline implies. TP of 135p likely maintained or cut marginally to 125–130p. At 75p, there is 73% upside to TP on paper but the low price reflects sustained earnings disappointments and a challenging European market backdrop. The main watch point is Belgium housing recovery timing and whether the FX headwind persists. 🏁 Verdict: EPS beat is tax-distorted; underlying performance continues to disappoint against pre-2022 peak; Floren structural headwind + CFO instability + FX drag make this a cautious hold. FX-adjusted score 32/100.

MEGP — PHASE 0

Phase 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (12 months ended 31 October 2025). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

ME Group generates the majority of revenue outside GBP. Continental Europe £215.5m (68% of total) — EUR-denominated. Asia Pacific £49.8m (16%) — JPY-dominated. Total non-GBP revenues ~84%.

EUR: >30% of revenues threshold clearly breached. JPY: ~16%, below 30% individually but additive.

Focusing on EUR (largest single non-GBP currency — approximately 55–60% of revenues given Continental Europe is mostly Eurozone):

Searched the web

Current GBP/EUR spot: ~1.157 (23 Mar 2026). ME Group's prior year average rate (FY2025): EUR/£ 1.178 (stated in RNS footnote 4). So GBP is weaker vs prior year average (1.157 vs 1.178) — GBP has depreciated ~2.1c vs the EUR.

EUR exposure: Continental Europe revenues £215.5m / total £315.4m = 68%. This is >50% exposure.

Direction: GBP/EUR spot 1.157 vs prior year avg 1.178 = GBP weaker by 1.8c (within ±2c band). This is neutral.

Penalty: 50%+ exposure · Neutral (±2c) → −5 to −6 pts. Applying mid-point: −5 pts.

Also checking JPY (Asia Pacific ~16% of revenues — below 30% trigger individually, so JPY assessed separately only if >30%. It is not. Skip JPY separately.)

Phase 0B result: EUR exposure ~68% of revenues · GBP/EUR spot 1.157 · prior year avg 1.178 · GBP weaker by ~2c (within ±2c band) → 🟡 neutral rate · FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · ~68% EUR · neutral rate

Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 15.0p/£314m/248p since late Jan 26). Revenue net change −4.8% over period.

Group revenue at constant currency +3.0%. "Total Group revenue increased by 2.4% to £315.4 million (+3.0% at constant currency)"
  2. EPS / earnings: Diluted EPS 14.91p vs consensus 15.0p = −0.6% miss (marginal). PBT £78.2m vs consensus implied ~£76.2m (FY1 fc PBT) = +2.6% beat. The EPS slight miss vs PBT beat is explained by higher effective tax rate (27.7% vs 26.3% prior year) from French tax reassessments. EBITDA £120.4m vs consensus £119.4m = +0.8% beat. "Record profit before tax at £78.2 million, up 6.5% (+7.1% at constant currency)"
  3. Order book / laundry pipeline: 7,607 laundry machines in operation (+17.7% YoY vs 6,462). Target 1,300+ installations in FY26. Next-gen photobooth programme: 3,079 installed vs 8,000 target by FY27. Laundry now 46.1% of total Group EBITDA. "1,145 net increase in laundry units (1,326 gross installations)"
  4. Margin / profitability: EBITDA margin improved to 38.2% (FY24: 37.1%). Laundry EBITDA margin 49.4% (+30bps). Photo.ME EBITDA margin 35.2% (stable). Germany regulatory impact limited to −£3.0m revenue in H2. Printer supplier issue (H1) now fully resolved; compensation received. Capex FY26 guided £57–59m (down from FY25 £65.6m). "Group EBITDA margin improved to 38.2% (2024: 37.1%)"

Net cash £26.5m (FY24: £29.5m). Gross cash £56.5m. "Launch of £18m share buyback" "Total dividend increased by 9.5%; returning £32.6 million to shareholders in respect of 2025"
  6. Qualitative tone / FY26 guidance: "Year-to-date performance is in line with expectations." Germany regulatory: deployment of new-gen machines begins H2 2026, recovery thereafter. Note: shares were suspended pending publication of this annual report — the announcement also includes "the Company will apply for the restoration of the listing and trading of its shares."   • EPS trend: Net −2.6% over full period (15.4p → 15.0p). Revenue cut −4.8% (£330m → £314m). TP cut from 297p to 248p (−16.5%). Steady stream of modest downgrades reflecting Germany photobooth regulatory headwind, FX, and strategic review uncertainty.

  • Divergence: Price 136.6p vs TP 248p = 81.5% upside to consensus TP. Extraordinary discount — reflects: (1) shares suspended pending annual report publication; (2) terminated strategic review; (3) declining EPS estimates; (4) declining TP. This is a recovery/re-listing catalyst, not a fundamental upgrade cycle.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

Share suspension and re-listing: Shares were suspended pending publication of the annual report. Today's announcement triggers restoration of listing. This is a technical re-listing event, not a fundamental change, but it removes an overhang.

"the Company will apply for the restoration of the listing and trading of its shares"

Germany photobooth regulatory change (permanent): Government regulation requiring ID photos at official offices or certified photographers — introduced May 2025. Revenue impact £3.0m in H2 2025. Group developing new-gen biometric booths for compliance (deployment H2 2026). This is a structural negative for German photobooth revenue until new machines deployed.

"The Group expects the impact to continue in FY 2026, with revenue recovering thereafter."

Strategic review terminated — no offer received: The Board confirmed in Dec 2025 that no acceptable offer was received and discussions terminated. Removes M&A premium from price, removes uncertainty — but also confirms no near-term exit catalyst.

£18m share buyback: Announced alongside results. At 136.6p, £18m buys approximately 13.2m shares (~3.5% of shares outstanding). Positive for EPS accretion in FY26.

MEGP — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — Laundry estate growth (+17.7% machines, EBITDA £55.5m +18.1%): This is the core thesis. Laundry now 46.1% of Group EBITDA. The roll-out momentum (1,326 gross installs in FY25 vs 1,168 in FY24) and FY26 target of 1,300+ machines confirms the structural growth engine is intact. Brokers will lead with laundry unit economics and trajectory.

#2 Driver — £18m buyback + 9.5% dividend increase: The capital return package is the second-order catalyst. At 136.6p the shares trade at a significant discount to intrinsic value (consensus TP 248p). The £18m buyback is ~3.5% of market cap, providing meaningful EPS accretion and signalling Board confidence at the current price.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) Revenue: consensus £314m — expect hold or slight trim to £310–315m as Germany photobooth headwind continues and laundry growth partially offsets. No material revision.
  • FY1 EPS: consensus 15.0p — with FY25 actual 14.91p and buyback accretion (+0.15–0.2p), expect hold to slight upgrade 15.1–15.5p.
  • FY2 Revenue: £326.2m — hold, consistent with ~3–4% growth as laundry mix continues to increase.
  • FY2 EPS: 15.5p — expect upgrade to 15.8–16.2p as buyback accretion folds in and Germany normalises.
  • TP: Consensus 248p vs price 136.6p. Expect hold at 248p or possible slight increase to 255–265p as re-listing removes discount. Brokers may revisit sum-of-parts given laundry's high EBITDA margin (49.4%) and growth rate.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with expectations" for FY26 YTD is neutral — not a "comfortable with current forecasts" or "not less than" statement. It does not increase upgrade probability but de-risks the FY26 start, especially given the listing restoration uncertainty.

Key risk: Germany photobooth regulatory impact continuing into FY26. The new biometric machines are not deploying until H2 2026, meaning the £3m+ revenue headwind continues for at least 9 months of FY26. Additionally, JPY weakness (1.9% depreciation vs GBP in FY25) will persist as a structural translation drag on Asia Pacific.

"The Group expects the impact to continue in FY 2026, with revenue recovering thereafter."

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — results are essentially in line, the structural laundry story is excellent, but the growth rate is decelerating, Germany is an ongoing headwind, the strategic review failed, and the stock was suspended. Re-listing removes the overhang but the underlying upgrade dynamics are muted.
