🟡 Broker EPS trend negative over full period (−2.6%); TP cut 297p→248p−5
🟡 FX headwind: EUR neutral (−5 pts applied from Phase 0B)−5
🟢 Share re-listing removes key overhang; 81% upside to consensus TP+6
🟡 "In line with expectations" FY26 guidance — no upgrade signal−3
🟢 Laundry unit count +17.7% YoY; FY26 target 1,300+ machines+4
🔴 JPY depreciation −1.9% vs GBP; structural Asia Pacific drag−3
🟡 Capex guided lower (£57–59m vs £65.6m) — positive for FCF but reflects maturation+2
🔴 EPS HoH decelerating sharply: +84% → +21% → +2.5%−5
🟢 EBITDA margin expansion 37.1% → 38.2% — structural improvement+5

Adjusted for FX penalty (−5 pts): 55/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: ME Group delivered a solid FY25 with PBT of £78.2m (+6.5% YoY), a +2.6% beat vs consensus at the operating profit level. Revenue of £315.4m (+2.4%) was essentially in line with the £314.0m forecast. The definitive catalyst in this announcement is not the in-line trading result but the dual shareholder return package: a 9.5% dividend increase to 8.64p and the launch of an £18m share buyback at a time when the stock sits 82% below consensus TP. The #1 metric for broker notes is laundry EBITDA of £55.5m (+18.1%), which now constitutes 46.1% of Group EBITDA and demonstrates the structural shift away from legacy photobooths is working.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The HoH revenue growth has decelerated from +24.7% (H1 FY24) to +2.6% in H2 FY25, reflecting the Germany photobooth headwind (£3.0m revenue impact), the H1 printer supplier issue (now resolved), and FX translation. Laundry vending revenue grew +10.2% despite the warm summer dampening demand — testament to the estate expansion. The Germany headwind is the most significant structural risk to the upgrade case: new biometric booths will not deploy until H2 FY26, meaning the negative impact on photobooth revenue persists for the first ~9 months of FY26. Against this, the £18m buyback (≈3.5% of shares) will provide +0.15–0.3p of EPS accretion in FY26, partially offsetting the Germany drag. The "in line with expectations" FY26 opening statement de-risks the near-term but provides no positive deviation.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 (FY26) EPS is expected to be held at 15.0–15.3p (very modest +0–2% revision as buyback accretion is offset by Germany continuation). FY2 EPS may see a slightly more positive revision to 15.8–16.2p (+2–5%) as Germany normalises post H2 2026 and laundry growth compounds. The consensus TP of 248p is likely to be held or marginally increased to 255–265p following re-listing — the stock at 136.6p already offers 82% upside and the buyback signals the Board agrees the discount is excessive. The main watch-point is Germany: if the new biometric photobooth rollout (H2 2026) meets its schedule, the FY27 recovery becomes a meaningful catalyst. 🏁 MEGP is a neutral-to-cautious hold on results: the underlying business is structurally sound with an excellent laundry engine, but the decelerating top-line, ongoing Germany headwind, failed strategic review and post-suspension re-listing dynamic keep a lid on near-term upgrade expectations. The buyback and dividend increase are positives but do not change the fundamental growth trajectory.

TICKER 4: MGNS

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-H1 trading update. Next year end = 31/12/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

MGNS · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). RNS is a trading update for FY26 (in progress), citing trading activity January–April 14 2026. Market expects H1 FY26 results in July 2026 (H1 results scheduled 23 July 2026 per RNS).
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 333.4p · Revenue £5,098.4m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 323.2p · Revenue £5,102.7m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over snapshot: +15.6% (288.5p → 333.4p). Major upgrade in June 2025 (+12.1% to 323.6p), then progressive upgrades through Oct–Nov 2025 (+346p, +350p, +355p), then a step DOWN in March 2026 (from 355p to 333.4p). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 333.4p for 6 weeks). The March 2026 EPS cut from 355p to 333p (−6.2%) reflects FY25 full year results (published Feb 25 2026) — Sharescope shows the current FY1 is FY26. The 333.4p is the post-FY25-results consensus for FY26.

⚠️ Consensus vintage check (Phase 4): The pre-RNS FY1 consensus of 333.4p was set AFTER the FY25 full year results (published 25 February 2026, which showed FY25 EPS of 352.7p actual). This means the 333.4p FY26 consensus reflects a decline vs the FY25 actual (−5.5%) — brokers are modelling a pullback from the exceptional FY25 out-turn. The RNS today significantly upgrades that view.

  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.6% of FY = 47.6% × £5,098.4m = £2,426.8m · EPS 40.2% of FY = 40.2% × 333.4p = 134.0p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £2,369.5m · EPS 146.8p (note: FY25 H1 = current H1 in Sharescope as FY25 results published Feb 2026)
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc £5,098.4m − expected H1 ~£2,426.8m (baseline) = implied H2 ~£2,671.6m vs FY25 H2 £2,649.1m → +0.8% flat. But this RNS changes the picture materially — see Phase 2.
  • FX: MGNS is a UK construction/partnerships group — GBP revenues. Phase 0B: N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): 3y ago −£74.2m / 2y ago −£191.8m / FY25 −£154.2m (net cash) / current (avg daily FY26 YTD) −£445m / FY1fc −£494.4m / FY2fc −£515.5m · Net cash position (deeply cash-generative). Average daily net cash FY26 YTD: £445m (vs £372m FY25 same period). Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — deeply net cash, no leverage constraints.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MGNS · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (trading and outlook update for FY26, dated 16 April 2026; H1 results scheduled 23 July 2026).

  1. Revenue — no explicit FY26 revenue guidance. Construction revenue guided "towards £1.4bn" (previously stated; confirmed maintained). Infrastructure and other divisions unchanged revenue guidance. No aggregate FY26 revenue figure provided — untrackable for revenue at group level. Partnership Housing growth: modest vs FY25.
  2. EPS/earnings — FY26 expected "significantly ahead of previous expectations." This is the headline phrase. Fit Out profits: "significantly ahead of previous expectations and further exceed the top-end of its Medium-Term Target of £80m–£100m." Construction margin: "top end of 3.0%–3.5% Medium-Term Target range." Infrastructure margin: "top end of 3.75%–4.25% range." Partnership Housing: "modest growth" vs FY25 (£42m — disappointing vs prior expectations of stronger growth).

"the Group now anticipates that its full year results for 2026 will be significantly ahead of its previous expectations following strong trading activity and increased visibility"

  1. FY27e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base: FY25 actual EPS = 352.7p. Pre-RNS FY26 consensus = 333.4p (already below FY25 actual). This RNS implies FY26 will be "significantly" ahead of 333.4p — potentially back towards or above the 355p level consensus reached in November 2025.
  • (2) Fit Out: "significantly ahead" of £80–100m MT target = likely £110–130m. This is a major positive surprise. FY25 Fit Out was strong but Fit Out at £110–130m vs prior £80–100m assumption drives the bulk of the upgrade.
  • (3) Construction: top-end 3.5% margin on £1.4bn revenue = £49m OP vs prior mid-range assumption.
  • (4) Partnership Housing: "modest growth" vs FY25 £42m = ~£43–46m — below prior expectations of £50m+. Partial offset.
  • (5) Interest: deep net cash (average daily £445m), no interest charge drag.
  • Implied FY26 EPS: with Fit Out at ~£115m (vs prior £95m assumption = +£20m) and Construction at top-end, implied FY26 EPS upgrade from 333.4p to approximately 370–390p (+11–17% vs pre-RNS consensus).
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS at 323.2p consensus is set BELOW FY25 actual (352.7p). The RNS doesn't explicitly upgrade FY27, but a higher FY26 base implies FY27 consensus must also rise.
  1. Order book / forward work: Fit Out: "greater visibility for the rest of the year from preferred bidder work." Construction: high-quality orderbook supporting £1.4bn revenue. Infrastructure: large frameworks deployment. Average daily net cash FY26 YTD: £445m (vs £372m same period FY25 = +19.6%).

"For the period between 1 January to 14 April 2026, daily average net cash was £445m"

  1. Margin / profitability: Fit Out: significantly above top-end of £80–100m MT target. Construction: top-end 3.0–3.5% range. Infrastructure: top-end 3.75–4.25%. Partnership Housing: modest growth vs £42m. Mixed Use: in line. The compound of top-end delivery across multiple divisions simultaneously is the upgrade driver.
  2. Capital: Average daily net cash >£400m expected for full year. Dividends growing (FY1fc DPS 157.5p). Balance sheet remains an exceptional competitive advantage.
  3. Qualitative tone: "Group PBT is expected to be significantly ahead of previous expectations." No hedging language. Strong confidence across Fit Out and Construction.

EPS quality check: No tax distortions cited. No exceptional items flagged. Net cash position means no finance cost drag. EPS is clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

"Significantly ahead of previous expectations" — this is explicit beat language with "not less than" equivalent certainty.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — "significantly ahead," Fit Out "significantly ahead of top-end" of target, "record" order/pipeline signals implicit. Provisional points: +14.

Divergence check: Partnership Housing modest growth (below prior expectations) partially offsets the Fit Out/Construction beats. Net: strongly positive. No divergence flag.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

MGNS · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

  • FY24: H1 £1,935.2m + H2 £2,182.5m = £4,117.7m ✓. EPS H1 97.4p + H2 146.6p = 244.0p ✓.
  • FY23: H1 £1,697.5m + H2 £1,914.7m. FY stated in Sharescope as 3y ago sum = £3,612.2m. EPS 93.4p + 140.4p = 233.8p.

Revenue growth trajectory: 🟢 Steady then accelerating (FY24 +14%, FY25 +22%). EPS growth trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — FY24 modest, FY25 exceptional (+44.6%). FY26 to sustain or improve.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: FY26e consensus ~flat vs FY25 +21.9% → no acceleration (consensus-derived). No ACC REV.
  • EPS: pre-RNS FY26 consensus 333.4p shows DECLINE vs FY25 352.7p — therefore no ACC EPS on consensus basis. However, this RNS upgrades FY26 significantly — after revision ~370–390p implies acceleration. Pre-RNS consensus shows no ACC.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline & H1 Tracking (pre-H1 mode — SCORES in Phase 5)

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net +15.6% over snapshot but key feature is the FALL from 355p to 333.4p in March 2026 following FY25 results (brokers reset for a moderating FY26). This RNS reverses that reset aggressively.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING at 333.4p — consensus has been frozen awaiting Q1 trading update.
  • Revenue: £4,699m → £5,098m upgrade cycle (+8.5%). Flat for 6 weeks.
  • Divergence: Share price fell from £55+ peak (Feb/Mar 2026) back to £44.78 current — share price already discounted the March 2026 downgrade. This RNS should re-rate the share back towards the prior highs.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

  • Net cash: 3y ago £74.2m / 2y ago £191.8m / FY25 £154.2m / FY26 YTD avg £445m / FY1fc £494.4m / FY2fc £515.5m
  • ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash) — deeply unlevered
  • Interest cover: not applicable (net cash)

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — exceptional balance sheet; average daily net cash £445m is a competitive advantage enabling working capital investment in Partnerships. Does not score in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY1 fc EPS 333.4p vs FY25 actual 352.7p → 🚨 FY1 fc EPS forecast −5.5% below prior year actual. However, this is pre-RNS. Post-RNS upgrade to ~370–390p = above FY25 352.7p. FY1 fc Revenue £5,098m vs FY25 £5,019m → ✅ marginally growing.

Step 2: FY2 fc EPS 323.2p vs FY1 fc 333.4p → 🚨 FY2 fc EPS −3.1% below FY1 fc. Again, pre-RNS. Post-RNS FY26 upgrade will also lift FY27 consensus.

Both steps show declining consensus pre-RNS — this RNS reverses both. The declining FY1 and FY2 consensus was set post-FY25 results when brokers modelled normalisation from exceptional FY25 Fit Out. The "significantly ahead" language today invalidates those cuts.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

MGNS · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 and #2 Drivers:

#1 Fit Out "significantly ahead of previous expectations AND top-end of £80–100m MT target." This is the most specific and impactful phrase in the RNS. Fit Out was already exceptional in FY25 — if FY26 Fit Out exceeds £100m (which the language implies), this drives the bulk of the FY26 EPS upgrade. Brokers who had modelled £85–95m Fit Out profit face a material revision.

#2 "Group PBT significantly ahead of previous expectations" — direct, unambiguous language. This phrase in a MGNS context has historically triggered large consensus upgrades. Combined with top-end margin delivery across Construction and Infrastructure, the group-level beat is broad-based, not single-division.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 (FY1) Revenue: modest upgrade, £5,100–5,150m (+0–1%) — revenue was already in line; the beat is margin-driven.
  • FY26 (FY1) EPS: material upgrade from 333.4p → 370–390p (+11–17%) as Fit Out and construction margins beat. This is a large move for a FTSE 250 construction group.
  • FY27 (FY2) EPS: upgrade from 323.2p → 340–360p (+5–11%). FY27 consensus was already anomalously low (below FY25 actual) — this RNS provides the catalyst to reset FY27 to a more appropriate level.
  • FY27 Revenue: modest upgrade to £5,200–5,300m.

Target price and recommendation: Current consensus TP £54.27 (price £44.78 — 21% upside). After EPS upgrades of +11–17% for FY26 and +5–11% for FY27, broker TPs move to approximately £58–62 range (+7–14% from current TP). Price has significant room to recover — it was at £55 just weeks ago.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Significantly ahead" is MGNS's strongest language. In prior years this has consistently preceded large consensus upgrades. Partnership Housing modest growth (below prior expectations) is the only cautionary note, but its OP contribution (£42–45m) is small relative to Fit Out and Construction. Net: the conservatism is in Partnership Housing; the aggression is everywhere else.

Key risk: Partnership Housing subdued due to consumer sentiment — "near-term consumer sentiment continues to remain subdued due to wider macro-economic events." If housing market sentiment deteriorates further, partnership housing volumes could miss even the modest growth expectation. Capital employed in Partnerships growing (£490–550m average FY26) — working capital heavy division.

Consistency check: Net revision direction: material upgrade (FY1 +11–17%). Tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. ✓ consistent.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The operative phrase is: "Group PBT is expected to be significantly ahead of previous expectations." The single largest contributor is Fit Out, which is "significantly ahead of previous expectations and further exceeds the top-end of its Medium-Term Target of £80m–£100m" — implying Fit Out OP of approximately £110–130m, up from the prior analyst consensus of ~£90–95m. This represents a £15–35m OP surprise from one division alone. Simultaneously, Construction operating margin is guiding to the top end of its 3.0–3.5% MT target on revenues "towards £1.4bn" (implying £49m OP), and Infrastructure margin is also at the top end of 3.75–4.25% range. Average daily net cash of £445m for Jan–April 2026 (+19% vs the same FY25 period) confirms this is not a working capital-distorted result — the cash generation is real and accelerating.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, H1 FY26 figures are not yet disclosed (H1 results: 23 July 2026). The upgrade resilience case is unusually clear for a pre-H1 update because the language is group-level rather than H1-specific: "significantly ahead" refers to the full year FY26, not just Q1/H1. The implied FY26 EPS post-upgrade is approximately 370–390p vs pre-RNS consensus 333.4p — itself set at a discount to FY25 actual (352.7p) following the February 2026 full-year results. The H2 FY26 implied EPS on an upgraded FY26 basis of ~380p minus an estimated H1 of ~134p (based on 40.2% historical H1 split) = ~246p H2 vs FY25 H2 205.9p = +19.5% YoY. The key risk to the upgrade is Partnership Housing, where near-term consumer sentiment "remains subdued" — but with OP contribution of only ~£43–46m vs Fit Out at £110m+, the Partnership Housing miss is significantly outweighed.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will raise FY26 EPS from 333.4p → approximately 370–390p (+11–17%) — the most substantial single-RNS consensus upgrade in this MGNS cycle. FY27 EPS must also rise from the anomalously low 323.2p (below FY25 actual) to approximately 340–360p (+5–11%). Target prices move from current consensus £54.27 to approximately £58–62 — the share price at £44.78 was already discounting the post-FY25 EPS reset and is substantially behind fundamental value. The watch point is H1 results on 23 July 2026: with the company now guiding FY26 "significantly ahead," the H1 print needs to confirm the Fit Out momentum is holding (order conversion from preferred bidder) and that Construction discipline is maintained. Any weakening of Fit Out pipeline conversion by H1 could temper the FY27 upgrade.

🏁 Strongly positive — "significantly ahead" is MGNS's clearest upgrade trigger; FY26 EPS heading to 370–390p from 333.4p; FY27 also needs resetting; share price at £44.78 substantially lags fundamental value; largest upgrade magnitude of this session.

Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY 2025 results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state. Next event is H1 FY26 results.
  • FX — Phase 0B triggered: EMEA revenue £517.5m = ~40.7% of continuing group revenue £1,270.8m. EUR is the dominant EMEA currency, implying EUR exposure of approximately 35–40% of group revenue, exceeding the 30% threshold.
  • Missing baseline fallback applied: No formal Currency Movements table with prior-year average rates present in the RNS. However, the RNS discloses the net FX impact explicitly: currency headwinds reduced both Group revenue and adjusted operating profit in the year by 0.6%. Prior year impact was −1.8% / −1.6% — improving trend.
  • Direction: GBP modestly stronger vs prior year average (confirmed by headwind disclosure). Headwind is mild — only 0.6% revenue impact, at the low end of the 35–50% exposure band.
  • Penalty applied: −5 pts (35–50% exposure band, neutral-to-mild headwind, lower-end of −10/−5 range given actual disclosed impact of only 0.6%). Confidence range widened ±5pp per missing baseline fallback rule.
  • Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−5 pts) · ~38% EUR · GBP headwind (mild)
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY 2025 full year results. Sharescope reflects pre-RNS state: FY1 consensus EPS 21.6p, FY1 revenue £1,305.5m; FY2 consensus EPS 23.9p, FY2 revenue £1,354.0m.
  • Consensus momentum: EPS net change over full 10-month snapshot period = 0.0%. Zero upgrades, zero downgrades — consensus completely static at 21.6p throughout. Revenue equally static at ~£1,305m. 4-week trend: FLAT. Remarkable stasis; brokers had no conviction to move either direction.
  • Seasonal H1 baselines: 3-year average H1 revenue split = 47.9% of full year. 2-year average H1 EPS split = 44.1% of full year (3y unusable: FY23 shows H2 as −15.0p placeholder). These baselines apply to FY26 forecasting; H1 FY26 not yet reported.
  • Implied H2 FY25 context (from actuals): H2 revenue = £1,270.8m − £620.3m (Sharescope H1) = £650.5m; H2 EPS = 22.37p − 6.7p = 15.67p. H2 revenue YoY = −2.7% vs prior H2 £668.5m. H2 EPS YoY = +8.1% vs prior H2 14.5p.
  • FX summary: EUR exposure ~38%, GBP mild headwind, −0.6% revenue impact disclosed. No prior-year average rate in RNS (missing baseline fallback). −5 pts penalty applied and carried to Phase 5.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS Type: FY Results — Year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue — FY actual £1,270.8m (continuing), −1.5% vs prior year (−0.8% constant currency). vs FY1 consensus £1,305.5m = miss of −2.7%. H1 actual £620.3m; implied H2 £650.5m = −2.7% YoY vs H2 FY24 £668.5m. H1 FY25 was −2.4% YoY; H2 FY25 was +0.8% YoY — return to H2 growth confirmed.
    "Group revenue of £1.27bn was marginally below 2024 (by 1.5%), with gross margins flat at 17.7%."
    "Group revenue declined by 2.4% in the first half of the year compared with growth of 0.8% in the second half."
  2. Adjusted EPS — FY actual 22.37p vs FY1 consensus 21.6p = beat of +3.5%. YoY decline −17.0% (FY24: 26.96p). H1 FY25 actual 6.7p; H2 FY25 actual 15.67p = +8.1% YoY vs H2 FY24 14.5p. Adjusted profit before tax £30.5m (2024: £39.1m, −22.1%).
    "Adjusted EPS decreased by 17% (2024: 30%) to 22.37p (2024: 26.96p)."
  3. H2 profit weighting — 60% of adjusted operating profit generated in H2 (vs 54% in FY24). Implies H2 adjusted operating profit ≈ £26.2m, H1 ≈ £17.4m. This H2 skew is increasing structurally and is a key read-through for FY26 H1 expectations.
    "Adjusted operating profit of £43.6m (2024: £48.9m), with 60% (2024: 54%) generated in the second half."
  4. Gross margin — record 17.7% maintained on continuing basis (2024: 17.7%). UK&I improved to 18.6% (2024: 18.0%); EMEA 17.1% (2024: 17.0%); APAC 16.6% (2024: 16.4%); North America 17.5% (2024: 19.3% — vendor loss drag). No margin deterioration at group level despite revenue pressure.
    "Gross profit margins excluding exited businesses remain at record levels of 17.7% (2024: 17.7%)."
  5. Adjusted operating profit £43.6m (2024: £48.9m) = −10.7%; margin 3.4% (2024: 3.8%). Adjusted net finance costs increased to £13.1m (2024: £9.8m) due to full-year impact of prior M&A debt. UK&I operating profit +30% to £25.7m; EMEA −21% to £19.9m; North America −46% to £5.1m.
    "Adjusted operating profit fell by £5.3m to £43.6m, with adjusted profit before tax being £8.6m lower at £30.5m."
  6. Cash conversion exceptional — 123% (2024: 97%); well above long-term average of ~80%. Adjusted net debt reduced to £126.0m (2024: £130.6m). Leverage 2.17x adjusted EBITDA, improved from H1 2025 peak of 2.5x; within 3.0x covenant. Total facilities >£300m; RCF matures mid-2028.
    "Adjusted cash flow conversion of 123% (2024: 97%), reflecting the continued focus on driving near term working capital management efficiencies."
    "Adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio at the period end was 2.17x, in line with Board and market expectations. This also reflects a positive reduction since H1 2025 (H1 2025: 2.5x)."
  7. Dividend reset — total 5.25p (2024: 13.0p) = −60% YoY. New policy: ~25% payout ratio of adjusted EPS. Final 3.5p proposed (2024: 7.5p), interim 1.75p paid (2024: 5.5p). Covered 4x by adjusted earnings. DPS progressive medium-term commitment maintained.
    "Proposed final dividend of 3.5p (2024: 7.5p) plus interim dividend of 1.75p (2024: 5.5p) equates to total dividends for 2025 of 5.25p (2024: 13.0p), reflecting the Group's updated dividend policy."
  8. Exceptional items — £38.3m total. Dominated by £27.0m ERP impairment (ERP rollout paused; only one country live). Restructuring costs £8.7m (headcount fell 1,900 to ~1,750). Loss on derecognition of acquired intangibles £4.4m. Insurance recovery £1.8m (Dubai warehouse fire Dec 2024). Statutory loss before tax £30.5m (2024: £22.3m profit). All exceptional — not in adjusted figures.
    "Following a comprehensive review of the ongoing deployment and future cost and benefits, the Board concluded that the ERP programme rollout should be paused, with only one country fully live. This resulted in a one-off impairment charge of £27.0m in the year."
  9. Outlook — no improvement assumed in 2026 market conditions; return to profit growth expected. New digital/AI strategy replacing ERP to deliver benefits faster and cheaper. M&A paused in 2025 but pipeline healthy; expected to resume in 2026. Germany expected to improve from 2026. New CFO Adam Councell joined 2 March 2026.
    "Whilst there have been no material improvements in the macroeconomic backdrop or the Pro AV market at the start of 2026, the Board expects that the actions taken by the Group will support a return to profit growth in 2026."
  10. Regional highlights — UK&I the standout; EMEA and North America remain drags. UK&I: revenue +6.7% to £508.3m, operating profit +30% to £25.7m. EMEA: revenue −5.3% to £517.5m (Germany entirely responsible; rest of EMEA +9.7%). North America: revenue −8.9% to £201.0m (Canada vendor loss + US tariff disruption). APAC: revenue −4.2% to £44.0m (+1.4% constant currency); being restructured into UK&I and EMEA regions from 2026.
    "Strong revenue and profit growth in UK&I due to market share gains and new vendors, despite challenging market conditions continuing."
    "A robust performance in EMEA, with revenue growth in the region excluding Germany, which is expected to improve from 2026."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Half-on-Half revenue trajectory: Decelerating. FY23 YoY ~+8%; FY24 YoY ~+6.8%; FY25 YoY −1.5%. H1 FY25 £620.3m = +1.6% YoY (slowing from H1 FY24 +7.3%). H2 FY25 £650.5m = −2.7% YoY vs H2 FY24 £668.5m — though improved vs H1 trend (+0.8% actual H2 YoY per RNS, reflecting mix of continuing vs exited base).
  • Half-on-Half EPS trajectory: Recovering in H2. H1 FY25 EPS 6.7p = −38.5% YoY vs H1 FY24 10.9p. H2 FY25 EPS 15.67p = +8.1% YoY vs H2 FY24 14.5p. Full year −17.0%. The H2 recovery is the bull case underpinning FY26 expectations.
  • Seasonal baselines for H1 FY26 (pre-H1 mode — next event): Revenue H1 baseline = 47.9% × FY2 consensus £1,354.0m = £648.5m. EPS H1 baseline = 44.1% × FY2 consensus 23.9p = 10.5p. Buy trigger: H1 Rev > £657.5m (+1.5pp); H1 EPS > 10.7p (+1.5pp). Sell trigger: H1 Rev < £638.6m; H1 EPS < 10.3p. Note: FY2 baselines will shift post broker revisions; update triggers once consensus resets.
  • H1 FY26 UNTRACKABLE — both REV and EPS (H1 FY26 results not yet reported; no H1 data in current RNS which is FY results). H1 indicator on card: na for both metrics.
  • H2 momentum vs 3-year average: H2 FY25 revenue £650.5m vs 3yr avg H2 £651.5m = −0.2% (flat classification). H2 FY25 EPS 15.67p vs 3yr avg H2 EPS 16.66p = −6.0% (weak classification). However YoY H2 EPS was +8.1% — the 3yr average is depressed by the prior two weak years. The directional trend is improving.
  • Forecast momentum overlay: EPS flat at 21.6p for entire 10-month period. Revenue flat at ~£1,305m. Zero broker activity. 4-week trend FLAT. Price also unchanged at 329p throughout — extraordinary stasis. Actual EPS of 22.37p is a +3.5% beat into completely static consensus; this should prompt first broker revisions in months.
  • Structural flags: (1) ERP write-off £27.0m removes ongoing capex drag — future FCF improves. (2) H2 profit weighting increasing (60% in FY25 vs 54% FY24) — H1 FY26 will likely disappoint seasonally; manage expectations. (3) Dividend reset to 25% payout — balance sheet prioritised; removes progressive dividend expectation near term. (4) CFO change March 2026 — Adam Councell new; Stephen Lamb departed. (5) APAC folded into UK&I/EMEA from 2026 — operational simplification.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1 #1 Driver — Revenue miss vs consensus (−2.7%): At £1,270.8m vs £1,305.5m, this is the headline number brokers must address first. Despite being only −0.8% at constant currency, the reported shortfall against a static consensus will dominate initial coverage. #2 Driver — EPS beat (+3.5%, 22.37p vs 21.6p): The mitigant. Better-than-expected profit conversion driven by H2 profit weighting (60%), margin discipline and cost reduction — the first meaningful data point in 10 months of total consensus stasis.
2 Forecast revision direction: FY26 (new FY1) EPS: +3–6% upward from current FY2 base of 23.9p, driven by higher FY25 base, ERP capex removal and cost restructuring benefits. FY26 revenue: −1–3% downward from £1,354.0m given cautious "no improvement assumed" outlook, Germany still weak, North America restructuring. Net result: modest EPS upgrade cycle accompanied by revenue estimate reduction.
3 Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 329p vs current price 160p = 106% implied upside — stock screens extremely cheap at ~7x FY26 EPS. Most brokers will reiterate Buy/Overweight with TPs held in 300–350p range; no cuts warranted given EPS beat and recovery narrative. No recommendation upgrades either — the stock has been at a deep discount to TP for months with no catalyst. Re-rating awaits H1 FY26 evidence of recovery.
4 Conservative guidance read-through: The outlook — "working assumption that there will be little improvement in 2026" — is deliberately cautious framing paired with "greater confidence in our performance in 2026 and beyond." Classic AIM sandbagging: set low bar, beat it. Restructuring complete, ERP overhang cleared, UK&I firing, H2 conversion improving — probability of FY26 EPS consensus beating if Germany shows any recovery is meaningful. This language increases upgrade cycle probability in H2 FY26.
5 Key risk brokers will highlight: Leverage trajectory — adjusted net debt/EBITDA 2.17x (improved from 2.5x at H1 but above FY24's 2.0x). Finance costs increased to £13.1m (2024: £9.8m) from prior M&A debt. Dividend reset signals balance sheet strain. North America vendor loss and Canada restructuring not fully resolved. M&A paused — removes a key historical growth driver. CFO transition adds execution risk. North America gross margin structurally lower at 17.5% (2024: 19.3%) until new vendor secured.
6 Overall broker-note tone forecast: Constructive / modest upgrades likely. EPS beat will prompt first broker estimate revisions in months. Revenue miss and cautious macro cap enthusiasm. H2 recovery narrative (60% H2 profit weighting, UK&I +30% operating profit) is credible. Most houses reiterate Buy with unchanged or slightly higher TPs. Midwich's FY25 results present a genuinely split picture. The revenue miss of −2.7% vs a completely static consensus is the headline negative — £1,270.8m vs £1,305.5m — and brokers who had sat on their hands for 10 months must now acknowledge the softer revenue environment. Germany and North America remain material drags. Yet the adjusted EPS beat of +3.5% (22.37p vs 21.6p) is real and structural: record gross margins at 17.7%, H2 profit conversion increasing to 60%, exceptional cash conversion at 123%, and UK&I operating profit up 30%. The ERP write-off removes an overhang and future capex drag.

The key structural positive is the improving H2 profit weighting. H2 EPS of 15.67p was +8.1% YoY — the first meaningful H2 recovery after two years of sharp declines. Cash conversion of 123% (long-term average ~80%) signals working capital discipline and de-leveraging progress. Adjusted net debt/EBITDA improved from 2.5x at H1 to 2.17x at year end, with £300m+ of facilities available. The dividend reset to 25% payout (5.25p vs 13.0p) is painful for income holders but signals balance sheet prioritisation ahead of an expected M&A resumption in 2026.

The score sits at the amber band floor (50) because the upgrade impulse is real but constrained. Brokers will revise FY26 EPS +3–6% upward from the 23.9p FY2 base while trimming revenue estimates. Most will reiterate Buy with 300–350p TPs — giving 90–120% upside from 160p — but the re-rating catalyst is absent until H1 FY26 shows Germany recovering, North America stabilising, and the new digital/AI productivity investments delivering. The H2 FY26 profit seasonality (60%+ expected again) means H1 FY26 will likely disappoint relative to full-year hopes, making patience essential.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MNDI · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 Trading Update)

  1. Q1 2026 EBITDA — explicit figure, YoY miss: Q1 2026 underlying EBITDA = €212m (including €8m forestry fair value gain). Prior year Q1 2025 = €290m (including €2m forestry fair value gain). YoY decline = −26.9%. Ex-forestry: Q1 2026 = €204m vs Q1 2025 = €288m = −29.2% ex-forestry. "Market conditions in the first quarter of 2026 remained challenging resulting in an underlying EBITDA of €212 million, including €8 million of forestry fair value gain (Q4 2025 €214 million, including €1 million of forestry fair value gain)." vs consensus: FY26fc EBITDA consensus = €962.5m. Simple quarterly run-rate from Q1: €212m × 4 = €848m vs €962.5m consensus = Q1 annualised is ~12% below FY26 EBITDA consensus. Market expects a significant H2 recovery — Q1 alone is a negative read-through.
  2. Sequential comparison — marginal stability: Q4 2025 EBITDA = €214m; Q1 2026 = €212m. Broadly flat sequentially. This means EBITDA has been running at ~€210–215m per quarter for two consecutive quarters while consensus requires a large H2 uplift to reach €962.5m. Implied H2 requirement = €962.5m − (Q1 + Q2 est.) ≈ very elevated.
  3. Volume trends — positive but offset by pricing: Corrugated Packaging and Flexible Packaging volumes increased sequentially, supported by capacity expansions. However, "lower average selling prices" offset volume gains. No numeric volume or price figure given. "On a sequential basis, our Corrugated Packaging and Flexible Packaging business units increased sales volumes across our range of paper grades... The increase in volumes was offset by lower average selling prices."
  4. Energy/input cost escalation — Q2 and Q3 headwind: "Towards the end of the quarter, higher energy-related input costs" began to weigh. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East cited as driver. Pricing actions initiated but "customary lag" — impact expected to take "full effect in the third quarter." "We expect the impact of these price increases to take full effect in the third quarter of this year." This means Q2 will also be impacted by the cost-price lag — a direct negative for H1 EBITDA.
  5. Forestry fair value guidance — nil for full year 2026: Following a recent reduction in wood prices in South Africa, the full-year forestry fair value gain for 2026 is expected to be nil (vs €39m in FY25: Q1 €2m + Q2 €16m + Q3 €20m + Q4 €1m = €39m). This is a €39m headwind to reported EBITDA in FY26. "Following a recent reduction in wood prices in South Africa, and assuming the market environment does not change significantly for the remainder of the year, the full-year forestry fair value gain for 2026 is expected to be nil."
  6. Plant closures — restructuring actions: Three further converting plant closures announced (Consumer Flexibles Hungary + Corrugated Solutions Poland + Germany). Total headcount reduction: 450. Total recent closures: six plants. "In April, we announced the closure of a further three converting plants comprising a Consumer Flexibles plant in Hungary and Corrugated Solutions plants in Poland and Germany. Together these closures will reduce headcount by 450 over the course of this year." This implies restructuring charges in FY26. Positive medium-term margin impact but near-term cash cost.
  7. Q2 headwinds persist: CEO explicitly states: "These pressures persist into the second quarter and we are taking pricing actions to mitigate their impact." "These pressures persist into the second quarter and we are taking pricing actions to mitigate their impact."
  8. FY26e EPS bridge (FY26 → FY27):
    • New FY26 base: consensus 49.8p — this is already heavily downgraded and may still be too high given Q1 run-rate.
    • Inorganic annualisation delta: nil
    • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY27fc EBITDA = €1,143.1m vs FY26fc €962.5m = +18.8%. This implies brokers expect a substantial FY27 recovery. Applied to a revised FY26 base, the quantum depends on whether FY26 needs further cuts.
    • Interest delta: ND/FCF 13.5x and interest cover 3.6x — interest burden is significant. Finance costs likely stable to marginally rising with debt at €2,515m.
    • Implied: if FY26 EPS is cut to ~40–45p (based on Q1 run-rate), FY27 at 77.4p would represent +70–90% recovery — which may be achievable given pricing actions and H2 cost recovery, but carries high uncertainty.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure in this update. Consistency check against EBITDA run-rate: Q1 annualised EBITDA of €848m vs FY26fc €962.5m suggests FY26 EPS consensus of 49.8p is at risk of further cuts. Q1 ex-forestry = €204m; annualised ex-forestry = €816m vs FY26fc consensus implying meaningful H2 recovery.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

  • Q2 headwinds persist explicitly.
  • Pricing actions initiated but "customary lag" — full effect Q3.
  • No numeric FY26 guidance.
  • Forestry fair value guided to nil (€39m headwind).
  • Six plant closures — restructuring charges in numbers.
  • Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — sequential EBITDA running at €212m (annualised €848m vs consensus €962.5m = −12% annualised), Q2 headwinds explicitly persistent, forestry gain eliminated, cost pressures ongoing.
  • Provisional: −13 pts
  • Divergence check: Q1 EBITDA worse than prior year by −27%; consensus for FY26 implies H2 recovery that appears challenged. No positive current-year delivery to counter.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

MNDI · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

  • FY25: H1 €3,909m + H2 €3,754m = €7,663m ✓; EPS 42.7p + 5.4p = 48.1p ✓

  • FY23: H1 €4,505m + H2 €4,397m = €8,902m; EPS 108.6p + 182.1p = 290.7p

Pre-RNS consensus — at material risk of further downgrade post this Q1 update.

Revenue growth trajectory: −17.7%, +4.5%, +1.8% — 🟡 Volatile (steep decline then partial recovery; momentum fragile).

EPS growth trajectory: −50.0%, −66.9%, +3.5% — 🟡 Volatile / marginally 🟢 attempting recovery, but from a dramatically collapsed base with near-zero EPS. The +3.5% recovery is minimal and the Q1 run-rate suggests even this is at risk.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS provides no FY guidance. Using FY26fc consensus +1.8% vs prior year +4.5% → no acceleration. 🔴 No acceleration (consensus-derived).
  • EPS: FY26fc +3.5% vs prior year −66.9% — technically positive YoY but from a near-zero base; consensus-derived and at risk. 🟡 Ambiguous (consensus-derived; Q1 run-rate questions the +3.5%).

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

EPS trajectory (HoH): FY25 H1 −54.0%, FY25 H2 −89.7%, FY26 H1 implied +71.7% — technically 🟢 Accelerating from a collapsed base, but the absolute EPS levels remain very depressed. The implied H1 EPS of 30.6p (61.4% of 49.8p) may be too optimistic given Q1 EBITDA running −27% YoY.

Revenue trajectory (HoH): FY25 H1 +0.7%, FY25 H2 +8.8%, FY26 H1 implied +2.4% — 🟡 Volatile (low single-digit growth; no clear acceleration).

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Mode: pre-H1 — this section applies.

Data source gate: No H1 revenue or EPS figure for FY26 in the RNS (Q1 only). No FY guidance given.

Revenue — UNTRACKABLE: No H1 or FY figure. Q1 EBITDA implies FY26 revenue will be challenged; annual run-rate from Q1 EBITDA of €212m vs consensus €962.5m suggests downside risk.

  • Baseline: 51.3% × €7,801.2m = €4,002.0m
  • No implied signal calculable — flag UNTRACKABLE.
  • Buy trigger threshold: Rev > €4,002m × 1.015 = €4,062m. State for use on H1 results date.

EPS — UNTRACKABLE: No H1 figure. Q1 run-rate strongly suggests FY26 EPS consensus of 49.8p is too high.

  • Baseline: 61.4% × 49.8p = 30.6p
  • No confirmed signal — flag UNTRACKABLE.
  • Buy trigger threshold: EPS > 30.6p × 1.015 = 31.1p. State for use on H1 results date.

H1 results date: not specified in this RNS. MNDI typically reports H1 in late July/August.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode: Compare implied H2 vs average of last 3 historical H2 figures.

Revenue:

  • FY26 H2 implied (consensus) = €3,799.2m
  • Historical H2 avg (FY23–FY25): (€4,397m + €3,449m + €3,754m) / 3 = €3,866.7m
  • Implied H2 vs avg: −1.8% → 🟡 flat (−5 to +5%)

EPS:

  • FY26 H2 implied = 19.2p
  • Historical H2 avg (FY23–FY25): (182.1 + 52.5 + 5.4) / 3 = 80.0p
  • Implied H2 vs avg: −76.0% → 🔴 severe (<−15%)
  • The historical average is skewed by the FY23 H2 (182.1p) — even excluding FY23, avg = (52.5 + 5.4) / 2 = 28.95p vs implied 19.2p = −33.7% — still severe.

Profit warning feasibility gate (fires: H1 tracking is UNTRACKABLE but Q1 EBITDA provides a proxy):

  • H2 hurdle test: Q1 EBITDA €212m; Q2 guided to have "persistent pressures." If H1 2026 EBITDA = ~€200m + €200m = ~€400m, then H2 2026 must deliver €962.5m − €400m = ~€562.5m in just H2 to meet consensus — vs H2 2025 €437m. H2 implied requirement is >10pp above recent run-rate. ✓ Elevated H2 hurdle.
  • Fixed cost headwind: energy cost inflation explicitly flagged, geopolitical cost escalation, restructuring charges from six plant closures. ✓
  • Operating leverage: ND/FCF 13.5x, interest cover 3.6x — both trigger the non-linear flag. ✓

⛔⛔ Profit warning risk ⛔⛔ — H2 burden implausible given: (1) Q1 EBITDA €212m vs consensus implying ~€480m+ H2 EBITDA requirement; (2) energy/input cost inflation explicitly persistent into Q2 with pricing lag to Q3; (3) ND/FCF 13.5x — EPS drop-through is non-linear. FY26 EBITDA consensus €962.5m is at material risk of a cut to €850–880m range.

Note: Phase 3.3 does not contribute a scored row in Phase 5 under pre-H1 routing mode.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: −52.4% over snapshot period (104.7p → 49.8p). Persistent and severe downgrade cycle. No upgrade events visible in the data.
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (50.0p → 49.8p — continued marginal decline).
  • Revenue trend: Revised from €8,000.5m to €7,801.2m — gradual downward drift.
  • Divergence: Price declined sharply (£14.11 → £8.50p, −39.8% over snapshot period) in line with EPS downgrades. No positive divergence — price and EPS moving together downward.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

  • Reporting currency: EUR (EPS in pence)
  • Net borrowing: FY23 H2 €−216m (net cash) / FY24 H2 €−767m (net cash) / FY25 H1 €1,605m / FY25 H2 €−52m / FY26fc €2,515.3m / FY27fc €2,399.8m (positive = net debt)

    Note: The FY25 year-end net debt appears to show €−52m (net cash at H2 FY25) but FY26fc shows €2,515m net debt — this step-up likely reflects acquisitions or capex in FY26. Capex FY26fc = €562.9m which is substantial.

  • ND/EBITDA: FY23 0.50x / FY24 0.40x / FY25 1.70x / FY26 2.60x fc / FY27fc 2.10x — rapid deterioration.
  • Interest cover FY26fc: 3.6x (marginal — below 4x threshold, non-linear EPS flag applies) · FY27fc: 4.5x
  • ND/FCF FY26fc: 13.5x — very elevated (>8x gate met; confirms non-linear drop-through risk)
  • Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — ND/FCF 13.5x FY26fc, interest cover 3.6x (<4x threshold), ND/EBITDA 2.6x at a time of compressed and declining EBITDA. This warrants a scored row in Phase 5. Interest cover <4x: IFRS16 lease interest should be included in bridge — note operating structure includes significant leased industrial facilities.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26fc vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26fc EPS 49.8p vs FY25 actual 48.1p → ✅ marginal growth (+3.5%)
  • FY26fc Revenue €7,801.2m vs FY25 actual €7,663.0m → ✅ marginal growth (+1.8%)
  • ✅✅ Both growing — but marginally; Q1 run-rate places both at risk.

Step 2 — FY27fc vs FY26fc:

  • FY27fc EPS 77.4p vs FY26fc 49.8p → ✅ +55.4% growth — large FY27 recovery baked in
  • FY27fc Revenue €8,164.7m vs FY26fc €7,801.2m → ✅ +4.7% growth
  • ✅✅ Both growing. The FY27 EPS jump of +55% looks ambitious if FY26 base is cut further.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • Nil forestry fair value for FY26: Full-year impact = €0 vs €39m in FY25 = €39m headwind to reported EBITDA. This affects reported EPS directly. "The full-year forestry fair value gain for 2026 is expected to be nil."
  • Six plant closures: Restructuring charges will weigh on reported numbers. Customer transfers to alternative plants carry execution risk.
  • Pricing lag structural dynamic: Energy/input costs rise immediately; pricing actions take effect in Q3. This creates a structural 1–2 quarter earnings drag that is difficult to model precisely.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

MNDI · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 Driver — Q1 EBITDA €212m implying ~12% annualised miss vs FY26 consensus: Q1 underlying EBITDA (ex-forestry €204m) annualises to ~€816m vs consensus €962.5m. This is the dominant driver. Brokers will cut FY26 EBITDA forecasts meaningfully. Combined with the nil forestry guidance (−€39m vs prior year), FY26 consensus faces a double hit.

#2 Driver — Q2 headwinds persistent + pricing lag to Q3: The CEO explicitly states "these pressures persist into the second quarter." This means Q2 is also below-trend. With full pricing recovery only in Q3, H1 EBITDA is structurally compressed. Brokers will lower H1 2026 estimates and the H2 recovery requirement will look increasingly unrealistic.

Forecast revisions: FY26: EBITDA cut from €962.5m to ~€850–880m (−8–12%); EPS cut from 49.8p to approximately 38–43p (−14–24%). Revenue likely held or modest trim (~−2–4%). FY27: EPS likely trimmed from 77.4p to ~65–70p (−9–16%) as the base effect pushes recovery expectations further out.

Target price and recommendation: Current TP consensus = £10.06 vs current price = 850.6p = 18.3% upside on pre-RNS basis. Post-downgrade, TP likely cut to £7.50–£8.50 — implying current price may be fair value or slightly cheap on a bear case basis. Recommendations may move from hold toward sell at some brokers.

Conservative guidance read-through: No conservative "not less than" language present. The RNS contains no positive guidance anchor — it is almost entirely a negative update with a management self-help narrative (plant closures, pricing actions). Q3 pricing recovery is acknowledged but uncertain.

Key risk: The pricing lag dynamic creates a window where input costs rise faster than output prices can be adjusted. If geopolitical tensions escalate further and energy costs remain elevated through Q3, the assumed Q3 pricing recovery may be delayed, pushing FY26 EBITDA further below consensus.

"While there is a customary lag, we expect the impact of these price increases to take full effect in the third quarter of this year."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = cut (−14–24%). Tone = Cautious / downgrades or TP cuts probable → consistent. The scale of implied cuts (>10%) arguably warrants Negative/material downgrades territory.

Overall tone: 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected — Q1 EBITDA −27% YoY, Q2 guided similarly challenged, nil forestry gain, ND/FCF 13.5x with <4x interest cover. EPS cuts of 14–24% expected.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

MNDI

22/100 · Confidence: 16–28 · No FX adjustment · 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected

ComponentPts
🟢 Volume growth sequential: Corrugated + Flexible Packaging volumes up QoQ+4
🟢 Pricing actions initiated: recovery expected Q3+3
🟢 Plant closure programme: cost structure rationalisation (6 plants, 450 headcount)+2
🔴 Outlook: profit warning — Q1 annualised EBITDA ~12% below FY26 consensus−13
🔴 Q2 headwinds explicitly persistent: "pressures persist into the second quarter"−8
🔴 Leverage elevated: ND/FCF 13.5x FY26fc, interest cover 3.6x (<4x threshold)−6
🔴 Nil forestry fair value FY26: €39m EBITDA headwind vs FY25−5
🔴 Persistent EPS downgrade cycle: −52.4% over snapshot; 4-week FALLING−5
🔴 Profit warning feasibility gate triggered: H2 recovery implausible at current run-rate−5
🔴 Lower average selling prices offsetting volume gains: no pricing power near-term−4
🔴 Restructuring charges FY26: six plant closures, cash cost to hit numbers−3
🟡 FY25 H2 EPS near-zero (5.4p): any H2 FY26 delivery = large % YoY improvement, limiting downside optics−2

Raw total: +9 + (−51) = −42 → floored at minimum meaningful score: 22

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst is Q1 2026 underlying EBITDA of €212m (including €8m forestry fair value), representing a −26.9% YoY decline from Q1 2025's €290m. On an ex-forestry basis the decline is −29.2%. Annualising Q1 yields ~€848m EBITDA against FY26 consensus of €962.5m — a structural shortfall of approximately €114m or −12% before any H2 recovery. The Q1 figure is essentially flat with Q4 2025 (€214m), confirming that sequential stabilisation has occurred but at a level materially below what consensus requires for the full year.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, H1 tracking is UNTRACKABLE (no H1 actuals). However, the Q1 EBITDA data provides a clear directional signal. With Q2 headwinds explicitly persistent and pricing recovery only expected in Q3, H1 2026 EBITDA is likely to run at ~€400–420m — requiring H2 2026 to deliver ~€540–560m to meet consensus, versus H2 2025's €437m. This H2 requirement (+24–28% above the most recent comparable) is structurally challenging. The profit warning feasibility gate has been triggered: H2 burden implausible, energy/input cost headwinds confirmed ongoing, and ND/FCF at 13.5x confirms that any revenue shortfall drop-through to EPS is non-linear due to the high fixed cost and leverage structure.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS consensus will be cut from 49.8p to approximately 38–43p (−14–24%); FY27 likely trimmed from 77.4p to 65–70p (−9–16%). Consensus TP likely to be cut from £10.06 to £7.50–£8.50. Current price 850.6p sits within this range, meaning the stock may be pricing in some (but not all) of the downgrade. The nil forestry guidance alone represents a known €39m EBITDA headwind that is straightforward to model. The main watch point is whether Q3 pricing actions materialise as guided or are delayed by further geopolitical escalation — if the latter, FY26 EPS could fall below 38p. 🏁 Material downgrade cycle underway; FY26 EPS cuts of 14–24% and TP reductions to £7.50–£8.50 are probable; avoid until Q3 pricing recovery is evidenced in H1 results.

scorecards.analysisText:
MOTR

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

MOTR · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS is a pre-FY trading update. Market expects full-year confirmation and FY27 guidance.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 6.7p · Revenue £1,265.8m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 10.5p · Revenue £1,351.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS started 3.5p in May 2025, jumped to 6.3p in June 2025 (post-H1 results), then to 6.9p in October 2025, settling to 6.7p by November 2025. Flat since. Net change +91.4% over period. Last 4 weeks: 🔴 FLAT. Revenue: £1,153m → £1,265.8m (+9.8%) over same period.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 52.8% of FY = £668.1m · EPS: only 1yr avg (47.2%) = 3.2p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £563.1m · EPS 1.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 fc £1,265.8m − H1 actual £647.7m = implied H2 £618.1m vs FY25 H2 £610.0m → +1.3% YoY. EPS: FY1 fc 6.7p − H1 actual 3.1p = implied H2 3.6p vs FY25 H2 1.9p → +89.5% YoY.
  • FX: MOTR is a UK domestic business (buys and sells used cars in GBP). No material FX exposure. Phase 0B: skip.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net borrowing: FY23 £1.2m (H2) / FY24 −£0.1m (net cash) / FY25 H2 £4.0m → H1 FY26 £50.5m → FY1fc −£6.5m (net cash) / FY2fc −£14.8m. Note: the move from £50.5m net borrowing at H1 to −£6.5m net cash at FY end is an extraordinary H2 deleveraging — reflecting the IFRS16 lease liabilities and seasonal working capital pattern (bulk inventory funded by floorplan). Interest cover FY1fc: 1.7x — low but improving to 2.2x FY2. ND/FCF: −1.1x (net cash). Debt flag requires careful assessment.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

MOTR is a UK domestic used car retailer. No non-GBP revenue. Phase 0B: skip, no penalty.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MOTR · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

1. Revenue Record retail volumes of ~65,000 in FY26, up 8.0% on FY25. No explicit revenue figure disclosed. FY1 consensus: £1,265.8m. Volume +8% is a strong leading indicator; revenue per unit likely broadly stable (metal margin performance was "record"). Implied revenue: if FY25 was ~60,185 units (65,000 / 1.08) at ~£19,500/unit = £1,173m (consistent with actual £1,173.1m), then FY26 at 65,000 units × ~£19,500/unit = ~£1,267m — essentially in-line with consensus £1,265.8m on volumes alone. However "record metal margin performance" could lift revenue/unit slightly.

"Record retail volumes of c.65,000 in FY26, up 8.0% on FY25"

2. EPS / Earnings PBT: "expected to be c.£7.5m, up 83% (FY25: £4.1m)." Consensus FY1 PBT: £7.4m. Beat: +£0.1m, +1.4% vs consensus — essentially in-line, very slight beat.

EBITDA: "c.£27.0m, up 13.0% (FY25: £23.9m)." Consensus FY1 EBITDA: £28.5m. This is a miss: −£1.5m, −5.3% vs consensus EBITDA. The PBT beats consensus but EBITDA misses — this implies higher depreciation/amortisation or IFRS16 lease costs than modelled, or a different adj/reported bridge.

FY26e EPS bridge (FY27):

  • FY26 base: PBT c.£7.5m → tax at ~25% → PAT ~£5.6m → diluted EPS ~7.0p (79.6m shares). FY1 consensus 6.7p → slight beat.
  • FY27 bridge:
    • (1) New base EPS: ~7.0p
    • (2) New Leeds store (summer 2026): incremental revenue c.£50–60m p.a. at maturity, PBT contribution c.£1.0–1.5m at ~2% PBT margin → EPS +1.2–1.9p at full run-rate (not until FY28)
    • (3) Organic volume growth: used car market growing 2.2%, MOTR growing 6% in calendar 2025. If sustained: ~4% organic volume growth → 67,600 units FY27 → revenue +£50m → PBT +£1m → EPS +1.2p
    • (4) Metal margin normalisation: "record" FY26 metal margin may partially normalise in FY27
    • (5) Leeds store pre-opening costs: ~£2–3m drag in FY27
    • Implied FY27 EPS: 8–9p — below FY2 consensus 10.5p. The 10.5p consensus may be too aggressive given Leeds is unlikely to fully contribute until FY28, and metal margins may normalise. Alternatively, additional store openings could be announced. Current FY2 consensus looks stretched.

3. Volume and market share Record retail volumes ~65,000 units FY26, +8.0% vs FY25. MOTR grew 6.0% in calendar year 2025 vs market +2.2% — "continued outperformance of the used car market."

Agentic AI tool for reactivating closed quotes: ~900 incremental vehicle sales attributed (1.4% of FY26 volumes). Supply normalising: "more bulk deals" and "more vehicles directly through Sell Your Car channel."

"Since launching our new agentic AI tool to reactivate historic closed quotes, c.900 incremental vehicle sales can be attributed to this channel."

4. Margin / profitability "Record metal margin performance" — metal margin is the gross profit per vehicle (selling price minus buying price). This is the key operational metric. Record metal margin + record volumes = strong FY26.

EBITDA £27.0m vs consensus £28.5m = miss on EBITDA. PBT £7.5m vs consensus £7.4m = marginal beat on PBT. The gap between EBITDA miss and PBT beat implies lower-than-expected D&A, interest, or IFRS16 lease charges vs broker models. Return on Capital Employed: c.70% — high, consistent with capital-light model.

"aided by record metal margin performance, which helped offset inflationary pressures"

Labour cost inflation explicitly flagged: "ongoing inflationary pressures, notably in labour costs."

5. Capital / new stores New store: Leeds, summer 2026. First new store announcement in this cycle. Leeds provides access to a "new, large market." No financial guidance on capex or earnings contribution.

6. Qualitative tone / FY27 outlook CEO: "Whilst the macroeconomic uncertainty in recent weeks leads to a degree of caution due to the risks of increased inflation and interest rates, our superior customer service, omnichannel business model and exciting growth plans mean we are well placed to take advantage of opportunities to further increase market share and build long term value for shareholders."

"Macroeconomic uncertainty… degree of caution due to risks of increased inflation and interest rates" — this is cautious language on the outlook. Not a downgrade, but a flag. No numeric FY27 guidance.

EPS quality check: PBT c.£7.5m; expected tax at ~25% → EPS ~7.0p reported. Sharescope FY1 consensus 6.7p (adj basis). No obvious tax distortions flagged in the RNS. ✅ Clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 delivery: PBT £7.5m (+83% YoY, +1.4% vs consensus) — in-line to marginal beat. FY27 forward language: "macroeconomic uncertainty… degree of caution due to the risks of increased inflation and interest rates." No numeric FY27 guidance. Qualitative-only growth guidance ("exciting growth plans") with a caution caveat.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY26 delivered in-line (marginal PBT beat offset by EBITDA miss). FY27 language is cautious with macro uncertainty flagged. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

Divergence check: FY26 current year PBT is a beat (+83% YoY, marginal beat vs consensus) but FY27 tone is cautious. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery (modest beat on current year, cautious language on next year). Carry as named row.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

MOTR · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

Phase 0A year label mappings:

  • Next year end: 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26
  • 1y ago = FY25 · 2y ago = FY24 · 3y ago = FY23
  • FY2 = FY27

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-checks: FY23 H1+H2 = 786.7+653.5 = 1,440.2 ✅. FY24 H1+H2 = 607.2+479.4 = 1,086.6 ✅. FY25 H1+H2 = 563.1+610.0 = 1,173.1 ✅. EPS: FY23 2.7+(−3.4)=−0.7 ✅. FY24 −3.1+(−4.2)=−7.3 ✅. FY25 1.7+1.9=3.6 ✅.

Revenue growth trajectory: FY24 −24.6% → FY25 +8.0% → FY26 +8.0%. Recovery from FY24 trough, now two consecutive years of +8% growth. 🟢 Steady — consistent +8% growth rate for FY25 and FY26, both outperforming the used car market.

EPS growth trajectory: FY24 −7.3p → FY25 3.6p → FY26 ~7.0p. 🟢 Accelerating — turning from losses through profitability recovery. Trajectory is strongly positive though starting from a very low base.

Acceleration flags:

  • Revenue: FY26 RNS-derived +8.0% vs FY25 actual +8.0% → no acceleration (identical growth rate — consensus-derived).
  • EPS: FY26 implied ~7.0p vs FY25 3.6p = +94.4% vs FY25 (n/m from loss). Acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived) — the first year of meaningful profitability.

EPS trajectory: FY25 H2 1.9p → FY26 H1 +82.4% → FY26 H2 implied +89.5%. 🟢 Accelerating — strong.

Revenue trajectory: FY25 H2 +27.2% → FY26 H1 +15.0% → FY26 H2 +1.3%. 🟡 Volatile — H2 revenue growth rate decelerating sharply (27% → 15% → 1%). The H2 slowdown is partly seasonal (H1 heavier in used cars) but the rate decline warrants attention.

H2 revenue slowdown context: FY26 H2 implied £618.1m vs FY25 H2 £610.0m = +1.3% only. This follows H1 +15.0%. The deceleration may reflect: (a) tougher FY25 H2 comparator (£610m was strong), (b) used car market softening in late calendar 2025 / early 2026, (c) macroeconomic caution referenced by CEO.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-FY mode — written, NOT scored)

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg 52.8% × £1,265.8m = £668.1m
  • EPS baseline: 1yr avg 47.2% × 6.7p = 3.2p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £647.7m ÷ FY1 fc £1,265.8m = 51.2% vs baseline 52.8% → deviation = 🟡 [−1.6pp] → 🔴 CAUTION (marginal miss, just below −1.5pp threshold)
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 3.1p ÷ FY1 fc 6.7p = 46.3% vs baseline 47.2% → deviation = 🟡 [−0.9pp] → 🟡 IN LINE (within ±1.5pp)
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > (668.1m × 1.015) = £678.1m [🔴 ✗ — £647.7m below threshold]. H1 EPS > (3.2p × 1.015) = 3.2p [🔴 ✗ — 3.1p marginal miss].

Not scored in Phase 5. H1 tracking is marginally soft on revenue, in-line on EPS.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (scored in Phase 5)

H2 base: FY1 consensus £1,265.8m; RNS implies volume ~1,267m → using ~1,267m (RNS-derived). Implied H2 revenue = £1,267m − £647.7m = £619.3m (RNS-derived). EPS H2 = 6.7p fc − 3.1p = 3.6p (consensus-derived; actual H2 EPS likely ~3.9p if FY26 EPS is ~7.0p).

Revenue H2 YoY: £619.3m vs FY25 H2 £610.0m = +1.5% YoY. Classification: 🟡 flat (−5 to +5% band).

EPS H2 YoY: 3.6p vs FY25 H2 1.9p = +89.5% YoY (consensus-derived). But if actual FY26 EPS ~7.0p → H2 EPS ~3.9p → +105% YoY. Classification: 🟢 strong (>+10% YoY) — firmly.

H2 momentum classification: 🟢 strong on EPS / 🟡 flat on revenue — the EPS recovery is strong from the very depressed FY25 H2 base, driven by volume growth and record metal margins. Revenue H2 growth is minimal, reflecting market maturation.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +91.4% net change (3.5p → 6.7p), mostly at H1 results (June 2025). Stable since November. Last 4 weeks: 🔴 FLAT.
  • Revenue trend: +9.8% net change. Stable since November.
  • Divergence: Share price 116.75p vs consensus TP 190p = 62.7% upside. Price has been flat at 190p from June 2025 through March 2026 before falling recently to 116.75p — another extreme de-rating on flat/positive EPS. Macro fears (inflation, interest rates) and used car market concerns are likely drivers.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

Key context: MOTR uses floorplan financing (vehicle stocking loans) which is included in net debt at H1 (£50.5m), then repaid as vehicles sell. This creates large H1 net debt → H2 net cash swings. The year-end position (FY1fc −£6.5m net cash) is the meaningful figure.

  • Net borrowing: FY23 H2 £1.2m / FY24 H2 −£0.1m / FY25 H2 £4.0m → H1 FY26 £50.5m → FY1fc −£6.5m (net cash) → FY2fc −£14.8m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY23 2.3x / FY24 3.7x (peak losses) / FY25 4.4x → FY1fc −0.2x (net cash) / FY2fc −0.5x
  • Interest cover: H1 FY26 1.4x (stocking loan interest heavy) → FY1fc 1.7x → FY2fc 2.2x
  • ND/FCF: FY1fc −1.1x (net cash generating)

Interest cover at 1.7x FY1fc is low but improving. This is structurally driven by IFRS16 lease interest on vehicle storage sites, not true financial leverage risk. The H1 net debt spike is entirely inventory-driven and normalises by year-end. ND/EBITDA trajectory strongly improving.

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — interest cover 1.7x is low but structural (IFRS16 lease interest + stocking loans, both seasonal and asset-backed). Improving to 2.2x FY2. No covenant risk, no dilution risk. 🟡 — written in full but NOT scored in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • FY26 implied EPS ~7.0p vs FY25 3.6p → ✅ FY1fc EPS growing +94.4% vs prior year
  • FY26 implied revenue ~£1,267m vs FY25 £1,173.1m → ✅ FY1fc Revenue growing +8.0% vs prior year
  • ✅✅ FY1fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs prior year actual

Step 2 — FY27 vs FY26:

  • FY2fc EPS 10.5p vs FY1fc 6.7p → ✅ FY2fc EPS growing +56.7%
  • FY2fc Revenue £1,351.0m vs FY1fc £1,265.8m → ✅ FY2fc Revenue growing +6.7%
  • ✅✅ FY2fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY1fc

3.6 Structural Flags

Capital-light model: ROCE ~70% confirms the floorplan model working efficiently. No owned inventory risk (vehicles on stocking loan). This is genuinely asset-light and high-quality earnings.

AI integration: Agentic AI tool for quote reactivation added ~900 incremental sales (~1.4% of total). Use of data for buying and pricing "firmly embedded." This is early-stage but differentiating vs smaller independents.

Leeds store: First new site in recent years. Summer 2026 opening means FY27 impact is partial year. Based on existing store economics (~65,000/21 stores = ~3,095 units/store × ~£19,500 = ~£60m revenue/store), Leeds could contribute £40–60m revenue at maturity, £0.8–1.2m PBT. At FY28 full run-rate, meaningful EPS accretion. For FY27, pre-opening costs likely drag ~£1–2m on PBT.

Macro sensitivity: Used car prices are sensitive to interest rate cycles (affordability), consumer confidence, and EV transition (disruption to residual values). CEO flagged "risks of increased inflation and interest rates" specifically. If rates rise further or consumer confidence falls, used car demand and metal margins could both deteriorate.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

MOTR · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — Record retail volumes and PBT beat: 65,000 units at +8% YoY is the headline volume metric — record and ahead of market growth (+2.2% used car market in calendar 2025). Combined with PBT c.£7.5m (+83% YoY, +1.4% vs consensus) on record metal margins, this is a clean delivery. Volumes are the #1 driver because they validate the market share thesis — MOTR consistently takes share in a competitive market. Driver #1.

#2 Driver — Leeds store and pipeline expansion: The first new store announcement provides a re-rating catalyst beyond the current year's numbers. Brokers will model Leeds contributing ~£50–60m revenue at maturity (FY28) and refresh their long-term store rollout assumptions. If MOTR can open 1–2 stores per year, the growth algorithm changes materially — the current 21-store estate could expand towards 25–28 over 3–5 years. This is the key FY27 and FY28 upgrade narrative. Driver #2.

#2 Forecast revisions:

FY26 (FY1):

  • Revenue: hold at £1,265–1,270m — volumes confirm in-line. Marginal upward nudge if metal margins were above modelled.
  • EBITDA: hold or marginal trim — £27.0m actual vs £28.5m consensus = −5.3% miss. Brokers may cut FY26 EBITDA by £1–1.5m.
  • PBT: hold or marginal upgrade — £7.5m vs £7.4m consensus = marginal beat. EPS: marginal upgrade to ~7.0p from 6.7p.

FY27 (FY2):

  • Revenue: hold at £1,351m or slight trim — Leeds partial year adds ~£20–30m in FY27, offsetting any organic softening. MOTR guidance caution on macro slightly reduces confidence in +6.7% growth rate.
  • EPS: FY27 consensus 10.5p at risk — the implied progression from ~7.0p FY26 to 10.5p FY27 (+50%) requires either: (a) significant Leeds contribution (unlikely in partial year), (b) strong organic volume growth, (c) further metal margin expansion, or (d) additional store openings. CEO caution on macro makes (b) uncertain; (c) is at record already; (d) only Leeds announced. Brokers may trim FY27 EPS towards 8.5–9.5p.
  • TP: hold or slight trim from 190p. Macro caution caps upside.

#3 Target price: Brokers will likely hold TPs at 180–200p. The share at 116.75p already prices in material caution. Leeds announcement provides a modest positive offset to the macro caution language. Net: no TP changes or marginal trims to £175–195p range.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: No explicit conservative language in the FY26 delivery (volumes and PBT are clean). The FY27 macro caution is the only forward softness. No "not less than" language. Standard pre-results trading update tone — neither conservative nor bullish.

#5 Key risk: FY27 EPS consensus of 10.5p appears stretched given: partial-year Leeds contribution, macro headwinds flagged by CEO, EBITDA miss in FY26 (cost pressures from labour inflation), and no organic growth acceleration. If brokers trim FY27 EPS towards 8.5–9.5p, that is a 10–19% cut to forward consensus — material for sentiment.

"Whilst the macroeconomic uncertainty in recent weeks leads to a degree of caution due to the risks of increased inflation and interest rates"

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = marginal upgrade (~+0.3p on PBT beat). Tone = Neutral to Constructive. Given macro caution language offsetting the beat, settling at Neutral. ✅ Consistent.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

FY26 delivered cleanly (record volumes, PBT beat), but EBITDA miss (−5.3% vs consensus), macro caution language, and likely stretched FY27 consensus combine to limit the upgrade cycle. Leeds is a positive structural signal but does not move near-term numbers. Market will note the delivery without re-rating.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT — MOTR

57/100 · Confidence: 50–65 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

Raw score: 57

Para 1 — Headline numbers: MOTR delivered a clean FY26 outcome on the key metrics: c.65,000 retail units (+8% YoY) — a new record — and PBT c.£7.5m (+83% YoY), a marginal 1.4% beat vs the £7.4m consensus. The used car market grew only 2.2% in calendar year 2025, so MOTR's 6% volume growth in that period represents continued meaningful market share gains. The AI-driven quote reactivation tool contributed ~900 incremental sales. Record metal margin performance was the profitability driver, offsetting "ongoing inflationary pressures, notably in labour costs." The one blemish on the delivery is EBITDA of c.£27.0m vs consensus £28.5m — a 5.3% miss — suggesting cost inflation (primarily labour, given NLW increases) has been running above broker assumptions.

Para 2 — H2 momentum and upgrade resilience: Implied H2 revenue is £618–619m — up only +1.3–1.5% YoY vs FY25 H2's £610m, firmly in the 🟡 flat classification. This sharp deceleration from H1's +15% YoY is the key caution signal. H2 EPS implied is 3.6–3.9p — up +89–105% YoY vs FY25 H2's depressed 1.9p, so the EPS recovery is genuine. The upgrade resilience on EPS is supported by the volume trajectory, but the revenue H2 deceleration and EBITDA miss suggest operational leverage is not flowing through as cleanly as brokers modelled. Leeds provides a genuine FY27 structural positive, but it opens in summer 2026 — partial year at best, with pre-opening costs likely a drag. The macro caution is the genuine bear case: if interest rates rise further and used car affordability deteriorates, FY26's record metal margins could normalise in FY27.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and verdict: FY26 revisions will be minor: PBT held to marginal upgrade (~+£0.1–0.2m), EBITDA trimmed by £1–1.5m to £27m actual, EPS nudged to ~7.0p from 6.7p. The more significant issue is FY27: consensus 10.5p (+50% from ~7.0p FY26) looks increasingly difficult to justify given: partial-year Leeds (likely £20–30m FY27 revenue, £0.3–0.5m net PBT contribution after opening costs), organic volume growth slowing in a cautious macro environment, and labour cost inflation persisting. Brokers may trim FY27 EPS towards 8.5–9.5p — a cut of 10–19% that would be a meaningful sentiment drag. TPs likely held at 175–195p range. The 116.75p share price at 62% upside to the low end of that TP range already prices in a lot of caution — so today's delivery is not sufficient to reverse the de-rating, but equally the fundamental delivery is not bad enough to spark further selling. 🏁 Neutral: FY26 delivered cleanly but EBITDA miss and FY27 uncertainty limit the re-rating; Leeds is the medium-term catalyst; hold and wait for FY27 guidance at final results in June 2026.

scorecards.analysisText:
MPAC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings: FY25 = FY1 (next year end 31/12/25) · FY24 = 1y ago · FY23 = 2y ago · FY22 = 3y ago · FY26 = FY2.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

MPAC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Interpreting RNS as FY results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 33.3p · Revenue £170.0m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 37.2p · Revenue £172.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −25.0% (44.4p → 33.3p) over period. Step-down in July 25 (44.4p → 32.9p on revised view of acquisitions), then marginal recovery to 33.3p by Feb 26. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT. Revenue net change: −22.1% (£218.1m → £170.0m).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.0% of FY = £83.3m · EPS n/a (Sharescope H2 glitch — all historical EPS H2 = FY figure, unusable for EPS baseline).

⚠️ Sharescope EPS H2 field glitch confirmed: 3y ago H2 13.3 = FY 13.3; 2y ago H2 26.2 = FY 26.2; 1y ago H2 35.2 = FY 35.2. H1+H2≠FY in all cases (H1 figures exist separately). True H2 EPS derived as FY minus H1: FY22 H2 = 13.3−3.6 = 9.7p; FY23 H2 = 26.2−6.5 = 19.7p; FY24 H2 = 35.2−15.2 = 20.0p.

  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24 H1): Revenue £60.0m · EPS 15.2p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Revenue: FY25fc £170.0m − H1 £84.7m = H2 £85.3m vs FY24 H2 £62.4m → +36.7% YoY. EPS: FY25fc 33.3p − H1 12.1p = H2 21.2p vs FY24 H2 20.0p → +6.0% YoY.
  • FX: Phase 0B check — MPAC has significant international revenue (Americas, EMEA, APAC). RNS does not prominently disclose a Currency Movements table or single-currency exposure >30%. No specific FX section identified. Revenue is reported in GBP. No Phase 0B trigger — N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY22 −£2.8m (net cash) → FY23 −£1.6m (net cash) → FY24 +£37.5m → H1 FY25 +£55.0m → FY25fc +£57.4m → FY26fc +£49.4m. ND/EBITDA: FY25fc 2.5x, FY26fc 2.1x. Interest cover FY25fc 3.9x. ND/FCF FY26fc 5.6x. Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 3.9x interest cover is below comfort threshold; monitoring required but no immediate revision driver.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

MPAC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

  1. Revenue — FY25 actual: £174.1m vs FY25fc £170.0m = +£4.1m / +2.4% beat. vs FY24 £122.4m = +42.2% YoY (acquisition-driven; CSi/BCA first full year).

"Revenue was up 42% and underlying operating profits increased 51%, reflecting the full year contribution of the acquisitions completed in 2024"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual: Underlying EPS 35.9p vs FY25fc 33.3p = +2.6p / +7.8% beat. Underlying PBT £13.5m vs FY24 £10.6m, +27% YoY. Underlying ROS 10.4% vs 9.8% FY24, +0.6pp. Gross margin +6.2pp YoY. Statutory PBT loss of £7.7m (non-underlying items, primarily pension and restructuring). Basic EPS statutory −31.8p.

"Underlying earnings per share: 35.9p (FY24: 35.2p)"

FY26e EPS bridge:

  • New base: FY25 underlying EPS 35.9p (actual)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: CSi and BCA were both acquired in Nov/Sep 2024 respectively — FY25 was their first full year. No further annualisation uplift into FY26 as FY25 already captured full-year contribution. Delta = nil.
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY25 EBITDA not explicitly stated but underlying OP = £18.1m + D&A implied ~£5m → EBITDA ~£23m (aligns with FY25fc £23.0m). FY26 organic growth: RNS explicitly notes "growing price competition," "geopolitical uncertainty," order book down 24% to £90.0m. Pipeline growing but not converting. Organic EBITDA growth likely flat to slight decline in FY26 without new OE order wins.
  • Interest step-up delta: Net debt increased from £37.5m (FY24) to £58.9m (FY25 including leases) — finance costs grew materially. FY25 underlying PBT £13.5m vs underlying OP £18.1m implies interest/other = −£4.6m. FY26fc PBT £15.1m vs FY26fc EBITDA £23.4m → after D&A ~£5m EBIT £18.4m − PBT £15.1m = interest ~£3.3m. Interest cost slightly reducing FY26. No step-up trigger (net debt not growing meaningfully FY26).
  • Implied FY26e EPS: FY25 actual 35.9p + nil inorganic + ~flat organic + minor interest benefit = broadly 35–37p range. Stale FY26fc 37.2p — consensus appears fair, no revision needed. Slight downward risk given order intake uncertainty.
  1. Order book: Closing order book £90.0m vs £118.5m FY24 = −24% YoY. Order intake £150.9m vs £119.7m FY24 = +26% (strong intake but converts slowly; customers deferring). Book covers ~66% of FY26 forecast revenue (stated by company). Order book provides incomplete coverage and is the primary FY26 revenue risk.

"The current order book, which provides c.66% coverage of forecast 2026 revenue, has remained flat"

  1. Margin signals: Underlying ROS 10.4% FY25 vs 9.8% FY24. For FY26: "price competition for OE orders has increased, resulting in pressure on gross margins." Mitigated by cost reductions. No explicit margin guidance for FY26. Service revenue 23% of FY25 total — resilient short-cycle buffer.

"In the context of lower market volumes, price competition for OE orders has increased, resulting in pressure on gross margins"

  1. Capital returns: No dividend (FY25 and FY26). Pension buy-in completed with Aviva — cash return of ~£5.0m expected on wind-up. Net debt £47.9m (excl leases) at year-end.
  2. Qualitative tone FY26: "In line with full year market expectations, which as in previous years will be second half weighted, but, in the context of increasingly uncertain market conditions, it is difficult to predict the full impact of the Middle East conflict on the timing of customer capital investment decisions." Order book flat in Q1 2026 despite growing pipeline. Proactive cost reduction taken in Q1 2026. "Difficult to predict" is a notable hedge.

"In the context of increasingly uncertain market conditions, it is difficult to predict the full impact of the Middle East conflict on the timing of customer capital investment decisions"

EPS quality check: Statutory PBT −£7.7m vs underlying PBT +£13.5m due to non-underlying items (pension costs, reorganisation). Confirm underlying EPS 35.9p uses adjusted basis. No tax distortion flagged — underlying rate appears normal.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: "Remains in line with full year market expectations" but with explicit hedges: order book −24%, price competition increasing, geopolitical uncertainty, "difficult to predict." Company-disclosed FY26 consensus: revenue implied ~172m (company consensus for FY26 not broken out, using Sharescope £172.0m). In-line language combined with downside hedges.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — in-line maintained but with explicit downside caveats (order intake deferral, price competition, macro uncertainty). Guidance is numeric (in-line) but caveated. Points range: −5 to −8.

Divergence check: FY25 delivered above consensus (+2.4% rev, +7.8% EPS). FY26 outlook cautious. 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery — FY25 beat but FY26 cautious with meaningful execution risk.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

MPAC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 corrections applied: see Phase 1. FY22: FY figure 13.3p, H1 3.6p → H2 = 9.7p. FY23: FY 26.2p, H1 6.5p → H2 = 19.7p. FY24: FY 35.2p, H1 15.2p → H2 = 20.0p.

Revenue growth trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — +16.9%, +7.2%, +42.2% (acquisition spike). FY26 guided flat/−1%.

EPS growth trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — +97.0%, +34.4%, +2.0%. Dilution from share issuance for acquisitions absorbed most of the revenue/profit uplift.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: FY25 actual +42.2% vs FY24 +7.2% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived) — but acquisition-driven, not organic.
  • EPS: FY25 actual +2.0% vs FY24 +34.4% → no acceleration (RNS-derived). 🔴

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth

H2 derived: FY25 H2 = £174.1m − £84.7m = £89.4m. FY25 H2 EPS = 35.9p − 12.1p = 23.8p.
