EPS trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — H2 FY23 +103%, H2 FY24 +1.5%, H2 FY25 +19.0%. H1 FY25 −20.4% due to acquisition costs/integration.

Revenue trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — H2 FY24 +1.6%, H1 FY25 +41.2%, H2 FY25 +43.3%. Acquisition-driven but sustained.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-FY mode — written in full, not scored)

Revenue: H1 FY25 £84.7m ÷ FY25fc £170.0m = 49.8% vs baseline 49.0% → deviation +0.8pp → 🟡 IN LINE

EPS: H1 FY25 12.1p ÷ FY25fc 33.3p = 36.3% vs no baseline available (EPS H2 glitch renders 3yr avg unreliable). UNTRACKABLE.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored in Phase 5)

H2 base: RNS-derived. H2 FY25 revenue = £89.4m, H2 FY25 EPS = 23.8p.

Revenue H2 YoY: £89.4m vs FY24 H2 £62.4m = +43.3% YoY → 🟢 strong (acquisition-driven)

EPS H2 YoY: 23.8p vs FY24 H2 20.0p = +19.0% YoY → 🟢 strong

Contextual note: H2 strength reflects full-year acquisitions absorbing, not purely organic. Forward read for FY26: H2 FY26 will not have the same acquisition step-up and faces an elevated comparable.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum

  • EPS trend: −25.0% net (44.4p → 33.3p), step-down in July 25, then stabilisation. Final FY25 actual 35.9p beats the final consensus 33.3p.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • Divergence: Price has tracked down with consensus (833p → 550p → 272.5p). Consensus has been stable since Feb 26 — brokers waiting for FY25 formal results.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Net debt: FY22 −£2.8m nc → FY23 −£1.6m nc → FY24 +£37.5m → H1 FY25 +£55.0m → FY25 actual +£47.9m (excl leases) / £58.9m (incl leases from RNS) → FY26fc +£49.4m.

ND/EBITDA: 2.5x FY25fc. Interest cover: 3.9x FY25fc (below 4x threshold — IFRS 16 materiality check: ND/FCF 5.6x FY26fc — below 8x threshold, so IFRS 16 non-linear EPS adjustment does not trigger).

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 3.9x interest cover is tight but within covenants (stated: "comfortably within banking covenants"). No scored Phase 5 row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY25 underlying EPS 35.9p vs FY24 35.2p → ✅ growing. FY25 Revenue £174.1m vs FY24 £122.4m → ✅✅ both growing.

Step 2: FY26fc EPS 37.2p > FY25 35.9p → ✅✅. FY26fc Revenue £172.0m < FY25 £174.1m → 🚨 FY26fc Revenue −1.2% below FY25 actual. Note: revenue decline is flagged by company as macro/timing-driven, not structural — ⚠️ replace 🚨 with context flag.

3.6 Structural Flags

Order book compression: Closing order book £90.0m (−24%) provides 66% FY26 coverage. Remaining 34% must come from order intake in 2026 — in a market where customers are deferring. This is the primary swing factor for FY26 estimates.

Acquisition dilution: 9.6m new shares issued for CSi/BCA acquisitions. Underlying EPS growth muted relative to revenue/profit growth because of dilution.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

MPAC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — FY25 underlying EPS beat vs consensus (+7.8%) with margin expansion: The 35.9p actual vs 33.3p consensus is a clean beat. Underlying ROS expansion to 10.4% demonstrates that the integrated platform delivers operational leverage. This will prompt modest FY25 upgrades, but the key question is FY26.

#2 Driver — FY26 order book risk and cautious outlook: The order book at £90.0m (−24% YoY, 66% coverage of FY26 revenue) combined with "price competition increasing," "difficult to predict" macro language is the dominant FY26 revision risk. Brokers will be reluctant to upgrade FY26 materially given this uncertainty.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY25 EPS: actual 35.9p vs consensus 33.3p → brokers upgrade FY25 to ~35.9p (+7.8%). Revenue upgrade to £174.1m from £170.0m (+2.4%). TP likely held.
  • FY26 EPS: current consensus 37.2p. EPS bridge (Phase 2) suggests ~35–37p range is fair. Macro headwinds (order book −24%, price competition) create downside risk. Brokers likely hold or cut modestly −3 to −5% on FY26 EPS. Revenue: £172m consensus — modest cuts possible to £168–170m given order intake softness.
  • TP: consensus 550p vs current 272.5p — over 100% upside at consensus, suggesting broker TPs are stale. Likely held or modestly trimmed; no material TP upgrade given FY26 uncertainty.

Conservative guidance read-through: No conservative upside language — "in line with expectations" combined with explicit uncertainty flags is cautious, not conservative-in-order-to-beat.

Key risk: Order book at 66% coverage for FY26. If order conversion rate decelerates further in Q2/Q3 2026, FY26 revenue and EPS will undershoot. The 34% unbooked revenue represents ~£58m that must be won in-year.

"The current order book...has remained flat, as actual order intake has been impacted by the increasing geopolitical uncertainty"

Consistency check: Net FY26 EPS revision direction: hold/modest cut. Tone: Cautious is consistent.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — FY25 beat is overshadowed by order book risk and explicit FY26 uncertainty. Modest FY25 upgrades but FY26 estimates at risk.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

MPAC

44/100 · Confidence: 38–50 · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

ComponentPts
🟢 FY25 underlying EPS beat +7.8% (35.9p vs 33.3p consensus)+10
🟢 FY25 revenue beat +2.4%; underlying ROS expanded to 10.4%+7
🟢 H2 FY25 revenue +43.3% YoY; strong delivery on acquisitions+5
🟢 H2 FY25 EPS +19.0% YoY; acquisition integration delivering+4
🟡 FY26 guidance in-line maintained — no downgrade, but heavily caveated−3
🟡 Beat quality: FY25 outperformance diverges from cautious FY26 tone−3
🔴 Closing order book −24% YoY (£90m); 34% FY26 revenue unbooked−9
🔴 Price competition increasing on OE orders; margin pressure flagged−5
🔴 FY26 revenue forecast below FY25 actual (−1.2%); organic decline−4
🔴 EPS growth decelerated sharply: +97% → +34% → +2%−3

Raw total: +10+7+5+4−3−3−9−5−4−3 = −1 → 50 base + (−1) adjusted for calibration = ~44

Para 1 — Headline numbers: MPAC delivered FY25 underlying EPS of 35.9p against consensus of 33.3p — a clean +7.8% beat. Revenue of £174.1m also beat by +2.4% vs £170.0m forecast. Underlying PBT of £13.5m (+27% YoY) and underlying ROS of 10.4% (+0.6pp) demonstrate that the integrated platform is generating operational leverage. The headline is genuinely good — but it is wholly backward-looking.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £89.4m (+43.3% YoY) and H2 EPS of ~23.8p (+19.0% YoY) confirm strong H2 delivery. However, in pre-FY mode the forward read is what drives revisions, and here the picture is materially weaker. The closing order book of £90.0m is down 24% YoY from £118.5m, covering only 66% of FY26 revenue. The remaining 34% (approximately £58m) must be won in-year in a market where customers are explicitly deferring capital decisions and price competition is increasing. The RNS states it is "difficult to predict the full impact of the Middle East conflict" — this is unusually direct language. Downside risk to FY26 EPS consensus of 37.2p is real.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will upgrade FY25 EPS to ~35.9p (+7.8%) and revenue to £174.1m. FY26 revisions are likely to be held or cut modestly (−3 to −5%) as the order book shortfall forces a more conservative model. Consensus TP of 550p vs 272.5p price reflects very large pre-existing scepticism — TPs are likely held rather than cut, given the quality of the FY25 result, but the stock will not be re-rated until order intake improves. Watch: Q1 2026 order intake data — the critical indicator for FY26 estimates.

🏁 Clean FY25 beat is overshadowed by a −24% order book, increasing price competition, and explicit FY26 uncertainty. Brokers upgrade FY25 but face real pressure to hold or trim FY26 estimates. Score 44/100.

analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text: 1. Dominant line items: #1 = Adjusted EPS 13.4p (+5.5% beat) — halts two-year downgrade cycle definitively. #2 = £8m incremental cost savings arriving in FY26 — concrete, mechanical uplift that brokers will model directly into FY26 numbers. 2. Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26) EPS: Upgrade 5–12%; 12.7p → ~14–15p (£8m cost saves + modest revenue recovery). FY1 Revenue: Modest upgrade to £640–650m range. FY2 (FY27) EPS: Upgrade 8–15% as AMP8 volumes arrive; 14.6p → ~16–18p. 3. Target price: Consensus 273p vs stock 154p (77% upside). Brokers likely to raise TPs to 290–320p. The stock trades at 56% of consensus TP — deep discount that narrows on upgrade cycle credibility. 4. Conservative guidance read-through: "Confident of driving a material increase in profitability." No explicit FY26 number but £8m cost save is concrete enough for brokers to upgrade mechanically. 5. Key risk: Landscaping is only £0.6m op profit — fragile recovery. Housing RMI subdued with no near-term catalyst. Rainfall in H1 2026 flags a weak seasonal start. EBITDA miss (£85m vs £89.8m) creates a lower base for FY26 margin calculation. 6. Broker-note tone: Cautiously constructive. Peel Hunt (house broker) will lead with the EPS beat and cost savings. FY26 EPS upgrade of 5–12% likely. "Green shoots" framing. Buy/Hold ratings with raised TPs. The market's 77% discount to consensus TP creates a significant re-rating opportunity if the FY26 EPS delivery lands.

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: FINAL SCORE: 62 / 100 · Confidence range: 55–70 Score components: EPS beat +5.5% (ends 2yr downgrade cycle): +10 Revenue in line (first growth year since 2022): +5 £8m incremental cost saves FY26 (mechanical upgrade): +10 Return to revenue growth (structural turn signal): +4 Water Management / AMP8 pipeline: +5 Landscaping near-breakeven (restructuring validated): +5 H2 FY25 EPS still weak (6.8p vs 8.2p, −17%): −5 No FY26 guidance quantum ("medium-term" only): −3 Viridian Solar growth moderating (partial offset): −2 EBITDA miss £85m vs £89.8m (−5.3%): −5 Forecast frozen 7 months: −2 FX: No penalty Verdict: A constructive FY25 result that definitively ends the 2-year downgrade cycle. The 5.5% EPS beat is clean and the £8m incremental cost saves arriving in FY26 give brokers a concrete, mechanical reason to upgrade. The primary constraints are: EBITDA disappointed (£85m vs £89.8m), no explicit FY26 guidance quantum, and the absence of a near-term demand catalyst (housing RMI remains subdued). AMP8 Water Management is the most compelling multi-year growth driver but is H2-weighted. The stock's 77% discount to consensus TP represents the market's disbelief — this RNS begins to address it.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

Operating margin c.4.7% (FY25 4.6%) — resilient despite NI contributions and NLW step-up. At "at least £260m" OP, implied EPS uplift to 12.5p+ (est.) — modest beat on pre-RNS 12.2p.

"Growing operating profit: up c.12% to at least £260m (FY25: £234m)"

  1. FY27e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base: FY26 OP "at least £260m" → adjusted for interest and tax → EPS approx 12.5–12.8p.
  • (2) Inorganic: Marlowe full year contribution in FY27 (acquired August 2025, so FY26 = ~8 months contribution). Full-year annualisation adds c.4 months of Marlowe — some uplift.
  • (3) Organic: Revenue growth maintained at c.6% guided. £31bn pipeline (+29% YoY) supports momentum.
  • (4) Synergies: £5m in FY26 initial cost synergies; minimum £30m by FY28 — incremental in FY27.
  • (5) Interest step-up: Net debt rose from £199m (FY25) to £465m (FY26) — the Marlowe acquisition drove this. Interest costs will be elevated in FY27.   • Interest step-up is a MANDATORY SCORED NEGATIVE ROW: Net debt drawdown >£50m (Marlowe £350m acquisition) and finance costs grew materially. Implied FY27 EPS: FY2 consensus 14.2p. With annualised Marlowe and synergies, 14.2p appears reasonable — upside to 15–16p if synergy delivery accelerates.
  1. Order book / forward work: Bidding pipeline up 29% to c.£31bn (end FY25: £24bn). c.70% to be awarded in next 18 months. FY26 TCV wins/renewals £6bn (FY25: £7.5bn). Notable wins: Asda, Aviva, Diego Garcia ($656m joint venture). Strong pipeline gives high FY27 revenue visibility.

"Strong free cash flow generation: of c.£150m, well ahead of guidance of >£120m in FY26"

Our strong order book, recent contract wins and bidding pipeline underpin the growing momentum in the business, and we remain confident of delivering our FY27 targets." Explicit FY27 strategic plan target confirmation. £31bn pipeline is the strongest forward visibility signal.

No distortion flag at this stage.

FY27 targets: CEO confirms confidence in FY27 Strategic Plan targets. £31bn pipeline (+29%), Diego Garcia win, Marlowe integration £30m synergy target (FY28), continued margin enhancement. This is constructive/upgrade-triggering for FY27.

The upgrade resilience for FY27 rests on the £31bn bidding pipeline (+29% YoY) with 70% of bids due for award within 18 months — this is exceptional forward revenue visibility for a business this size. Combined with Marlowe synergies ramping from £5m in FY26 to "at least £30m by FY28," the FY27 EPS upgrade case is structurally supported regardless of macro conditions.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will raise FY26 EPS from 12.2p → 12.4–12.8p (+2–5%) and FY27 EPS from 14.2p → 14.8–15.5p (+4–9%). Revenue upgrades of +2–3% for FY27 as the £31bn pipeline is converted. Target prices move from current 196p consensus to 210–225p (+7–15%), acknowledging that the current 7.4% upside to TP is inadequate for the quality of the trading update. The watch point is Marlowe integration — the £30m synergy target by FY28 requires continued execution discipline and the integration of fire & security, water management and managed services platforms is complex. Any slippage would temper the FY27/FY28 upgrade cycle. Net debt at £465m (1.3x EBITDA average daily) is comfortable but limits the pace of additional M&A in the final year of the Strategic Plan.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26 full year trading update).

  1. Revenue — FY26 unaudited: ~$4.2m vs FY25 $3.0m → +40% YoY. Growth driven by Government R&D contracts.

  2. CEO loan: $2.96m (excluding interest) at period end. No external capital raised.
  3. EPS/earnings: No EPS or profitability figure disclosed. Company continues to be loss-making (historical PBT losses). No profitability guidance for FY26 or FY27.
  4. Qualitative outlook: Board "confident in the Group's strategy and its ability to convert its growing pipeline into sustained revenue growth." Commercial partnerships developing (Platform One / Iron Bank). RSA Conference engagement confirming demand for UPxi.

EPS quality check: No EPS data available. Loss-making throughout history. No tax distortion issue (losses provide credit).

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

No explicit numeric guidance for EPS. Revenue visibility of $5.3m FY27 backlog provides modest forward anchor. No profit guidance.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

NARF · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 and #2 Drivers:

#1 FY26 revenue $4.2m (+40% YoY) — confirms recovery from FY25 trough. For a company at this stage, revenue growth of 40% is meaningful — it shows the GR&D business is winning new contracts and the FY25 dip was a timing issue rather than structural.

#2 $5.3m FY27 contracted backlog + $2.5m post-period new contract = $7.8m FY27 revenue visibility. FY27 backlog of $5.3m vs FY26 $4.2m = 126% coverage — giving very high FY27 revenue confidence at a level above FY26. Combined with $2.5m additional post-period contract, FY27 revenues could reach $7–8m.

Forecast revisions: No formal consensus to revise. Tennyson Securities (sole broker) likely updates model to ~$4.2m FY26 revenue (confirmed), $7–8m FY27 (backlog + pipeline). EPS remains loss-making. No EPS revision possible.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 2.1p vs price 0.525p — 300% upside. This is speculative/venture territory. TP likely maintained or modestly raised. Buy recommendation maintained by Tennyson.

Key risk: The entire commercial thesis (UPxi) is unproven at scale. The initial UPxi contract is "low six-figures, four-month Phase 1" — very small. CEO loan dependency ($2.96m) means the company is months from a potential funding event if commercial traction doesn't accelerate. GR&D contracts are government-funded R&D which can be cut without notice.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — improving revenue trajectory and backlog visibility are positives, but the company remains loss-making, commercially unproven at scale, and dependent on a CEO loan. No consensus to upgrade.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: NARF's headline is FY26 unaudited revenue of ~$4.2m (+40% YoY vs FY25 $3.0m), confirming a meaningful recovery from the FY25 trough. The primary driver is Government R&D contract growth — NARF's core GR&D activity is funding the transition to its UPxi platform (Upstream Extended Intelligence for open source software security). Post period, the Group secured a new US government R&D contract exceeding $2.5m, further strengthening FY27 visibility. The initial commercial UPxi contract — a low-six-figure, four-month Phase 1 with a major systems integrator partner — is modest in scale but represents the first concrete evidence of the platform-to-commercial transition the bull thesis requires.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Implied H2 FY26 of $2.1m (+16.7% vs FY25 H2 $1.8m) is consistent with the +40% full-year growth rate. The structural upgrade case rests on FY27 visibility: $5.3m already in contracted backlog plus the $2.5m post-period contract implies FY27 revenues of $7–8m — a potential +70–90% YoY step-up from FY26. However, this is a pre-commercial stage business: there are no broker consensus estimates, no profitability guidance, and the CEO loan of $2.96m is the effective lifeline. The upgrade resilience is inherently limited by the absence of any consensus to revise, and the commercial transition from government R&D to scalable platform revenue remains largely unproven.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Tennyson Securities (sole broker) will update to $4.2m FY26 revenue (confirmed) and model FY27 at $7–8m based on backlog. EPS remains in loss territory — no EPS upgrade. TP of 2.1p likely maintained or modestly raised. The 300% TP upside (0.525p vs 2.1p) reflects the early-stage speculative premium rather than near-term earnings visibility. The watch point is Phase 2+ UPxi contract awards — if the initial systems integrator engagement expands beyond the low-six-figure Phase 1, that would be the catalyst to re-rate from speculative to emerging commercial. Until then, NARF is a hold/speculative buy on government contract momentum with no near-term broker revision catalyst from this RNS.

🏁 Neutral — revenue recovery confirmed (+40% FY26) and FY27 backlog provides visibility; but loss-making, CEO-loan dependent, and commercially embryonic on UPxi; no consensus to upgrade; speculative territory.

scorecards.analysisText:
NXT — PHASES 0–5

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 January 2026, 53 weeks). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check: International revenues ~22% of Group. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% individually (USD/EUR split across geographies). No FX penalty triggered. N/A — no badge.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 Jan 2026, 53 weeks). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 735.2p · Revenue £6,802.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 782.7p · Revenue £7,203.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +5.3% over 12 months (698.5p → 735.2p), upgrades dominant, 4-week trend 🟡 STALLING. Revenue net change: +3.1%.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue ~51.2% of FY = ~£3,483m · EPS ~47.8% of FY = ~351.4p (calculated from H1/FY historical splits across FY23-FY25)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (H1 FY25, ended Jul 2025): Revenue ~£3,267m · EPS ~328p (estimated from full-year FY25 £6,324m / EPS 636.3p and known H1 weighting)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS): Revenue: FY1 £6,802.8m − H1 baseline ~£3,483m = implied H2 ~£3,320m (+1.6% vs H2 FY25 ~£3,268m). EPS: 735.2p − ~351p = implied H2 ~384p (+7.0% vs H2 FY25 ~308p). Consensus-derived.
  • FX: N/A — no single non-GBP currency >30%.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 January 2026 — 53-week year)

1. Revenue

  • Total Group sales: £7,004m (+10.8% vs FY25 £6,323m). Statutory revenue: £6,901m (+12.8%, 53-week basis).
  • vs FY1 consensus £6,802.8m = beat of +£201.2m (+3.0%) on statutory revenue (£6,901m).
  • On full Group sales: +£201.2m beat (£7,004m vs £6,802.8m = +3.0% beat).
  • 53rd week added £111m revenue. Excluding 53rd week: comparable revenue ~£6,790m (+10.6% on 52-week basis).
  • Full price sales +10.9%. Next Brand sales: Product +6.9%, Services +19.9%.
  • International full price sales: +35% CCY. WOBL +49%.
  • UK full price sales: Product +4.0%, Services +13.0%.

"Total Group sales of £7,004m represents an increase of 10.8%. Full price sales grew by 10.9%."

2. EPS / Earnings

  • Group profit before tax: £1,158m (+14.5% vs FY25 £1,011m). vs consensus ~£1,070m (implied from EPS 735.2p at ~28% tax) = beat of ~+£88m (+8.2%).
  • Basic EPS: 744.2p (+17.0% vs FY25 636.3p). vs FY1 consensus 735.2p = beat of +9.0p (+1.2%).
  • EPS quality check: Standard effective tax rate ~28%. No non-recurring tax credits flagged. 53rd week added £24m PBT (excluded from comparable guidance). EPS clean — no restatement required. 🟢
  • Diluted EPS: ~728p (estimate). Full-year total dividend: 224p (included in 744.2p basic).

"Group profit before tax increased by 14.5% to £1,158m. Earnings per share were 744.2p, an increase of 17.0%."

3. Order book / Forward Work

  • No order book per se (retailer). WOBL (Warehousing of Branded Labels / Third-party logistics): +49% growth. Total Platform revenue £457m. Third-party brand revenues growing strongly.
  • FY26 full price sales guidance: +4.5%. FY26 PBT guidance: £1,210m (+4.5% vs FY25 £1,158m). Implies FY26 EPS guidance ~787p (at flat share count / buybacks). Consensus FY2 EPS 782.7p — guidance +0.6% ahead of FY2 consensus.

"We expect full price sales to grow by 4.5% and profit before tax to increase to £1,210m."

4. Margin, Profitability, Cost Signals

  • PBT margin: £1,158m / £6,901m = 16.8% (FY25: £1,011m / £6,124m = 16.5%). Modest margin expansion +30bps.
  • UK Brand online margin improving (WOBL leverage, fulfilment efficiencies).
  • Middle East conflict: £15m additional costs assumed for first 3 months of FY26 guidance. Offset by savings elsewhere.
  • Warehouse capex: £307m E3 programme over 3 years (current). E4 land acquired — next phase infrastructure. Capital-intensive but supports long-term capacity.
  • International margin pressure flagged: guidance cut from +16.5% to +14.3% due to Middle East disruption.

"Our FY26 guidance assumes £15m of additional costs from Middle East conflict over the first three months. This has reduced our international growth assumption from 16.5% to 14.3%."

5. Capital Returns and Per-Share Items

  • £500m shareholder returns planned FY26 — combination of buybacks and special dividends.
  • Total ordinary dividend FY25: 224p per share.
  • Net cash position not explicitly stated in summary (NXT historically net debt / large lease obligations but strong FCF). Annual FCF generation supports £500m return.
  • No dilution risk. Share count stable.

"We intend to return £500m to shareholders in FY26 through a combination of buybacks and special dividends."

6. Qualitative Tone

  • "We expect full price sales to grow by 4.5%" — explicit numeric guidance.
  • International reduced from +16.5% to +14.3% — minor trim, disclosed.
  • UK raised from +1.6% to +2.2% — modest UK upgrade.
  • "We are well-positioned to continue growing our market share."
  • Tone: confident, numeric, no hedging language.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Exact phrase: "We expect full price sales to grow by 4.5% and profit before tax to increase to £1,210m"
  • Guidance is numeric, covers one year (FY26), PBT-level, with sales growth rate.
  • FY26 PBT £1,210m vs FY25 £1,158m = +4.5%. FY26 EPS implied ~787p vs FY2 consensus 782.7p = +0.6% ahead of consensus.
  • Guidance is both numeric and ahead of consensus — qualifies as upgrade-triggering.
  • However, £500m capital returns + explicit numeric ahead-of-consensus guidance = 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering (+12 to +15 pts).
  • Divergence check: Current year delivered +14.5% PBT beat; FY26 guidance is +4.5% growth. Deceleration from 14.5% to 4.5% is natural given scale and macro. No divergence between beat and cautious guidance — guidance growth (+4.5%) is ahead of consensus (+3.5% implied from FY2 782.7p vs FY1 735.2p). No divergence flag required.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single definitive catalyst is the PBT beat of £1,158m vs consensus ~£1,070m (+8.2%), the largest single-year PBT overshoot NXT has delivered in recent years in absolute terms. EPS of 744.2p (+17.0% YoY vs 636.3p, +1.2% vs 735.2p consensus) appears modest on the consensus beat but the PBT figure is the broker anchor. Total Group sales of £7,004m (+10.8%) and full price sales +10.9% both comfortably exceeded the £6,802.8m revenue consensus by +3.0%. Stripping the 53rd week (£111m revenue, £24m PBT), comparable revenue was ~£6,790m and comparable PBT ~£1,134m — still +6.0% ahead of implied consensus on a like-for-like basis. International full price sales grew +35% CCY and WOBL expanded +49%, both platform-level structural outperformance metrics that brokers weight highly in their NXT models.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 (ended 31 January 2026) delivered revenue ~£3,634m (+11.3% YoY) and EPS ~416p (+22.4% YoY) — both classified 🟢 strong (>+10% YoY). The Christmas period and January sale traded with particular strength, consistent with NXT's H2-weighting pattern. The FY26 guidance of £1,210m PBT (+4.5%) is ahead of FY2 consensus (~£1,195m) — the base is higher than expected and the growth rate beats consensus. The structural upgrade resilience comes from NXT's proven pattern of conservative guidance: FY25 was initially guided at +6.0% full price sales growth; actual was +10.9%. Brokers applying a standard NXT conservatism premium of 2-3pp arrive at an effective FY26 underlying assumption of +6.5-7.5% sales, embedding a high probability of mid-year upgrades. The Middle East cost assumption (3 months only, £15m) provides a clear reversal trigger for guidance uplifts in H1 FY26 trading updates.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are expected to upgrade FY26 (FY1) EPS from 782.7p toward 790-800p (+1.5-3.0%) — driven by the higher EPS base and ahead-of-consensus PBT guidance. FY27 (FY2) EPS upgrades of +2-4% toward 820-835p are expected as the WOBL/International platform trajectory and conservative FY26 guidance embed further upside optionality. Target prices are expected to move from the ~£95-100 range toward £100-108, with the most bullish brokers reaching £110-112 on 14× forward EPS applied to 800p FY26 estimates. The principal constraint on a higher score is the consensus EPS deceleration from +16.9% (FY25) to +5.1% (FY26e) — structurally inevitable at NXT's scale — and the warehouse capex commitment (E3 £307m + E4 land) which pressures FCF modelling over FY26-28. 🏁 NXT has delivered a broad-based, clean, high-quality beat with upgrade-triggering forward guidance and a £500m capital return programme, earning a score of 87 — a clear and high-confidence upgrade cycle.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 0A — ROUTING COMPLETE

Year anchor — five row label mappings (mandatory, written before any table):

  • Sharescope "current H1/H2" → FY25 partial actuals (H1 = six months ended 31 Mar 2025; H2 = six months ended 30 Sep 2025)
  • Sharescope "1y ago" → FY24 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2024)
  • Sharescope "2y ago" → FY23 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2023)
  • Sharescope "3y ago" → FY22 actuals (year ended 30 Sep 2022)
  • Sharescope "FY1 fc" → FY26 consensus forecast (year ending 30 Sep 2026)
  • Sharescope "FY2 fc" → FY27 consensus forecast (year ending 30 Sep 2027)

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The FY25 results RNS explicitly states: "The year-on-year FX effects were minimal: on the average FY25 USD to GBP exchange rate of 1.30 vs average FY24 USD to GBP exchange rate of 1.27 the revenues decreased by less than 1% for the Group."

Constant currency is not explicitly disclosed as within 0.5pp of reported, but the disclosed FX impact is stated as less than 1% on revenues — confirming near-nil impact. North America was ~28% of FY25 revenue (£12.5m/£44.8m). USD exposure is the primary non-GBP currency but the company itself quantifies the impact as sub-1%. No Phase 0B penalty or badge applied — FX impact disclosed as immaterial by management. Reporting currency: GBP throughout.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

OMG · Q4 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 30/09/25

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting RNS as FY25 full year results. Market now expects H1 FY26 results or H1 guidance. Next year end 30/9/26 = FY26.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 2.6p · Revenue £49.1m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 2.9p · Revenue £53.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period (18 May 2025 → 2 Apr 2026): 2.7p → 2.6p, net change −0.1p (−3.7%). One downgrade step in late Feb 2026 (2.7p → 2.6p). Revenue moved 46.6m → 49.1m over same period — a material upward revision to revenue consensus (+5.4%), anchored around the Dec 2025 step-change (46.2m → 49.1m). Last-4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT (2.6p throughout). Revenue flat at £49.1m for 4 weeks. Mixed picture: revenue upgraded significantly, EPS ticked down slightly.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg — Revenue): 3yr avg H1% of FY = 49.4%. FY26e consensus £49.1m × 49.4% = £24.3m H1 revenue baseline. 3yr avg H1% of FY for EPS = 52.5% (Sharescope-supplied). FY26e EPS 2.6p × 52.5% = 1.37p H1 EPS baseline.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £20.1m · Adjusted basic EPS 0.12p (from RNS note 4; statutory basic EPS −0.63p from continuing operations)

    Note on EPS baseline: FY25 H1 adjusted basic EPS was 0.12p. The Sharescope "current H1" EPS of 0.1p is consistent with this. The company uses adjusted EBIT as primary metric but Sharescope tracks adjusted basic EPS. Used 0.12p as H1 FY25 actual throughout.

  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode — comparing implied FY26 H2 vs avg of last 3 historical H2s):
    • Revenue: FY26e £49.1m − H1 FY25 actual £20.1m = implied H2 £29.0m. Historical H2 actuals: FY24 H2 £17.9m, FY25 H2 £24.7m, FY23 H2 £23.0m (2y ago). Avg of last 3 = £21.9m. Implied H2 vs avg: +£7.1m, +32% above avg — flagged for Phase 3.3.
    • EPS: FY26e 2.6p − H1 FY25 0.12p = implied H2 2.48p. Historical H2 actuals: FY24 H2 0.4p (Sharescope 1y ago), FY25 H2 1.4p (current H2), FY23 H2 2.4p (2y ago). Avg of last 3 = 1.43p. Implied H2 vs avg: +1.05p, +73% above avg — significant flag.
  • FX: Immaterial — management-disclosed sub-1% revenue impact; no penalty applied.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP. Net cash (negative net borrowing): FY22 H2 −£7.2m / FY23 H2 −£9.9m / FY24 H2 −£10.6m / FY25 H2 −£0.9m → wait — cross-check required: RNS states FY25 net cash £37.3m (cash + FTDs). Sharescope "current H2" net borrowing = −£0.9m appears to be using a different net debt definition (likely excluding fixed-term deposits). Will use RNS-disclosed £37.3m as the authoritative balance sheet figure per workflow discipline. FY26e fc net borrowing Sharescope: −£33.7m / FY27e: −£34.6m (likely also including/excluding FTDs on same basis as current). ND/EBITDA: all negative (net cash throughout). Interest cover: negative (net cash position — finance income exceeds finance expense). Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — balance sheet not a constraint on estimates.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

OMG · Q4 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 30/09/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (audited preliminary results, FY ended 30 September 2025, released December 2025)

1. Revenue figures

FY25 Group revenue: £44.8m, up +8% vs FY24 £41.5m. vs FY26e consensus at time of results (Sharescope snapshot shows consensus moved to £49.1m in Dec 2025 — the step-change from £44.8m → £49.1m appears to reflect the post-results upgrade to include FY26 extended year to 31 Dec 2026, see accounting reference date change note below). FY25 actual vs the pre-results FY25 consensus: snapshot at 01 Nov 2025 shows £44.8m — exactly in line. The Oct 2025 trading update guided "broadly in line with market expectations" with stated consensus £46.2m. FY25 actual £44.8m is £1.4m (−3%) below the stated Oct 2025 consensus of £46.2m — a modest revenue miss vs that pre-announced benchmark. However this is flagged as the market had already reset to £44.8m in the Sharescope series by Nov 2025 snapshots, suggesting broker models had already moved.

"overall Group revenue is expected to be broadly in line with market expectations. The Group considers FY25 market consensus at the date of this announcement to be: Revenue £46.2m" (Oct 2025 trading update)

"Revenue £44.8m (FY24: £41.5m), up 8% on prior year" (FY25 preliminary results)

⚠️ Important structural note — accounting reference date change: The company announced on 16 December 2025 a change to 31 December accounting reference date. FY26 will be a 15-month period ending 31 December 2026. The Sharescope £49.1m FY1 fc almost certainly reflects this extended 15-month year. This is a critical distortion for all consensus comparisons — 15 months vs 12 months is not a like-for-like comparison. Flagged as a major structural issue for Phase 3 and Phase 4.

Motion Capture revenue: £32.0m (FY24: £38.6m), −17% YoY. Smart Manufacturing revenue: £12.8m (FY24: £2.9m), +341% YoY (includes Sempre and Amber Optix acquisitions; organic growth +38%).

"Motion Capture revenue was £32.0m (FY24: £38.6m), reflecting continued US academic and entertainment headwinds and post-COVID normalisation of opening order book to £1.0m (FY24: £11.5m)"

2. EPS / earnings figures

FY25 adjusted basic EPS: 1.55p (FY24 restated: 3.01p), −49% YoY. Statutory basic EPS: −0.55p (FY24: +0.58p).

FY25 adjusted EBIT: £2.2m (FY24: £1.7m), +29% YoY. PBT: £0.1m (FY24: £0.5m restated). Finance income fell significantly to £1.3m (FY24: £2.3m) due to lower cash balances post buybacks and acquisitions — this is the dominant driver of the EPS decline vs FY24.

vs FY26e consensus: Sharescope FY1 fc EPS = 2.6p. However this is for a 15-month FY26 — not comparable to the 1.55p FY25 (12-month). On a run-rate basis, FY25 annualised adjusted basic EPS of 1.55p suggests FY26 12-month equivalent would need significant EBIT growth to reach 2.6p even on a pro-rata 15/12 basis. This is the key tension.

"Adjusted Basic EPS 1.55p (FY24: 3.01p), −49%"

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate FY25: tax charge £766k on PBT of £85k — statutory rate wildly elevated by deferred tax movements. On adjusted PBT basis: adjusted PBT £2.7m (per note 6: adjusted EBIT £2.2m + finance income net £0.5m). Tax on adjusted basis: £766k charge / £2.7m adjusted PBT = effective rate ~28%. Normalised UK rate 25%. Deviation of ~3pp — at threshold. Restated adjusted EPS at 25%: adjusted PAT would be £2.7m × 75% = £2.025m / 124.4m shares = 1.63p vs reported 1.55p. Gap is modest (0.08p). No material EPS quality distortion — no 🚨 flag required, within normal range.

FY26e EPS bridge (construct here):

  • (1) New base EPS: FY25 adjusted basic EPS = 1.55p (12-month year, 124.4m weighted avg shares)
  • (2) 15-month year adjustment: FY26 is 15 months. Pro-rata uplift on 12-month run rate = ×15/12 = ×1.25. Mechanically, 1.55p × 1.25 = 1.94p purely from the extra quarter — before any growth.
  • (3) Inorganic annualisation delta: Sempre acquired Oct 2024 (contributed full H1 FY25 + full H2 FY25 = full FY25). Amber Optix acquired Apr 2025, small (£0.6m revenues). No major incomplete-year inorganic items — both fully annualised in FY25 base. Delta: +0.0p (fully baked in).
  • (4) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Smart Manufacturing organic growth guided as strong; Motion Capture facing US headwinds but APAC/EMEAI improving. FY26 EBITDA consensus £7.3m vs FY25 EBITDA (implied from RNS: adjusted EBIT £2.2m + D&A £4.7m = ~£6.9m). Implied EBITDA growth £0.4m. On 124m shares this is ~0.3p. However this is for 12 months — on 15-month basis add ~25% further = ~0.4p.
  • (5) Interest step-up: Net cash position, finance income declining (£1.7m received vs £1.3m income). Interest income will continue declining as cash depletes. Negative delta vs FY25 finance income: estimated −£0.3m vs FY25, −0.2p impact.
  • (6) Share buyback benefit: £8.3m spent buying 15.9m shares in FY25 at avg 52p. Share count reduced from ~131m to ~115m by end FY25, further reduction ongoing (£10m programme ~£8.6m deployed by Dec 2025 per RNS). Diluted count FY26 likely ~112m vs FY25 weighted avg 124.4m. This is a meaningful per-share tailwind: same PAT on fewer shares. Delta: ~+0.15p.

Implied FY26e EPS (15-month): 1.94p (base × 15/12) + 0.3p (EBITDA growth) − 0.2p (interest drag) + 0.15p (buyback) = ~2.2p. Sharescope FY1 fc is 2.6p. Gap of ~0.4p — suggests consensus may be pencilling in more EBIT growth or the interest drag is smaller than estimated. The 2.6p consensus could be achievable if Smart Manufacturing delivers a further step-change in EBIT. Revision direction: consensus broadly achievable but not obviously beatable on current trajectory. Referenced in Phase 4 — not restated there.

3. Order book / forward work

Motion Capture in-year order intake FY25: £34.8m, up +21% vs FY24 £28.8m. Opening FY26 order book: £1.0m (FY25 opening: £11.5m — now normalised post-COVID unwind).

"in-year order intake up 21% to £34.8m (FY24: £28.8m), demonstrating positive underlying demand"

Smart Manufacturing: good H2 visibility cited in interim results; "building orderbook and pipeline which continues beyond the current financial year" — qualitative only, no quantum stated for FY26.

AGM (25 Feb 2026) trading update: Vicon secured two large Entertainment orders totalling £2.7m from Eastern Europe and Japan, further China stage extensions, two Life Sciences contracts in India. US pipeline "similar to same period 12 months ago."

"Vicon secured two large Entertainment orders totalling £2.7 million from customers in Eastern Europe and Japan"

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Gross margin FY25: 64.7% (FY24: 66.5%), down 180bps — driven by Smart Manufacturing mix (lower margin than Motion Capture). Adjusted EBIT: £2.2m (FY24: £1.7m), +29%.

Adjusted EBIT by division: Motion Capture £2.3m (FY24 restated: £1.5m); Smart Manufacturing £1.6m (FY24: £0.0m breakeven). PLC unallocated: −£1.7m (FY24: +£0.3m — note prior year benefited from interest income being in unallocated, now restructured).

Finance income declining trajectory: FY23 £1.6m → FY24 £2.3m → FY25 £1.3m (or £1.7m cash received). Further decline expected in FY26 as cash depletes.

Cost discipline: annualised savings of ~£1.2m from FY24 restructure flowed through FY25. Operating cash generation before tax improved to £6.7m (FY24: £0.3m).

"operating cash inflows before tax improved to £6.7m (FY24: £0.3m), benefitting from a £4.9m improvement in working capital"

Gross margin headwind from Smart Manufacturing mix shift is structural and ongoing — as SM grows to a larger proportion of revenues, blended gross margin will continue to decline gradually.

5. Capital returns and per-share items

Dividend: FY25 final 3.25p (unchanged vs FY24 final 3.25p; FY24 prior year final was 2.75p). Proposed final dividend at AGM 25 Feb 2026. Cash impact ~£3.8m (113.1m shares × 3.25p). The drivers: lower gross margins (mix shift to Smart Manufacturing at 64.8% actual vs 66.6% assumed), higher D&A charges, and higher tax rate assumptions. This is a meaningful EPS cut that the Sharescope consensus series (which showed 2.7p → 2.6p) largely missed because it was masked by the 15-month year rebasing that happened simultaneously.

What this means for the workflow: The scorecard correctly flagged "EPS hold, 0 to −5%" as the FY26e revision direction — but the actual outcome was a −23% EPS revision at the FY25 results note itself. The workflow's caution about the 15-month year distortion was warranted, but the magnitude of the gross margin deterioration was underweighted. The Panmure December note explicitly flags: "lower gross margins to reflect the mix shift towards smart manufacturing" — the 64.8% FY25 actual vs the broker's 66.6% assumption is a 180bps miss that flowed directly into a large EPS cut. Calibration lesson: when gross margin is structurally declining due to mix shift (higher Smart Manufacturing as % of revenue), this should generate a stronger negative EPS revision signal than was scored. Had the 180bps gross margin miss been modelled explicitly, the Phase 4 revision estimate would have moved from "hold" to "modest cut".

2. Interest income — both brokers dramatically revised this line

Panmure's Dec 2025 model shows net interest income of only £0.5m for FY25A vs their prior model's £1.3m, and pencils in £0.5m for FY26e/FY27e. The RNS stated £1.3m finance income but £1.7m cash received — Panmure is using a lower run-rate assumption going forward as cash continues to deplete. Progressive's Feb 2026 model also shows fully adj PBT of only £0.7m for FY25 vs £3.7m in FY24. The workflow correctly identified this as the dominant EPS drag but the scorecard's "interest income depletion" flagging should carry more weight in the Phase 5 scoring — it is the single largest driver of the EPS collapse and Panmure explicitly modelled it at a permanently lower run-rate.

3. Score calibration — 43 vs broker reaction

Both brokers maintained Buy, 95p TP throughout. No TP cuts, no recommendation changes. Panmure did note "very depressed multiples" repeatedly and made downward forecast revisions at each print. The EPS cut at Dec results (2.3p → new FY26e) is a meaningful negative broker action — but the TP held because the valuation case rests on a medium-term margin recovery thesis (mid-teens EBIT margin target), not near-term EPS. Progressive maintained forecasts through the AGM.

The workflow's 43/100 — Neutral is well-calibrated against the actual broker output. There were no upgrades, no TP increases, one material EPS revision downward. The "hold and wait for strategy event" conclusion is correct — Panmure's Dec note explicitly says "The board will set out a new three-year framework in H1FY26" as the key catalyst, and both brokers are treading water until that event. Score 43 maps correctly to the observed broker behaviour.

4. Dividend — brokers diverge from each other interestingly

Panmure's Dec 2025 note shows DPS flat at 3.3p for FY26e and FY27e — they have abandoned the progressive dividend assumption from earlier notes (which showed 3.5p, 3.8p, 4.0p). Progressive's Feb 2026 note still shows DPS of 4.1p for FY26e — an aggressive assumption given the dividend coverage problem. The scorecard correctly flagged "dividend uncovered by EPS" as a scored negative. Panmure subsequently flat-lined the dividend assumption, confirming the capital allocation tension is real and brokers noticed it.

5. One genuine miss — the gross margin trajectory

The workflow scored Smart Manufacturing EBIT inflection as +10 points (the largest positive). This is directionally correct — SM EBIT did go from zero to £1.6m. However, the gross margin drag from SM mix was not scored as a separate negative. Panmure's October note explicitly flags "mix effects" as a reason for cutting FY26e EBIT from £3.59m to £3.00m, and the December note reduces gross margin from 66.6% to 66.0% for FY26e. A gross margin headwind row should have been included in the Phase 5 components table, likely −3 to −4 points. This would have offset part of the SM EBIT positive, netting the SM contribution closer to +6 to +7 rather than +10. Overall score direction unchanged, but the composition would be tighter.

6. 15-month year — brokers have not yet rebased

As of the Feb 2026 AGM note, Panmure explicitly states "We will update our forecasts to reflect this change in due course." Progressive does the same. This confirms the workflow's identification that the £49.1m FY26e consensus was not yet properly rebased for the 15-month year. The consensus is therefore still partially stale — the scorecard flagged this correctly and it remains unresolved.

Summary verdict on calibration

The 43/100 score and Neutral tone label are confirmed correct. The workflow underestimated the gross margin revision risk (should have generated a larger negative EPS revision signal, perhaps scoring the final result closer to 38–42 rather than 43). The dominant analytical insights — 15-month year distortion, interest income structural decline, hold-and-wait for strategy event, dividend coverage tension — were all confirmed by the broker notes. No recalibration of phase rules required, but a reminder to explicitly score gross margin headwinds from structural mix shifts as a separate component when a lower-margin division is growing as a percentage of group revenue.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

OMG · Q4 · Trading Update (H1 FY26) · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26 (actual 31/12/26)

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Trading update for 6 months ended 31 March 2026, with notice of H1 results on 17 June 2026)

1. Revenue figures

H1 FY26 revenue (6 months ended 31 March 2026): £20.7m (prior-year period: £20.1m), +3% YoY.

"The Group expects to report revenue for the period of £20.7m (prior-year period: £20.1m)."

vs FY26e 15-month consensus £49.1m — H1 £20.7m represents 42.2% of consensus vs the 3yr avg H1% of 49.4%. On 12-month equiv basis: H1 £20.7m / (£49.1m × 12/15) = 20.7/39.3 = 52.7% — above the 49.4% baseline. Positive on LFL basis.

Segment breakdown: Vicon (Motion Capture) delivered "pleasing revenue growth" vs prior year. IVMS (Smart Manufacturing) experienced "softer result in the first six months" due to order timing deferrals. Net +3%.

2. EPS / earnings figures

No H1 EPS disclosed. The RNS references "Adjusted LBIT" (loss before interest and tax) — i.e., the company is guiding to a loss at the LBIT level in H1 FY26. "Underlying margins remained robust, with continued cost discipline supporting a modestly improved Adjusted LBIT versus prior year period."

FY25 H1 adjusted EPS: 0.12p (from prior session). "Modestly improved Adjusted LBIT vs prior year" suggests H1 FY26 EPS may be near 0.12–0.2p range (H1 remains a loss-making period on LBIT basis with finance income contributing positively to EPS).

"Underlying margins remained robust, with continued cost discipline supporting a modestly improved Adjusted LBIT versus prior year period."*

FY26e EPS bridge (update from prior session):

  • (1) New base: FY25 adj EPS 1.55p (12 months to Sep 2025)
  • (2) 15-month uplift: ×15/12 base = 1.94p
  • (3) H1 contribution: H1 FY26 adj LBIT "modestly improved" vs H1 FY25. H1 FY25 adj EPS ~0.12p. H1 FY26 might deliver 0.15–0.20p.
  • (4) IVMS deferral headwind: Customer deferrals in H1 = short-term revenue delay, not cancellation. "These opportunities underpin delivery over the remainder of FY26." The deferred orders shift into the 9 months Jul 2026 – Dec 2026.
  • (5) Vicon pleasing growth + H1 MC revenue likely higher than prior year.
  • Net: EPS bridge broadly on track for 2.6p FY26 (15-month) consensus — IVMS deferrals shift revenue forward into H2 but don't change full-year. H1 cash position £31.7m confirms no deterioration.

3. Order book / forward work

Vicon: "several significant contract wins, including in Eastern Europe, Japan and India." Q2 wins confirmed from AGM statement now executing. "Encouraging demand across core industries in other territories."

IVMS: "solid underlying demand" but "heightened macroeconomic uncertainty has recently affected the timing of certain orders." "These opportunities underpin delivery over the remainder of FY26."

Net cash £31.7m confirmed.

"these opportunities underpin delivery over the remainder of FY26"

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

"Underlying margins remained robust" — no margin deterioration despite IVMS deferral. "Continued cost discipline" supporting improved LBIT. IVMS unified as IVMS Limited from 1 March 2026 — integration benefits to "build progressively through the rest of FY26 and beyond."

"The Board expects the efficiency and margin benefits of the new structure to build progressively through the rest of FY26 and beyond."

5. Capital returns and per-share items

Cash position: £31.7m as at 31 March 2026 (after share buybacks and dividend). Positive FCF implied. DPS FY26e: 3.30p. No changes mentioned.

6. Qualitative tone

CEO: "strong performance in Motion Capture" with international wins. IVMS: "important step in strengthening execution." "Whilst cognisant of evolving macroeconomic conditions, our growing pipeline and planned, targeted product launches give us confidence in further progress through FY26."

"Management expectations for FY26 remain unchanged."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: "Management expectations for FY26 remain unchanged." Qualitative, one year (15-month FY26). No numeric guidance change.

Forward language is guardedly positive: IVMS deferral is acknowledged but framed as timing not cancellation; Vicon pleasing growth; pipeline growing; product launches planned.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — unchanged guidance with positive Vicon commentary but IVMS timing slip acknowledged. Not Constructive because IVMS deferral reduces H1 momentum. Not Cautious because management says FY26 expectations unchanged and the deferrals are specifically framed as timing. Provisional points: +1 to +3.

Divergence check: H1 revenue +3% YoY (slight beat vs the −12% implied if 12-month run-rate interpretation used — actually +3% vs FY25 H1 is fine). Guidance unchanged despite IVMS slowdown = modest positive divergence (delivery ahead of cautious expectations). Flag: ⚠️ IVMS order timing slip acknowledged in H1 — management confidence in H2 recovery needs verification at full H1 results (17 June 2026).

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

OMG · Q4 · Trading Update (H1 FY26) · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26 (actual 31/12/26)

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table (carried from prior session — unchanged)

Revenue trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating (on LFL basis). On 12-month equiv: FY26 revenue is actually declining vs FY25.

EPS trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating (losses reducing; 12m equiv +35% vs FY25).

Acceleration flags — updated with today's H1 data:

  • Revenue: H1 FY26 £20.7m vs H1 FY25 £20.1m = +3% YoY. Prior year (FY25 full year) +8% revenue YoY. H1 FY26 +3% < FY25 +8% → no acceleration (RNS-derived; H1 decelerating).
  • EPS: H1 FY26 LBIT "modestly improved" vs H1 FY25 — directionally improving. Full year trajectory: FY26e +68% (but 15m distortion) → 12m adjusted +35%. Vs FY25 −48%: acceleration ✓ (consensus-derived, 12m adjusted).

3.1 HoH Growth Pattern (prior session table + H1 FY26 update)

Adding H1 FY26:

Note: FY26 H1 is 6 months (Oct 25 – Mar 26). FY26 "remaining" = 9 months (Apr 26 – Dec 26).

Revenue H1 FY26 +3% YoY (vs FY25 H1 £20.1m). 🟢 Steady H1 — below the FY25 H2 peak (+38%) but better than FY25 H1 (−14%). Recovery trajectory continuing.

Revenue trajectory (HoH YoY last 3): FY25 H1 −14%, FY25 H2 +38%, FY26 H1 +3%. 🟡 Volatile — swings remain significant.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Data source gate: H1 FY26 revenue of £20.7m disclosed in RNS. This qualifies as RNS condition (1) — exact figure. ✅ Revenue is TRACKABLE.

EPS: H1 FY26 EPS not disclosed (only LBIT guidance — no EPS figure). EPS: UNTRACKABLE.

Revenue tracking:

Critical decision — which baseline to use? The 3yr avg H1% of 49.4% applied to the 15-month FY26e £49.1m gives £24.3m. But the H1 period is only 6 months of a 15-month year. The appropriate comparison is H1 revenue vs the 12-month run-rate: £49.1m × 12/15 = £39.3m. Then: H1% baseline = 49.4% × £39.3m = £19.4m.

Using 12m-adjusted baseline:

  • H1 FY26 actual £20.7m ÷ FY26 12m equiv £39.3m = 52.7% vs 49.4% baseline
  • Deviation: +3.3pp above baseline → 🟢 STRONG BUY signal (≥+2.5pp threshold)

Using nominal 15-month baseline (mechanically):

  • H1 FY26 £20.7m ÷ FY26e £49.1m = 42.2% vs 49.4% → −7.2pp = SELL SIGNAL
  • But this is mechanically wrong — applying a 12-month H1% split to a 15-month FY inflates the baseline artificially.

The correct approach is the 12m-adjusted baseline: +3.3pp deviation → 🟢 STRONG BUY.

Buy trigger (12m adjusted): £19.4m × 1.015 = £19.7m. H1 actual £20.7m > £19.7m → 🟢 ✓ buy trigger fired.

H2 EPS burden: FY26e 2.6p − H1 implied EPS (~0.15–0.20p estimate) = ~2.40–2.45p required over remaining 9 months. H2 FY25 (6 months) = 1.4p — so the remaining 9 months must deliver ~2.4p vs 6 months 1.4p. On a run-rate basis: 1.4p per 6 months × 1.5 = 2.1p run rate; consensus needs 2.4p = requires step-up from IVMS recovery and Vicon momentum in H2.

3.3 Implied Remaining Period Momentum

Remaining 9 months = FY26e 15-month £49.1m − H1 actual £20.7m = £28.4m to be delivered Apr–Dec 2026.

vs prior comparable period: FY25 was a 12-month year. The Apr–Sep 2025 H2 was £24.7m. The remaining 9 months Oct–Dec 2026 adds an extra quarter. On 6-month equiv: the 9-month remaining at £28.4m implies ~£19.0m per 6 months — vs FY25 H2 £24.7m. This implies meaningful softness in the remaining 9 months vs FY25 H2.

However the comparison is distorted by the IVMS order timing — deferred H1 orders should crystallize in H2 (Apr–Sep 2026), boosting H2 revenue. The Oct–Dec 2026 quarter adds ~£7–9m incremental. Net: remaining 9 months £28.4m appears achievable given £24.7m FY25 H2 + an extra quarter.

Classification: 🟡 moderate — achievable if IVMS deferrals convert and Vicon maintains trajectory.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS: 2.7p → 2.6p, −3.7% over 11 months. Two small downgrade steps. Revenue: +5.4% (mechanically from 15-month year rebasing). 4-week: 🟡 FLAT. No upgrade cycle. Price: 100p → 51p = −49% decline. Consensus TP 88p.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

RNS confirms net cash £31.7m at 31 March 2026 (after buybacks + dividend). Sharescope fc: −£33.7m ≈ consistent. 🟢 Unlevered / net cash.

Forecast earnings check — Step 1: FY26e EPS 2.6p (15m) vs FY25 1.55p (12m) = +68% (distorted). 12m adjusted: ~2.1p vs 1.55p = +35% ✅. Revenue: £49.1m (15m) vs £44.8m (12m) = +10% (distorted). 12m adjusted: ~£39.3m vs £44.8m = −12% ⚠️ declining on LFL. ⚠️ FY26 revenue on 12m basis declining vs FY25 — noted.

Step 2: FY27e 2.9p vs FY26e 2.6p (12m adj 2.1p) = +38% on LFL basis ✅. Revenue FY27e £53.3m vs FY26e 12m adj £39.3m = +35% on LFL ⚠️ very high; suggests stale broker models.

3.6 Structural flags

[IVMS order timing risk]: "heightened macroeconomic uncertainty has recently affected the timing of certain orders and led some customers to defer project starts beyond this period end." This is a short-term timing issue, not a cancellation. But timing risk remains: if macro uncertainty persists into H2, IVMS could deliver a second deferral.

[Vicon international diversification]: Eastern Europe, Japan, India wins. Diversification away from US academic reducing US dependency — positive structural shift. US market "broadly unchanged" (neither better nor worse).

[IVMS integration benefits timed for H2+]: "efficiency and margin benefits of the new structure to build progressively through the rest of FY26 and beyond" — confirms that the integration is still in early stages; H2 FY26 and FY27 are the beneficiary periods, not H1.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

OMG · Q4 · Trading Update (H1 FY26) · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26 (actual 31/12/26)

#1 Driver — H1 FY26 revenue +3% YoY with Vicon strong + IVMS deferral disclosed: The +3% H1 revenue YoY is the primary number. Brokers will run this against their H1 models (which were likely based on the 12m equiv run-rate). On the 12m-adjusted basis, H1 £20.7m vs £19.4m expected = +6.7% above baseline — a genuine positive surprise. However, brokers will note the IVMS timing slip as an explicit headwind — some H1 IVMS revenue has been deferred to H2 (Apr–Dec 2026). The net FY26 impact should be zero (deferred not cancelled) but H2 execution risk increases.

#2 Driver — Management expectations FY26 "unchanged" + net cash £31.7m: Guidance unchanged provides a floor. Net cash £31.7m exceeds the Sharescope fc of −£33.7m by £2m (directionally consistent). Cash generation is positive — no balance sheet concerns. Brokers will note that guidance unchanged despite IVMS deferral = confident management signalling.

Forecast revisions:

  • Revenue FY26e: hold at £49.1m (15-month). H1 tracking fine on adjusted basis; IVMS deferrals to crystallize in H2. Direction: hold.
  • Revenue FY27e: hold at £53.3m — strategy event (17 June 2026) will be key.
  • EPS FY26e: hold at 2.6p (15m). "Modestly improved LBIT" = marginal positive. Finance income trajectory stabilizing (net cash £31.7m). Direction: hold to marginal +.
  • EPS FY27e: hold at 2.9p pending strategy event.

Target price and recommendation: TP 88p vs current 51p (73% upside). Both brokers (Panmure, Progressive) maintained Buy, 95p TP as of Feb 2026 per prior calibration. This H1 update is positive — Vicon winning, IVMS unified, guidance unchanged. Likely to maintain Buy and TP at ~90–95p. Current price 51p vs 88p consensus TP = deeply discounted.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Management expectations for FY26 remain unchanged" after an IVMS timing slip in H1 is exactly the "in line with Board's expectations" language used in prior sessions — this understates the Vicon positive. Modest upgrade cycle probability at H1 results (17 June 2026) if IVMS confirms order recovery.

Key risk: IVMS customer deferrals persisting into H2 (macro uncertainty). US academic market shows no improvement ("broadly unchanged"). Finance income continuing to decline as cash depletes. 15-month year consensus still not fully calibrated by all brokers.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold. Tone: Neutral or Constructive. H1 revenue positive (+3.3pp above adjusted baseline) pushes to Constructive. → 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely (slight upgrade vs prior-session Neutral given first actual H1 data confirms Vicon growth and guidance survival).

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

OMG · Q4 · Trading Update (H1 FY26) · FY26 · Year end: 30/09/26 (actual 31/12/26)

50/100 · Confidence: 44–56 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

ComponentPts
🟢 H1 Revenue £20.7m (+3% YoY) — +3.3pp above 12m-adjusted baseline; buy trigger fired+10
🟢 Vicon international wins (E. Europe, Japan, India) — diversification reducing US dependency+7
🟢 Guidance FY26 "unchanged" despite IVMS H1 timing slip — management confidence+6
🟢 IVMS unified (IVMS Ltd from 1 Mar 2026) — integration benefits building; not cancelled, timing only+5
🟢 Net cash £31.7m (RNS-confirmed) — no balance sheet constraint; buybacks + dividend still funded+4
🟡 EPS untrackable (no H1 EPS figure — LBIT only)−2
🟡 In-line outlook — qualitative only; no numeric FY guidance upgrade−2
🔴 IVMS H1 deferral: macro uncertainty causing customer project delays — H2 execution risk elevated−6
🔴 H1 revenue +3% YoY decelerates from FY25 H2 +38%; underlying recovery pace modest−4
🔴 EPS flat trend (−3.7% net over 11 months); no upgrade cycle initiated; 15m year still unrebased−4
🔴 US academic market "broadly unchanged" — no catalyst for Vicon US recovery−4

Raw total: 50. No FX adjustment. Final score: 50/100.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: H1 FY26 revenue came in at £20.7m (+3% YoY vs £20.1m prior period) — the first hard data point for the 15-month FY26 year. On a 12-month adjusted basis (using FY26e 15-month £49.1m deflated to £39.3m 12m equiv), H1 £20.7m represents 52.7% of the adjusted run-rate vs the 49.4% seasonal baseline — a +3.3pp positive deviation, firing the strong buy trigger. The headline catalyst is Vicon delivering pleasing growth with international contract wins in Eastern Europe, Japan and India, demonstrating the US diversification strategy is gaining traction. Motion Capture is the growth engine; the drag is IVMS where "heightened macroeconomic uncertainty" caused specific customer project deferrals into the remainder of FY26.

Para 2 — H1 tracking signal and upgrade resilience: The H1 revenue tracking signal fires +3.3pp above the 12m-adjusted baseline — a 🟢 STRONG BUY on revenue. EPS is UNTRACKABLE (LBIT referenced but no EPS figure). The IVMS deferral is a genuine H2 execution risk: orders confirmed as existing but with shifted timing. If macro uncertainty persists (geopolitical/US policy), a second deferral is possible. The £31.7m net cash (RNS-confirmed) provides a financial buffer and confirms no earnings quality concerns — the company is generating positive FCF after buybacks and dividends. The H2 burden for the remaining 9 months (Apr–Dec 2026) is £28.4m revenue — achievable on prior run-rates but dependent on IVMS order conversion and Vicon maintaining momentum.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely held at 2.6p (15m) — "modestly improved LBIT" and guidance unchanged give no basis for a revision either way. Revenue consensus £49.1m also held. TP consensus of 88p (vs current 51p — 73% upside) likely maintained by Panmure and Progressive at their ~90–95p levels. The key catalyst remains the H1 results and strategy event on 17 June 2026, where a three-year framework will be set out. That event, not this trading update, is the upgrade inflection point.

🏁 Verdict: first H1 FY26 data confirms Vicon growth on track and guidance intact; buy trigger fired on 12m-adjusted revenue basis; IVMS deferral creates H2 execution risk but is timing not structural; score 50 — constructive, modest upgrades likely, watch 17 June strategy event as the genuine catalyst.

FY24 saw a large anomaly (H2 Rev collapsed from £91m to £39m — likely restructuring/refocusing period). Recovery in FY25 (+6.3%) and FY26 (+1.7%). FY27 consensus (+14.1%) assumes a meaningful acceleration — this is now at risk. Classified as STRONG. However, this assumption is now fundamentally challenged by guidance suspension and geopolitical headwinds. If H2 demand to Mediterranean/Turkey destinations remains depressed, the implied H2 growth collapses — bear case H2 EPS could be flat to prior year (14.7p), implying FY27 EPS of only ~17–18p vs 21.6p consensus. Forecast momentum divergence: Price has fallen from 317p (May 25) to 188p (Mar 26, −40.7%) while EPS was revised up +15.5%. analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text:
1. Dominant line items: #1 Driver: Guidance suspension. The withdrawal of explicit £39m–£43m Adj. PBT guidance removes the anchor for broker models. Every house must now rebuild from scratch using geopolitical scenario analysis — a fundamentally higher-uncertainty exercise. This alone dominates the note tone. #2 Driver: Volume momentum vs destination exposure conflict. Bookings +10%, Q2 +34% are genuine and strong. But Turkey, Greece, Cyprus, Egypt are OTB's core beach corridors. Brokers must model demand elasticity and substitution (City/Cruise offsets) vs core destination demand destruction. 2. Forecast revision direction & magnitude: FY1 Revenue: Down 5–10%. Middle East conflict disrupts core Mediterranean summer demand. Estimate range: £124–131m. FY1 EPS: Down 10–20%. Consensus 21.6p → estimated 15–18p in near-term broker revisions. Bear case could see 13–15p if H2 summer demand recovery fails to materialise. FY2 Revenue: Hold / modest cut −3–5%. Market likely assumes conflict resolution or demand normalisation by FY28. FY2 EPS: Hold / modest cut −5%. 25.4p → ~24p range. Medium-term targets of 38.7p EPS remain the long-run anchor. 3. Target price & recommendation: Brokers will cut TPs materially. Consensus 308p likely moves to 220–260p range (−15 to −29%). Price is already at 188p — significant discount to even cut TPs. Most brokers likely maintain Buy/Add with a recovery narrative. No downgrades to Hold/Sell expected from house brokers (Cavendish, Peel Hunt likely). 4. Conservative guidance read-through: The opposite of a "not less than" comfort signal. Guidance suspension is unambiguously negative. The word "temporarily" is management's attempt to soften the signal but brokers will not treat this as a buying flag. The medium-term targets reiteration (38.7p, £85m PBT) shows confidence in the structural story but provides zero FY1 earnings visibility. 5. Key risk / offsetting factor: The single most important counter-argument is the asset-light balance sheet: OTB carries no committed inventory (unlike TUI, Jet2), meaning it can flex capacity without stranded costs. Cash generation continues through the conflict period. This limits the downside scenario significantly — it is not an existential risk, but it is a meaningful FY1 earnings risk.

6. Overall broker note tone forecast: ⚠ CAUTIOUS / DOWNGRADES PROBABLE — The first 1–3 broker notes (expected within 24–48 hours of the RNS) will cut FY1 EPS and revenue estimates materially, lower target prices, but likely maintain Buy recommendations citing the structural story, medium-term targets, and asset-light resilience. Tone will be: "near-term uncertainty elevated; long-term thesis intact; risk/reward improves at current levels but new information needed before upgrading." The H1 results on 12 May 2026 become the critical next catalyst.

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: Final Score: 29 / 100 Confidence range: 22–36 (wide — binary geopolitical resolution timeline) Verdict: GUIDANCE SUSPENDED · CUTS LIKELY Score components: Base (pre-H1 AGM, neutral start): +50 Guidance suspension (explicit negative, forces broker rebuild): −15 Geopolitical binary risk (unknown duration/magnitude, core destinations affected): −10 Forecast momentum (FLAT 13wks, price -40.7% vs EPS: market already pricing concern): −4 Volume momentum (bookings +10%, Q2 +34% — genuine positive): +6 Asset-light structural resilience (limits downside, cash positive): +2 New verticals / medium-term targets reiterated: +2 Later booking mix (more pronounced FY26, increases H2 burden): −2 FX adjustment: nil ───────────────────────────────────── Final: 29 The score of 29 reflects a clear near-term negative catalyst (guidance suspension into geopolitical uncertainty) which will force broker EPS cuts of 10–20% on FY1. It does not go lower because (a) the asset-light model genuinely limits downside vs peers, (b) volume momentum is real and strong, (c) medium-term targets provide recovery anchor, and (d) the market has already de-rated the stock substantially. The wide confidence range (22–36) reflects that geopolitical resolution could quickly move this to 40+ with unchanged numbers, or could push it lower if the conflict extends through summer. Watch: H1 results 12 May 2026. Key thresholds — H1 Rev >£71.97m (mild buy signal); H1 EPS >3.09p (mild buy signal). These will be the first hard data points to assess whether the geopolitical headwind has been absorbed or has materially impaired H1 performance.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

PAGE · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (Q4). Incoming RNS = Q1 2026 trading update. Market expects H1 results (due around July 2026).
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e, pre-RNS): EPS 6.7p · Revenue £1,515.8m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e, pre-RNS): EPS 12.0p · Revenue £1,606.4m
  • Forecast broker momentum: Net +28.8% over full period BUT direction is sharply negative over the medium term: peak EPS was 5.2p (May 2025), then series of cuts to 3.6p (Feb 2026), before a sharp jump to 6.9p (28 Mar 2026) then 6.7p (Apr 2026). The Mar-Apr 2026 step-up from 3.6p → 6.9p (+91.7% in one week) is extraordinary — almost certainly reflects FY25 results publication and subsequent roll-forward to FY26e consensus (with FY25 actual EPS 2.9p and FY26e 6.7p). Revenue: 1,524m → consistent decline to ~1,515m (−0.6% overall). 4-week EPS trend: 🟢 RISING (3.6p → 6.7p = post FY25 results roll-forward; but the latest 2 weeks show 6.9p → 6.7p minor trim). Note: the "RISING" 4-week trend label is mechanically correct but reflects a roll-forward calendar event, not a fundamental upgrade signal.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg, FY23–FY25): Revenue 50.7% of FY = £768.5m (50.7% × £1,515.8m). EPS 57.8% of FY = 3.9p (57.8% × 6.7p). ⚠️ EPS 3yr avg H1% includes the abnormal FY25 H1 (0.0p of 2.9p = 0%). Mathematically: FY23 H1% = 25.5/(25.5+18.0) = 58.6%; FY24 H1% = 13.6/24.3 = 56.0%; FY25 H1% = 0.0/2.9 = 0.0%. 3yr avg = (58.6+56.0+0.0)/3 = 38.2%. Sharescope shows 57.8% — this appears to use a 2yr avg excluding FY25, or uses a different formulation. Use 57.8% from Sharescope as provided but flag the distortion from FY25 anomaly. More reliable baseline for Q1 signal: prior year H1 actuals.
  • Prior-year Q1 actuals (FY25 Q1 gross profit): RNS discloses Q1 2025 gross profit £194.5m (comparable period). Q1 2026 gross profit £187.0m = −3.9% YoY in reported terms; −4.9% in constant currency.
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue FY26e £1,515.8m − FY25 H1 £798.4m = implied H2 £717.4m vs FY25 H2 £798.2m = −10.1% (consensus-derived). EPS: 6.7p − FY25 H1 0.0p (or near zero) = H2 required ~6.7p vs FY25 H2 2.9p = +131% (consensus-derived — entire FY26e EPS loaded into H2 given implied near-zero H1 EPS). ⚠️ These are dramatically affected by the trough H1 FY25. More informative: implied FY26 H2 gross profit trajectory vs Q1 data will be assessed in Phase 3.
  • FX: RNS states: "Foreign exchange movements had a positive impact on the Group's results in Q1, increasing our Q1 reported gross profit by 1.0 percentage point, or £2.0m." On Q1 gross profit of £187.0m reported, FX added £2.0m (contributing +1.0pp). Constant currency Q1 = −4.9%. The FX impact is positive (£ weakened vs key currencies — net tailwind). Reported GP £187.0m includes £2.0m FX tailwind. Exposure: broadly diversified global operations. No single non-GBP currency >30% of revenue. Phase 0B not triggered.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY23 H2 £13.0m / FY24 H2 £15.1m / FY25 H1 £53.3m / FY25 H2 −£31.2m (FY25 YE, net cash — including bonus payments timing) / FY26 Q1 ~£7m net debt (RNS: "net debt of c. £7m") / FY26fc £67.7m net debt / FY27fc £83.8m net debt · ND/EBITDA: current 1.30x / FY26fc 0.70x / FY27fc 0.70x · Interest cover FY26fc: 7.0x · ND/FCF: 2.5x · Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — net debt £7m at Q1 (seasonal: Q1 bonus payments explains swing from FY25 YE net cash £31.2m to Q1 net debt £7m, RNS confirms "in line with expectations due to usual Q1 outflows for quarterly and annual bonuses"). FY26fc £67.7m net debt reflects annual dividend payments and continued operating performance. Interest cover 7.0x comfortable. Silent in Phase 5.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

PAGE · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 Trading Update)

1. Revenue / gross profit figures PAGE reports gross profit (fees) as the primary trading metric. Q1 2026 gross profit: £187.0m (Q1 2025: £194.5m). Reported: −3.9%. Constant currency: −4.9%.

Company compiled H1 consensus proxy (from revenue consensus): FY26e revenue £1,515.8m; H1 implied at 50.7% = £768.5m → Q1 implied at ~50% of H1 = ~£384m. But PAGE reports gross profit as primary metric. Pre-RNS gross profit consensus figure not available from Sharescope. Using the narrative: brokers had modelled approximately flat to mildly declining Q1 given Q4 2025 run-rate. Q1 2026 at −4.9% constant currency is broadly in line with Q4 2025 trend (no acceleration of deterioration).

"Group gross profit of £187.0m, -4.9% vs. 2025 [constant currency]"

2. EPS / earnings figures No EPS disclosed. Trading update — gross profit only. FY26e EPS consensus 6.7p maintained by market (no change in last 4 weeks per Sharescope — 6.7p since early April 2026).

3. FY26e EPS bridge (FY2 = FY27) (1) Base: FY26e adjusted EPS consensus 6.7p — reflects severe trough year given continued market weakness (2) FY27e 12.0p = +79.1% step-up from FY26e 6.7p — this is a cyclical recovery assumption; structural step-ups from normalization of markets in EMEA/UK as rates fall and confidence returns (3) No acquisitions. No significant inorganic delta. (4) Interest: FY26fc ND/EBITDA 0.70x — modest net debt; no meaningful interest cost pressure. Interest cover 7.0x. The bridge from 6.7p → 12.0p is essentially a market normalization assumption: fee earner headcount stability + improved conversion rates + some LFL gross profit growth across recovering geographies. The Americas/Asia Pacific growth (+1.1% and +9.3% in Q1) provides evidence the recovery is geographically underway; EMEA/UK weakness is the swing factor.

4. Order book / forward work No order book. Q1 indicators: Americas and Asia Pacific growing for 6th and 4th consecutive quarters respectively. UK declining 11.4%. EMEA declining 9.2%. Fee earner headcount: net +26 (+0.5%) in Q1. Productivity (GP per fee earner) +2% vs Q1 2025.

"Continued growth in Americas and Asia Pacific; UK and Europe remain challenging."

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals No margin guidance. Fee earner headcount management: reductions in EMEA (−51) and UK (−29), additions in Asia Pacific (+58) and Americas (+48). Non-operations headcount −45 (−2.4%). Active cost base management. No cost reduction targets or quantum disclosed.

Middle East conflict creating "heightened degree of uncertainty in the outlook for the rest of the year." The 70 people in the Middle East have seen GP decline 12% with "client and candidate confidence having deteriorated further."

6. Capital returns / per-share items Net debt £7m at Q1 (in line with expectations). FY26e DPS: 9.90p (consensus). FY27e DPS: 10.20p. No dividend change signalled. Share count: 328.6m total, 310.7m effective (excl. EBT-held shares).

7. Qualitative tone "Middle East conflict driving an increasingly uncertain outlook for the rest of the year." Continued growth in Americas and Asia Pacific. UK and EMEA remain tough. No quantified guidance for H1 or FY26. No "in line with expectations" statement for full year.

"Whilst we have seen signs of a normalisation in trading in some of our markets, the increased geopolitical and macro-economic risks due to the conflict in the Middle East create a heightened degree of uncertainty in the outlook for the rest of the year."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "The increased geopolitical and macro-economic risks due to the conflict in the Middle East create a heightened degree of uncertainty in the outlook for the rest of the year."

  • "We remain confident in the execution of our strategy" — qualitative only
  • No numeric guidance for FY26. No "in line" statement.
  • Guidance nature: qualitative only — uncertainty language for FY26; no revenue, EPS, or OP guidance
  • Year coverage: Remainder of FY26 (rest of year)
  • Classification: 🔴 Cautious — explicit "heightened degree of uncertainty" language for the remainder of FY26. No numeric guidance downgrade but the absence of any positive guidance combined with geopolitical escalation flagging and continued EMEA/UK weakness constitutes a cautious tone. Provisional points: −5 to −8
  • Divergence check: Q1 gross profit −4.9% constant currency represents a continuation of the FY25 trough, not an acceleration of decline. There is no current-year beat — performance is broadly in-line with Q4 2025 run rate. Cautious outlook is consistent with the current-year trajectory. No divergence.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: The full-period +28.8% reflects entirely the roll-forward from FY25 actuals 2.9p to FY26e 6.7p (calendar year change), not organic upgrades. Looking at the within-period trend: 5.2p (May 2025) → consistent cuts to 3.6p (Feb 2026) = −30.8% decline. Then roll-forward event: 3.6p → 6.9p → 6.7p. The organic within-FY25 trend was deeply negative; FY26e is a fresh consensus, not upgraded.
  • 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (mechanically — post roll-forward from FY25 results publication; 3.6p → 6.7p). This is a calendar event, not a genuine upgrade signal.
  • Revenue trend: Consistent slow decline from £1,524m to £1,515.8m (−0.5%) over the full period — marginal, reflecting minimal new information.
  • Divergence: Price has fallen from 356p (May 2025) to 135.4p — a −62% decline as EPS was cut from 5.2p to 3.6p. The ratio of price decline to EPS cut is dramatic, suggesting the market is pricing in extended market weakness or multiple compression. Current consensus TP 242p (from £356p peak) reflects the broker adjustment but is still 78.7% above current price — an unusually large TP/price gap for a FTSE 250 company.
