6. Structural / One-off Flags

Middle East escalation — structural uncertainty flag: The escalation of Middle East conflict is a new risk specifically cited as causing "heightened degree of uncertainty for the rest of the year." With 70 people in the Middle East and GP declining 12% there, and with oil-sensitive clients reducing hiring (energy sector slowdown potential), this is not a minor caveat. The CEO's language — "increasingly uncertain outlook for the rest of the year" — is stronger than typical boilerplate.

"The Middle East conflict driving an increasingly uncertain outlook for the rest of the year."

Americas and Asia Pacific structural positives: US GP growing for 6th consecutive quarter; Asia Pacific for 4th consecutive quarter. These represent 35% of Group GP and are genuine fundamental positives, not cyclical bounces. If EMEA/UK normalises even modestly, the recovery in EPS could be rapid given operating leverage.

Productivity resilience: GP per fee earner +2% vs Q1 2025 despite overall decline — this means the quality of the remaining workforce is high; when volume recovers, EPS will leverage sharply (as the FY26→FY27 EPS forecast implies).

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

PAGE · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 Driver — Q1 gross profit −4.9% constant currency: broadly in-line with Q4 run-rate, no acceleration of decline: The critical read for brokers is whether Q1 is better or worse than Q4 2025. Q4 2025 GP was −3.7% constant currency (implied from annual performance). Q1 2026 at −4.9% represents a mild deterioration vs Q4 — not a dramatic worsening, but also not the recovery inflection brokers need to see. Combined with the explicit Middle East uncertainty language, this is a hold at best.

#2 Driver — Middle East escalation language: new guidance qualifier introducing downside risk: The explicit "heightened degree of uncertainty for the rest of the year" due to the Middle East conflict is new compared to previous updates. This is not routine boilerplate — the CEO is specifically noting an escalating risk not present to this degree in prior quarters. The 12% GP decline in the Middle East (~£2–3m GP impact) is manageable in isolation, but the read-through to broader EMEA hiring sentiment and oil-sector activity is the broker concern.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e GP/Revenue: hold to minor cut — Q1 at −4.9% constant currency against an implied broker expectation of c.−3 to −5% suggests broadly in line. However, Middle East worsening and EMEA stubbornness may prompt 1–2 brokers to trim H2 assumptions. Range: −1% to −3% on FY26e revenue.
  • FY26e EPS: hold to minor cut — if revenue consensus is cut 1–2%, operating leverage magnifies this to a larger EPS cut. With EPS at 6.7p and cost structure finely tuned, a 2% GP miss could cut EPS by 10–15% (operating leverage in staffing). Range: −5% to −10% on FY26e EPS (6.7p → 6.0–6.4p).
  • FY27e: hold — no new structural information to change recovery thesis. FY27e 12.0p depends on EMEA/UK normalization which remains speculative. Minor downward drift possible if Middle East persists. Range: 0% to −5%.
  • Target prices: hold to minor cut — consensus TP 242p vs current 135.4p (78.7% implied upside). Post-update, TPs may be trimmed modestly (−5 to −10%, 242p → 217–230p) to reflect the Middle East risk and extended EMEA weakness. The large TP/price gap means any cut is absorbed into the structural discount without changing the long-term case.

Conservative guidance read-through: There is no "in line with expectations" or "comfortable with" language in this update. The absence of any FY guidance (combined with explicit uncertainty language) is a mild negative signal — brokers typically require either a confirmation or a warning; the absence of confirmation is directionally negative.

Key risk: The single largest risk is an escalation of the Middle East conflict into a broader regional disruption affecting oil prices, multinational capex budgets, and EMEA hiring confidence. The RNS explicitly raises this as a current concern. If EMEA deterioration accelerates beyond the current −9.2% rate, the FY26e trough may prove too optimistic. France at −14% is a particular concern — France is the Group's second-largest market.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: PAGE's Q1 2026 trading update shows gross profit of £187.0m — down 4.9% constant currency vs Q1 2025 £194.5m. This is broadly in line with the Q4 2025 run-rate of approximately −3.7% constant currency, representing no material acceleration of decline but also no inflection. The key watch point is Q2 results on 13 July 2026: if EMEA decline rate stabilises or improves vs Q1's −9.2%, and if the Middle East escalation is contained, the recovery thesis accelerates; if EMEA deteriorates further or France falls >14%, a formal EPS downgrade cycle recommences. 🏁 Cautious: Q1 in-line but with worsening qualitative signals on Middle East and no FY guidance anchor — brokers will trim modestly; structural recovery narrative intact but deferred.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results for year ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Facilisgroup revenues are USD-denominated (~£17.2m / £124.7m total = 13.8% of Group revenue). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues. Brand Addition invoices in multiple currencies with no single currency exceeding 30%. No FX Rule 1 penalty applies.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 3.8p, Revenue £126.5m. FY2 consensus: EPS 4.5p, Revenue £131.8m.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over snapshot period = 0.0% (completely static at 3.8p throughout ~10 months). Revenue drifted from £128.8m to £126.5m (−1.8%). Zero upgrades in EPS. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Momentum classification: dormant — the RNS is the first new information in nearly a year.
  • 3-year average H1 % of FY: Revenue H1 avg = 48.2%; EPS H1 avg = 39.9%.
  • H1 actuals (from Sharescope): H1 Revenue = £58.6m; H1 EPS = 1.2p. Implied H2 actual = £66.1m revenue (+2.5% vs prior H2 £64.5m); 2.66p EPS (−1.5% vs prior H2 2.7p).
  • FY results vs consensus: Adj EPS 3.86p vs 3.8p cns (+1.6% beat). Revenue £124.7m vs £126.5m cns (−1.4% miss). EBITDA £15.8m = exactly in line with cns £15.8m.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Group revenue: £124.7m (FY24: £125.3m) = −0.5% YoY, and −1.4% vs cns £126.5m.
    "Group revenue of £124.7m (FY 24: £125.3m) was in line with the prior year."
  2. Adjusted EPS: 3.86p (FY24: 4.63p) = −16.6% YoY, but +1.6% vs cns 3.8p.
    "Basic adjusted earnings per share was 3.86 pence per share (FY 24: 4.63 pence per share), a decrease of 0.77 pence per share."
  3. Adj EBITDA: £15.8m (FY24: £16.7m) = exactly in line with cns £15.8m. The planned investment in Facilisgroup sales/marketing (~$1m incremental) absorbed as guided.
    "Group Adjusted EBITDA was £15.8m (FY 24: £16.7m), reflecting the signalled investment to accelerate new Partner acquisition at Facilisgroup."
  4. Facilisgroup Partner wins: 30 new Partners in FY25 vs 16 in FY24. Total: 253 Partners (FY24: 239). Underlying retention 97% (FY24: 96%). Average LTV ~$0.5m per new Partner.
    "Secured 30 new Partners during the year (FY 24: 16), following an incremental investment of approximately $1m in sales and marketing."
  5. Facilisgroup ARR flat in USD: ARR $21.6m both FY24 and FY25. GBP decline due to FX only. Revenue recognition lag — Partner subscription build lagged churn impact in FY25. FY26 to benefit from in-year cohort.
    "ARR from Partner subscriptions was flat in the year reflecting reduced Partner numbers entering FY25. The in-year build of subscriptions from new Partner acquisition lagged the impact of Partner churn."
  6. Brand Addition margin improvement: EBITDA margin 10.6% (FY24: 10.0%). Gross margin 37.0% (FY24: 35.2%). EBITDA £11.4m (FY24: £10.8m). Revenue flat at £107.5m. New client wins £6.5m (FY24: £5.3m).
    "Adjusted EBITDA returns increased to 10.6% (FY 24: 10.0%) and gross margin increased to 37.0% (FY 24: 35.2%)."
  7. Free cash flow conversion: 91% (FY24: 68%). Operating cash flow £7.5m. Reduced capex (£4.9m vs £6.8m) driving improvement.
    "Free cash flow conversion increased to 91% (FY 24: 68%), reflecting reduced capital expenditure and demonstrating the inherent cash-generative characteristics of the business."
  8. Capital returns: £11.7m in FY25 (FY24: £3.4m) via £3.0m dividend, £2.2m market buybacks, £6.5m tender offer. New £5.0m share buyback commencing today.
    "Capital returns to shareholders totalled £11.7m in FY 25 (FY 24: £3.4m)... Today we announce our intention to commence a share buyback for consideration of up to £5.0m."
  9. Dividend: Final 2.0p per share (FY24: 1.85p), +8.1%. Payable 11 May 2026.
    "The Board is pleased to propose the payment of a final dividend of 2.0 pence per share for FY 25 (FY 24: 1.85 pence per share)."
  10. FY26 outlook: Facilisgroup expected revenue growth from accelerating Partner cohort; Brand Addition seeking revenue growth with maintained margin improvement above 10%.
    "At Facilisgroup, we are becoming increasingly confident in the high Partner lifetime value and the ability to convert new Partners at a healthy acquisition cost which underpins expected revenue growth... PEN — PHASE 0

Phase 0A — Routing

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue breakdown: UK & Europe £7.1m (73%), North America £3.4m, Asia Pacific £2.5m. No single non-GBP currency >30% — USD/CAD revenues are North America focused but constitute only ~27% of total. Below threshold. Phase 0B: skip, no penalty.

Note: North America was £3.4m of £9.7m = 35% — this is above 30% but the functional currency risk here relates to CAD primarily (Canadian defence) and USD. Checking: North America Rev £3.4m = 35%. USD/CAD exposure. However, ME Group precedent was EUR/JPY — for PEN, USD/CAD on revenues:

  • USD: North America revenues mixed CAD/USD. CAD dominates given Canadian DND contracts.
  • CAD <30% plausible given US operations also included. Given ambiguity and small absolute scale, and that the company's reporting currency is GBP with overseas revenue modest in absolute terms (~£3.4m), applying conservative judgment: insufficient information to confirm >30% single-currency — skip, no penalty, flag.

PEN — PHASE 1

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 Dec 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS −2.8p · Revenue £10.0m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 0.0p · Revenue £13.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net −2900% over full period (0.1p → −2.8p). Revenue cut from £12.3m to £10.0m (−18.7%). TP cut from 61p to 40p (−34.4%). Multiple downgrades. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at −2.8p/£10m/40p since mid-Feb 26).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.1% × £10.0m = £5.0m · EPS n/a (all negative; cannot construct meaningful EPS % of FY baseline)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (Sharescope current H1): Revenue £4.5m · EPS −5.1p
  • Implied H2 YoY: FY25 actual £9.7m vs FY24 £13.8m = −29.6% (severe). FY25 consensus was £10.0m — actual £9.7m = −3.0% miss.
  • FX: N/A

PEN — PHASE 2

RNS type: FY Results — year ended 31 December 2025

  1. Revenue: £9.662m vs FY1 consensus £10.0m = −3.4% miss vs consensus. vs FY24 £13.775m = −29.9% YoY. Software & Services £7.645m (−20.1%), Training Systems £2.017m (−52.1%). Apache contract in FY24 (£3.5m) not repeated. "Group revenue of £9.7m represents a 30% year over year reduction (2024: £13.8m)"
  2. EPS / losses: Adjusted loss before tax −£1.9m vs consensus −£1.8m = slightly worse. Statutory loss before tax −£2.5m. Adjusted EBITDA −£0.4m (FY24: +£1.7m). Adj loss per share −£1.9m / 44.5m shares ≈ −4.3p adjusted vs consensus −2.8p = worse than expected. Note: going concern material uncertainty flagged by auditors. "Adjusted EBITDA loss of £0.4 million (2024: £1.7 million profit)"
  3. Order book: Three-year order book £23.3m (FY24: £15.9m) — +46.5% YoY improvement. Of which £9.7m scheduled for FY26. Order intake £18m in FY25. Post-period: Training Systems order book £10.3m (vs £nil at FY24). "Order intake of £18 million substantially strengthened the Group's contracted three-year order book of £23.3 million (2024: £15.9 million)"
  4. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 49% (FY24: 50%) — held well despite −30% revenue decline. Admin costs reduced to £6.6m adjusted (FY24: £7.0m) from restructuring savings. ARR software £2.4m (FY24: £1.9m) = +26.3% — best ever. 60% of revenues now recurring. "Gross margin levels remain strong at 49% (2024: 50%)"
  5. Capital / cash / going concern: Net debt £0.5m (FY24: £2.3m) — improved via property sales (£3.2m gross proceeds). Shareholder loan £0.3m outstanding (due April 2026 — post-period). Equity raise £0.9m (Oct 2025). HSBC facility renewed post-period at £1m. Going concern material uncertainty disclosed — dependent on new business conversion timing. "The Directors have concluded that there are scenarios whereby the levels of forecast new business converted...represents a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt upon the company's ability to continue as a going concern."
  6. Qualitative tone / FY26 guidance: Return to break-even adjusted PBT in FY26 guided. ARR to exceed £3.0m by end FY26. £23.3m order book gives FY26 revenue confidence. Siemens Digital Industries OEM partnership signed. Sales reps appointed South Korea, Japan, India. "we anticipate a return to a break‑even adjusted PBT in FY26"

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-FY mode — FY actuals available)

Revenue: £9.662m vs consensus £10.0m = −3.4% miss. Order book expansion to £23.3m is the positive counter: £9.7m in FY26 pipeline = essentially the entire FY26 consensus revenue already contracted.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

FY25 revenue £9.7m vs FY24 £13.8m = −29.7% → 🔴 severe (<−15%)

H2 FY25 £5.2m vs H2 FY24 £6.4m = −18.8% → 🔴 severe

However, the order book lens is critical: FY26 has £9.7m already in contracted book — which implies consensus revenue of £13.0m requires only ~£3.3m of new wins in the year. Achievable if pipeline converts.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: From +0.1p (Jun 25) to −2.8p (current) — a ~2900% deterioration. Revenue cut from £12.3m to £10.0m. TP slashed from 61p to 40p.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at −2.8p/£10m/40p since mid-Feb 26)
  • Divergence: Price 22p vs TP 40p = 82% upside — but TP itself is a loss scenario company. The TP may need revisiting post-results given slight revenue miss and deeper-than-expected adj loss.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

Going concern material uncertainty: Auditors have flagged a material uncertainty for both FY24 and FY25. This is the dominant structural risk. "scenarios whereby...forecast new business converted...or the timings of conversion are delayed...material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt."

Order book step-change (+46.5%): The £23.3m three-year order book (vs £15.9m) is the single most positive metric. Specifically the Training Systems order book growing from £nil (FY24) to £10.3m post-period is transformational for near-term revenue visibility.

ARR +26% to £2.4m: Structural positive — recurring software revenues provide a floor. Target £3.0m ARR by end FY26 appears achievable given trajectory.

Siemens OEM partnership: Global distribution for Auxilium — potentially transformative for new geography penetration but entirely unquantified in financial terms.

PEN — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — Order book expansion to £23.3m (+46.5%): This is the one metric that brokers will cite as justification for maintaining the recovery thesis. With £9.7m of FY26 deliveries already contracted and Training Systems at £10.3m post-period (up from £nil), the revenue visibility for FY26 is materially better than FY25. The return to break-even PBT guided by management is credible if the contracted work delivers on schedule.

#2 Driver — Going concern uncertainty: The auditor's material uncertainty flag overshadows everything. Brokers will note that the HSBC facility has been renewed post-period (only £1m limit) and the shareholder loan (£0.3m, due April 2026) requires repayment. If new business conversion is delayed, the Group may need further equity raises. At 22p this is partially priced in, but it is the dominant risk.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26): Revenue — consensus £10.0m may be trimmed slightly given FY25 miss; however the £9.7m contracted order book supports £10–11m with new wins. Hold/slight trim £9.5–10.5m.
  • FY1 EPS (loss): −2.8p may worsen slightly given deeper FY25 adj loss; break-even adj PBT guided — so FY26 loss likely narrows to −1.5 to 0.0p.
  • FY2: 0.0p EPS / £13.0m revenue — hold if order book converts; risk skewed to downside if delays.
  • TP: 40p likely to be held or trimmed to 35–40p pending more clarity on FY26 execution.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Return to break-even adjusted PBT in FY26" — affirmative and specific. Not typical cautious language. But set against a going concern flag, the credibility requires order book execution.

Key risk: Going concern — new business conversion timing. The Group explicitly states the auditors have flagged this for both FY24 and FY25. "scenarios whereby the levels of forecast new business converted...may cast significant doubt upon the company's ability to continue as a going concern."

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — the results missed consensus slightly, the adj loss was deeper than expected, going concern flag persists, and the company remains dependent on new contract wins to survive. The order book expansion is positive but insufficient to remove the tail risk at current liquidity levels.

PEN — PHASE 5

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

30/100 · Confidence: 22–40 · No FX adjustment · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Pennant's FY25 was a deeply challenging year, with revenue of £9.66m down −29.7% YoY, missing consensus of £10.0m by −3.4%. The definitive catalyst — and the only positive one — is the order book expansion to £23.3m (+46.5%), of which £9.7m is contracted for FY26 delivery. The adjusted EBITDA loss widened to −£0.4m from +£1.7m in FY24, and the adjusted loss before tax of −£1.9m was slightly worse than the consensus forecast of −£1.8m. The one metric brokers will anchor to is that the contracted FY26 backlog (£9.7m) is essentially equivalent to the FY26 revenue consensus (£10.0m) before any new wins — this changes the risk profile for FY26 significantly relative to FY25.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £5.2m was better than H1's £4.5m, showing sequential improvement even if H2 YoY was still −18.8%. The going concern material uncertainty — flagged by auditors for the second consecutive year — is the primary constraint on the upgrade thesis. The HSBC overdraft facility stands at only £1m, the shareholder loan (£0.3m) fell due in April 2026, and the Group needs new contract wins beyond the existing order book to sustain operations beyond the near-term. The structured cost base (admin down to £6.6m after restructuring) and ARR of £2.4m (+26%) provide a floor, and the Siemens OEM partnership could accelerate new territory penetration — but both are too early-stage to de-risk the going concern in isolation.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Expect the single covering broker to trim FY1 revenue slightly (from £10.0m to £9.5–10.0m) and widen the FY26 adj loss range (from −2.8p towards −1.5 to −3.0p range). The TP of 40p is likely held or marginally trimmed to 35–40p; at 22p the stock already prices significant execution risk. The main watch-point is order book conversion: if the £9.7m of FY26 contracted work delivers on schedule and two to three Training Systems wins arrive in H1 2026, the break-even PBT guide becomes credible. If conversion is delayed by even one quarter, the going concern risk becomes acute. 🏁 PEN is a speculative recovery play: the order book transformation is genuine and the software ARR is growing, but the going concern flag, minimal liquidity, and consecutive year of deteriorating broker estimates make this unsuitable for anything other than a very high risk appetite. Cautious hold at best pending FY26 H1 trading confirmation.

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Personal Group is a UK-domiciled insurance and benefits provider. All revenues in GBP. Skip — no FX threshold breach.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 20.2p · Revenue £48.2m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 24.8p · Revenue £54.5m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +2.5% (19.7p → 20.2p) over snapshot period, with one upgrade in Sept 2025 (19.7p → 20.1p) and minor revision in March 2026 (20.1p → 20.2p). Last-4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (20.1p → 20.2p over last 4 weeks). Revenue net change: +0.4% (£48m → £48.2m). TP raised from 316p to 416p over period (+31.6%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 55.1% of FY = £26.6m (but note FY22 data skewed by legacy B2C). H1 split is unusual for insurance business. EPS 40.7% of FY = 8.2p.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £23.4m (Sharescope current H1) · EPS 9.2p (current H1)
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Revenue actual £48.4m vs prior (FY24) £43.8m = +10.5% FY YoY. vs FY1 consensus £48.2m = +0.4% beat. EPS actual 23.3p vs FY1 consensus 20.2p = +15.3% beat.
  • FX: N/A

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual £48.4m (+11% YoY, 2024: £43.8m). vs FY1 consensus £48.2m = +£0.2m beat (+0.4%).

"Group revenue up 11% to £48.4m (2024: £43.8m), with growth across all divisions"

2. Adjusted EBITDA — ahead of consensus £12.1m (+22% YoY, 2024: £10.0m). Company states "ahead of market expectations" of £11.6m → actual beat = +4.3%.

"Adjusted EBITDA up 22% to £12.1m (2024: £10.0m), ahead of market expectations (consensus £11.6m)"

3. EPS — materially ahead of consensus Basic EPS from continuing operations: 23.3p (2024: 17.7p) = +31.6% YoY. vs FY1 consensus 20.2p = +3.1p beat (+15.3%). This is the dominant figure. The beat was driven by a £0.4m R&D tax credit on benefits platform development.

"Basic EPS up 32% to 23.3p (2024: 17.7p)"

4. PBT — ahead £8.4m (+23%, 2024: £6.8m). vs FY1 consensus implied ~£8.2m = beat of ~2.4%.

"Profit before tax up 23% to £8.4m (2024: £6.8m)"

5. Annualised Recurring Revenue (ARR) ARR up 12% to £48.6m at 31 December 2025 (2024: £43.4m). Over 90% of FY25 revenue from recurring sources. This provides exceptional FY26 revenue visibility.

"Annualised recurring revenue streams (ARR) up 12% to £48.6m as at 31 December 2025"

6. Insurance new sales — record Annualised new insurance sales +11% to £15.4m. API (annualised premium income) +12% to £40.5m. Retention 81.7%.

"Annualised new insurance sales increased 11% to £15.4m and Annualised Premium Income (API) increased 12% to £40.5m"

7. Dividend — dramatically increased Total dividend 23.3p per share (2024: 16.5p) — +41.2% increase. Policy amended to pay approximately 1x basic EPS. Final dividend 15.1p.

"Total ordinary dividend for 2025 of 23.3 pence per share, representing an increase of 41% year-on-year"

8. Balance sheet — net cash, no debt Cash and deposits £29.0m (2024: £27.4m). Zero debt. Solvency ratio Personal Assurance: 299%. Fortress balance sheet.

9. Sage partnership expanded New multi-year contract signed March 2025; launched in Ireland Q2 2025. Sage SEB ARR grew to £4.6m (2024: £4.1m). Long-term growth platform.

10. FY26 outlook — strong momentum "Entered 2026 with strong momentum." 2030 aspirations: £100m revenue, £30m EBITDA, £20m SaaS ARR. No specific FY26 guidance numbers provided, but ARR of £48.6m provides ~90% FY26 revenue visibility at current run rate.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Revenue growth trajectory (FY23 onwards): +13.5% → +10.5% → 🟢 Steady (normalising from the step-change restructuring year) EPS growth trajectory: +263.9% → +35.1% → +31.6% → 🟢 Steady (compounding at ~30% per year on continuing basis)

Revenue trajectory: +10.9% → (implied) +10.1% → 🟢 Steady EPS trajectory (H2s): +43.6% → +25.9% → 🟢 Steady (high growth rate maintained, slight moderation which is expected)

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline and Tracking Deviation

  • Revenue baseline: 55.1% × £48.2m = £26.6m. H1 actual £23.4m ÷ £48.4m = 48.3% vs baseline 55.1% → deviation = 🔴 [−6.8pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL

However, the 55.1% H1 baseline is heavily distorted by FY22 data (H1 £34.4m from old operations). Using FY23-FY24 only: H1 = 18.4/(18.4+20.2) = 47.7%; FY24 = 21.1/(21.1+22.7) = 48.2% → 2yr avg = ~48.0%. On this adjusted basis, H1 FY25 at 48.3% is essentially IN LINE. The Sharescope 3yr avg is distorted and should be noted.

  • EPS baseline (adjusted): Using 2yr avg H1 split = ~40% (from FY23 H1 5.3/13.1=40.5%; FY24 H1 5.9/17.7=33.3% → 2yr avg ~36.9%). H1 actual 9.2p ÷ 20.2p = 45.5% vs adjusted baseline ~36.9% → deviation = 🟢 [+8.6pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY

Buy triggers: Rev (using adjusted baseline 48% × £48.2m = £23.1m) × 1.015 = £23.5m: H1 actual £23.4m → borderline 🔴 ✗ · EPS > 7.4p × 1.015 = 7.5p: H1 actual 9.2p → 🟢 ✓

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 implied revenue £25.0m vs 2yr avg H2 = (£20.2m + £22.7m)/2 = £21.5m → +16.3% → 🟢 strong

H2 implied EPS 14.1p vs 2yr avg H2 = (7.8p + 11.2p)/2 = 9.5p → +48.4% → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS +2.5% net change — relatively flat estimates indicating market underestimated the R&D tax credit and claims ratio improvement
  • TP +31.6% (316p → 416p) — significant broker conviction building
  • 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING
  • Divergence: TP rises while EPS estimates barely moved — suggests brokers are lifting the PE multiple, not just earnings. Growing confidence in the compounding business model.

5. Structural Flags

  • ARR £48.6m > FY25 reported revenue £48.4m: This is the key structural flag. The ARR exiting FY25 already exceeds the full-year FY25 reported revenue, providing exceptional FY26 revenue floor visibility. Even with zero new insurance sales or new platform clients in FY26, revenue is ~90% locked in.
  • New dividend policy (1x EPS): The 23.3p/share dividend at a 294p stock price = 7.9% dividend yield — exceptional for a growth company. This fundamentally changes the investor base and re-rates the valuation framework.
  • Claims ratio improvement: 27.1% (2024: 29.1%) — lower-than-expected claims directly boost underwriting profit margin. This is partially structural (better risk selection) and partially volatile.
  • Simplyhealth partnership (post-period): Access to 12,000 Simplyhealth business relationships — potentially a major B2B distribution channel for insurance sales.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — EPS 23.3p vs consensus 20.2p: +15.3% beat This is a material beat that will dominate broker notes. The combination of higher insurance premiums, lower claims ratio, R&D tax credit, and operating leverage drove the outperformance. Brokers will need to upgrade FY26 EPS estimates materially — prior FY2 consensus of 24.8p now looks too low given the 23.3p base.

#2 Driver — 41% dividend increase + ARR £48.6m exit run rate The dividend raise to match EPS (23.3p/share = 7.9% yield at 294p) is a powerful capital return statement. Combined with ARR at £48.6m already exceeding FY25 revenue, brokers will upgrade their FY26 revenue estimates with high confidence. The Simplyhealth partnership post-period provides an additional new distribution channel catalyst.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: consensus currently ~24.8p (FY2 pre-results); given FY25 base of 23.3p and ARR growth of 12% supporting similar revenue trajectory, FY26 EPS likely upgraded to 27–28p (+8–15% vs prior FY2 consensus).
  • FY1 (FY26) revenue: prior FY2 consensus £54.5m. ARR exit of £48.6m + expected new business growth implies £52–55m; broadly confirmed.
  • TP: Currently 416p; likely to move toward 450–500p post-results given the earnings upgrade cycle and yield re-rating.

Conservative guidance: Company provides no specific FY26 numerical guidance, but "entered 2026 with strong momentum" + ARR visibility + Simplyhealth partnership = strongly constructive qualitative guidance. The 2030 aspirations (£100m revenue, £30m EBITDA) anchor a long-term upgrade path. This is an emerging growth upgrade cycle.

Key risk: The R&D tax credit of £0.4m inflated EPS in FY25 by ~1.3p — one-off and not recurring in FY26. Brokers will strip this out when forecasting FY26, creating a slightly higher hurdle. Also, the UK insurance market is competitive and new digital insurance products (hospital cover, death plan) being tested are not yet in revenue.

Overall tone: 🟢 🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 88/100 · Confidence: 82–93 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

🟢 Dividend +41% to 23.3p — 7.9% yield triggers re-rating+10

🔴 No explicit FY26 numerical guidance — some uncertainty on quantum of upgrades−3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: PGH delivered an exceptional FY25 with adjusted EBITDA of £12.1m (+22%), explicitly "ahead of market expectations" of £11.6m, and EPS of 23.3p — a 15.3% beat against the 20.2p consensus. The #1 catalyst was the combination of a record insurance sales year (API +12% to £40.5m, new sales +11% to £15.4m), a claims ratio improvement to 27.1% from 29.1% boosting underwriting margin, and operating leverage across both Insurance and Benefits & Reward. The R&D tax credit contributed ~1.3p but the underlying beat is ~14p — still materially above consensus.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The structural driver protecting the upgrade thesis is ARR of £48.6m exiting FY25 — higher than FY25's total reported revenue of £48.4m. This means over 90% of FY26 revenue is already contractually secured, making the upgrade story a matter of how much growth is added on top of a highly visible base. H2 implied EPS of 14.1p (+48% above the 2yr historical H2 average) confirms the earnings power has structurally stepped up. The insurance business reached penetration of 14.5% in top 100 sites (up from 13.0%), a key operational KPI showing continued organic progress. The Simplyhealth partnership (post-period end) adds access to 12,000 business relationships as a new distribution channel not in any current FY26 estimate.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS should be upgraded from the current FY2 consensus of ~24.8p toward 27–28p range, reflecting the higher 23.3p base, the ARR growth trajectory and the Simplyhealth incremental opportunity. The FY26 revenue consensus of £54.5m is broadly achievable — ARR growing at 12% against a £48.6m exit base implies ~£54m naturally before new sales. TP should move from 416p toward 450–500p range. At 294p, the stock offers an estimated 7.9% yield plus earnings growth — an unusual and compelling combination for an AIM-listed growth company. The key watch point is FY26 guidance confirmation and the success of the new digital insurance products in testing. 🏁 Verdict: Exceptional beat across all metrics with ARR visibility making FY26 upgrades a near-certainty; dividend re-rating and Simplyhealth partnership add incremental positive drivers. Score 88/100.

PINE — Pinewood Technologies Group PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

The PINE RNS (Business Update, 25 March 2026) contains no Currency Movements section. Revenue base: FY1 consensus £44.7m. Operations are UK-headquartered with Netherlands reseller acquisition (£3.3m). North America rollout is in pre-revenue testing phase. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of disclosed revenues — the Netherlands acquisition adds ~£0.75m EBITDA and is GBP-reported. Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY update or trading update. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 5.9p · Revenue £44.7m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 11.5p · Revenue £61.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot period: 8.7p → 5.9p = −2.8p (−32.2%). Sustained step-down: first cut Sept 2025 (8.9p → 6.5p), second cut Nov 2025 (6.5p → 6.1p → 5.9p). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 5.9p since Nov 2025). Revenue net change: £45.2m → £44.7m = −£0.5m (−1.1%). Direction of EPS revisions is firmly negative over the year.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.3% of FY = £21.6m · EPS 61.3% of FY = 3.6p (1yr avg — only one H1 EPS data point available; used as proxy)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £16.1m · EPS 3.3p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): Current H1 revenue £19.6m. FY1 consensus £44.7m minus H1 £19.6m = implied H2 £25.1m vs prior-year H2 £15.1m → +66.3% YoY — heavily H2-weighted, driven by Lookers rollout acceleration in H2. Implied H2 EPS: 5.9p − 0.6p = 5.3p vs prior-year H2 −3.3p — prior year H2 was loss-making, so H2 is the inflection point year.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Business Update, 25 March 2026, contains inside information)

1. Revenue / Guidance — FY26 EBITDA warning

FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations due to Marshalls implementation delay from Q1 2026 to H2 2026. No numeric EBITDA or revenue figure provided. Implied downward revision to FY26 estimates — magnitude unquantified in the RNS.

"As a result of the change in timing of the Marshalls implementation, FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations."

2. Marshalls — delay confirmed, not cancelled

Previously guided Q1 2026 commencement. Now commencement expected H2 2026. Planning process described as "approaching completion." Since October 2024 Marshalls has added Geely Auto, Omoda, Jaecoo, BYD and Genesis dealers — network has grown, not contracted.

"This planning process is approaching completion, and the rollout of the Pinewood.AI system is now expected to commence in the second half of 2026."

3. Lookers — on track

Lookers rollout commenced 21 July 2025, progressing to schedule. Simultaneous 13-store Mercedes-Benz go-live in February 2026. Remaining Lookers dealers scheduled to complete on time in Q4 2026.

"In February, we executed a simultaneous 13 store go-live across Lookers' Mercedes-Benz dealers. The rollout into the remaining Lookers dealers is scheduled to complete on time, in quarter four 2026."

4. North America — pre-revenue testing stage

System live in various stages, testing major functions with Lithia. Rollout expected to commence H2 2026.

"We are looking forward to commencing the system rollout in North America in the second half of 2026."

5. Netherlands reseller acquisition

Acquired for £3.3m cash. Expected to add £0.7–0.8m incremental annual EBITDA. Supports Central European growth.

"The acquisition is aligned with Pinewood.AI's strategy to fully control its international sales and customer service functions, and it will support the Group's growth ambitions in the Central European market."

6. FY28 EBITDA guidance reaffirmed

Board reaffirms £58–62m underlying EBITDA by FY28, underpinned by existing signed contracts and strong pipeline.

"The Board of Pinewood.AI also reaffirms its expectation that the Group will achieve underlying EBITDA of £58-62m by FY28."

7. FY25 results date

FY25 results to be released 22 April 2026. No FY25 guidance or figures disclosed in this RNS.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed. The RNS is a trading update only — no income statement. No tax rate deviation to check.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations" — explicit below-consensus language for the current year. Numeric range: none. Forward coverage: one year (FY26). FY28 £58–62m reaffirmed (two years out).
  • The RNS is an explicit profit warning for FY26 combined with a reaffirmation of the medium-term (FY28) target. Current year delivery: Lookers on track, North America testing. Marshalls the sole source of miss.
  • Classification: 🔴🔴 Profit warning — explicit below-expectations EBITDA guidance for FY26. Provisional points: −12 to −15.
  • Divergence check: No current-year H1 results in this RNS (FY25 results due 22 April). FY26 guidance is the primary content. Lookers progress provides a partial offset to the Marshalls delay but does not neutralise the profit warning. No divergence — delivery and guidance are directionally consistent (both reflect a delay story). No separate divergence row required.

  • H2 EPS: implied 5.3p vs prior-year H2 −3.3p → recovery from loss to profit (n/m % YoY)

Marshalls was expected to contribute H2 revenue — now commencing H2 2026 rather than Q1 2026, a ~2-quarter slip. The magnitude of downgrade is uncertain but brokers will reduce H2 estimates materially.

H2 classification (pre-RNS): consensus implied 🟢 strong (+66% YoY revenue). Post-RNS: likely to downgrade to 🟡 moderate or 🔴 weak depending on Marshalls contribution quantum.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 8.9p → 5.9p, net −3.0p (−33.7%) over snapshot. Two downgrade events: Sept 2025 (strategy day reset) and Nov 2025 (further cuts). Revenue: £45.9m → £44.7m.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 5.9p / £44.7m for 4+ months)
  • Divergence: Price peaked at 759p (Feb 2026) then fell to 689p by March — 9% off peak. EPS has been flat for months, suggesting the market anticipated stability before this RNS. The RNS resets the downgrade cycle.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Marshalls delay — timing not cancellation]: The key structural point is that Marshalls has grown its network (added 5 OEM brands) during the delay. The integration is strategic, not indicative of contract risk. Revenue slips from H1 2026 to H2 2026 — a timing issue, not a permanent impairment.

"Since October 2024, Marshalls has added a significant number of new dealerships and brands to its portfolio, including Geely Auto, Omoda, Jaecoo, BYD and Genesis dealers which have enhanced and grown the Marshalls network."

[FY28 reaffirmation — unchanged medium-term path]: The £58–62m FY28 EBITDA target is explicitly reaffirmed. This is the anchor for long-duration valuation models and limits structural damage to the investment case.

[North America upside — binary option]: North America (Lithia, >$9bn addressable revenue per CEO) remains in testing phase. Commencement H2 2026. If execution begins on schedule this represents a step-change in the revenue trajectory.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 EBITDA profit warning: The dominant broker note catalyst. Explicit "below market expectations" language on underlying EBITDA for FY26 is a mandatory downgrade trigger. Brokers will cut FY26 estimates by the quantum of the Marshalls H2 2026 revenue that was previously embedded. Marshalls was expected to commence Q1 2026; the slip to H2 2026 removes 1–2 quarters of Marshalls contribution from FY26. The magnitude of Marshalls in the FY26 model is unknown from the RNS, but given it was the centrepiece contract, estimates likely move down 15–25% on EBITDA.

#2 Driver — FY28 reaffirmation vs near-term pain: Brokers will frame the note as "near-term impaired, medium-term intact." The explicit £58–62m FY28 reaffirmation provides a floor for target price cuts — models anchored to FY28 will see less TP erosion than those anchored to near-term multiples. This limits the downgrade magnitude on target prices relative to the EPS cut.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: DOWN — estimated cut of 20–30% (5.9p → likely 4.0–4.8p range). Revenue: DOWN 10–15% (£44.7m → £38–40m). EBITDA: DOWN materially from current consensus.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: Modest DOWN 5–10% — Marshalls fully on-platform by end FY26, so FY27 should see full-year Marshalls contribution. FY28 reaffirmation anchors FY27 estimates.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers likely to cut target prices by 15–25% from current levels (~689p consensus → likely £520–590p new range). Recommendation changes possible from Buy to Hold for some houses. Current price 252p is already deeply discounted — 63% below consensus TP. That discount partially reflects the downgrade risk already priced in.

Conservative guidance read-through: No "comfortable with" language. This is straightforward below-expectations language — no deliberate understatement. No upgrade cycle read-through.

Key risk: The Marshalls delay is the third delay announcement (original timeline, Sept 2025 reset, now March 2026 further delay). Each delay erodes credibility with investors who may question whether Marshalls ever commences. The RNS attempts to mitigate this with the network expansion narrative, but pattern of delays is damaging to sentiment.

"Both parties have been focused on optimising the sequencing and efficiency of these key technology projects. This process has taken longer than originally anticipated, compared with the expectations set out in the 24 September 2025 announcement."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: cut (−20–30%). Tone must be Cautious or Negative. → 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected.

Overall tone: 🔴🔴 Negative / material downgrades expected

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The dominant catalyst in this RNS is an explicit FY26 EBITDA profit warning — "FY26 underlying EBITDA will be lower than current market expectations." The trigger is the Marshalls implementation delay, now pushed from Q1 2026 to H2 2026, a further ~two-quarter slip beyond the September 2025 guidance. This is the third announced delay to the Marshalls rollout and constitutes the single most damaging element of the update. The only partially offsetting factor is the Lookers rollout remaining on track for Q4 2026 completion, with the 13-store simultaneous Mercedes-Benz go-live in February 2026 demonstrating execution capability.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: PINE's H1 EPS tracking deviation of −51pp against the seasonal baseline was already extreme — pre-RNS consensus required 5.3p of H2 EPS from 5.9p full-year (90% H2 loading). The Marshalls delay directly impairs this H2 burden. Brokers will need to reduce the Marshalls contribution embedded in H2 FY26 estimates, meaning the revised H2 implied EPS burden falls even further short of what is achievable. The H2 revenue tracking deviation of −4.5pp fired a sell signal even before this RNS. The FY28 £58–62m reaffirmation is the primary structural floor — if credible, it prevents complete re-rating to distressed multiples, but it is two years away and requires Marshalls, Lookers AND North America to all land sequentially without further slippage.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Expect FY1 EPS cuts of 20–30% (5.9p → ~4.0–4.8p range) and revenue cuts of 10–15% (£44.7m → £38–40m). FY2 (FY27) revisions are likely 5–10% lower as the Marshalls runway extends. Target price cuts of 15–25% are probable (689p consensus → ~£520–590p), with some brokers potentially moving to Hold from Buy. The watch point is the FY25 results on 22 April 2026 — these will provide the first clean baseline from which to model FY26 and will likely be accompanied by updated guidance. Until then, estimates remain open. 🏁 Significant negative: explicit profit warning on FY26, third Marshalls delay, H2 tracking already deeply negative — material downgrades expected; the FY28 reaffirmation limits structural damage but near-term sentiment severely impaired. Score 18/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

PINE · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (12 months ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY25 actual:

  • Revenue: £40.5m (FY24: £31.2m) = +29.8% YoY on a reported basis. However FY24 was 11 months vs FY25 12 months — on a comparable annualised basis FY24 revenue = £31.2m × (12/11) = £34.0m annualised → FY25 +19.1% on annualised comparable.
  • vs Sharescope FY1 fc £41.7m: miss of −£1.2m = −2.9%.
  • Recurring revenue: £33.7m = 83.2% of total (FY24: 86.5%). Slight decline in recurring mix — Seez AI bringing some non-recurring implementation revenue.
  • H1: £19.6m / H2: £20.9m — modest H2 weighting, consistent with 2yr avg split.

"Revenue up 29.8% to £40.5m in FY25 (from £31.2m in FY24)...the revenue growth was due to a combination of FY24 being an 11 month period and FY25 being a 12 month period, the Seez acquisition in March 2025, revenue from new customers and revenue from upselling."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY25:

  • Underlying PAT: £5.7m (FY24: £6.4m) = −10.9% YoY. On 104.7m shares = 5.4p underlying adj EPS.
  • vs FY1 fc 6.0p consensus: miss of −0.6p = −10%.
  • Underlying EBITDA: £16.4m vs fc £15.8m = +3.8% beat.
  • Underlying PBT: £8.8m vs fc £8.8m = in-line exactly.
  • The EBITDA beat / EPS miss paradox: EBITDA £16.4m beat, but underlying PAT fell from FY24 £6.4m to FY25 £5.7m. The bridge: EBITDA £16.4m → D&A £8.1m (up £2.5m YoY, driven by Seez intangibles amortisation) → underlying EBIT £8.3m → net finance income £0.5m → underlying PBT £8.8m → tax £3.1m (effective rate 35.2% vs FY24 rate 24.8%) → underlying PAT £5.7m. The EPS miss vs EBITDA beat is entirely explained by (a) D&A step-up from Seez acquisition (£7.0m amortisation in FY25 vs £5.0m FY24) and (b) the higher effective tax rate (35.2% vs 24.8% prior year). Both reduce EPS below what the EBITDA beat implies.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 35.2% vs prior 24.8% = +10.4pp. This is a significant deviation. If restated at 24.8% normalised rate: underlying PAT = £8.8m × (1 − 0.248) = £6.62m → EPS = 6.3p — which would have beaten consensus 6.0p. The tax rate increase is the primary driver of the EPS miss. The RNS does not explain the higher effective tax rate. The deferred tax liability jumped from £2.5m to £35.0m — a £32.5m increase driven by the Seez AI acquisition intangibles recognition for tax purposes. This is acquisition accounting-driven, not indicative of underlying trading deterioration. 🚨 Flag: EPS miss is tax-driven (acquisition accounting), not operational. Restated normalised EPS ~6.3p would have been a beat.

EPS bridge FY26e (constructed here):

  • (1) New base: FY25 underlying EPS 5.4p (at 35.2% effective tax rate) or 6.3p (at normalised 24.8%). Using 5.4p as reported base.
  • (2) Inorganic annualisation delta: Seez acquired March 2025 → contributed ~10 months in FY25. Full 12-month Seez contribution in FY26 = ~2 additional months → incremental EBITDA ~£0.7m. Also Netherlands reseller acquired Feb 2026 → £0.7–0.8m EBITDA additive in FY26.
  • (3) Organic EBITDA growth delta: Company guides FY26 underlying EBITDA consensus = £21.3m (confirmed in RNS footnote). FY25 = £16.4m → FY26 = £21.3m = +£4.9m = +29.9% YoY growth. Revenue consensus FY26 = £57.8m vs FY25 £40.5m = +42.7% — very large step-up implying Lookers rollout completion and Lithia early revenue recognition.
  • (4) Interest step-up: Net cash £34.1m → growing; interest income growing. No step-up concern.
  • (5) Tax normalisation: If effective tax rate normalises from 35.2% toward the UK statutory 25% in FY26 (deferred tax adjustments may reverse partially), underlying PAT uplift is material.
  • Implied FY26 EPS bridge: EBITDA £21.3m → D&A est. £9–10m (Seez amortisation continuing, £4m/yr acquired intangibles + £5–6m underlying) → EBIT ~£11–12m → net finance income ~£1.0m (cash growing) → PBT ~£12–13m → tax at normalised ~25% → PAT ~£9–10m → on ~115m shares → EPS ~7.8–8.7p. Sharescope FY2 fc = 9.3p — at the top of my implied range; achievable if tax normalises and D&A is lower than estimated. No major revision expected.
  • vs stale FY2 consensus 9.3p: my bridge implies broadly in-line. No material EPS revision triggered by today's results.

3. Order book / TCV:

  • Total Contract Value (TCV): £64.5m at end of FY25. This is future incremental revenue from signed contracts. Against FY25 revenue £40.5m, TCV represents 1.59x annual revenue in contracted future revenue — exceptional forward visibility.
  • "c.85% of the projected EBITDA growth [to £58–62m by FY28] covered by signed contracts." This is the dominant investment case signal — the path to the FY28 target is not speculative; 85% is contracted.

"Total Contract Value (TCV) of £64.5m at end of 2025 - future incremental revenue from signed customer contracts."

4. Margin / profitability:

  • Gross margin: 85.7% (FY24: 90.4%) = −4.7pp. Decline explained by Seez AI's lower gross margin pulling down the blended rate. Underlying cloud hosting cost structure unchanged.
  • Underlying EBITDA margin: 40.5% (FY24: 44.9%) = −4.4pp. Admin costs +33.3% vs revenue +29.8% — negative operating leverage in FY25 due to investment.
  • H1/H2 EBITDA: H1 £7.9m (margin 40.3%) / H2 £8.5m (margin 40.7%) — consistent margins across halves, no H2 deterioration.
  • Marshall Motor Group rollout delayed: previously expected Q1 2026, now H2 2026. This is a revenue timing slip but the contract is signed. Impact: ~£0.7–1.0m of revenue pushed from H1 to H2 FY26, compressing H1 FY26 but not the full year.
  • Pinewood North America LLC costs: £4.2m charged through P&L as non-underlying in FY25 (subsidiary from July 2025 onwards). This is a cash drag that increases in FY26 as the US rollout scales.

"The decrease in the gross margin rate from 90.4% in FY24 to 85.7% in FY25 was due to the impact of the Seez acquisition."

5. Capital / North America:

  • Cash: £34.1m (FY24: £9.3m). £34.1m equity raise in March 2025 offset by £26.5m Seez acquisition cost + operating cash generation £6.8m.
  • Going concern: forecast net cash inflow FY26 = £1.8m. This is extremely thin for a company with £34.1m cash and £16.4m EBITDA. The forecasted near-zero FCF in FY26 implies significant capex/investment cash outflow (~£10m guided capex + North America costs).
  • Lookers rollout: "progressing well, due to finish Q4 2026." Lookers is a major UK dealer group — completion in Q4 FY26 unlocks full Lookers recurring revenue from FY27 onwards.
  • North America: system testing underway at Lithia's US dealers. OEM integration with ~90% of Lithia's North American dealers. No revenue from North America yet — this remains a cost centre.

6. Qualitative tone:

  • FY26: "expects underlying EBITDA for FY26 to be in line with market expectations" — confirms FY26 EBITDA consensus £21.3m.
  • FY28: "reaffirms its expectation that the Group will achieve underlying EBITDA of £58–62m by FY28. This is underpinned by strong visibility from our existing signed contracts and a significant pipeline of opportunities, with c.85% of the projected EBITDA growth covered by signed contracts."
  • The FY28 target implies ~£58–62m EBITDA vs FY25 £16.4m = 3.5–3.8x growth in 3 years. The magnitude is extraordinary but the contractual coverage (85% of EBITDA growth signed) provides credibility.

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

FY26 guidance: explicit numeric confirmation of EBITDA consensus £21.3m. Covers FY26 only. FY28 medium-term target reaffirmed with 85% contracted coverage.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — FY26 in-line guidance with no upgrade language; the FY28 reaffirmation is the constructive signal but that's medium-term, not a near-term broker revision trigger. Provisional points: +2.

Divergence: FY25 EBITDA beat (£16.4m vs £15.8m fc) but EPS miss (5.4p vs 6.0p fc). The divergence is explained by acquisition accounting tax effects — not a fundamental deterioration. Flag: 🟡 EBITDA beat / EPS miss — divergence driven by Seez acquisition deferred tax, not operational.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

PINE · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

H2 derivations (using RNS operating review table):

  • FY25: H1 rev £19.6m / H2 £20.9m ✅; H1 EBITDA £7.9m / H2 £8.5m ✅; H1 underlying PBT £4.4m / H2 £4.4m ✅
  • FY24 (11 months, Feb–Dec 2024): H1 rev £16.1m / H2 £15.1m = £31.2m ✅ (Sharescope "1y ago" H1/H2 confirmed). Note H2 FY24 was a 5-month period per the RNS footnote.
  • FY24 adj EPS from RNS: underlying PAT £6.4m / 111.4m shares = 5.7p (Sharescope shows 5.0p — using RNS 5.7p).
  • Sharescope "3y ago" revenue: FY = £19.1m. This appears to be the period prior to the motor retail disposal (FY23 technology-only revenue). Sharescope H1/H2 revenue fields for 3y ago are corrupt (1,845.5/−1,826.4). Unusable.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-FY mode)

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — this scores)

H2 base: RNS-derived FY25 £40.5m → H2 = £20.9m vs H2 FY24 £15.1m = +38.4% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%). However the FY24 H2 was only 5 months — on an annualised basis H2 FY24 revenue rate = £15.1m × (6/5) = £18.1m → FY25 H2 +15.5% on annualised comparable. Still 🟢 strong.

Classification: 🟢 strong — RNS-derived.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: −31.0% net (8.9p → 6.0p). Dramatic pre-results downgrade over 11 months. The step-changes: 27 Sep 25 (8.9p → 6.5p), then 22 Nov 25 (6.5p → 5.9p), stabilising at 6.0p. Revenue also cut −7.7%. This is an unusually large pre-results downgrade for a business whose EBITDA came in ahead of consensus.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 6.0p since 28 Mar 26).
  • The snapshot reveals a crucial disconnect: price rose from 595p (Jul 25) to 714–759p (Sep 25 to Feb 26) even as EPS consensus was being cut by 32%. This confirms the investment thesis is not built on near-term EPS but on the FY28 EBITDA target of £58–62m. The price then fell from 759p (Feb 26) to 654p (Mar 26) to current 232p — a fall of −69% from the Feb 26 peak to today's closing price. ⚠️ This is an extraordinary price collapse that is not reflected in the Sharescope data which shows 654p at the 17 Apr 26 data point. The RNS states the current price as 232p (from the brief context provided). This requires investigation — either there has been a catastrophic news event between 17 Apr and today, or the price data reflects pre-market / different date. Proceeding with 232p as stated.

At 232p vs consensus TP 654p = 181% upside stated. However, at 232p the market cap = 232p × 114.5m shares = £265.7m. Against FY26 EBITDA consensus £21.3m = 12.5x EV/EBITDA (approx, ignoring net cash). Against FY28 EBITDA target £60m midpoint = 4.4x EV/EBITDA on FY28. The extreme price dislocation from TP suggests a loss of confidence in the FY28 target delivery — likely driven by the Marshalls delay announcement (25 March 2026) and broader market risk-off for high-multiple growth stocks.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Currency: GBP.

RNS vs forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash = £34.1m vs Sharescope fc −£35.3m (net cash £35.3m). RNS £1.2m below Sharescope forecast — trivial, consistent with FY25 capex of £11.4m vs fc £10.0m (slightly higher investment).

  • Net cash/(debt): FY23 ~−£19.9m (Sharescope 3y ago H2) / FY24 H2 +£3.5m (Sharescope 1y ago H2 — this is RCF repayment timing) → RNS FY24 = −£9.3m wait: RNS cash = £9.3m at 31 Dec 2024 / H1 FY25 = −£28.2m (Sharescope current H1; sign = net cash) / FY25 year-end RNS: £34.1m / fc £35.3m / FY2 £43.4m.
  • ND/EBITDA: deeply net cash throughout post-disposal. No leverage risk.
  • Going concern note flags forecast net cash inflow of only £1.8m in FY26. This implies near-zero FCF despite £21.3m EBITDA guidance: capex ~£10m + Pinewood North America cash losses ~£4–6m + working capital investment as Lookers scales. This is a material cash burn signal for FY26 — the company will consume cash on investment even while EBITDA grows.
  • Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — no leverage concern in absolute terms, but FCF conversion is poor in the investment phase.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24 actual:

  • Revenue: £40.5m > FY24 £31.2m ✅✅
  • EPS: 5.4p < FY24 5.7p 🚨 FY25 underlying EPS −5.3% below FY24 actual — acquisition dilution year.

Step 2 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • Revenue: £57.8m > £40.5m ✅✅ (+42.7%)
  • EPS: 9.3p > 5.4p ✅✅ (+72.2%)

3.6 Structural / One-Off Flags

  • North America — cost centre turning to revenue: Pinewood North America LLC generated £4.2m of losses charged through P&L as non-underlying in FY25. OEM integration with ~90% of Lithia's North American dealers underway. System testing in US dealers commenced. Until North America reaches 20 dealers at full implementation (per the non-underlying policy), these costs remain excluded from underlying. The moment this threshold is crossed, North America shifts to underlying — adding both revenue and costs to the underlying P&L and changing the EPS trajectory significantly.
  • Marshalls delay (Q1 2026 → H2 2026): This was the news on 25 March 2026 that likely drove the price from ~650p toward 232p. Marshalls is a major dealer group (signed contract, TCV included in £64.5m). The 6-month delay pushes Marshalls revenue recognition into H2 FY26 from H1, creating a likely H1 FY26 miss vs seasonal baseline while preserving the full-year FY26 guidance of £21.3m EBITDA. This is not a demand cancellation — Marshalls is committed — but it is a timing slip that has materially damaged market confidence.
  • FY28 target credibility: £58–62m EBITDA by FY28 = 3.5–3.8x FY25 EBITDA in 3 years. The contractual support is genuine (85% signed) but the execution risk is high — particularly the Lithia US rollout which is still at system testing stage. Any further delays to either Lithia US or Lookers (due to finish Q4 2026) compress the FY28 delivery window significantly.
  • Deferred tax liability £35.0m (FY24: £2.5m) — driven by Seez AI intangibles recognition for tax purposes. This is a real cash liability over time as the acquired intangibles unwind. It partially explains the high FY25 effective tax rate and will continue to suppress reported PAT vs EBITDA for several years.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

PINE · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — FY26 EBITDA guidance £21.3m in-line + FY28 reaffirmation with 85% contracted coverage: The market has been shaken by the Marshalls delay (25 March 2026) and the price has collapsed to 232p from 650p+. Today's results confirm: (a) FY25 EBITDA ahead of consensus at £16.4m vs £15.8m fc; (b) FY26 in-line confirmation at £21.3m; (c) FY28 target fully reaffirmed with 85% signed contract backing. For brokers, the key question is whether the FY28 target remains credible after the Marshalls delay — today's results provide management's strongest possible reaffirmation.

#2 Driver — TCV £64.5m and North America momentum: TCV of £64.5m represents contracted future revenue. With OEM integration at ~90% of Lithia's North American dealer network and system testing underway in US dealers, the North America story is progressing — just more slowly than the market had assumed when the price was at 700p+. The NADA conference (February 2026) generated "thousands of visits" — qualitative evidence of commercial interest.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY25e EPS: stale consensus 6.0p; actual underlying 5.4p = −10% miss. Brokers will cut FY25 EPS from 6.0p to ~5.4p — already partially reflected in the pre-results downgrade cycle.
  • FY26e EPS: from 9.3p (Sharescope FY2 fc). In-line EBITDA guidance + EPS bridge suggests ~7.5–9p landing depending on D&A and tax normalisation. Risk of minor FY26 EPS trim, particularly given the Marshalls delay compressing H1 FY26. Brokers may cut FY26 EPS modestly toward 8.0–8.5p.
  • FY26e Revenue: from £57.8m. Marshalls delay means H1 rev may be softer; full-year likely maintained around £55–58m given Lookers remains on track for Q4 2026 completion.
  • FY28e: reaffirmed £58–62m EBITDA target — brokers cannot cut this today given management's explicit reaffirmation with 85% contracted backing. But investor confidence in the delivery timeline has been structurally damaged by the Marshalls slip.
  • TP: consensus TP 654p vs actual price 232p. Brokers will likely maintain TPs (which are based on the FY28 DCF) but the market is applying a much higher execution discount. No imminent TP cut expected from today's results alone, but the gap between TP and price reflects the market pricing in a higher probability of further delivery slippage.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with market expectations" is as strong a FY26 statement as the company can give. The FY28 reaffirmation with 85% signed contracts is unusually specific — management is laying its credibility squarely on that number. If any further delays emerge on Lookers (Q4 2026 completion) or Lithia US, the FY28 target becomes at risk.

Key risk: Execution slippage on large enterprise rollouts. The Marshalls delay has established a pattern. Lookers is "progressing well" but due to finish Q4 2026 — a tight window. Lithia US is at "system testing" stage, which is pre-revenue. The FY28 EBITDA target requires multiple large contracts all executing on schedule simultaneously. "The implementation of the Pinewood.AI platform across Lookers' dealerships is progressing well and is due to finish in Q4 2026."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision: cut (5.4p vs 6.0p fc = −10%). Tone: Cautious or Neutral. But FY26 guidance in-line and FY28 reaffirmed = leaning Neutral despite the EPS miss. Retaining 🟡 Neutral — the EPS miss is acquisition accounting, not operational.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — EBITDA beat, EPS miss (tax-driven), FY26 in-line, FY28 reaffirmed. The story is intact but the Marshalls delay has structurally reduced investor confidence in execution timing. The real test is H1 FY26 delivery (likely soft due to Marshalls) and any update on Lithia US progress.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline tension in Pinewood's FY25 results is the gap between the metrics that matter to the underlying business and the reported EPS outcome. On the metrics that matter: underlying EBITDA of £16.4m beat consensus £15.8m by +3.8%; TCV reached £64.5m in signed contracted future revenue; North America OEM integration is at ~90% completion; and the FY28 EBITDA target of £58–62m has been explicitly reaffirmed with 85% of the projected growth already under signed contract. On the reported headline: underlying EPS of 5.4p missed consensus 6.0p by 10% — entirely explained by a deferred tax liability step-up from Seez AI acquisition accounting (£32.5m DTL increase) pushing the effective tax rate from 24.8% to 35.2%. At a normalised 24.8% tax rate, EPS would have been ~6.3p — a beat. Revenue of £40.5m missed £41.7m consensus by 2.9%, a modest shortfall driven by the annualisation period difference vs FY24 and Seez revenue mix. The operational delivery is sound; the noise is acquisition accounting.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 FY25 revenue of £20.9m (+38.4% vs H2 FY24 £15.1m) and H2 EBITDA of £8.5m (+21.4% YoY) confirm the second-half weighting of the growth trajectory is intact. The 🟢 strong H2 classification is RNS-derived and contractually supported. The critical forward risk is the Marshalls delay: previously expected Q1 2026, now H2 2026. This six-month slip will compress H1 FY26 revenue and EBITDA vs the 48.3% seasonal baseline, almost certainly generating a SELL SIGNAL on the H1 tracking metric in the next update — but it is a timing event, not a cancellation. Lookers (completion Q4 2026) and Lithia US (system testing underway) are the two other execution dependencies. The upgrade resilience case rests entirely on these three programmes delivering on revised schedules. The FY26 EBITDA consensus of £21.3m (company-confirmed) implies £4.9m EBITDA growth YoY — achievable from Lookers and Seez full-year contribution even without Marshalls in H1, but with zero margin for further slippage. Net cash of £34.1m provides runway, though the FY26 FCF forecast of only £1.8m highlights that the investment phase is consuming cash aggressively.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY25 EPS brokers revise from 6.0p to approximately 5.4p (−10%); the EBITDA beat provides some offset and TP reductions are unlikely given the FY28 reaffirmation. FY26 EPS from 9.3p current consensus — at risk of modest cuts toward 8.0–8.5p driven by the Marshalls H1 timing slip and continuing North America pre-revenue losses, partially offset by Seez full-year contribution. FY26 revenue consensus £57.8m may be trimmed toward £54–56m if Marshalls H2 ramp takes time to crystallise. Consensus TP 654p vs current 232p = 181% implied upside — the gap reflects the market pricing a significant execution risk premium onto the FY28 DCF. This is a binary story: if Lookers completes Q4 2026 on schedule, Lithia US moves from testing to rollout, and Marshalls starts H2 as guided, the FY28 target remains credible and the 232p price is deeply cheap. If any further slippage emerges, the FY28 timeline extends and the multiple contracts further. 🏁 FY25 delivered on the metrics that matter — EBITDA ahead, TCV at record, FY28 reaffirmed with 85% contracted — but the execution credibility deficit from the Marshalls delay, the EPS miss (accounting-driven), and the near-zero FY26 FCF forecast leave the score squarely in neutral territory; the real catalyst is H1 FY26 delivery and any Lookers/Lithia update.

Three things worth flagging on PINE specifically:

The −31% EPS downgrade cycle before results is significant context — the market already knew FY25 would disappoint vs original 8.9p expectations, so today's 5.4p print is not a shock. But it also means there's little to upgrade from here on FY25; the debate shifts entirely to FY26 and FY28.

The EPS miss being tax-driven is genuinely important and something a broker note will need to address explicitly — because it means the underlying business generated £8.8m PBT in-line with consensus, and the 5.4p vs 6.0p gap is purely the deferred tax liability from Seez intangibles winding through the P&L. A normalised EPS of ~6.3p would have been a beat. Brokers who model normalised tax rates will frame FY25 as an operational beat, not a miss.

The 232p price vs 654p Sharescope TP is flagged in the sparkline — the price collapse from ~650p to 232p since the Marshalls delay (25 Mar) is embedded in the chart and visible. That's where the real story is today: not the results themselves, but whether management's FY28 reaffirmation is enough to arrest a share that has lost two-thirds of its value in under a month.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The defining catalyst is the explicit full-year upgrade. Q1 2026 revenue of $242.1m is up +18% YoY and +24% QoQ, representing the strongest quarterly trading in recent years and establishing a base that makes the existing FY26 consensus of $780.8m clearly too low. Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will upgrade FY26e revenue by +5–10% to approximately $820–860m, and FY26e EPS by +5–8% to approximately 415–430¢ (vs stale 396.8¢). The primary watch point is Q2 EBITDA given deliberately elevated acquisition spending; if margin stays compressed in Q2, some brokers may trim the EBITDA upgrade. The EPS upgrade is principally revenue-driven and remains robust even at flat margin.

🏁 PLUS is a clear pre-H1 upgrade play with explicit "ahead of expectations" language, Q1 five-year record Customer Income, and an accelerating EPS trajectory. Score: 76/100.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

PROC · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = Q4 full year trading update, 12 weeks ended 29 March 2026. Discloses full FY26 unaudited revenue.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e, pre-RNS): EPS 2.1p · Revenue £82.0m (Note: company compiled consensus footnote states £83.5m revenue, £11.7m EBITDA, £4.8m OP, £2.3m PBT)
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e, pre-RNS): EPS 3.0p · Revenue £91.7m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change full period: +40.0% (1.5p → 2.1p). Series of upgrades: 1.5p → 1.6p (Jun 2025), 1.6p → 1.8p (Sep 2025), 1.8p → 2.1p (Oct 2025). Revenue: £68.8m → £82.0m (+19.2%), with a final nudge to £82.0m Jan 2026. Clear upgrade cycle through the year, now flat for 4+ weeks at 2.1p. 4-week EPS trend: 🟡 FLAT.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg, FY24–FY26 H1): Revenue 42.2% of FY = £34.6m (42.2% × £82.0m). EPS: H1 is structurally negative in all years (PROC is heavily H2-weighted retail); baseline n/a for EPS H1%.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £28.3m · EPS −2.0p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY26 actual £85.5m (RNS-disclosed) − H1 actual £34.1m = H2 actual £51.4m vs FY25 H2 £41.2m = +24.8% YoY (RNS-derived). EPS: FY26e 2.1p − H1 actual −2.0p = implied H2 4.1p vs FY25 H2 3.1p = +32.3% YoY (partially consensus-derived as EPS not disclosed in this update).
  • FX: RNS mentions "significant FX volatility" affecting PBT ("PBT also anticipated to be in line with expectations, after impact of significant FX volatility"). PROC sources products internationally (predominantly Asia/USD). No specific % exposure or rate disclosed in this update. Flagged: FX is a stated PBT headwind but unquantified. Phase 0B: no disclosed prior-year average rate available. Apply missing baseline fallback: FX headwind noted but unquantified. Does not trigger formal penalty without exposure % data. N/A penalty — flagged qualitatively.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY23 H2 −£3.0m net cash / FY24 H2 −£9.8m / FY25 H2 −£4.4m (FY25 YE, net cash) / FY26 H1 £28.9m (net debt including IFRS16 leases) / FY26fc £23.3m (consensus) → RNS discloses net cash £4.4m at FY26 year end (31 Mar 2026) vs consensus fc £23.3m net debt — major positive surprise vs consensus debt figure. ⚠️ Sharescope fc net borrowing £23.3m likely includes IFRS16 lease liabilities (£26.7m at FY25 H1). RNS "net cash" of £4.4m is likely pre-IFRS16. Clarified: RNS states "strengthened balance sheet with net cash position of £4.4m at year end (FY25: net cash of £1.0m) ahead of market expectations." Pre-IFRS16 net cash £4.4m is better than FY25 £1.0m. ND/EBITDA: FY23 3.9x / FY24 3.6x / FY25 4.5x (IFRS16-included) / current 2.6x / FY26fc 2.0x (IFRS16) · Interest cover FY26fc: 2.4x · ND/FCF FY26fc: 12.6x.

IFRS16 gate check: ND/FCF >8x (12.6x FY26fc) ✅ triggered. PROC is discretionary store-based retail. Interest cover 2.4x = <3x ✅ triggered. IFRS16 lease liabilities material. Apply discretionary store-based retail rules. Non-linear EPS downside rules: interest cover <3x + ND/FCF >10x gate met → non-linear EPS downside applicable where relevant. ND/FCF drops to 5.4x FY27 — improving rapidly.

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — pre-IFRS16 net cash positive and improving strongly. IFRS16-included leverage concerning (ND/EBITDA 2.0x FY26fc, interest cover 2.4x), but trajectory is positive. Not 🔴 Leverage elevated in context of the improving cash position. Silent in Phase 5.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

PROC · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Q4 full year trading update)

1. Revenue figures FY26 full year actual (unaudited): £85.5m vs company compiled consensus £83.5m = +£2.0m / +2.4% beat vs consensus. Sharescope FY1 fc £82.0m → beat of +4.3% vs Sharescope figure. Q4 revenue: £18.5m (+19.2% YoY). Full year LFL +11.8%; total +23.0% YoY.

H2 FY26 derived: £85.5m − £34.1m H1 = £51.4m vs FY25 H2 £41.2m = +24.8% YoY.

"Record full year revenue of £85.5m, ahead of market expectations, +23.0% year on year and +11.8% on a like for like basis"

2. EPS / earnings figures No EPS disclosed in trading update (final results expected 24 June 2026). EBITDA: "slightly ahead of market expectations" — consensus £11.7m, RNS implies c.£11.8–12.0m. Operating profit: "in line with market expectations" — consensus £4.8m. PBT: "in line with expectations, after impact of significant FX volatility" — consensus £2.3m; FX ate into PBT, indicating that EBITDA/OP beat did not fully translate to PBT level.

Implied FY26e EPS: no change signal from PBT guidance; EPS 2.1p consensus likely maintained.

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed. Cannot apply quality check. Note: PROC has structurally negative H1 EPS in all historical years; annual EPS is entirely H2-derived. Seasonal pattern is reliable. No non-recurring item disclosed.

3. FY26e EPS bridge (for FY27) (1) New base: FY26 EPS likely ~2.1p (consensus maintained per OP/PBT in-line guidance) (2) Inorganic: New store openings — 13 new stores in FY26 (net 12 after one closure). FY26 store total: 78. New stores are dilutive initially (pre-opening costs, ramp-to-maturity), but 8 in new format. The medium-term case assumes stores reach maturity and contribute meaningfully. No acquisition activity. (3) Organic EBITDA growth: RNS states EBITDA "slightly ahead." FY26e EBITDA ~£11.8m. FY27e consensus £13.8m = +16.9% step-up. Supported by: 100-store target, £100m revenue ambition, 10% OP margin target (current ~5.6%). The step-up is ambitious but underpinned by LFL growth +11.8% in FY26. (4) Interest step-up: Pre-IFRS16 net cash £4.4m — no interest cost concern excluding leases. IFRS16 interest is the cost pressure. Implied FY27e EPS: Sharescope FY2 fc 3.0p (+42.9% from FY26e 2.1p). This is a large step requiring FY27 to benefit from the maturing store estate and LFL momentum continuing. Plausible given the LFL trajectory (+11.8% FY26).

4. Order book / forward work No order book. Retail: 13 new stores opened FY26, total 78. Revenue guidance for FY27: "continue to increase market share." Medium-term ambition: 100 stores, £100m revenue, 10% OP margin. New customer acquisition +25% YoY; L12M active customer base +24%. Paid social revenue +67% Q4.

"Our ongoing store openings, initiatives to increase brand awareness, and disciplined investments to support growth, position us well to deliver on our medium term ambition of 100 stores, £100m revenue and 10% operating profit margin."

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • EBITDA: "slightly ahead of market expectations" (consensus £11.7m → ~£11.8–12.0m)
  • OP: "in line with market expectations" (consensus £4.8m) — note: new store pre-opening costs are dilutive: 13 new stores in FY26 creates higher than normal pre-opening charges and below-maturity revenue in early periods
  • PBT: "in line" but "after impact of significant FX volatility" — FX is absorbing the EBITDA beat. No quantification of FX impact.
  • New format stores (8 of 78): expected to improve store productivity and margins as the estate evolves.
  • RCF increased to £15m (from £10m) post year-end, committed to April 2029 — demonstrates banking confidence and provides working capital headroom for store programme.

6. Capital returns / per-share items No dividend (FY26); FY27e DPS 1.80p (first dividend). Net cash £4.4m vs FY25 £1.0m — improvement of £3.4m pre-IFRS16. Capex: £5.3m in new store openings (FY26).

"Strengthened balance sheet with net cash position of £4.4m at year end (FY25: net cash of £1.0m) ahead of market expectations, after £5.3m of investment capex on new store openings."

7. Qualitative tone "Well positioned to deliver on our medium term ambition of 100 stores, £100m revenue and 10% operating profit margin." Mindful of potential macroeconomic effects of geopolitical instability. Continued market share gains (+13pp Q4, +20pp full year vs UK kitchenware market).

"Whilst we are mindful of the potential macroeconomic effects of any protracted geopolitical instability, we look forward to building on our recent progress and continuing to increase market share as we drive profitable growth."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase (forward-looking): "Position us well to deliver on our medium term ambition of 100 stores, £100m revenue and 10% operating profit margin."

FY26 (current year closing): EBITDA slightly ahead, OP in line, PBT in line after FX. Implicit FY27 message: store rollout continuing, LFL momentum strong.

  • Guidance nature: qualitative only for FY27; medium-term ambition numeric (£100m, 10% OP), not a FY27 EPS guidance
  • Year coverage: medium-term directional, not FY27 explicit
  • Classification: 🟢 Constructive — revenue beat, EBITDA slightly ahead, strong LFL, customer acquisition momentum, medium-term targets reiterated. The combination of a FY revenue beat and positive forward language on market share and store openings clearly exceeds "in line." Provisional points: +6 to +10
  • Divergence check: FY26 revenue beat (+2.4% vs company consensus); FY26 EBITDA slightly ahead; PBT in line after FX. Outlook Constructive. No divergence — beat in current year aligns with Constructive forward guidance.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

PROC · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26
