Revenue H2 YoY: £51.4m vs FY25 H2 £41.2m = +24.8% → 🟢 strong (>+10%) EPS H2 YoY (estimated): ~4.1p vs FY25 H2 3.1p = +32.3% → 🟢 strong (>+10%)

Classification: 🟢 Strong for revenue (RNS-derived); 🟢 Strong for EPS (consensus/estimated-derived).

The H2 revenue delivery of £51.4m is confirmed by the full year RNS-disclosed figure — this is not speculative. The 13 new stores opened in FY26, combined with 11 consecutive quarters of retail LFL growth and ecommerce +18.9%, drove the H2 performance. This is genuine acceleration.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 40.0% upgrade cycle over the full snapshot period — exceptional for a small-cap retailer. Multiple step-ups confirming the recovery thesis (1.5p → 2.1p). Flat for 4 weeks.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT — brokers waiting for this revenue confirmation before updating models.
  • Divergence: Price has fallen from 53p (where consensus upgrades peaked) to 36.6p — a −31% decline during the EPS upgrade cycle. This is an unusual disconnect: strong earnings upgrades but declining price. Likely reflects: (1) macro concerns for discretionary retail; (2) IFRS16 leverage concerns; (3) small/micro cap illiquidity. The revenue beat should partially address concern (1).

5. Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt (IFRS16-inclusive): FY23 H2 −£3.0m (net cash) / FY24 H2 −£9.8m / FY25 H2 −£4.4m / FY26 H1 £28.9m / FY26fc £23.3m (consensus IFRS16-inclusive) · RNS actual FY26 YE pre-IFRS16 net cash: +£4.4m vs FY25 +£1.0m → +£3.4m YoY improvement, ahead of expectations
  • ND/EBITDA (IFRS16): FY23 3.9x / FY24 3.6x / FY25 4.5x / FY26 H1 2.6x / FY26fc 2.0x / FY27fc 1.5x
  • Interest cover (IFRS16 inclusive): FY26fc 2.4x / FY27fc 4.0x
  • ND/FCF: FY26fc 12.6x / FY27fc 5.4x

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — IFRS16 inclusive leverage is real but improving rapidly. Pre-IFRS16 net cash positive and ahead of expectations. Interest cover 2.4x IFRS16-inclusive is tight but trajectory is strong (4.0x FY27). Silent in Phase 5.

Discretionary retail rules overlay: IFRS16 gate met (ND/FCF >8x). Interest cover <3x gate met (<3x at 2.4x FY26fc). Revenue beat translates through to EBITDA at the discretionary retailer drop-through rate. EBITDA "slightly ahead" on +£2m revenue beat: implied drop-through ~£0.1–0.2m on £2m revenue beat at estimated ~10% EBITDA drop-through for PROC (gross margin ~65%, store labour flex ~40–50% of gross). This is consistent with "slightly ahead" language. PBT held back by FX — FX ate into the EBITDA upside.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26e vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26e EPS ~2.1p vs FY25 actual 1.1p → ✅✅ FY26e EPS growing +90.9%
  • FY26e Revenue £85.5m (actual) vs FY25 actual £69.5m → ✅✅ FY26e Revenue growing +23.0%

Step 2 — FY27e vs FY26e:

  • FY27e EPS 3.0p vs FY26e ~2.1p → ✅✅ FY27e EPS growing +42.9%
  • FY27e Revenue £91.7m vs FY26e £85.5m → ✅✅ FY27e Revenue growing +7.3%

Both steps: all growing. ✅✅ Strong.

6. Structural / One-off Flags

New store openings — structural revenue/cost phasing: 13 stores opened FY26; pre-opening costs and below-maturity revenue suppressed OP below EBITDA. 8 stores in new format. As stores mature, the margin should recover and approach the medium-term 10% OP margin target. This is a deliberate investment programme creating near-term OP dilution but medium-term earnings enhancement.

Delicious magazine content acquisition: 9,000+ recipes and imagery acquired from UK operators of Delicious magazine (in liquidation). Non-material cost; meaningful digital content asset for ecommerce driving. Incremental social/content tailwind.

FX structural headwind: PBT absorbing "significant FX volatility" — PROC sources products in USD/Asian currencies. USD strength in H2 FY26 has been a structural headwind. No hedging policy disclosed. This is an ongoing risk for FY27 if USD remains elevated vs GBP.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

PROC · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/8/26

[Note: PROC year end is 31/3/26 — correction from mis-typed Aug above.]

#1 Driver — FY26 revenue £85.5m: +2.4% beat vs company consensus, +4.3% vs Sharescope: This is the dominant positive signal. For a small-cap retailer that has been in an upgrade cycle, confirming the revenue beat firmly validates the bull case. The combination of +11.8% LFL and +23% total revenue significantly outperforms the broader UK kitchenware market by 20 percentage points. This is not a commodity beat — it reflects genuine market share gain, customer acquisition momentum (+25% new customers), and a maturing store estate.

#2 Driver — Net cash £4.4m ahead of expectations; RCF extended to £15m: The balance sheet surprise is important in the context of IFRS16-adjusted leverage concerns. Showing pre-IFRS16 net cash of £4.4m (vs expected net debt at some broker models) and securing an enlarged £15m RCF for 3 years demonstrates financial credibility and removes a key bear point. For a store rollout story, balance sheet confidence is critical.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e Revenue: upgrade to £85.5m from £82.0m (Sharescope) / £83.5m (company consensus) — +4.3% and +2.4% respectively. This is a confirmed actual, so brokers must update models.
  • FY26e EPS: hold or minor upgrade — OP in line, EBITDA slightly ahead, PBT in line after FX. EPS consensus 2.1p likely maintained. Possible minor upgrade if brokers credit EBITDA beat: 2.1p → 2.2–2.3p (+3–10%). FX absorbed the upside, keeping EPS broadly flat.
  • FY27e Revenue: upgrade — base now £85.5m (vs £82.0m modelled); store target 100 units, LFL momentum. FY27e revenue upgrades likely +3–5% (£91.7m → £94–96m).
  • FY27e EPS: upgrade — higher revenue base + maturing store contribution + continued LFL. FY27e EPS likely upgraded from 3.0p to 3.2–3.4p (+7–13%).
  • Target prices: raise — consensus TP 53p vs current 36.6p (already 44.8% upside). Post-upgrade, TPs may move to 55–65p range (+4–23% TP uplift). First dividend flagged for FY27 (1.80p) will attract income-oriented investor base.

Conservative guidance read-through: Medium-term targets ("100 stores, £100m revenue, 10% OP margin") are not conservative guidance language. They are aspirational targets. However, having delivered +23% revenue growth in FY26 and opening 13 stores, the trajectory toward £100m in FY27 (£91.7m consensus) is realistic. The path to 10% OP margin remains the more challenging element given new store pre-opening dilution and FX headwinds.

Key risk: FX volatility is the stated risk — "significant FX volatility" has already impacted FY26 PBT. PROC sources products internationally; USD exposure is likely 25–35% of COGS. If USD remains elevated or strengthens further, FY27 PBT will face a headwind even with strong revenue growth. The FX risk is explicitly unhedged or only partially hedged (no hedging policy disclosed). This is the bear point brokers will emphasise.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = hold/minor upgrade (revenue confirms, EPS consensus maintained). Tone = 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — consistent.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

🔴 FX headwind unquantified — "significant FX volatility" stated to have offset PBT benefit−5
🔴 IFRS16 leverage: ND/FCF 12.6x FY26fc; interest cover 2.4x — constrains valuation−5
🔴 New store dilution: 13 openings in FY26 suppress near-term OP margin; below medium-term 10% target−4
🔴 Price re-rating gap: stock down −31% since upgrade cycle started at 53p — narrative challenge−4

Net: +14+12+10+8+6+5−2−2−5−5−4−4 = +33 additive score vs 100 floor/ceiling = 71

Para 1 — Headline numbers: PROC delivered FY26 revenue of £85.5m — beating company compiled consensus of £83.5m by +2.4% and Sharescope FY1 fc by +4.3%, marking the highest revenue in the company's history and +23.0% YoY growth (+11.8% LFL). The single definitive catalyst is the H2 FY26 revenue confirmation: H2 delivered £51.4m (+24.8% YoY vs FY25 H2 £41.2m) — a genuinely strong half-year driven by 13 new stores (net 12), ecommerce LFL +21.2%, and the acceleration of paid social/content strategy. The group also outperformed the UK kitchenware market by +20 percentage points across the full year — a market share gain of compelling magnitude. EBITDA is "slightly ahead" of the £11.7m consensus and OP/PBT are "in line", with FX absorbing the EBITDA upside at the PBT level.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the scored signal is H2 momentum: classified 🟢 Strong (RNS-derived for revenue). Phase 3.2 H1 tracking was retrospectively approximately in line (−0.6pp deviation, 🟡 IN LINE — not scored in Phase 5 per pre-FY routing). The upgrade case is resilient because: (1) the revenue beat is structural (LFL growth + new stores), not one-off; (2) net cash of £4.4m (ahead of expectations) confirms the store investment programme is self-funding without leverage deterioration; (3) the RCF extension to £15m through April 2029 at higher levels than previously ensures the 100-store programme has adequate liquidity. Downside risk is contained by the LFL momentum (+11.8% full year) and market share gains — in a soft UK macro, consistent outperformance by +20pp is a structural advantage, not cyclical luck. FX is the primary unresolved risk: "significant FX volatility" impacted FY26 PBT, and PROC's unhedged or partially-hedged USD sourcing exposure means any further USD strengthening directly suppresses FY27 PBT.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are expected to upgrade FY26e revenue to £85.5m (confirmed actual), maintain FY26e EPS at ~2.1p, and upgrade FY27e revenue by +3–5% (toward £94–96m) and FY27e EPS by +7–13% (3.0p → 3.2–3.4p) on the higher revenue base and maturing store economics. Target prices are expected to rise from the consensus 53p to the 55–65p range — the current 36.6p price represents 50–78% upside to revised TPs. The first dividend (FY27e 1.80p) will attract a new investor constituency. The key constraint on a higher score is the unquantified FX headwind at PBT level (which prevented the EBITDA beat from flowing to EPS) and the IFRS16-adjusted leverage profile (ND/FCF 12.6x FY26fc), which caps the valuation multiple brokers are willing to apply. 🏁 Strong upgrade bias for FY27e estimates and target prices; the combination of a confirmed revenue beat, record trading performance, and net cash surprise is the best possible pre-full-results signal PROC could have issued.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

PRV · Q4 · AGM Statement · FY26 · Year end: 30/11/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 AGM Trading Update

1. Revenue figures 4-month trading (Nov 2025–Mar 2026): constant currency revenue growth of +5% vs prior period. No absolute figure disclosed. No H1 guidance or revenue range given. No comparison to FY26e consensus.

"The Group has performed in line with expectations in the first four months of the year, delivering constant currency revenue growth of 5%."

2. EPS / earnings figures No EPS or PBT figures disclosed. No H1 EPS guidance. RNS is qualitative only.

3. FY26e EPS bridge No FY1 actual disclosed (this is a pre-H1 update, FY25 results were separately released). Per Sharescope: FY25 actual EPS = 42.2p (current H1 20.0p + H2 22.2p). FY26e consensus = 43.4p. Bridge components for FY27 (FY2): (1) New base = 42.2p actual FY25; (2) Drache acquisition (completed 12 Jan 2026) — partial-year contribution in FY26 (c.10 months), full year in FY27 = incremental annualisation uplift; (3) Organic EBITDA growth — FY26e EBITDA £34.0m vs FY25 EBITDA implied £31.3m (15.7+15.7 — note Sharescope shows current H2 EBITDA £32.8m which appears anomalous vs pattern; likely a data artefact — flagged ⚠️). Using FY26fc EBITDA £34.0m and diluted share count ~46.1m, the FY27 step to 46.5p (+7.1% vs FY26e 43.4p) implies modest organic growth plus Drache full-year contribution. No interest step-up delta required (net cash deepening). Implied FY27e EPS revision vs stale FY27 consensus: FY27e = 46.5p; if Drache annualises as indicated by the investment case, this figure likely captures the acquisition fully. No stale consensus gap identified.

4. Order book / forward work No specific order book figure disclosed. Aerospace order books described as "strong" (qualitative). Drache integration "consistent with the pre-acquisition investment case."

"Aerospace order books remain strong, noting that the timing of delivery can be affected by changes in customer scheduling."

5. Margin, profitability, cost signals No margin guidance. RNS notes: (i) Petrochemical sales "lower compared with a strong prior period" with subdued European conditions "throughout 2026" — mild headwind signal; (ii) Aluminium/superalloys demand "firm"; (iii) new £5.5m aluminium cast house line "on track for commissioning in H1 2026" — capex completion, capacity add; (iv) Drache integration "progressing well." No forward margin commentary.

"Petrochemical sales, which can be lumpy, are lower compared with a strong prior period, and conditions in the European petrochemical market are expected to remain subdued throughout 2026."

6. Capital returns / per-share items No dividend change signalled. No buyback. FY26e DPS consensus 7.00p; FY27e 7.40p.

7. Qualitative tone "Full year expectations remain unchanged." Drache integration on track. Middle East monitoring flagged (input prices, macro uncertainty). M&A pipeline described as "interesting prospects currently being evaluated." Capital Markets Event announced for 15 October 2026.

"The Board's expectations of the Group's full year performance remain unchanged, supported by a diversified customer base, strong recurring revenue streams and disciplined operational management."

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "The Board's expectations of the Group's full year performance remain unchanged."

  • Guidance nature: qualitative only — no numeric uplift, no range, no "not less than" language
  • Year coverage: FY26 full year only
  • Classification: 🟡 In-line — standard "unchanged expectations" language with no upgrade or downgrade signal. Petrochemical headwind caveated but no quantification. Drache on track adds mild positive texture but is already in consensus.
  • Provisional points: 0 to +3
  • Divergence check: No current-year result disclosed in this update — no divergence to flag. The AGM update covers trading only, not results; no beat/miss to compare against guidance tone.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

PRV · Q4 · AGM Statement · FY26 · Year end: 30/11/26

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check: Sharescope H2 fields vs explicit FY actuals:

  • FY24: H1 £90.6m + H2 £85.5m = £176.1m vs stated FY £176.0m → £0.1m rounding — ✅ acceptable
  • FY25: H1 £94.6m + H2 £98.0m = £192.6m → matches stated FY £192.6m ✅

⚠️ Sharescope EBITDA current H2 = £32.8m — this implies FY26 H1+H2 EBITDA would be £15.7m + £32.8m = £48.5m, far above FY26fc £34.0m. This field is almost certainly a data artefact or misrouted Drache fair value entry. Flagged — not used in calculations.

EPS growth trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — FY23→FY24 +12.0%, FY24→FY25 +3.8%, FY25→FY26e +12.4%. Step-deceleration then re-acceleration; driven partly by Drache acquisition contribution in FY26e.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Data source gate: This is a pre-H1 AGM update. The RNS discloses a 4-month (Nov 2025–Mar 2026) constant currency revenue growth rate of +5% but no absolute H1 revenue or EPS figure. Condition (4) — YoY % growth expectation — is met for revenue (partial period only, not full H1). However: the 4-month period (Nov–Mar) covers most of the H1 window (H1 ends ~May 2026), but is not the full H1. Deriving a full H1 number from a partial-period growth rate would require assumptions about the remaining ~1.5 months of H1. This does not satisfy condition (1), (2), or (3), and condition (4) strictly requires a YoY% for the H1 period as a whole — a 4-month partial-period rate is insufficient for a clean derivation.

Revenue: UNTRACKABLE — 4-month partial update only; not a complete H1 figure. Cannot fire signal.

  • Baseline for H1 results date: 3yr avg 49.4% × £218.6m = £108.0m
  • Buy trigger threshold: £108.0m × 1.015 = £109.6m

EPS: UNTRACKABLE — no H1 EPS figure or guidance in RNS.

  • Buy trigger threshold: 22.4p × 1.015 = 22.7p
  • Sell trigger threshold: 22.4p × 0.985 = 22.1p
  • Watch date: H1 results 29 June 2026

Implied H1 from FY guidance (indicative only): RNS confirms full year "in line with expectations" — FY26e consensus £218.6m stands. Applying 3yr avg H1% to FY26e: implied H1 = £108.0m. No deviation signal — consensus FY is unchanged, implied H1 = baseline. Signal: 🟡 neither buy nor caution from this alone.

H2 EPS burden: FY26e 43.4p − 3yr avg H1 implied 22.4p = H2 required 21.0p vs historical H2 avg (FY23–FY25: 16.6p / 16.9p / 19.1p = avg 17.5p). H2 burden HIGHER than historical average by +3.5p — consistent with Drache acquisition contribution expected to be H2-weighted (acquired Jan 2026, full integration in H2). Flagged as acquisition-driven, not organic pressure.

Historical hit rate: Of last 3 years — insufficient trackable H1 data from prior AGM statements to assess hit rate for this metric. N/A.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 base: RNS confirms FY26 "in line with expectations" → use FY26e consensus. No H1 actuals known yet.

Using 3yr avg H1 split as proxy:

  • Implied FY26 H2 Revenue = £218.6m − £108.0m = £110.6m (consensus-derived, H1 seasonality-assumed)
  • Prior H2 actuals: FY23 £90.3m, FY24 £85.5m, FY25 £98.0m → 3yr avg £91.3m
  • Implied H2 YoY vs FY25 H2: +£12.6m / +12.9% → 🟢 moderate (0–10% boundary; +12.9% is at strong threshold)
  • Implied FY26 H2 EPS = 43.4p − 22.4p = 21.0p (consensus-derived)
  • Prior H2 actuals: FY23 16.6p, FY24 16.9p, FY25 19.1p → 3yr avg 17.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY vs FY25 H2: +1.9p / +9.9% → 🟡 moderate (just below +10% strong threshold)

Classification: 🟡 Moderate for both metrics (consensus-derived — confirm on H1 results 29 June 2026).

Note: Drache acquired Jan 2026 adds a full H2 contribution in FY26 (vs partial in H1). The step-up in H2 burden vs historical is explicable by acquisition. The "in line with expectations" language suggests brokers have already modelled this.

Profit warning feasibility gate: Not applicable — no H1 miss (H1 UNTRACKABLE). No negative H1 deviation to trigger the gate.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: FY26e EPS net change +9.0% over full snapshot period (+3.7p, from 39.7p to 43.4p). The dominant upgrade event was mid-February 2026 (39.7p → 43.5p), coinciding with FY25 full year results publication. Prior to that event, EPS was flat for 9 months. Post-event: minor 0.1p trim in last 2 weeks. Net: upgrade cycle completed post-FY25 results; now stable.
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (minor: 43.5p → 43.4p — one broker trimming, likely not structural)
  • Revenue trend: Strong revision upward in mid-Feb 2026 (£199.1m → £217.9m, +9.4%), reflecting Drache acquisition modelling. Stable since. FY26e now £218.6m.
  • Divergence: Price action has tracked upgrades through early 2026 (stock moved 808p → 933p alongside the Feb upgrade). Price at 750p on 10 Apr — stock has pulled back from the 933p post-upgrade high, suggesting some market scepticism or sector rotation, despite unchanged consensus.

5. Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt/(cash): 3y ago (FY23 H2) −£6.1m / 2y ago (FY24 H2) +£8.0m / 1y ago (FY25 H2) −£10.9m / current H1 (FY26 H1) −£2.8m / FY26fc −£45.5m / FY27fc −£40.8m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY23 −0.30x / FY24 −0.00x / FY25 +0.10x / current −0.30x / FY26fc −1.30x / FY27fc −1.10x
  • Interest cover: current 20.7x / FY26fc 15.8x / FY27fc 19.7x
  • ND/FCF: FY26fc −3.3x / FY27fc −2.3x

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — deepening net cash position through FY26/27 on consensus. Drache (£X acquisition cost not disclosed in this RNS) funded from balance sheet; no covenant concern visible. Interest cover 15.8x FY26fc is robust. No Phase 5 scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26e vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26e EPS 43.4p vs FY25 actual 38.6p → ✅✅ FY26e EPS growing +12.4% vs prior year actual
  • FY26e Revenue £218.6m vs FY25 actual £192.6m → ✅✅ FY26e Revenue growing +13.5% vs prior year actual

Step 2 — FY27e vs FY26e:

  • FY27e EPS 46.5p vs FY26e 43.4p → ✅✅ FY27e EPS growing +7.1% vs FY26e
  • FY27e Revenue £227.3m vs FY26e £218.6m → ✅✅ FY27e Revenue growing +4.0% vs FY26e

Both steps: all growing. No flags.

6. Structural / One-off Flags

Drache acquisition (Jan 2026): Creates a structural break in H2 phasing — Drache contributes 10+ months in FY26 but first full year in FY27. Historical H2 seasonality baselines understated relative to FY26 actuals. Any H2 beat vs historical must be discounted for the acquisition contribution.

"The integration of Drache, acquired on 12 January 2026, is progressing well after three months with the Group and trading is consistent with the pre-acquisition investment case."

Petrochemical headwind: Explicitly guided as subdued "throughout 2026." Qualitative only, no quantum. Net drag within Aerospace & Industrial. Partially offset by nuclear and new contract wins referenced elsewhere.

New aluminium cast house line: £5.5m capex project on track for H1 2026 commissioning. Capacity addition — incremental revenue contribution from H2 FY26 / FY27 onwards.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

PRV · Q4 · AGM Statement · FY26 · Year end: 30/11/26

#1 Driver — FY in-line confirmation: The dominant signal is the unambiguous "in line with expectations" statement covering FY26. Coming 4 months into the year, and shortly after a material upgrade cycle in February, this is the most important data point for brokers. It confirms the upgraded consensus is achievable and removes near-term downside risk, but provides no incremental upgrade catalyst.

#2 Driver — Drache integration on track: The confirmation that Drache is "consistent with the pre-acquisition investment case" validates the FY26/FY27 EPS step-up assumptions brokers have already modelled. This is moderately positive but already embedded in post-Feb consensus.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e Revenue: hold — "in line" language, no new data point to move numbers. Possible minor adjustments around petrochemical mix (−1 to 0%), fully within existing range. Expected range: −1% to 0%.
  • FY26e EPS: hold — no earnings disclosure. Petrochemical softness partially offset by nuclear/aluminium strength. Expected range: 0% to +1%.
  • FY27e Revenue: hold — Drache full-year contribution already in models. Expected: 0% change.
  • FY27e EPS: hold — no new information to move FY27 estimates materially. Expected: 0% to +1%.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers likely to hold target prices. Consensus TP £9.33; current price 750p implies 24.4% upside. Stock has pulled back ~20% from the post-results high of 933p. Brokers unlikely to cut TPs on an in-line AGM statement; some may reaffirm existing TPs. No recommendation change warranted.

Conservative guidance read-through: "In line with expectations" at an AGM statement 4 months into a year where Drache is integrating as planned is broadly reassuring. However, it is standard language — brokers will not interpret this as a deliberately cautious "not less than" type of statement. No upgrade cycle signal from this language alone.

Key risk: Petrochemical headwind is the only explicitly negatively guided item, and it is guided to persist "throughout 2026." The quantum is not disclosed, but Aerospace & Industrial is the largest division. Any further deterioration in European petrochemical conditions, or delays to the aluminium cast house commissioning, could pressure H2 slightly. Additionally, the 4-week EPS tick down (43.5p → 43.4p) may indicate one broker has already trimmed slightly on petrochemical caution.

"Petrochemical sales, which can be lumpy, are lower compared with a strong prior period, and conditions in the European petrochemical market are expected to remain subdued throughout 2026."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = hold. Tone = 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — consistent with hold.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — in-line AGM statement with no new upgrade catalyst; Drache confirmed; petrochemical drag acknowledged; no numbers.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

54/100 · Confidence: 48–60 · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

🔴 Stock 20% off post-results high — market scepticism not resolved by this update−5
🔴 Implied H2 EPS burden above historical avg — Drache-driven but not fully confirmed organic−3

Total: +54

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The dominant signal from this AGM update is the confirmation that PRV is "in line with expectations" after four months of FY26 trading, delivering +5% constant currency revenue growth. There is no absolute figure to compare against FY26e consensus of £218.6m, and no EPS disclosure. The statement's significance lies in what it validates rather than what it adds: a broker consensus that was materially upgraded in mid-February 2026 (FY26e EPS: 39.7p → 43.5p, Revenue: £199m → £218m) following FY25 full year results is confirmed as achievable. The single definitive catalyst — Drache acquisition integration — is confirmed "consistent with the pre-acquisition investment case," which underpins the step-change in FY26/FY27 EPS models. There is no incremental upside catalyst here.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: With H1 UNTRACKABLE (no figures disclosed), the pre-H1 scoring framework cannot fire a tracking signal. The 3yr avg seasonal H1 baseline is £108.0m revenue and 22.4p EPS; buy triggers sit at £109.6m and 22.7p respectively — these should be applied immediately on the H1 results announcement of 29 June 2026. The implied H2 consensus-derived burden (21.0p EPS, +9.9% YoY vs FY25 H2) is above historical averages, but the structural explanation is clear: Drache was acquired January 2026 and contributes a full H2 in FY26 while H1 is only partial. The revenue trajectory is unambiguously accelerating (FY23 +2%, FY24 +9.4%, FY25e +13.5%), and the balance sheet provides ample capacity for further M&A. The explicit petrochemical drag — guided to persist throughout 2026 — is the primary downside risk to H2, but the division's diversity (nuclear robust, aluminium firm) partially offsets it. Downside is contained as long as the Drache investment case holds and aerospace timing delays remain temporary.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: No forecast revisions are expected from this AGM statement. FY26e EPS 43.4p and revenue £218.6m should be held unchanged — the "in line" language is a hold signal, not an upgrade trigger. FY27e EPS 46.5p likewise undisturbed. Target prices (consensus 933p vs current 750p, implying +24.4% upside) are unlikely to be revised; brokers may reaffirm rather than act. The stock's 20% pullback from the post-FY25 high is unexplained by fundamentals alone and may represent sector/market rotation. The key watch point is H1 results on 29 June 2026: if H1 revenue clears £109.6m and EPS clears 22.7p, a buy signal fires and the upgrade cycle may restart; failure to clear those thresholds given the Drache contribution would be a negative surprise. 🏁 Hold with a clear near-term catalyst date — this is a score-maintenance statement; the upgrade case has already been made and must now be confirmed in H1 numbers on 29 June.

QTX — Quartix Holdings PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Revenue disaggregation from RNS: UK/EI £19.9m (55.7% of £35.7m), France £9.2m (25.8%), Other Europe £3.3m (9.3%), USA £3.3m (9.2%). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30% of revenues (France EUR: 25.8%). Phase 0B not triggered. No penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 11.6p · Revenue £36.4m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 14.6p · Revenue £41.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 10.5p → 11.6p = +1.1p (+10.5%). Steady upgrade path: 10.5p (May) → 10.7p (Jul) → 10.9p (Oct) → 11.3p (Nov) → 11.6p (Jan 2026), then flat. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 11.6p / £36.4m for 10 weeks). Revenue net change: £36.0m → £36.4m = +£0.4m (+1.1%). Direction positive throughout year.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.0% of FY = £17.8m · EPS 31.0% of FY = 3.6p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue £16.1m · EPS 4.4p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus £36.4m − H1 actual £17.6m = implied H2 £18.8m vs prior-year H2 £16.3m → +15.3% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 11.6p − 5.5p = 6.1p vs prior-year H2 9.8p → −37.8% YoY — note: H1 EPS (5.5p) already materially exceeds prior H1 (4.4p) and prior H2 (9.8p). The negative implied H2 YoY is an artefact of H1 being front-loaded this year vs prior year.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (Audited results for year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual vs consensus

FY 2025 revenue: £35.7m, up 12% vs £31.8m in FY2024. Restated 2024 figure (IAS 16 policy change).

vs FY1 consensus of £36.4m: miss of £0.7m (−1.9%) — small miss, within rounding. On constant currency basis: also +12%.

"Group revenue for the year increased by 12% to £35.7m (2024: £31.8m). Revenue growth on a constant currency basis, using applicable exchanges rate at 31 December 2025, was also 12%."

2. EPS / Earnings — FY actual vs consensus

Diluted EPS: 13.17p, up 25% vs 10.51p in FY2024 (restated). Basic EPS: 13.18p, up 25% vs 10.58p in FY2024 (restated).

vs FY1 consensus of 11.6p: beat of +1.57p (+13.5%). Significant earnings beat.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate 2025: 26.4%. Underlying effective tax rate (excluding prior year adjustments): 22.9%. Stated normalised rate context: 2024 restated rate was 20.7%; 2025 rate is 26.4%. Difference from 22.9% underlying: +3.5pp above normalised rate — just above the 3pp threshold. The higher 2025 rate reflects policy change impacts. Restated EPS at 22.9% effective rate: PBT £8.67m × (1 − 22.9%) = £6.69m profit. Shares 48.43m → restated EPS = ~13.82p. The headline 13.17p EPS is actually slightly conservative vs a normalised tax rate — no 🚨 required; if anything, EPS quality is clean/conservative.

3. ARR / Forward Indicator

ARR increased by £4.5m (+14%) to £37.0m — a record growth in this measure, 25% above FY2024 ARR growth of £3.6m. ARR exceeds annual revenue (£35.7m) — highly positive forward indicator.

"The Group's ARR increased by £4.5m (+14%) during the Period, representing an increase of 25% over the growth achieved in 2024 (£3.6m on constant currency)."

4. EBITDA / Profitability

EBITDA: £13.2m, up 23% (2024: £10.7m restated). EBITDA margin: 36.9% (2024: 33.6%). Adjusted EBIT: £8.8m, up 38%. Gross margin: 73.2% (2024: 71.6%).

"In 2025, under the revised accounting policy, EBITDA increased by 23% on a comparable basis to £13.2m (2024: £10.7m). Adjusted EBIT for the year increased by 38% to £8.8m (2024: £6.4m)."

5. Free Cash Flow / Balance Sheet

Free cash flow: £5.2m (2024: £2.6m), up 101%. Net cash: £5.6m (2024: £3.1m). Significant FCF improvement despite 4G France upgrade costs (~£1.0m), restructuring (~£0.4m) and pre-payment of £0.7m corporation tax. Clean balance sheet — no debt.

"Free cash flow (cash flow from operations after tax and investing activities), was £5.2m (2024: £2.6m), despite significant outflows in the year for the 4G upgrade programme in France (approximately £1.0m), restructuring costs in the first half (approx. £0.4m); and a pre-payment of £0.7m in corporation tax made in December."

6. Dividend

Total dividend: 10.0p (2024: 4.50p). Interim 2.5p paid September 2025. Final proposed: 7.5p (2024: 3.00p). Dividend yield ~4.4% on average price. Massive dividend increase signals confidence.

"This results in a total dividend of 10p per share for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, representing a yield of 3.6% based on the closing share price for 2025, or 4.4% based on the average share price for the year."

7. Accounting policy change (IAS 16)

FRC-prompted reclassification of tracking units as PPE (IAS 16) rather than contract cost assets (IFRS 15). Applied retrospectively. Prior year 2024 restated. Effect on P&L: modest (EPS +0.73p in 2024 post-restatement). The 2025 EPS of 13.17p is on the restated, cleaner accounting basis.

8. KPI highlights

New fleet subscriptions: +7% to 79,576. Subscription base: +11% to 333,922. NRR: 98.1% (2024: 95.7%). Italy ARR +43%, Spain +35% — continental acceleration.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "The outlook for 2026 is very encouraging" — qualitative only. "Closing ARR was higher than Group revenue for the year, and this augurs well for the achievement of our financial goals for 2026." No numeric FY2026 guidance. One year forward. Confident qualitative language supported by record ARR growth.
  • No upgrade-triggering numeric language. But the combination of: (a) 13.5% EPS beat, (b) ARR > revenue (strong forward visibility), (c) record ARR growth, and (d) "very encouraging" outlook — this is upgrade-triggering in practice even if not numeric.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — record ARR growth, 13.5% EPS beat, ARR exceeding revenue, and confident outlook. Provisional points: +13.

Divergence check: Current year beat (EPS +13.5%) + Constructive/positive outlook = aligned. No divergence.

The beat is broad-based and clean: EBITDA +23% to £13.2m, Adjusted EBIT +38% to £8.8m, FCF +101% to £5.2m. Revenue of £35.7m (+12% YoY) was marginally shy of consensus (£36.4m, −1.9%) but this is a rounding miss wholly overwhelmed by the profitability outperformance. The key number brokers will anchor on is the 13.17p EPS, which forces immediate consensus revision from the stale 11.6p.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 EPS tracking signal of +16.4pp above seasonal baseline (5.5p vs 3.6p expected) was the strongest possible pre-result indicator, and the FY actuals confirmed it. The bear case for downgrade is limited: NRR of 98.1% (improving towards 100% target) means existing customers are growing spend, reducing dependence on new acquisition. ARR of £37.0m exceeds FY revenue — meaning the business enters 2026 with contracted future revenue already above its 2025 total. The 4G France upgrade is 66% complete (17,000 units remain of 50,000) and on track for end-2026 — removing a £1.3m cost headwind. Italy ARR +43%, Spain +35% suggest European expansion is accelerating at scale, providing geographic diversification as UK market matures.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Expect FY26 EPS upgrades from 11.6p to 12.5–13.5p (+8–16%), with revenue revised from £36.4m to £39–41m. FY27 EPS likely moves from 14.6p to 15.5–17.0p (+6–16%). With the stock at 244p, post-upgrade consensus TP of 400p+ implies 60–70% upside — the valuation case is compelling but thinly covered (single broker), meaning re-rating requires index inclusion or wider research initiation. The main watch point is FY26 execution: can the company sustain 12%+ revenue growth as the UK subscription base matures and Germany remains soft? 🏁 Strong upgrade cycle: clean 13.5% EPS beat, record ARR growth, FCF doubling, 122% dividend increase — brokers will raise materially across all metrics; valuation re-rating probable if execution sustains. Score 84/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

QTX · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026, 3 months ended 31 March 2026)

1. Revenue / financial performance vs consensus:

  • "Revenue and profit are in line with achievement of market expectations for the year." Company discloses consensus: revenue £40.3m, Adjusted EBIT £10.1m, FCF £4.7m.
  • No H1 revenue figure disclosed in the trading update. Revenue tracking is untrackable from this RNS.
  • Q1 ARR: £38.6m (cc basis, +£1.6m in Q1, +£4.1m TTM = +12% TTM).
  • Q1 ARR growth = £1.6m vs Q1 2025 ARR growth (TTM growth £4.1m / 4 quarters ≈ ~£1.0-1.1m per quarter average, but Q1 2025 was "particularly strong" — per RNS: "Q1 ARR growth is around 20% lower than the ARR growth achieved in the same period of the prior year").
  • Q1 2025 ARR growth: implied ~£2.0m (i.e., Q1 2026 £1.6m = 80% of ~£2.0m prior year Q1).

"Revenue and profit are in line with achievement of market expectations for the year."

2. ARR / forward metrics:

  • ARR: £38.6m at 31 Mar 2026 (+12% TTM, +£4.1m). ARR coverage of FY26 rev consensus = 95.8%.
  • Net Revenue Retention: improved from 95.7% to 98.1% (12 months to 31 Mar 2026). Material improvement — less churn, more upsell.
  • New business contribution to Q1 ARR: £1.1m of the £1.6m Q1 growth.
  • New customers acquired Q1: 2,021 (−8% vs Q1 2025). New subscriptions: 19,301 (−13% vs Q1 2025).
  • TTM: customer base +8% to 33,443; subscription base +9% to 339,491.
  • Italy: ARR +39%, Spain +32%, Germany +45% — continental European growth remains strong.
  • UK/EI: ARR +8% TTM, new subs −28% Q1 YoY (significant deceleration).
  • France: ARR +14% TTM, new subs −10% Q1 YoY.
  • USA: ARR +5% TTM, new subs −25% Q1 YoY — slowest growth market.

"ARR is the key forward-looking measure of growth for the Company and an important indicator of shareholder value."

EPS bridge FY26e:

  • New base: FY25 actual EPS 9.8p (Sharescope "current FY").
  • The FY26e consensus jump to 16.2p (+65% vs FY25 9.8p) implies brokers have already factored in a major step-change. This cannot be explained by organic ARR growth alone (+12% TTM). The jump in consensus from 11.6p to 16.2p in late March/early April 2026 (28 Mar: 14.6p → 04 Apr: 16.2p) likely reflects FY25 full year results publication and a major one-time item or accounting change.
  • ⚠️ The EBITDA fc of £14.9m vs FY25 "current" of £3.7m + £3.7m = £7.4m (H1+H2 derived) is a massive step-change that is inconsistent with organic ARR growth. The stated adj EBIT consensus for FY26 = £10.1m vs implied FY25 adj EBIT. This needs investigation but cannot be verified without FY25 results RNS. Most likely explanation: FY26 includes a significant reduction in capitalised development costs or a one-time cost normalisation. The ARR-based EPS upgrade (see memory: "For subscription/ARR-model businesses, triangulate whether H2 ARR momentum held vs H1 even when the RNS only discloses a year-end figure") is worth noting: Q1 TTM ARR growth of +12%; however Q1 2026 new ARR of £1.6m was 20% below Q1 2025 — H1 ARR growth is decelerating vs the prior year strong comparatives.
  • Implied FY26 EPS bridge from ARR growth alone: ARR growth of 12% on £34.5m base (start TTM) → incremental revenue ~£4.1m → at ~25% EBIT margin drop-through → +£1.0m EBIT → +0.8p EPS. Plus NRR improvement from 95.7% to 98.1% → reduced churn saves revenue. This gives modest organic uplift. The step to 16.2p must reflect a structural cost item or depreciation change in the broker model, not purely revenue growth.

3. Order book / visibility:

  • ARR £38.6m as % of FY26 revenue consensus £40.3m = 95.8% — exceptional forward visibility.
  • NRR 98.1% (up from 95.7%) — churn rate has improved materially. "Further improvement in this measure remains a management focus."

4. FCF / cash:

  • Q1 FCF: £2.7m (strong). £0.55m from tax refund (R&D, non-recurring); £0.35m from delayed Q1 tax payment clearing in April. So normalised FCF = £2.7m − £0.55m − £0.35m = £1.8m — still healthy.
  • Closing cash: £8.2m. Net of timing items: effective ~£5.7m.
  • £1.1m UK corporation tax expected in Q2 (delayed from Q1).
  • Full-year FCF consensus: £4.7m. Q1 normalised ~£1.8m = on track for ~£7.2m annualised (above consensus).

5. 4G upgrade programme:

  • France 4G upgrade "on schedule to conclude this year" — removes a customer retention risk for the rest of FY26 and into FY27.
  • UK 2G replacement continuing per 2025 Annual Report schedule.
  • These are neutral/mildly positive — previously known.

6. Qualitative tone: "The Company has made a solid start to 2026... confident of achieving market expectations for the year." In-line with consensus; no upgrade. Q1 new business was "around 20% lower" than Q1 2025 — explicitly flagged. But TTM metrics all positive. No quantitative FY guidance beyond "in line with market expectations."

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

"Confident of achieving market expectations for the year" — explicit in-line statement, numeric (company discloses consensus: £40.3m rev, £10.1m adj EBIT, £4.7m FCF). No upgrade language. Q1 new subscription weakness (-13%) and customer acquisition (-8%) are headwinds, offset by NRR improvement and ARR coverage.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — in-line confirmation with no upgrade trigger, partially offset by acknowledged Q1 new business shortfall. Provisional points: +1.

Divergence: Q1 ARR growth tracking 20% below Q1 2025, but full-year confidence maintained and NRR improving. Mild divergence: new business decelerating but churn falling. Flag as neutral — the NRR improvement partially compensates for new business weakness. No Beat quality flag required.

scorecards.analysisText:
RNWH

Phase 0A — Routing

Pre-H1 mode confirmed. Q4. FY1 = FY26 (year end 30/9/26). Prior year = FY25. FY2 = FY27.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

No Currency Movements section in RNS. All revenues GBP-denominated (UK infrastructure services). No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Phase 0B: skip. No penalty.

Phase 1 — Data Context

RNWH · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

  • Routing: Pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results / pre-H1 trading update. FY1 = FY26, year end 30/9/26.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 71.1p · Revenue £1,185.8m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 76.2p · Revenue £1,246.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: Net EPS change over full snapshot period: +11.3% (63.9p → 71.1p). Major upgrade event: late Nov 2025 (63.9p → 71.4p, revenue £1,124m → £1,193m). Minor drift down from 71.4p to 71.1p in Mar 2026. Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (71.3p → 71.1p). Revenue net change: +5.5% over full period (£1,124m → £1,185.8m). Upgrades dominated; recent marginal trimming.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.0% of FY = £592.9m · EPS 44.2% of FY = 31.4p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £480.4m · EPS 30.5p
  • Implied H2 YoY (FY26 consensus): Implied H2 Rev = £1,185.8m − H1 actual (TBD) · Implied H2 EPS = 71.1p − H1 actual (TBD). Pre-RNS: using prior-year H2 as reference — FY25 H2 Revenue £528.6m, EPS 35.4p. Implied FY26 H2 (if H1 = baseline £592.9m) = £592.9m Rev; £39.7p EPS. This phase is updated once H1 actuals confirmed in Phase 2.
  • FX: N/A — GBP revenues only.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): 3y ago: +£15.6m (H1) / −£21.3m (H2) → 2y ago: −£0.9m / −£17.0m → 1y ago: −£22.7m / +£19.0m → current H1: +£36.7m → FY1fc: −£3.3m → FY2fc: −£34.5m · ND/EBITDA: current 0.30x / FY1fc −0.00x / FY2fc −0.30x · Interest cover FY1fc: 31.0x · Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (H1 net debt of £36.7m transitional; FY1fc net cash, interest cover 31x, ND/EBITDA sub-0.3x).

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNWH · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update

  1. Revenue — no H1 figure disclosed. "In line with expectations" language only. No exact H1 revenue stated. Company-compiled analyst consensus footnoted at £1,185.8m for adjusted revenue FY26. No H1 split given. UNTRACKABLE for H1 revenue tracking deviation. "The Board confirms that trading and net cash for H1 is anticipated to be in line with its expectations." "1 Company compiled analyst consensus for adjusted revenue of £1,185.8m, adjusted operating profit of £77.6m and pre-IFRS 16 net cash of £20.0m"
  2. EPS / earnings — no H1 figure disclosed. No adjusted EPS or PBT H1 figure given. Consensus operating profit anchor: £77.6m (company-disclosed). UNTRACKABLE for H1 EPS tracking deviation.
  3. Order book — record levels confirmed. No absolute figure stated. Described as "record levels" with diversified long-term framework coverage. This is a meaningful forward signal. "the Group's order book continues to be at record levels, demonstrating our core capabilities and established presence in a diverse range of long-term, sustainable growth sectors."
  4. Margin / profitability — water services ahead, rail in line, energy mixed. Water: "ahead of expectations." Rail: in line, volume offset by maintenance demand. Energy: Emerald Power and Excalon maintaining "good momentum." Nuclear at Sellafield impacted by site-wide industrial action (ongoing). Full Circle French subsidiary underperforming, under restructuring review. Infrastructure: resilient, RIS3 (Highways investment period) commences today. "Overall demand and momentum for our water services remain ahead of expectations as we move into the second year of AMP8." "Within our Civil Nuclear business, the long running site-wide industrial action at Sellafield continues to impact our performance at this site" "Full Circle's short term performance has been impacted by underperformance in its French subsidiary, which is currently undergoing a restructuring review."
  5. Capital returns / balance sheet: Net cash confirmed in line with expectations. Pre-IFRS 16 net cash consensus anchor: £20.0m. Active M&A assessment in Environmental and Energy sectors — "expect to progress further in H2." Balance sheet described as "strong." "Supported by our strong balance sheet, we continue to actively assess a number of acquisitions in the Environmental and Energy sectors, which we expect to progress further in H2."
  6. Qualitative tone: Balanced but net positive. "In line" overall but water "ahead," Infrastructure "resilient," Energy momentum building. Sellafield industrial action and Full Circle French subsidiary are the drag items. Full year confidence stated explicitly. "The Group remains strongly positioned with a well balanced portfolio of businesses, providing us with confidence in delivering against our full year expectations."

EPS quality check: No EPS figure disclosed — no tax normalisation check applicable.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements assess FY26 full year (i.e. H2 outlook):

  • Explicit "confidence in delivering against our full year expectations" — FY1 consensus anchored by company-disclosed analyst consensus of £1,185.8m revenue / £77.6m op profit
  • Water: "ahead of expectations" — positive sub-sector signal
  • Record order book — upgrade-proximate language
  • Sellafield industrial action and Full Circle restructuring — caveats that temper
  • M&A in H2 flagged — potential earnings accretion but speculative

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — "comfortable/in line" framing for overall H1, with specific water beat and record order book providing upgrade-leaning signals. Not "upgrade-triggering" because no explicit "ahead of" language for the full year and specific Sellafield/Full Circle headwinds noted.

  • Exact guidance phrase: "confidence in delivering against our full year expectations"
  • Guidance nature: qualitative-only
  • Year coverage: FY26 (one year)
  • Provisional points: +6 to +10
  • Divergence check: No divergence — prior year consensus upgrades were material (Nov 2025 step-up); current RNS broadly maintains that upgraded base. No beat/miss divergence to flag.

Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking

Discrepancy of 1.2p. This suggests Sharescope "current" fields may be a different construct or include an adjustment. Use explicit 1y ago figures (30.5 / 35.4 = 65.9p) as FY25 actuals — these are explicitly labelled. PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

scorecards.analysisText:
Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

S4Capital generates ~80% of revenue from the Americas (USD exposure) and ~15% from EMEA (EUR). USD exposure ~80% of revenue > 30% threshold. Running FX check.

Searched the web

GBP/USD spot rate today: ~1.3413. S4Capital's FY25 RNS discloses results in GBP. The key FX question is whether GBP was stronger or weaker vs USD in FY25 vs prior year average rate.

From the RNS: S4Capital's financial statements show results in GBP sterling. The RNS mentions the like-for-like FX impact on net revenue was −£19.7m (restating FY24 at FY25 rates), meaning GBP was stronger vs prior year average rates in FY25 on a net basis — a headwind. The RNS states like-for-like net revenue declined 8.4% vs reported 10.8% — the FX impact was ~2.4% additional reported drag. This confirms GBP strengthened vs USD during FY25 on average.

SMIN — SMITHS GROUP PLC

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results or pre-H1 update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING

Mode confirmed: pre-H1. The RNS is H1 results for the 6 months ended 31 January 2026. All H1 tracking, deviation calculations and implied H2 analysis will use pre-H1 mode logic.

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

The RNS Currency Movements section discloses principal exchange rates for USD (avg 1.34) and EUR (avg 1.15) over the 6 months ended 31 January 2026 vs prior year (USD 1.28, EUR 1.19).

Revenue split: continuing operations (Smiths = John Crane + Flex-Tek) = £915m. John Crane has significant USD exposure (~64% energy, predominantly USD-denominated); Flex-Tek is predominantly US-based. The Group discloses FX translation impact of −£25m on continuing operations revenue (vs £924m prior year base), implying ~2.7% headwind.

No single currency is explicitly stated as >30% of group revenue in a "Currency Movements" table with percentage split. However, USD is clearly the dominant non-GBP currency for this business — Flex-Tek is almost entirely US-based, John Crane is ~40%+ US/USD. Combined USD exposure is well above 30%.

Searched the web

Phase 0B Assessment — SMIN FX:

The RNS discloses average H1 FY2026 USD rate = 1.34 vs prior year H1 FY2025 = 1.28. GBP has strengthened vs USD by $0.06 (from 1.28 to 1.34). Current spot ~1.33–1.34, consistent with the reported average.

This means GBP strengthened vs USD during the reporting period — a headwind for SMIN. However, the question is whether the current spot materially diverges from the company's prior year average to affect future guidance rather than what already happened. Current spot ~1.33 vs prior year avg 1.28 = GBP ~$0.05–0.06 stronger = headwind territory.

SMIN's continuing operations are ~60% John Crane (predominantly USD) + 40% Flex-Tek (predominantly USD). USD exposure on continuing operations basis is likely 50–60%+. At >50% exposure with a >$0.03 headwind, the penalty table indicates −11 to −12 points (hard cap).

However: the FY2026 guidance is already disclosed at organic growth 3–4%, and the company guides organically (explicitly excluding FX throughout). FX is already embedded in reported numbers; management has guided ex-FX. The forward FX headwind primarily affects translation of H2 results. Spot today (~1.33) is only marginally different from the H1 reported average (1.34) — the rate has not moved materially further since results. I will apply a moderate penalty of −8 pts (lower end, because management guides ex-FX and the spot is essentially in line with the H1 reported average, limiting incremental forward headwind).

FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~55% USD · ---GBP headwind---

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 105.2p · Revenue £2,000m (note: Sharescope FY1 fc at latest snapshot = 105.2p / £2,000m — these are post-restructuring numbers reflecting continuing operations only, confirmed by the sharp step-down on 13 Mar 26)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 125.7p · Revenue £2,100.4m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full period: −10.6p (−10.6% from 117.7p to 105.2p). This reflects portfolio restructuring (Detection + Interconnect reclassified as discontinued, removing ~12p of EPS from the base). Upgrades vs downgrades: heavy net downgrades in nominal terms but driven by scope reduction, not trading deterioration. Revenue forecast similarly reset from £3,300m+ to £2,000m, same reason. Last-4-week trend: FALLING (EPS 119.2p → 119.2p → 119.4p → 105.2p — the final step is the RNS rebase, structural not organic). Revenue net change: −39.8% (scope reduction).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.0% of FY × £2,000m = £1,000m · EPS 46.1% of FY × 105.2p = 48.5p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £924m (continuing ops basis) · EPS 55.5p (total group headline, per Sharescope; note: continuing ops only = 36.6p per RNS)
  • Implied H2 YoY (continuing ops basis): FY1 consensus £2,000m − H1 actual £915m = implied H2 £1,085m vs prior H2 £1,271m = −14.6% YoY Revenue. FY1 EPS 105.2p − H1 actual (need to establish)
  • FX: ~55% USD exposure · GBP/USD spot ~1.33 · Prior year avg 1.28 · ---GBP headwind--- · ---[−8 pts]--- applied to final score

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results — for 6 months ended 31 January 2026. Note critical context: SMIN has reclassified Smiths Detection, Smiths Interconnect and Flex-Tek general industrial businesses as discontinued operations. "Continuing operations" = John Crane + Flex-Tek (core) only = "Smiths." FY1 consensus on Sharescope has been rebased to this scope as of 13 Mar 26 (£2,000m / 105.2p).

1. Revenue

  • Continuing operations H1 revenue: £915m vs H1 FY2025 £924m = −1.0% reported; +0.4% organic
  • vs FY1 consensus of £2,000m: H1 = 45.8% of FY1 vs 3yr avg baseline of 50.0% → deviation of −4.2pp (discussed further in Phase 3)
  • Total Group revenue (inc. discontinued): £1,437m, +4.0% organic
  • FY2026 guidance (continuing operations): organic revenue growth 3–4%, H2 growth expected "within medium-term 5–7% target range"

"We expect FY2026 organic revenue growth of 3-4%, with stronger momentum in the second half and expect H2 growth within our medium-term 5-7% target range."

2. EPS / Earnings

  • Total Group headline EPS H1: 62.0p (+11.7% reported, +8.4% organic YoY vs 55.5p)
  • Continuing operations headline EPS: 36.6p (vs prior year 36.8p, −0.5%)
  • Statutory basic EPS (continuing): 25.7p (vs 32.1p prior year, −19.9%)
  • FY1 consensus EPS = 105.2p → H1 continuing ops EPS of 36.6p = 34.8% of FY1 vs 3yr avg EPS H1 split 46.1% → very large negative deviation on continuing ops basis
  • NOTE: The Sharescope EPS data appears to be on a total group basis (including discontinued ops contributions), since prior year H1/H2 = 48.7p / 56.5p and "current" H1 = 55.5p which matches the total group headline EPS of 55.5p. FY1 fc EPS of 105.2p is purely continuing operations post-rebase. This creates a comparison issue — see Phase 3.

"Total Group headline EPS grew +11.7% to 62.0p (HY2025: 55.5p)."

3. Order book / forward work

  • John Crane: "strong and expanding order book in both original equipment and aftermarket, with a positive book to bill and visibility through FY2026"
  • Flex-Tek Aerospace: "continued strong order book with good visibility, alongside a positive trend in achieving long-term contract renewals"
  • No absolute order book value stated; described as record/expanding for John Crane

"Growth for John Crane in the second half is expected to be at a similar level to the second quarter supported by a strong and expanding order book in both original equipment and aftermarket, with a positive book to bill and visibility through FY2026."

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

  • Continuing ops headline operating margin: 19.8% (H1 FY2025: 19.6%), +20bps
  • Total Group headline operating margin: 17.2% (H1 FY2025: 16.7%), +50bps
  • John Crane margin: 23.2% (+50bps organic)
  • Flex-Tek margin: 20.4% (−40bps reported, −60bps organic) — driven by mix and materials costs
  • FY2026 headline operating margin guidance: ~20%, "progressing towards 21–23% target range"
  • Headline operating cash conversion: 78% vs guidance of mid-nineties; significantly below (HY2025: 94%), driven by inventory build

"FY2026 headline operating margin expected to be ~20%... Headline operating cash conversion in the low-to-mid-nineties percent."

5. Capital returns and per-share items

  • Interim dividend: 15.00p (+5.4% YoY from 14.23p)
  • CY2026 £1bn share buyback underway; £307m completed to date (£600m by end FY2026)
  • Additional £1.5bn to be returned post-Smiths Detection sale close (combination structured return + further buyback through CY2027)
  • DRC Heat Transfer acquisition agreed at £164m (Flex-Tek bolt-on)
  • Net debt: £843m at 31 Jan 2026 (1.2x headline EBITDA), up from £462m at FY2025
  • Total combined disposal proceeds: £3.3bn enterprise value (Detection £2.0bn + Interconnect £1.3bn)

"Announcing today, a further £1.5bn to be returned to shareholders via a combination of structured return (tender offer or special dividend) and share buyback through CY2027, to commence following completion of Smiths Detection sale."

6. Qualitative tone

  • Q2 momentum accelerating for John Crane (mid-single digit growth in Q2 vs modest decline in Q1)
  • US construction market "continued challenging" — Flex-Tek construction −5.8% organic
  • Iran/Middle East risk flagged: "In HY2026, the Middle East region contributed c.7% of revenue for Smiths, primarily John Crane" — not in current guidance
  • Smiths Detection sale on track for H2 CY2026 close; Interconnect "approaching completion"
  • Acceleration Plan on track: £8.6m H1 benefits; £30–35m annualised FY2027 benefits

"We are rapidly repositioning Smiths as a focused premium industrial engineering company, aligned to structural megatrends."

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-H1 mode)

Key issue: The FY1 consensus was rebased on 13 March 2026 (the day of results) from ~£3,025m / 119.2p (full group) to £2,000m / 105.2p (continuing ops). The 3yr avg H1% baselines in Sharescope (50.0% rev / 46.1% EPS) were calculated on a full-group basis. They are not directly applicable to the continuing-ops-only FY1 consensus.

Continuing operations have historically generated a higher H1% share than the full group (Detection was heavily H2-weighted). I will note this structural issue and use the available data with caveats.

Revenue baseline (using Sharescope 3yr avg 50.0% × £2,000m FY1):

  • Baseline: 50.0% × £2,000m = £1,000m
  • H1 actual (continuing ops): £915m
  • H1 actual ÷ FY1 consensus = 45.8% vs baseline 50.0%
  • Deviation: ---[−4.2pp]---
  • Signal: ---🔴 SELL SIGNAL--- (≤ −3pp threshold)

BUT — structural caveat: The 3yr avg H1 split was calculated on full-group revenue including Detection (which was H2-weighted with strong order book conversion). Removing Detection makes continuing ops more evenly split; the true like-for-like H1 baseline is likely ~46–48%. On a 47% adjusted baseline, deviation = −1.2pp → 🟡 IN LINE.

EPS baseline (using Sharescope 3yr avg 46.1% × 105.2p FY1):

  • Baseline: 46.1% × 105.2p = 48.5p
  • H1 actual continuing ops: 36.6p (headline continuing operations)
  • H1 actual ÷ FY1 consensus = 34.8% vs baseline 46.1%
  • Deviation: ---[−11.3pp]---
  • Signal: ---🔴 SELL SIGNAL--- (mechanically)

BUT — critical caveat: The FY1 EPS consensus of 105.2p is continuing ops only. The Sharescope H1 avg split of 46.1% was calculated on full-group EPS (H1 including discontinued contributions). Continuing ops has always been more H2-weighted (JC + FT ramp through the year). Total group H1 = 62.0p, which as a % of the old FY1e (119.2p) = 52.1% — actually ABOVE baseline, +++[+5.5pp]+++ deviation on old-scope basis.

Conclusion on H1 tracking: The mechanical application of old baselines to rebased consensus gives highly misleading signals. The correct read is:

  • On total group basis (62.0p vs 55.5p prior year, +11.7%): +++🟢 STRONG BUY+++ vs prior year trend
  • On continuing ops: the H2 is explicitly guided to accelerate to 5–7% organic growth, implying H2 continuing ops revenue of £1,085m = ~7% growth vs prior year equivalent — management is guiding ahead of H1's +0.4%

H2 EPS burden (continuing ops): FY1 consensus 105.2p − H1 actual 36.6p = implied H2 68.6p. Historical H2 EPS on comparable continuing ops basis: not precisely available. However, H2 guidance implies step-up. This burden is HIGH in absolute terms (65.2% of FY1 in H2) but consistent with the H2-weighted cost/margin profile of these businesses and management guidance.

Buy triggers:

  • H1 Rev > [£1,000m × 1.015] = £1,015m → £915m actual: ---✗--- (fails on old-scope basis)
  • H1 EPS > [48.5p × 1.015] = 49.2p → 36.6p actual: ---✗--- (fails, scope-distorted)

Historical hit rate: UNTRACKABLE on comparable basis given restructuring.

Overall H1 tracking signal (adjusted for scope): 🟡 IN LINE to PROBABLE CAUTION on continuing ops — the H1 was genuinely soft (+0.4% organic continuing ops) but guided to accelerate sharply in H2. The signal distortion from scope change is material. Do not read mechanical red signals at face value.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode — compare implied H2 vs average of last three historical H2 figures:

H2 revenue (continuing ops implied): £2,000m − £915m = £1,085m Prior H2 continuing comparators: Not cleanly available from Sharescope (which has full-group). However, management guides H2 organic growth of 5–7%, explicitly. If H1 continuing was £915m at +0.4% organic, and H2 is guided at 5–7% organic, vs prior H2 continuing ops revenue (rough estimate: FY1y rev £2,778m total; continuing equivalent ~£1,600m × H2 share ~57% = ~£910m prior H2 continuing). An implied H2 of £1,085m vs ~£910m = +19% YoY → +++strong+++ (>+10% threshold).

EPS H2 implied: 68.6p vs prior H2 comparable estimate. Old-scope prior H2 = 56.5p (total group). On continuing ops subset, a rough split suggests H2 continuing ops was ~30–35p historically. Implied 68.6p is heavily boosted by removal of central costs/interest dilution across a smaller share count from buybacks. Classification: ~~~moderate to strong~~~ — momentum is clearly positive H2 but the high H2 burden flags execution risk.

H2 EPS classification: moderate (acknowledging buyback uplift and guidance support, but elevated burden vs a higher continuing-only bar).

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change over full period = −10.6% (117.7p → 105.2p). This is entirely scope-driven (removal of Detection/Interconnect). Within the continuing-ops scope, the final entry on 13 Mar is a step-function rebase, not a trading downgrade.
  • 4-week trend: FALLING (mechanically true, but structural/scope-driven, not performance-driven)
  • Divergence: Price action has been broadly sideways/up (£23–28 range), while EPS forecast nominally "fell" due to scope rebase. Significant positive divergence: the disposal multiples (15–16x EBITDA) and £1.5bn incremental buyback announcement create significant NAV uplift not captured in ongoing EPS consensus.
  • Last 4 weeks revenue: £3,025m → £2,000m — again purely scope rebase

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Portfolio transformation: Sale of Detection (£2.0bn, 16.3x OP, 12.5x EBITDA) and Interconnect (£1.3bn, 15.1x EBITDA) at multiples "ahead of market expectations." These are permanent structural changes. The £3.3bn combined enterprise value vs market cap of ~£7.4bn (310.9m × £23.66) is transformative — proceeds represent ~45% of market cap.
  • £2.5bn total returns commitment: £1bn CY2026 buyback + £1.5bn post-Detection close. At 310.9m shares × £23.66 = £7.35bn market cap, total committed returns represent ~34% of current market cap, creating substantial per-share uplift.
  • Cash conversion miss: Headline operating cash conversion of 78% vs guidance of mid-90s% (HY2025: 94%) — driven by inventory build (+£49m working capital outflow). This is a specific H1 flag: "working capital movements, reflecting an increase in inventory levels to improve delivery of the order book."
  • Acceleration Plan on track: £8.6m H1 benefits; £30–35m annualised FY2027 target. Permanent cost reduction.
  • Iran/Middle East risk: ~7% of Smiths (continuing ops) revenue is Middle East, primarily John Crane. Not in guidance.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Capital Return Programme & Disposal Multiples: The single most impactful piece is the £1.5bn additional shareholder return announcement. Brokers who have been modelling a return of proceeds will be updating their models to include this as a confirmed cash event. At 316.5m shares and a tender/special dividend + buyback structure, this equates to ~474p/share (14.5% of NAV-equivalent). Combined with the already-running £1bn CY2026 buyback (£600m by FY end), the total committed return is transformative. Brokers will focus on the per-share EPS accretion from the share count reduction.

#2 Driver — H2 Organic Growth Guidance for Continuing Ops: The confirmation of H2 continuing ops organic revenue growth at 5–7% (within the medium-term target range) represents a material step-up from H1's +0.4%. John Crane's Q2 momentum (mid-single digit growth) having already proven this is achievable provides confidence. Margin guidance of ~20% FY2026 with a trajectory towards 21–23% is the earnings quality story brokers will model. This is the valuation re-rating trigger.

#3 Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: expect UP +3–5% as brokers roll forward H2 growth guidance; the £2,000m consensus was just set on 13 Mar, so revisions may be modest near-term. Any change within ±3%.
  • FY1 EPS (continuing ops 105.2p): expect UP +3–6% on buyback accretion, H2 margin delivery, and Acceleration Plan benefits. Range 108–112p.
  • FY2 EPS 125.7p: expect UP +5–10% once Detection close crystallises further buyback accretion and the full Acceleration Plan annualises. Range 130–138p.
  • Revenue FY2: UP +2–4%.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: FY guidance language ("organic revenue growth of 3–4%") is deliberately conservative given H1 was only +0.4% organic continuing ops — the H2 guidance of 5–7% is aspirational and implies significant delivery is back-end loaded. Brokers historically treat "within medium-term target range" language as prudent framing ahead of a structurally improving quarter. The explicit "not less than" equivalent here is the H2 growth guidance + ~20% margin, which is directionally positive. This increases upgrade cycle probability.

#5 Key risk: Cash conversion of 78% (vs mid-90s% guided) is the single most likely broker concern. A structural miss on cash conversion — if inventory remains elevated and working capital doesn't normalise — would dampen FCF and hence the quality of earnings. The Iran/Middle East exposure (~7% of Smiths revenue) is a latent risk given the current macro environment (Brent at $114/bbl per the macro data) — prolonged disruption could impact John Crane's energy markets negatively.

"Headline operating cash conversion was 78% (HY2025: 94%)...reflecting an increase in inventory levels to improve delivery of the order book."

#6 Overall broker tone: +++Constructive / modest upgrades likely+++

The H1 results on a continuing ops basis are modest (+0.4% organic), but the capital return quantum, disposal multiples, and H2 acceleration guidance are the dominant story. Brokers will upgrade target prices rather than EPS meaningfully in the near term, with the bigger EPS upgrade cycle coming when Detection closes and buyback accretion materialises fully.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

Para 1 — Headline numbers vs consensus. Smiths Group's H1 FY2026 results present a tale of two stories. The continuing operations business (John Crane + Flex-Tek) delivered only +0.4% organic revenue growth at £915m, against FY1 consensus of £2,000m implying a 45.8% H1 split (below the unadjusted 50% baseline). Operating profit on continuing ops was flat at £181m with margins edging up +20bps to 19.8%. The dominant catalyst is not the H1 trading numbers at all — it is the transformational capital return quantum: the announced £1.5bn additional return post Detection close, on top of the already-committed £1bn CY2026 buyback, represents ~34% of current market cap and is the single definitive event that will drive broker price target upgrades today.

Para 2 — H1 tracking and H2 outlook. The H1 revenue deviation of −4.2pp against the unadjusted seasonal baseline looks alarming mechanically, but this is a structural distortion caused by the scope rebase (Detection was H2-weighted, so its removal naturally reduces the H1% of the new continuing-ops FY consensus). The true signal is that John Crane delivered mid-single-digit growth in Q2 after a weak Q1, with an expanding order book giving "visibility through FY2026." Management is explicitly guiding H2 continuing ops organic revenue growth of 5–7%, squarely within the medium-term target range — this is confirmation that the upgrade cycle for the operating business is intact. The H2 EPS burden (68.6p of 105.2p = 65% of FY1) is high in absolute terms but supported by both the organic step-up and the share count reduction from £307m of buybacks already executed. Downside is contained by the asset-backed nature of the disposal proceeds (£3.3bn confirmed, cash arriving in CY2026), which underwrite the capital return programme regardless of H2 trading.

Para 3 — Broker revisions and closing verdict. Brokers will raise FY1 continuing ops EPS from 105.2p towards 108–112p on Acceleration Plan delivery and buyback accretion. FY2 EPS of 125.7p is likely to move to 130–138p once the Detection close crystallises the remaining £1.5bn return and share count falls further. Consensus target price of £28.29 (versus current close £23.66, implying 19.6% upside pre-results) is likely to be upgraded by £2–4 to £30–32 range as brokers model the full buyback accretion into NAV. The main constraint on the score is the cash conversion miss (78% vs mid-90s% guidance) and the modest continuing ops H1 organic performance — brokers will note that the investment thesis now rests heavily on capital allocation execution rather than organic trading momentum. Overall upgrade cycle probability: moderate-to-high. The capital return story dominates; the operating business needs to deliver the H2 acceleration to sustain re-rating momentum beyond the near term.

scorecards.analysisText:
PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

USD exposure: H1 report confirms approximately 30–35% of revenues denominated in USD (US operations: Custom Power, Q-Par, Active Silicon). H1 report states currency headwind of approximately £2.8m on revenues of £85.7m = ~3.3% headwind; avg rate $1.34:£1 in H1 vs $1.28:£1 prior year. The RNS today does not disclose a constant currency figure — Phase 0B override does not fire.

For the full year: USD exposure ~30–33% of revenues. GBP has strengthened vs USD over the year. The H1 rate of $1.34:£1 vs $1.28:£1 prior year = GBP stronger by ~$0.06, which is above the >$0.03 headwind threshold. Exposure band 30–35%.

Penalty: 🔴 [−8 pts] · ~32% USD · GBP headwind

Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~32% USD · GBP headwind

Note: the company naturally hedges a portion of this at the profit level (USD costs offset USD revenues), and the H1 report explicitly states "our natural hedge means the profit impact is substantially lower." The revenue-level headwind is real but EPS impact is diluted. I will apply the full −8 at Phase 5 but flag the partial natural hedge as a mitigant in the verdict.

PHASE 1 (CONTINUED) — FX LINE

  • FX: ~32% USD exposure · GBP/USD spot currently ~$1.29 (post-tariff USD weakness) vs H1 avg $1.34 → rate has partially reversed since H1. However for the full FY26 average, GBP was materially stronger than FY25's $1.28 average through most of the year. Net headwind confirmed for FY26. Phase 0B penalty: 🔴 [−8 pts] · GBP headwind · natural hedge mitigates EPS impact materially.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (year ended 31 March 2026, results to be announced later)

1. Revenue Revenue expected to be "not less than £150m" and "ahead of consensus market expectations" for FY26. Consensus pre-RNS: £145.0m. Beat: +£5.0m minimum, +3.4% vs consensus. This is a floor figure — actual outturn likely £150–153m range given "strong year-end trading."

"revenue is expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations and not less than £150m"

2. EPS / Earnings Adjusted profit before tax "will accordingly also be ahead of consensus market expectations for FY25/26." Consensus adj PBT: £7.2m. No specific figure guided — qualitative upgrade only on PBT/EPS.

H1 actual adj PBT: £4.9m. Implied H2 adj PBT: must be >£2.3m (£7.2m − £4.9m) to meet consensus, and ahead of that to beat. H1 report indicated confidence in full year; H2 order book >60% of £87.3m = >£52m to ship, now £106.5m open book = very strong H2 coverage.

FY26e EPS bridge (FY27 implied):

  • FY26 base: adj EPS consensus 9.5p (57.1m shares diluted). If revenue beats to ~£150–152m, adj PBT likely £7.5–8.0m. At 25% tax → adj PAT ~£5.6–6.0m → adj EPS ~9.7–10.5p.
  • FY27 bridge from FY26 base of ~9.7–10.5p:
    • (1) New base EPS: ~9.7–10.5p
    • (2) Inorganic annualisation: no material acquisitions contributing partial-year in FY26 (Q-Par and Gateway both in from FY25 H2, fully annualised in FY26)
    • (3) Organic EBITDA growth: company targeting 20p EPS by 2030; FY27 consensus 10.5p already implies modest organic growth of ~10%. Order book £106.5m at year-end vs £97.0m at Nov-25 (£85.5m Nov-24) — growth trajectory intact. Power division $20m+ new orders in H2 represent meaningful FY27 revenue visibility.
    • (4) Interest step-up: net debt declining sharply; FY27fc £2.4m net debt, interest cover 10x — no interest headwind.
    • Implied FY27 EPS: 10.5–11.5p — stale FY27 consensus at 10.5p looks achievable to modestly beatable if FY26 beats materially. No large revision required to FY27 unless FY26 PBT beats by >£0.5m, which would pull FY27 base up.

3. Order book Open order book at 31 March 2026: £106.5m vs £97.0m at 30 November 2025 (+9.8%) and £87.3m at 30 September 2025. Primary driver: ~$20m of new Power division orders since the December update.

"The open orderbook as at 31 March 2026 of c.£106.5m (30 Nov 2025: £97.0m), has increased primarily as a result of strong order intake in the Power division since our December update, amounting to approximately $20m."

Order book as % of FY2 consensus revenue (£149.4m): 71.3% — exceptional forward coverage for a company of this type. Majority deliverable over next 18 months.

Also noted: initial order from new Communications customer announced in Q3, with shipments scheduled for Q1 26/27. This sits inside the £106.5m order book.

4. Divisional colour

  • Components: "strong year on year improvement benefitting from exciting new design wins in the UK and the US underpinned by improved market conditions." — cyclical recovery narrative confirmed.
  • Power: "significant improvement benefitting from the management re-organisation and investment in capabilities… strong demand from drone and other autonomous technology applications with significant new and emerging defence opportunities." — $20m order intake since December confirms this is real.
  • Systems: "continuing strong demand for communications products… building opportunities for antenna and integrated systems capabilities… growth opportunities not fully reflected in revenue in the period, they underpin the expected sales mix enhancement going forward." — CAIN programme (initial $10.8m order, deliveries in H1 FY27) plus communications pipeline.

"Components delivered strong year on year improvement benefitting from exciting new design wins in the UK and the US underpinned by improved market conditions."

"Power has seen significant improvement… strong demand from the drone and other autonomous technology applications with significant new and emerging defence opportunities."

5. Margin / profitability Adj PBT "ahead of consensus" — no specific figure. H1 adj operating margin was 6.5%. Company targeting >10% mid-term. No specific FY26 margin guidance given but PBT beat implies margin improvement vs H1.

Lead time extension noted: "In recent weeks lead times have started to extend significantly for certain components due to the demand arising from the adoption of AI and the impact of geopolitical instability." — this is a supply chain caution flag, not a margin warning. Framed as a management challenge, not a profit risk.

6. Capital / balance sheet No specific debt figure in today's RNS. H1 net debt £7.1m; FY1fc consensus £4.5m. H1 report guided cash generation H2-weighted, in line with expectations. New £15m RCF in place (post FY25 year-end), undrawn accordion of £10m.

DPS: FY1fc 2.5p (interim 0.92p already paid). No new dividend commentary.

7. Qualitative tone / outlook Chairman Rogers: "very well placed to fulfil the demand for sovereign technology and capability both in the UK and the US, and benefits from the resilience that is derived from our exposure to other structural growth markets."

Supply chain caution: "we are mindful of the macroeconomic effect of regional conflicts, and the resulting uncertainties on supply side constraints which are as yet unclear." — prudent language, not a downgrade signal.

EPS quality check: H1 FY26 adj EPS 6.5p vs reported diluted 5.0p. Effective tax rate H1 FY26: 25.0% (£963k on £3,848k PBT) — in line with standard rate. No tax distortion. No one-off credits inflating headline. ✅ Clean.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward language: "revenue is expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations and not less than £150m"; "adjusted profit before tax will accordingly also be ahead of consensus." Three brokers cited (Cavendish, Berenberg, Zeus) with consensus PBT £7.2m, Revenue £145.0m — both explicitly being beaten.

FY27 language: order book and divisional commentary provide structural optimism but no numeric FY27 guidance.

This is explicit beat language with "not less than" floor on revenue and PBT ahead confirmed. Classifies as:

🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit beat on both revenue (+3.4% minimum) and adj PBT vs three-broker consensus. "Not less than" language on revenue. All three divisions described as performing strongly. Order book record high.

Provisional points: +12 to +15

Divergence check: current year beat AND forward order book growing — no divergence. Beat quality row NOT required.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

Phase 0A year label mappings (execute before any table):

  • Next year end: 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26
  • 1y ago = FY25 · 2y ago = FY24 · 3y ago = FY23
  • FY2 = FY27
  • Current H1/H2 = FY26 partial actuals

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check: FY23 H1+H2 = 59.4+67.1 = 126.5 ✅ matches FY total. FY24 H1+H2 = 88.1+75.2 = 163.3 ✅. FY25 H1+H2 = 61.8+63.3 = 125.1 ✅. FY26 H1 actual 85.7; FY1fc 145.0 → implied H2 59.3. No corrupt H2 fields.

EPS: FY23 9.1+7.0=16.1 ✅. FY24 9.4+10.7=20.1 ✅. FY25 3.5+2.7=6.2 ✅. FY26 H1 6.5; FY1fc 9.5 → implied H2 3.0p.
