Revenue growth trajectory: FY24 +29.1% → FY25 −23.4% → FY26 ≥+19.9%. The FY25 decline was entirely mechanical (NSPA communications pull-forward into FY24, SDR-related delay of $25m order into FY26). Underlying trajectory with comms normalised: 🟡 Volatile — but the volatility is structural/contractual, not demand-driven. On a normalised basis, revenue ex-comms lumpiness is 🟢 Steady.

EPS growth trajectory: FY24 +24.8% → FY25 −69.2% → FY26 ≥+56.5%. Same dynamic — comms programme timing dominates. 🟡 Volatile structurally, but recovery trajectory from the FY25 trough is strong and company-guided.

Acceleration flags:

  • Revenue: RNS-implied FY26 ≥+19.9% vs FY25 −23.4% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived) — but base effect driven. More meaningfully, ex-comms underlying H1 revenue +3.6% YoY, with Components recovering and Power inflecting.
  • EPS: RNS-implied FY26 ≥+56.5% vs FY25 −69.2% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived) — again base-effect driven by FY25 trough. H1 adj EPS 6.5p vs 3.5p prior year = +85.7%, confirming operational momentum is real.

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

H2 derivations: all cross-checked above. FY26 implied H2 = £145.0m (FY1fc) − £85.7m (H1 actual) = £59.3m rev; 9.5p − 6.5p = 3.0p EPS. These are consensus-derived for H2 (no updated FY figure beyond "not less than £150m" — using the floor of £150m: implied H2 rev = £64.3m*).

*Important nuance: the "not less than £150m" language means the actual H2 revenue could be £64.3m+, making the HoH below a floor, not a point estimate.

EPS trajectory (last three HoH YoY): FY24 H2 +52.9% → FY25 H2 −74.8% → FY26 H2 +11.1% (consensus-derived). 🟡 Volatile — again, comms programme timing. The underlying FY26 H2 is genuinely improving: H2 order book coverage is strong (>60% of £106.5m = >£64m already committed), and Power/Components both recovering. If adj PBT beats to £7.8–8.0m, implied H2 EPS is 3.3–3.5p, making H2 YoY +22–30%.

Revenue trajectory (last three HoH YoY): FY24 H2 +12.1% → FY25 H2 −15.8% → FY26 H2 ≥+1.6% (floor). 🟡 Volatile for same structural reasons. The revenue cadence is intrinsically lumpy due to periodic communications project deliveries.

Structural H2 note: The NSPA communications delivery (£23.3m) was entirely H1 FY26, creating an optically high H1 and relatively modest implied H2. This is not operational weakness — it is the reverse of FY25 where H2 was flattered by the comms order timing.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Mode = pre-FY → Phase 3.2 written in full but does NOT contribute a scored row to Phase 5.

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% = 50.1% × FY1fc £145.0m = £72.7m
  • EPS baseline: 3yr avg H1% = 53.2% × FY1fc 9.5p = 5.1p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 actual £85.7m ÷ FY1fc £145.0m = 59.1% vs baseline 50.1% → deviation = 🟢 [+9.0pp] → 🟢🟢 STRONG BUY signal on revenue. However — this deviation is almost entirely explained by the £23.3m comms delivery (£23.3m / £145.0m = 16.1pp). Ex-comms, H1 revenue = £62.4m = 43.0% of FY → deviation = −7.1pp. The H1 tracking signal is therefore misleading at face value — the comms pull-forward mechanically inflates H1's share.
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 6.5p ÷ FY1fc 9.5p = 68.4% vs baseline 53.2% → deviation = 🟢 [+15.2pp] → 🟢🟢 STRONG BUY. Same caveat: comms contribution to H1 EPS was significant.
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1fc 9.5p − H1 actual 6.5p = 3.0p vs historical H2 avg (FY23–25: 7.0p, 10.7p, 2.7p) = avg 6.8p. The implied H2 burden of 3.0p looks LOW vs history — but the comms lumpiness explanation applies in reverse. With adj PBT beating, H2 actual EPS will likely be 3.2–3.5p.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > (72.7m × 1.015) = £73.8m [🟢 ✓ — £85.7m achieved]. H1 EPS > (5.1p × 1.015) = 5.2p [🟢 ✓ — 6.5p achieved].

Signal deferred from Phase 5 scoring (pre-FY mode). Baselines recorded for reference.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Mode = pre-FY → Phase 3.3 DOES contribute a scored row to Phase 5.

H2 base figure: RNS provides "not less than £150m" full-year revenue floor. Using this: implied H2 revenue = £150m − £85.7m = £64.3m minimum (RNS-derived floor). EPS: no specific FY EPS figure guided — using FY1fc 9.5p as base; implied H2 EPS = 9.5p − 6.5p = 3.0p (consensus-derived). Flagging: actual H2 revenue and EPS will exceed these floors given "ahead of consensus" language on PBT too.

Revenue H2 YoY: £64.3m (minimum) vs FY25 H2 £63.3m = +1.6% minimum. Actual likely +3–6% given PBT beat. Classification: 🟡 moderate (floor basis) to 🟢 strong (on actual outturn likely £66–68m → +4–7%).

EPS H2 YoY: 3.0p (consensus-derived) vs FY25 H2 2.7p = +11.1%. Classification: 🟢 strong (>+10% YoY). If PBT beats to £7.8m, H2 EPS = ~3.3p → +22% YoY → firmly 🟢 strong.

Profit warning feasibility gate: Not applicable — H1 tracking is strongly positive, no H1 miss, no H2 burden issue. Gate does not fire.

Implied H2 classification: 🟢 strong — EPS firmly above +10% YoY on both consensus and beat basis; revenue at floor is moderate but beats to strong on adj PBT guidance.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change +63.8% (5.8p → 9.5p) over full snapshot period. All movement at the July 2025 final results date. Post-July: stable at 9.5–9.6p with marginal drift. Last 4 weeks: 🔴 FLAT (9.5p unchanged).
  • Revenue trend: £124m → £145m, all moving at July 2025. Last 4 weeks: flat at £145m.
  • Divergence: Price has been flat to weak (247p → 247p in recent weeks, down from 232p in January). The share price is well below the consensus TP of 247p... wait — close price is 142.5p, consensus TP is 247p. That is 73.3% upside to consensus TP. This is a significant disconnect. The EPS consensus is flat but the price has materially de-rated. The price was 247p in Feb–Mar 2026 and has since fallen to 142.5p — a de-rating of ~42% with flat EPS forecasts. This implies either the market is pricing in risk to consensus (supply chain, comms lumpiness, tariffs) or there has been recent selling unrelated to fundamentals. Today's RNS is a direct counter to the de-rating thesis.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

  • Net debt: FY23 £0.0m / FY24 £2.5m / FY25 £7.4m / H1 FY26 £7.1m (excl. IFRS16) → FY1fc £4.5m → FY2fc £2.4m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY23 0.1x / FY24 0.3x / FY25 0.4x / H1 FY26 1.9x → FY1fc 0.4x / FY2fc 0.2x. H1 spike to 1.9x was temporary working capital effect of large NSPA shipment at period-end with receivables outstanding; unwound in H2 per company guidance.
  • Interest cover: FY1fc 8.4x / FY2fc 10.0x — very comfortable.
  • ND/FCF: FY1fc 0.6x / FY2fc 0.3x — strong cash conversion confirmed.
  • Facility: £15m RCF (Lloyds/Comerica), committed to May 2028, £10m accordion undrawn.

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash trajectory — FY1fc 0.4x ND/EBITDA; trajectory is towards net cash by FY28. No scored row in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26 vs FY25 actual:

  • FY1fc EPS 9.5p vs FY25 actual 6.2p → ✅ FY1fc EPS growing +53.2% vs prior year actual
  • FY1fc Revenue £145.0m vs FY25 actual £125.1m → ✅ FY1fc Revenue growing +15.9% vs prior year actual
  • ✅✅ FY1fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs prior year actual

Step 2 — FY27 vs FY26 consensus:

  • FY2fc EPS 10.5p vs FY1fc 9.5p → ✅ FY2fc EPS growing +10.5%
  • FY2fc Revenue £149.4m vs FY1fc £145.0m → ✅ FY2fc Revenue growing +3.0%
  • ✅✅ FY2fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY1fc

3.6 Structural Flags

Communications programme lumpiness: Revenue is structurally lumpy due to periodic large defence communications deliveries. FY24 pulled forward £33.4m of comms revenue; FY25 had almost none (SDR delay); FY26 received £23.3m NSPA + initial CAIN delivery expected in H1 FY27. This creates YoY swings of 20–30% that mask underlying ~5–10% organic growth in the core business. Brokers must model comms cadence separately; simple YoY growth rates are misleading.

"The revenue generated from these communications programmes arise from close relationships with commercial partners, and with national and international agencies. These projects are typically long term in nature and may span several years. Such contracts typically generate high value revenue with an irregular cadence as they complete." (H1 FY26 report)

CAIN programme: Initial $10.8m order, deliveries expected H1 FY27. The company flagged this as a "foundation for potentially significant follow-on revenues." This is currently inside the £106.5m order book and represents FY27 revenue that is already contracted — not speculative.

Power division inflection: The $20m order intake since December 2025 (in addition to the $7.4m announced in November 2025) represents a genuine step-change in Power order intake. The division was loss-dilutive in FY25; management reorganisation and Tier-1 customer focus is now generating results. At sustained order intake of ~$25–30m p.a., Power could contribute meaningfully to FY27 EPS.

AI-driven lead time extension: "In recent weeks lead times have started to extend significantly for certain components due to the demand arising from the adoption of AI and the impact of geopolitical instability." This is a double-edged flag: it validates SOLI's Components division positioning (they benefit from extended lead times through their specialist sourcing capabilities) but could create short-term supply chain friction for customers.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

SOLI · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — Revenue beat and order book record: The "not less than £150m" revenue floor (+3.4% vs £145.0m consensus) is the primary catalyst. At £150m+, this is a clean top-line beat with all three divisions contributing. The £106.5m order book — a new record and up ~£20m since the last update — provides the most tangible evidence of FY27 revenue sustainability. Brokers will lead with this: it converts a one-year beat into a multi-year upgrade narrative. This is the #1 driver.

#2 Driver — Power division order intake and defence structural tailwind: The ~$20m of Power orders since December, on top of $7.4m in November 2025, signals that the Power division reorganisation has genuinely worked. The H1 report showed Power revenue of £17.0m at 6.5% adj operating margin — below the Group average but recovering. With annualised order intake now running at ~$50–60m equivalent, FY27 Power revenues could materially exceed current broker models. Coupled with the CAIN programme (initial $10.8m in the book) and broader NATO defence spending uplift, brokers will raise FY27 revenue and margin forecasts for this division. This is the #2 driver and feeds directly into FY27 EPS upgrades.

#2 Forecast revisions:

FY26 (FY1):

  • Revenue: up £5–8m, from £145.0m to £150–153m (+3–5%). The "not less than £150m" floor + "strong year-end trading" language supports the upper end.
  • Adj PBT: up £0.3–0.8m, from £7.2m to £7.5–8.0m. H1 actual £4.9m; H2 must deliver £2.6–3.1m vs H1's run-rate. Order book coverage provides high confidence.
  • EPS: up 0.2–0.5p, from 9.5p to ~9.7–10.0p. Small per-share impact given 57m shares.

FY27 (FY2):

  • Revenue: up £5–10m, from £149.4m to £154–159m. The £106.5m order book (majority over 18 months) implies £70–75m of visible FY27 revenue at year-end — covering ~45–50% of prior consensus already. Power division order intake alone adds ~£8–12m incremental FY27 revenue vs current broker models.
  • EPS: up 0.5–1.5p, from 10.5p to 11.0–12.0p. Driven by revenue beat dropping through at improving margins (company targeting >10% adj operating margin mid-term; currently 6.5% H1).

#3 Target price and recommendation: Brokers will almost certainly raise target prices. Cavendish, Berenberg and Zeus will need to reflect: (a) FY26 beat, (b) improved FY27 revenue visibility from order book, (c) Power division inflection. Current consensus TP: 247p vs close 142.5p — 73% upside already in the model. With upgrades, TPs likely move to 270–310p range (implying 90–120% upside from current price). No rating changes expected — all likely already at Buy/Add. The share de-rating from 247p to 142.5p while EPS was flat is the anomaly; this RNS directly addresses the concern.

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: "Not less than £150m" is explicitly cautious language — a floor, not a central case. The H1 report commentary, the record order book, and the all-three-divisions-strong message suggest actual revenue is likely £151–154m. Brokers familiar with SOLI's history of understating outturns will treat £150m as the floor and model above it. This increases the probability of a second wave of upgrades when full-year results are published (typically July 2026).

#5 Key risk: Supply chain lead time extension. "In recent weeks lead times have started to extend significantly for certain components due to the demand arising from the adoption of AI and the impact of geopolitical instability." If lead time extensions prevent shipment of orders already in the book, FY26 outturns could be softer and FY27 revenue could be deferred rather than incremental. The company frames this as a management challenge, but it is the single most credible bear case: a replay of the FY25 scenario where an order was delayed by external events (SDR delay) reducing an expected £10m H2 shipment.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = upgrade (~+0.2–0.5p). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. ✅ Consistent.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

The combination of: explicit revenue beat with "not less than" floor language, adj PBT also ahead of consensus, all three divisions performing strongly, record order book at £106.5m, Power inflection confirmed, CAIN programme in the book for FY27 — this is a clean, broad-based upgrade trigger. The share price de-rating to 142.5p (vs 247p TP) makes the risk/reward particularly compelling from a broker perspective; expect initiation of a re-rating narrative alongside the number upgrades.

SOLI has guided revenue "not less than £150m" against a three-broker consensus of £145.0m — a minimum 3.4% outperformance — with adjusted PBT also explicitly ahead of the £7.2m consensus. analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text: 1. Dominant line items: #1 = Underlying EPS 10.51p (+5.1% vs 10.0p cns) — clean beat with synergies proven 2 years early. #2 = €825m investment-grade refinancing — de-risks the balance sheet and signals M&A optionality at a lower cost of capital. 2. Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26) EPS: Modest upgrade 3–7%; 10.0p → ~10.3–10.7p. German H2 tailwind + synergy run-rate support. FY1 Revenue: Hold at £1,036–1,050m; weather disruption limits H1 but H2 stronger. FY2 (FY27) EPS: More meaningful upgrades 5–10% as German stimulus and steel recovery materialise; 10.9p → ~11.5–12.0p. 3. Target price: Consensus 158p = current stock price. Immediate re-rating required. Brokers likely to move TPs to 170–190p (reflecting EPS beat + refinancing + synergy acceleration). Upside to revised TP ~30–46%. 4. Conservative guidance read-through: "Cautiously optimistic" with explicitly H2-weighted tailwinds (German stimulus, steel recovery) — classic conservative framing that sets up H2 FY26 upgrades. Brokers will interpret as management sandbagging H1 to under-promise H2. 5. Key risk: Proforma revenue −1.0% YoY. Volume recovery entirely dependent on German/European construction and steel cycle — neither has yet materialised in numbers. Winter disruption in Poland/Belgium could weigh on Q1 FY26. Leverage at 1.8x is comfortable but limits dividend initiation. 6. Broker-note tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. FY25 EPS beat, synergies ahead of schedule, refinancing completed — three positive catalysts in one announcement. Panmure Liberum and Deutsche Numis will raise TPs. FY26 and FY27 EPS upgrades expected.

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: FINAL SCORE: 53 / 100 · Confidence range: 48–60 (Raw score 64 − FX Rule 1 penalty 11 = 53) Score components (raw): EPS beat +5.1% (synergies ahead): +10 Revenue in line (−0.01%): +2 Synergies achieved 2 years early (structural margin step): +12 Refinancing €825m investment-grade (M&A optionality): +8 FCF +18%, leverage 1.8x (ahead): +6 FY26 guidance "cautiously optimistic" with H2 tailwinds: +5 Volume headwind (proforma −1%): −5 German stimulus H2-weighted (delayed uplift): −3 Winter weather FY26 H1 disruption: −3 Forecast momentum +9.9% (modest, now frozen): +4 Stock at consensus TP (no re-rating buffer): −2 Raw total: 64 FX Rule 1: ~51% EUR exposure, neutral rate, no prior avg available. Mid-point penalty 50%+ band = −11 pts. Confidence ±5pts. Verdict: A genuinely strong set of FY25 results constrained by the EUR FX penalty and volume headwinds. The synergy delivery 2 years early is the single most important structural positive — it proves the EBITDA improvement is permanent and not volume-dependent. The €825m refinancing is transformational for future M&A. The FX penalty reflects legitimate uncertainty about EUR translation on a 51% EUR revenue base. Brokers will upgrade EPS modestly for FY26 and more meaningfully for FY27 as German infrastructure stimulus arrives. The 9th consecutive year of EPS growth (now confirmed) is a powerful re-rating narrative.

scorecards.analysisText:
Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Staffline — 98% of revenues UK, ~2% Ireland. No single non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. Skip — no FX penalty.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results (year ended 31 December 2025). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 4.2p · Revenue £1,106.7m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 5.5p · Revenue £1,233.7m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +31.3% (3.2p → 4.2p) with large step-change upgrade in late Jan 2026. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT at 4.2p). Revenue net change: +3.2% (£1,072.7m → £1,106.7m). TP flat at 60p throughout.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.2% of FY = £522.4m · EPS 19.8% of FY (3yr avg) = 0.8p (using 3yr avg H1 split, but note this is very H2-weighted business)
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £485.8m · EPS 0.6p (Sharescope current H1)

Wait — Sharescope "Current H1" is the H1 FY25 period (Jan-Jun 2025 for Dec year-end). "Current H2" would be Jul-Dec 2025 = the second half. So "current H1 / H2 = 0.6 / -" means only H1 FY25 is known from the data snapshot. But the RNS is FY Results = the full year to 31 December 2025.

  • Implied H2 YoY (FY actual vs prior FY): Revenue actual £1,106.7m vs prior (FY24) £992.9m = +11.5% FY YoY. EPS: actual 4.5p (continuing basic) vs prior 3.0p continuing = +50.0%. vs FY1 consensus 4.2p = +0.3p beat (+7.1%). Revenue vs FY1 consensus £1,106.7m = exact match.
  • FX: N/A

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: FY Results (year ended 31 December 2025)

1. Revenue — FY actual £1,106.7m (+11.5%, 2024: £992.9m). vs FY1 consensus £1,106.7m = exact match.

"Revenue: £1,106.7m (2024: £992.9m) +11.5%"

2. Operating profit — significantly ahead of consensus Operating profit £13.0m (+31.3%, 2024: £9.9m). Company-compiled consensus was £12.7m → actual +2.4% beat. Described as "significantly ahead of market expectations."

"Operating profit significantly ahead of market expectations, up 31.3% to £13.0m (2024: £9.9m)"

3. EPS — continuing activities Basic EPS from continuing activities: 4.5p (2024: 3.0p), +50%. vs FY1 consensus of 4.2p = +0.3p beat (+7.1%).

"Statutory basic earnings per share on continuing activities in 2025 was 4.5p (2024: 3.0p)"

4. Gross profit conversion Gross profit £78.3m (+10.6%). Conversion ratio (GP→operating profit): 16.6% (2024: 14.0%) — +2.6pp improvement. This is the key margin story.

"Conversion ratio of gross profit to operating profit improved to 16.6% (2024: 14.0%), demonstrating both the improving quality and efficiency of the business"

5. PBT £7.4m (+48%, 2024: £5.0m). vs company consensus £7.1m = +4.2% beat.

"Operating profit significantly ahead of market expectations…Profit before taxation £7.4m (2024: £5.0m) +48.0%"

6. Net cash (pre-IFRS 16) — better than expected £1.5m (consensus also £1.5m — exact match). Despite buybacks and working capital investment from new logistics contract.

7. FY 2026 outlook — "in line with expectations" "The Board expects trading to continue in line with its expectations for the year ending 31 December 2026." No specific upgrade language.

"The Board expects trading to continue in line with its expectations for the year ending 31 December 2026."

8. New strategic logistics partnership c.2,000 workers onboarded at year-end from new logistics partnership secured May 2025. Provides organic revenue visibility for FY26.

9. Share buyback completion Tranche 2 completed 5 March 2026. Total since 2023: 27% reduction in share count (166m → 121m). Weighted average shares now 121.96m. This is a significant per-share EPS enhancer.

10. Cost reduction programme c.£3.0m p.a. cost savings implemented in H1 2025. Direct overheads reduced in Ireland by £0.6m. Group-wide cost discipline a recurring theme.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Revenue trajectory (H2s): −9.9% → +23.7% → +13.7% → 🟢 Steady EPS trajectory (H2s): −71.1% → +130.8% → +30.0% → 🟢 Steady (normalising from depressed base)

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 47.2% × £1,106.7m = £522.4m. H1 actual £485.8m ÷ £1,106.7m = 43.9% → deviation = 🔴 [−3.3pp] → 🔴 CAUTION
  • EPS baseline: 19.8% × 4.2p = 0.8p. H1 actual 0.6p ÷ 4.2p = 14.3% → deviation = 🔴 [−5.5pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL

However, this is a strongly H2-weighted business by nature (peak Q4 logistics/festive volumes). The EPS split in the three prior years was: FY22 = 21%, FY23 = 35%, FY24 = 3.2%. The EPS H1 seasonal pattern is unreliable as a signal for Staffline specifically. The actual FY result (4.5p) beats consensus (4.2p) by 7.1%, validating that the H2 bias is structural rather than a red flag.

Buy triggers: Rev > 47.2% × 1.015 × £1,106.7m = £530.1m: H1 actual £485.8m → 🔴 ✗ · EPS > 0.8p × 1.015 = 0.8p: H1 actual 0.6p → 🔴 ✗

Historical hit rate: 1 of 3 years showed positive H1 deviation preceding FY beat (the metric is largely UNTRACKABLE for STAF given extreme H2 weighting and small H1 EPS).

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 implied revenue £620.9m vs 3yr avg H2 = (£490.1m + £441.3m + £546.1m)/3 = £492.5m → +26.1% → 🟢 strong

H2 implied EPS 3.9p vs 3yr avg H2 = (4.5p + 1.3p + 3.0p)/3 = 2.9p → +34.5% → 🟢 strong

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS +31.3% over full period, with large step-change upgrade in late Jan 2026 (3.6p→4.2p)
  • TP flat at 60p throughout — suggesting only one covering broker who updated the TP but hasn't moved it further post-results
  • 4-week trend: FLAT
  • Divergence: The share price (40.8p) is well below the TP (60p), suggesting the market either doubts the TP or the stock is illiquid/under-followed.

5. Structural Flags

  • Pure-play recruitment transformation: PeoplePlus disposed February 2025; Staffline now fully focused on recruitment, improving margins and simplifying story.
  • 27% share count reduction since 2023: Mechanical EPS enhancer that will continue if buyback programme is renewed. Material tailwind for per-share metrics.
  • Defensive market position: Food, logistics, supermarkets — largely recession-proof volumes. The new £50m+ logistics partnership is meaningful scale.
  • No dividend until balance sheet "strength is restored": Reinvestment into buybacks preferred. Not a near-term income stock.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Operating profit +31.3%, significantly ahead of consensus £12.7m The explicit consensus-beat language is the dominant driver. Brokers wrote to £12.7m; result was £13.0m — a 2.4% beat that comes after a 31.3% increase. The conversion ratio improvement (14.0% → 16.6%) is structurally significant and will be the broker note highlight.

#2 Driver — Share buyback mechanical EPS enhancement 27% share count reduction over three years, with Tranche 2 now complete. FY26 weighted average share count will be ~120m (vs 122m in FY25), providing continued per-share earnings leverage. Brokers will need to flag this vs. FY25 to show a higher EPS for FY26 on flat nominal profit.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: currently 4.2p in consensus (pre-results this was the FY25 est; post-roll it becomes FY26). Given 4.5p FY25 actual + guidance "in line," FY26 EPS likely set at ~5.0–5.5p = the FY2 consensus. Modest upgrade plausible.
  • FY1 revenue: £1,233.7m FY2 consensus becomes FY1; the new logistics partnership provides visibility.
  • TP: Likely to move from 60p toward 70–80p range given the earnings upgrade trajectory.

Conservative guidance: "Trading to continue in line with its expectations" is standard UK cautious language, not explicitly conservative. However the company says "cautiously optimistic for FY 2026" given "defensive nature of its key GB markets." This is NOT aggressive, but the share buyback programme provides buyback support.

Key risk: The lack of dividend and the leveraged working capital structure (RFA facility) create a financial complexity risk. Net finance charges of £5.6m are a meaningful drag on PBT for a business of this size. "Despite ongoing sector and geopolitical headwinds, we remain cautiously optimistic about FY 2026."

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 72/100 · Confidence: 65–79 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

🔴 FY26 guidance "cautiously optimistic" — not upgrade-triggering language−5
🔴 Net finance charges £5.6m — material drag, limits operating leverage−4

Para 1 — Headline numbers: STAF delivered FY25 results that were explicitly "significantly ahead" of the company-compiled consensus, with operating profit of £13.0m beating the £12.7m benchmark and PBT of £7.4m beating consensus £7.1m by 4.2%. The primary catalyst is the gross profit-to-operating profit conversion ratio improvement from 14.0% to 16.6% — a structural quality signal indicating that every £1 of gross profit is now generating 19% more operating profit than last year. EPS from continuing activities of 4.5p (+50% YoY) beat the consensus of 4.2p by 7.1%.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 implied revenue of £620.9m (+26.1% above three-year H2 average) and H2 EPS of 3.9p (+34.5% above historical H2 average) confirm the business has structurally improved its earnings power. The H2 seasonal bias is well-understood and does not undermine the bull case — peak Q4 logistics volumes (record +11.1% hours in Q4) are structural and recurring. The upgrade resilience argument is anchored by: (1) ongoing share buyback reducing the denominator; (2) the new logistics partnership adding a minimum baseline contribution in FY26; and (3) cost reduction programme savings of £3m p.a. fully embedded from FY26. The downside risk — no dividend, net finance charges at £5.6m — is known and priced.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS likely upgraded from the current FY2 consensus of 5.5p toward 5.5–6.0p range, with the lower end already in consensus. TP should move from 60p toward 70–75p range as brokers lift estimates to reflect the FY25 beat and improving conversion ratio. At 40.8p, the stock trades at only 9x FY26E earnings even at the current consensus — extremely cheap for a business generating 50%+ EPS growth with visible deleveraging of the share count. The watch point is whether the logistics partnership continues to grow (currently 2,000 workers, with "significant new business" description) and whether macro deterioration risks the food/logistics volume base. 🏁 Verdict: Explicit consensus beat with structural margin improvement; upgrades incoming as conversion ratio story resonates. Score 72/100.

scorecards.analysisText:
SUP

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update / FY guidance update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings:

  • FY23 = 3y ago · FY24 = 2y ago · FY25 = 1y ago · FY26e = FY1 (1y fc) · FY27e = FY2 (2y fc)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update accordingly.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 18.4p · Revenue £245.7m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 20.5p · Revenue £290.4m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full period −17.5% (22.3p → 18.4p). Material downgrade cycle in Jul 25 (22.3→17.9p, -4.4p event). Partial recovery Oct 25 (17.9→18.4p). Then flat from Oct 25 to Apr 26 — stalled at 18.4p for six months. Revenue: £235.1m → £245.7m (+4.5%). 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.0% of FY = £113.1m · EPS 42.9% of FY = 7.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £113.0m · EPS 10.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): H1 FY26 actual = £132.6m (per Sharescope current H1). H2 implied = FY26e £245.7m − £132.6m = £113.1m. Prior H2 FY25 = £118.1m. Implied H2 YoY = £113.1m − £118.1m = −4.2%. EPS: FY26e 18.4p − H1 actual 8.8p = H2 implied 9.6p vs FY25 H2 = 10.2p → −5.9%
  • FX: Currency = GBP. No FX exposure. Phase 0B N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY25 H2 £0.5m → FY26 H1 £19.9m (net debt) → FY1fc £7.3m → FY2fc £1.1m. ND/EBITDA FY1fc 0.20x. Interest cover 23.2x. ND/FCF 0.6x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (essentially).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26 — twelve months ended 31 March 2026)

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: "expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)." vs FY26e consensus £245.7m → beat of £19.3m = +7.9%.

"The Company expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)"

  1. EBITDA — FY26 actual: "Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations." vs consensus £37.0m → beat of £3.6m = +9.7%. EBITDA margin: £40.6m/£265.0m = 15.3% vs FY25 £40.5m/£231.1m = 17.5%. Margin compression of 2.2pp despite revenue growth — driven by acquisition costs and investment in new facilities.

"Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations"

  1. EPS bridge (FY27e):
  • New base: FY26 EBITDA £40.6m. Finance costs: net cash ~£7.3m FY26. Interest income likely positive. Capex £5.0m. Tax ~25%. Adj PBT ~ EBITDA − D&A − interest cost. Working: EBITDA £40.6m, D&A estimated ~£3–4m (from asset base), interest net ~nil, PBT ~£37m, tax ~£9.25m, PAT ~£27.75m, shares ~117.3m → EPS ~23.7p (basic). But wait — Sharescope FY26e EPS is only 18.4p on consensus, implying significant adjustments. The company uses "Adjusted EBITDA" which excludes share-based payments, fair value movements, exceptional items. Statutory EPS will be lower. Using 18.4p consensus as adjusted EPS benchmark.
  • EPS bridge: FY26 actual adj EBITDA = £40.6m vs consensus £37.0m → +£3.6m upside. FY27e drivers: SlimFast (acquired during FY26) full year contribution; new manufacturing facilities operational; vaping resilience continues. Vaping +10%+ despite ban confirms structural resilience.
  • Organic EBITDA growth: FY26 £40.6m achieved despite acquisitions of £12.4m (SlimFast etc.) and £5.0m capex. FY27 benefit from full-year SlimFast + margin normalisation as acquisition costs fall away.
  • 🏗️ Investment step-up: "investment in two brand new manufacturing facilities." New wellness facility 40,000 sq ft. RNS states "positioned for long-term growth" — cost timing in FY26/FY27. FY26 capex £5.0m confirmed (matches Sharescope fc). FY27 ongoing running costs from new facilities = mild negative. Score as FY+1 consideration.
  • FY27e EPS bridge: FY26 consensus 18.4p will upgrade to ~20–22p on EBITDA beat alone (+9.7%). FY27e 20.5p (current) will be revised to ~22–24p on SlimFast full year + margin recovery. Implied FY27e EPS upgrade +7–17% vs stale 20.5p.
  1. Vaping: "expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025." This directly addresses the key bear case — ban proved manageable. Demonstrates market resilience and category strength.

"Sales from the Group's Vaping category are expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025"

  1. Drinks & Wellness / SlimFast: "boosted by an excellent contribution from SlimFast." SlimFast acquired during FY26, no full-year contribution in FY26 → FY27 gets full year.
  2. Capital returns / Balance sheet: After £12.4m acquisitions + £5.0m capex, "the Group remains net-cash positive at 31 March 2026." Robust balance sheet. RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash positive vs Sharescope FY1fc net debt £7.3m (positive = debt). RNS explicitly says net-cash positive — variance vs Sharescope. RNS supersedes: FY26 ended net cash, not net debt of £7.3m. Modest positive surprise.
  3. Qualitative outlook: "The Board remains confident in the Group's future trading prospects."

EPS quality check: Adjusted EBITDA measure. EBITDA £40.6m vs consensus £37.0m. No non-recurring benefit flagged. Revenue beat from organic vaping growth + SlimFast acquisition. Quality of beat appears genuine. Tax rate: not disclosed, but effective rate stable. No EPS quality concern.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification: Forward guidance for FY27: "Board remains confident in the Group's future trading prospects." Qualitative only. No numeric FY27 guidance. However, context suggests: record FY26, vaping resilience proven, SlimFast full year in FY27, new facilities operational. Growth drivers visible.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive (+6 to +10 pts provisional)

  • Phrase: "Board remains confident in the Group's future trading prospects"
  • Guidance qualitative only, but FY26 record results and multiple visible FY27 drivers (SlimFast full year, new facilities, vaping resilience) justify Constructive
  • Covers FY27 only
  • No divergence: FY26 beat strongly + outlook constructive = consistent. ✅

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

3.1 Full-Year YoY Growth Table

H2 cross-check: FY23 H1+H2 = 64.6+91.0 = 155.6 ✓. FY24 H1+H2 = 105.1+116.2 = 221.2 ✓. FY25 H1+H2 = 113.0+118.1 = 231.1 ✓. Current H1 = £132.6m; H2 pending (FY26 not yet closed in Sharescope pre-RNS). FY26 actual: RNS provides £265.0m. So H2 FY26 actual = £265.0m − £132.6m = £132.4m.

FY - MarRev £mRev YoY %EPS pEPS YoY %
FY23155.6—11.2—
FY24221.2+42.2%19.8+76.8%
FY25231.1+4.5%21.0+6.1%
FY26 (actual†)265.0+14.7%~22p†~+5%†
FY27e*290.4+9.6%20.5~−6%†

†FY26 actual EPS not yet disclosed. Using EBITDA beat to estimate: EBITDA £40.6m beats consensus £37.0m by +9.7%. If EPS scales similarly from consensus 18.4p → estimated ~20–21p. FY27e stale 20.5p will be upgraded.

⚠️ Note: Sharescope FY27e EPS (20.5p) appears LOWER than estimated FY26 actual (~20–21p). This is likely stale pre-upgrade data. Post-upgrade FY27e will be ~22–24p.

Revenue trajectory: FY24 +42%, FY25 +5%, FY26 +15% → 🟢 Accelerating (recovery from FY25 slowdown) EPS trajectory: FY24 +77%, FY25 +6%, FY26 ~+5% → 🟡 Volatile (FY24 spike, then moderation, FY26 flat)

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS-implied FY26 +14.7% vs prior year +4.5% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)
  • EPS: FY26 ~+5% vs FY25 +6.1% — modest deceleration on flat/similar growth rates. EBITDA beat is large but revenue outperformance with margin compression → EPS flat relative to prior trend. No acceleration (RNS-derived)

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode → write but do not score)

H1 FY26 actual = £132.6m (Sharescope current H1). FY1 fc pre-RNS = £245.7m. H1 as % of FY26e = £132.6m / £245.7m = 54.0% vs 3yr avg 46.0% → deviation = +8.0pp — massively ahead of baseline.

But now FY26 actual = £265.0m (RNS). H1 as % of actual FY = £132.6m / £265.0m = 50.0% vs 46.0% → deviation = +4.0pp

Signal (had this been pre-H1 mode): 🟢🟢 STRONG BUY on revenue (+4.0pp above baseline — well above +2.5pp threshold). This validates the strength of the full-year outcome.

EPS H1 tracking (pre-FY mode — informational): H1 EPS 8.8p / FY26e 18.4p = 47.8% vs 3yr avg 42.9% → deviation = +4.9pp — strongly ahead. H2 EPS actual = ~£265m/£245.7m × 18.4p × H2 weight... wait: H2 EPS = FY26 actual EPS (~20–21p) − H1 8.8p = ~11–12p vs FY25 H2 10.2p → H2 up YoY. No burden issue.

Phase 3.2 scored row: pre-FY mode → no Phase 5 score row. Written for completeness. Column 5 still renders na for pre-FY.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — contributes to Phase 5)

H2 base figure: RNS provides FY26 actual £265.0m. H2 actual = £265.0m − £132.6m = £132.4m (RNS-derived). Prior year H2 FY25 = £118.1m. Implied H2 YoY = (£132.4m − £118.1m) / £118.1m = +12.1%

Classification: 🟢 strong (+12.1% YoY, above +10% threshold). RNS-derived.

EPS H2 check: FY26 actual EPS ~20–21p. H2 EPS = ~11–12p vs FY25 H2 10.2p → +8–18% YoY. 🟢 strong/moderate.

Phase 3.3 scored row: pre-FY mode → included in Phase 5. 🟢 strong +12.1% H2 YoY revenue.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net −17.5% over period (22.3p → 18.4p). Downgrade cycle completed by Jul 25. Recovery +2.5% Oct 25. Then flat 6 months at 18.4p. This is stale — the material upgrade has not yet been captured.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • Divergence: Price unchanged at 237p over 6 months as EPS flat — no divergence. Both stalled. This RNS will break the stasis.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS states net-cash positive at 31 March 2026. Sharescope FY1fc net borrowing = £7.3m (positive = net debt). Variance: RNS net cash vs Sharescope net debt £7.3m. RNS figure supersedes Sharescope. Actual FY26 net cash position — positive surprise vs forecast. ND/EBITDA actual: negative (net cash) vs FY1fc 0.20x. Slight better-than-forecast.

  • Net debt/(cash): FY23 H2 −£2.8m (net cash) → FY24 H2 −£16.7m → FY25 H2 £0.5m (minimal net debt) → FY26 H1 £19.9m (net debt, mid-year post-acquisitions) → FY26 year-end: net cash (RNS)
  • ND/EBITDA: FY1fc 0.20x → now negative (net cash)
  • Interest cover: 23.2x FY26fc
  • ND/FCF: 0.6x

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — Phase 5 silent.

Forecast year earnings check:

  • Step 1: FY26 actual revenue £265.0m vs FY25 £231.1m → ✅✅ growing +14.7%. EPS TBD but EBITDA growing → ✅ growing.
  • Step 2: FY2fc EPS 20.5p (stale) likely upgrades to ~22–24p. FY2fc Revenue £290.4m vs FY1fc £245.7m → ✅✅ growing. Note FY27e EPS stale — pre-upgrade.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • Vaping ban resilience: UK disposable vape ban June 2025 proved manageable (+10% YoY). Structural positive — removes overhanging bear case risk.
  • SlimFast full year in FY27: Acquired during FY26; only partial contribution in FY26 actuals. Full year = meaningful EPS uplift in FY27.
  • New manufacturing facilities: Two new facilities (including 40,000 sq ft wellness facility, £5m capex). Operational going forward — provides capacity for Drinks & Wellness growth. 🏗️ Running cost step-up in FY27 modest.
  • Margin compression: FY26 EBITDA margin 15.3% vs FY25 17.5%. Acquisition integration costs + new facilities + SlimFast dilutive in year 1. FY27 margin recovery expected as these normalise.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 Driver — Revenue and EBITDA "significantly ahead of expectations": Revenue £265.0m vs consensus £245.7m (+7.9% beat). EBITDA £40.6m vs consensus £37.0m (+9.7% beat). This is unambiguous — brokers will upgrade. The vaping resilience (+10%+ despite ban) removes the most significant bear case that triggered the Jul 25 downgrade cycle.

#2 Driver — FY27e upgrade from SlimFast full year: SlimFast contributed partially in FY26, delivering "excellent contribution." FY27 gets full year. Combined with FY26 EBITDA base of £40.6m beating consensus, FY27 estimates need substantial revision upward from stale 20.5p.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue (FY26e): Upgrade from £245.7m to £265.0m (actual). +7.9%
  • FY1 EPS (FY26e): Upgrade from 18.4p. EBITDA +9.7% above consensus. Estimated FY26 EPS ~20–21p. +9–14%.
  • FY2 Revenue (FY27e): Upgrade from £290.4m. SlimFast full year + organic growth → ~£300–310m. +3–7%.
  • FY2 EPS (FY27e): Upgrade from 20.5p to ~22–24p. +7–17%.
  • Target price: Consensus TP £2.37 (equals current close at 144p — wait, TP is 237p vs close 144p). Large discount already embedded. Brokers will upgrade TPs toward £2.60–2.90. Meaningful re-rating potential.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Significantly ahead of market expectations" is not cautious language — it's the strongest upgrade signal available in UK RNS parlance.

Key risk: EBITDA margin compression (15.3% FY26 vs 17.5% FY25) — brokers will need to model whether this is temporary (acquisition costs) or structural (higher cost base from new facilities). If margin does not recover toward 17%+ in FY27, EPS upside is limited. SlimFast's FY27 contribution magnitude is unknown.

Net FY1 EPS revision: upgrade. Consistency check: Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. ✅

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

(Not "Strongly positive" because margin compression creates uncertainty on the EPS outcome despite the revenue beat, and FY27 upgrade magnitude is hard to pin down without SlimFast full-year figures.)

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The definitive catalyst is "significantly ahead of market expectations" across both revenue and EBITDA. FY26 revenue of c.£265.0m (+15% YoY) beats consensus of £245.7m by +£19.3m (+7.9%) — the single largest metric move in this session. scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-H1 (Q4). RNS = H1 Results for six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26). SWG changed year-end to 30 June 2025. No FX rule — UK-domiciled revenues 78% of total.
  • Comparability note: SWG restated prior periods for revised revenue recognition policy (cloud-hosted software spread over contract life). H1 FY25 restated = Jul–Dec 2024 (£10.7m). The gross margin decline (20% H1 FY26 vs 30% restated prior) is policy-driven, not a deterioration of underlying economics.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 cns: EPS 4.5p, Revenue £35.5m. FY2: not in consensus.
  • Momentum: EPS +200% (1.5p → 4.5p — two large upgrade steps Jul and Nov 2025). Revenue: 39m → 35.5m (−8.9% — reflects revised recognition methodology). Last-4-week FLAT. Stock: 78p → 90p (Nov 2025) → 42p (current — de-rated despite EPS upgrades).
  • 3yr avg H1%: Revenue 37.7% (3yr avg). EPS: 20.0% (1yr avg only — unreliable).
  • H1 tracking baseline: Revenue 37.7% × £35.5m = £13.4m. Actual H1 = £14.0m.
  • H1 tracking (Revenue): £14.0m / £35.5m = 39.4% vs 3yr avg 37.7% → +1.7pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL (just above threshold).
  • EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE — adj EPS −1p H1 vs 4.5p FY cns; entire EPS delivery deferred to H2 in SWG's established pattern.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

H1 Results — Six months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26)

  1. Revenue: £14.0m vs H1 FY25 restated £10.7m = +31% YoY. H1 tracking: 39.4% vs 3yr avg 37.7% = +1.7pp 🟢 Mild Buy.
    "Revenue of £14.0m, an increase of 31% on the equivalent period in the prior year"
  2. Adj EBITDA: £0.0m (£9k) vs H1 FY25 £0.1m = flat. Entire FY26 cns EBITDA (£2.4m) must be delivered in H2 — binary H2 risk.
    "small Adjusted EBITDA profit for the period of £0.0m, broadly in line with that in the equivalent period of the prior year"
  3. Key H1 contract wins: £7.3m MNO extension (£3.5m revenue in FY26); ~£1m Government expansion.
    "A £7.3m contract extension and expansion with a leading mobile network operator… with £3.5m of revenue from this contract expected to impact FY26 results"
  4. Post-period wins (H2 already contracted): £9m financial organisation renewal; £1.3m UK telco network monitoring. Total >£13m H2 contracted.
    "we have more than £13m of contracted business since the start of H2, which support the delivery of FY26 expectations"
  5. FY26 full-year guidance: in line with market expectations. "confident in delivering improved profitability in H2."
    "the Board is confident in delivering improved profitability in H2 and achieving full-year expectations"
  6. Gross margin 20% vs 30% restated prior — policy-driven, not structural. H1 FY26 revenue = £10m new on-premise solutions at 21.5% margin + carry-forward from FY25; H2 expected to deliver higher-margin new solutions.
    "This component of revenue has a lower margin profile than up-front revenue recognised on the delivery of new solutions"
  7. Cash: £2.2m (H1 FY25: £3.6m). Adjusted for £1.5m post-period receipt = £3.7m (in-line). Timing distortion.
    "period-end cash of £2.2m… the receipt of £1.5m from the customer only arriving on 20 January 2026"
  8. Pentest: return to profitability. G-Cloud 15 application: expanding from 32 to 55 products.
    "Return to profitability in the Pentest business… expanding the number of Shearwater products available to public sector organisations from 32 to 55"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • H1 Revenue tracking: £14.0m / £35.5m = 39.4% vs 3yr avg 37.7% = +1.7pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL. H2 required = £21.5m. Business is deeply H2-weighted historically (Sharescope shows "current H2" = £28.2m estimated). The £13m+ H2 contracted business already provides strong visibility.
  • EPS: UNTRACKABLE. H1 adj EPS = −1p. FY cns 4.5p. H2 must deliver 5.5p — entirely consistent with SWG's established H2-dominated pattern (FY25 showed H1/H2 −1.0/4.0 → adj EPS 3.0p).
  • Revenue recognition caveat: The 37.7% 3yr avg H1% may be affected by the accounting policy change which defers recognition into later periods. Treat tracking signal with some caution — the underlying tracking signal is directionally correct but the exact percentage point deviation carries wider error bars than usual.
  • Structural flags: Revenue growth (+31%) driven by ongoing revenues from FY25 cloud-hosted contracts. Gross margin dilution is temporary and policy-driven. Software division declining (−12% H1) but small (8% of revenue). Cybersecurity market growing at 10–14% CAGR per industry data.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 — Revenue +31% and £13m+ H2 already contracted: Cavendish will lead with the revenue growth momentum and the strength of the H2 pipeline. The £9m post-period financial organisation win de-risks H2 delivery significantly.
2#2 — H1 EBITDA £0.0m — binary H2 delivery risk: Entire FY EBITDA (£2.4m cns) must come from H2. This is structurally consistent with SWG's pattern but will alarm investors who don't know the business well. Cavendish will need to explain the H2 weighting robustly.
3FY1 estimates: Hold at 4.5p EPS / £35.5m revenue. No change to FY1 forecasts — H1 tracking broadly in line. FY2: Cavendish may initiate first FY27 estimates (~5–7p EPS if H2 delivers). No third-party FY2 consensus yet.
4TP: Cavendish likely holds 90p (BUY). Current 42p = 53% discount to TP. Stock de-rating from 90p reflects investor scepticism of H2 delivery — not a fundamental issue. The £13m+ H2 contracted business is the key evidence Cavendish will cite.
5Key risk — gross margin 20% H1 vs 30% restated prior: Policy-driven but visually alarming. Cavendish will need to educate investors on the revenue recognition mechanics. If not clearly explained, the market may wrongly interpret this as permanent margin deterioration. Cash £2.2m (£3.7m adjusted) is also a concern for the uninitiated.
6Overall tone: Neutral / hold and wait. Cavendish publishes a note confirming FY26 trajectory on track with BUY maintained. The H1 near-zero EBITDA will not help rebuild investor confidence. The stock needs H2 delivery evidence before re-rating. Binary: strong H2 = 90p target achievable; H2 disappointment = further de-rating from 42p.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
50
/100
Confidence range: 44–56 · Pre-H1 mode · Rev H1 tracking +1.7pp 🟢
H1 Revenue tracking: +1.7pp → 🟢 MILD BUY SIGNAL (just above threshold)+5

Pentest profitable; G-Cloud 15 → 55 products; FY26 guidance confirmed+3
FY26 guidance confirmed in line — no negative surprise+2
H1 EBITDA £0.0m — entire FY cns £2.4m deferred to H2; high risk−7
Gross margin 20% vs 30% prior — policy-driven but confusing to market−4
Cash £2.2m (adj £3.7m); working capital swings; low liquidity−3
No FY2 consensus; micro-cap illiquidity; stock de-rated 90p→42p−3
EPS adj −1p H1; statutory loss; entirely H2-dependent−3
Software declining (−12%); revenue recognition policy risk perception−2
Baseline+50

Shearwater delivered H1 FY26 results with H1 revenue of £14.0m tracking +1.7pp above the seasonal norm (39.4% of FY1 consensus vs 3yr avg 37.7%), triggering a 🟢 Mild Buy Signal. Revenue grew +31% YoY (Services +37%), reflecting strong demand from blue-chip telco, financial services and government clients. Post-period, the Group has already secured >£13m of H2 contracted business — including a £9m financial organisation renewal — which substantially de-risks H2 delivery. Pentest returned to profitability and G-Cloud 15 will expand available public sector products from 32 to 55.

The dominant concern is that H1 adj EBITDA was £0.0m (£9k), meaning the entire FY26 consensus EBITDA of £2.4m must be delivered in H2. This is structurally consistent with SWG's established H2-weighted pattern (FY25 showed H1 EBITDA £0.6m vs H2 £1.5m annualised), and management confirms confidence in H2 delivery. The gross margin decline from 30% to 20% is driven by the revenue recognition policy change (cloud-hosted services spread over contract life) rather than a fundamental deterioration — but this will require broker education. Cash of £2.2m (adjusted £3.7m for one timing receipt) is low in absolute terms.

Cavendish is expected to publish a BUY-maintained note citing the revenue trajectory and H2 contracted pipeline, but near-zero H1 EBITDA and the gross margin optics will prevent a meaningful re-rating until H2 results in September/October 2026. This is a binary outcome: strong H2 delivery confirms the 90p TP case; any H2 slippage would create further downside from the already de-rated 42p. Watch points: H2 gross margin recovery as new high-margin solutions are delivered, and whether the Software division shows any sign of returning to growth in line with the FY26 expectation.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Full Year Trading Update (Q4/Full Year)

No EPS figure stated in this update — implied EPS derivation: PBT £2.1m, shares 12.7m; at ~25% tax → adj PAT ~£1.6m → adj EPS ~12.5p vs consensus 11.3p = +10.6% beat.   • Organic EBITDA growth delta: FY27fc EBITDA £5.7m vs FY26 actual £3.6m = +£2.1m uplift, driven by cost savings (£1m annualised) + revenue growth to £38.8m. Incremental EBIT uplift ~£1.9m after minor D&A step.

FY27 platform NRR was 72% in FY26 (FY25: 106%) — significant erosion, partially offset by new client wins. Active clients 626 vs 536 prior year (+17%). No order book figure disclosed. For ARR-model businesses: SYS1 has ≥80% recurring platform revenue — ARR coverage rule applies. ARR metric not explicitly disclosed in this update.

FY27 EBITDA margin guided "no less than 15%" (vs FY26 actual ~9.7%). This is a substantial guided recovery of ~5pp+. FY26 EBITDA contraction was wholly anticipated (investment year).

"Cost savings implemented in FY26 position the business for an improved EBITDA margin of no less than 15% in FY27, with the opportunity for further margin expansion as revenue scales"

  2. Qualitative tone: Board "comfortable with consensus Revenue forecasts for FY27 and the recently upgraded adjusted EBITDA expectations." Specifically mentions biggest ever sales contract signed in Q4 with new US client for delivery in FY27. Strong new business pipeline provides H2 FY27 revenue confidence.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements cover FY27. Company explicitly "comfortable with consensus Revenue forecasts for FY27 and the recently upgraded adjusted EBITDA expectations." EBITDA margin guided "no less than 15%" — floor language on upgraded forecasts. Biggest-ever US contract for FY27 delivery is an explicit new earnings driver.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — comfortable with upgraded EBITDA consensus, visible FY27 drivers (new US contract, cost savings), quantified margin floor. Points range: +6 to +10.

Guidance: qualitative + quantified margin floor · covers FY27 · language is confirmatory of recently upgraded numbers, not a new upgrade trigger.

No divergence: FY26 delivered in line/slightly ahead → FY27 guidance constructive. No contradiction.

3.6 Structural Flags

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

SYS1 · Q2 · Full Year Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — FY27 EBITDA margin guidance and new US contract: The "no less than 15%" EBITDA margin floor for FY27, combined with the disclosure of SYS1's biggest-ever US sales contract for FY27 delivery, is the dominant catalyst. Brokers have been waiting seven months with frozen estimates (11.3p EPS) for confirmation that the investment year delivered as planned and FY27 growth is real. The margin floor guidance of 15%+ on £38.8m revenue = EBITDA ≥ £5.8m vs FY27fc £5.7m — a validation, not an upgrade, but it confirms the thesis.

#2 Driver — NRR erosion and platform retention risk: FY26 Platform NRR of 72% (vs 106% FY25) is a significant negative for a subscription-model business. While offset by new client wins, brokers will scrutinise whether existing customer churn is structural. This tempers enthusiasm for the upgrade cycle.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 EPS: formal EPS not yet released; adj PBT £2.1m beats consensus £2.0m by ~5%. Revenue £37.0m beats £36.4m by +1.6%. Brokers likely to hold FY26 numbers pending July formal results — minor upward tilt possible (+2–5%).
  • FY27 EPS: margin guidance of ≥15% on revenue consensus £38.8m = EBITDA ≥ £5.82m vs fc £5.7m — hold / modest upgrade +0–5%. Revenue: company "comfortable with consensus" → hold. The bridge from EBITDA to EPS needs D&A (~£1.2m) and net interest credit (~£0.4m cash) → adj PBT ~£5.0m → EPS ~29.6p vs fc 23.0p. Wait — this implies a significant beat on the EPS bridge. Let me recheck: EBITDA £5.82m − D&A ~£1.2m = EBIT ~£4.6m + interest income ~£0.5m (net cash) = PBT ~£5.1m × 75% / 12.7m = ~30.1p vs fc 23.0p. That is a ~+31% implied upgrade from the margin floor alone. This is the key revision driver — brokers who rebuild the EPS bridge from the guided margin floor will upgrade FY27 EPS materially. Direction: upgrade, +15–30% range.
  • TP: consensus TP 446p — current price 291p, 53% upside already. Brokers likely to raise TPs, potentially back toward 400–500p range.

Conservative guidance read-through: "No less than 15%" is floor language — historically signals deliberate conservatism. "Comfortable with consensus" on revenue is also cautious phrasing. Combined, these suggest the actual FY27 EBITDA outcome could exceed the floor materially as revenue scales, implying upgrade cycle probability is elevated.

Key risk: NRR of 72% — if existing customer churn accelerates in FY27, new client additions may not fully offset, and the £38.8m revenue consensus could prove optimistic. Brokers will watch Q1 FY27 retention data closely.

Overall tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely — margin floor guidance + new US contract confirm FY27 recovery thesis; formal accounts in July will trigger formal broker upgrades. Score deferred to Phase 5 given NRR headwind acting as a brake on full upgrade-cycle classification.

EBITDA of £3.6m was in line with the pre-guided figure, reflecting the fully-anticipated investment year.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the implied H2 momentum is mixed — revenue H2 YoY +3.7% (🟡 moderate) but EPS H2 YoY −45.8% (🔴 severe), the latter wholly explained by the guided investment in sales headcount and restructuring charges totalling £0.5m. The bear case is capped: cost savings of £1m annualised are now embedded, cash is robust at £12.4m, and the guided EBITDA margin floor of ≥15% FY27 — applied to consensus revenue £38.8m — implies FY27 adj EBITDA ≥ £5.82m. Running the EPS bridge (EBITDA ≥ £5.82m − D&A ~£1.2m + interest income ~£0.5m = PBT ~£5.1m × 75% / 12.7m shares) yields implied FY27 EPS of ~30p, materially above the current stale consensus of 23.0p. The upgrade cycle is real but deferred to July full results.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are likely to formally upgrade FY27 EPS — the margin floor guidance alone supports a +15–30% revision to the 23.0p consensus. FY26 formal EPS will be confirmed in the July 8 results; expect minor upward revision (+2–5%) there. TP consensus is 446p vs current 291p — brokers are likely to reaffirm or raise toward 400–500p as the FY27 recovery thesis is now validated. The primary constraint on a higher score is the NRR erosion to 72% — if existing customer spend continues declining, new client additions may not fully offset, limiting the re-rating. SYS — SysGroup

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

SYS · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode. Interpreting as pre-FY trading update for year ended 31 March 2026.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 0.2p · Revenue £20.5m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 0.9p · Revenue £24.2m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change: 0.1p → 0.2p (+100%). Revenue: £20.5m held flat (no change). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT). One upgrade (Aug 2025: 0.1p → 0.4p), one cut (Dec 2025: 0.4p → 0.2p). Net flat from May start to now (+100% from 0.1p base but low absolute level).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue: 50.1% × £20.5m = £10.3m. EPS: 69% × 0.2p = 0.1p (2yr avg, limited reliability).
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £10.2m · EPS −0.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY26 actual £22.1m − H1 £9.9m (Sharescope current H1) = H2 £12.2m vs FY25 H2 £10.3m → +18.4% YoY → 🟢 strong. EPS H2: FY26e 0.2p − H1 (−0.1p) = 0.3p vs FY25 H2 0.3p (derived: 0.3 − (−0.8) = 1.1p — wait, Sharescope FY25 1y ago H2 shows 0.3p glitch where H2 = FY; deriving: FY25 EPS 0.3p − H1 −0.8p = H2 1.1p — however RNS states FY26 EBITDA £1.2m, FY25 £0.9m).
  • FX: SYS is UK-focused cloud/cybersecurity provider. No material non-GBP revenues. No Phase 0B.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Gross cash £7.7m · Net cash £2.7m (post-Saxis acquisition £1.3m cash consideration). FY26e net cash £1.1m (Sharescope) — slight discrepancy vs RNS £2.7m (RNS definition may differ). Interest cover FY26e 1.7x — low but not critical given net cash position. Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage (IFRS 16 lease liabilities included in net cash calculation; interest cover 1.7x is below threshold of comfort). No scored row unless 🔴.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SYS · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update

1. Revenue — FY26 actual £22.1m vs FY1 consensus £20.5m Beat: +£1.6m, +7.8% ahead of consensus. Total growth +7.6% vs FY25 £20.5m. H2 revenue +17.2% vs FY25 H2. Organic H2 +7.0% (excluding Saxis £1.1m contribution).

"Group revenue increased by 7.6% to £22.1m (FY25: £20.5m)"

2. EPS / earnings No EPS figure disclosed. Adjusted EBITDA £1.2m vs FY25 £0.9m (+33%). "Ahead of current market expectations" (vs FY26e consensus £1.0m EBITDA). H1 FY26 EBITDA was £0.2m, implying H2 EBITDA = £1.0m vs H1 £0.2m — strongly H2-weighted.

FY27e EPS bridge:

  • New base: FY26 EBITDA £1.2m, RNS-confirmed. EBITDA → EPS: D&A, interest, tax required. Adj EBITDA £1.2m; less D&A (estimated ~£0.8m based on prior periods), less interest (~£0.2m on leases), less tax (nominal given low taxable profit) → PBT ~£0.2m → EPS ~0.2p (83.7m shares). Consistent with FY26e consensus 0.2p.
  • FY27e: Organic H2 +7.0% annualised + Saxis full-year (£1.1m H2 contribution → ~£2.2m annualised). FY27e revenue consensus = £24.2m = +9.5% vs FY26 £22.1m — plausible.
  • FY27e EBITDA: If margins hold at FY26 rate (EBITDA/rev ~5.4%), £24.2m × 5.4% = £1.3m. But Saxis full-year integration should add operating leverage. Brokers likely model £1.9m (consensus). Revised EPS ~0.9p (consensus FY27e) — plausible.
  • Inorganic annualisation (Saxis): Saxis £1.1m in H2 → full-year contribution ~£2.2m incremental FY27 revenue vs FY26. Delta = positive for FY27.

3. Order book / forward work No order book metric. "Enhanced capabilities following the Saxis acquisition" — cybersecurity capability enhancement. "Positive momentum" entering FY27. "Improved go-to-market effectiveness."

4. Margin / profitability Adjusted EBITDA £1.2m vs £0.9m FY25 (+33%). "Increased use of AI across go-to-market and service delivery activities" — cost leverage. H2 EBITDA significantly above H1 (£1.0m vs £0.2m). Operating leverage visible in H2.

5. Capital / cash Gross cash £7.7m (FY25 £8.7m). Net cash £2.7m (FY25 £3.6m) post-Saxis payment. Net cash movement: −£0.9m after £1.3m Saxis cash consideration. DPS = 0.

6. Qualitative tone / outlook "Entered FY27 with positive momentum." "Further detail on performance and outlook" at July full results. No specific FY27 numeric guidance.

"With improved profitability, a robust cash position, and enhanced capabilities following the Saxis acquisition, we have entered FY27 with positive momentum"

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Guidance: qualitative positive for FY27. "Positive momentum" + Saxis integration complete. No numeric FY27 guidance. Revenue beat materially ahead of consensus.

Classification: 🟢 Constructive — clear revenue beat, EBITDA ahead of expectations, Saxis integration adding capability. FY27 guidance qualitatively positive but not quantified. Provisional points: +6 to +8.

No divergence: revenue beat, EBITDA beat, constructive outlook — consistent.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS-implied FY26 +7.8% vs prior year FY25 −9.7% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived). Column 6 REV: pos ✓
  • EPS: FY26 ~0.2p vs FY25 0.3p — marginally declining. FY27e 0.9p. Column 6 EPS (FY27e vs FY26): pos ✓ on FY27 forward basis; but FY26 actual EPS may be flat-to-declining vs FY25 0.3p. Using FY27e vs FY26e consensus: 0.9p vs 0.2p = acceleration → pos ✓

FY25 H2 EPS: glitch confirmed; derived 0.3 − (−0.8) = 1.1p — however this seems high given FY25 adj EBITDA was £0.9m full year. Using Sharescope FY25 full year EPS 0.3p and H1 −0.8p → H2 = 1.1p (derived). This is consistent with the H2-weighted EBITDA pattern.

Revenue trajectory: −7.3% → −2.9% → H2 +18.4% → 🟢 Accelerating (strong H2 recovery).

EPS trajectory: Volatile (loss-making H1s, H2 profits). Not reliably classifiable — 🟡 Volatile.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY (pre-H1 mode only — written in full, no Phase 5 row)

Revenue H1 3yr avg = 50.1%. At FY26 £22.1m: baseline = £11.1m. H1 actual = £9.9m → only 44.8% of FY — significantly H2-weighted vs norm. Buy trigger next H1: £11.1m × 1.015 = £11.3m.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Mode = pre-FY → contributes scored row in Phase 5.

RNS-derived: H2 revenue £12.2m vs FY25 H2 £10.3m → +18.4% YoY → 🟢 strong. H2 EBITDA: £1.0m vs FY25 H2 estimated ~£0.5m → strong improvement. H2 EPS: 0.3p vs FY25 H2 1.1p → decline on EPS (H2 FY25 was exceptionally strong on EPS). 🔴 severe on EPS basis — but this is against a comparison that included one-off items in FY25 H2.

Revenue H2: 🟢 strong. EPS H2: ambiguous given comparison base issues.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS: 0.1p → 0.2p (+100%), with one upgrade (Aug 2025) and one partial cut (Dec 2025). Revenue: £20.5m held static (no revision despite Saxis acquisition Dec 2025). 4-week: STALLING. Consensus revenue of £20.5m is clearly stale (actual £22.1m = +7.8% above). EBITDA consensus £1.0m vs actual £1.2m = +20% beat.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Net cash: FY23 −£0.6m (net debt) → FY24 £0.0m → FY25 H1 £4.6m → FY25 actual £3.6m → FY26 H1 £3.1m → FY26 actual £2.7m (RNS). Contingent consideration £0.5m (Saxis). Interest cover FY26e = 1.7x (Sharescope) — low. FY27e = 6.0x (improving as EBITDA grows).

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — interest cover 1.7x is tight but FY27e 6.0x shows trajectory. IFRS 16 leases in net cash calculation. No Phase 5 scored row (only 🔴 contributes).

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY26 revenue £22.1m vs FY25 £20.5m → ✅ growing +7.8%. FY26 EPS ~0.2p vs FY25 0.3p → 🚨 FY1 EPS marginally below prior year (−33%). However, FY25 EPS includes one-off items — flagging ⚠️ rather than 🚨 as decline is driven by accounting treatment differences and restructuring.

Step 2: FY27e EPS 0.9p vs FY26 0.2p → ✅ growing. FY27e Revenue £24.2m vs FY26 £22.1m → ✅ growing. ✅✅

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

SYS · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 Driver — Revenue beat +7.8% vs stale consensus + EBITDA +20% ahead: £22.1m vs £20.5m is unambiguous. Revenue consensus had not moved since May 2025 and did not update when Saxis was acquired in December 2025. Both organic (+7% H2) and inorganic Saxis (+£1.1m) beat the static consensus. EBITDA £1.2m vs consensus £1.0m = +20% — more directly earnings-relevant.

#2 Driver — H2 revenue +17.2% + organic H2 +7%: The H2 acceleration demonstrates the business has genuine operating momentum beyond the Saxis addition. AI deployment in go-to-market and service delivery is being cited as an early benefit — a credible and timely narrative in the current market.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26e) Revenue: upgrade from £20.5m → £22.1m (+7.8%). Confirmed actual.
  • FY1 (FY26e) EBITDA: upgrade from £1.0m → £1.2m (+20%). Confirmed actual.
  • FY1 (FY26e) EPS: Likely broadly held at 0.2p or marginally upgraded — EBITDA beat partially offset by Saxis integration/amortisation.
  • FY2 (FY27e) Revenue: Expected upgrade — from £24.2m toward £25–26m (full Saxis year + organic momentum).
  • FY2 (FY27e) EPS: Expected upgrade — from 0.9p toward 1.0–1.2p (higher FY26 EBITDA base, Saxis full year, operating leverage).

Target price / recommendation: No consensus TP available (Sharescope shows "−"). Zeus Capital (NOMAD) will rebuild model. Given the small scale and near-breakeven EPS, TP likely set on EV/Revenue or EV/EBITDA multiples. Post-upgrade, target likely in 15–20p range (vs current 13.5p). Modest upside at current price.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Positive momentum" entering FY27 + AI-driven efficiency gains cited. Standard constructive framing for a recovery story. No "not less than" language.

Key risk: Interest cover of only 1.7x in FY26e — if EBITDA disappoints in FY27, the leverage (predominantly IFRS 16 leases) becomes constraining. Revenue consensus for FY27 at £24.2m requires continued organic growth and full Saxis integration — execution risk is real for a company that has been restructuring. "This update marks an important milestone ahead of our full year results in July, where we will provide further detail on performance and outlook." — full results not until July, so detailed broker revision may be delayed.

Consistency check: Net FY2 EPS revision: upgrade. Tone: 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

SYS

62/100 · Confidence: 55–68 · No FX adjustment · 🟢 Constructive / modest upgrades likely

ComponentPts
🟢 Revenue beat +7.8% vs stale consensus — unambiguous upgrade trigger+15
🟢 EBITDA £1.2m — +20% ahead of consensus, first material beat+12
🟢 H2 revenue +17.2% YoY — strong acceleration vs depressed prior+10
🟢 Saxis acquisition adding scale (£1.1m H2 revenue) + cybersecurity capability+6
🟢 Organic H2 +7% — confirms core business recovery not just acquisition+5
🟡 FY26 EPS ~0.2p — marginally below FY25 0.3p (EPS still de minimis)−3
🟡 No formal FY27 guidance — upgrade magnitude uncertain−3
🔴 Interest cover FY26e 1.7x — tight leverage position−4
🔴 Full results not until July — broker model updates delayed−3
🔴 Small absolute scale (£22m revenue, £1.2m EBITDA) — limited analyst following, liquidity risk−3
🔴 EPS recovery nascent — FY27e 0.9p requires full Saxis integration execution−3
🔴 No consensus TP — limited price discovery mechanism−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: SYS delivered FY26 revenue of £22.1m (+7.6% vs FY25, +7.8% ahead of the stale £20.5m consensus) and Adjusted EBITDA of £1.2m (FY25: £0.9m, +33%, +20% ahead of £1.0m consensus). This is a clean double-beat against a consensus that failed to incorporate the Saxis acquisition (December 2025) or the improving organic trajectory. The #1 signal is the H2 composition: H2 revenue of £12.2m = +17.2% YoY with organic component +7% — the cybersecurity/AI narrative is translating to actual revenue growth, not just pipeline.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: H2 revenue growth of +17.2% (🟢 strong classification) is the operating proof point. EBITDA was heavily H2-weighted (H2 £1.0m vs H1 £0.2m), consistent with the executive team's commentary that operational and go-to-market changes deployed in H2 began to deliver in Q4. The upgrade resilience rests on: Saxis full-year contribution (~£2.2m revenue FY27 vs £1.1m H2 FY26), continued organic momentum in cybersecurity demand, and AI efficiency deployment reducing cost-per-deal. The downside scenario — revenue consensus misses in FY27 against a 1.7x interest cover base — is the genuine leverage constraint.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Zeus Capital will revise FY26e revenue to £22.1m (+7.8%) and EBITDA to £1.2m (+20%). FY26e EPS likely broadly held at ~0.2p (EBITDA beat offset by Saxis amortisation). FY27e revenue will be upgraded toward £25–26m and FY27e EPS toward 1.0–1.2p from current 0.9p. No consensus TP exists — Zeus will likely set a target in the 15–20p range (vs 13.5p current). Detailed model updates await the July full results. The watch point is FY27 organic revenue momentum — the Saxis inorganic contribution is visible, but whether the core SysGroup IT managed services business sustains +7% organic growth in a competitive UK mid-market is the key execution question. 🏁 Score 62 — clean beat on revenue and EBITDA against a consensus that hadn't been updated since Saxis acquisition; constructive upgrades expected from Zeus when full results publish in July; main constraint is small scale and tight interest cover limiting conviction.

scorecards.analysisText:
TICKER 6: TBTG

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY25 Full Year Results. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025). First full-year results since October 2025 IPO.
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 15.9p · Revenue £136.1m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 22.2p · Revenue £160.0m
  • Forecast broker momentum: Only 2 data points available (20 March 2026 and 21 March 2026) — EPS 16.1p, Revenue £136m. Essentially no broker momentum data; stock has minimal coverage history being IPO'd only in October 2025. 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat, minimal history).
  • H1 baselines (1yr avg): Revenue: 43.0% (1yr avg; FY24 H1/FY = 43.5/101.1 = 43.0%). EPS: H1 history too limited and distorted (pre-IPO structure). FY1 fc Revenue £136.1m → baseline H1 rev = 43.0% × £136.1m = £58.5m (note: FY24 H1 was on old structure with third-party revenue).
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24 H1): Revenue £43.5m · EPS negative (pre-IPO structure)

⚠️ Sharescope EPS data anomaly: FY25 H1 shows 640.2p and FY25 H2 shows 333.4p. These are clearly wrong — actual FY25 EPS should be ~15p range per consensus. The Sharescope EPS history (1y ago H1/H2 showing −35.3/333.4) appears garbled — likely pence vs dollars conversion error or data loading issue. Using FY25 actual EPS from the RNS: basic EPS = £0.11 (11p) reported; adjusted EPS = ~27p (adj PBT £29.5m / ~110.7m shares). Consensus FY1 EPS 15.9p is pre-RNS; will assess vs actual in Phase 2.

  • Implied H2 YoY: FY1 fc £136.1m − H1 actual £52.2m = implied H2 £83.9m vs FY24 H2 £57.6m → +45.7% YoY — 🟢 strong.
  • FX: USD and EUR exposure significant — US largest market (39.8% FY25 revenue). Non-GBP exposure clearly >30%. Phase 0B required.

Phase 0B — FX: US & Canada = 39.8% of FY25 revenue (GBP). No Currency Movements table in RNS. GBP/USD: current spot ~1.32 (approximate April 2026). Prior year avg rate from RNS: not disclosed. The RNS notes: "The Group does not expect its growth ambitions nor cost base to be notably impacted by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East" — no explicit FX commentary on tariffs or rates.

US revenues are priced in USD but costs are mixed (manufacturing in UK/India; some US warehousing). The business is not purely USD P&L — it's primarily a GBP cost base selling into USD markets. GBP strengthening vs USD would compress GBP-reported margins. However: the company guided FY26 revenue "in line with market expectations" of £160.0m — this guidance is stated in GBP, implying any FX impact is already embedded or hedged.

Given: no currency movements table, but ~40% USD exposure. GBP/USD April 2026 ~1.32; FY25 avg likely ~1.28–1.30. GBP slightly stronger vs prior avg = mild headwind. However, the guidance is in GBP and in-line with consensus → applying missing baseline fallback: neutral band (±2c from prior avg = neutral). Apply mid-point of 30–35% exposure band → −4 pts. However, given the company's guidance is explicitly in GBP at £160.0m consensus and no currency headwind is mentioned in the outlook, this is likely already reflected. Applying Phase 0B override: company's guidance stated in GBP at £160.0m matches consensus — no incremental FX adjustment. No FX badge displayed. ±5pp confidence widening applied.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results (year ended 31 December 2025).

  1. Revenue — FY25 actual: £141.0m vs FY1 consensus £136.1m → beat of +£4.9m / +3.6%. Own-brand revenue £140.9m (+60% YoY vs FY24 £88.1m). Third-party revenue discontinued by design (fell to £0.1m from £13.1m). All five geographic regions grew >25%.

"Total revenue increased by 39.4% to £141.0m (FY24: £101.1m)"

  1. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual: Reported basic EPS £0.11 (11p) vs FY1 fc 15.9p — reported miss. However: adjusted PBT £29.5m (+98% vs FY24 £14.9m). Adjusted PBT consensus was pre-IPO at £24.8m (Sharescope FY1 fc PBT). Adjusted PBT beats consensus by £4.7m / +18.9%.

The 11p reported EPS vs 15.9p consensus gap: reported PBT £15.2m, impacted by exceptional IPO costs (£8.0m) and pre-IPO finance costs (£6.3m) — both non-recurring and fully expected. Adjusted EPS equivalent: adj PBT £29.5m less tax ~£5.9m (34.9% reported; ~25% normalised = £7.4m) = adj PAT ~£22.1m / 110.7m shares = ~20p adj EPS. This significantly exceeds the 15.9p consensus.

Tax rate gate: Effective rate 34.9% vs normalised ~25% (UK statutory). Deviation = +9.9pp > 3pp threshold. Restated adj EPS at 25% normalised: adj PBT £29.5m × (1−0.25) / 110.7m shares = ~20.0p. Reported 11p is depressed by the 34.9% effective rate caused by non-deductible IPO costs. The 34.9% rate will normalise in FY26. 🚨 Tax-distorted year — FY25 reported EPS understates underlying. Use ~20p as the true underlying base for bridge.

  1. FY26e EPS bridge:
  • (1) New base EPS: ~20p (adj, normalised tax from FY25).
  • (2) Inorganic: nil.
  • (3) Revenue growth: FY26 guidance = £160.0m (consensus). Gross margin maintained at ~62.7% → gross profit ~£100.3m. EBITDA guided: company says "profit ahead of expectations" while revenue in line at £160.0m. Consensus EBITDA FY2 = £38.3m.
  • (4) Interest: pre-IPO finance costs (£6.3m) fall away entirely in FY26. Only lease/other interest (£0.5m ongoing). This is the key EPS driver — the removal of £6.3m interest charge + £8.0m exceptional IPO costs = £14.3m additional pre-tax flowing through FY26 vs FY25 reported.
  • (5) Tax normalisation: from 34.9% to ~25%.
  • Implied FY26 EPS (reported basis): Adj PBT ~£29–32m (revenue growth + margin) minus zero bank interest (post-IPO) → reported PBT ~£28–31m × (1−0.25) / 110.7m shares = ~19–21p reported EPS vs FY2 consensus 22.2p. The company says "profit ahead of expectations" for FY26 → implies above 22.2p, suggesting actual FY26 adj EPS heading to 23–26p (+3–17% above consensus).
  1. Order book / forward visibility: Q1 FY26 "very encouraging start... strong growth across the Group's core business and across all key markets." Tria Laser relaunched March 2026. ZIIP FY27 targeted as "breakthrough year." 40+ product pipeline.

"Very encouraging start to Q1 FY26, with strong growth across the Group's core business and across all key markets and channels"

  1. Margin / profitability: Gross margin 62.7% (+590bps vs FY24 56.8%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 26.6% (+400bps). FCF conversion 91.7% of adj EBITDA. Operating ROCE >50%. Balance sheet: net cash £40.8m, zero borrowings.
  2. Capital: No dividend (policy under review as business matures). Net cash £40.8m (vs net debt £27.1m FY24 = swing of ~£68m from IPO). £12.5m undrawn working capital facility (extended from £5.0m in March 2026).
  3. Qualitative tone — FY26 outlook: "Revenue in line with current market expectations [£160.0m]... due to stronger margins, it is anticipated that profit will be ahead of expectations." This is explicit upgrade-triggering language for FY26 profit.

"due to stronger margins, it is anticipated that profit will be ahead of expectations"

EPS quality check: See above. 34.9% effective rate for FY25 restated to ~25% normalised. Adj EPS ~20p is the correct base. FY26 removes all non-recurring costs (£14.3m combined IPO + pre-IPO interest). FY26 will show dramatically improved reported EPS even on identical underlying performance.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification:

FY26: Revenue "in line with market expectations" (£160.0m) + "profit ahead of expectations." This is the clearest possible split-guidance signal.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit "profit ahead of expectations" for FY26. Revenue in-line but margin beat driving profit upgrade. Exceptional balance sheet (£40.8m net cash, zero debt). Q1 FY26 "very encouraging." Provisional points: +14.

Divergence check: FY25 revenue beat (+3.6%) but reported EPS missed (11p vs 15.9p). The miss is entirely IPO/pre-IPO non-recurring costs. Outlook is explicitly better than expectations. Divergence: reported EPS miss but adj EPS significantly ahead + profit ahead guidance for FY26. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — reported EPS miss is structural (one-off costs), not operational. Adj EPS ahead. Forward guidance diverges positively from reported EPS.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

Limited history — IPO October 2025. FY24 H1/H2 split available. FY23 H1/H2 not split. Sharescope EPS data corrupted for FY25 H1/H2 — using RNS actual.
