FY2364.6———
FY24101.1+56.5%——
FY25141.0+39.5%~20 (normalised)—
FY26e*160.0+13.5%~23–26~+15–30%

*FY26e: company guidance £160.0m revenue, profit "ahead of expectations"; EPS uplift driven by removal of non-recurring costs (£14.3m) and margin improvement.

Revenue growth trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — +56.5%, +39.5%, +13.5% forecast. Deceleration is expected as base grows; still strong absolute growth. EPS growth trajectory: Insufficient clean history for EPS trajectory classification. Treat as 🟡 Volatile pending FY26 establishing a clean baseline.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: FY26e +13.5% vs FY25 +39.5% → no acceleration. No ACC REV.
  • EPS: FY25 first meaningful positive year; FY26 uplift from non-recurring removal. Directional acceleration. No historical base for comparison.

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

PeriodRev £mYoY %EPS pYoY %
FY24 H143.5———

FY25 H152.2†+20.0%——

†FY25 H1 actual £52.2m per Sharescope current H1. FY25 H2 derived: £141.0m − £52.2m = £88.8m. FY26 H2 = £160.0m − £58.5m baseline = ~£101.5m.

Revenue trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating on a HoH basis — H2 is consistently stronger than H1 (seasonal — Q4 Christmas gift-giving peak for beauty devices). H2 FY25 £88.8m = 62.9% of FY25 revenue. EPS trajectory: Insufficient data.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline & H1 Tracking (pre-FY mode — written in full, does NOT score in Phase 5)

H1 tracking (pre-FY mode — informational): Revenue: H1 FY25 actual £52.2m ÷ FY1 fc £136.1m = 38.4% vs 43.0% baseline → deviation −4.6pp 🔴 CAUTION — H1 FY25 tracking below baseline. But this is expected: the business is heavily H2-weighted (beauty devices have strong Q4 seasonality).

Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [43.0% × 1.015 × £136.1m] = £59.4m → £52.2m → 🔴 ✗

Seasonal note: 62.9% of FY25 revenue was in H2 vs 57% historical H2 norm — increasingly H2-weighted as the product mix moves towards premium LED therapy masks (peak gifting season). This makes the 43% H1 baseline misleading — the actual H1/H2 split is evolving. Phase 3.2 written in full. Does not score in Phase 5 in pre-FY mode.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (SCORES in Phase 5)

H2 base figure: FY1 fc £136.1m − H1 actual £52.2m = implied H2 £83.9m (pre-RNS basis; but actual FY25 H2 = £88.8m as derived above — H2 was actually stronger than consensus implied).

More precisely: RNS-derived FY25 H2 = £88.8m vs FY24 H2 £57.6m = +54.2% YoY → 🟢 strong (actual H2 delivered).

For FY26: FY2 fc £160.0m − H1 baseline ~£58.5m = implied H2 FY26 ~£101.5m vs FY25 H2 £88.8m = +14.3% → 🟢 strong (>+10%).

Mode = pre-FY → Phase 3.3 scores in Phase 5.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Only 2 data points (20–21 March 2026) — 16.1p → flat. No meaningful trend. Pre-RNS estimate was 15.9p (Sharescope current FY1).
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING — insufficient data.
  • Revenue trend: £136m, flat over minimal history.
  • Divergence: Share price 303p vs IPO-era TP of 470p — 35% below TP. Market has not engaged post-IPO; limited analyst coverage explains the discount.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

  • Net debt/(cash): FY24 −(net debt £27.1m) / FY25 net cash +£40.8m / FY1fc net cash +£30.6m / FY2fc net cash +£51.5m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY24 2.7x → FY25 −0.9x (net cash) → FY2fc −1.3x
  • Interest cover: FY25 1.6x (distorted by pre-IPO interest); FY1fc 5.4x (normalised)

Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — transformation from net debt £27.1m to net cash £40.8m via IPO. Zero borrowings. Does not score in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY1 fc EPS 15.9p vs FY24 adj ~0.6p → ✅✅ massive improvement. Revenue £136.1m vs FY24 £101.1m → ✅✅ +34.6% growing. Note: actual FY25 revenue £141.0m already beats FY1 fc — FY1 will be restated upward.

Step 2: FY2 fc EPS 22.2p vs FY1 fc 15.9p → ✅✅ +39.6% growing. Revenue £160.0m vs £136.1m → ✅✅ +17.6% growing.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

TBTG · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 and #2 Drivers:

#1 "Profit ahead of expectations" for FY26 — explicit upgrade-triggering language. For a newly listed company with limited coverage, this is a very strong signal. Brokers initiating or maintaining coverage will upgrade FY26 EPS from 22.2p to approximately 23–26p, driven by removal of £14.3m non-recurring costs and margin improvement. The company is explicit: "due to stronger margins."

#2 FY25 revenue beat (+3.6% vs consensus) and adjusted PBT £29.5m (+98% YoY). The quality of the FY25 delivery — gross margin 62.7% (+590bps), EBITDA margin 26.6%, FCF conversion 91.7%, net cash £40.8m — is significantly ahead of the IPO prospectus case. This validates the bull thesis and should attract incremental analyst coverage.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY25 (FY1) Revenue: upgrade from £136.1m → £141.0m (+3.6%). Confirmed actual.
  • FY25 (FY1) EPS: reported 11p — miss vs 15.9p consensus, but fully explained by non-recurring IPO/interest costs. Adj EPS ~20p = beat. Brokers will restate to adj basis.
  • FY26 (FY2) Revenue: hold at £160.0m (company guidance "in line with expectations").
  • FY26 (FY2) EPS: upgrade from 22.2p → approximately 23–26p (+4–17%). "Profit ahead" + removal of £14.3m non-recurring + gross margin expansion are the drivers.
  • FY26 (FY2) EBITDA: upgrade from £38.2m (company-disclosed consensus) to ~£39–42m.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 470p vs price 303p — 55% upside. FTI Consulting (IR) handling analyst presentation today. With FY25 beat and FY26 upgrade, initial/reinitiating coverage notes likely to set TPs in the 450–550p range. Canaccord Genuity (broker at IPO?) will likely publish a positive note.

Conservative guidance read-through: The split FY26 guidance (revenue in-line, profit ahead) is deliberately conservative on revenue. Brokers who model margin expansion may find upside to £160m on the revenue line if Tria launch and ZIIP acceleration are better than expected. The "40+ product pipeline" creates optionality not captured in consensus.

Key risk: US tariff environment for manufacturing/imports. The company is investing in Indian manufacturing to "diversify production base and optimise tariff positioning" — this is a proactive mitigation but the tariff risk to US revenues (39.8% of group) is real. Any USD/GBP FX headwind (GBP strengthening) would compress GBP-reported margins.

Consistency check: Net FY2 EPS revision direction: upgrade (22.2p → ~23–26p). Tone: Upgrade-triggering. ✓ consistent.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

TBTG

77/100 · Confidence: 68–84 (±5pp FX confidence widening applied) · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 FY26 "profit ahead of expectations" — explicit upgrade signal; non-recurring £14.3m removal transforms reported EPS+15
🟢 FY25 revenue beat +3.6% vs consensus; adj PBT £29.5m +98% YoY; adj EBITDA margin 26.6% (+400bps)+12
🟢 Implied H2 FY26 ~£101.5m vs FY25 H2 £88.8m = +14.3% — strong momentum (RNS-derived)+10
🟢 Balance sheet transformation: net cash £40.8m, zero debt, 91.7% FCF conversion+8
🟢 Q1 FY26 "very encouraging" — Tria relaunched March 2026; ZIIP FY27 breakthrough targeted+7
🟡 Revenue guidance in-line at £160.0m — deceleration from 39.5% FY25 growth to 13.5% FY26−4
🟡 Reported EPS 11p vs 15.9p consensus — headline miss easily misread without IPO cost context−3
🔴 USD/tariff risk: US 39.8% of revenues; Indian manufacturing mitigates but doesn't eliminate−5
🔴 Very limited broker coverage; minimal consensus history; price discovery not yet complete post-IPO−4
Total+36 raw → 77/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline is the combination of a +3.6% revenue beat (£141.0m vs £136.1m consensus) and the explicit FY26 guidance that "profit will be ahead of expectations" due to stronger margins. FY25 adjusted EBITDA reached £37.5m (+63.8% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 26.6% — 400bps above FY24's 22.6%. Reported basic EPS of 11p missed the 15.9p consensus, but this miss is 100% attributable to non-recurring IPO exceptional costs (£8.0m) and pre-IPO interest (£6.3m) that will not recur in FY26. On a normalised adjusted basis, TBTG delivered approximately 20p EPS — a material beat. The balance sheet transformation from net debt £27.1m (FY24) to net cash £40.8m (FY25) removes all financial risk and enables investment-led growth with zero reliance on external funding.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-FY mode, the H2 signal is striking: FY25 H2 delivered £88.8m revenue (derived: £141.0m − £52.2m H1), a +54.2% YoY improvement vs FY24 H2's £57.6m — well ahead of the seasonal pattern. For FY26, implied H2 of ~£101.5m (£160.0m FY2 guidance − ~£58.5m H1 baseline) represents +14.3% YoY — firmly in the 🟢 strong category. The upgrade resilience is structural: the removal of £14.3m of non-recurring costs (IPO exceptional + pre-IPO interest) from the FY26 P&L creates a permanent earnings uplift independent of topline growth. Even if FY26 revenue grows at only 10% (below the £160.0m guidance), the non-recurring removal alone drives reported EPS well above FY25's 11p. The margin thesis (62.7% gross margin, +590bps trend) and the 91.7% FCF conversion at operating ROCE >50% confirm this is not a revenue-dependent story — the quality is embedded.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will raise FY26 EPS from 22.2p → ~23–26p (+4–17%) as the non-recurring cost removal flows through and margins sustain above prior assumptions. Revenue held at £160.0m (company guidance). Target prices likely in the 450–550p range for initiating brokers — the 55% current discount to 470p consensus TP is primarily a coverage gap that today's full-year results presentation will begin to close. The key watch point is Tria Laser commercial traction following its March 2026 relaunch — the brand contributed only £2.0m in FY25 but is targeted as a "meaningful scaling opportunity" in FY26. If Tria gains early US distribution momentum, FY26 revenue could exceed £160.0m, driving a second upgrade cycle. The tariff risk on US revenues (39.8% of group) via potential USD import duties is the structural watch point for FY26/FY27, mitigated by the Indian manufacturing investment underway.

🏁 Strongly positive — FY25 adj EBITDA beat, explicit FY26 profit-ahead guidance, £14.3m non-recurring removal transforms reported EPS; price at 303p represents 55%+ discount to fair value; upgrade cycle starting as coverage builds post-IPO.

scorecards.analysisTitle: TENG · Ten Lifestyle Group PLC · 16 Mar 2026

analysisSections.title: Phase 0 — Routing & FX
analysisSections.text: Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (FY ends 31 August 2026). Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state. FX Check: No Currency Movements section in this trading update. TENG operates globally — the 3pp gap between reported growth (+6%) and constant currency growth (+9%) implies a GBP headwind of approximately 3pp. No single non-GBP currency confirmed >30% from this update. No FX Rule 1 triggered — however, the constant-currency differential is noted as a modest drag on reported numbers. This has been reflected qualitatively in scoring.

analysisSections.title: Phase 1 — Data Context
analysisSections.text: FY1 consensus: EPS 5.3p, Revenue £73.0m. FY2: EPS 6.3p, Revenue £76.6m. Forecast momentum: EPS net change +43.2% over period (3.7p→5.3p). Two clean upgrade events (Sep 2025, Nov 2025). Now frozen 4+ months. Last 4-week trend: FLAT. 3yr avg H1% of FY: Revenue 47.3% (3yr); EPS H1 avg = N/A (company was loss-making in H1 for most of history — EPS seasonal norm untrackable). H1 FY26 actuals from RNS: Net Revenue c.£33.7m; Adj EBITDA c.£7.0m. No H1 EPS figure disclosed. H1 tracking — Revenue: £33.7m / £73.0m = 46.2% vs 47.3% avg = −1.1pp (IN LINE, just within neutral band). H1 tracking — EPS: UNTRACKABLE (no H1 EPS figure in this update). Buy trigger: H1 Rev > £73.0m × 48.8% = £35.6m (not achieved). Sell trigger: H1 Rev < £73.0m × 45.8% = £33.4m (H1 at £33.7m — just above sell trigger, very narrow margin). H2 carries: £39.3m / £73.0m = 53.8% of FY1 consensus revenue.

analysisSections.title: Phase 2 — RNS Extraction
analysisSections.text: RNS Type: H1 Trading Update (H1 FY26, six months ended 28 February 2026) 1. Net Revenue H1: c.£33.7m vs H1 FY25 £31.8m = +5.7% YoY; +9% constant currency. 2. Adj EBITDA H1: c.£7.0m vs H1 FY25 £6.0m = +16.7% YoY. Margin 20.7% vs 18.9%. 3. Active Members: +23% to 436k (H1 FY25: 354k) — leading indicator for platform revenue scaling. 4. FY guidance confirmed: "We remain on track to deliver in line with the market's expectations for the full financial year." 5. New contracts won in H1: • Ten Digital Platform launched with leading UK bank (Large contract) • New digitally-enabled concierge with leading global technology company (new segment) • New Medium fully digital contract in Europe • New Large contract in AMEA — both to launch H2 FY26 6. Net cash: c.£9.3m (FY25: £9.6m). New £5.0m RCF with NatWest at lower cost. 7. FX headwind: +6% reported vs +9% constant currency = ~3pp GBP drag.
analysisSections.quote: "We continue to strengthen our market position through improvements to our leading customer loyalty platform. This provides 'better than the internet' results for the users of our service and supports contract wins and drives margin, efficiency, scalability and service quality."

analysisSections.title: Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
analysisSections.text: HoH GROWTH PATTERN (Revenue): H1 3yr ago: £21m | H2: £27m H1 2yr ago: £32m (+52.4%) | H2: £34m (+25.9%) H1 1yr ago: £33m (+3.1%) | H2: £34m (0%) H1 FY26 act: £33.7m (+2.1%) | H2 FY26 implied: £39.3m (+15.6%) FY revenue trajectory: +42.9% (FY24), +2.9% (FY25), +7.0% (FY26e). Normalising from hyper-growth to mid-single digit organic. H1 TRACKING SIGNAL (Pre-H1 mode): REV: 46.2% vs 47.3% avg = −1.1pp → 🟡 IN LINE EPS: UNTRACKABLE (no H1 EPS disclosed) H2 burden: £39.3m required (53.8% of FY). vs H2 FY25 £34m = +15.6% YoY needed. Classification: Strong — two new contract launches (AMEA Large + European Medium) support this step-up. H2 EBITDA implied: FY1 fc £15.5m – H1 £7.0m = £8.5m required. vs H2 FY25 ~£9.0m (Sharescope H2 EBITDA 7m). Doable but requires delivery of new contract ramp-up. FORECAST MOMENTUM: +43.2% upgrade cycle (3.7p→5.3p). Now frozen. Price completely flat (130p→71p net decline over period). Classic value gap — fundamentals improving, price stagnant. STRUCTURAL FLAGS: • Digital platform launch with leading UK bank — replicable template for other large bank clients. • New customer segment (global tech company) opens TAM expansion beyond financial institutions. • Active Members +23% is a lagging-to-revenue indicator: conversion typically 12–24 months. • Net cash position strengthening despite repaying loan notes — confirms cash generation.

analysisSections.title: Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
analysisSections.text: 1. Dominant line items: #1 = Active Members +23% + three new contracts across segments = platform scaling confirmed, with H2 launch visibility. #2 = EBITDA margin expansion to 20.7% from 18.9% — structural margin improvement, not one-off. 2. Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26) EPS: Upgrade 5–10% on better margin trajectory; EPS 5.3p → ~5.6–5.8p. FY1 Revenue: Hold at £73.0m; FY guidance explicitly confirmed. FY2 (FY27) EPS: Upgrade 8–15% as digital platform scales and new segment contributes; 6.3p → ~6.8–7.2p. 3. Target price: Consensus 130p vs stock 71p (83% implied upside). Brokers likely to hold/modestly increase TPs to 140–155p. The gap reflects execution risk that is now being steadily reduced. 4. Conservative guidance: "In line with market expectations" is clean and unambiguous. No profit warning. Combined with +23% member growth and new contracts, this is the strongest positive language available. 5. Key risk: H2 requires £39.3m revenue (+15.6% YoY) — dependent on two new contracts launching on time in H2. EBITDA acceleration from £7.0m H1 to £8.5m+ H2 is significant. FX headwind could reduce reported growth by ~3pp. 6. Broker-note tone: Constructive. Singer Capital Markets (Nomad) will likely issue a note reinforcing the upgrade cycle. Modest EPS and TP upgrades. Active Member metric will be highlighted as the leading indicator. Tone: Green shoots, platform model scaling.
analysisSections.quote: "The new contracts that we won during the period are expected to launch during H2 2026 and support continued growth into FY 2027. We remain on track to deliver in line with the market's expectations for the full financial year."

analysisSections.title: Phase 5 — Score Rationale
analysisSections.text: FINAL SCORE: 63 / 100 · Confidence range: 56–70 Score components: EBITDA margin expansion +1.8pp (structural): +8 Active Members +23% (leading indicator): +7 New contracts won across 3 categories: +8 FY guidance confirmed (no profit warning): +5 Revenue +6% / +9% CCs (clean delivery): +5 H2 FY26 contract launches (de-risk H2 gap): +4 H1 Rev tracking in-line (−1.1pp): +3 EPS UNTRACKABLE (information vacuum): −5 H2 EBITDA acceleration required (£8.5m vs ~£5m prior): −5 FX headwind ~3pp drag: −3 Price stagnant despite +43% EPS upgrade (credibility discount): −2 Forecast stalled 4+ months: −2 FX: No formal penalty triggered Verdict: A solid H1 update confirming the upgrade cycle is intact. EBITDA margin expansion, member growth, and new contract wins are all moving in the right direction. The FY guidance confirmation prevents any negative surprise. The primary constraint on a higher score is the EPS untrackability (no H1 EPS figure), the significant H2 delivery requirement, and the persistent FX headwind. A clean FY result in October 2026 would re-rate the stock meaningfully.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS -0.1p · Revenue £38.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 1.5p · Revenue £52.6m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +88.9% over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: STALLING (flat at -0.1p since late March).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 45.7% of FY1 consensus £38.6m = £17.6m.
  • Implied H2 YoY: Using RNS-confirmed H1 26 actual of £16.2m revenue, implied H2 26 = £38.6m - £16.2m = £22.4m, representing +36.6% YoY vs corrected H2 25.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B does not fire (no qualifying single non-GBP currency exposure disclosed; Middle East exposure is geographic, not currency).
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: current H1 £3.1m → FY1fc £1.6m → FY2fc -£1.0m · ND/EBITDA: FY1fc 0.60x / FY2fc -0.20x · Interest cover FY1fc: 0.9x — very thin · Debt flag: Manageable leverage
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Half Year Results (Unaudited Interim Results for the 6-month period ended 31 March 2026).

  1. Revenue figures — H1 26 revenue £16.2m, up 31% YoY vs HY25 £12.3m. Implied H2 26 = £22.4m, representing continued strong growth.
Revenue of £16.2m up 31% (HY25: £12.3m) with higher gross margins of 30.5% (HY25:28.7%) delivering a positive adjusted EBITDA of £0.1m (HY25: loss £0.7m)
  1. EPS / earnings figures — H1 26 Loss per share 0.83p, a 57% improvement YoY vs HY25 loss of 1.93p. H2 needs to deliver roughly +0.73p to hit the full-year -0.1p consensus.
Loss per share of 0.83p (HY25: loss of 1.93p), a 1.1p per share (57%) improvement on prior year
  1. Order book / forward work — Order book £31.7m at 31 March 2026, a 2.5x increase on March 2025 (£12.6m). This represents 82% of FY1 consensus revenue of £38.6m already secured. Order intake of £29.5m in H1 26 alone vs £10.0m HY25. Rebalanced order book weighted 23% Oil & Gas / 77% Offshore Wind.
Order intake during the Period of £29.5m (HY25: £10.0m), builds on the strong momentum evident in Q425, with a cumulative order intake of over £50m since 1 July 2025
  1. Margin, profitability, cost signals — Gross margin 30.5% (HY25: 28.7%), a +180bps improvement YoY. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at £0.1m (HY25: loss of £0.7m) — a swing of £0.8m.
Realised gross margin increased 180 basis points year over year, reflecting commercial discipline and ongoing improvements in operational delivery
  1. Capital returns — No dividend. Sale of Innovation House completed February 2026 for £2.84m net. CBILS loan repaid in full, replaced with smaller £2.0m GGS Loan. The Convertible Loan Note with SCF Capital Partners has expired, removing dilution overhang.
Following the third anniversary of the Convertible Loan Note... the CLN has expired... the absence of the CLN mechanism provides a cleaner balance sheet for equity investors
  1. Qualitative tone — Strongly constructive, with explicit second-half and FY27 visibility language, balanced against an explicitly flagged geopolitical headwind.
The Company expects trading momentum to continue and to deliver a material improvement in FY26 financial performance vs FY25 despite the regional impact and continued uncertainty caused by the events in the Middle East.

EPS quality check: No effective tax rate disclosed (loss-making, nil tax charge both periods). No one-off credits inflating the result — only exceptional item this period was a cost (£70k share-based payment charge). HY25's comparative loss was burdened by one-offs (£467k restructuring, £154k warranty/legal) absent in H1 26, meaning the underlying trading improvement is cleaner like-for-like than the headline suggests.

Outlook & Guidance Classification: "the Board anticipates strong revenue and profit delivery in the second half" — qualitative, with very specific supporting earnings drivers named (record order book at 82% of FY consensus revenue). Classification: Constructive. Provisional points: +6 to +10.

Divergence check: No divergence — H1 26 results came in "consistent with our guidance," and forward outlook is consistently constructive.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING
  1. Half-on-Half (HoH) growth pattern

H2 derivation check: 1y ago (FY25): Sharescope shows H1 -0.3 + H2 -1.0 = -1.3, but FY listed as -1.0 — GLITCH CONFIRMED. Corrected H2 FY25 = -1.0 - (-0.3) = -0.7p.

Sharescope H1 historical series for TGP does not reconcile with the RNS-stated HY25 comparator (£12.3m revenue / -1.93p loss per share) — treating the RNS-stated comparator as authoritative for YoY calculations.

Revenue trajectory: Accelerating — RNS-stated +31% YoY in H1 26 is a strong acceleration versus the FY25 full-year growth rate of -8.7% YoY, representing a clear inflection from a declining revenue base.

  1. Seasonal H1 tracking — RNS discloses exact H1 26 figures, qualifying as RNS-disclosed. Revenue tracking: H1 actual £16.2m / FY1 consensus £38.6m = 42.0% vs baseline 45.7% → deviation = -3.7pp → mechanically SELL SIGNAL territory.

However — critical context override: the -3.7pp deviation is driven by the FY1 consensus already embedding management's own guidance for a dramatically stronger H2, with Offshore Wind contracts explicitly stated to deliver revenue "beyond FY26 H1." This is a structural H2-weighting shift that should override a mechanical SELL SIGNAL read. Signal classification downgraded to IN LINE, pending H2 confirmation.

  1. Implied H2 momentum — Implied H2 26 (£22.4m) vs 3yr avg of corrected H2 figures (£17.8m) = +25.8% above historical average. Classification: strong — directly validated by the £31.7m order book.

Profit warning feasibility gate: Two of three conditions arguably met (H2 hurdle + fixed cost headwind from geopolitical disruption). However, the H2 hurdle here is specifically and concretely evidenced by a contracted order book exceeding the full implied H2 revenue requirement — declining to apply the full profit warning flag given this contracted-backlog evidence, but flagging elevated execution risk given the unprecedented scale of the required H2 step-up and live geopolitical disruption.

  1. Forecast Broker momentum overlay — EPS trend: net change +88.9% (small absolute base). Divergence: Share price rose from 20p to 30p (+50%), broadly tracking the EPS forecast improvement — non-divergent relationship.
  1. Balance sheet & debt profile — RNS-actual net debt at H1 26 (£2.7m) higher than HY25's £1.8m, driven by working capital absorption from delayed Middle East receipts, already reversing per management commentary. Debt flag: Manageable leverage — thin interest cover (0.9x) warrants monitoring but not a structural risk at this leverage level.
  1. Structural or one-off flags

H2-weighting structural shift: Management explicitly frames this period as front-loaded toward H1 Oil & Gas delivery, with higher-value Offshore Wind order book converting to revenue predominantly in H2 26 and beyond.

The recently announced large Offshore Wind Farm contracts anticipated to deliver revenue from FY26 H2 onwards

CLN expiry: Removes a £18m potential dilution overhang that had existed since 2023.

Geopolitical risk: Live, evolving risk factor already causing project delays, vessel idling, and delayed customer receipts.

Offshore Energy Services has seen a temporary deferral of activity as vessels remained out of commission due to the prevailing uncertainty in the region.
PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 and #2 Drivers — #1: Record order book of £31.7m exceeds entire FY1 consensus revenue of £38.6m, the strongest possible numeric evidence for guided "stronger second half." #2: Margin and EBITDA inflection (gross margin +180bps to 30.5%, Adjusted EBITDA swinging from -£0.7m to +£0.1m), demonstrating genuine operating leverage.

Forecast revisions — FY1: Revenue modest upward revision (+0-5%); EPS more meaningful potential upward revision (+10-20% in absolute pence terms). FY2: Revenue and EPS both likely +3-8%.

Target price and recommendation — Brokers likely to hold or modestly raise consensus TP (currently 30p vs close of 15p), given the order book de-risks the path to existing consensus.

Conservative guidance read-through — "consistent with our guidance" is constructive and specific; the order book disclosure functions as an unusually concrete, quasi-numeric form of guidance.

Key risk — The live, unresolved Middle East conflict has already caused measurable disruption and could worsen, threatening the magnitude of guided H2 delivery.

Whilst certain projects and service lines have experienced delays, and some increased costs, bottlenecks have recently shown signs of easing.

Consistency check — Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade. Tone label consistent: Constructive.

Overall tone — Constructive / modest upgrades likely

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
68
/100
Confidence range: 58–73 · Constructive / modest upgrades likely
Record order book (£31.7m, 2.5x YoY) — exceeds entire FY consensus revenue+12
Adjusted EBITDA swing to positive (-£0.7m → +£0.1m)+8
Gross margin expansion (+180bps to 30.5%) despite unfavourable mix+5
CLN expiry removes dilution overhang+2
Mechanical H1 revenue tracking below seasonal baseline (-3.7pp), though structurally explained-3
Live Middle East geopolitical disruption — unresolved execution risk to H2-4
Thin interest cover (0.9x FY1fc) — balance sheet flag to monitor-2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Tekmar delivered H1 26 revenue of £16.2m, up 31% YoY against HY25's £12.3m, with the standout figure being Adjusted EBITDA turning positive at £0.1m, a swing of £0.8m from HY25's loss of £0.7m. The single definitive catalyst is the record order book of £31.7m, a 2.5x increase YoY, which alone exceeds the entire FY1 consensus revenue figure of £38.6m and is now weighted 77% toward higher-value Offshore Wind contracts.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: As a pre-H1 mode ticker, mechanical H1 revenue tracking shows a -3.7pp deviation below the 3yr-average seasonal baseline, which would ordinarily flag as a CAUTION signal — but this is explicitly and concretely explained by a structural H2-weighting shift: the recently-won Offshore Wind contracts are stated to deliver revenue predominantly from H2 26 onwards. The implied H2 26 figure of £22.4m represents +36.6% YoY growth versus H2 25, a hurdle that would normally trigger profit-warning-feasibility concern, but the already-secured £31.7m order book exceeds that entire H2 revenue requirement, providing numeric quantum rather than vague management optimism. The principal offsetting risk is the live, unresolved Middle East conflict, which has already caused delayed receipts and vessel idling.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are likely to hold-to-modestly-raise FY26 revenue (+0–5%) and EPS (potentially +10–20% in pence terms off a near-zero base), with FY27 also likely to see modest upward revisions (+3–8%). Consensus target price (30p vs close of 15p) is likely to be held rather than aggressively re-rated, since today's results are confirmatory of an already-recognised recovery story. The main watch point and constraint on the score is the combination of thin interest cover (0.9x FY1fc) and the unresolved Middle East disruption, both of which inject genuine execution risk into an otherwise well-evidenced second-half recovery thesis.

🏁 CONSTRUCTIVE — record £31.7m order book (2.5x YoY) exceeds entire FY26 consensus revenue and substantiates the "stronger H2" narrative with contracted quantum rather than forecast optimism; EBITDA inflection to positive confirms genuine margin improvement; geopolitical disruption and thin interest cover are the key offsetting risks to monitor through to FY26 year-end.

HASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

THG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (Q1 2026 trading statement)

  1. Revenue — Q1 2026: Total £393.1m, +4.6% reported YoY (+7.0% CCY). THG Beauty £233.3m (+2.4% reported, +5.8% CCY). THG Nutrition £159.8m (+8.1% reported, +8.8% CCY). No H1 split yet — this covers Q1 only (Jan-Mar 2026).

"Q1 2026 revenue growth of +7.0% representing the Group's best Q1 growth performance since 2021"

Implied H1 FY26: Q1 £393.1m × 2 (rough estimate) ≈ ~£786m for H1 if Q2 broadly similar — vs FY25 H1 £783.4m = roughly flat to slightly positive H1 implied.

  1. EPS/earnings: No profit data disclosed. Q1 trading statement only. Pre-H1 mode.
  2. Free cash flow guidance: "Strongest Q1 cash flow performance in three years." Full year FCF guidance maintained at £25m–£50m. This is a significant positive for a business with elevated leverage — FCF will reduce net debt.

"Strongest Q1 cash flow performance in three years, underpinning full year free cash flow guidance of £25m to 50m"

  1. Guidance maintained: "Group maintains its guidance for FY 2026." Full-year guidance reiterated. Beauty accelerating vs H2 2025 (+5.8% vs +5.4% H2 2025). Nutrition +8.8% CCY — diversification into higher-margin categories (activewear, creatine, hydration).
  2. Structural developments: Activewear approaching £100m annualised run-rate. Dermstore (US) partnering with Flex (HSA/FSA). Lookfantastic Bristol store outperforming. Myprotein entering Kroger 1,200 stores (June 2026). K-Beauty revenue "more than doubled YoY."
  3. Risks: Elevated whey commodity pricing offsetting Nutrition margin. Middle East disruption ~30bps headwind. Asia (Nutrition) intentional decline as business transitions to licensing model.

EPS quality check: Not applicable — loss-making; no EPS data in this update.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

FY26 guidance: reiterated in-line, no upgrade/downgrade language. "Maintains its guidance for FY 2026." FCF guidance maintained. Q1 beat on CCY basis (+7.0%).

Classification: 🟡 In-line — guidance maintained, no new numeric upgrade, but operational momentum is positive. Points: +1 to +3.

However: the Q1 FY26 +7.0% CCY momentum suggests H2 could improve on this. Not scored in pre-H1 mode.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum

  • EPS trend: Losses deepening from −2.7p → −5.6p during snapshot period, then latest data shows −4.9p (recent improvement). Revenue upgraded by ~£94m over period.
  • 4-week trend: 🟢 RISING (loss improving −5.6p → −4.9p).
  • Divergence: Price has been broadly flat/slightly up (43p → 55p) in recent months while consensus EPS has been improving slightly — modest positive divergence recently.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

⚠️ THG balance sheet is complex due to IFRS 16. Sharescope FY26fc net debt £266.4m. FY25 H2 actual showed net cash £93.9m — this is likely the operating cash position before IFRS 16 lease liabilities.

Interest cover FY26fc 0.1x is alarming on face value but reflects IFRS 16 lease interest in denominator. Full operating interest cover is better. FCF guided £25–50m for FY26 — meaningful deleveraging in progress.

ND/FCF 8.2x FY26fc. Applying IFRS 16 materiality gate: ND/FCF >8x AND discretionary demand business → IFRS 16 retail regime applies. Non-linear EPS downside possible if revenues miss.

Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — IFRS 16 dominated; FCF trajectory positive but starting point concerning. Scored in Phase 5.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1: FY26fc EPS −4.9p vs FY25 −13.0p → 🚨 both losses, but loss narrowing. Revenue FY26fc £1,804m > FY25 £1,717m ✅.

Step 2: FY27fc EPS −3.0p vs FY26fc −4.9p → loss narrowing ✅ (directionally positive). Revenue FY27fc £1,878m > FY26fc £1,804m ✅.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

THG · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/12/26

#1 Driver — Q1 CCY revenue growth +7.0%, best since 2021: This is the headline number that will drive broker sentiment. THG has been in operational decline/restructuring for several years; a Q1 CCY growth rate of +7.0% — with Beauty accelerating vs H2 2025 and Nutrition +8.8% CCY — validates the recovery thesis. Lookfantastic UK orders +7%, US beauty market share gains, activewear approaching £100m run-rate.

#2 Driver — FY26 guidance maintained with FCF guidance £25–50m: The FCF guidance is critical for THG's re-rating. ND reduction toward manageable levels is the path to equity re-rating. £25–50m FCF guides net debt toward £216–241m by year-end (FY26fc £266m − FCF range = £216–241m). Modest de-leveraging but directionally positive.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26 EPS: Current consensus −4.9p. Q1 beat on CCY basis (+7.0% vs implied ~+5.1% FY26 consensus). Revenue likely revised up modestly (+1–2% = £1,822–1,840m range). EPS remains negative; modest loss reduction possible: −4.5 to −4.7p revised from −4.9p (−6 to −8% loss improvement).
  • FY27 EPS: Hold at −3.0p until H1 results.
  • TP: Consensus 55p vs current 37.78p = 45.5% upside. Brokers likely to maintain TP, no catalyst for raise. Possible modest upward revision on volume trajectory.

FX impact: The 240bps gap between reported (+4.6%) and CCY (+7.0%) growth in Q1 is a persistent headwind. If GBP remains strong vs USD, FY26 reported revenue will underperform CCY. This is the principal drag on the brokers' model — and supports the FX penalty of −10 pts.

Key risk: Whey commodity pricing elevated — directly impacts Nutrition margins. IFRS 16 leverage elevated. Loss-making consensus EPS means any revenue miss flows through non-linearly to widened losses. Asia transition reducing Nutrition revenue near-term.

Consistency check: Net FY26 EPS revision: modest loss improvement / hold. Tone: Neutral consistent.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — operational recovery on track; guidance maintained; but no new upgrade trigger, loss-making throughout, FX headwind elevated.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

THG

Raw score before FX: 44 → −10 FX penalty = 34/100 · Confidence: 27–41 (widened ±5pp for missing FX baseline) · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable · FX Rule 1 applied (−10 pts) · ~35% USD estimated · GBP headwind

ComponentPts
🟢 Q1 CCY revenue +7.0% — best Q1 since 2021; Beauty accelerating+10
🟢 FCF guidance £25–50m maintained; Q1 strongest cash flow in 3 years+7
🟢 FY26 guidance fully maintained; no profit warning+5
🟢 Activewear ~£100m run-rate; Nutrition diversification into higher-margin categories+4
🟡 Revenue PROBABLE BUY (Q1-derived, unconfirmed full H1)−2
🟡 Reported growth 4.6% vs CCY 7.0% — FX drag structural−3
🔴 Loss-making EPS throughout FY26/FY27; no path to positive EPS visible−6
🔴 Leverage elevated: IFRS 16 ND/FCF 8.2x; interest cover 0.1x−6
🔴 Asia Nutrition intentional revenue decline — disrupts FY26 numbers−3
🔴 No H1 actuals disclosed; Q1 data insufficient for EPS tracking−3
🔴 FX headwind: ~35% USD exposure, ~240bps Q1 reported vs CCY drag−10

Raw total (pre-FX): +10+7+5+4−2−3−6−6−3−3 = +3 → 50 base + 3 = ~44, −10 FX = 34

Para 1 — Headline numbers: THG's Q1 FY26 headline is CCY revenue growth of +7.0% — described as the strongest Q1 since 2021 — on total revenues of £393.1m (+4.6% reported). The 240bps gap between reported and CCY figures is the critical nuance: FX headwinds (GBP stronger vs USD) are depressing reported revenues by an estimated ~£9m per quarter relative to operational performance. THG Beauty accelerated to +5.8% CCY (from +5.4% H2 2025) and Nutrition delivered +8.8% CCY. The operational recovery thesis is intact.

Para 2 — H1 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the H1 tracking signal is 🟡 PROBABLE BUY (revenue) on Q1 run-rate alone — but this is unconfirmed without Q2 data. The seasonal baseline is £887.8m for H1 FY26; Q1 alone of £393.1m suggests H1 will be close to or modestly above this if Q2 maintains trajectory. FCF guidance of £25–50m is the most important balance sheet datapoint — this signals meaningful deleveraging from FY26fc net debt of £266m. The IFRS 16 leverage flag (ND/FCF 8.2x, interest cover 0.1x) is a persistent constraint: even a modest revenue miss generates non-linear EPS downside through lease interest coverage.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers will modestly revise FY26 revenue up (+1–2% = £1,822–1,840m), with EPS loss modestly improved to approximately −4.5 to −4.7p from −4.9p. TP consensus 55p likely maintained with no catalyst for a raise. The FX penalty of −10 pts reflects the structural USD headwind that brokers will embed in their models — reported growth will consistently underperform CCY until GBP weakens. Main watch point: H1 FY26 results for confirmation that Q1 momentum carried into Q2, and FCF delivery for debt reduction.

🏁 Operational recovery is real and Q1 CCY momentum is encouraging; but FX headwinds, IFRS 16 leverage, loss-making EPS, and a Q1-only data disclosure cap the score at 34/100.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

#1 Driver — Headline EPS 2.0p misses revised consensus of 3.0p by 33% Despite the Sharescope consensus having been cut from 5.2p to 3.0p over the year, the actual 2.0p is still a −33% miss vs the pre-RNS consensus. #2 Driver — Accounting reference date change complicates forecasting The move to a September year-end means FY26 is a 9-month stub period. Brokers will need to re-forecast on a different time basis. This introduces uncertainty and may delay analyst updates.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: TMG delivered FY25 results that missed the already-heavily-downgraded consensus: headline EPS from continuing operations of 2.0p vs the consensus 3.0p — a 33% miss. The headline operating profit of £5.1m (−34% YoY) and operating margin of 7.4% (2024: 10.3%) confirm the business has not yet stabilised. The reported loss of £18.8m was dominated by a £15.7m goodwill impairment — the largest single red flag, signalling that prior acquisitions are worth materially less than carrying value. Revenue at £68.5m is broadly in-line with the downgraded consensus but still −7.6% below the prior year.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience case is weak. The £4.0m annualised cost savings provide a mechanical earnings recovery in FY26 — adding approximately 3–4p of EPS on a 12-month basis. However, the 9-month FY26 stub period (September year-end) means only ~3p of this is captured in the next financial year. Revenue visibility is limited given the "Client caution" theme extends into early 2026. There is no order book or ARR equivalent to provide hard forward visibility, and the Sports & Entertainment segment (the only growth area in FY25, with +8% revenue) is modest in scale. The leverage ratio of 2.8x heading into FY26 on declining EBITDA is a constraint on investment and shareholder returns.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS consensus of 3.0p will likely be cut toward 2.0–2.5p as brokers absorb the FY25 miss and the accounting reference date complexity. TP likely cut from 55p toward 40–50p. The stock at 18.5p already prices in significant distress — the 197% upside gap to TP will narrow as the TP is cut rather than the stock re-rating. The main watch point is whether the CEO's strategic reset (simplified structure, AI investment, US Sports growth) can deliver a meaningful FY27 profit recovery when comparing on a 12-month basis. 🏁 Verdict: Material miss vs revised consensus, goodwill impairment, suspended dividend and accounting year change create multiple headwinds; downgrades and possible TP cuts incoming. Score 22/100.

PHASE 0A — ROUTING COMPLETE

Next year end: 30/6/26 → FY1 = FY26, prior year actual = FY25, FY2 = FY27. Routing: pre-H1 mode. RNS = H1 Results for the 6 months ended 31 December 2025 (H1 FY26).

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

TMO · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 30/06/26

The RNS discloses average exchange rates used in consolidation: USD average $1.34 (HY25: $1.29), EUR average €1.15 (HY25: €1.19). No single non-GBP currency exposure percentage is explicitly stated as exceeding 30% of revenues in a Currency Movements section. However, the company operates materially in USD (Manhattan, Lisbon, New York, Dubai all reported in USD) and EUR. The RNS does not provide a single-currency breakdown as a % of total revenue.

Given absence of an explicit breakdown and no Currency Movements table quantifying exposure per currency, the 30% threshold cannot be confirmed for any single currency. Applying the conservative default: Phase 0B not triggered — no penalty applied.

Note: USD consolidated at $1.34 vs prior year $1.29 — GBP has strengthened modestly vs USD (+3.9%), which would represent a marginal headwind on USD-denominated revenues. However, without confirmed >30% single-currency exposure this cannot be scored. FX: not scored. Note for context only.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

TMO · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 30/06/26

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting RNS as H1 FY26 results. FY1 = FY26, prior year = FY25.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS −0.3p · Revenue £109.6m (last broker entry 11 Oct 25 — consensus appears stale; no updates from mid-Oct 25 through Mar 26. All subsequent weeks blank. ⚠️ Consensus highly likely stale — no broker updates captured since October 2025.)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS — · Revenue — (no FY2 estimates in Sharescope)
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change full period: +0.0% (flat throughout at −0.3p). Zero upgrades/downgrades captured. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (all blank — no data). Revenue: unchanged at £109.6m throughout snapshot period. ⚠️ Consensus is frozen — no broker has updated Sharescope since mid-October 2025; any revisions post-Oct 25 are not reflected.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg — revenue only; EPS n/a): Revenue 3yr avg H1% = 48.8% of FY → 48.8% × £109.6m = £53.5m baseline. EPS: H1 avg split = n/a — EPS baseline cannot be set.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1, 6m to Dec 2024): Revenue £38.9m · EPS −1.9p (per Sharescope: 1y ago H1 = −1.6p; RNS states HY25 EPS −1.9p basic loss per share — using RNS figure as authoritative)

⚠️ Year-labelling note: Sharescope '1y ago' = FY25 H1 (6m ended Dec 2024). '2y ago' = FY24 H1 (6m ended Dec 2023). 'Current H1' = FY26 H1 (6m ended Dec 2025 — this RNS). The RNS FY year end is 30 June; H1 = July–December half.

  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode): FY1 consensus £109.6m − H1 RNS actuals £39.8m = implied H2 £69.8m vs prior H2 £50.6m (Sharescope '1y ago' H2) → +38% YoY (consensus-derived — confirm on FY results date. This looks implausible given stale consensus — ⚠️ consensus likely set before FY25 impairments and portfolio restructuring). EPS implied H2: consensus −0.3p FY1 minus H1 actual −1.9p = implied H2 +1.6p vs prior H2 +0.1p — also likely stale consensus distortion.
  • FX: Not triggered (no single currency confirmed >30%). USD average $1.34 vs prior $1.29 noted — modest GBP strengthening vs USD, informational only.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Adjusted net debt (ex-IFRS 16): current H1 = £50.7m (31 Dec 25) vs FY25 = £44.3m · FY1fc = n/a · FY2fc = n/a. IFRS 16 lease liabilities additional £41.8m. Total debt inc leases = £92.5m. ND/EBITDA: 3y ago 36.5x · 2y ago 9.2x · 1y ago 8.1x · current = n/a (EBITDA forecast unavailable). Interest cover: n/a. Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — see Phase 3.5.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

TMO · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 30/06/26

RNS type: Half Year Results — unaudited interim results for the 6 months ended 31 December 2025.

1. Revenue figures

H1 FY26 Group revenue: £39.8m (+2% YoY vs H1 FY25 £38.9m). Markets revenue £24.9m (+2%); Media revenue £14.9m (+3%).

vs FY1 consensus basis: H1 of £39.8m vs 3yr avg baseline of £53.5m → H1 actuals materially below the FY1 consensus-implied baseline — but this is almost entirely a consequence of stale/inflated consensus (£109.6m FY1 vs FY25 actual of £73.2m), not underlying performance miss.

"Group revenues increased 2% to £39.8m (H1 FY25 £38.9m)"

2. EPS / earnings figures

H1 FY26 basic and diluted loss per share: −1.9p (H1 FY25: −1.9p). No adjusted EPS disclosed. Group adjusted EBITDA: £6.0m (+23% YoY vs £4.8m). Operating loss: −£0.3m (H1 FY25: −£2.6m). Loss before tax: −£7.0m (H1 FY25: −£6.8m).

No FY guidance or EPS guidance provided for FY26. No adjusted EPS figure; headline EPS is statutory loss per share.

"Basic and diluted loss per share (pence): (1.9) [H1 FY26] vs (1.9) [H1 FY25]"

3. Order book / forward work

No order book metric. Pipeline of management agreements: Vancouver (2026), Abu Dhabi (2026), Delhi franchise (2026), Riyadh (2028), Prague (2028). No revenue quantum attached to pipeline.

"We have a strong pipeline of management agreements in negotiation and expect to sign more in the year ahead"

4. Margin, profitability, cost signals

Group gross margin: 84% (H1 FY25: 83%, +1pp). Adjusted EBITDA margin implied: £6.0m / £39.8m = 15.1% (H1 FY25: £4.8m / £38.9m = 12.3%). Media adjusted EBITDA turned from −£0.6m loss to +£1.9m profit. Corporate costs rose materially to £2.6m (HY25: £1.4m, +87%). Media opex fell 23% (−£2.7m). Exceptional items £3.1m (HY25: £2.0m, +55%). Net finance costs £6.7m (HY25: £4.2m, +58%) — driven by PIK interest on Crestline facility and increased borrowings.

Chicago Market closed January 2026. Boston Market licensed to local real estate developer January 2026. Pro forma benefit of cost reductions of ~£1m in future periods flagged.

"Media operating costs for the period were 23% or £2.7m lower than H1 FY25"

"Savings implemented part-way through H1 will also have a proforma benefit in future periods of approximately £1m"

5. Capital returns and per-share items / debt

No dividend. £8m equity placing: £2.9m received Dec 2025, £4.8m received Jan 2026 (post-balance sheet). Borrowings increased materially: adjusted net debt £50.7m (FY25: £44.3m). Crestline facility €34.4m loan notes — term expires 24 November 2026 ⚠️ — PIK interest reverting to cash pay at 8.5% + EURIBOR. Oakley Capital £5.2m unsecured loan extended to 30 June 2027 at SONIA+12%. Additional £6.0m Oakley loan raised; £4.9m converted to equity via placing. Going concern: material uncertainty disclosed regarding requirement to refinance senior debt within forecast period.

"The preparation under the going concern basis of accounting is subject to a material uncertainty with regards to the requirement for the Group to refinance its senior debt facilities within the forecast period"

6. Qualitative tone

CEO: "Time Out Group is well-positioned for sustainable, profitable growth." GCC/Middle East markets note: "All Time Out partners in the GCC region are currently trading, but with significantly reduced footfall due to the conflict." Management agreement portfolio now majority of mix. Media returned to profitability. Cost base described as streamlined.

No numeric FY26 guidance provided. No revenue or EBITDA guidance for the full year. Qualitative language only.

"With a more streamlined cost base, a growing portfolio of high-margin management agreements, and a Media division back in the black, Time Out Group is well-positioned for sustainable, profitable growth."

EPS quality check:

No adjusted EPS figure reported — company reports only statutory LPS. Loss before tax H1 FY26: −£7.0m driven by net finance costs of £6.7m (primarily PIK interest and lease interest). Tax charge: £0.46m (effective rate not meaningful on a pre-tax loss). No material tax-rate distortion applicable. Exceptional items £3.1m included in the statutory figure; EBITDA-based metric is the primary performance measure used by the company.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Exact guidance phrase: "Time Out Group is well-positioned for sustainable, profitable growth" — qualitative only, no numeric FY26 revenue or earnings guidance. Covers general trajectory, no specific year coverage. GCC conflict flag noted as a headwind with no quantum.

Nature: Qualitative-only. No numeric uplift. No "in line with consensus", no "ahead of", no "not less than" language.

Classification: 🔴 Cautious — qualitative-only growth guidance with no numeric support, issued in context of going concern material uncertainty, rising net finance costs, a portfolio restructuring (Chicago closure, Boston licensing), and GCC conflict headwind. The absence of any numeric guidance following an EBITDA beat is a cautious signal rather than constructive.

Provisional points: −5 to −8

Divergence check: Current H1 EBITDA beat (+23% YoY) but outlook guidance is qualitative-only with material uncertainty disclosed. This is a divergence — positive current delivery vs absent/cautious forward guidance. → 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery (EBITDA materially up but no numeric guidance provided and going concern material uncertainty flagged).

Note: Management commentary does not provide H2 or FY26 guidance. The only forward signals are qualitative trajectory statements.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Flat throughout — constant at −0.3p from June 2025 to mid-October 2025, then all entries blank. Net change full period: 0.0%. Zero upgrades or downgrades registered in Sharescope.

  • Divergence: Significant divergence between improving operational trajectory (EBITDA +23%, Media turnaround, cost reduction) and frozen/blank consensus — consistent with brokers having withdrawn or suspended coverage, or Sharescope failing to capture updates. The operational picture is materially more positive than the stale consensus implies, but the market (price 8.25p vs last broker TP of — ) reflects deep uncertainty around refinancing.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

Data rows:

  • Net debt (adjusted, ex-IFRS 16): 3y ago H1 £34.6m / 2y ago H1 £51.1m / 1y ago H1 £49.0m / current H1 £50.7m / FY1fc — / FY2fc —

🔴 Debt flag: Leverage elevated

Key issues:

  • Adjusted net debt £50.7m against trailing EBITDA (FY25: £7.1m) implies ND/EBITDA ~7x on last known full-year EBITDA.
  • Crestline facility €34.4m expires 24 November 2026 — within the current financial year. Directors have flagged material uncertainty on going concern regarding refinancing requirement.
  • Interest costs surging: net finance costs £6.7m in H1 alone (HY25: £4.2m) — at this rate, £13.4m annualised interest vs Group adjusted EBITDA run-rate of ~£12–14m annualised. Interest broadly consumes all operating EBITDA.

Forecast year earnings check:

Both figures flagged as stale — not usable for forecast-year earnings check in the normal sense.

Step 2 — FY2 vs FY1: No FY2 consensus available. Cannot assess.

Structural/one-off flags:

  • FY25 impairment: £35.1m — one-off, explains the severe FY25 H2 EPS distortion.
  • FY26 exceptional items H1: £3.1m (restructuring) — elevated vs prior year.
  • Chicago/Boston closures: materially reduce future reported revenue but improve cash generation.
  • Corporate costs +87% YoY in H1 — one-off restructuring/transition costs in play.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • Portfolio restructuring (permanent): Chicago Market closed Jan 2026; Boston licensed. Reduces reported revenue permanently but materially improves cash conversion. "These two changes are expected to materially improve Markets operating cash generation for future periods."
  • Media turnaround (structural): Shift from programmatic/affiliate to direct campaign revenues. Indirect revenues now <11% of media (was 25% in FY24). "Indirect revenues now account for less than 11% of total media revenue, a strategic reduction from 25% in FY24."
  • Debt maturity wall (critical): Crestline €34.4m expires 24 Nov 2026 — within FY26. "Material uncertainty with regards to the requirement for the Group to refinance its senior debt facilities within the forecast period."
  • Negative equity: Book equity −£32.7m — covenant and refinancing risk material.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

TMO · Q4 · Half Year Results · FY26 · Year end: 30/06/26

#1 Driver — Going concern / debt refinancing: The Crestline facility (€34.4m) expires 24 November 2026 — within the current financial year. Brokers will focus primarily on whether the Group can refinance this facility at acceptable terms. The material uncertainty going concern disclosure is the single most significant item in this announcement. It overrides operational improvements in terms of broker note priority. Any broker maintaining or reinstating coverage will lead with refinancing risk and timeline.

#2 Driver — Adjusted EBITDA trajectory / Media turnaround: The +23% EBITDA improvement and Media division returning to profitability (+£1.9m vs −£0.6m loss) represent the most credible operational positive. Brokers will note cost reduction is working and the shift to direct revenues in Media is structurally sound. However, with annualised interest costs (~£13m) exceeding annualised EBITDA run-rate (~£12m), the EBITDA improvement does not yet translate to cash generation sufficient to service debt.

Forecast revisions — FY1 (FY26) and FY2 (FY27): Consensus is stale (frozen since Oct 2025). Any broker reviewing this announcement will need to substantially revise:

  • FY26 Revenue: Cut materially — from stale £109.6m toward a realistic £76–80m range (H1 £39.8m + H2 implied ~£36–40m, ex-Chicago/Boston on a continuing basis). Direction: down sharply.
  • FY26 EPS/LPS: Likely to worsen vs stale −0.3p given surging finance costs (£13m+ annualised) vs EBITDA ~£12m — direction down (larger loss).
  • FY27: No basis to set given lack of medium-term guidance and refinancing uncertainty.

Target price and recommendation: No current consensus TP (Sharescope shows —). Price is 8.25p. Any broker reinstating or updating coverage is unlikely to set a TP above 10–15p without refinancing clarity. The risk is to the downside on any recommendation until refinancing is secured. Probability of recommendation change: hold/reduce at best until refinancing secured.

Conservative guidance read-through: No "not less than" or "comfortable with" language. The company provides no numeric guidance. Qualitative language ("well-positioned for sustainable, profitable growth") is standard boilerplate. Brokers will not read this as containing deliberate conservatism signalling an upgrade cycle.

Key risk: Crestline refinancing — if not completed before November 2026 the Group faces significant liquidity pressure. "The preparation under the going concern basis of accounting is subject to a material uncertainty with regards to the requirement for the Group to refinance its senior debt facilities within the forecast period." Even in a scenario where EBITDA continues to recover, the equity is deeply subordinated to ~£92m of total debt plus leases.

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = cut (stale consensus will be reset lower). Tone must be: Cautious or Negative.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable — driven by going concern disclosure, refinancing maturity in FY26, surging finance costs, and stale consensus requiring a reset downward on revenue. Operational improvements (EBITDA, Media turnaround) are real but insufficient to offset structural risk signals.

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

38/100 · Confidence: 28–48 · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

(Confidence range wide given stale consensus — scores are calibrated against operational delivery relative to prior period, not vs consensus)

🔴 Leverage elevated — adj net debt £50.7m; negative equity −£32.7m−8
🔴 Stale consensus — FY1 £109.6m / −0.3p requires material downward reset−12

Raw total: −22 → adjusted to 38/100 (floor applied; absolute score reflects that broker consensus is being reset downward but operational trajectory is genuinely improving within a constrained financial structure)

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The #1 metric is not revenue or EPS performance — it is the going concern material uncertainty disclosure, which will dominate any broker note. On the operational scorecard, the headline positive is Group adjusted EBITDA of £6.0m (+23% YoY vs £4.8m), with the Media division turning from a −£0.6m loss to +£1.9m profit — a genuine strategic inflection point. Revenue grew a modest +2% to £39.8m (vs H1 FY25 £38.9m), with Markets +2% and Media +3%. On a like-for-like basis ex-Chicago and Boston, management states revenue grew +5%. Statutory loss per share was flat at −1.9p (H1 FY25: −1.9p), with the improvement in EBITDA fully consumed by exceptional items (£3.1m) and surging net finance costs (£6.7m, +58% YoY).

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: In pre-H1 mode, the H1 tracking calculation is UNTRACKABLE — Sharescope consensus is frozen at stale pre-restructuring levels (FY26 revenue £109.6m vs H1 actuals of £39.8m, implying a £69.8m H2 which bears no relationship to current Group reality). The Cautious outlook classification (−6 pts) reflects the absence of any numeric FY guidance and the explicit going concern disclosure. The upgrade resilience case rests on the Media turnaround being sustained (direct revenues 77% of media mix, repeat clients 63%), the portfolio rationalisation releasing operational cash (Chicago/Boston exit improving cash generation materially), and the pro forma £1m annualised benefit from H1 cost actions. However, the structural constraint is severe: annualised net finance costs of ~£13m (H1: £6.7m) broadly match or exceed the annualised adjusted EBITDA run-rate (~£12m), meaning the operational recovery does not yet translate to free cash flow. The downside is not contained — the Crestline facility refinancing is the single binary risk event for this investment case.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Any broker covering TMO must reset FY26 consensus materially. Revenue: the stale £109.6m FY1 consensus requires a downward revision toward a realistic £76–82m range (H1 £39.8m; H2 guided by portfolio changes and recent run-rates). EPS/LPS: the stale −0.3p FY26 consensus is likely to be revised to −3p to −5p or wider loss per share, reflecting £13m+ annualised finance costs against ~£12m EBITDA. Target price: no current consensus TP — any reinstated TP will be heavily caveated on refinancing outcome. The watch point is the Crestline €34.4m facility expiry on 24 November 2026 — resolution of this (refinancing, asset disposal, or equity raise) is the single gating event for any re-rating. Until that is resolved, the share price (8.25p) and market cap (~£43m) will remain depressed relative to operational asset value. 🏁 Verdict: Operationally improving but financially distressed — broker consensus will be reset sharply lower on revenue and EPS; going concern disclosure makes this uninvestable for mainstream funds until refinancing is secured. Score 38/100.

Net profit £850k (FY24: loss £60k). The dramatic EPS beat vs consensus (15.4p vs 10.3p) is primarily driven by a £282k deferred tax credit (vs expected tax expense) — not pure underlying earnings. Adjusted for the tax benefit, underlying EPS would be closer to consensus. "Diluted EPS of 15.4 pence per ordinary share (FY24: loss of 1.1 pence)" "reflecting the benefit of deferred tax credits during the year, statutory net income of £850k"
  3. Order book / forward work: No explicit order book. Trading momentum entering 2026 described as "positive, with early sales performance tracking in line with the Board's expectations." Toys Sports & Leisure FOB and domestic channels "ahead of the prior year." New licensed brands for 2026 (Toy Story, Dora, Marvel Avengers, Netflix K-Pop Demon Hunters). Bicycle international launch. Net debt halved from £4.3m to £1.9m. Inventory reduced £5.9m to £4.4m — significant working capital improvement. "Gross profit margin of 31.1% - an increase of 120 bps (FY24: 29.9%)"

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode)

Full-year actuals available: FY25 revenue £26.2m vs FY24 £24.6m = +6.5% — classify 🟡 moderate (+0–10%).

H2 FY25 revenue implied £15.0m vs H2 FY24 £14.8m = +1.4% — 🟡 flat-to-moderate.

H2 FY25 was the stronger half operationally (Bicycles +37.5% full-year, strong H2 seasonality). The margin expansion to 31.1% was the standout.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Flat at 8.5p from May 25 through Feb 26, then single upgrade to 10.3p in mid-Feb 26. Consensus TP unmoved at 350p throughout. Revenue forecast trimmed from £27.3m to £26.2m (−4%) suggesting brokers anticipated the TSL division weakness.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat since mid-Feb)
  • Divergence: Price 167.5p vs TP 350p = 109% upside to consensus TP — extraordinary discount. However, this is an illiquid AIM stock with single-broker coverage. The TP represents a single broker's view and should be treated with caution in context.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

Tax credit distortion: The £282k deferred tax credit inflates statutory net profit to £850k and EPS to 15.4p. Underlying (pre-deferred tax) net profit is £568k, implying underlying EPS ~10.3p — which coincidentally matches consensus exactly.

"reflecting the benefit of deferred tax credits during the year, statutory net income of £850k"

Toys Sports & Leisure decline −17.5%: A material drag. Brokers will watch for whether the FOB/domestic channels ahead of prior year statement in the outlook section holds through H1 FY26. If TSL recovers, FY26 revenue growth accelerates.

Dividend reinstatement: 3.0p proposed — signals Board confidence but modest yield at 167.5p (1.8%).

TND — PHASE 4

#1 Driver — Gross margin expansion to 31.1% (+120bps): Brokers will focus on this as evidence that the business model is improving structurally, not just cyclically. Better hedging, less clearance, and mix shift to Bicycles (higher margin) drove the improvement. This is repeatable and supports FY26 margin forecasts.

#2 Driver — EPS beat of +49% vs consensus — but caveat essential: The headline EPS of 15.4p vs 10.3p looks dramatic. Brokers will immediately strip out the £282k deferred tax credit and benchmark against underlying PBT. Underlying EPS of ~10–11p vs consensus 10.3p = essentially in line. The tax credit boost is real cash (deferred tax asset recognition) but not recurring. Brokers will note the beat cautiously.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (now FY26): Revenue — expect hold/slight upgrade to £26.5–27.0m, reflecting FY25 in-line print and positive early trading. EPS — expect upgrade to 11.0–12.0p as brokers revise up underlying PBT given 31.1% gross margin and net debt trajectory; the FY25 statutory 15.4p sets a high bar that will not be maintained.
  • FY2 (FY27): Revenue £27.5–28.5m. EPS £10.5–11.5p — gradual progression.
  • Target price: Consensus TP 350p — single-broker coverage, unlikely to move dramatically. Price at 167.5p with 109% upside to TP already priced in a recovery thesis. Hold TP at 350p or minor tweak.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Trading in line with Board's expectations" and TSL ahead of prior year is positive but not quantified. Does not contain "not less than" language. Tone is measured rather than bullish.

Key risk: Toys Sports & Leisure — a £2.2m YoY decline that remains the structural weak spot. If retailer purchasing patterns do not normalise in FY26, revenue could disappoint. "reflecting softer demand across certain discretionary categories, changes in retailer purchasing patterns" — these are macro factors not fully in management's control.

Overall tone: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — the underlying print is in line, the EPS beat is tax-driven rather than operational, and the growth story is intact but gradual. Dividend reinstatement is a positive signal. Very limited broker coverage limits upgrade cycle dynamics.

TND — PHASE 5

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

58/100 · Confidence: 50–65 · No FX adjustment · 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait

ComponentPts
🟢 Gross margin +120bps to 31.1% — structural improvement+14
🟢 Revenue in line with consensus (£26.15m vs £26.2m)+10
🟢 Net debt halved £4.3m → £1.9m; inventory down £1.5m+10

🔴 Toys Sports & Leisure −17.5% — significant structural weakness−8
🟡 Single-broker coverage limits upgrade cycle−6

🟡 "In line with expectations" outlook — no upgrade catalyst−4
🟢 Property revaluation +£1.8m; net assets £26.1m vs market cap ~£9.2m+4
🟡 AIM illiquidity; micro-cap; limited institutional following−3
🟢 Early FY26 trading positive across TSL and Bicycles+4
🔴 Middle East shipping cost risk flagged−3
🟡 Underlying PBT £692k vs £510k: solid but modest absolute level−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: TND delivered FY25 revenue of £26.15m (+6.2% YoY), landing essentially spot-on consensus of £26.2m. The headline EPS of 15.4p vs consensus 10.3p appears a dramatic +49% beat, but the definitive catalyst beneath the surface is the gross margin expansion to 31.1% (+120bps), which is the genuine operational outperformance. The EPS beat is materially inflated by a £282k deferred tax credit that pushes statutory net profit to £850k. Strip this out and underlying EPS aligns with consensus at ~10.3p. Bicycles was the standout division at +37.5% revenue growth to £10.2m, outperforming the broader sector.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The business is structurally improving — net debt halved from £4.3m to £1.9m, inventory reduced by £1.5m, and gross margin expanded for a second consecutive year. The implied H2 FY25 revenue of £15.0m (+1.4% vs H2 FY24) confirms the seasonal H2-weighting is intact and growing. The bear case is the Toys Sports & Leisure division, which declined 17.5% YoY (a £2.2m revenue shortfall), driven by retailer purchasing pattern changes and softer discretionary demand. This drag was known to brokers (consensus revenue came down from £27.3m to £26.2m in mid-Feb) and is already in the base. The dividend reinstatement at 3.0p and early FY26 trading described as TSL "ahead of prior year" in both FOB and domestic channels is the key reason the downside risk is contained — the TSL recovery appears underway.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: With single-broker coverage (Cavendish), the revision dynamics are muted. Expect FY26 (now FY1) EPS to be revised to 11.0–12.0p as brokers model the 31.1% gross margin into the forward and recognise the underlying operating leverage. Revenue for FY26 likely moves to £26.5–27.0m. TP likely held at 350p — already representing 109% upside and reflecting the significant discount to net assets (NAV £26.1m vs market cap ~£9.2m). The main watch-point is whether TSL's positive early momentum sustains through H1 FY26; if it does, FY26 revenue could surprise to the upside. 🏁 TND is a hold: the results are solid and in line operationally, the balance sheet improvement is real, and the dividend reinstatement is encouraging — but the EPS beat is largely a tax artefact and the upgrade cycle is structurally limited by single-broker coverage and micro-cap illiquidity.

TPFG delivered record FY25 results with adjusted EPS of 40.3p — a 8.9% beat against the 37.0p consensus — and revenue exactly in line at £84.3m. The beat was broad-based: all three divisions (Franchising, Financial Services, Licensing) delivered growth; EBITDA grew 49% to £30.3m with adjusted operating margin expanding to 38% (+400bps); and the balance sheet improved dramatically to net debt of £2.3m (leverage <0.1x), significantly ahead of expectations.

The structural improvement in earnings quality is the key investment thesis. The integration of Belvoir and GPEA has delivered synergies ahead of schedule, the Privilege programme generated £1.5m incremental revenue in year one, and the SAFS acquisition (315 advisers, immediately accretive) provides FY26 EPS accretion. The AI sales agent deployed in early 2026 is generating 25% more valuation appointments — a structural productivity improvement. The balance sheet at <0.1x leverage provides significant M&A firepower for further platform building.

FY26 EPS should be upgraded from 37.0p to the 42–45p range. The primary near-term risk is the Renters' Rights Act driving further portfolio moderation, but the franchise model's regulatory navigation capability and Privilege programme provide meaningful mitigation. Canaccord will issue a strongly positive upgrade note; the stock at 412.5p trades at a significant discount to what should be a revised TP of 700–750p+.

Critical structural note: The EPS SELL SIGNAL is a baseline artefact, not an earnings failure. The enlarged group post-acquisitions has materially shifted its H1/H2 EPS split to approximately 45%/55% vs the historical 49%/51%. H2 EPS of 22.2p (+36% YoY) confirms this — the group deliberately loaded more earnings into H2 through Privilege programme timing, full-year synergy delivery and structural tax rate improvement. Brokers should update H1 baselines to reflect the new post-acquisition seasonal pattern.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

  • H2 FY25 Revenue: £44.0m vs prior H2 £40.5m → +8.6% YoY → moderate classification
  • H2 FY25 EPS: 22.2p vs prior H2 16.3p → [+36.2% YoY] → strong classification

H2 EPS surge driven by: full-year synergy delivery, improved tax rate (22% vs 29%), Privilege programme H2 weighting, FS productivity gains. Classic operating leverage from largely fixed cost base.

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net +5.1% (+1.8p) across full 10-month snapshot. Upgrade steps: Jun +0.6p, Aug +0.5p, Sep +0.5p, Dec +0.7p, Jan-Feb minor volatility around 37.0p.
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (37.0p vs 37.0p four weeks prior)
  • Revenue trend: £83.5m → £84.3m (+1.0%) — modest upward drift
  • Price divergence: Stock fell from 649p (Sep–Nov 2025 peak) to 412p — a 36% price decline against broadly flat-to-rising EPS forecasts. Market pricing Renters' Rights Act risk; FY results demonstrate this is overdone.

5. Structural / One-Off Flags

  • H1/H2 EPS split shift (structural): Post-acquisition group has moved to approximately 45%/55% H1/H2 EPS split vs historical 49%/51%. Brokers using pre-acquisition baselines will systematically underestimate H2 delivery. "The Group benefits from a relatively fixed cost base, where cost increases typically lag revenue growth, creating opportunities for operating leverage as the Group continues to scale."
  • Tax rate step-down (partly structural): Effective rate 22% vs 29% prior year. Deferred tax on acquired intangibles is a multi-year structural benefit. Model at 22–24% going forward.
  • Managed portfolio contraction — Renters' Rights Act (watchpoint): 149k vs 153k (−2.6%). Management frames as temporary and manageable; Privilege programme offsets. Risk: if RRA accelerates structural landlord exit, lettings MSF faces multi-year headwind. "Managed portfolio of 149,000 properties (2024: 153,000), reflecting landlord caution ahead of the Renters' Rights Act"
  • AI initiatives (emerging upside): AI sales agent live in 2026, 25% more valuation appointments. Property management automation to roll out H2 FY26. Not yet in consensus — potential future upgrade catalyst.
PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 — Adjusted EPS +8.9% beat (40.3p vs 37.0p consensus). This is the primary actionable signal for broker models and TP revisions. The beat is material, clean and flows through margin expansion and tax improvement rather than one-off items. #2 — Margin expansion + cash generation quality. Adjusted operating margin 38% (vs 34% prior year), net debt £2.3m, cash conversion 116%. These validate the quality of the EPS beat and support higher EV-based TPs. Franchise models are valued on recurring revenue multiples and FCF yield; near-zero leverage removes the only remaining valuation concern.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 (FY26) EPS: Pre-RNS 37.0p → expect upgrades of +8–12% to approximately 40–42p. Revenue: +2–4% to ~£87–88m. FY2 (FY27) EPS: Pre-RNS 38.7p → expect upgrades of +5–9% to approximately 42–45p. Revenue: FY2 likely moves to £90–92m.
  1. Target price and recommendation: Current price 412.5p vs consensus TP 649p — 57% upside. Brokers will reaffirm or raise TPs. At 15x on ~41p FY26 EPS, fair value is 615p+. Potential for upgrades from HOLD to BUY at several houses given price dislocation. No cuts expected.
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: No explicit "comfortable with" language but multiple specific FY26 growth drivers cited (AI, Privilege, SAFS accretion, remortgage cycle) without qualifying language. Board described as "confident in delivering the full potential." Brokers will interpret this as implicitly guiding ahead of current stale FY26 consensus — upgrade cycle probability high.
  1. Key risk: Managed lettings portfolio declining from 153k to 149k properties. If the Renters' Rights Act accelerates landlord exits in 2026, lettings MSF (the highest-margin recurring revenue stream, 38% of group revenue) could face structural pressure. "Managed portfolio of 149,000 properties (2024: 153,000), reflecting landlord caution ahead of the Renters' Rights Act and a more measured pace of portfolio acquisitions." Brokers will sensitise for a further 3–5% portfolio decline in bear cases.
  1. Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

TPFG delivered a definitive EPS beat as the single most important catalyst: adjusted basic EPS of 40.3p versus FY1 consensus of 37.0p, a beat of +3.3p (+8.9%). Revenue of £84.3m matched consensus exactly. Adjusted PBT of £31.0m versus consensus £30.7m was a marginal beat at the top line, with the real earnings surprise flowing through a sharply improved effective tax rate of 22% (prior year: 29%) and 4pp margin expansion to an adjusted operating margin of 38%. This is unambiguously a results beat driven by structural quality improvement, not one-off items.

The H2 FY25 EPS implied from full-year actuals is 22.2p versus prior-year H2 of 16.3p — a +36% YoY H2 EPS surge that confirms the operating leverage thesis and validates the post-acquisition consolidation. Although the H1 EPS tracking appeared soft at the interim stage (18.1p representing only 44.9% of the eventual FY versus the 48.9% historical baseline — a −4.0pp deviation), this was a structural artefact of the enlarged group's H2 weighting rather than a genuine earnings shortfall. The bear case is further contained by net debt of just £2.3m (leverage 0.1x) and cash from operations of £22.1m (+50% YoY), giving the group a fortress balance sheet. The only genuine structural risk — the managed lettings portfolio declining by 4,000 properties (−2.6%) to 149,000 due to Renters' Rights Act landlord caution — is partially offset by the Privilege programme (£1.5m incremental revenue) and does not threaten the overall growth trajectory given Financial Services and Licensing division momentum.

FY26 EPS consensus will need to move from 37.0p to approximately 40–42p (a +8–12% upgrade cycle) to reflect the higher earnings base now established. FY27 follows at 42–45p range. Target price consensus of 649p — already implying 57% upside from the current 412.5p — is unlikely to be cut and may see modest uplifts to 650–700p on updated models anchored to 40p+ FY26 EPS at 15–16x. The primary constraint on a higher score is the absence of a revenue beat (exact match only), the EBITDA undershoot versus consensus, and the mild overhang from the lettings portfolio contraction narrative. However, the upgrade cycle is highly probable: a clean 9% EPS beat with margin expansion, near-zero debt, a raised dividend, and confident multi-driver FY26 outlook represents exactly the conditions that generate sustained broker upgrades and price target re-ratings on AIM franchise businesses.
