TPT

Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results / pre-H1 update accordingly. Next year end = 30/9/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Phase 0A — Routing

Pre-H1 mode confirmed. Q4. FY1 = FY26 (year end 30/9/26). Prior year = FY25. FY2 = FY27.

Phase 0B — FX Revenue Check

UK-only tile retail business. All revenues GBP. No non-GBP currency exposure. Phase 0B: skip. No penalty.

Phase 1 — Data Context

TPT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

  • Routing: Pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = Q4). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 trading update for 26-week period ended 28 March 2026. FY1 = FY26, year end 30/9/26.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 4.2p · Revenue £310.1m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 5.2p · Revenue £327.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change full period: +18.9% (3.7p → 4.4p, with step-up in early Dec 2025 from 3.3p → 4.4p). Revenue: +6.1% (£292.2m → £310.1m over same period, with major step in Dec 2025). Last-4-week trend: FLAT (4.4p → 4.2p marginal drift, then stable). Note: latest EPS = 4.2p vs snapshot high of 4.4p — slight trimming from Dec 2025 step.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 48.9% of FY = £151.7m · EPS 41.0% of FY = 1.72p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £122.8m · EPS 1.0p
  • Implied H2 YoY: H1 actual disclosed (£142.7m per RNS). Implied H2 = £310.1m − £142.7m = £167.4m vs FY25 H2 £129.0m → +29.8% YoY (consensus-derived). EPS: H1 actual from RNS needed (see Phase 2 extraction).
  • FX: N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt/(cash): 3y ago: £93.2m → 2y ago: £79.6m → 1y ago: £70.1m → current H1: £97.5m → FY1fc: £91.4m → FY2fc: £88.3m · ND/EBITDA: current 3.00x / FY1fc 2.30x / FY2fc 2.00x · Interest cover FY1fc: 2.7x (low) / FY2fc: 3.2x · ND/FCF: FY1fc 14.0x (elevated) / FY2fc 8.7x · Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — ND/EBITDA 3.0x at H1, ND/FCF 14x FY1fc, interest cover 2.7x. IFRS16 lease debt is the primary driver (tile retail store estate). Phase 5 gate: contributes a scored row.

Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

TPT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (H1 period 26 weeks ended 28 March 2026; interim results 19 May 2026)

  1. Revenue — H1 total disclosed: £142.7m. Group revenue (including CTD): £142.7m, −0.1% YoY. Excluding CTD: +2.1% YoY. LFL Topps Tiles: +0.1%. CTD LFL: +1.0% (but CTD impacted by CMA process volume loss from store disposals). H2 implied = £310.1m − £142.7m = £167.4m vs FY25 H2 £129.0m → +29.8% YoY (note: this appears inflated vs prior period; FY25 H2 was a weak period). % vs FY1 baseline (Phase 3.2): calculated below. "Total Group revenue (including CTD) for the first half was £142.7m, which is 0.1% lower year-on-year" "Group revenue (excluding CTD) grew year-on-year by +2.1%"
  2. EPS / earnings — no H1 EPS figure disclosed. No H1 adjusted EPS, PBT or profit stated. UNTRACKABLE for H1 EPS tracking. H1 profit: Sharescope "current H1" PBT = £1.5m and EPS = 1.1p — these are Sharescope pre-RNS fields. Data source gate: per Phase 3.2, cannot use Sharescope current H1 EPS for tracking deviation. H1 EPS UNTRACKABLE from RNS.
  3. Forward work / self-help measures: 23 store closures planned across FY26 (8 closed already in H1: 297 → 289 Topps stores; remainder in H2). Expected to "reduce overall Topps Tiles revenue but improve profitability through sales transference and cost reduction." Savings weighted toward H2. Trade App launching April 2026. ERP/tills modernisation began March 2026. "The Group expect this will reduce overall Topps Tiles revenue but improve profitability through sales transference and cost reduction."
  4. Margin / profitability: Pro Tiler +21% YoY (digital brand, higher-margin). Fired Earth profitable in H1 already, further H2 growth expected. Online revenue 21% of total (+2pp vs FY25). Self-help measures (H2-weighted cost savings) to "underpin in-year profit as well as provide sustainable profit improvement." No margin % disclosed. "Savings are expected to be weighted toward the second half of the year and will underpin in-year profit as well as provide sustainable profit improvement."
  5. Capital returns: No specific interim dividend or buyback mentioned. Balance sheet not specifically updated beyond what Sharescope provides.
  6. Qualitative tone — market context negative; company outperforming. Wider market declined ~−2.5% (Barclays Home Improvements & DIY). TPT LFL +0.1% and excluding CTD +2.1% — described as "continued trading outperformance within challenging market conditions." Management tone pragmatic: implementing self-help measures, acknowledging headwinds, H2 weighted cost actions. "Topps continues to outperform a softer market. In light of subdued consumer sentiment and geopolitical uncertainty as well as the cumulative impact of cost inflation, the management team is implementing a targeted programme of self-help measures weighted towards the second half."

EPS quality check: No H1 EPS figure in RNS — no EPS quality check applicable. Note: FY26e consensus EPS 4.2p vs FY25 actual 2.4p — this is a large forecast step (+75%) that was driven by the Dec 2025 consensus revision (3.3p → 4.4p). The CTD acquisition (Aug 2024) explains some structural uplift. The self-help measures and store closures are expected to drive the majority of the FY26 consensus EPS vs actual FY25 delivery.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

Forward-looking statements for FY26 H2 / full year:

  • "On track to return the CTD business to profit in the financial year" — positive, specific
  • "H2-weighted cost savings will underpin in-year profit" — explicit H2 profit support
  • Market context: challenging (−2.5% industry), but TPT outperforming
  • No explicit full-year numeric guidance
  • Geopolitical uncertainty and consumer sentiment headwinds flagged

Classification: 🟡 In-line — the update confirms the company remains on track with the H2-weighted plan. Guidance is "in line" with the narrative that underpinned the Dec 2025 consensus step-up. No upgrade trigger ("ahead of expectations") and no profit warning. The store closures and self-help plan were known.

  • Exact guidance phrase: "The Group expect this will reduce overall Topps Tiles revenue but improve profitability through sales transference and cost reduction"
  • Guidance nature: qualitative-only
  • Year coverage: FY26 (one year)
  • Provisional points: 0 to +3
  • Divergence check: No material divergence. H1 revenue slightly below prior year (−0.1% including CTD) but in a market down −2.5% — relative outperformance is the operative frame. No divergence flag required.

Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking

TPT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

So "current H1 = 142.9" in Sharescope may be stale/forward estimate or a different period. Cross-check: "1y ago H1 = 122.8" = FY25 H1 ✓ (confirmed by prior year). "Current H1 = 142.9" ≈ £142.7m as disclosed in today's RNS — very close match (+£0.2m rounding). 3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal

Data source gate:

  • Revenue: RNS discloses exact H1 figure: £142.7m. ✓ Qualifies as RNS-disclosed (exact figure).
  • EPS: No H1 EPS figure in RNS. UNTRACKABLE.

Revenue tracking:

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% 48.9% × £310.1m = £151.7m
  • H1 actual: £142.7m
  • H1% of FY1 consensus: 142.7 / 310.1 = 46.0%
  • Deviation vs baseline: 46.0% − 48.9% = −2.9pp
  • Signal: 🔴 CAUTION (−1.5 to −3pp band)
  • Buy trigger: £151.7m × 1.015 = £154.0m → actual £142.7m → 🔴 ✗ (not met)
  • Sell trigger: £151.7m × 0.985 = £149.5m → actual £142.7m < £149.5m → deviation is below the sell trigger boundary

Wait — recalculate: deviation = −2.9pp, which is in the CAUTION band (−1.5 to −3pp). The sell signal threshold is ≤ −3pp. At −2.9pp, this is one tenth of a pp above the sell signal boundary. Classify as: 🔴 CAUTION — borderline SELL SIGNAL.

  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 4.2p minus H1 EPS actual (UNTRACKABLE) = cannot calculate. For reference: if H1 EPS = 1.72p baseline, implied H2 = 4.2 − 1.72 = 2.48p vs historical H2 avg ((3.3+2.9+1.4)/3 = 2.53p) — burden approximately in line with historical average.

EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE (no H1 EPS in RNS). Baseline: 41.0% × 4.2p = 1.72p. Buy trigger: 1.75p. Confirm on 19 May 2026.

Historical hit rate: In the 3 years of available data, H1 revenue tracked as follows:

  • FY24 H1: 130.3 / 262.7 = 49.6% vs 48.9% baseline → +0.7pp (positive deviation, small)
  • FY25 H1: 122.8 / 251.8 = 48.8% vs 48.9% baseline → −0.1pp (in line)
  • FY26 H1: 142.7 / 310.1 = 46.0% vs 48.9% baseline → −2.9pp (CAUTION)

In 2 of the last 3 years, H1 deviation was approximately in line or positive. FY26 represents a material negative break from this pattern. Historical hit rate for positive deviation preceding FY beat: 1 of last 3 years with sufficient data.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-H1 mode → Phase 3.3 written in full. Does not contribute a scored row to Phase 5.

H2 base: No updated FY figure in RNS. Use FY1 consensus: £310.1m. Implied H2 = £310.1m − £142.7m = £167.4m. Consensus-derived.

  • Implied H2 Rev: £167.4m vs FY25 H2 £129.0m → +29.8% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%)
  • Note: this reflects both CTD consolidation and self-help H2 weighting. Prior 3yr H2 avg: (£128.0m + £132.4m + £129.0m) / 3 = £129.8m. Implied H2 £167.4m = +28.9% vs 3yr avg — strongly elevated.

Classification: 🟢 strong (consensus-derived, H2-weighted plan). Caveat: H2 delivery at £167.4m would require significant H2 momentum step-up; the self-help store closures and H2-weighted savings are the stated mechanism.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: Net change full period +18.9% (3.7p → 4.4p step in Dec 2025, then drift to 4.2p). The Dec 2025 step (+33% in one week from 3.3p to 4.4p) was a major broker revision event — likely post H2 FY25 results or CTD integration update. Since then: slight trim from 4.4p to 4.2p.
  • 4-week trend: FLAT (4.2p maintained, no change in last 4 weeks per snapshot).
  • Revenue trend: Similar Dec 2025 step (+£40m to £311m) then slight trim to £310.1m.
  • Divergence: Price has fallen from 60p (May 2025) to 34.7p (−42%) while EPS estimates rose +18.9%. Same de-rating dynamic as RNWH but more severe — market is discounting the earnings recovery significantly.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

  • Net debt/(cash): 3y ago: £93.2m → 2y ago: £79.6m → 1y ago: £70.1m → current H1: £97.5m → FY1fc: £91.4m → FY2fc: £88.3m
  • ND/EBITDA: 3y ago 2.20x → 2y ago 2.00x → 1y ago 2.40x → current 3.00x → FY1fc 2.30x → FY2fc 2.00x
  • Interest cover: FY1fc 2.7x / FY2fc 3.2x
  • ND/FCF: FY1fc 14.0x / FY2fc 8.7x

Debt flag: 🔴 Leverage elevated — primarily IFRS16 lease debt from tile store estate. ND/EBITDA 3.0x at H1 (improving to 2.3x FY1fc). Interest cover 2.7x FY1fc is tight. ND/FCF 14x is very high. The store closure programme (23 stores in FY26) will reduce lease liabilities and improve these metrics structurally. But in the near term: rate-sensitive IFRS16 leases on 289 stores mean any additional cost inflation could squeeze cover further. Phase 5: contributes a scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY1 vs prior year actual:

  • FY1fc EPS 4.2p vs FY25 actual 2.4p → ✅ growing (+75%)
  • FY1fc Revenue £310.1m vs FY25 actual £251.8m → ✅ growing (+23.1%)
  • ✅✅ FY1fc EPS and Revenue growing vs prior year actual (acquisition and recovery driven)

Step 2 — FY2 vs FY1:

  • FY2fc EPS 5.2p vs FY1fc 4.2p → ✅ growing (+23.8%)
  • FY2fc Revenue £327.8m vs FY1fc £310.1m → ✅ growing (+5.7%)
  • ✅✅ FY2fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY1fc

Structural / one-off flags:

  • Store closure programme — revenue headwind, profit tailwind. The deliberate closure of 23 underperforming stores will reduce revenue but improve the profit quality of the estate. This creates a short-term revenue headwind but is explicitly expected to improve underlying profitability. "The Group expect this will reduce overall Topps Tiles revenue but improve profitability through sales transference and cost reduction."
  • CTD integration — headwind from CMA-driven store disposals. CTD down from 31 stores to 22 (CMA process). Volume loss from this process has been flagged as weighing on H1 Group revenue. Rebuilding from H2.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation

TPT · Q4 · Pre-H1 Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/9/26

#1 Driver — H1 revenue £142.7m vs seasonal baseline £151.7m: −2.9pp deviation (borderline CAUTION/SELL SIGNAL). This is the primary negative signal. The company is tracking below the seasonal norm for H1 in a market that is itself declining (−2.5%). While the relative outperformance narrative is intact, the absolute revenue shortfall vs the baseline underpinning the £310.1m FY1 consensus means brokers will immediately stress-test whether H2 can compensate. The implied H2 requirement of £167.4m represents +29.8% YoY vs a prior-year H2 of £129.0m — a substantial ask.

#2 Driver — H2-weighted self-help measures as the bridge to FY consensus. The explicit CEO statement that savings are "weighted toward the second half" and will "underpin in-year profit" is the primary reason brokers should not immediately cut FY1 estimates. The H2 cost saving programme, Pro Tiler growth (>21%), Fired Earth profitable, and CTD rebuilding from H2 all support the H2 step-up narrative. However, these are qualitative assurances against a quantitative H1 shortfall.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue: Cut likely (−2% to −5%). H1 actuals of £142.7m vs baseline £151.7m creates a £9m H1 shortfall. Even with H2 catch-up, some brokers will trim FY revenue by £5–15m. The store closure revenue reduction further compounds this.
  • FY1 EPS: Hold to marginal cut (0% to −5%). The H2 cost actions may offset revenue softness on the bottom line. If cost savings are as guided, EPS may be maintained near 4.2p. But the low interest cover (2.7x) means any revenue undershoot creates disproportionate EPS leverage.
  • FY2: Hold — structural recovery story intact, FY27 estimates not affected by H1 trading.
  • Net FY1 EPS revision direction: hold to marginal cut.

Target price and recommendation: Brokers likely to hold TP at ~50p but risk of cuts to 40–45p range if revenue shortfall concerns persist. Current price 34.7p = 44% upside to consensus TP. Recommendation: Hold/neutral likely; no upgrade catalyst present.

Conservative guidance read-through: "Savings weighted toward H2" and "underpin in-year profit" are management's signalling that EPS will be protected even if revenue misses. Brokers will test this assumption in the H1 results (19 May 2026). The language is cautious framing for a difficult H1, not upgrade language.

Key risk: H2 self-help measures may be insufficient to offset both the H1 revenue shortfall and continued market weakness. The Barclays data shows consumer DIY spending declining every month Oct 2025–Feb 2026. If Q3 (H2 start) maintains this trajectory, the £167.4m H2 requirement becomes very challenging.

"the management team is implementing a targeted programme of self-help measures weighted towards the second half"

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction = hold to marginal cut. Tone: Cautious is appropriate — the negative H1 tracking signal and challenging market context drive downside bias even with H2 self-help protection.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable.

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

38/100 · Confidence: 32–44 · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

🟢 Outlook guidance — In-line (full year plan maintained, H2-weighted savings confirmed)+2
🟢 EPS acceleration signal — FY26e +75% vs FY25 −46.7% (consensus-derived, recovery)+3
🟢 Revenue acceleration — FY26e +23.1% vs FY25 −4.1% (acquisition + recovery)+2
🟢 Pro Tiler +21% YoY, Fired Earth profitable H1 — portfolio growth drivers+2
🟡 H2 implied revenue +29.8% YoY — strong implied but consensus-derived; execution risk−2
🟡 Market outperformance (+2.1% excl CTD vs −2.5% market) — positive but limited upside signal+1

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The most important number in this RNS is H1 Group revenue of £142.7m — a figure that, on the surface, looks innocuous (+16.2% YoY including CTD) but which, against the seasonal baseline, reveals a −2.9pp deviation from the 3yr average H1% of FY. This places TPT in CAUTION territory, borderline SELL SIGNAL on revenue tracking. The seasonal baseline for H1 is £151.7m (48.9% × £310.1m consensus), meaning the actual H1 came in £9.0m short of what is needed to remain on track with the full-year consensus. The #1 catalyst is therefore a negative tracking signal, partially mitigated by the explicitly H2-weighted self-help programme. The market context is not helping: Barclays data shows UK DIY/Home Improvements declining every month from October 2025 to February 2026, averaging approximately −2.5%.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H1 tracking signal fires red (CAUTION) on revenue (−2.9pp) and UNTRACKABLE on EPS (no H1 EPS disclosed — confirm on 19 May 2026; baseline 1.72p, buy trigger 1.75p). The H2 burden is significant: consensus requires £167.4m revenue in H2 (implied, consensus-derived), representing +29.8% YoY vs FY25 H2 £129.0m — classified 🟢 strong in absolute terms but almost entirely dependent on the H2 cost-saving programme delivering as guided. The upgrade resilience case rests on three pillars: (1) H2-weighted store closure cost actions explicitly confirmed; (2) CTD rebuilding from end-FY25 with LFL +1.0% in H1 and housebuilder volume recovering; (3) Pro Tiler running at +21% YoY. However, the leverage position (ND/EBITDA 3.0x, ND/FCF 14x, interest cover 2.7x) means any revenue undershoot in H2 creates disproportionate downside to EPS given thin interest cover headroom.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are expected to trim FY1 revenue by £5–15m (−2% to −5%) reflecting the H1 shortfall, with the range depending on confidence in the H2 self-help delivery. FY1 EPS at 4.2p likely held or marginal cut (0% to −5%) as H2 cost savings may protect the bottom line even with top-line pressure. TP likely held near 50p in the near term but risk of 40–45p cuts if brokers lose confidence in the H2 step-up. The 44% upside gap to consensus TP at current price 34.7p signals the market has already heavily discounted the FY26 recovery story. The key watch point is the 19 May 2026 H1 interim results, which will disclose H1 EPS and the precise H2 self-help savings quantum — these will determine whether the FY1 consensus is maintained or cut materially. 🏁 Score 38 — cautious: H1 revenue is running −2.9pp below the seasonal baseline with an elevated H2 burden, market conditions remain headwind, and leverage is elevated; the H2-weighted self-help programme is the sole upgrade buffer; EPS tracking deferred to 19 May results where the borderline sell signal may be confirmed or reversed.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

TPX · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26, year ended 31 March 2026)

This RNS explicitly states it "expects to comfortably exceed the recently upgraded consensus across all key financial metrics."

1. Revenue — FY26:

  • Revenue: c.£78.1m (FY25: £77.3m) = +1.0% YoY.
  • vs RNS-disclosed consensus £76.2m → beat of +£1.9m = +2.5%.
  • vs Sharescope fc £75.0m → beat of +£3.1m = +4.1%.
  • H2 implied: £78.1m − £36.2m = £41.9m vs H2 FY25 £39.5m = +6.1% YoY.

"Revenue of c.£78.1m (FY25: £77.3m), representing 1% year on year growth and finishing ahead of market consensus of £76.2m."

2. Adj EBITDA / earnings:

  • Adj EBITDA: c.£8.6m (FY25: £5.6m) = +53.6% YoY. vs consensus £7.1m → beat of £1.5m = +21.1% on adj EBITDA.
  • Adj EBITDA margin: 11.0% (FY25: 7.3%) = +370bp expansion.
  • Gross Margin: 31.7% (FY25: 28.6%) = +310bp — significant operational improvement.
  • Net debt: c.£4.2m (FY25: £8.5m) — strong FCF generation; vs consensus £5.7m = £1.5m better. Leverage: 0.5x (FY25: 1.5x) — vs consensus 0.8x.
  • Adj EPS: not disclosed. Sharescope fc 3.9p. With EBITDA £8.6m vs consensus £7.1m (+21%), adj EPS will be revised up significantly.

EPS bridge FY26e (constructed here):

  • (1) Base: FY25 adj EPS 3.0p (on 94.8m shares weighted).
  • (2) Organic growth: adj EBITDA £8.6m vs £5.6m = +£3.0m. D&A capex-driven (capex fc £0.1m = negligible for digital services). Adj EBITDA ~= adj EBIT for low-capex business → adj PBT ~= adj EBITDA − net interest. Net debt £4.2m at ~7% → interest cost ~£0.3m. Adj PBT ~£8.3m.
  • (3) Tax: at ~25% → PAT ~£6.2m. On ~94.8m shares → EPS = ~6.6p — materially above consensus 3.9p.
  • Wait: checking. The Sharescope fc EBITDA = £6.9m; actual = £8.6m. The significant difference between my EPS bridge (6.6p) and consensus (3.9p) needs explanation. Possible: (a) adj EPS uses a different calculation to adj EBITDA; (b) significant amortisation of acquired intangibles below EBITDA line; (c) prior year losses carried forward affect tax differently. TPX is a services company — amortisation of acquired intangibles from historic M&A may be substantial. Pre-PBT items between EBITDA and EPS could include: D&A of intangibles ~£3–5m (based on prior acquisition history at £150m+ spend). If D&A = £4m → adj EBIT = £4.6m → adj PBT = £4.3m → tax = £1.1m → PAT = £3.2m → EPS = 3.4p. This is below consensus 3.9p. Alternatively, if D&A = £2–3m → EBIT = £5.6–6.6m → EPS = ~4.5–5.5p. The bridge is uncertain without D&A disclosure. Flag: adj EPS revision likely to be in the range +15–30% above stale 3.9p consensus = revised FY26e EPS ~4.5–5.5p range.
  • vs FY2 (FY27) consensus 5.0p: FY26 revised 4.5–5.5p → FY27 5.0p consensus may need upward revision depending on landing point.

3. Order book / pipeline:

  • New business wins: £122m in FY26. This is the key forward metric — £122m won vs £78.1m revenue = 1.56x book-to-bill ratio. Strong pipeline conversion signal.
  • "New three-year strategic phase focused on sustainable growth."

"TPXimpact is now entering its new three-year strategic phase focused on sustainable growth, supported by new business wins of £122m."

4. Margin:

  • Gross margin +310bp (31.7% vs 28.6%). "Driven by improved project mix and operational efficiencies." This is the key operational achievement — structural margin improvement, not one-off.
  • Adj EBITDA margin +370bp (11.0% vs 7.3%). "Result of the improvement in gross margin and tight control of discretionary costs and other overheads."
  • These margin improvements are structural and should be carried into FY27 as a base.

5. Capital / balance sheet:

  • Net debt £4.2m vs FY25 £8.5m = £4.3m reduction in net debt despite operational investment. "Strong cash generation of the Company in the year."
  • Leverage 0.5x vs 1.5x prior year — major deleveraging. Below consensus forecast of 0.8x.
  • No dividend (DPS fc = 0.00 in Sharescope). No mention of dividend introduction.

6. Qualitative tone: "Three-year strategic turnaround" declared complete. New three-year plan to be unveiled "in the next few months." CEO: "adjusted EBITDA margin now at 11.0% and leverage down to 0.5x, we have a very stable base on which to grow as we move into FY27."

B. OUTLOOK & GUIDANCE CLASSIFICATION

"Comfortably exceed the recently upgraded consensus" = explicit beat language across all key metrics. FY27 guidance: "new three-year strategic plan... to be unveiled in next few months" — no numeric FY27 guidance in this RNS. New business wins of £122m provide visible FY27 revenue backlog. CEO's phrase "very stable base on which to grow" = constructive qualitative guidance.

Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering for FY26 (comfortably exceeds consensus on all metrics — revenue, EBITDA, margin, net debt). Provisional +12 pts. FY27 guidance qualitative-only (new plan upcoming) — treat as Constructive.

Divergence: FY26 beat is clean — no non-recurring items flagged. Gross margin structural improvement. No divergence. No Beat quality flag.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +30.0% net (3.0p → 3.9p). However, the trend has been stalling since late February 2026 at 3.9p. Post-today's beat (EBITDA +21% vs consensus), brokers must revise substantially upward.
  • Revenue: £76.5m → £75.0m (Sharescope) = slight decrease, but RNS beat of £76.2m consensus.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 3.9p since 28 Feb 26). Post-RNS: revision to ~4.5–5.5p adj EPS likely.
  • Divergence: Share price 36.7p vs consensus TP 73p = 99% upside — extreme discount. Price has fallen from 66p (May 2025) to 36.7p. Given the strong operational delivery, this discount is extreme for a business with demonstrated margin improvement, £122m new business wins, and deleveraging trajectory.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

  • Net debt trend: FY23 £3.7m / FY24 −£6.0m (net cash) / FY25 £0.3m / H1 FY26 £8.0m / FY26 year-end £4.2m (RNS confirmed).
  • ND/EBITDA: FY26 £4.2m / £8.6m (adj EBITDA) = 0.49x (RNS implied) vs Sharescope fc 0.80x — materially better.
  • Interest cover fc: 5.6x (Sharescope). At £4.2m net debt at ~7%, interest ~£0.3m. adj EBITDA £8.6m / £0.3m = ~29x — much better than Sharescope forecast 5.6x. Sharescope interest cover calculation may include IFRS 16 lease interest. In any case, leverage is not a concern.
  • Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — improving rapidly toward 🟢.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY26 vs FY25:

  • Revenue: £78.1m > FY25 £77.3m ✅✅
  • EPS: ~4.5–5.5p > FY25 3.0p ✅✅

Step 2 — FY27 vs FY26:

  • Revenue: £81.0m > FY26 £78.1m ✅✅
  • EPS: 5.0p vs ~4.5–5.5p estimated FY26. If FY26 adj EPS >5.0p, FY27 consensus is stale. ⚠️ If adj EPS for FY26 confirmed at >5.0p, FY27 consensus of 5.0p represents a year-on-year decline → 🚨 FY27 fc EPS [X]% below FY26 actual — pending confirmation.

3.6 Structural / One-Off Flags

  • Turnaround complete — new growth phase commencing: "The Group's performance in FY26 marks the successful conclusion of its three-year strategic turnaround." Entering FY27 with a new three-year plan (details forthcoming). This is a regime change in how brokers will model the stock.
  • Gross margin structural expansion to 31.7%: +310bp represents genuine operational improvement. New state, not a one-off reversal.
  • £122m new business wins: 1.56x book-to-bill implies a significantly larger revenue potential in FY27 relative to current FY27 consensus £81m. The conversion of the £122m win figure to FY27 revenue depends on contract timing and delivery schedules — but the pipeline is visible.
  • Emma Broom appointed Chief Growth Officer: Operational signal that FY27 is growth-oriented.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

TPX · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/03/26

#1 Driver — Adj EBITDA £8.6m (+21% vs consensus £7.1m): This is the headline upgrade trigger. A 21% beat on adj EBITDA is a large surprise for a company of this size with a relatively tight consensus (2 brokers: Cavendish). The adj EBITDA margin of 11.0% vs 7.3% prior year is a structural step-change and brokers will carry this into FY27 models. The gross margin expansion to 31.7% confirms the project mix improvement is genuine.

#2 Driver — Net debt £4.2m vs consensus £5.7m; leverage 0.5x vs 0.8x: The balance sheet improvement exceeds expectations. For an AIM company with a history of elevated leverage and restructuring, delivering below the leverage target ahead of schedule is a strong signal of cash generation quality. This reduces the discount rate brokers apply to the stock and supports multiple expansion.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY26e EPS: From 3.9p to estimated 4.5–5.5p (centred at ~5.0p). At adj EBITDA £8.6m and applying ~£3m D&A for intangibles → adj EBIT ~£5.6m → adj PBT ~£5.3m → tax ~£1.3m → PAT ~£4.0m → EPS on 94.8m shares = ~4.2p. More likely 4.5–5.5p as D&A may be lower than estimated. Consensus upgrade: +15–40%.
  • FY27e EPS: From 5.0p to 5.5–7.0p range — new three-year plan and £122m new wins support a meaningfully higher FY27 EPS on the back of the improved margin base.
  • Revenue FY26e: From £76.2m (RNS consensus) to RNS actual £78.1m = +2.5% upgrade.
  • Revenue FY27e: From £81m to £83–86m (book-to-bill of 1.56x implies pipeline strength).
  • TP: Consensus 73p vs current 36.7p = 99% upside. Brokers will revise TPs meaningfully upward — likely to 80–100p range — reflecting turnaround completion and FY27 growth re-rating.

Conservative guidance read-through: No numeric FY27 guidance — new three-year plan "in next few months." The absence of FY27 guidance is actually a neutral-to-positive indicator: management is clearly confident enough to announce turnaround completion and a new growth phase without feeling the need to caveat expectations. The CEO's language is unambiguously positive.

Key risk: Revenue grew only +1% YoY (£78.1m vs £77.3m FY25) despite strong H2 recovery. If the H1 public sector revenue contraction (which was structural — delayed procurements, spending cuts) continues into FY27, the £122m new business wins may take longer than expected to convert to revenue. The three-year plan details (when disclosed) will be the key determinant of whether FY27 consensus of £81m / 5.0p EPS proves adequate. "Revenue of c.£78.1m (FY25: £77.3m), representing 1% year on year growth."

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting — across all key metrics.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: TPXimpact's FY26 trading update is an unambiguous beat across all key metrics, explicitly using the words "comfortably exceed the recently upgraded consensus." Adj EBITDA of c.£8.6m (+54% vs FY25 £5.6m) beat the company-disclosed consensus of £7.1m by +21% — the single most important number. Gross margin expanded +310bp to 31.7% (FY25: 28.6%), confirming that the profit beat is structural — driven by improved project mix and operational efficiencies — not a one-time item. Revenue of £78.1m (+1% YoY, +2.5% vs £76.2m consensus) is a modest beat that matters less than the margin story; the H2 implied revenue of £41.9m (+6.1% YoY vs H2 FY25 £39.5m) shows the public sector demand recovery is real. The "three-year strategic turnaround" is officially declared complete.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The H2 revenue and profitability profile is the upgrade foundation. H2 FY26 implied revenue (+6.1% YoY) and the structural gross margin expansion (from 28.6% to 31.7%) mean that the adj EBITDA margin of 11.0% achieved in FY26 becomes the base for FY27 modelling — not a peak. The £122m new business wins in FY26 (1.56x book-to-bill vs £78.1m revenue) represent a visible forward pipeline that should support FY27 revenue growth ahead of the current 3.7% consensus assumption. Net debt of £4.2m — better than the £5.7m consensus forecast — confirms strong operating cash conversion (FY26 FCF significantly positive despite the deleveraging challenge). The leverage trajectory from 1.5x to 0.5x in a single year is exceptional for an AIM digital services company and removes the discount rate overhang that has depressed the share price. The upgrade resilience case is simple: even if FY27 revenue grows only at 3–4%, applying the new 31.7% gross margin and 11% EBITDA margin baseline generates EPS of ~5.5–7.0p vs the stale 5.0p consensus.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e EPS likely revised from stale 3.9p to approximately 4.5–5.5p (central estimate ~5.0p) on the back of adj EBITDA £8.6m beat — a +15–40% EPS upgrade at full results on 16 June 2026. FY27e EPS (current 5.0p) will need upward revision once the three-year plan is disclosed — likely toward 5.5–7.0p depending on management's growth ambitions. FY27 revenue consensus of £81m will move toward £83–86m on book-to-bill evidence. Consensus TP of 73p vs current 36.7p = 99% upside — this gap has become untenable for a business with demonstrated 11% adj EBITDA margin, declining leverage, and £122m new wins, and broker TPs will revise to the 80–100p range. The main constraint on full score is the absence of numeric FY27 guidance and the adj EPS uncertainty until 16 June. 🏁 Turnaround complete, metrics beat across the board, and the upgrade cycle is starting — the adj EBITDA margin expansion of 370bp, £122m book-to-bill, and leverage halving create a compelling setup for a sustained re-rating from the current deeply discounted share price.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX: TruFin derives 98% of revenues from the UK (segmental note 4). No non-GBP currency exceeds 30%. No FX penalty applied.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • Consensus: FY1 EPS 8.0p, revenue £63.0m; FY2 EPS 9.3p, revenue £66.1m. FY1 EBITDA £11.8m. No FY1 PBT consensus available in Sharescope.
  • Forecast momentum: EPS surged 1.9p → 8.0p over ~10 months (+321.1%) with multiple distinct upgrade steps: May (1.9→3.0p), August (3.0→5.0p), September (5.0→5.6p), December (5.6→7.8p), January 2026 (7.8→8.0p). Last 4 weeks: FLAT — consensus plateaued waiting for results.
  • Critical H2 finding: H1 actuals in Sharescope = £36.0m rev / 5.6p EPS. Consensus-implied H2 = £63.0m − £36.0m = £27.0m rev; 8.0p − 5.6p = 2.4p EPS. Actual FY25 H2 (from RNS) = £29.9m rev / 6.4p EPS → H2 EPS beat vs consensus-implied: +167%. This is the central finding of the analysis.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification
  1. Gross revenue: £65.9m, +20% (2024: £55.0m). vs FY1 consensus £63.0m → beat +£2.9m / +4.6%.
    "Gross revenue grew 20% to £65.9m (2024: £55.0m)"
  2. Adjusted EBITDA: £12.6m, +66% (2024: £7.6m). vs FY1 fc £11.8m → beat +£0.8m / +6.8%. 20% revenue growth producing 66% EBITDA growth — exceptional operating leverage in action.
    "Adjusted EBITDA was £12.6m (2024: £7.6m), a 66% year-on-year improvement"
  3. Adjusted PBT: £8.4m (2024: £0.9m), +848%. Step-change in profitability quality — the central investment case validation point.
    "Adjusted Profit Before Tax was £8.4m (2024: PBT of £0.9m), an 848% year-on-year improvement"
  4. Adjusted EPS: 12.0p (basic 11.3p). vs FY1 consensus 8.0p → beat +50%. Complete reset of FY2 estimates required — maintaining 9.3p FY2 is immediately untenable when FY1 delivered 12.0p.
    "Basic EPS: 11.3 pence… Adjusted EPS: 12.0p"
  5. Playstack: revenue £55.3m, +24%. EBITDA £13.5m, +20%. PBT £12.2m, +59%. Exceptional catalogue performance (Abiotic Factor, Balatro). 20m new installs; combined catalogue exceeded $100m lifetime Steam revenues.
    "Playstack grew revenue by more than 24% to £55.3m (2024: £44.6m). EBITDA increased 20% to £13.5m"
  6. Oxygen: revenue £9.1m, +18%. EBITDA £3.8m, +67%. EBIT +383% to £2.1m. Dividend to group £2.5m (2024: £1.3m, +92%). 100% client retention; 65 Early Payment clients; average committed tenure 7.7 years.
    "Oxygen grew revenue by 18% to £9.1m. EBITDA increased 57% to £3.8m (2024: £2.3m)"
  7. Satago: revenue £1.2m, −50%. Net loss £2.6m (2024: £4.8m, −47%). Planned transition from own-book lending. Cost base cut 45%. Loss narrowing — improving trajectory.
    "Satago saw revenues decline by 50% to £1.2m after losing its contract with a Tier-1 Bank in July 2024"
  8. Share buybacks: £8m in 2025 (7.5m shares at avg 106p). Post year-end: further £6m buyback announced January 2026. Third and fourth capital returns since IPO. Share count declining — accretive to remaining holders.
    "Two share buybacks totalling £8m executed during the year acquiring 7.5m shares at an average price of 106p."
  9. Current trading Jan–Feb 2026: "not less than £9.3m" (unaudited). Conservative floor language. Jan–Feb is seasonally lighter for Playstack pre-launches — not a negative signal.
    "Group revenue for the two months ended 28 February 2026 are tracking in line with the Board's expectations at not less than £9.3m (unaudited)"
  10. Oxygen FY26 visibility: "more than 98% of forecast 2026 Early Payment revenue expected from existing clients." Near-full-year cover before any new business — structural moat in revenue predictability.
    "More than 98% of forecast 2026 Early Payment revenue is expected to be generated from existing clients"
  11. Playstack 2026: Mortal Shell II (PC/PS/Xbox), 8 total titles. Board has "immense confidence" in pipeline. Mortal Shell II set wish-list records when announced at Summer Game Fest June 2025.
    "Playstack expects to release 8 titles in 2026 including the hotly anticipated Mortal Shell II and Raccoin"
  12. Deferred tax asset: £7.0m recognised (2024: £3.8m) — £3.2m uplift in year. Auditor/management recognition signals high confidence in sustained future profitability from Oxygen and Playstack. Total unutilised losses without DTA: £51m.
    "Deferred tax assets related to carried-forward tax losses in Oxygen Finance Limited and Playstack Limited have been recognised."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue trajectory: Strongly Accelerating. FY23: £13.9m, FY24: £55.0m (+296%), FY25: £65.9m (+20%). Growth on a much larger base in FY25 is commercially meaningful — Playstack's model is scaling, not just growing from a tiny starting point.
  • EPS trajectory: Step-change positive. FY23 adj: −11.7p (losses), FY24: 5.4p (first full profit year), FY25: 12.0p (+122%). Operating leverage is real and demonstrated.
  • Critical H2 beat finding: Consensus-implied H2 EPS was only 2.4p (= 8.0p FY − 5.6p H1). Actual H2 delivered 6.4p — +167% beat on implied H2 expectation. The market had severely under-modelled the back-half operating leverage of Playstack's catalogue and Oxygen's EBIT inflection. The full-year +50% EPS beat was essentially an H2 phenomenon.
  • Implied H2 momentum (pre-FY mode): H2 revenue £29.9m vs H2 FY24 £29.7m = +0.7% (flat). H2 EPS 6.4p vs H2 FY24 2.1p = +205% (strong base effect). Revenue flat but EPS strong — reflects operating leverage working as designed, not revenue acceleration.
  • Forecast momentum: +321.1% EPS upgrade — highest in the batch. FLAT last 4 weeks. The 50% EPS beat will require FY2 (currently 9.3p) to be fully reset upward. Direction is unambiguous.
  • Structural flags: (1) Playstack 84% group revenue concentration — single-title risk is real. (2) Oxygen 7.7yr avg client tenure + 100% retention = genuine structural moat. (3) DTA £7m recognition = independent auditor validation of profitability sustainability. (4) Buyback at avg 106p signals board confidence at current 126p price. (5) Satago losses narrowing — optionality, not drag, going forward.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — EPS 50% beat vs consensus (12.0p adj vs 8.0p): A complete reset of FY2 estimates is required. TruFin has 1–2 brokers (Panmure Liberum); the note will lead with this beat and the implied FY2 step-up. Maintaining FY2 below 12p would be seen as immediately too conservative.
2#2 Driver — Simultaneous beats across revenue (+4.6%), EBITDA (+6.8%), and PBT (+848%): The beat is not a fluke — it occurred across all metrics simultaneously. Playstack +24% revenue and +59% PBT on a £55m base is exceptional for an AIM games publisher. Oxygen EBIT +383% demonstrates the leverage model working precisely as described.
3Forecast revisions — FY2 EPS reset to 13–16p (from 9.3p = +40–72% upgrade): Revenue FY2 from £66.1m → ~£72–76m. EBITDA from £15.4m → ~£17–20m. Significant revisions executed over 1–3 broker notes post-results.
4Conservative guidance read-through — "not less than £9.3m" for Jan–Feb 2026: Typical small-cap floor language. Jan–Feb below annualised run-rate, but Playstack revenues are highly non-linear around game launches. Mortal Shell II has not yet launched. Brokers will model above this floor for 2026.
5Key risk — Playstack concentration (84% of group): Mortal Shell II commercial reception is unverifiable pre-launch. A single underperforming title or launch delay could knock 15–25% off FY2 estimates. Satago's continued losses (£2.6m) also a drag, though on an improving trajectory.
6Overall tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. A 50% EPS beat on a stock that has already had +321% EPS upgrades over 10 months is exceptional. DTA recognition + buyback at 106p avg + Mortal Shell II pipeline = strong upgrading thesis. AIM liquidity constraints may slow broker update timing but direction is unambiguously positive.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
92
/100
Confidence range: 87–96 · No FX adjustment applied
EPS beat +50% vs consensus (12.0p adj vs 8.0p — full estimate reset required)+22
Revenue beat +4.6%+8
EBITDA beat +6.8%+6
H2 EPS actual 6.4p vs consensus-implied 2.4p (+167% H2 beat)+12
Playstack +24% revenue, PBT +59% — structural proof of repeatable model+7
Oxygen EBITDA +67%, 100% retention, £2.5m dividend to group+6
Ongoing buybacks (£6m post-YE) — capital discipline signal+4
Deferred tax asset £7m recognition (auditor confidence in future profits)+3
Satago still loss-making (£2.6m net loss)−5
Playstack revenue concentration (84% of group — single-title risk)−5
AIM liquidity / limited broker coverage (upgrade lag risk)−3
Jan–Feb guidance "not less than £9.3m" — below implied annualised run-rate−2

TruFin has delivered a remarkable full-year result that materially exceeds all consensus expectations across every metric. The adjusted EPS of 12.0p vs 8.0p consensus (+50%) requires a complete reset of FY2 estimates — maintaining 9.3p FY2 is untenable when FY1 has delivered 12.0p. The critical finding: consensus-implied H2 EPS was only 2.4p (= 8.0p FY − 5.6p H1 known), yet actual H2 delivered 6.4p — a +167% beat on the implied H2 expectation, indicating the market had severely under-modelled the back-half operating leverage of Playstack's catalogue and Oxygen's EBIT inflection.

The quality of the beat is excellent across all subsidiaries. Playstack's +24% revenue and +59% PBT on a £55m base demonstrates repeatable, scalable economics not reliant on a single blockbuster. Oxygen's EBIT +383% confirms the leverage model embedded in the Early Payment SaaS business. The recognition of a £7m deferred tax asset provides independent auditor validation of management's confidence in sustained future profitability.

Primary constraint on a higher score is Playstack concentration (84% of group) and AIM-market limitations on broker coverage. FY2 estimates require upgrades of 40–72% from 9.3p — a protracted process with a small broker team. Direction is unambiguous. Buyback accretion, DTA uplift, and Mortal Shell II launch optionality make TruFin one of the highest-conviction upgrade situations in the small-cap space today.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 0A — ROUTING
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-H1 trading update. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
PHASE 0B — FX
  • No Currency Movements section present. No single non-GBP currency explicitly disclosed exceeding 30%. Phase 0B skipped — no FX penalty applied.
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-H1 trading update. Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 18.0p · Revenue £186.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 19.9p · Revenue £173.2m
  • Forecast momentum: EPS net change over full period +0.9p (+5.3%). Volatile path: crashed to 14.5p Oct 25, surged to 20.5p Dec 25, settled 18.0p. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Revenue net change +£24.2m (+14.9%) — large upgrade Nov–Dec 25, now partially unwound.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 49.1% of FY = £91.6m · EPS 47.4% of FY = 8.5p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £76.9m · EPS 7.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-RNS): Revenue +16.4% YoY · EPS [−7.8% YoY]
  • FX: N/A
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-H1 Trading Update (18-month transition period)

Critical structural note: Focusrite changed year-end from 31 August to 28 February. Next audited results cover 18 months to 28 Feb 2026. RNS provides 12-month and 6-month figures. Sharescope FY1 consensus (£186.6m) is on the old August year-end and is NOT directly comparable.

  1. 12-month revenue (to Feb 2026): ~£164m. Disclosed sell-side consensus range: £165.0–168.1m. Miss of approx £1–4m (−0.6% to −2.4% vs midpoint £166.5m).

"Group revenue is expected to be slightly ahead of the prior 12 month period at approximately £164 million on a reported basis"

  1. H2 revenue (6m to Feb 2026): ~£76m, down approx 5% YoY. Disclosed 6m consensus: £77.0–80.1m. Below bottom of range (miss £1–4m).

"For the six months to 28 February 2026, Group revenue is expected to be approximately £76 million, representing a decrease of approximately 5% on a reported basis"

  1. 12m EBITDA: In-line with market expectations (range £23.7–25.3m). No 6m EBITDA figure provided.

"The Board expects adjusted EBITDA for the 12 months to February 2026 to be in-line with current market expectations"

  1. Gross margin: Slightly ahead of prior 12 months despite US tariff impact. Pricing discipline + supply chain management cited.

"Gross margins for the period have remained strong and slightly ahead of the prior 12 months, notwithstanding the impact of tariffs in the US"

  1. Operating margin: Stable. Cost control maintained.

"Operating margins are also expected to remain stable reflecting an ongoing focus on cost control"

  1. Net debt: £9.0m at 28 Feb 2026 vs £10.8m at 31 Aug 2025. £1.8m improvement. Improved working capital + inventory reduction.

"Net debt at 28 February 2026 was approximately £9.0 million compared to £10.8 million at 31 August 2025"

  1. H2 structural explanation: Content Creation division impacted by strong prior-period comparator (US channel loading pre-tariff) + continued US inventory destocking.

"this reflects a particularly strong comparator for the Content Creation division in the prior period, which benefitted from stock levels being increased in the US distribution channel ahead of anticipated tariff increases"

  1. Audio Reproduction recovery: Martin Audio returned to growth as markets normalised.

"Audio Reproduction, including the Martin Audio brand, returned to growth during this period as markets normalised"

  1. Forward tone: CEO flags geopolitical/macro uncertainty but "no material impact to date." Confidence in future progress. Agility + product portfolio + route-to-market strengthening cited.
PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Half-on-Half Table

Period · H1 FY22: Rev £92.9m · H2 FY22: Rev £90.8m / EPS 23.7p

H1 FY23: Rev £86.2m (−7.2%) / EPS 18.0p (−31.3%)

H2 FY23: Rev £92.2m (+1.5%) / EPS 20.4p (−14.0%)

H1 FY24: Rev £76.9m (−10.8%) / EPS 7.7p (−57.2%)

H2 FY24: Rev £81.6m (−11.5%) / EPS 10.3p (−49.5%)

H1 FY25: Rev £80.9m (+5.2%) / EPS 6.6p (−14.3%)

H2 FY25: Rev £88.0m (+7.8%) / EPS 10.1p (−1.9%)

H1 FY26*: Rev ~£76m (−6.1%) / EPS not disclosed

Implied H2 FY26*: Rev ~£110.6m (+25.7% vs H2 FY25) — artefact of old-year-end consensus

1. Half-on-Half Growth Pattern

  • H2 derivation: Old FY1 consensus £186.6m − H1 actual £76m = implied H2 required £110.6m vs prior H2 £88.0m
  • Revenue trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — H1 FY25 +5.2%, H2 FY25 +7.8%, H1 FY26 [−6.1%] — recovery in FY25 fully reversed
  • EPS trajectory: 🟡 Volatile — H1 FY24 −57.2%, H1 FY25 −14.3% (improving), H2 FY25 −1.9% (near-stable); H1 FY26 EPS not disclosed

2. Seasonal H1 Tracking (pre-H1 mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 3yr avg H1% (49.1%) × FY1 £186.6m = £91.6m
  • EPS baseline: 3yr avg H1% (47.4%) × FY1 18.0p = 8.5p
  • Revenue tracking: H1 £76m ÷ FY1 £186.6m = 40.7% vs baseline 49.1% → [−8.4pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL
  • ⚠ STRUCTURAL DISTORTION: −8.4pp deviation is heavily distorted by year-end change. On undistorted basis (£76m vs company-disclosed 6m consensus £77–80.1m), real deviation is approximately −1.3 to −5pp → 🟡 IN LINE to 🔴 CAUTION
  • EPS tracking: UNTRACKABLE — no H1 EPS figure disclosed in RNS
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > £92.9m ✗ · H1 EPS > 8.6p ✗ (EPS untrackable)
  • H2 EPS burden: Elevated on old consensus basis; contained by EBITDA in-line message

3. Implied H2 Momentum

  • Implied H2 £110.6m vs last 3 H2 avg £87.3m = +26.8% — strong classification, but entirely an artefact of old-year-end consensus structure. Implausible as standalone forecast; signals urgent need to rebase consensus to Feb year-end.

4. Forecast Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: +0.9p (+5.3%) net over period. Volatile: 14.5p trough Oct 25, 20.5p peak Dec 25, settled 18.0p. FLAT last 4 weeks.
  • Revenue: £162.4m → £186.6m (+14.9%) — major upgrade in Nov–Dec 25 driven by consensus reset, but today's RNS puts the 12m figure at £164m, suggesting Dec upgrade cycle was premature.
  • Divergence: Price −39.8% (349p → 210p) while EPS consensus slightly higher. Market pricing structural concern, not captured in EPS line.

5. Structural Flags

  • [Year-end change]: Aug → Feb year-end change is the dominant structural factor. All Sharescope FY1/FY2 figures need to be re-based to Feb year-end before any meaningful comparison can be made. "the Group has changed its financial year end from 31 August to 28 February"
  • [US tariff / inventory distortion]: One-off; inflated H1 FY25 comparator, depressed H1 FY26. "stock levels being increased in the US distribution channel ahead of anticipated tariff increases"
  • [Content Creation vs Audio Reproduction divergence]: Mixed divisional picture complicates clean recovery narrative.
PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION
  1. #1 and #2 Drivers: #1 = 12-month revenue miss vs disclosed range (£164m vs £165–168m) — forces full model reset due to year-end change. #2 = EBITDA in-line with margin resilience — the key positive offset preventing a full downgrade cycle. Brokers who haven't yet rebased models face the most disruptive reaction.
  1. Forecast revisions: FY1 Revenue: old £186.6m consensus is obsolete; new Feb y/e FY1 likely to settle £170–180m. FY1 EPS: rebased 16–18p for new Feb year-end (modest net downward revision of 5–10% on like-for-like basis). FY2: too early to model reliably pending new year-end framework.
  1. Target price / recommendation: Consensus TP 340p vs close 210p (62% implied upside — unsustainable given reset). Brokers likely to cut TPs to 260–285p range. Most retain Hold/Buy but reduce targets. Significant recommendation changes unlikely in immediate reaction.
  1. Conservative guidance read-through: EBITDA "in-line with current market expectations" is neutral confirmatory language. "Slightly ahead" on 12m revenue vs prior year, while missing the sell-side range, does not trigger upgrade cycle language. No "not less than" signal present.
  1. Key risk: Full consensus rebuild required due to year-end change, concurrent with ongoing US tariff uncertainty. The Dec 25 upgrade cycle (EPS to 20.5p, Rev to £186.6m) now appears premature. "notwithstanding the impact of tariffs in the US, with the Group benefiting from continued pricing discipline and strong supply chain management"
  1. Overall tone: Neutral / hold and wait — EBITDA in-line and margin resilience prevent a negative reaction; revenue miss and year-end structural disruption prevent a positive one.
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
42

Structural/transitional complexity depresses scoring confidence−5

Focusrite's pre-H1 trading update for the 18-month transition period delivers a net miss on revenue against the company's own disclosed consensus range. The 12-month revenue of approximately £164 million falls at or below the bottom of the disclosed sell-side range of £165.0–168.1m (midpoint miss approximately −1.5%), while the critical 6-month figure (the H1 equivalent) of approximately £76 million comes in below the bottom of its own disclosed range of £77.0–80.1m. The single definitive catalyst — and it is a negative one — is the confirmation that H2 (September 2025–February 2026) saw a 5% revenue decline YoY, driven by US distribution channel destocking following pre-tariff loading. The #1 metric is the H2 revenue figure, which at £76m is the weakest 6-month print since at least FY24 H1, signalling that the tariff/inventory disruption is taking longer to clear than the market had priced.

The mechanical H1 tracking calculation produces a revenue deviation of −8.4pp against the 3-year seasonal baseline — nominally a SELL SIGNAL — but this figure is heavily distorted by the year-end change from August to February. The Sharescope FY1 consensus of £186.6m was built on the old August year-end and includes the next H2 period (March–August 2026) which has not yet traded. Stripping out this distortion and measuring H1 revenue of £76m against the company's own disclosed 6-month consensus of £77–80.1m produces a real-world deviation of approximately −1.3 to −5pp — more consistent with IN LINE to CAUTION rather than a SELL SIGNAL. The single credible positive that contains downside risk is the EBITDA in-line message: despite the revenue miss, gross margins are "slightly ahead" of the prior year and operating margins are stable. The Martin Audio recovery is a secondary positive. The US tariff and channel inventory unwinding are explicitly presented as known, temporary, and manageable; if this characterisation holds, the H1 FY27 comparator will be clean.

Brokers face an unusual task: the entire consensus framework needs to be restructured around the new February year-end before any meaningful revision can be made. The current FY1 EPS consensus of 18.0p and FY1 revenue of £186.6m are not directly comparable to today's figures and are likely to be rebased to a Feb 2027 year-end consensus settling in the range of £170–180m revenue and 16–18p EPS — implying a 5–10% net downward revision on a like-for-like basis. The consensus target price of 340p vs a current price of 210p represents 62% implied upside that will not survive the reset; target prices are likely cut to the 260–285p range. The main constraint on the score — and the reason it sits at 42 rather than lower — is the EBITDA in-line message and the margin story, which prevent a full downgrade cycle. Upgrade cycle probability: low in the near term (3–6 months) until the new consensus framework is established and the next trading update confirms destocking is complete.

scorecards.analysisText:
VLX — Volex Group PLC

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update accordingly. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

Volex reports in USD. Revenue is global across 25 countries. The RNS does not include a Currency Movements section with explicit GBP breakdowns by currency. However, Volex reports in USD and has significant USD-denominated operations (North America, Asia manufacturing). The consensus revenue in the Sharescope data is in USD ($1,172.9m FY1). Revenue exposure: manufacturing primarily in Asia (RMB), selling globally (USD, EUR, GBP). Management typically guides on a USD basis. GBP-reporting is likely to introduce some FX noise but the core metric is USD operating profit margin.

From the RNS: "full year data centre revenues are now expected to be approximately double the $118 million achieved in the prior year" — USD revenue metric. No formal currency percentage breakdown vs prior average rate. However, given Volex's global footprint and USD reporting basis, and that consensus TP/EPS in Sharescope is in GBP pence (38.2p), there is a GBP/USD translation effect. No explicit Currency Movements table present. Given the complexity and no formal disclosure, cannot calculate a precise FX penalty. Phase 0B not triggered by the strict RNS disclosure requirement. No penalty applied. Note: GBP/USD translation will be a minor factor in broker modelling — not scored here.

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (latest qtrly report = Q2). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update (year ending 31 March 2026, so this is a trading update with ~1 month to go). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 38.2p · Revenue $1,172.9m (~£869m at 1.35 USD/GBP)
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 41.0p · Revenue $1,237.3m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full snapshot: 32.8p → 38.2p = +5.4p (+16.5%). Strong continuous upgrade cycle: 32.8p (May) → 35.1p (Jul, H1 results) → 37.3p (Nov–Dec) → 38.2p (Feb 2026). Revenue: $1,061m → $1,172.9m (+10.5%). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 38.2p / $1,172.9m for 6 weeks pre-RNS). Direction: firmly positive year, multiple upgrade steps.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.9% of FY = $549.9m · EPS 44.3% of FY = 16.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (1y ago): Revenue $518.2m · EPS 15.1p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): FY1 consensus $1,172.9m − H1 actual $583.9m = implied H2 $589.0m vs prior H2 $568.3m → +3.7% YoY. Implied H2 EPS: 38.2p − 19.6p = 18.6p vs prior H2 20.7p → −10.1% YoY — but this is now overtaken by the RNS upgrade.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not triggered per disclosure criteria.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Year ending 31 March 2026, ~1 month to go)

1. Revenue — FY guidance vs consensus

FY2026 revenue: "at least $1,220 million" vs FY1 consensus $1,172.9m.

Beat vs consensus: $1,220m − $1,172.9m = +$47.1m (+4.0%) minimum. Upper bound not stated but range of analyst estimates was $1,149.3m–$1,192.2m — the "at least $1,220m" guide is above the entire analyst range.

"The Board now expects Group revenue for FY2026 to be at least $1,220 million."

2. Operating profit / margin

Underlying operating margin expected to be "slightly above the top end of the Group's 9–10% target range" — i.e. >10%. Prior consensus underlying operating profit: average $114.8m (range $111.5m–$117.0m). If revenue ≥$1,220m and margin >10%: implied operating profit ≥$122m vs consensus $114.8m = beat of +$7.2m (+6.3%) minimum.

"Underlying operating margins are expected to be slightly above the top end of the Group's 9-10% target range, reflecting both operating leverage from higher revenues and a continued focus on operational efficiency."

3. Data centre driver

Full-year data centre revenues expected to be approximately double $118m achieved in prior year = ~$236m in FY26. This is the primary driver of outperformance. Accelerated customer requirements fulfilled (near-term capacity needs), reflecting Volex's global scale advantage.

"Full year data centre revenues are now expected to be approximately double the $118 million achieved in the prior year."

4. Geopolitical/tariff caveat

Limited direct exposure to Middle East markets. Broader macroeconomic implications "difficult to predict." Board does not anticipate material near-term impact given diversified end markets. No quantification.

5. Capital markets event — 22 April 2026

New medium-term growth targets to be presented. AIM → Main Market listing being considered (FTSE250 eligibility anticipated). Largest shareholders being consulted.

"The Board believes that a move to the Main Market would facilitate access to deeper pools of capital and a broader range of investors, supporting increased liquidity in trading of the Group's shares."

6. FY27 caveat on data centre accelerated demand

Management explicitly flags that the accelerated customer demand dynamic "may not recur at the same level in FY2027" — important forward qualifier.

"The Board is encouraged by the strength of the Group's positioning in this market, although this particular dynamic may not recur at the same level in FY2027."

EPS quality check: No EPS disclosed in trading update. Operating profit metric is underlying (pre-amortisation, restructuring, SBC). No tax rate deviation check possible from this RNS alone. Note: Volex has a history of acquisition-related adjusting items; headline EPS will be adjusted figure.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

  • Guidance phrase: "full year results now expected to be significantly ahead of current market expectations" + revenue "at least $1,220 million" + margin "slightly above the top end of 9–10% target range." Covers current FY (FY26). Forward-looking FY27 caveat on data centre explicitly included.
  • Classification: 🟢🟢 Upgrade-triggering — explicit "significantly ahead" language, "at least" revenue figure above entire analyst range, new medium-term targets to follow. Provisional points: +14.
  • Divergence check: Current year beat + FY27 mild caution on data centre dynamic. This is a divergence: FY26 🟢🟢 vs FY27 mildly 🟡. Not a full reversal — FY27 caveat is about one specific dynamic (accelerated demand) not the underlying business. Flag: 🟡 Beat quality — FY27 data centre dynamic explicitly flagged as potentially non-recurring at same level. Carry as separate row in Phase 5.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

Revenue growth trajectory: +26.3%, +19.0%, +12.3%+ (minimum) → 🟡 Volatile/moderating — rate of growth has been slowing but still very strong. The data centre acceleration may re-accelerate FY26 result above trend.

EPS growth trajectory: +14.6%, +8.5%, ~+13% → 🟢 Steady — consistent mid-teens growth.

Revenue trajectory (HoH YoY): +30.4%, +10.3%, +12.6%, +11.9%+ → 🟢 Steady — consistent double-digit growth.

EPS trajectory (HoH YoY): +6.3%, +10.1%, +29.8% (H1 FY27 surge) → 🟢 Accelerating on H1 basis.

2. Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode)

  • Revenue baseline: 46.9% × $1,172.9m = $549.9m
  • EPS baseline: 44.3% × 38.2p = 16.9p
  • Revenue tracking (pre-RNS): H1 actual $583.9m ÷ FY1 consensus $1,172.9m = 49.8% vs baseline 46.9% → deviation = 🟢 [+2.9pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY
  • EPS tracking: H1 actual 19.6p ÷ FY1 consensus 38.2p = 51.3% vs baseline 44.3% → deviation = 🟢 [+7.0pp] → 🟢 STRONG BUY
  • H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 38.2p − H1 actual 19.6p = 18.6p required vs historical H2 avg 18.2p — burden essentially equal to consensus assumption. Post-RNS upgrade: burden increases to ~20.9p (≥40.5p FY − 19.6p H1), which is still achievable given the data centre strength.
  • Buy triggers: H1 Rev > [$549.9m × 1.015] = $558.1m → 🟢 ✓ ($583.9m > $558.1m) · H1 EPS > [16.9p × 1.015] = 17.2p → 🟢 ✓ (19.6p > 17.2p)
  • Historical hit rate: Both buy triggers fired. Revenue and EPS both in Strong Buy territory pre-results. RNS has confirmed and exceeded.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

Pre-FY: compare implied H2 vs prior H2.

  • H2 Revenue: ≥$636.1m vs prior H2 $568.3m → ≥+11.9% YoY → 🟢 strong
  • H2 EPS: ~20.9p vs prior H2 20.7p → ~+1.0% YoY → 🟡 flat (driven by H1 capturing more EPS this cycle and data centre revenue H2-weighted)

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS trend: 32.8p → 38.2p, net +5.4p (+16.5%). Consistent upgrades throughout year with H1 results (Jul), Capital Markets update (Nov), and quarterly progress.
  • 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat 6 weeks before this RNS — pre-result consolidation)
  • Divergence: Price has run from 354p (May 2025) to 499p (peak Mar 2026) — +41% alongside +16.5% EPS upgrades. Pre-RNS price at 427.5p already pricing in a beat (price pulled back slightly from 499p peak — some caution). RNS now confirms and extends the upgrade.

5. Structural/One-Off Flags

[Data centre doubling — partly one-off accelerated demand]: Revenue doubling from $118m to ~$236m includes a component of "accelerated customer requirements" where Volex fulfilled near-term capacity needs other suppliers couldn't meet. This is explicitly flagged as potentially non-recurring at the same level in FY27. Structural growth in data centre is intact; the acceleration boost is a one-off component.

[AIM → Main Market migration]: Potential FTSE250 inclusion would significantly expand the institutional investor base. Capital Markets Event on 22 April will be a major catalyst — new medium-term targets expected.

"The Board believes that a move to the Main Market would facilitate access to deeper pools of capital and a broader range of investors."

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — Revenue "at least $1,220m" + "significantly ahead" language — above entire analyst range: The dominant catalyst. With consensus range of $1,149–$1,192m, a floor of $1,220m is a 2–6% beat at the bottom and potentially 5–10%+ if the actual lands closer to $1,250–1,270m. Operating margin >10% adds further punch. This forces an immediate revenue and EPS upgrade cycle.

#2 Driver — Data centre revenues doubling (~$236m) — confirms structural positioning: Data centre was the growth thesis. A doubling in one year confirms Volex as a credible, scaled beneficiary of AI infrastructure capex. The FY27 caveat is important but does not undermine the structural case — it only flags that the accelerated-order dynamic (customer stockpiling/urgency) may moderate.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: UP — from 38.2p to estimate 42–44p (+10–15%). Revenue: UP from $1,172.9m to $1,220m+ consensus floor; broker estimates likely $1,230–1,260m range.
  • FY2 (FY27) EPS: UP more cautiously — from 41.0p to 42–44p (+2–7%), reflecting new medium-term targets from Capital Markets Event (22 April) offset by data centre normalisation caveat.

Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP 496p likely revised upward to 540–600p range. At 427.5p, upside to revised TP: 26–40%. Brokers will reiterate/upgrade to Buy/Strong Buy. Potential for new initiations post-AIM migration.

Conservative guidance read-through: "At least $1,220m" is classic conservative floor language. "Significantly ahead" is strong. Taken together, actual result likely $1,230–1,260m. This increases upgrade cycle probability.

Key risk: The FY27 data centre caveat is real. If accelerated demand created channel inventory builds (customers stockpiling), FY27 data centre revenues could step back to $180–200m rather than sustaining $236m. This would cap the FY27 upgrade. Additionally, AIM → Main Market listing uncertainty and macro/tariff headwinds cited.

"The Board is encouraged by the strength of the Group's positioning in this market, although this particular dynamic may not recur at the same level in FY2027."

Consistency check: Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade (+10–15%). Tone must be Constructive or Strongly positive. → 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting.

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

87/100 · Confidence: 82–92 · No FX adjustment · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Revenue "at least $1,220m" — above entire analyst range ($1,149–$1,192m)+18
🟢 Underlying operating margin >10% — above 9–10% target range+12
🟢 Data centre revenues doubling ($118m → ~$236m) — AI infrastructure beneficiary confirmed+12
🟢 H1 tracking: Rev +2.9pp, EPS +7.0pp — both STRONG BUY signals fired+10
🟢 EPS upgrade cycle +16.5% over year, pre-results momentum confirmed+8
🟢 AIM → Main Market migration — FTSE250 catalyst, capital markets event 22 April+6
🟡 Beat quality — FY27 data centre acceleration may not recur at same level−5

🔴 No numeric EPS guidance — full extent of beat unclear pre-results−3
🔴 "Significantly ahead" is qualitative; final result could disappoint vs elevated expectations−2

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The single definitive catalyst is the statement that "full year results are now expected to be significantly ahead of current market expectations" with revenue guided to "at least $1,220 million" — a floor that exceeds the entire analyst range of $1,149–1,192m. The #1 metric is data centre revenues, now expected to be approximately double the prior year's $118m (~$236m), driven by AI infrastructure demand and Volex's ability to fulfil accelerated customer capacity needs when competitors could not. Underlying operating margin is expected above the top of the 9–10% target range, implying underlying operating profit of ≥$122m vs consensus $114.8m (+6.3% at minimum).

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-RNS H1 tracking signalled strength: revenue +2.9pp above seasonal baseline (Strong Buy) and EPS +7.0pp above baseline (Strong Buy) — both buy triggers fired. The implied H2 revenue of ≥$636m is +12% vs prior H2 $568m, consistent with data centre-driven acceleration. The FY27 caveat — that accelerated demand "may not recur at the same level" — is the key constraint on the upgrade cycle. Brokers will need to assess how much of the $236m data centre revenue is structural vs pull-forward. The bear case for FY27 is a step-back to $180–200m in data centre rather than sustaining $236m; even in this scenario, Volex's other divisions (EV, Medical, Consumer, Industrial) are described as trading "broadly in line" with H1 — providing a resilient base.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26 EPS upgrades from 38.2p to 42–44p (+10–15%) are highly probable. Revenue consensus will be revised to $1,230–1,260m. FY27 EPS upgrades are likely more modest (41p → 42–44p, +2–7%) pending new medium-term targets at the Capital Markets Event on 22 April 2026 — this event is the next major catalyst and may provide guidance that underpins a further upgrade cycle. TP from 496p to 540–600p range, implying 26–40% upside from 427.5p. AIM→Main Market migration is an additional non-earnings catalyst. 🏁 Strongly positive: revenue floor above entire analyst range, data centre doubling, margin above target — immediate upgrade cycle starting; FY27 normalisation caveat limits the second-year upgrade but the Capital Markets Event on 22 April is the next major catalyst. Score 87/100.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update for year ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check — Missing Baseline Fallback: Water Intelligence is a US-centric business reporting all revenues in USD. The trading update contains no Currency Movements table and no prior year average exchange rate disclosure. USD exposure is effectively ~100% of revenues (all actuals reported in USD). GBP/USD spot rate as at 17 March 2026: approximately 1.3226 (sourced via web search). No prior year average rate disclosed in RNS — missing baseline fallback applied. Rule: >50% USD exposure, missing rate baseline → apply mid-point penalty of –11 points; widen confidence range by ±8pp. Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−11 pts) · ~100% USD · missing rate baseline · confidence ±8pp.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 39.2p, Revenue £94.0m. FY2: EPS 41.9p, Revenue £99.6m.
  • Consensus net change: EPS nominally +2.9% (38.1p → 39.2p) but with massive volatility: peaked at 44.2p in July 2025, fell sharply to 39.6p Feb 2026 then settled at 39.2p. Revenue consensus equally volatile: started £84.3m, spiked to £130.3m, fell back to £94.0m. Last-4-week EPS trend: FALLING. Momentum: reversing.
  • 3yr avg H1 % of FY: Revenue 50.2% (3yr avg); EPS 67.2% (3yr avg — H1 very heavily weighted for EPS).
  • H1 known from Sharescope (current period): Revenue £45.0m; EPS 22.4p.
  • FX: Rule 1 applied (−11 pts). ~100% USD. GBP/USD spot 1.3226. No prior avg disclosed. Missing baseline. Confidence ±8pp.
  • Critical FX translation note: FY25 revenue of $90.4m at 2025 average GBP/USD ~1.312 = approximately £68.9m GBP — a massive shortfall vs £94.0m consensus. This creates a systematic translation issue that brokers must address in their model revisions.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: Pre-FY Trading Update (year ended 31 December 2025)

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — GBP revenue miss vs consensus: The translation of $90.4m at current GBP/USD 1.3226 produces approximately £68.4m GBP — against a consensus of £94.0m. This is a ~27% shortfall. The combination of a large GBP revenue shortfall, falling EPS trend, H1 EPS –10.1pp below seasonal norm, and no explicit FY26 guidance creates a cautious backdrop. Water Intelligence reported FY25 revenue of $90.4m (+9% USD), but at the current GBP/USD rate of 1.3226 this translates to approximately £68.4m GBP — representing a ~27% miss against the £94.0m consensus. The fundamental challenge for WATR is that it operates and reports in USD while the Sharescope consensus is denominated in GBP, creating a systematic translation gap that brokers must now reconcile with materially lower GBP revenue and EPS estimates.

The H1 EPS tracking data confirms structural weakness in the consensus: at 22.4p, H1 represents only 57.1% of the 39.2p FY1 consensus, against a 3-year seasonal average of 67.2% — a deviation of –10.1pp, which fires the SELL SIGNAL. The implied H2 EPS burden of 16.8p is nearly double the historical H2 average of 9.7p, making the current consensus structurally implausible without a transformational change in H2 profitability that has no historical precedent.

The FX Rule 1 penalty of –11 points is applied for ~100% USD exposure with no prior-year average rate disclosed. Despite solid underlying operational execution (EBITDA +15%, margins improving, balance sheet strong at 1.17x ND/EBITDA), the GBP translation issue and EPS H1 tracking weakness together point firmly to a cut cycle. The market has already priced in significant deterioration (share price –68% from peak), but formal broker downgrades to revenue and EPS are expected following this RNS. The IoT/Bluebot strategy is interesting but early-stage and insufficient to prevent near-term cuts.
