scorecards.analysisHtml:
PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT
  • Routing: Routing mode: pre-H1 (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 36.1 (cents) · Revenue $90.4m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 43.1 (cents) · Revenue $99.6m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change -5.2% over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: STALLING (flat at 36.1 since mid-May).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 50.2% of FY = $45.4m · EPS 67.2% of FY = 24.3 cents
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue $41.5m · EPS 20.7 cents
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY1 fc $90.4m vs FY actual just reported $90.4m — exact match. EPS: FY1 fc 36.1 cents vs FY actual Adjusted Basic EPS 39 cents — a beat.
  • FX: N/A — Phase 0B not applicable (wholly USD-reporting entity).
  • Reporting currency & debt: USD · Net debt: current H1 $27.7m → FY1fc $19.0m → FY2fc $17.0m · ND/EBITDA: current 1.90x / FY1fc 1.20x / FY2fc 0.90x · Interest cover FY1fc: 5.4x · Debt flag: Manageable leverage
PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: Full Year Results (Audited Results for Year Ended 31 December 2025).

  1. Revenue figures — FY25 revenue $90.4m vs FY24 $83.3m = +9% YoY. Against FY1 consensus of $90.4m, this is an exact match — 0% beat/miss, in line with consensus.
During 2025, Group revenues grew 9% to $90.4 million (2024: $83.3 million).
  1. EPS / earnings figures — Adjusted Basic EPS grew 8% to $0.39 (2024: $0.36) — 39 cents vs consensus 36.1 cents — a +8.0% beat vs consensus.
Adjusted Basic Earnings Per Share grew 8% to $0.39 (2024: $0.36).
  1. EBITDA / profitability — EBITDA Adjusted grew 15% to $16.5m (2024: $14.3m), margin improved 110bps to 18.2%. Adjusted PBT grew 9% to $9.2m. Sharescope FY1fc EBITDA ($74.5m) is inconsistent with RNS-reported FY25 actual EBITDA Adjusted of $16.5m and is treated as unreliable.
EBITDA Adjusted grew 15% to $16.5 million with margins improving 110 basis points reflecting focus on increased efficiencies in corporate operations
  1. Segmental performance — Core ALD grew sales 4% to $75.7m; international WII grew 44% to $14.7m, now 16.3% of total revenue. "Same store" corporate revenue flat at ~$54m but profit +6% with margin improving from 17.8% to 18.9%.
Corporate-operated "same store" revenue remained flat at approximately $54 million (2024: $54 million) and profit before tax increased 6% to $10.3 million (2024: $9.7 million) as we continue to create more efficient operations. Margins on same store locations increased to 18.9% from 17.8% in 2024.
  1. Order book / forward visibility — Not a backlog-disclosing business model, but Q1 2026 revenue +9% YoY, "more than doubled the rate of growth of 4% reported in Q1 2025," despite severe weather disruption.
Group revenue increased in Q1 2026 by 9% to $23.2 million (Q1 2025: $21.3 million). 9% Q1 2026 growth for the Group reinforces the momentum from the 9% annual revenue growth of 2025.
  1. Capital returns — No dividend. Share buybacks of $1.6m executed in 2025. Credit facility expansion with M&T Bank (subsequent event, Feb 2026).
Disciplined Capital Allocation Policy focusing on organic growth with allocations for selective acquisitions and consistent repurchase of shares
  1. Qualitative tone — Highly confident, multi-pronged growth narrative: TES platform positioning, AI/IoT tailwinds, Dallas Template cost-efficiency rollout, continued M&A optionality.
Through May, we have maintained the momentum of our 2025 and Q1 2026 financial performance.

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate for 2025 was 22% (2024: 17%) — a +5pp deviation, above the 3pp threshold. This works against the EPS beat, not in favour — a higher tax rate is a headwind overcome to still post an 8% beat. The FY25 beat is delivered despite a 5pp higher effective tax rate — underlying pre-tax profit growth is stronger than the bottom-line EPS growth suggests.

Outlook & Guidance Classification: "remain on track to meet full year expectations" / "maintained the momentum" — qualitative, not numeric. Classification: Constructive — confident qualitative language with multiple visible earnings drivers named. Provisional points: +6 to +10.

Divergence check: No divergence — FY25 delivered a genuine beat and the FY26 outlook is consistently constructive.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING
  1. Half-on-Half (HoH) growth pattern

H2 derivation check: 3y ago (FY22): Sharescope shows H1 13.0 + H2 19.2 = 32.2, but FY is listed as 19.2 — GLITCH CONFIRMED. Corrected H2 = 19.2 - 13.0 = 6.2 cents.

EPS trajectory: Volatile — H1 FY24 +1.5%, H2 FY24 +30.2%, H1 FY25 +8.2% — large swings consistent with structural H2-light EPS pattern.

Revenue trajectory: Steady — H1 FY24 +7.2%, H2 FY24 +12.1%, H1 FY25 +8.4% — consistently positive mid-to-high single digit growth.

  1. Seasonal H1 tracking — pre-H1 mode, but today's RNS is itself FY25 results; H1 26 has not occurred. UNTRACKABLE this round due to timing, not disclosure gap. Q1 2026 revenue +9% YoY provides early informal context for H1 26 momentum.
  1. Implied H2 momentum — H2 FY25 (just-completed) vs 3yr avg of corrected H2 figures: 5.4 cents historical avg vs H2 FY25 actual of 16.6 cents = +207% YoY vs 3yr avg. Classification: strong, but this is now historical fact, not forward-looking, so no incremental scoring weight under the pre-H1 routing gate.
  1. Forecast Broker momentum overlay — EPS trend: net change -5.2% over snapshot period; brokers had been net cutting forecasts, steepest cuts Feb-Mar 26. 4-week trend: STEADY. Divergence: Share price fell from 825p to 245p (~70% decline) while EPS forecasts only fell ~5% — a major divergence. Not a scored Phase 5 component — recorded in commentary only.
  1. Balance sheet & debt profile — Net Total Debt $19.3m (2024: $15.7m), 23% increase YoY funding acquisitions. ND/EBITDA 1.17x actual (2024: 1.10x) — modest increase, still low leverage. Debt flag: Manageable leverage — no direct revision impact expected.
  1. Structural or one-off flags

Tax rate step-up: Effective tax rate rose from 17% to 22% YoY — a permanent headwind to bottom-line conversion if it persists.

WII international mix shift: International revenue mix grown from 12.5% to 16.3% in two years, WII losses narrowing 52% YoY.

Preventive Maintenance product sales ramp: Management flags 2H 2026 as inflection point for new product-sales revenue stream.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

#1 and #2 Drivers — #1: Adjusted EPS beat (39c vs 36.1c consensus, +8%) combined with exact revenue in-line print — signals margin/cost-efficiency outperformance, viewed as higher quality and more durable. #2: Q1 2026 momentum commentary (+9% YoY, more than double the +4% pace of Q1 25), de-risking FY26 numbers.

Forecast revisions — FY1 (now actual): establishes higher actual base than brokers modelled. FY2: Revenue modest upward revision (+1-3%); EPS more meaningful upward revision (+5-10%) given higher base and margin efficiency gains.

Target price and recommendation — Brokers likely to raise consensus TP given the beat and margin trajectory, though tempered by the extreme share price de-rating (245p vs consensus TP of 515p — a 53% discount).

Conservative guidance read-through — "remain on track to meet full year expectations" reflects genuine confidence given specificity of supporting detail, increasing probability brokers treat commentary as credible upside support.

Key risk — The 75% share price decline against only a 5% EPS forecast cut suggests the market is pricing in risks not yet visible in the numbers — US economic slowdown risk, interest rate/inflation pressure on costs.

EBITDA Adjusted margins for Q1 2026 remained constant at 19% despite rising gas and consumables prices due to the Iranian conflict.

Consistency check — Net FY1 EPS revision direction: upgrade. Tone label consistent: Constructive.

Overall tone — Constructive / modest upgrades likely

Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
71
/100
Confidence range: 64–77 · Constructive / modest upgrades likely
Adjusted EPS beat (+8% vs consensus, on in-line revenue)+10
Margin expansion (EBITDA margin +110bps; same-store margin +110bps)+7
Q1 2026 momentum (+9% YoY, more than double prior-year pace)+6
Constructive forward outlook with specific named drivers+5
Tax rate step-up (17%→22%) partially offsets EPS quality-3

Para 1 — Headline numbers: Water Intelligence delivered Adjusted Basic EPS of 39 cents, an 8% beat against the Sharescope FY1 (FY25) consensus of 36.1 cents, while revenue of $90.4m landed exactly in line with consensus, up 9% YoY from $83.3m. The single definitive catalyst is the quality of the beat: with revenue precisely matching expectations, the entire EPS outperformance came from margin execution — EBITDA Adjusted margin expanded 110 basis points to 18.2%, and on a "same store" basis, corporate-operated margins improved from 17.8% to 18.9%, evidence of genuine operating leverage rather than acquisition-driven optical growth.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: As a pre-H1 mode ticker, the conventional H1-tracking framework is untrackable this round since today's release is itself the FY25 full-year print — the relevant forward signal instead comes from the disclosed Q1 2026 revenue growth of +9% YoY, which more than doubled the +4% pace seen in Q1 2025, despite severe weather disruption early in the quarter. The upgrade case holds even in a cautious scenario because the beat was driven by structural margin improvement (Dallas Template cost efficiencies) rather than a one-off item — and this occurred despite a 5pp step-up in the effective tax rate (17% to 22%), meaning underlying pre-tax profit growth was even stronger than the EPS print suggests.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: Brokers are likely to revise FY26 EPS upward by roughly 5–10%, since the FY26 consensus of 43.1 cents was built on a now-superseded FY25 base of 36.1 cents rather than the actual 39 cents delivered — the higher actual base mechanically lifts FY26 modelling even before any operational re-rating, while FY26 revenue is likely to see a smaller +1–3% uplift given it was already broadly in line. Consensus target price (currently 515p) is likely to be raised modestly, though the main watch point and constraint on the score is the extraordinary 70% share price decline (from 825p to 245p) against only a 5% net EPS forecast cut over the same period — a divergence this stark suggests the market has been pricing in risks that a single quality beat does not fully resolve, even as it supports the fundamental upgrade case.

🏁 CONSTRUCTIVE — high-quality EPS beat (+8%) driven by margin execution on in-line revenue; Q1 26 momentum doubles prior-year pace; FY26 consensus likely to see modest upward EPS revision (+5-10%) off the higher actual base, tempered by the unresolved share price/fundamentals divergence.

scorecards.analysisText:
WISE — Wise PLC

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

WISE · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY mode. Interpreting as Q4/FY trading update for year ended 31 March 2026. This is a Q4 FY26 + full year FY26 metrics announcement.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 37.0p · Revenue £1,868m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 38.8p · Revenue £2,157m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change: 39.8p → 37.0p = −7.0%. Complex pattern: initial downgrade from 39.8p to 36.9p (Jun 2025 — probably H1 FY26 results), then recovery to 37.5p (Oct 2025), then cut to 34.4p (Nov 2025), recovery to 37.0p (Jan 2026), held flat since. Revenue: 1,644m → 1,868m (+13.6%). 4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (FLAT).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue: 46.0% × £1,868m = £859m. EPS: 41.3% × 37.0p = 15.3p.
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25 H1): Revenue £892.6m · EPS 20.7p
  • Implied H2 YoY: Revenue: FY26 actual £1,609.2m (disclosed in RNS as underlying income for FY26) vs FY25 £1,806.2m. Wait — note Wise reports "underlying income" not revenue per standard P&L. Sharescope consensus uses £1,868m as "Revenue" — this appears to include interest income on customer holdings. RNS states FY26 underlying income £1,609.2m (reported) vs £1,619.7m (constant currency). Sharescope FY1 fc £1,868m — large gap vs RNS £1,609m. This requires reconciliation.

Critical data note: Wise's RNS reports "underlying income" = £1,609.2m for FY26. Sharescope consensus of £1,868m appears to include customer holdings interest income or is using a different revenue definition. The RNS states FY26 revenue grew 18% to £1,609m. Sharescope may be using a broader "total income" basis. This reconciliation is material for the scoring.

  • FX: WISE reports in GBP but has revenues across USD, EUR, AUD, SGD, and many other currencies globally. Constant currency disclosure = reported ±0.5pp (actually 18% reported vs 19% constant currency = 1pp difference on FY full year). Phase 0B constant currency override assessment below.

Phase 0B FX assessment: RNS explicitly discloses: FY26 underlying income £1,609.2m reported vs £1,619.7m constant currency = 1.0pp difference. This exceeds the 0.5pp threshold for the constant currency override. Override does NOT fire. FX impact = ~£10m drag (0.6% of revenue). Wise's currency exposure is heavily diversified across multiple currencies — no single non-GBP currency >30% is likely given global diversification across 40+ currencies and the natural hedging from cross-currency flows in the business model itself. Applying Phase 0B: no single currency >30% confirmed from business context. No penalty triggered.

FX: No Phase 0B penalty — diversified currency exposure, no single currency >30%.

  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP. Note: Wise's "net borrowing" in Sharescope is misleading — the large negative figures (e.g. −£11.8bn FY25 H1) represent customer holdings/float, not corporate debt. Corporate cash position is separate. This is a payment institution — interest cover/ND/EBITDA metrics from Sharescope are not applicable as standard leverage metrics. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered (at corporate level).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

WISE · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (Q4 + FY metrics)

1. Revenue — FY26 underlying income £1,609.2m vs consensus £1,868m

This requires the revenue definition reconciliation. Sharescope £1,868m likely includes interest earned on customer float (~£29.4bn at 37.5bps spread = ~£110m) plus broader income items. The RNS "underlying income" of £1,609.2m may be the fee/transaction-based income only.

Using RNS figure: FY26 underlying income +18% reported = £1,609.2m. Prior year FY25 = £1,809.2m/0.18+1 → actually: £1,609.2/1.18 = £1,364.6m. Wait — RNS states FY26 +18% growth to £1,609.2bn (note: the RNS appears to erroneously say "£1,609.2bn" — this is clearly £1,609.2m). Prior year FY25 = £1,609.2/1.18 = £1,364.6m. But Sharescope shows FY25 (1y ago) Revenue = £1,806.2m.

The discrepancy is ~£441m. Wise's financial reporting basis is changing: "FY26 results will be presented in USD and in accordance with US GAAP, rather than GBP and IFRS" — this is a significant disclosure. The Sharescope consensus was set under GBP/IFRS; FY26 results will be reported under USD/US GAAP. The revenue definition change (IFRS → US GAAP) likely drives the apparent miss.

Critical conclusion: Revenue comparison between RNS £1,609m underlying income and Sharescope £1,868m consensus is NOT apples-to-apples due to pending US GAAP restatement. Standard broker revision analysis cannot be applied to this metric without the full US GAAP restatement.

RNS key metrics (using RNS definition consistently):

  • FY26 cross-border volume: £181.7bn (+25% vs FY25)
  • FY26 underlying income: £1,609.2m (+18% reported, +19% constant currency)
  • Q4 FY26 underlying income: £435.3m (+24% YoY)
  • Q4 cross-border volume: £49.4bn (+26% YoY, +27% constant currency)
  • Active customers FY26: 18.9m (+21% YoY)
  • Customer holdings: £29.4bn (+37% YoY)
  • Cross-border take rate: 51bps (Q4, down 1bp vs Q3, down 2bps vs prior year 53bps)

"For FY26, growth in active customers, up 21% to 18.9m, combined with the greater adoption of Wise account features, drove a 25% increase in cross-border volume to £181.7bn"

2. EPS / earnings No FY26 EPS disclosed. PBT margin guidance: "towards the top of the 13–16% range" for FY26 underlying PBT margin. At FY26 underlying income £1,609m × top-of-range ~15.5% = underlying PBT ~£249m. On ~1.0m shares (Sharescope — this seems low for Wise; likely 1.0bn shares). EPS calculation: if £249m PAT at ~25% tax = ~£187m; at 1.0bn shares (Sharescope shows 1.0m which must be in millions, so 1,000m = 1.0bn) → EPS = 18.7p. Consensus 37.0p is significantly higher — suggesting either the PBT margin calculation is on a different income base or the share count in Sharescope is wrong.

⚠️ WISE data anomaly: Sharescope shows 1.0m shares in issue. WISE has approximately 1.0 billion shares. Sharescope figures appear to be in millions (standard), so shares = 1,000m = 1.0bn. EPS consensus 37.0p × 1.0bn shares = £370m PAT. At 25% tax → PBT = £493m. Against underlying income of £1,609m this implies a ~31% PBT margin — above the guided "top of 13–16% range."

The reconciliation: Sharescope Revenue £1,868m × 13–16% PBT margin = £243–299m PBT → EPS 24–30p. Sharescope EPS consensus 37.0p requires either higher income or higher margin. The US GAAP restatement and different income definitions make this irreconcilable without the full FY26 accounts.

FY27e bridge: Given the accounting restatement complexity (IFRS → US GAAP), constructing a meaningful FY27e EPS bridge from the available data is not reliable. Noting: cross-border volume growing 25%, take rate declining ~2bps, customer numbers +21% — the operational trajectory is healthy but the translation to EPS under the new reporting basis cannot be derived from this RNS alone.

3. Volume / customer metrics (primary KPIs for Wise) Cross-border volume FY26: £181.7bn (+25%). Active customers: 18.9m (+21%). Customer holdings: £29.4bn (+37%). Wise Business active customers: +26% YoY to 572,000.

4. Take rate / margin Take rate Q4: 51bps (−2bps YoY). FY26 take rate structurally declining as scale grows — priced in. Underlying PBT margin "towards top of 13–16% range." Card/other revenue +29% YoY (diversification).

5. Capital / dual listing No dividend. Dual listing: US Nasdaq listing expected 11 May 2026. FY26 results will be presented in USD/US GAAP. This is a transformational reporting change.

6. Qualitative tone / outlook "Continue to expect FY26 underlying PBT margin to be towards the top of the 13–16% range." Dual listing on track. Physical branch concept launched on Oxford Street. Payments Canada membership granted (direct access). No explicit FY27 guidance.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

For FY26 (current year): "towards top of 13–16% range" — this is borderline Constructive to In-line. The FY25 margin was presumably above this range (given the EPS trajectory), suggesting this could represent caution if brokers were modelling above 16%. Given the RNS says "towards the top" (implying ~15.5–16%), and the take rate is declining: 🟡 In-line with current consensus expectations. Provisional points: 0 to +3.

For FY27 (forward year, mode-relevant): No explicit guidance. Operational momentum healthy (volume +25%, customer +21%). But the accounting change to USD/US GAAP makes forward-year EPS guidance comparison impossible at this juncture. 🟡 In-line — structural growth intact but insufficient detail for upgrade signal.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

WISE · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

#1 Driver — US GAAP/USD reporting change from FY26: The most impactful event in this announcement for brokers is the confirmation that "FY26 results will be presented in USD and in accordance with US GAAP". This is a complete financial reporting transformation. Every broker covering WISE will need to restate all historical models in USD/US GAAP, redefine revenue, reclassify income items, and reset EPS consensus — making the existing £/IFRS consensus of EPS 37.0p and revenue £1,868m effectively redundant after FY26 results are published. This is the single most broker-disruptive event in the announcement.

#2 Driver — Volume growth +25% and customer growth +21% strong, but take rate declining 2bps: Operationally the business is delivering. Cross-border volume £181.7bn (+25%), active customers 18.9m (+21%), customer holdings +37%. These are healthy metrics. However, take rate at 51bps (−2bps YoY) means the revenue per £ of volume is structurally declining as Wise invests in pricing. PBT margin "towards top of 13–16%" — if FY25 margin was ~26% implied PBT/income (40.5p EPS × 1bn shares = £405m at 25% tax → PBT £540m / income £1,806m = 29.9%) then 13–16% is a severe margin step-down. This requires reconciliation with the income definition change but is directionally concerning.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26e): Will be reset under USD/US GAAP. All existing GBP/IFRS estimates are being superseded. Direction of reset: volume and customer metrics beat → positive; EPS margin guidance 13–16% range → below some broker models → negative on EPS.
  • FY2 (FY27e): Cannot be revised until FY26 USD/US GAAP baseline is established. All existing FY27e estimates will be superseded.
  • Consensus TP £11.57: Will be reviewed after US GAAP restatement. Current price 972p.

Conservative guidance read-through: PBT margin "towards top of 13–16% range" — this is the key phrase. If broker models had 16%+ margins, this is a ceiling confirmation. "Including costs related to the Dual Listing" moderates the margin slightly for FY26.

Key risk: The accounting restatement creates maximum uncertainty. Brokers must rebuild all models in USD/US GAAP from scratch. Until FY26 results (Nasdaq listing ~11 May 2026), the existing consensus is effectively stranded. Some brokers may suspend estimates temporarily. "FY26 results will be presented in USD and in accordance with US GAAP, rather than GBP and IFRS" — this is an unprecedented reporting change for a London-listed company of this scale.

Consistency check: FY2 EPS revision direction: uncertain / rebuild (all estimates superseded by accounting change). Tone considering both operational KPI beat and reporting complexity: 🟡 Neutral / hold and wait — strong volume metrics but maximum accounting uncertainty overhang.

Para 1 — Headline numbers: WISE delivered FY26 cross-border volume of £181.7bn (+25% YoY), underlying income of £1,609.2m (+18% reported, +19% constant currency), and active customers of 18.9m (+21%). These are strong operational KPIs. The critical complication is the reporting change: FY26 results will be presented in USD and US GAAP from the 11 May Nasdaq listing, making the existing GBP/IFRS consensus of EPS 37.0p and revenue £1,868m effectively redundant. The PBT margin guidance of "towards top of 13–16%" is the key earnings anchor — operationally robust, but the definition of "income" against which this margin is applied has changed.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: On the Sharescope-consistent (GBP/IFRS) basis, implied H2 revenue is essentially flat vs FY25 H2 (−0.1% YoY), and H2 EPS is similarly flat (−4% YoY). The upgrade resilience is high on volume/customer metrics (structural growth story intact) but the EPS upgrade narrative is constrained by: (i) take rate declining 2bps, (ii) PBT margin compression in the 13–16% range vs what brokers had modelled, and (iii) the reporting change requiring all estimates to be rebuilt in USD/US GAAP. Customer holdings growth of +37% to £29.4bn is strategically significant — this is recurring fee-bearing capital that diversifies income beyond FX transaction take rates.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: The existing consensus of EPS 37.0p / revenue £1,868m / TP £11.57 is being superseded by the move to USD/US GAAP. Brokers will suspend or revise GBP/IFRS estimates ahead of the 11 May 2026 Nasdaq listing and simultaneous FY26 results publication. The direction on volume/growth metrics is positive; the direction on EPS margins and yield per transaction is cautionary. Some brokers will move to Hold pending the new-format results. The key watch point is whether the USD/US GAAP income definition materially changes the apparent revenue base and what FY27e EPS in USD terms looks like against the new reporting baseline. 🏁 Score 52 — operationally strong KPIs (volume +25%, customers +21%) but the US GAAP reporting transition creates maximum estimate uncertainty, take rate compression is structural, and H2 earnings momentum is flat; neutral hold-and-wait verdict pending 11 May FY26 results in USD/US GAAP format.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). RNS is FY Results for 52 weeks to 27 December 2025.
  • FX Check: Wickes operates entirely in the UK. Zero non-GBP revenue exposure. FX derivative losses of £2.1m (cost-side procurement hedges) treated as adjusting item. FX Rule 1 does not apply. No penalty.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 15.9p, Revenue £1,627.7m. FY2: EPS 18.9p, Revenue £1,700.2m. Consensus TP £2.60.
  • Consensus net change: +1.3% (15.7p → 15.9p). Very modest upgrades; revenue barely moved. Last-4-week: FLAT. Momentum: stalling. Note: consensus TP = current close — zero priced-in upside.
  • 3yr avg H1 % of FY: Revenue 52.7%; EPS 56.3%.
  • H1 actual: Revenue £847.9m; EPS 9.8p.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: FY Results (52 weeks to 27 December 2025)

  1. Revenue: £1,636.2m (+5.9% YoY; LFL +4.9%) vs cns £1,627.7m = +0.5% fractional beat.
    "Total revenue of £1,636.2m (2024: £1,544.5m) +5.9% year-on-year"
  2. Adj EPS: 17.4p (+23.4% YoY) vs cns 15.9p = +9.4% beat.
    "Adjusted basic earnings per share 17.4p (2024: 14.1p)"
  3. Adj PBT: £49.9m (+14.4%) vs cns £48.4m = +3.1%. Adj gross margin 37.0% (+44bps). Adj op margin 4.6% (+20bps).
    "Adjusted profit before tax +14.4% year-on-year to £49.9m (2024: £43.6m)"
  4. FY26 guidance confirmed: "We remain comfortable with consensus expectations for adjusted PBT in 2026." Consensus adj PBT FY26 = £57.6m (range £52.0–59.8m).
    "We remain comfortable with consensus expectations for adjusted PBT in 2026."
  5. H1/H2 EPS split: H1 9.8p; H2 implied 7.6p vs prior H2 6.8p = +11.8% YoY. H1 EPS tracking: 9.8/15.9 = 61.6% vs 3yr avg 56.3% = +5.3pp → STRONG BUY SIGNAL.
    "Strong Retail market share with particular gains in timber, tiling & flooring and paint"
  6. Cash: £91.7m (from £86.3m). Average cash £153m. £44.8m returned to shareholders. New £10m buyback announced.
    "Net cash position of £91.7m (£86.3m) after growth investments and £44.8m returned to shareholders"
  7. 300-store ambition: 5 stores opened in FY25; accelerating to 10+ pa from 2028. FY26 capex £40–45m (up from £28.7m). Working capital benefit £5–10m to unwind in FY26.
    "Accelerating investment in future growth with ambition to reach 300 stores"
  8. TradePro +9%, 643k active members (+10.7% YoY). D&I: 5 consecutive quarters of ordered sales growth, 3 consecutive quarters of delivered sales growth. Record market share.
    "TradePro membership scheme continues to attract local traders... sales from TradePro members increased by 9% year-on-year"
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • H1 EPS tracking: 9.8p / 15.9p = 61.6% vs 3yr avg 56.3% = +5.3pp → 🟢 STRONG BUY SIGNAL. H2 burden: 15.9 – 9.8 = 6.1p / 15.9 = 38.4% of cns — well within norms.
  • H1 Revenue tracking: £847.9m / £1,627.7m = 52.1% vs 3yr avg 52.7% = –0.6pp → IN LINE.
  • H2 EPS momentum: 7.6p vs prior H2 6.8p = +11.8% YoY → Moderate/Solid.
  • Revenue trajectory: FY23 £1,562m → FY24 £1,554m (–0.5%) → FY25 £1,636m (+5.3%). Recovering from 2-year period of flat/negative LFL.
  • EPS trajectory: 23.7p → 14.9p (–37%) → 13.9p (–6.7%) → 17.4p (+25.2%). Strong recovery from trough. D&I recovery and TradePro growth driving structural improvement.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — Adj EPS +9.4% beat (17.4p vs 15.9p) + explicit FY26 confirmation (£57.6m PBT): Both elements will dominate. The EPS beat removes downside risk for FY25 and the explicit FY26 PBT confirmation provides the floor for revisions. Brokers can now upgrade with confidence.
2#2 Driver — Record market share + 300-store strategic ambition: The step-up in capex to £40–45m and the 300-store announcement represents a material strategic signal. Medium-term earnings power is significantly higher than consensus implies.
3Forecast revisions: FY26 EPS upgrade from 15.9p to ~18–19p (+13–19%), consistent with confirmed £57.6m adj PBT / ~229m shares × (1–22.4% tax) ≈ 19.4p. Revenue upgrade to ~£1,700–1,720m. FY27 EPS ~21–22p. TP from £2.60 to ~£2.80–3.00.
4"Comfortable with consensus" guidance: The explicit citation of £57.6m consensus adj PBT is unusually precise and provides a direct, unambiguous floor. Not conservative colouring — just confirmed. This removes all downside risk from FY26 estimates.
5Key risk — Capex step-up and working capital unwind: £40–45m capex (vs £28.7m FY25) will compress FCF. The £5–10m working capital unwind creates a further headwind in FY26. Together these reduce the FY26 cash generation story, which may moderate the TP upgrade. "2025 working capital benefit to unwind by £5–10m"
6Tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. EPS beat nearly 10%, record market share, 5 consecutive quarters D&I ordered growth, explicit FY26 confirmation, 300-store ambition. Brokers will upgrade FY26/FY27 and raise TPs. Stock at 215p vs revised TP ~£2.80–3.00 is attractive.
Strongly Positive · Upgrade Cycle Starting
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict

H1 EPS tracking +5.3pp (strong buy)+6
H2 EPS +11.8% YoY (moderate)+3
Revenue +0.5% (fractional beat)+1
Explicit FY26 PBT confirmation £57.6m+2
Record market share + 300-store ambition+3
New £10m buyback+1
FY26 capex step-up / WC unwind FCF pressure–3
DPS flat (no dividend increase)–2
EPS consensus FLAT / mild de-rating YTD–1
Base (pre-FY, significant beat)+60

Wickes delivered a strong set of FY25 results with adjusted EPS of 17.4p — a 9.4% beat against the 15.9p consensus — alongside revenue of £1,636.2m (+0.5% above consensus) and adjusted PBT of £49.9m (+14.4%). Record retail market share was achieved across timber, tiling & flooring and paint, with TradePro active membership growing to 643,000 (+10.7% YoY). Design & Installation recorded five consecutive quarters of ordered sales growth and three consecutive quarters of delivered sales growth. Net cash of £91.7m reflects strong underlying cash generation.

The H1 EPS tracking signal of +5.3pp above seasonal norm was the leading indicator that a FY beat was probable. The explicit FY26 guidance — "comfortable with consensus expectations for adjusted PBT" citing the specific £57.6m midpoint — provides an unusually direct confirmation of the FY26 floor. The 300-store ambition with capex accelerating to £40–45m from FY26 creates a clear long-term growth runway, even if near-term FCF is modestly compressed by the investment step-up.

Brokers will upgrade FY26 EPS from ~15.9p to the 18–19p range (consistent with the confirmed £57.6m adj PBT) and raise TPs from £2.60 to approximately £2.80–3.00. The main near-term headwind is the working capital unwind of £5–10m in FY26 and the capex acceleration, but these are investment for sustainable growth rather than structural concerns. The stock at 215p versus a revised TP of ~£2.80 represents meaningful upside.

WPHO — PHASES 0–5

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as Pre-FY Trading Update. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

  • 3y ago = FY22 · 2y ago = FY23 · 1y ago = FY24 · FY1 fc = FY25e · FY2 fc = FY26e

PHASE 0B — FX REVENUE CHECK

WPHO reports in EUR (Currency: EUR). Revenues are predominantly EUR (European wind market). >30% non-GBP revenue — clearly exceeded (100% EUR revenues). Phase 0B triggered.

GBP/EUR spot (from hVIVO data cross-reference and RWA data): 2025 avg EUR/GBP = 1.17, implied GBP/EUR rate 2025 avg = 1/0.855 = ~1.17. Current GBP/EUR — search not needed; from hVIVO note 26: year-end 2025 rate = 1.15. 2024 avg = 1.18. Direction: GBP weakened slightly vs EUR (1.18 → 1.17 average) = GBP weaker = tailwind for EUR-reporting WPHO. However: WPHO reports IN EUR — its revenues and EPS are already in EUR. The question for Phase 0B is whether GBP investors face a FX tailwind/headwind on translation. Since WPHO reports in EUR and Sharescope consensus is in EUR (stated Currency: EUR), Phase 0B doesn't directly affect the consensus figures. The GBP share price reflects the EUR results.

Revised Phase 0B assessment: Currency: EUR. Consensus figures (EPS, Revenue) are in EUR. No GBP translation adjustment to consensus needed. Phase 0B: the FX exposure check is about company revenue vs company costs in non-reporting currency. WPHO is a Danish/European LiDAR company — revenue EUR, costs mix of DKK/EUR/GBP. No Currency Movements section in RNS. Applying Phase 0B as a tailwind (GBP weakened vs EUR = WPHO's EUR profits worth more in GBP = slight boost for GBP investors). EUR exposure >50% → tailwind → but since company reports in EUR, Sharescope consensus already captures this. Phase 0B override: company reports in EUR; consensus denominated in EUR; no GBP translation adjustment needed. No FX badge.

  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change +11.4% (19.3p → 21.5p) over snapshot period. Steady upward trend. Revenue +13.4% (£231.2m → £262.1m). Last-4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT (locked at 21.5p since Dec 25). Multiple upgrades throughout the year.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.5% of FY = £124.5m · EPS 41.3% of FY = 8.9p

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: +13% YoY growth (stated headline). Organic growth +7% ("particularly pleasing given strong comparative"). The company is confirming in-line delivery.

"XPS has continued to perform strongly with revenues growing 13% and organic growth of 7%"

  1. EPS/earnings: No EPS figure disclosed — full results 18 June 2026. "Confident of achieving full year results in line with expectations." Board confidence stated explicitly.

"The Board is confident of achieving full year results in line with expectations"

FY27e EPS bridge:

  • New base: FY26 implied EPS ~21.5p (in-line with consensus)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: Polaris acquired Feb 2025 — this contributed ~1 month to FY25 and full FY26. FY26 was first full year of Polaris. FY27 will be second full year — no incremental annualisation uplift. Delta: nil.
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: Revenue growing to £279.9m FY27fc (+6.8%). Advisory business up 20% in FY26 with structural demand (surplus management, run-on, regulatory change). Organic revenue growth 7% FY26 → likely similar in FY27.
  • Interest step-up delta: Net debt declining (FY26fc £46.7m → FY27fc £35.8m). Interest cost reducing. Minor positive.
  • FY27e implied EPS: ~23.2p consensus. Bridge supports this — no material revision catalyst.
  1. Service line breakdown: Core Advisory (inc Insurance Consulting) +20%, 57% of group revenue. Administration +5% (McCloud comp), 38%. SIP +10% (4th consecutive double-digit). Insurer revenues tripled, now 10% of group — Polaris contribution.

  1. Structural demand: "Ongoing regulatory change, including run-on for surplus extraction, continuing to underpin strong demand. Inflation-linked contracts remain a structural benefit." Pensions market undergoing "structural shift."

  3. Qualitative tone: CEO: "excellent growth." Polaris "increasingly contributing." Confidence in FY26 in-line delivery.

EPS quality check: No tax or non-recurring flag visible. Services business — clean earnings quality.

FY26: "in line with expectations" — confirmed delivery, no upgrade language. No quantitative upgrade. Structural demand commentary is positive for FY27 but not a formal guidance statement.

Classification: 🟡 In-line — in-line language with positive structural backdrop. Points: +1 to +3.

PHASE 0B — FX Revenue Check

YouGov generates approximately 33% of revenue in the US (£63.1m of £194.8m = 32.4%) and 48% in Mainland Europe (primarily EUR). USD exposure exceeds 30% threshold.

Spot GBP/USD: ~1.34 (from earlier search). Prior year average rate for YouGov (FY to 31 July 2025): the RNS notes "Net appreciation of £ Sterling as its average exchange rate was 5% higher against the USD in the period than in the six months to 31 January 2025." This confirms GBP was stronger vs USD in H1 FY26 vs H1 FY25 — a headwind.

USD Americas revenue ~32.4%. Using the 30–35% band. Headwind (GBP stronger >3c — confirmed as "5% higher") → penalty = −8 pts.

FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~32% USD · 🔴 GBP headwind

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

  • Routing: pre-H1 mode (latest qtrly report = 'Q4'). Interpreting incoming RNS as H1 results (six months ended 31 January 2026). Sharescope data reflects pre-RNS state.
  • FY1 consensus: EPS 33.0p · Revenue £396.6m
  • FY2 consensus: EPS 36.6p · Revenue £409.5m
  • Forecast Broker momentum: EPS net change +2.5% (32.2p → 33.0p) over snapshot period, with a significant upgrade in Oct 2025 (+6.8%) that was subsequently partially reversed. Last-4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (33.4→33.4→33.4→33.0p — modest decline). Revenue net change: +3.1% (£384.9m → £396.6m). TP fell from 561p to 443p (−21.0%).
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.4% of FY = £184.1m · EPS 54.8% of FY (3yr avg) = 18.1p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals: Revenue £191.7m (Sharescope current H1 = FY26 H1 actual from RNS) · EPS H1 ~17.1p (prior year H1 per Sharescope = 16.7p underlying)
  • Note: YouGov has a July year-end (FY26 = Aug 2025–Jul 2026). H1 = Aug 2025–Jan 2026 = 6 months.
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-H1 mode from FY1 consensus): H2 implied = £396.6m − £194.8m = £201.8m vs prior H2 £197.2m = +2.3% H2 YoY. EPS H2 implied: 33.0p − H1 actual. H1 actual underlying EPS: 11.4p (from RNS).
  • FX: 🔴 GBP headwind — ~32% USD, GBP 5% stronger vs USD. FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts)

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

RNS type: H1 Results (six months ended 31 January 2026)

1. Revenue — H1 actual £194.8m (+2% YoY, H1 FY25: £191.7m). vs H1 baseline 46.4% × £396.6m = £184.1m → actual £194.8m = 49.1% of FY1 consensus → deviation = 🟢 [+2.7pp] → 🟢 MILD BUY

"Revenue: £194.8m (H1 FY25: £191.7m) +2%"

2. Adjusted operating profit — significantly below prior year £24.0m (−20% YoY, H1 FY25: £30.1m). Adjusted operating margin 12.3% (FY25: 15.7%).

"Adjusted operating profit: £24.0m (H1 FY25: £30.1m) (20%)"

3. Adjusted EPS — H1 actual 11.4p (H1 FY25: 17.1p) = −33% YoY. vs H1 baseline 54.8% × 33.0p = 18.1p → actual 11.4p = 34.5% of FY1 consensus → deviation = 🔴 [−20.3pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL

Buy trigger EPS: 18.1p × 1.015 = 18.4p: H1 actual 11.4p → 🔴 ✗

4. Shopper division — key drag Shopper adjusted operating profit £6.8m (H1 FY25: £13.9m) — −51% decline. Investment to grow future revenue cost ~£6m incremental in FY26.

"Shopper division's adjusted operating profit of £6.8m (HY25: £13.9m) was impacted by the additional investments to drive future growth"

5. Statutory operating profit improving Statutory operating profit £16.8m (+14% YoY) due to lower separately-reported items (£7.2m vs £15.3m prior year). Positive optics but adjusted is the operative measure.

6. Full-year guidance — FY26 adjusted operating profit £52–56m vs FY1 consensus implied EBITDA £91.7m... wait. The £52–56m is adjusted operating profit, not EBITDA. Reconciling: Sharescope EPS consensus 33.0p implies PBT roughly £38.5m; adjusted operating profit £52–56m vs prior FY (FY25) adjusted operating profit £60.7m — the guidance implies a significant FY26 decline.

"Considering the incremental investment in Shopper of £6m, the Group expects FY26 adjusted operating profit to be £52-£56m."

This implies FY26 adjusted EPS around 25–30p range (vs 33.0p consensus) if the decline in adjusted operating profit is proportional. This looks like a significant miss vs Sharescope consensus of 33.0p.

Wait — the company says "Without the investment in Shopper, our adjusted operating profit would have been broadly flat year on year." Prior FY25 adjusted operating profit = £60.7m. So ex-Shopper investment: £60.7m guidance, minus £6m Shopper = £54–55m midpoint — which is consistent with their £52–56m range.

The Sharescope FY1 EPS of 33.0p implies the market was expecting broadly flat adj EPS vs FY25 (which was 31.7p underlying). The £52–56m adjusted operating profit guidance implies FY26 adj EPS of approximately 27–30p (using 20% tax, net finance costs ~£8m, 117m shares). This is a cut of ~10–15% vs consensus.

7. Value Delivery Plan (VDP) — margin recovery roadmap Wave 1 executed this month (March 2026): expected to contribute £2.5m to FY27 profitability. Wave 2 in planning phase for summer 2026. Combined waves 1+2 expected to deliver >350bps annualised margin uplift relative to H1 FY26 margin (12.3%) — implying FY27 margin of ~16%+.

"Combined impact of the first two waves expected to deliver annualised margin uplift in excess of 350bps"

8. Strategic review of Shopper division Board commenced strategic review including potential disposal and synergy options.

"Board therefore continues to actively consider actions that could enhance the strategic positioning of Shopper and unlock long-term shareholder value."

9. Share buyback replacing dividend "Board intends to launch the share buyback programme later this year, upon completion of the aforementioned loan refinancing." Final dividend paid in December 2025 (9.25p); no interim dividend for H1 FY26.

10. Net debt £160.3m, leverage 2.1x Below the 2x medium-term target but still elevated. Term loan maturities in 2027.

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

2. Seasonal H1% Baseline and Tracking Deviation

  • Revenue baseline: 46.4% × £396.6m = £184.1m. H1 actual £194.8m ÷ £396.6m = 49.1% → deviation = 🟢 [+2.7pp] → 🟢 MILD BUY
  • EPS baseline: 54.8% × 33.0p = 18.1p. H1 actual 11.4p ÷ 33.0p = 34.5% → deviation = 🔴 [−20.3pp] → 🔴 SELL SIGNAL

Revenue H1 is mildly ahead of seasonal norm; EPS H1 is severely below (the Shopper investment is the explanation). The divergence signals the business is top-line performing but bottom-line impacted by investment spend.

H2 EPS burden: 33.0p − 11.4p = 21.6p required H2 vs prior H2 adjusted EPS = 31.7p − H1 prior 17.1p = 14.6p → burden HIGHER (+48%) than prior H2. The £52–56m FY guidance implies the burden cannot be met at the consensus level.

3. Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical

H2 implied revenue: £396.6m − £194.8m = £201.8m vs 2yr avg H2 (Aug-Jan period) = (£119.9m (FY23 H2) + £126.9m (FY24 H2) + £197.2m (FY25 H2))/3 = £148.0m → FY26 H2 implied +36.4% above historical — but this is distorted by the Shopper acquisition in FY24 which doubled revenue. Using last 1yr: prior H2 £197.2m vs implied £201.8m = +2.3% → 🟡 flat (modestly positive)

H2 EPS implied: The FY guidance of £52–56m adj operating profit with H1 at £24.0m → H2 adj OP needed = £28–32m vs H1 £24.0m. This requires a meaningful H2 improvement, consistent with seasonal H2 weighting and Shopper investment front-loaded in H1. Achievable but not guaranteed.

4. Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS +2.5% net over period but with large swing (Oct upgrade +6.8%, then cuts)
  • TP −21.0% (561p → 443p) — significant broker confidence deterioration
  • 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (marginal but directionally negative)
  • Divergence: TP has fallen substantially despite modest EPS upgrade — suggests market is applying a lower P/E multiple as growth visibility reduces.

5. Structural Flags

  • Shopper strategic review: The explicit statement that the Board is "considering a potential disposal" of Shopper is a significant M&A signal. If Shopper is sold (at FY24 acquisition price of ~£280m or even at a discount), the proceeds could fund debt repayment + buyback, dramatically simplifying the business and improving EPS quality.
  • VDP margin recovery: The >350bps margin uplift target (waves 1+2) restores adj operating margin from 12.3% toward ~16%, which is transformative for earnings quality from FY27.
  • Renewal rates stable at 80%: Core Data Products subscription business is not deteriorating, suggesting the revenue problem is primarily Shopper phasing.
  • Leverage 2.1x — refinancing risk: Term loan maturity in 2027 creates a refinancing event before recovery is fully demonstrated.

PHASE 4 — BROKER REACTION SIMULATION

#1 Driver — FY26 adjusted operating profit guidance £52–56m — implies EPS cut vs consensus The Sharescope consensus of 33.0p assumes ~flat adj EPS vs FY25's 31.7p. The £52–56m adj operating profit guidance implies adj EPS of approximately 27–30p (−10% to −18% cut vs consensus). This is the dominant broker reaction — guidance implies material downgrade.

#2 Driver — Shopper strategic review — disposal potential A Shopper disposal could be transformative: eliminating the £6m FY26 drag, simplifying the business, reducing debt by potentially £150–200m (vs £160m total net debt), and focusing resources on the higher-margin Data Products and Research divisions. Brokers will model the sum-of-the-parts value. This is a significant positive optionality.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 (FY26) EPS: cut from 33.0p toward 27–30p range
  • FY1 adjusted operating profit: cut to ~£54m midpoint (consistent with guidance)
  • TP: Currently 443p; likely to be maintained or modestly trimmed (the Shopper disposal optionality provides a floor). Range 400–450p.

Key risk: Term loan refinancing in 2027, and whether the Shopper strategic review delivers at a premium or discount to book value. Also, the Shopper investment being front-loaded creates H1 FY27 also looking light if returns are delayed.

Overall tone: 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT 30/100 · Confidence: 23–37 · FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~32% USD · 🔴 GBP headwind · 🔴 Cautious / downgrades or target cuts probable

Para 1 — Headline numbers: YOU's H1 FY26 results were mixed: revenue of £194.8m (+2%, slight beat vs seasonal baseline of +2.7pp) but adjusted EPS of 11.4p — 33% below the prior year H1 (17.1p) and a massive −20.3pp miss vs the seasonal baseline. The dominant negative was the Shopper division investment: adjusted operating profit of £6.8m vs £13.9m prior H1 — a £7.1m YoY decline driven by deliberate investment in panel expansion, semi-passive data collection technology, and operational capability. The company acknowledges the £6m incremental FY26 investment explicitly and provides FY26 guidance of adjusted operating profit £52–56m — materially below the ~£62m implied by the FY1 consensus of 33.0p EPS.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: The upgrade resilience is extremely limited for FY26, with the EPS cut inevitable as guidance implies ~27–30p vs 33.0p consensus. The structural positive — entirely forward-looking — is (1) the VDP with >350bps margin recovery target through Waves 1 and 2 (Wave 1 executed March 2026), expected to restore adj operating margin from 12.3% toward ~16% by FY27; and (2) the Shopper strategic review including potential disposal — if Shopper is divested, the remaining Data Products + Research business has far higher margins and simpler growth story, potentially unlocking meaningful value. The FX headwind (GBP 5% stronger vs USD, affecting ~32% of revenue) applies an additional −8pt adjustment to the raw score.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY1 EPS will be cut from 33.0p toward 27–30p as brokers align with the £52–56m operating profit guidance. TP likely trimmed from 443p toward 400–430p. At 178p, the stock is deeply undervalued vs TP (149% upside) — but the market is pricing in earnings disappointment and strategic uncertainty. The key watch point is the Shopper strategic review outcome — a value-accretive disposal could be a transformative catalyst that renders current estimates irrelevant in a positive direction. 🏁 Verdict: H1 adjusted EPS miss driven by deliberate Shopper investment; FY26 guidance implies ~10–18% EPS cut incoming; FX headwind adds −8pts. Offset partially by Shopper disposal optionality. Score 30/100.

scorecards.analysisHtml:
Phase 0 — Routing & FX
  • Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY Results for the year ended 31 December 2025. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.
  • FX Check: Approximately 91% of sales denominated in currencies other than sterling, mostly USD and EUR. USD/GBP average 2025 = 1.312 vs 2024 = 1.278 — GBP strengthened 2.7% against USD (adverse for USD revenues). EUR/GBP average 2025 = 1.173 vs 2024 = 1.177 — GBP marginally weaker vs EUR (near-neutral). USD exposure estimated at ~35% of revenues. GBP/USD change = ~3.5 cents, just above the ±2-cent neutral band. However, the company deployed forward exchange contracts and the net PBT impact of currency movements was effectively nil (+£0.1m). FX Rule 1 applied at the lower band: –8 points. Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~35% USD · GBP headwind largely hedged.
Phase 1 — Data Context
  • FY1 consensus (pre-RNS): EPS 32.0p, Revenue £158.3m. FY2: EPS 39.5p, Revenue £191.6m.
  • Consensus momentum: EPS net change +8.8% over full period (29.4p → 32.0p), with step upgrades in Aug 2025, Jan–Feb 2026. Last-4-week trend: FLAT. Momentum: building through the year, stalling immediately pre-results.
  • 3yr avg H1 % of FY: Revenue 48.5%; EPS 33.8% (highly H2-weighted for earnings).
  • H1 known from Sharescope: Revenue £77.4m; EPS 19.4p. Implied H2 = 38.0 – 19.4 = 18.65p vs prior H2 ~13.35p = +39.7% YoY.
  • FX: Rule 1 applied (−8 pts). USD ~35%. GBP/USD 2025 avg 1.312 vs 2024 avg 1.278. Net PBT impact after hedging: +£0.1m (effectively nil). Penalty carried forward.
Phase 2 — RNS Extraction & Quantification

RNS TYPE: FY Results (Preliminary, unaudited, year ended 31 December 2025)

  1. Revenue FY25: £158.5m (+7.2% YoY from £147.8m) vs FY1 cns £158.3m = +0.1% in line. Record Group revenue.
    "Record Group revenue of £158.5m, 7% higher than the prior year (2024: £147.8m)"
  2. Adjusted EPS: 38.0p vs FY1 cns 32.0p = +18.75% beat. vs prior year 25.95p = +46% YoY. This is the dominant metric and far exceeds even the FY26 consensus forecast.
    "Adjusted Basic EPS up 46% to 38.00p (2024: 25.95p)"
  3. Adjusted PBT: £21.2m (+38.6% YoY from £15.3m) vs FY1 cns PBT ~£21.1m = essentially in line. The EPS beat is partly driven by a favourable effective tax rate of 12.3% adjusted (R&D, patent box) and recognition of deferred tax assets in Poland (£3.6m) and US (£1.5m).
    "Adjusted profit before tax increased 38% to £21.2m (2024: £15.3m)"
  4. Adjusted operating margin: 14.4% (+220bps from 12.2%). Adjusted operating profit £22.8m (+26% from £18.1m). Structural margin expansion driven by MEL closure, mix improvement, operational efficiency.
    "Adjusted Operating Margin 14.4% · 220bps [improvement]"
  5. H1/H2 split: H1 EPS 19.4p (from Sharescope); implied H2 = 38.0 – 19.4 = 18.65p. Implied H2 vs prior H2 (FY24 adj EPS 25.95p – H1 12.6p = 13.35p): +39.7% YoY. H2 momentum: Strong.
    "2025 Adjusted Basic EPS 38.00p vs 2024 25.95p"
  6. Cash generation: £39.7m (+31% from £30.4m). Cash conversion 101%. FCF before M&A: £23.1m. Net debt (bank basis) £31.5m, leverage 0.8x (improved from 0.9x). Balance sheet described as "strong."
    "Cash generated from operations up 31% to £39.7m (2024: £30.4m) … FCF of >£23m … leverage ratio improved at 0.8x"
  7. Dividend: 7.85p total (5.35p final + 2.50p interim) vs cns DPS 8.00p = –0.15p (immaterial). +5% increase on prior year total of 7.48p. Subject to AGM approval.
    "Final dividend up 5% to 5.35p (2024: 5.10p)"
  8. OKC acquisition: Completed November 2025 at €27.6m initial + deferred up to €8.4m. Added £2m revenue in FY25 (partial year). Earnings accretive FY26. Full-year contribution targeted for 2026.
    "The acquisition is expected to be earnings accretive in 2026."
  9. Vietnam factory: £4.3m invested in FY25 of ~$32m total project. Partnership with Seoheung (17.5% stake, $10m contribution). Initial production expected late 2026/early 2027.
    "Construction and commissioning of the leased Vietnam site is underway, ahead of planned completion later this year / early 2027."
  10. Medium-term targets: FY2029 revenue >£230m (7% CAGR from £158.5m); operating profit >£40m by FY2029 (~75% above FY25 £22.8m); ROCE >20% by FY2029; cash conversion >95%. Longer-term ambition: revenue >£300m, operating profit >£60m.
    "Organic growth of 7% CAGR to deliver FY2029 revenue of >£230m; Operating profit of >£40m by FY2029; ROCE of over 20% by FY2029"
  11. FY26 trading outlook: "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations." Footwear volumes to moderate as customers normalise inventory. Transport & Smart Technologies continuing strong. OKC integration progressing well.
    "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations, supported by continued demand in Transport & Smart Technologies and improving order books across several markets."
  12. Footwear moderation caveat: "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025 as customers normalise inventory positions which is an expected transition."
    "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025 as customers normalise inventory positions which is an expected transition, and our operating plans reflect this shift."
Phase 3 — Historical Benchmarking
  • Revenue HoH trajectory: FY YoY growth: FY23 £127.3m → FY24 £126.9m (–0.3%) → FY25 est H1 £77.4m → FY25 actual £158.5m (+7.2%). H1 revenue growth: 9.5% → 10.1% → 8.8% (steady deceleration). H2 revenue: prior year £76.7m, implied FY25 H2 = £81.1m (+5.7% YoY). Classification: Volatile then Steady — large swing in FY24 due to MEL, underlying foams business showing consistent mid-to-high single digit revenue growth.
  • EPS HoH trajectory: FY23 adj EPS ~£29.8p (est); FY24 adj EPS 25.95p (–13%); FY25 adj EPS 38.0p (+46%). H1 EPS: 12.6p → 19.4p (+54% YoY). H2 EPS: FY24 H2 ~13.35p; FY25 H2 implied 18.65p (+39.7%). Classification: Accelerating — clear step-change in earnings power from MEL closure and margin expansion.
  • Implied H2 Momentum (pre-FY mode): H2 Revenue: +5.7% YoY vs prior H2 → Moderate. H2 EPS: +39.7% YoY vs prior H2 → Strong. The H2 EPS acceleration is structural (MEL eliminated, tax benefits, margin improvement).
  • Forecast momentum overlay: EPS consensus stepped up from 29.4p (May 2025) through multiple upgrades to 32.0p. Last 4 weeks flat at 32.0p pre-results. Now 38.0p actual = immediate comprehensive upgrade requirement. Net change full period +8.8% — understates the actual delivery. Revenue consensus very stable at £158.3m for most of the period, confirming revenue was well-flagged; the surprise is entirely in EPS/margins.
  • Structural flags: (1) MEL permanently closed — removes ~£4-5m annual loss drag permanently. (2) Margin step-change: 12.2% → 14.4% with medium-term target >18%. (3) OKC acquisition adds European revenue diversity. (4) Vietnam factory creates Consumer & Lifestyle capacity closer to Asian customers. (5) Tax benefits (R&D, patent box, deferred tax) structurally improve effective rate below 20%. These are durable earnings improvements, not one-offs.

Phase 4 — Broker Reaction Simulation
1#1 Driver — EPS +18.75% beat vs consensus: The 38.0p actual against 32.0p pre-results consensus is the dominant number. Every broker note will lead with this figure and note that the company has delivered FY25 EPS comfortably ahead of the existing FY26 forecast of 32.0p. This forces immediate comprehensive upgrades to FY26/FY27 EPS estimates.
2#2 Driver — Structural margin expansion: The 220bps improvement to 14.4% operating margin, with a stated medium-term target of >18%, provides a credible multi-year upgrade runway. Brokers will model the trajectory from 14.4% toward 18%+ and assign higher earnings multiples accordingly.
3Forecast revision FY1/FY2: FY26 (new FY1) EPS: upgrade from 32.0p to likely 42–46p range (+31–44%). Revenue FY26: upgrade to ~£165-170m (+5–8%), incorporating OKC full year contribution and organic growth. FY27 EPS: from 39.5p to approximately 48–54p. Target price: consensus £6.06 will almost certainly be revised to £7.00–£8.00+ range. At 379p close, the stock trades on a significant discount to likely revised TPs.
4"In line" FY26 guidance read-through: "Trading in the early part of the year has been in line with our expectations" is a contained, pragmatic statement — not a conservative flag in the traditional sense given the massive FY25 beat. Brokers will interpret this as management anchoring FY26 expectations while the footwear normalisation plays out. The medium-term targets (£230m revenue, £40m+ operating profit by 2029) are the more significant forward signals.
5Key risk — footwear moderation: The explicit caveat that footwear volumes will moderate in FY26 is the primary constraint on the upgrade narrative. Consumer & Lifestyle was 50% of revenue in FY25. If footwear declines materially, it could suppress H1 FY26 revenue growth. Brokers will model this conservatively, which is why FY26 revenue upgrades are likely to be modest (5–8%) even as EPS upgrades are more aggressive (driven by base effect and margin improvement). "In footwear, we expect volumes to moderate from the unusually high levels experienced in 2024 and 2025."
6Overall broker-note tone: Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting. Peel Hunt, Singer Capital Markets and others covering ZTF will issue immediate positive flash notes with material upgrades. The combination of a record-breaking EPS beat, clear structural margin improvement, strong cash generation, a multi-year growth strategy with explicit targets, and a FY25 EPS that has already exceeded FY26 consensus creates a compelling upgrade narrative. The stock at 379p will be seen as materially undervalued on revised estimates.
Strongly Positive · Upgrade Cycle Starting
Phase 5 — Final Score & Verdict
76
/100
Confidence range: 72–82 · FX Rule 1 applied (−8 pts) · ~35% USD · GBP headwind largely hedged
EPS beat +18.75% vs consensus+20
Margin expansion +220bps structural+5
H2 EPS momentum +39.7% YoY+4
Record cash generation / strong BS+2
Medium-term strategy roadmap clarity+3
Footwear moderation FY26 headwind–4
FX Rule 1 penalty (~35% USD)–8
Base midpoint (significant beat)+54

Zotefoams delivered a landmark set of FY25 results, with adjusted EPS of 38.0p representing an 18.75% beat against the 32.0p consensus — and, remarkably, already exceeding the FY26 consensus forecast. Revenue of £158.5m was essentially in line (+0.1%), confirming the EPS beat was entirely margin-driven: adjusted operating margin expanded 220bps to 14.4%, driven by the elimination of MEL losses, improved product mix and operational efficiency. Cash conversion hit 101% with FCF over £23m.

The structural improvement in earnings power is the key investment thesis: MEL is permanently closed, the effective tax rate has been reduced through R&D credits and patent box claims, deferred tax assets of £5.1m have been recognised in Poland and the US, and the OKC acquisition brings full-year FY26 accretion. The medium-term targets — £230m revenue and £40m operating profit by FY2029 — imply a 75% increase in operating profit from FY25 and provide a clear multi-year upgrade runway. Brokers must now comprehensively re-base FY26 EPS estimates from ~32p to the 42–46p range.

The primary constraint on a higher score is the footwear moderation caveat for FY26 (Consumer & Lifestyle = 50% of revenue) and the FX Rule 1 penalty reflecting GBP strength against USD. However, these headwinds are well-flagged and partly offset by OKC, Vietnam optionality and Transport & Smart Technologies strength. The upgrade cycle is clearly starting; the only debate among brokers will be the pace and magnitude of the re-rating.
